# TalentScan integration

TalentScan provides AI recruiting tools to simplify hiring.

Greenhouse Recruiting’s integration with TalentScan allows you to add candidates to jobs in Greenhouse Recruiting directly from platforms such as GitHub, Stack Overflow, and LinkedIn. The integration also allows you to add comments directly to a candidate's Greenhouse Recruiting candidate profile, and see all historic interactions with the candidate.

#### In this article

  * Create a Harvest API key for the TalentScan integration
  * Install the TalentScan for Greenhouse Recruiting Chrome add-on
  * Use the TalentScan integration with Greenhouse Recruiting
    * Add a candidate to Greenhouse Recruiting from LinkedIn or other platforms
    * Add a comment to a candidate profile from LinkedIn or other platforms
  * Additional resources



### Create a Harvest API key for the TalentScan integration

To configure the Greenhouse Recruiting / TalentScan integration, you'll need to create a Harvest API key.

Follow the steps in [this article](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/5888163769883) to create the key, and verify that the credentials and permissions below are selected when configuring the TalentScan integration.

#### Credentials

In the _Create New Credential_ box, make the following selections:

  * **API type:** Harvest
  * **Partner:** TalentScan
  * **Description:** TalentScan Harvest API key



#### Permissions

Verify that the following permissions are selected for the TalentScan integration:

**Activity feed**

  * Select all



**Candidates**

  * Select all



**Jobs**

  * Select all



**Users**

  * Select all



When finished, copy and save your Harvest API key, as you will need to provide it to TalentScan in the next step.

### Install the TalentScan for Greenhouse Recruiting Chrome add-on

Click [here](https://chrome.google.com/webstore/detail/cdhnmlboiakmdkjekahaajigphkbkibi/%20%20) to access the TalentScan Chrome add-on in the Chrome Web Store.

Click **Add to Chrome** to install the plugin.

Once the plugin is installed, open any profile on LinkedIn, then click the **TalentScan** icon.

Click to sign in with Google or LinkedIn.

Copy the Harvest API key created previously in Greenhouse Recruiting, and paste it into the TalentScan plugin.

Click **Sync**.

### Use the TalentScan integration with Greenhouse Recruiting

#### Add a candidate to Greenhouse Recruiting from LinkedIn or other platforms

To use the TalentScan plugin, navigate to a profile on LinkedIn, then click the **TalentScan** icon.

Select the vacancy / open job where you want to add the candidate in Greenhouse Recruiting, then click **Add**.

Navigate to Greenhouse Recruiting to view the candidate on the job you selected.

#### Add a comment to a candidate profile from LinkedIn or other platforms

Navigate to a profile on LinkedIn, then click the **TalentScan** icon.

Add your notes as a comment.

To view the comment, navigate to Greenhouse Recruiting and search for the candidate's profile. Any comments added to the candidate through the TalentScan plugin will appear on the **Private** tab under the _Private Notes_ section.

In addition, comments you add to the candidate's profile in Greenhouse Recruiting will appear in the TalentScan plugin when viewing the candidate on LinkedIn or other platforms.

### Additional resources

For additional information or troubleshooting not covered here, visit <https://beta.talentscan.pro> or reach out to [demo_gh@talentscan.pro](mailto:demo_gh@talentscan.pro).

# Custom options sync best practices

A custom options sync mirrors the list of options for a custom field in Greenhouse Recruiting with the list of options for a corresponding field in your HRIS platform. A custom options sync can be enabled to complement any job import or [candidate export](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360002158372) integration you may be using.

#### In this article

  * Which fields should use custom options sync?
  * When should I enable a custom options sync?



### Which fields should use custom options sync?

Common examples of fields built in Greenhouse Recruiting that require custom option syncs are supervisory org and cost center. If you create a custom job field in Greenhouse Recruiting called "Cost Center" that includes a list of all available cost centers in your HRIS platform, a custom options sync will keep the list of cost centers up to date with the options available in your HRIS platform.

### When should I enable a custom options sync for a field in Greenhouse Recruiting?

We recommend setting up custom options sync for fields that have a large number of options, such as hundreds or thousands of options that would be difficult to input manually into Greenhouse Recruiting. Maintaining this many options manually could result in human error. A custom options sync helps by automatically maintaining parity between your HRIS and Greenhouse Recruiting.

We also recommend custom option sync for fields whose options change frequently and require a sync to stay up-to-date with what's configured in your HRIS platform.

**Note** : While a custom option sync integration syncs the list of options on the field configured in your Greenhouse Recruiting account, it doesn't sync the selected value for the field on each Greenhouse Recruiting job.

For example, if you create 'Option A' on a field in your HRIS platform, the option will appear as an available option in Greenhouse Recruiting, but you still need to go to the specific job in Greenhouse Recruiting to change the value for the field to 'Option A.'

**Learn more**

[Custom options sync overview](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360044483232)

[Test a custom options sync](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360001032531)

# FlexJobs integration

The FlexJobs job feed application downloads job feed files (typically in XML format) from web and ftp sites, automatically parses jobs from the retrieved file, compares them to various filters to determine if the job meets our criteria for a 'flexible' job and, if so, places the job into a queue that is manually reviewed by our job researches before final posting to our website.

In the case of Greenhouse, we request a job feed file using the Greenhouse Job Board API. This API provides a JSON representation of all the jobs in your system for a specific company. To isolate the specific company in your Job Board API, we need to know the Job Board API token assigned to each company that we interact with.

### Retrieve Greenhouse job board token

Navigate to the job board that you want to track and choose the ellipses icon on the right side of the page. (**Configure** icon **Job Boards Posts****Ellipses** icon)

Choose **Edit Board Settings** from the dropdown menu.

Navigate to the **URL** section of the page, and **copy** the information in the text field.

Provide the **token** **URL** to FlexJobs.

Using that token, we pull job data from a url in the format:

<https://api.greenhouse.io/v1/boards/TOKEN/jobs?content=true> (for example: <https://api.greenhouse.io/v1/boards/studentloanhero/jobs?content=true>)

The URL must include **?content=true** at the end so that the data returned includes job description content. Once the JSON data for that company has been retrieved, we internally convert that to an XML file and pass it through the process described above.

# Job insights overview

**Permissions:** Site Admins, and Job Admins who can create new jobs and edit job info

**Product tier:** Available for new subscription tiers (Core, Plus, and Pro)

#### Balance expectations with insights

Job insights offer valuable data from your organization's existing jobs to help you set clear expectations for new jobs in Greenhouse Recruiting. You can quickly see how many applications to expect, how long it might take to reach an initial candidate offer, and which sources might produce the best candidates.

Use job insights to help your hiring teams plan more efficiently, craft expectations for operations and finance teams, and invest in the best sourcing strategies.

#### In this article

  * Feature highlights
  * Enable job insights
  * Use job insights
  * Available widgets



### Feature highlights

#### Leverage insights to set clear expectations for new jobs

Knowing how much time you might need to invest in sourcing and interviewing applicants for a new job can help you set individual and team goals. You can use job insights like total applicants to set expectations for the number of candidates to add per week, or you can use offers created insights to inform your operations team of how long it might take before an offer is made.

#### Invest in the best sourcing strategies

Determine which sourcing strategy works best for you and your organization. Job insights offer visualizations that show which sources produced the most candidates and the most hires for a similar job. Use job insights to invest in the most relevant job ad markets, third-party job boards, and marketing campaigns to produce the strongest pool of applicants.

### Enable job insights

To enable job insights, navigate to **Configure** >**Custom Options** , then select **Configure Job Setup Flow**.

Check the **Job insights** box.

Click **Save**.

### Use job insights

Once you've enabled them, you can access job insights when you [create a new job](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/200668380) or view an existing job's [dashboard](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/4402057774747) to help guide your hiring strategies.

#### Access job insights when creating a new job

Job insights are available as a step in the [new job setup flow](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/204923599). Any time you create a new job, you'll be able to access job insights to inform your hiring expectations based on performance metrics from similar jobs.

#### Access job insights on the job dashboard

You can also view job insights for any open jobs in Greenhouse Recruiting.

To access job insights for an existing job, navigate to the **Jobs** tab.

On the _All Jobs_ page, click on the job you'd like to review to open the job's dashboard.

Navigate to the **Job Insights** tab in the left panel of the _Job Dashboard_.

Select a job from the **Benchmark job** menu to review hiring insights from similar roles.

#### Understand and adjust your job insights data

With job insights, you'll use your previous jobs as benchmarks to gain insightful performance data and set clearer expectations for how your new job may perform.

Click the **Benchmark** **job** dropdown and select any of your organization’s existing jobs to get started with insights. You can select open, closed, or draft jobs as your benchmark job.

**Note:** Job insights data is only available for benchmark jobs that you have permission to view. If you don't have permission to view a selected benchmark job, the job insights page will remain blank.

Template jobs and jobs migrated from another applicant tracking system are not available to use as benchmark jobs.

**Tip:** We recommend selecting a benchmark job based on shared job qualities. For example, if you’re creating a new Customer Success job, you might select a job in your Customer Success department.

Selecting a benchmark job by similar function, office, or department can help you better understand how your new job might perform.

Once you've selected a benchmark job, the job insights page will display widgets that offer valuable benchmarking data, such as the number of applications you could expect, your top sources, pipeline history, and more. Use these widgets for a quick snapshot into how your hiring strategies have worked for previous jobs.

### Available widgets

Job insights include the following widgets to help you better understand how your new job might perform:

  * Total applicants
  * Number to reach assessment milestone
  * Offers created
  * Hires made
  * Top sources
  * Pipeline history



#### Total applicants

Use the total applicants widget to see how many applicants might apply to your new job, based on the total number of applications for your benchmark job.

#### Number to reach assessment milestone

Use the number to reach assessment milestone widget to see how many applicants made it past the application review and hiring manager review stages.

#### Offers created

Use the offers created widget to see the number of candidates who made it to the offer stage and the number who received offers for a similar job.

#### Hires made

Use the hires made widget to see the number of hires made for a similar job. You'll also see how long it took to source your benchmark job's first hire and how long it took to move this hire through the pipeline.

#### Top sources

Use the top sources widget to determine which sources might produce the best applicants for your new job. Sources are listed on the left in descending order by the number of candidates they produced, along with the number of hires per source in parentheses.

Use the donut chart for a visual breakdown of your top sources. Hover over any part of the visualization for more details.

**Note** : This widget only lists your benchmark job's top ten sources.

#### Pipeline history

Use the pipeline history widget to see the passthrough rate and the number of candidates who made it through each stage of your benchmark job. Hover over the visualization on the right for more details.

# Schedule an interview with automated scheduling

**Permissions:** Job Admin or above

**Product tier:** Available for new subscription tiers (Core, Plus, and Pro)

Automated scheduling helps you schedule faster and more accurately by automatically identifying the best available times for interviews. Instead of manually scanning calendars, you’ll get a list of suggestions that account for interviewer availability, candidate preferences, and your team's working hours.

#### In this article

  * Using automated scheduling
  * Send the interview invitations
  * How automated scheduling works
  * Troubleshooting
  * Additional resources



### Using automated scheduling

Your calendar must first be connected to your Greenhouse account before we can generate suggestions.

Use the primary email for the calendar you want to connect. Greenhouse can’t pull events from email aliases or subaddresses.

Once your calendar is connected, you can edit its [default settings](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/15730613131931) while you're scheduling the interview.

You can schedule an individual interview by clicking **Automated scheduling** in places such as the candidate profile and the All Candidates page. In a multi-interview stage, you can schedule multiple interviews quickly by clicking **Schedule All** , then **Automated scheduling**.

The left panel on the screen includes interview information, like the interviewer's name, candidate information, and resources. Suggestions will be generated in the main panel.

You can add an interviewer in one of three ways:

  * **Add interviewer from group:** Select the group you'd like to pull an interviewer from.

  * **Add interviewer by name:** Start typing in the text field to search for and select a specific person.
  * **Add interviewer by hiring team role:** If multiple people are assigned to that role, we’ll automatically choose one, based on how the role was configured during job setup.




If the interview you're scheduling is using default interviewers, suggestions will appear automatically. However, if there are no default interviewers, select them from the left panel and select **Save changes**.

Click the **Settings** icon in the top right to change the calendar type or name. This lets you schedule to a shared calendar or view times in a specific time zone.

The **Calendar name** dropdown lists the calendars you can create events on. When you schedule an interview and send invitations, the selected calendar appears on the invite for interviewers.

If you'd like to use the calendar to find time yourself, select the **Find time manually** button.

After selecting **Find Time Manually** , you'll be taken to a calendar interface where you can choose a time for the interview. Keep in mind that any interviewers previously added by group or Hiring Team role will need to be re-added by name using the left-hand panel. Some features, like [interviewer groups](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/205982075), aren’t supported when scheduling interviews manually.

Panel interviews can be scheduled over one day, or over multiple days.

If an interview plan is already set up, suggestions will be generated automatically.

You can confirm the schedule suggested by Greenhouse by selecting the **View in calendar** button. Select **Customize details** to configure the calendar invitations and finish scheduling.

### Send the interview invitations

The _Send Calendar Invite to Interviewers_ page allows you to configure interviewer invites and add any video interviewing options. 

**Note:** Interview times selected in the previous step are not sent to the interviewers' calendars until the steps below are completed. If you exit the scheduling process before sending the invites, the interviews will not be scheduled. 

The  _Schedule Summary_ panel on the right displays the finalized interview schedule. Add a _Location_ and _Video Conferencing_ in the right panel.

To use video interviews, your organization must have set up a video interviewing integration, such as [Zoom](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360042222612).

If any of the interview details listed in the  _Schedule Summary_ panel require updating, click **Back to suggestions** at the top right to return to suggestions.

If you are scheduling multiple interviews, you can use the same email template for all calendar invites, or create individual invites for each interview. The option to _Use the same email template for all interviews_ is selected by default.

You can customize invite emails manually or use an alternative template by unchecking the box next to _Use the same email template for all interviews._

**Note:** Because the information populated by email tokens is unique to each interviewer, if you use the same email template for all interviewer invitations, email tokens will not be added in the interviewer invite preview, but will show up when the interviewer gets the email in their inbox.

When you're ready, click **Send invites to interviewers.** If you're using Google Calendar or Outlook to schedule your interviews, click **Open in Google** to send the interviewer invitation and complete the scheduling process. 

The invitations are sent to the interviewer through their calendars. The scheduled interviews will appear on the candidate's profile shortly.

### How automated scheduling works

Automated scheduling suggests interview times that avoid conflicts, align with the availability submitted by the candidate, and incorporate what we know about your team's availability. Suggestions are based on the following criteria:

  * Suggested time slots fall within a scheduling window that starts tomorrow and extends 30 days out.
  * If the candidate has submitted availability, suggestions will only include times within that range. Interviewers' [working hours](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/28299067084315) in Greenhouse are also respected. Suggestions will not include times outside those hours.
  * When the scheduler’s calendar is connected and they have permission to view interviewer calendars, we avoid overlapping with any busy events, as marked by an interviewer's [availability.](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/28929396249115) Events marked as _Available_ can be scheduled over.
  * Interviewers who have [limits](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/33994471979419) set for the number of interviews they can participate in will still be suggested, but these suggestions will be shown lower on the list if better suggestions that do not set an interviewer over their limit are available.



### Troubleshooting

Many issues that may arise using automated scheduling can be resolved by disconnecting your calendar from Greenhouse and reconnecting it. Follow the instructions for your integration here:

  * [Google Calendar](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360021799232)
  * [Outlook 365](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/115003943972)



If you've selected an interviewer who is out of the office, you'll see an error when trying to generate suggestions. Replace the interviewer in the left panel, then select **Check available times.**

### Additional resources

To learn more about scheduling in Greenhouse Recruiting, including details regarding specific calendar integrations and scheduling across time zones, see the following Support Center resources: 

  * [Scheduling overview](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/36307427046555)
  * [Google Calendar](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360021799232)
  * [Outlook 365](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/115003943972)
  * [Schedule an interview manually](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360045420091)
  * [Schedule user as interviewer](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360050744912)
  * [Scheduling between time zones](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360000157052)
  * [Candidate availability and time zones](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/115002605483)
  * [Use buffer time during scheduling](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/46278259991835)

# Candidate quality by campaign report

**Permissions:** Job Admin and above

**Product tier:** Available for new subscription tiers (Core, Plus, and Pro)

The candidate quality by campaign report provides insight into the effectiveness of your [ad campaigns](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/202073249) by revealing which campaigns return the most candidates, and more importantly, the highest quality candidates, by assigning each campaign a quality percent.

The quality percent on this report is calculated by looking at the average distance a candidate travels through the pipeline. If every candidate was hired, the ad campaign would have produced 100% candidate quality. If every candidate was rejected in the first stage, the quality would be 0%.

**Example** – Imagine candidate Janelle applies through one of your ad campaigns. Janelle has a pretty strong background, so she makes it through five of your seven job stages. If she was the only candidate to apply through that campaign, your quality percent for that row would be 5/7, or roughly 71%.

#### In this article

  * Candidate quality by campaign report
  * Candidate quality by campaign report filters



### Candidate quality by campaign report

To create a candidate quality by campaign report, click **Reports** on your navigation bar.

Click **Essential** **reports** on the left.

Scroll to the _Learn from Past Recruiting Efforts_ section and click **Candidate** **Quality** **by** **Campaign**.

The candidate quality by campaign report will generate.

The candidate quality by campaign report will show information in the following columns where applicable:

  * Job ad campaign name
  * Total candidates in each stage
  * Total hires
  * Quality percentage



**Note** : The report will display data for jobs where you have the appropriate access.

### Candidate quality by campaign report filters

Click **Filters and more** to apply filters to further refine your report.

The candidate quality by campaign report can be filtered by the following:

  * Job
  * Job status
  * Department
  * Office
  * User
  * Hiring team role
  * Custom job field
  * Date applied
  * Include migrated candidates



**Note** : By default, the date applied filter for the report is set to current year.

Click **Apply** after applying any filters to your report.

# Candidate surveys by demographic report

**Permissions:** Site Admin who can see demographic reports

**Product tier:** Available for new subscription tiers (Core, Plus, and Pro)

The [candidate survey](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/202040375) feature allows your organization to configure a short survey that will be sent to candidates after they have exited your hiring process. Feedback captured in the candidate survey provides valuable insight into how candidates are experiencing your interview pipeline.

The candidate surveys by demographic report aggregates responses to candidate survey questions and organizes this data by responses to [U.S. standard demographic questions](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/7541739987355) or [custom demographic questions](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360004588971) on job posts.

#### In this article

  * Candidate survey by demographic report
  * Candidate survey by demographic report filters



### Candidate surveys by demographic report

To create a candidate surveys by demographic report, select **Reports** on your dashboard's navigation bar.

On the _Reports_ page, click **Essential** **Reports**.

Scroll to the _Measure the Impact of Inclusive Hiring Practices_ section. Select **Candidate Surveys By Demographic**.

The candidate surveys by demographic report will generate.

If necessary, click **Next** or adjust the **Page** to see additional rows in the report. You can also adjust the **number of rows** displayed per page.

**Note** : Due to the sensitive nature of the data, any emailed version of the candidate surveys by demographic report includes an expiring link to the spreadsheet.

### Candidate survey by demographic report filters

Click **Filters and more** to apply filters to further refine your report.

The candidate surveys by demographic report can be filtered by the following:

  * Department
  * Office
  * Use data from [U.S. standard demographic questions](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/7541739987355) or [custom demographic questions](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360004588971)
  * Submission date range



**Note** : By default, the Submitted Between date for the report is set to the current year.

Click **Apply** to run the report with your filter selections.

# LinkedIn Apply Connect integration

**Permissions:** Job Admin and above

**Product tier:** Available for new subscription tiers (Core, Plus, and Pro)

The Apply Connect integration provides a fast and seamless experience for Greenhouse customers posting jobs to LinkedIn. Jobs created in Greenhouse Recruiting are posted to LinkedIn in real-time, and with the LinkedIn Apply feature, job seekers can apply for your jobs without leaving LinkedIn.

With LinkedIn Recruiter seats, you can see candidate highlights in Greenhouse Recruiting with real-time views of LinkedIn profiles and how they match your job posts, enabling your teams to make more informed choices. You can also use candidate notification to improve the candidate experience.

**Notes about LinkedIn Apply Connect:**

  * On January 1, 2026 LinkedIn will require all Apply Connect posts to include a company email address.
  * All Greenhouse Recruiting users can access Apply Connect at no additional cost and can post free job posts to LinkedIn and receive applicants via LinkedIn Apply. However, additional features like applicant notifications, in-app LinkedIn profiles, and internal job posts require a LinkedIn Recruiter subscription.
  * Starting July 2025, free job postings through Apply Connect will have a limit on Apply applications via LinkedIn. Once this cap is reached, applicants will be redirected to the company’s career site to apply, while the job stays on LinkedIn. To keep unlimited Apply applications, you’ll need to promote your jobs using LinkedIn Job Slots. This update affects all ATS partners who offer Apply Connect.
  * All free job posts require at least one valid Searchable location to use LinkedIn Apply. If you don't add a Searchable location, you won't be able to select the Apply option. Learn more about [free job posts](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/sections/360009844991-Free-job-posts) on Greenhouse Recruiting.



#### In this article

  * LinkedIn's Automated Job Posting and Apply Connect
  * Set up LinkedIn Apply Connect
  * Update your LinkedIn Recruiter package to use Apply Connect
  * Add LinkedIn Apply Connect to your job board
  * Add your company email
  * Create free job posts
  * Posting status
  * Candidate profiles from LinkedIn job posts
  * View LinkedIn profiles in Greenhouse Recruiting
  * Send notifications to applicants
  * Frequently asked questions



### Feature overview

#### 

#### LinkedIn's Automated Job Posting and Apply Connect

LinkedIn requires that staffing customers use Automated Job Posting (job wrapping) with Apply Connect and recommends that non-staffing customers do too.

First, check if you've enabled Automated Job Posting in LinkedIn, then follow the instructions below. For additional support, review[ LinkedIn's Automated Job Setup Guide](https://content.linkedin.com/content/dam/me/business/en-us/talent-solutions/resources/pdfs/linkedIn-automated-jobs-set-up-apply-connect.pdf).

**If Automated Job Posting is not enabled:**

  * First, enable Apply Connect in Greenhouse by following the instructions in this guide.
  * Wait for 24 hours and then enable Automated Job Posting in LinkedIn Recruiter.
  * Do not enable Automated Job Posting before Apply Connect is enabled in your ATS.



**If Automated Job Posting is enabled:**

  * First, enable Apply Connect in Greenhouse by following the instructions in this guide.
  * Then, check that your ATS API source connection status is “Posting active.” 
  * If connected, close your manual jobs in LinkedIn Recruiter to prevent duplicates and ensure that all jobs collect applications via Apply Connect.



#### Set up LinkedIn Apply Connect

Existing LinkedIn Recruiter customers can add **LinkedIn Apply Connect** as part of their LinkedIn Recruiter package. Apply Connect enablement is done solely within Greenhouse Recruiting. Once Apply Connect is enabled, you do not need to take any additional steps within LinkedIn Recruiter.

As part of this setup, you'll need to integrate your job board with LinkedIn.

#### Update your LinkedIn Recruiter package to use Apply Connect

**Note** : Updating the LinkedIn integration is only required if your organization currently uses LinkedIn Recruiter. Customers who don't use LinkedIn Recruiter can still use Apply Connect, but just need to add it to their job board to finish setup.

To use advanced features available with Linkedin Recruiter, you need to enable the integration for your organization. In Greenhouse Recruiting, navigate to the Integrations page, locate LinkedIn, and sign into your LinkedIn Admin account.

When you choose a package, select the**Apply Package** box.

Once you click **Save changes** , LinkedIn Apply Connect will be available in your account. Any existing LinkedIn Recruiter submissions will automatically use the new Apply Connect integration. However, if you haven't integrated LinkedIn with your job board, follow the steps below to finish the setup.

#### Add LinkedIn Apply Connect to your job board

**Note** : Only [Site Admins](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360039614171-Permission-levels-overview) can enable this integration. 

Whether or not you use LinkedIn Recruiter, you'll need integrate LinkedIn Apply Connect with your job board and enter your company URL to finish setup.

To update your job board, navigate to a job board and click **Edit** **Board** **Settings**.

Scroll to _Turn on LinkedIn_ _Apply Connect,_ complete the fields, and click **Save**.

**Note:** You can retrieve your organization's public URL by searching for your company on LinkedIn and viewing your main company page.

After setup, LinkedIn Apply Connect will update the settings in Greenhouse Recruiting:

  * The job board's live job posts with valid Searchable locations will be sent to LinkedIn. Because LinkedIn requires job locations for free job posts, any job posts without at least one valid Searchable location will not be shared.
  * Candidate information will be synced with the new connection. While candidates are being synced, existing LinkedIn profiles may not be available.



If the candidate information doesn't sync within 24 hours, contact LinkedIn Support.

Add a company email address

**Note** : If you’re also enabling Automated Job Posting (Job Wrapping), confirm Apply Connect is active first and allow 24 hours before proceeding with Automated Job Posting setup.

#### Add your company email address

LinkedIn now requires organizations using Apply Connect to add a company email address. To add an email address, go to **Configure** > **Job boards and post.** Scroll to "Global Partner Settings."  
  
Add a company email address to the "API feed company email" field. Then click "Submit."

#### Create free job posts

With Apply Connect set up on a job board, you can share a new job for free on LinkedIn when [creating](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/200668380-Create-a-new-job) or [editing](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/115002791566-Edit-external-job-post) a job post.

You can enable the setting on a job post by navigating to **Job** > **Job Posts** > **Publish to Free Job** Boards. This setting has to be enabled on each job for Apply Connect to work. 

LinkedIn Apply requires job posts to have at least one valid Searchable location. 

**Note:** You can add up to seven searchable locations and select one work type per job post. If you add multiple searchable locations, LinkedIn may display them as separate job posts by location. If you don't add a valid Searchable location, you won't be able to select the Apply option. Learn more about [free job posts](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/sections/360009844991-Free-job-posts) on Greenhouse Recruiting.

#### Posting status

When you're using the Apply Connect integration, a job's **Posting Status** will be available on the _Job Posts_ page in the job dashboard.

Jobs can be **Posted** , **Pending** , **Inactive** , **Failed,** or **Not Listed** , based on whether the job is synced and displayed on LinkedIn. [A full list of errors is available on LinkedIn's help site.](https://www.linkedin.com/help/recruiter/answer/a6513542)

#### Candidate profiles from LinkedIn job posts

When a candidate applies using a LinkedIn job post, their profile will be created in Greenhouse Recruiting.

Any candidate sent over by LinkedIn Apply Connect will have the "LinkedIn" listed as a source, and replace any other sources that were assigned by other LinkedIn integrations, like Job Wrapping or Limited Listings.

**Note:** If your organization uses Automated Job Posting, Apply Connect must be enabled first to ensure proper job syncing and prevent duplicate posts.

#### View LinkedIn profiles in Greenhouse Recruiting

With Apply Connect enabled for your LinkedIn Recruiter contract, people with Recruiter seats can view applicants' LinkedIn profiles on their Greenhouse Recruiting candidate profiles under the **LinkedIn** tab on their candidate profile.

#### Send notifications to applicants

With Apply Connect enabled for your LinkedIn Recruiter contract, your organization can opt to send candidate notifications to applicants from LinkedIn:

  * Application submitted
  * Application viewed
  * Resume downloaded
  * Application rejected



[Learn more](https://www.linkedin.com/help/linkedin/answer/a514094/apply-connect-in-recruiter?lang=en) about candidate notifications on Apply Connect.

#### Frequently asked questions

#### Does LinkedIn Apply Connect cost money to use?

All Greenhouse Recruiting users have access to Apply Connect at no additional cost and can post free job posts to LinkedIn and receive applicants via LinkedIn Apply. However, additional features like applicant notifications, in-app LinkedIn profiles, and internal job posts require a [LinkedIn Recruiter subscription](https://business.linkedin.com/talent-solutions/linkedin-ats-integrations/greenhouse).

#### How long does it take for free job posts to appear on LinkedIn?

Unlike LinkedIn Limited Listings, which can require up to 48 hours for job posts to appear, Apply Connect offers free job posts that appear instantaneously to candidates on LinkedIn.

**Permissions:** Job Admin and above

**Product tier:** Available for new subscription tiers (Core, Plus, and Pro)

**Note** : This integration is not available for LinkedIn Recruiter Lite accounts.

LinkedIn Recruiter System Connect (RSC) is an integration that allows your organization to seamlessly source and manage candidate information across Greenhouse and LinkedIn Recruiter. With a Greenhouse Recruiting user [account connected to LinkedIn Recruiter](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/115005677303), a Greenhouse user can access the LinkedIn tab on a candidate's profile.

#### In this article

  * Export prospect from LinkedIn Recruiter
  * Export prospect with LinkedIn InMail
  * View candidate information in LinkedIn Recruiter
  * LinkedIn tab
    * View in Recruiter
    * Save to Project
    * Send InMail



### Export prospect from LinkedIn Recruiter to a job

From your LinkedIn Recruiter page, you can export a prospect to available jobs in your organization. To export a prospect to a job in your organization, click the **Ellipsis** icon  and select **Export to ATS**.

Use the _Export to your ATS_ panel on the right hand-side to select a job in your organization and click **Export**. The prospect will be assigned to the job within your Greenhouse user account.

**Note:** When you export a candidate from LinkedIn Recruiter to Greenhouse Recruiting, the candidate's source will show as LinkedIn (Prospecting), with 'Who gets credit' set as the person who exported the candidate.

**Note:** If the job location formatting in Greenhouse Recruiting does not match the location formatting for the LinkedIn job, LinkedIn will automatically set the location to United States of America on the LinkedIn posting. 1-click export can be deactivated through the LinkedIn Recruiter platform by a contract administrator. [Click here](https://www.linkedin.com/help/recruiter/answer/120456) to learn more.

### Export prospect via LinkedIn InMail

After an organization has enabled the LinkedIn RSC integration with contract-level access, a new prospect profile will be created in Greenhouse Recruiting when you take all of the following steps using LinkedIn InMail:

1\. LinkedIn user accepts a Recruiter InMail.  
2\. LinkedIn user responds to the InMail.  
3\. LinkedIn user elects to share their contact information.

**Note:** If a prospect is created via the InMail feature, the prospect will have a LinkedIn InMail candidate tag, and the candidate's source will show as LinkedIn (Prospecting), with 'Who gets credit' set as the person who imported the candidate.

### View candidate information from Greenhouse Recruiting in LinkedIn Recruiter

If you search for a candidate in LinkedIn Recruiter, you can easily ascertain information about the candidate. Once you have identified your candidate from your search results, click **ATS** to reveal information about that candidate, such as the job they are associated with and their email address.

Click **Interview & feedback** to view their stage within the interview process, the date they moved into their latest interview stage, and interview feedback collected in Greenhouse.

### Greenhouse LinkedIn Tab

To use the LinkedIn integration within Greenhouse Recruiting, navigate to a candidate's profile and click the **LinkedIn** tab.

The LinkedIn tab will only display candidate LinkedIn information if the candidate has an email attached to their Greenhouse profile.

If this candidate was added to your account through LinkedIn Recruiter's Export feature, you will need to manually add the prospect's email (for more information: [LinkedIn's Scraping Software Policy](https://www.linkedin.com/help/linkedin/answer/a1341387)).

Additionally, the initial sync of your Greenhouse account with LinkedIn Recruiter can take a few hours to fully sync depending on the number of your candidates.

**Note:** LinkedIn RSC is not compatible with the Safari internet browser. As a result, the LinkedIn tab on a candidate's profile will not work properly if you are logged into Greenhouse Recruiting in Safari. Please view [LinkedIn's support page](https://www.linkedin.com/help/recruiter/answer/a418519) to learn more.

Below are actions that can be performed from the LinkedIn tab on a candidate's profile:

#### **View in Recruiter**

Click **View in Recruiter** to view the candidate/prospect profile in LinkedIn Recruiter. The LinkedIn profile will populate on a subsequent page.

#### **Save to Project**

Click **Save to Project** to be directed to your LinkedIn Recruiter page, where you can save the candidate to a project you have established.

#### **Send InMail**

Click **Send InMail** to be redirected to your LinkedIn Recruiter account, where you can send an InMail directly to the candidate.

Greenhouse Recruiting's integration with Survale allows you to automatically gather candidate, recruiter, and hiring manager feedback after each stage in your recruiting process. From "always on" career site feedback to short pulse surveys following phone screens and interviews, Survale runs in the background in real time. Survale's analytics give you easy visual metrics that let you uncover issues with your candidate experience, but more importantly, with your entire recruiting process.

# Current pipeline per job

**Permissions:** Job Admin and above

**Product tier:** Available for new subscription tiers (Core, Plus, and Pro)

The current pipeline per job report shows candidates in each stage of a job's pipeline. This report can be used to assess the health of a job's pipeline, diagnose any potential bottlenecks, and compare jobs in a single department to find out whether candidates are making it much further through one pipeline than another.

#### In this article

  * Current pipeline per job report
  * Current pipeline per job report filters
  * Current pipeline per job report visualization 



### Current pipeline per job report

To create a current pipeline per job report, click **Reports** on your navigation bar.

Click **Essential** **Reports** on the left.

Scroll to the _Staying on top of your recruiting activity_ section and click **Current Pipeline Per Job**.

The current pipeline per job report will generate.

Each job on the report will show the following information:

  * Requisition ID
  * Department
  * Office
  * Total candidates currently in the stage
  * Total number of candidates to ever be in the stage
  * Total hires



**Note** : The current pipeline per job report will populate data for every job where you have the appropriate permissions.

**Note** : If a cell in the table shows 0, it means no candidates are currently in that stage. If a cell is blank, that particular stage does not currently exist on the job _._

### Current pipeline per job report filters

Click **Filters and more** to apply filters to further refine your report.

The current pipeline per job report can be filtered by the following:

  * Job
  * Job status
  * Department
  * Office
  * User
  * Hiring team role
  * Custom job field
  * Date applied



You can organize the columns on the current pipeline per job report by stage or [milestones](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/208319943-Milestones).

You can also control the report results using the _Stage Columns_ filter. This filter determines how your report displays current or historical data:

  * **Now:** Candidates currently in the stage.
  * **Ever:** Candidates who were previously in the stage and now are in a later stage.
  * **Both:** Includes both current and previous candidates in that stage.



Click **Apply** after applying any filters to your report.

**Note:** Since Greenhouse Recruiting is based on a candidate's linear progression through the hiring process, the current pipeline per job report will not correctly display candidates who went through the hiring process out of order.

  * If a candidate skipped a stage, they will still be included in the report results because they still technically passed through the stage. For example, if you move a candidate from Application Review directly to Offer, the report will show the candidate as being historically in all the stages between Application and Offer.
  * If a candidate is moved back to a previous stage, they will not be included in the results for any stages beyond the current one they are in. For example, if a candidate is moved from Face-to-Face back to Phone Screen, they will no longer be included in the calculation for candidates who were in the Face-to-Face stage.



### Current pipeline per job report visualization

The current pipeline per job report visualization will display the stages or milestones on a bar graph.

The names of the stages or milestones are represented on the _y-axis._ The number of candidates in each stage or milestone is represented on the _x_ -axis.

**Note** : The current pipeline per job report can only visualize your data when the report is filtered with the Now or Ever filter. A visualization will not appear if the report is filtered by Both.

Hover over any bar in the visualization for an exact number of candidates in that stage or milestone and to view the proportion those candidates represent in the pipeline.

Since the visualization displays data from your report, changes made to the report via **Filters and more** like adjusting the date filters will impact the visualization.

# Natural HR integration

Natural HR provides all-in-one HR and payroll software for mid-sized or enterprise organizations wanting to better engage, manage and pay their people.

Greenhouse Recruiting’s integration with Natural HR allows you to move candidates from Greenhouse into Natural HR automatically once you have marked them as ‘Hired’ in Greenhouse thereby removing the time and error potential of having to do this manually.

#### In this article

  * Retrieve Natural HR’s endpoint URL and secret key
  * Create a webhook
  * Create custom offer fields
    * Field 1: Salary
    * Field 2: Job Status
    * Field 3: Company
  * Use the Natural HR integration
  * Additional support



### Retrieve Natural HR’s endpoint URL and secret key

Before enabling the Greenhouse Recruiting/Natural HR integration, Greenhouse Recruiting will need two pieces of information:

  * Natural HR’s endpoint URL
  * Natural HR’s secret key



**Note:** While your secret key will always be unique, the endpoint URL will always be <https://www.naturalhr.net/hr/webhooks/greenhouse.php>.

You can find this information in Natural HR by navigating to **Admin** > **Company** > **Settings** > **Tokens** and clicking **Add**.

Enter a meaningful name for the integration (For example, "Greenhouse Recruiting"). Then, choose **Greenhouse** from the integration list.

Enter a _Secret key_. This is a kind of password that allows us to validate that the requests we receive have come from your Greenhouse Recruiting account. Click the icon to the right of the _Secret key_ field to randomly generate a secret key, or create your own.

**Tip:** If you decide to create your own secret key, we recommend using a random assortment of characters. This will make your key more secure. Be sure to write down your secret key so you don't forget it. You'll need it once you start working in Greenhouse Recruiting.

If you know the names of the Greenhouse Recruiting fields that contain salary, job status and company, you can enter these now.

When you're done, click **Submit**.

### Create a webhook

To integrate [COMPANY] with Greenhouse Recruiting, you'll need to create a webhook. Follow the steps in [this article](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/5888163727003) to create your webhook. Use the values listed below to configure the webhooks.

  * **Name** : A descriptive name for your integration. Most customers choose "Natural HR Integration."
  * **When** : Candidate has been hired
  * **Endpoint URL** : <https://www.naturalhr.net/hr/webhooks/greenhouse.php>
  * **Secret key** : This is the secret key you entered when setting up the integration in Natural HR.



### Create custom offer fields

You'll need to [create three custom offer fields](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360024551831) for the integration.

**Note:** If you already configured fields for this information, provide the Field Name to Natural HR during setup.

Use the following details to set up your custom offer fields. The **Field Name** in Greenhouse Recruiting must exactly match the field name in Natural HR.

#### Field 1: Salary

  * **Field Name:** Salary (including currency)
  * **Type:** Currency



#### Field 2: Job Status

  * **Field Name:** Salary
  * **Type:** Single select



#### Field 3: Company

  * **Field Name:** Salary
  * **Type:** Single select



**Note:** The field in Greenhouse Recruiting must exactly match the field names in Natural HR. For example, if Natural HR has a job status of "Full time" and you enter "Full-time," this will not synchronize properly.

### Use the Natural HR integration

When you[ mark a candidate as hired](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/200242039), Natural HR adds the employee based on the information in Greenhouse. This sync should take a few minutes. After each sync, the following fields are sent to Natural HR:

  * First name
  * Last name
  * Title
  * Home telephone number
  * Home mobile number
  * Home email address
  * Address (This will export as a single line due to how it's stored in Greenhouse Recruiting)
  * Job title
  * Department
  * Site
  * Start date
  * Salary (including currency)*
  * Job status*
  * Company*
  * All candidate documents (This includes the CV/resume, offer pack and any other documents uploaded during the recruitment process)



**Note:** Fields marked with an asterisk (*) need to be set up as custom offer fields in Greenhouse Recruiting to be able to synchronize.

Fields marked § must have the EXACT same values in both systems to synchronize. For example, if you have a department in Natural HR called "Sales," but it's called "Business Development" in Greenhouse Recruiting, the field will not synchronize.

If a candidate isn't appearing in Natural HR, you can verify that their information has been sent through the webhook by checking the [webhook log in the Dev Center](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/201794314).

You should then see something similar to the image below. If you do, that means the data has been sent to Natural HR and will be processed accordingly.

### Additional support

Contact [support@naturalhr.com](mailto:support@naturalhr.com) for troubleshooting assistance regarding the integration.

# ExponentHR integration

ExponentHR offers a single-source resource, simple, and robust platform that powers your team with HR, payroll, benefits, and compliance, amplifying the power of many by the power of one.

ExponentHR's integration with Greenhouse Recruiting allows draft employee records for new hires, rehires, and job changes to be created in ExponentHR with employee fields pre-populated with data gathered in Greenhouse ATS. ### Configure the ExponentHR integration

#### Client setup

#### Create a webhook

To integrate ExponentHR with Greenhouse Recruiting, you'll need to create a webhook. Follow the steps in [this article](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/5888163727003) to create your webhook. Use the values listed below to configure the webhook:

  * **Name:** A descriptive name for your integration. Most customers choose 'ExponentHR integration'
  * **When:** The ExponentHR integration offers two integration triggers for candidate workflow. A decision will need to be made on which trigger works best for your organization:
    * **Candidate has been Hired:** the integration will be triggered to send candidate data to ExponentHR when a candidate is marked as Hired in Greenhouse
    * **Offer Created:** the integration will be triggered to send candidate data to ExponentHR when an offer is extended to the candidate. If the candidate starts in ExponentHR (EAN Completion), the integration can mark them as Hired in Greenhouse at that time.
  * **Endpoint URL:** The Endpoint URL provided by ExponentHR
  * **Advanced Settings:** The Advanced settings option must be selected in order to add the ExponentHR credentials as 'Basic Authorization Credentials'
    * **Username:** the value provided by ExponentHR
    * **Password:** the value provided by ExponentHR



#### Authorize the ExponentHR integration

To configure the ExponentHR integration, you will need to authorize the integration in ExponentHR. In order to do so, you must be 1) a Greenhouse Site Admin and 2) an ExponentHR HRA or someone with Functional Access to the Company Configuration tool.

In ExponentHR, enter your Management tab, navigate to **Settings** on the left menu, then select **Company Configuration**.

In the Selection Menu on the left, select **Integrations**.

**Note:** The _Integrations_ tab is only available once an ExponentHR Integration Specialist has activated the required ExponentHR API configuration settings.

Click **Authorize**.

Review the permissions associated with the ExponentHR integration. After, enter your ATS admin credentials, and click **Log in to Greenhouse**.

It is recommended to check the box for **Authorize using a service account** to ensure that the connection remains even after you leave the company. Then select **Authorize**.

Once authorized, you will see the confirmation notice. Selecting **Close** will redirect you back to the Company Configuration tool in ExponentHR.

#### Create a custom field

In order to use the ExponentHR integration, you may need to create custom fields in Greenhouse Recruiting. An ExponentHR Integration Solution Specialist will host a field mapping call with you in which it can be decided which fields will be in scope for the integration using a client-specific field mapping document. The custom fields needed will be determined through this field mapping conversation.

To create a custom field, click the **Configure** icon  on your navigation bar, then click **Custom Options** on the left.

The Type will be determined by the field mapping discussion with an Integration Solution Specialist from ExponentHR. The integration supports the following Types: Candidates, Jobs, and Offers.

After a Type is selected, click **Add field** , and enter the following details to configure the new field:

  * **Name:** Generally speaking, the Name would match the name of the respective ExponentHR field
  * **Type:** will be determined by the respective ExponentHR field; your assigned Integration Specialist will advise on which Type to choose



#### ExponentHR setup

#### Field mapping

In order to determine what Greenhouse candidate data and ExponentHR employee data is in scope for your integration, and how they should be mapped to each other, it is necessary to join a field mapping call with an ExponentHR Integration Solution Specialist.

The ExponentHR Integration Solution Specialist will create a client-specific field mapping document that will be used to define the field scope and system mappings. Once reviewed, the respective fields and associated mappings will be configured on the ExponentHR side by the Integration Solution Specialist.

The standard fields that customers choose to transfer to ExponentHR are below:

  * Start Date
  * Activate Onboarding for New Hire
  * Onboarding Coordinator
  * Onboarding Template
  * First Name
  * Middle Initial
  * Last Name
  * Nick Name
  * Home Telephone #
  * Mobile Telephone #
  * Personal Email Address
  * Home Address fields
  * Job Title
  * Supervisor
  * Employment Type
  * Work Location
  * Department
  * Recruiting Source
  * Name of Recruiter



#### ID sync

In the field mapping conversation, it may be decided to use Greenhouse data such as the Hiring Manager or a custom field to populate the Supervisor value for a candidate in ExponentHR. In order to do this, it will be necessary to sync Greenhouse records to ExponentHR records.

You will need to provide the ExponentHR Integration Solution Specialist a list of Users or Candidates in Greenhouse, along with the respective ID (Candidate ID or User ID). To retrieve a list of User IDs, click the **Configure** icon  on your navigation bar and then click **Users** on the left.

Click **Export to Excel**.

A spreadsheet will be downloaded to your computer that includes the User ID for all Users. Please provide this spreadsheet to your ExponentHR Integration Specialist.

To retrieve a list of Candidate IDs, please utilize the Greenhouse reporting option to provide a report of candidate profiles.

The ExponentHR Integration Solution Specialist will work with you to match the Greenhouse IDs to ExponentHR records. Once live, the integration will automatically sync the two systems when the Candidate Workflow portion of the integration is used for the new employee.

#### Code sync

To use classification code data in ExponentHR to manage Jobs, Offices, and Departments in Greenhouse, your ExponentHR Integration Specialist will need to sync the current Greenhouse values with what is in ExponentHR.

In order to assist your ExponentHR Integration Specialist, you will need to provide a list of current Jobs, Offices, and Locations from Greenhouse.

Your Integration Specialist will work with you to match these to ExponentHR values. After, they will map the values between the two systems for the integration. Once live, the integration can automatically create new values in Greenhouse and map them for the integration when they are added in ExponentHR.

These processes will allow the Job, Office, and Location for candidates to be pre-populated in the employee records created in ExponentHR by the integration.

#### Testing

As part of your integration project, an ExponentHR Integration Solution Specialist will copy your live ExponentHR environment to a testing site where the initial configuration and testing can occur.

If a Greenhouse testing site is available, we can configure the ExponentHR testing site to the Greenhouse test environment. Otherwise, we can use our Greenhouse testing environment for initial testing and then work with you to apply the setup to your Production environment.

The ExponentHR Integration Specialist can also provide you access to the ExponentHR test environment so that you can perform your own testing to familiarize yourself with the integration. Once ready to go live, the Integration Specialist can move the integration configuration and setup to your live ExponentHR environment.

### Use the ExponentHR integration with Greenhouse Recruiting

#### Candidate workflow

The ExponentHR integration offers two integration triggers for candidate workflow:

  * **Candidate has been Hired:** the integration will be triggered to send candidate data to ExponentHR when a candidate is marked as Hired in Greenhouse
  * **Offer Created:** the integration will be triggered to send candidate data to ExponentHR when an offer is extended to the candidate. If the candidate starts in ExponentHR (EAN Completion), the integration can mark them as Hired in Greenhouse at that time.



#### Candidate hired

When the Candidate Hired workflow is being used, the integration will be triggered to send candidate data to ExponentHR when a candidate is marked as Hired in Greenhouse.

The candidate is marked as Hired once the offer has been accepted. When clicking on the **Mark Candidate as Hired** button, you will be prompted to populate the Offer Details:

Once you click **Save** , the integration will create a draft employee record (EAN) in ExponentHR:

Employee fields within the EAN will be pre-populated with data captured in Greenhouse via the candidate, job, and offer:

Within ExponentHR, the HR managers can review and enrich the data before submitting or approving the New Hire EAN.

#### Offer created

When the Offer Created workflow is being used, the integration will be triggered to send candidate data to ExponentHR when an offer is extended to the candidate.

When clicking on the **Create Offer** button, you will be prompted to populate the Offer Details:

Once you click **Save** , the integration will create a draft employee record (EAN) in ExponentHR:

Employee fields within the EAN will be pre-populated with data captured in Greenhouse via the candidate, job, and offer:

Within ExponentHR, the HR managers can review and enrich the data before submitting or approving the New Hire EAN.

Once the EAN has been completed, typically upon the new hire's hire date, the ExponentHR integration will mark the candidate as Hired in Greenhouse.

#### Job, dept, and office management

#### Creation

When a new Job Code, Location, or Department is added in ExponentHR, the integration can automatically add the respective Job, Location, or Department in Greenhouse.

Once the new code is added in ExponentHR, the integration will trigger the creation of a new value in Greenhouse:

The ExponentHR Description value can be used to populate the Job name, Department name, and Office name, respectively:

The integration will also store the connection between the two systems so that the candidate values coming back to ExponentHR are able to be successfully mapped into the ExponentHR employee record.

#### Updates

When an update occurs to an existing Job Code, Location, or Department in ExponentHR, the integration can trigger to update Greenhouse so the two systems can stay in sync.

If the ExponentHR Description value is changed, the integration can automatically update the respective Job name, Department name, and Location name in Greenhouse:

### Additional resources

For additional information or troubleshooting not covered here, reach out to [integrationreview@exponenthr.com](mailto:integrationreview@exponenthr.com) or [support@exponenthr.com](mailto:support@exponenthr.com). These resources can be used whether you are setting up the integration for the first time or would like to make any changes to the existing integration.

# Talent Filtering

**Permissions:** Site admin, Job admin

**Product tier:** Available for new subscription tiers (Core, Plus, and Pro)

Talent filtering streamlines app review by allowing you to easily search for keywords in applications, then filter the results to find the most qualified candidates.

#### In this article

  * Adding a talent filtering step to app review
  * Finding talent filtering
  * Searching for keywords
  * Filtering candidates
  * Reviewing filtered candidates



### Adding a talent filtering step to app review

You can add talent filtering as a default step to your organization's app review process.

To add a talent filtering step, go to the **Configure** icon in the upper right-hand corner, select **Permissions** on the left side panel, then, scroll to **Jobs**.

Click the checkbox next to "Display the talent filtering step during application review." Select the **Edit **icon to set the candidate threshold after which talent filtering will automatically display.

### Finding talent filtering

You can filter candidates' applications during the [application review stage](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/4401963991707). First, go to the job dashboard for the role you're interested in, then select **Review Applications**.

If you've added the talent filtering step and the application volume exceeds your threshold, you'll go directly to talent filtering.

Otherwise, select **Filter talent** within app review.

### Searching for keywords

Begin by searching for job titles, skills, locations, and other keywords in the full text of resumes and internal notes. Add as many keywords as you’d like.

To appear in your results, the keyword from your search must exactly match the keyword in the application. Keywords can be:

  * **Preferred** : Only one term must appear in a candidate’s application to be included in the search results (**OR** statements)
  * **Required** : All terms must appear in a candidate’s application to be included in the search results (**AND** statements)



To accelerate your workflow, include Greenhouse’s suggested keywords generated from your public job post.

### Filtering candidates

Once you’ve selected your keywords, use filters to prioritize your candidates by location, referrals, scorecard status, education, or custom criteria.

### Reviewing filtered candidates

After adding keywords and filters, see how many candidates have the qualifications you're looking for. Then, save time by reviewing the applications that meet your needs.

# Greenhouse Recruiting with Workday® position management

A Workday® position staffing model can be integrated with Greenhouse Recruiting using HRIS Link. This guide can help you decide which configuration works best for your organization.

#### In this article

  * Overview
    * What's a Greenhouse Recruiting job?
    * Can I import positions or job requisitions?
      * (Recommended) Import job requisitions
      * Import job positions



### Overview

#### What's a Greenhouse Recruiting job?

When integrating Greenhouse Recruiting with Workday® position management, it's important to clarify exactly what a job is! On Greenhouse Recruiting, a job encompasses more than just the job details that sync from Workday®. Each job can have multiple openings and represents an entire candidate pipeline with an interview plan, scorecards, hiring team, approvals, and more.

When someone is ready to hire a candidate for a job, the candidate will be hired onto a job _opening_. In this way, a Greenhouse Recruiting job may have one or more open openings. Check out **Job** >**Job Setup** > **Job Info** > and scroll to _Openings_ to view the openings on a job.

With this differentiation in mind, you can determine how to configure the integration for your organization. You can choose to import positions or to import requisitions and positions.

**Tip** : Learn more about openings: [Requisitions and openings](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360037953951).

#### Can I import positions or job requisitions into Greenhouse Recruiting?

Your team can choose to import positions only, or import job requisitions and positions from Workday®. In either case, they'll be imported as jobs in Greenhouse Recruiting, each with its job details. All data will be represented at the job-info level, whether the data comes from the position or requisition. The decision to import positions or job requisitions will primarily impact the way job openings will be represented in Greenhouse Recruiting.

### Import job requisitions

We recommend importing job requisitions to Greenhouse Recruiting. If you have job requisitions enabled in Workday®, this allows you to represent a many-to-one relationship on your Greenhouse Recruiting jobs. If you frequently have multiple positions associated with one job requisition, you can import your job requisitions and positions as one Greenhouse Recruiting job with multiple openings. This allows your team to see how many positions are associated with a job requisition in your HRIS through the import.

With this configuration, HRIS field values are typically mapped as follows:

**Workday® field** |  **Greenhouse Recruiting field**  
---|---  
Requisition ID |  Requisition ID  
Number of openings total |  Number of openings  
Position ID |  Opening ID  
  
**Learn more** : [Set up HRIS Link job import with job requisitions enabled](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/4403889907355).

### Import positions only

If you don't have job requisitions enabled and only import positions from Workday® to Greenhouse Recruiting, every new position will sync to Greenhouse Recruiting as a new job with a single opening. With this setup, it isn't possible to map multiple positions to a single Greenhouse Recruiting job because Workday® won't provide sufficient information to determine which positions should be tied together as multiple openings on one job.

**Learn more** : [Set up HRIS Link job import without job requisitions enabled](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/4403988430235).

**Note** : Greenhouse Recruiting is not sponsored by, endorsed by, or affiliated with Workday®️.

**Learn more**

[HRIS Link overview](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360055282972)

[Set up HRIS Link job import with job requisitions](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/4403889907355)

[Set up HRIS Link job import without job requisitions](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/4403988430235)

# Add a custom application question to a job post

**Permissions:** Site Admin, and Job Admin who can create, edit, and delete job posts

**Product tier:** Available for new subscription tiers (Core, Plus, and Pro)

Custom application questions allow your organization to collect information from candidates when they apply for a job.

#### In this article

  * Add custom application questions to future job posts
  * Add custom application questions to a single job post
  * Add custom application questions to job posts in bulk
  * Add custom application questions with a linked candidate field to job posts in bulk
  * View a candidate's response to a custom application question



### Add custom application questions to future job posts

Custom application questions can be added to future jobs by creating a [template job](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360038222812). Once the template job is created, it is saved as a draft that can be copied to future job posts.

**Note** : When adding a custom question to your template job, make sure to [link responses to a candidate field](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360024688071) if you intend to report on custom application questions across many jobs. This action allows you to report on the linked candidate fields across all associated jobs using the [essential candidate reports](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360042740232).

### Add custom application questions to a single job post

To add custom application questions to a job post, click**Jobs** from your navigation bar and select a **job** from the list.

From the _Job Dashboard_ page, click **Job Setup** and navigate to **Job Posts** on the left.

Navigate to the job post from the list and click the **Edit** icon .

From the _Edit Your Job Post_ page, scroll to the _Custom Application Questions_ section and click **Add Custom Question**.

From the _Add Custom Question_ box, input the following:

  * Question
  * Description (optional)
  * Answer type (including the option to [link responses to a candidate field](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360024688071))
  * Privacy setting
  * Required or not



**Note** : Responses to custom application questions can only be reported on one job at a time (read more [here](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360001114992)). If you intend to report on custom application questions across many jobs, be sure to **link responses to a candidate field**. This action allows you to report on the linked candidate fields across all associated jobs using the [essential candidate reports](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360042740232).  
  
Additionally, if you select **Attachment** as the _Answer Type_ , candidate attachments cannot exceed a file size of 500 MB.

When finished, click **Add**. Repeat this process for every question you'd like to add.

Scroll to the bottom of the page and click **Save** to confirm the addition of the custom application question(s).

Your custom question(s) is now added to the job application.

### Add custom application questions to job posts in bulk

To begin, click**Jobs** from your navigation bar.

Use the **filter panel** to narrow down your list of jobs as needed.

**Individually select** or use the **select-all** checkbox to include your list of jobs in the bulk action.

Once selected, click **External Jobs Posts** or **Internal Job Posts**.

Navigate to the **Custom Questions** tab and click **Add New Question**.

From the _Add Custom Question_ box, input the following:

  * Question
  * Description (optional)
  * Answer type
  * Privacy setting



**Note** : It isn't possible to link responses to a candidate field during the bulk workflow. Follow the steps in this section to add an existing custom question with a linked candidate field to job posts in bulk.  
  
Additionally, if you select **Attachment** as the _Answer Type_ , candidate attachments cannot exceed a file size of 500 MB.

When finished, click **Add**.

If you'd like to make the question required, click the **ellipsis** icon next to the newly created job and select **required** from the dropdown.

Repeat this process for every question you'd like to add.

Click **Save and Exit** at the bottom of the page when finished.

### Add custom application questions with a linked candidate field to job posts in bulk

**Notes:**

  * Bulk actions can only be completed by Site Admins with the user-specific permission to bulk edit jobs
  * Your custom question must already exist with a linked candidate field in order to complete this workflow. Follow the steps in this section to add a new question to a job post.



Linking a custom question to a candidate field is not available when creating a new question during the bulk workflow. This section provides a workaround to ensure your existing question is added to job posts in bulk.

To begin, open the _All Jobs_ page and narrow down the jobs using the filters panel. 

Select the checkbox next to each job you want included in the bulk action. All jobs on the page can be selected using the checkbox in the column header.

Once selected, click **External Jobs Posts** or **Internal Job Posts**.

Navigate to the **Custom Questions** tab.

Click the **ellipsis** icon next to the linked question and select **Required** or **Optional** from the dropdown.

Repeat this process for each question.

Click **Save and Exit** when done.

### View a candidate's response to a custom application question

A candidate's answers to custom application questions are located in the **Application** section of the candidate's profile.

# Delete company metadata

**Permissions:** Site Admin, or Job Admin with the user-specific permission 'Can manage company metadata'

**Product tier:** Available for new subscription tiers (Core, Plus, and Pro)

Company metadata allows you to capture and report on data custom to your organization in a standardized format. Greenhouse Recruiting includes company metadata for [candidate tags](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360045893411), [close reasons for job openings](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/213351483), [interviewer tags](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/205982075), [referrers](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360049637292), [rejection reasons](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360025225032), and [sources](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/200721664).

It may be necessary to delete company metadata as your organization grows or changes. This article covers how to replace or delete existing company metadata in Greenhouse Recruiting.

**Note** : Interviewer tags are only available to Plus and Pro subscription tiers.

#### In this article

  * Manage company metadata
  * Replace or delete company metadata



### Manage company metadata

To update your organization's company metadata, select **Configure** , then click **Custom** **Options**.

Scroll to the _Company_ _Metadata_ section.

Click any entity listed under  _Company Metadata_ to view all existing metadata for that entity. For example, click **Candidate Tags** to manage all existing candidate tags used by your organization.

### Replace or delete company metadata

Click **Remove** to delete any metadata entry.

When deleting company metadata, you'll have the option to replace the deleted metadata with existing metadata or delete the metadata permanently with no replacement.

#### Replace company metadata

Select **I want any entity using this**`[company metadata]`**to use this** **instead** to delete and replace this metadata with other existing metadata. Use the dropdown menu to select a replacement for your deleted metadata, then click **Delete**.

**Example** : In the example above, any existing entities using the [candidate tag](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360045893411) **C++** will instead use the candidate tag **SQL**. Any reports or existing candidates referencing the candidate tag **C++** will be updated to **SQL** after deleting the C++ candidate tag.

#### Delete company metadata

You can also select **I want to permanently delete this**`[company metadata]`**without re-assigning** to permanently delete any company metadata. Click **Delete** to confirm you'd like to remove this metadata.

When company metadata is permanently deleted without re-assigning, the metadata is completely removed from all candidates, reports, jobs, or other associated entities in the hiring software.

**Example** : In the example above, the candidate tag **C++** will be completely removed from all reports, candidates, and associated entities and won't be replaced.

# Allow other users to send emails on my behalf

**Permissions:** Job Admin or above

**Product tier:** Available for new subscription tiers (Core, Plus, and Pro)

By default, Greenhouse Recruiting allows you to send emails from your own address and any [org-wide email addresses](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/205759545) that have been set up on the **Configure > Dev Center > Email Settings** page. Additionally, users can also configure permissions to allow other users to send emails on their behalf.

In this article

Grant access

Revoke Access

### Grant access

Navigate to the upper right-hand corner to **Hi, Name** and click **Account Settings** from the dropdown menu.

Navigate to the _Email Permissions_ panel and determine whether anyone in the organization can send emails on your behalf or if this permission will be limited to certain users. 

If you want to allow only select users to send emails on your behalf, click the appropriate checkbox and use the provided search field to select Greenhouse users in your organization.

When emailing a candidate or setting up a new job template, users configured to send emails on your behalf can select your email address from the _From_ field.

### Revoke Access

If you revoke access from the user, the _From_ field will then default to send from the user's own email address instead.

Before you can revoke org-wide access, will need to make sure no org-wide templates use your email address. If they do, a user with Site Admin permissions will need to remove it before you have the option to revoke access. If you try to revoke access before doing this, you will receive a notification about which templates currently use your information.
