# Number of hires report

**Permissions:** Job Admin and above

**Product tier:** Available for new subscription tiers (Core, Plus, and Pro)

The number of hires made in a given period can be a strong indicator of how your recruiting teams are performing. You may discern patterns in an acquisition like bottlenecks or pain points to investigate further.

With the number of hires report, your organization can gain quick insight into how many new employees were hired per job, department, or recruiter over a given period of time.

#### In this article

  * Number of hires report
  * Number of hires report filters
  * Number of hires report visualization



### Number of hires report

To create a number of hires report, click **Reports** on your navigation bar.

Click **Essential** **Reports** on the left.

Scroll to the _Share Progress with Executives_ section, and click **Number of Hires**.

The number of hires report will generate.

The number of hires report will show information for the following:

  * Job
  * Requisition ID
  * Total hires 



**Note** : By default, the number of hires report will show every open job where you have the appropriate permissions.

### Number of hires report filters

Click **Filters and more** to apply filters to further refine your report.

The number of hires report can be filtered by the following:

  * Job
  * Job status
  * Department
  * Office
  * User
  * Hiring team role
  * Custom job field
  * Date hired



You can organize rows by job, recruiter, source, or department.

You can organize columns by week, month, quarter, or year.

**Note** : The number of hires report can display a maximum of 12 columns per report, regardless of the periodization or date ranges selected. If necessary, run multiple reports to capture the data you need. If there are not yet 12 weeks in the current year, the report will default to the last 12 weeks of the previous year.

Click **Apply** after applying any filters to your report.

### Number of hires report visualization

The number of hires report will visualize the total employee hires for the filters and periods set.

The visualization presents _Total hires_ row values as a single line with the number of hires displayed on the y-axis and the periodization (columns) on the x-axis.

**Note:** The number of hires report does not support individual trend lines per row.

Hover over any data point in the visualization for an exact number of hires made for that period.

Since the visualization displays data for the _Total_ row in your report, changes made to your report via **Filters and more** , like adjusting date filters or jobs selected, will impact the visualization.

# Job Admin levels and permissions

**Permissions:** Site Admin who can edit another user's advanced permissions

**Product tier:** Available for Plus and Pro subscription tiers

**Note:** Organizations with an Core subscription can assign users as [Job Admin: Standard or Job Admin: Private](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360040467451) but can't edit or customize them. Organizations with an Advanced or Pro subscription can customize the permissions assigned to Job Admin: Standard and Job Admin: Private, as well as [create custom Job Admin levels](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/207813806).

#### In this article

  * Job Admin levels overview
  * Creating job admin permission levels
  * Default Job Admin permissions
  * Additional Job Admin permissions
  * Additional resources



### Job Admin levels overview

Every time you assign a Job Admin user to a job, you must also choose which Job Admin level the user should have on that particular job.

Job Admin levels are defined sets of permissions that are granted to Job Admin users on for individual jobs.

By default, Greenhouse Recruiting includes the Job Admin: Standard and Job Admin: Private levels. Your team can edit these Job Admin levels and create custom Job Admin levels to fine-tune permissions for your organization. In a robust hiring process, you'll have multiple Job Admin permission levels to grant users the right level of access based on their role.

**Example** : A hiring manager and a recruiter are both assigned to a job as Job Admins, but they might need different levels of access on that job. For example, the recruiter might need to be able to edit the external job post.

In this case, your team might have two Job Admin levels:

  * Job Admin: Hiring Manager
  * Job Admin: Recruiter



Each of these levels have different permissions so that can be assigned to each user. This setup ensures that both users have the appropriate level of access required for their role and the specific job.

### Creating job admin permission levels

Job Admin levels can be created and modified by Site Admins who have permission to edit another user's advanced permission. The levels are created for your entire organization under the Configure page. Once created, these levels are assigned to individual jobs and users.

Permissions are assigned for individual jobs and users to give flexibility when a user needs to fulfill multiple roles across jobs.

For example, assume you had two roles, and a single user who needs to be a hiring manager on one, but on the second, needs additional permission to approve offers.

You could only have one permission level that gives the user access to approve offers on all jobs, but giving unnecessary access to job actions just leads to unnecessary risk and complication as the user could have access to actions in a job that they shouldn't. 

Instead, by creating two Job Admin levels, that user a single user could be assigned Job Admin: Approver on one job, and Job Admin: Hiring Manager on another. You could then reuse these permission levels to assign users the correct level of access on jobs. 

Since permission levels apply to the entire organization, changing the Job Admin Permission level under the Configure page will affect all users who have been assigned that permission across jobs

### Default Job Admin permissions

By default, a user who is assigned to a job as a Job Admin will have the following visibility and access available on that job, regardless of their Job Admin level on the job:

  * Can see the job's dashboard, pipeline, and reports
  * Can be assigned hiring team roles



These built-in permissions cannot be edited or removed.

A user configured with a Job Admin user permission level will have the permissions noted above only on jobs to which they explicitly are assigned. A user with a Job Admin user permission level will not have any access to or permissions on jobs to which they are not assigned.

### Additional Job Admin permissions

**Permission** | **Description**  
---|---  
Can view and edit candidates and prospects |  Allows users to see and update candidate and prospect details on a job. A Job Admin without this permission can still view the job page and basic job information, but will only see aggregated data in reports and will not have any access to candidate details. If the Job Admin without this permission is also a hiring manager, they will still be able to see candidate details in the context of the Hiring Manager Review stage.   
Can view identity verification details | Allows the user to view[ identity verification](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/40893011137179) results and related details for candidates, including verification status and related details returned by CLEAR. This permission does not allow the user to initiate or manage verification requests.  
Can request identity verification details | Allows the user to initiate identity verification requests for candidates.  
Can view fraud reports | Allows the user to view fraud reports and signals found by [Fraud Detection](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/42738009117467), including indicators that help assess potential fraud or misrepresentation. This permission is read-only and does not allow the user to run reports.  
Can run fraud reports | Allows the user to generate and run new fraud reports.  
Can edit job info |  Allows the user to edit information on the **Job Info** tab. **Note:** Any job information tied to approvals must be edited from the job's **Approvals** tab instead.  
Can delete jobs |  Allows the user to delete a closed job from the job's dashboard. This permission stripe can be granted to a Job Admin level only if that Job Admin level also includes the permission stripe for 'Can edit job info.' **Note:** Deleted jobs cannot be recovered. We recommend granting this permission to select users only.  
Can create, edit, and delete job posts | Allows the user to create new job posts, and edit or delete existing job posts. A Job Admin without this permission can still view the Job Post page, but the only action available to the user on this page is to generate tracking links.  
Can change job posts status | Allows the user to toggle job post status between **Off** and **Live** , impacting the visibility of a job post on your job board.  
Can edit forms | Allows the user to create and make changes to forms.  
Can configure scorecard attributes | Allows the user to see the job's scorecard page under the job > **Job Setup** tab > **Scorecard**. Users who can see this page can add and remove sections and attributes from the job's scorecard.  
Can view candidate scorecards submitted by other users | Controls visibility to scorecards submitted by other users; can be set to **Never** , **Always** , or **After submitting their own**.  
Can edit interview plans | Allows the user to view the job's interview plan page. Users who can view this page can add, remove, and reorganize stages on the job; adjust milestones; and edit interview kits. The user-specific permission '[Can create new job stage names (Job Admin only)](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/205614645-Job-Admin-Interviewer-User-Specific-Permissions#h_b8afbfd2-83a8-48e9-ad0e-a9a581ad325a)' further defines the access a Job Admin user has to edit interview plans.  
Can edit hiring teams | Allows the user to assign and unassign other users to/from Hiring Team roles, as long as those users have permissions on the job. Also allows the user to set a recruiter or coordinator as responsible for new candidates on the job. A Job Admin without this permission can view the hiring team page but will be unable to edit the roles.  
Can add and remove agencies from jobs | Allows the user to grant agency recruiters access to jobs, as well as remove agency recruiters from jobs.  
Can view and edit private candidate and application fields | Allows the user to view candidate fields and application fields marked as private. These fields appear on the candidate's profile under the **Private** tab. This permission also allows the user to request candidate background checks through third-party integrations that initiate the background check from the **Private** tab.  
Can create, edit, and view job notes | Allows the user to create, edit, and view [job notes](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/38050301918363).  
Can create, edit, and view private job notes | Allows the user to create, edit, and view private [job notes](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/38050301918363). These notes are only visible to users with the same permission.  
Can view and create private notes on the candidate profile | Allows the user to create private notes on a candidate profile or a candidate scorecard, and to view private notes created by other users.  
Can view and edit e-Signature agreements, and can send agreements to candidates | Allows the user to see available [e-Signature agreement](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/27637882883995) templates, send agreements to candidates during the hiring process (excluding the [offer stage](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/200721744)), and view agreements associated with candidates.  
Can view and edit private job fields and approve/request approval on jobs | Allows the user to view custom job fields marked as private; these fields appear on a job > **Job Info**. Also allows the user to request [approval to start recruiting and / or official job approval](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360025756071), and to be configured as a job approver.  
Can edit job approvals | Allows the user to edit the job's approval chain. [Click here](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360039866511) to learn more. This permission stripe can be granted to a Job Admin level only if that Job Admin level also includes the permission stripe for 'Can view and edit private job fields and approve / request approval on jobs.'  
Can view and edit offers and approve/request approval on offers | Allows the user to create and edit candidate offers, and to [request offer approval](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/201165300). Also allows the user to be configured as an offer approver.  
Can edit offer approvals | Allows the user to edit the offer approvals chain for the job as well as for individual candidates on the job. [Click here](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360039866551) to learn more.  
This permission stripe can be granted to a Job Admin level only if that Job Admin level also includes the permission stripe for 'Can view and edit offers and approve/request approval on offers.'  
Can advance candidates / prospects |  Allows the user to move candidates to a new stage in an interview plan, or to move prospects to a new stage in a pool. Without this permission, the user will not be able to advance candidates at any point, including in the Application Review stage. To learn more, [click here](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360039463552).  
Can reject candidates / prospects |  Allows the user to mark a candidate as rejected or choose **Stop Considering as Prospect** on a prospect. Without this permission, the user will not be able to reject candidates at any point, including in the Application Review stage. To learn more, click [here](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360039463972).  
Can email candidates / prospects | Allows the user to email candidates and prospects from Greenhouse Recruiting. Without this permission, the user will not see the option to email a candidate or prospect available on their profile. To learn more, [click here](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360039464292).  
Can create and view private candidates / prospects | Allows the user to mark existing candidates as private, as well as view private candidates. To learn more, click [here](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360039867171).  
Can merge candidates and prospects |  Allows the user to manually merge duplicate profiles for both candidates and prospects. **Note:** The user must have the exact same Job Admin level on both profiles in order to merge them. If a Job Admin attempts a merge where they do not have the same permission on both profiles, an error message will appear warning they lack the permissions for the action. To learn more, [click here](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360039867211).  
Can add and remove users to their assigned jobs | Allows the user to assign other Job Admin users to the job. A user with this permission cannot assign another user to a Job Admin level which includes permission stripes the assigning user's own Job Admin level does not include.  
Can create, edit, and delete Stage Transition rules |  Allows the user to create and manage [stage transition rules](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360053129752). **Note:** This permission stripe is enabled by default for all newly created Job Admin levels. This permission stripe is available only for organizations with an Plus or Pro subscription tier.  
Can create, edit, and delete Company Goals | Allows the user to create, edit, and delete [company goals](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/8382420999835).   
Can create, edit, and delete organization report templates | Allows the user to create, edit, and delete organization [report templates](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/5676138233115).  
Can view Talent Matching AI match score | Allows the user to view AI-generated match scores for candidates on a job. Match scores indicate how well a candidate's profile aligns with the job's requirements based on Talent Matching.  
Can create Talent Matching calibration | Allows the user to create a Talent Matching calibration for a job. Calibrations help refine AI match scoring by providing examples of strong and weak candidate fits for that job.  
Can edit and delete Talent Matching calibration | Allows the user to edit or delete existing Talent Matching calibrations on a job.  
Can view AI opt-out status | Allows the user to view whether a candidate has opted out of AI-assisted evaluation on a job.  
Can see demographics reports | Gives the user access to the [pipeline by demographic ](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360007254531)and [sourcing by demographic](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360017457032) reports and allows them to see report results for jobs where they are a Job Admin. Available for Expert tier only.   
  
### Additional resources

To learn more about Job Admin levels, check out the following articles:

  * [Default Job Admin levels](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360040467451)
  * [Create custom Job Admin level](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/207813806)
  * [Edit or delete Job Admin level](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360039863731)
  * [CRM permissions](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/4411120566299)

# Assign custom access to manage employee tasks

**Permissions:** Owners

**Product tier:** Available for Greenhouse Onboarding and Greenhouse Welcome subscription tiers

Greenhouse Onboarding allows [Owners](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360019575491) to manage who in your organization can manage and report on tasks for current employees.

You can create custom access roles with the **Can manage and report on assigned tasks** permission stripe. This permission allows specific users the ability to view and edit employees' tasks in the [task report](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/13260067443995).

You can assign permissions to manage assigned tasks based on an employee's department, location, employment status, or other criteria.

#### In this article

  * Add task permissions to a new or existing custom role
  * Assign users to a custom task role
    * Define rules to see and edit specific employee tasks
  * Additional resources



### Add task permissions to a new or existing custom role

To get started, you'll need to configure a new or existing custom role with permission to manage employees' tasks.

From the Greenhouse Onboarding homepage, navigate to **Settings** > **Data Flow** > **Permissions**.

In the  _Custom Access_ panel, click an existing custom access role to edit its permissions.

You can also click **Create New** to [create a new custom role](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360019516351). Give your new role a **Name** , then click **Save and Close** to begin editing this role's permissions.

Navigate to the **Settings** tab in your custom access role.

Under  _Permissions_ , mark the checkbox **Can manage and report on assigned tasks**. 

Your changes are saved automatically.

Any user who's assigned this custom role will now have access to manage all employee tasks in the [task report](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/13260067443995). In the next step, you can limit access to manage specific employees' tasks based on the rules that you define for each user assigned to this role.

### Assign users to a custom task role

Next, assign permission to view and edit tasks to specific users in your organization. You can also add rules to define which employees' tasks can be edited by users with this role.

Navigate to the **Users** tab for your custom role, then click **Add User**.

Under the **Add user(s)** field, use the dropdown menu to select each user in your organization that you'd like to assign to this custom role.

**Note:** You can add multiple users simultaneously during this step. Be aware that adding multiple users at once will give them all the same match rules, which are defined below. If you need custom users to have different rules for task access, add them one at a time or in batches.

#### Define rules to see and edit specific employee tasks

Use any of the following fields to define which tasks this custom access user can manage in the task report:

  * **Department matches** – view or edit tasks assigned to employees from specific departments
  * **Location matches** – view or edit tasks assigned to employees from specific locations
  * **Employment Status matches** – view or edit tasks assigned to employees with specific employment statuses
  * **Other Criteria matches** – view or edit tasks assigned to employees tagged with [other criteria](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360000863252)



**Example:** You'd like to give **two Sales managers** a custom access role with permission to view and edit tasks assigned to employees in the **Sales** department and based in **San Francisco**.

Select the two managers' **names** from the **Add user(s)** menu.

Select **Sales** from the **Department matches** menu.

Select **San Francisco** from the **Location matches** menu.

Once you save, these two managers will be able to see and edit only the tasks that have been assigned to employees from the Sales department who are based in San Francisco.

Click **Save and Close**. Repeat the process of adding users and defining their specific access rules as needed. 

Once you're finished, custom access users will be able to manage employee tasks that meet their role's match rules in the [task report](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/13260067443995).

**Note:** If a user is assigned two or more custom roles with permission to see and edit tasks, they'll be able to edit tasks that match the rules for both custom roles.

### Additional resources

  * [Custom access roles](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360019516351)
  * [Task report](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/13260067443995)

# Untapt integration

With this integration, users are able to source, access, engage, and track candidates from Untapt**.** Once this integration is enabled, each primary hiring manager in Untapt who also has a Greenhouse account can authorize Untapt to synchronize jobs with Greenhouse and send Untapt candidates to Greenhouse.

#### In this article

  * Connect to Greenhouse Recruiting through Untapt
  * Create a webhook
  * Use the Untapt integration with Greenhouse Recruiting
    * Adding candidates to Greenhouse
    * Editing jobs in Untapt



### Connect to Greenhouse Recruiting through Untapt

As the primary hiring manager, log into **U****ntapt** and go to your **account page**.

Next, click **Connect with Greenhouse**.

Enter your **Greenhouse email address**.

Then, enter your **Greenhouse** **password**.

Once the connection is authorized, you will see the following screen in Untapt:

For **each Untapt job** , select the corresponding job in Greenhouse. Then, click **Continue**.

When the integration is complete, all Untapt jobs are mapped to their corresponding Greenhouse jobs. Any open candidate applications are also sent to Greenhouse.

### Create a webhook

To integrate Untapt with Greenhouse Recruiting, you'll need to create a webhook. Follow the steps in [this article](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/5888163727003) to create your webhook. Use the values listed below to configure the webhook:

  * **Name** : Untapt integration
  * **When** : The time that the event will be sent to Untapt. Select the following options for this integration: 
    * New application
    * Stage change
    * Reject
    * Hire
  * **Endpoint URL** : Use the following endpoints for their associated webhook 
    * New application: https://www.Untapt.com/ats/api/web-hook/greenhouse/new-application
    * Stage change: https://test.Untapt.com/ats/api/web-hook/greenhouse/stage-change
    * Reject: https://www.Untapt.com/ats/api/web-hook/greenhouse/reject
    * Hire: https://www.Untapt.com/ats/api/web-hook/greenhouse/hire
  * **Secret Key** : Each webhook uses the same Secret Key. Please contact untapt to obtain your Secret Key



### Use the Untapt integration with Greenhouse Recruiting

#### Adding candidates to Greenhouse

When a candidate applies to a role in Untapt, their basic details and a PDF of their resume will be automatically sent to Greenhouse. Prospects will not be sent to Greenhouse, as submitted candidates will need to be tied to a specific job.

Normally, the pipeline in Untapt will display the following columns, and candidates can be rejected or moved through the pipeline:

  * Applied
  * Connected
  * Interviewing
  * Offer
  * Hired



A Greenhouse-integrated pipeline is changed as follows:

The pipeline view more accurately reflects the status of each application in Greenhouse. These are **Active** , **Rejected** , or **Hired**.

The pipeline is **Read O****nly**. Status changes to applications in Greenhouse are automatically synchronized to Untapt via the webhooks configured above.

Untapt displays the candidate's stage in Greenhouse and a link to the candidate's Greenhouse profile.

#### Editing jobs in Untapt

Untapt jobs will still need to be maintained so that they can be effectively marketed to candidates and continue to relay information about the role and your company.

Jobs created after this integration should be mapped to a job in Greenhouse. For example, the "VP of Engineering" job below should be mapped to a corresponding "VP of Engineering" position in Greenhouse. This ensures that applicants for the role in Untapt flow to the same role in Greenhouse.

The below dropdown menu will show all of the jobs that the manager is authorized to view in Greenhouse. Select the corresponding Greenhouse job from the dropdown to link these two jobs.

# Best practices: Rebranding

**Permissions:** —

**Product tier:** Available for new subscription tiers (Core, Plus, and Pro)

It's natural for companies to rebrand and evolve; Brad’s Drink rebranded to Pepsi-Cola in 1898 and Sound of Music became Best Buy in 1983. If your organization is currently rebranding your company or considering the possibility, follow this guide to ensure your careers page and Greenhouse account reflects this exciting next step for your company!

Use the below checklist to help launch your new careers page and start accepting candidates as your new company. 

#### In this article

  * Change your organization's name
  * Update your users' email addresses to the new domain
  * Update your organization's communication copy
  * Update your job board
  * Add your new email domain



### Change your organization's name

Go to the _Organization_ page. _(**Configure** icon  > **Organization**)_

Click the **Edit** icon  next to _Organization Name_. Enter your organization's new name, then click **Save**.

### Update your users' email addresses to the new domain

Site Admins can update email addresses for multiple users by using the [Email Migration Tool](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/37235866041371) under **Configure** > **Dev Center** > **Email Settings** > **Bulk Email Migration Tool**.

To use this tool, you'll download a .csv of all users in your system, add new emails to the spreadsheet, and upload it. After the migration, the new addresses will be added as Secondary emails to all affected users.

Once a migration is complete, an email notification will be sent to the submitter's email.

### Update your organization's communication copy

Comb through any communications where you use your organization’s name (where the `{{COMPANY}}` token is not used). This may include Social Media Templates, Email Templates, job post descriptions, and referral program descriptions.

### Update your job board

If your rebrand also includes a new website, make sure to have your developers check out the [Job Board Integration](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/sections/360000686192-Job-Board) options and [Dev Center](https://app.greenhouse.io/configure/dev_center). This will help provide the necessary documentation to QA your new careers page.

### Add your new email domain

From the [Configure > Dev Center > Email Settings](https://app.greenhouse.io/account/email_settings) page, input your new domain. From that page, you can email your IT team with all the information they need to verify it through Greenhouse. This helps to prevent emails sent to candidates and coworkers from going to Spam.

# Greenhouse Onboarding settings overview

**Permissions:** Owners and Coordinators

**Product tier:** Available for Greenhouse Onboarding and Greenhouse Welcome subscription tiers

Owners and Coordinators can access the _Settings_ page to manage various settings for your organization's Greenhouse Onboarding or Greenhouse Welcome account.

#### In this article

Introduction

Company info

Onboarding plan

Welcome experience

Data flow

### Introduction

Navigate to **Settings** > **Introduction** >**Settings Overview** to get started with essential settings for your organization's account. Here, you can set up [onboarding plan defaults](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360000508312), add department info, and craft your organization's [new hire experience](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360013327271).

### Company info

Use **Company Info** settings to add departments and locations, set new hire fields, and manage 3rd-party task systems.

**Note:** Deleting a department or location will impact any onboarding plan which uses that department or location to assign specific onboarding activities. We recommend editing your onboarding plan to change selected departments or locations rather than deleting these options in _Company Info_.

#### Departments

Add departments for your organization. You can also edit or delete any existing departments.

**Note:** Coordinators have access to view departments. Only Owners can add or edit departments.

#### Locations

Add, edit, or delete office locations and addresses for your organization.

**Note:** Coordinators have access to view locations. Only Owners can add or edit locations.

#### Fields

Add, edit, and organize a variety of [fields](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360024972792) to collect information about your new hires during onboarding.

#### 3rd-party task systems

Connect Greenhouse Onboarding to your [3rd-party task systems](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360022403771) to manage new hire tasks within your established ticketing processes.

### Onboarding plan

Use **Onboarding Plan** settings to manage and preview elements of your organization's onboarding plan for new hires.

#### Other criteria

Configure [other criteria](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360000863252) beyond a new hire's department, location, and employment status to generate flexible and tailored onboarding plans.

**Note:** Deleting other criteria will impact any onboarding plan which uses these criteria to assign specific onboarding activities. We recommend editing your onboarding plan to change your selected other criteria rather than deleting these criteria.

#### Tasks

Build, edit, and manage [tasks](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360000525691) that you can assign to new hires, managers, and other users during the onboarding process.

#### E-Signature templates

Build and manage [E-Signature templates](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/115003695071) to streamline e-signature requests sent to onboarding employees.

#### Emails

**Note:** Only users with [Owner access](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360019575491) can set up a SAML configuration in Greenhouse Onboarding.

On the  _Single Sign-On_ page, fill out or edit the following fields with your organization's SSO credentials:

  * Single logout URL (optional)
  * IdP certificate fingerprint (in SHA1 format)



Mark the checkbox above the Save button if your organization **uses Azure AD as an Identity Provider**.

Click **Save** when you're done.

# Fairgo.ai integration

Fairgo.ai’s integration with Greenhouse Recruiting allows users to screen candidates with AI powered live video interviews.

Use the [fairgo.ai](https://www.fairgo.ai/) integration to connect with Greenhouse to fetch jobs and candidate applications. Jobs are used to automatically create interview questions from the posted content. Candidate resumes are evaluated against the job requirements.

When an assessment integration is set up, hiring managers send a test to a candidate. Fairgo will invite the candidates to a live video interview, where our AI will ask four questions relevant to the role. On completion the interview transcript will be used to evaluate the candidate for the role, and a score along with a deep link to [fairgo.ai](https://www.fairgo.ai/) will be sent back to Greenhouse.

There are three steps to integrate [Fairgo.ai](http://fairgo.ai) with Greenhouse. The first step is to configure the integration, second to configure the assessment using the Fairgo Key, and third to configure webhooks.

#### In this article

  * Set up the fairgo.ai integration
  * Configure an assessment stage
  * Configure webhooks (optional)
  * Additional resources



### Set up the fairgo.ai integration 

In the [fairgo.ai](https://www.fairgo.ai/) application click “settings” in the drop down menu from top right hand corner

Then select the **Integrations** tab in the settings

Then when you are on the integrations tab click the **Add integration** button

Then select “Greenhouse” from the platform drop down.

This will create an integration entry with a unique “Fairgo Key”, to complete the integration use “Click to configure” which will pop up the partner authorization dialog.

Once the user inputs their email address, they will be asked to authorize the scopes:

  * List job posts
  * List jobs
  * List job hiring managers
  * Create job notes
  * List users
  * List user emails
  * List candidates
  * List attachments
  * List applications
  * Reject applications
  * Unreject applications



Once complete they will have a platform key populated with the refresh token. They can optionally choose to sync all open jobs, future jobs, or a specific job then hit Save.

You will then see the [fairgo.ai](https://www.fairgo.ai/) integration and jobs will now get synchronized with [fairgo.ai](https://www.fairgo.ai/). The Fairgo Key is the unique key you’ll need to provide to Greenhouse support to setup Assessment and you will also use it when setting up webhooks

### Configure an assessment stage

Follow the steps in [this article](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/5888163696923) to add the assessment stage in your interview plans.

Once the [fairgo.ai](https://www.fairgo.ai/)’s integration is enabled for your organization, you will be able to add the [fairgo.ai](https://www.fairgo.ai/) assessment as an interview stage.

Once [fairgo.ai](https://www.fairgo.ai/) is set up as an assessment provider, users can add the Fairgo stage:

You can send an assessment to a candidate by selecting the **Send Test** button next to the interview stage. The assessment instructions will be sent by [Fairgo.ai](http://fairg.ai)

After it has been sent, an assessment’s status will display in Greenhouse Recruiting.

Once the candidate has submitted their test, the Interview Kit will contain a link to view the submitted test in the [fairgo.ai](https://www.fairgo.ai/) application.

To see a candidate’s results in [fairgo.ai](https://www.fairgo.ai/), click **View Report**.

### Configure webhooks (optional)

To integrate [fairgo.ai](https://www.fairgo.ai/) with Greenhouse Recruiting, you’ll need to create two webhooks. Follow the steps in this article to create your webhook. Use the values listed below to configure the webhook:

#### Webhook 1: Jobs

  * **Name** : fairgo-job-post-updated
  * **When** : Job Post Updated
  * **Endpoint URL** : <https://webhook.prod.fairgo.ai/v1/greenhouse/inbound>
  * **Secret key** : your “Fairgo Key” from the previous step
  * **Associated partner** : Fairgo.ai
  * **Advanced Settings**
  * **Username** : your “Fairgo Key” from the previous step



#### Webhook 2: Candidate applications

  * **Name** : fairgo-candidate-application
  * **When** : Candidate has submitted application
  * **Endpoint URL** : <https://webhook.prod.fairgo.ai/v1/greenhouse/inbound>
  * **Secret key** : your “Fairgo Key”
  * **Associated partner** : Fairgo.ai
  * **Advanced Settings**
    * **Username** : your “Fairgo Key” from the previous step



Use the [fairgo.ai](https://www.fairgo.ai/) integration with Greenhouse Recruiting by copying the Fairgo Key from the integrations tab from the settings.

By configuring these two integrations [fairgo.ai](https://www.fairgo.ai/) will automatically fetch new jobs and candidate applications. Without the webhook, these records will still be fetched, but only every hour.

When a job is imported, job requirements and interview questions will be generated from the content, and used in the video interview assessment. They can be edited after being generated.

When a candidate is imported, the resume will be downloaded if available. This will be parsed and an evaluation will be available within the [fairgo.ai](https://www.fairgo.ai/) platform based on job requirements.

### Additional resources

For additional information not covered here, reach out to julian@fairgo.ai

You can also access [documentation](https://docs.fairgo.ai/manage/integrations/greenhouse) on the Greenhouse integration on Fairgo.ai’s website.

# Disclose GDPR information on prospect form in Greenhouse Events

**Permissions:** Job Admin and above who have access to CRM

**Product tier:** Available for new subscription tiers (Core, Plus, and Pro)

Companies are required to provide a variety of details at the time data is requested (for example, when a prospect submits their information at a career fair), including why they are requesting certain information, how long it will be stored, where it will be sent, and the safeguards in place relating to the transfer.

Using Greenhouse's Events app, you can provide the required GDPR notification on the prospect form as a custom question.

#### In this article

  * Add GDPR information on a prospect form
  * Greenhouse GDPR notice example text



### Add GDPR information on a prospect form

To add GDPR Information to an _Open_ or _Planned_ Event, click **CRM** on your navigation bar.

Scroll to the _Events_ section, and click the **Ellipsis** icon  beside an event. Click **Edit Event** from the dropdown.

**Note** : If you don't see the event you're looking for, click **See All** and choose the event from the subsequent list.

Scroll to the _Prospect Info Form_ section and click **Add a Question**.

Use the Edit a Custom Question box to input your organization's GDPR information in the _What is your question?_ field.

Select **Single-select** from the _Answer type_ dropdown and input a statement of acknowledgment in the _Options_ field.

Select **Required**.

When finished, click **Add Custom Question**.

Click **Update Event** to confirm the change. Your organization's GDPR information will be added to the prospect form.

### Greenhouse GDPR notice example text

**Note:** You should seek the advice of your legal counsel to prepare your GDPR notice text as it applies to your business. What follows is an example of an Article 13 notification. Greenhouse cannot guarantee that this text will ensure GDPR compliance for your company.

**Example** : When you apply to a job on this site, the personal data contained in your application will be collected by `[CONTROLLER]` (“Controller”), which is located at `[ADDRESS]` and can be contacted by emailing `[EMAIL]`. Controller’s data protection officer is `[DPO NAME]`, who can be contacted at `[CONTACT INFORMATION]`. Your personal data will be processed for the purposes of managing Controller’s recruitment related activities, which include setting up and conducting interviews and tests for applicants, evaluating and assessing the results thereto, and as is otherwise needed in the recruitment and hiring processes. Such processing is legally permissible under Art. 6(1)(f) of Regulation (EU) 2016/679 (General Data Protection Regulation) as necessary for the purposes of the legitimate interests pursued by the Controller, which are the solicitation, evaluation, and selection of applicants for employment.

Your personal data will be shared with Greenhouse Software, Inc., a cloud services provider located in the United States of America and engaged by Controller to help manage its recruitment and hiring process on Controller’s behalf. Accordingly, if you are located outside of the United States, your personal data will be transferred to the United States once you submit it through this site. Because the European Union Commission has determined that United States data privacy laws do not ensure an adequate level of protection for personal data collected from EU data subjects, the transfer will be subject to appropriate additional safeguards under `[either the standard contractual clauses or the Privacy Shield]`. You can obtain a copy of the standard contractual clauses by contacting us at `[example@yourcompany.com](mailto:example@yourcompany.com)`.

Your personal data will be retained by Controller as long as Controller determines it is necessary to evaluate your application for employment. Under the GDPR, you have the right to request access to your personal data, to request that your personal data be rectified or erased, and to request that processing of your personal data be restricted. You also have to right to data portability. In addition, you may lodge a complaint with an EU supervisory authority.

# Manage custom offer field dependencies

**Permissions:** Site Admin, and Job Admin who can manage custom fields

**Product tier:** Available for Plus and Pro subscription tiers

Dependent custom offer fields allow organizations to control which fields (and which field options) appear during offer creation, based on values selected in other custom fields. This setup helps teams reduce clutter, avoid data entry mistakes, and guide users through only the fields relevant to the offer being built.

#### In this article

  * Create custom offer field dependency
  * Configure option-level dependencies
  * Create nested parent/child dependency
  * Edit or remove an existing dependency



### Create custom offer field dependency

To create a parent/child custom offer field dependency, begin by identifying the child field (the field that should appear conditionally).

Click the **Configure** icon  on your navigation bar and select **Custom Options** in the left panel.

On the next page, click **Offers**.

Click the name of the custom offer field that should serve as the **child** in the dependency.

Select the **Dependencies** tab.

In the **Define the parent field** section, choose a **parent** field from the dropdown. The child field will appear only when a specified option is selected in this parent field.

**Note** : 

  * Only custom offer fields with the type Yes/No or Single select can be used as parent fields.
  * Single select custom offer fields with more than 25 options cannot be a parent.
  * For option-level filtering, the parent field type must be Single select with 25 options or fewer.
  * Fields already used in a [nested parent/child dependency](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360038889992#h_3c71ae60-e10c-4743-bd9b-2150a80d2263) cannot be used again as a parent.



In the **Map parent options to child** table, check the boxes next to each parent field option that should trigger the child field to appear.

Each selected option defaults to **All options** , meaning all values in the child field will be available unless you configure option-level filtering.

Click **Save** when finished. The parent/child dependency is now active.

When a user creates an offer, the child field will only appear if the selected parent field value matches your configuration.

### Configure option-level dependencies

To limit which child field options are shown for each parent field selection:

In the **Map parent options to child** table, click **Edit options** next to a selected parent field option.

In the modal that appears, select the specific child field options that should be available when that parent value is selected.

For example, if Career Level = 3 – Senior Associate, you might include (and remove the rest):

  * Annual Bonus
  * Equity Grant
  * Performance Bonus



Click **Apply** to save the configuration for that parent field option.

Repeat this process for other parent options as needed.

Click **Save** to finalize the full dependency setup.

Users will now see a filtered list of child field options based on the selected parent value.

### Create nested parent/child dependency

**Note** : Greenhouse Recruiting supports a three-level nesting structure for dependent custom offer fields (i.e. grandparent/parent/child).

To create a nested dependency:

From **Custom Options** > **Offers** , click the custom offer field that serves as the parent in an existing dependency.

Open the **Dependencies** tab.

In the**Define the parent field** section, choose a new parent field. This becomes the grandparent in the hierarchy.

**Note** : 

  * Only Yes/No or Single select custom offer fields fields can be used as grandparent fields. 
  * Fields already in a [nested structure](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360038889992#h_3c71ae60-e10c-4743-bd9b-2150a80d2263) can't be reused as grandparents.



In the **Map parent options** to child table, select which grandparent options should trigger the parent (and child) fields to appear.

Click **Save**. 

Now, when users create an offer, the fields will appear only if the correct combination of grandparent and parent values is selected.

### Edit or remove an existing dependency

To make changes to an existing dependency or remove it entirely, follow the same instructions above and start at the child field. Those steps are:

Go to **Configure** > **Custom Options** > **Offers**.

Click the name of the **child** custom offer field.

Open the **Dependencies** tab.

#### To edit the dependency:

Use the dropdown to change the **parent field** if needed.

In the **Map parent options** to child table, update which parent options should trigger the child field.

To change the list of visible child options for a given parent value, click **Edit options** and select the desired options in the modal.

Click **Apply**(if in the modal editing options), then **Save** when finished.

**Note:** Edits to dependencies do not apply retroactively to existing offers.

#### To remove the dependency:

In the **Define the parent field** section, click the **X** icon next to the parent field name.

In the confirmation dialog box, click **Remove.**

Click **Save** to finalize.

**Note:** If the child field is also a parent in a nested dependency, removing the parent will dissolve the entire chain.

# Connect to Harvest v3 partner integrations

**Permissions:** Site Admins or users who can manage ALL organization’s API credentials

**Product tier:** Available for new subscription tiers (Core, Plus, and Pro) 

Harvest v3 partner integrations use OAuth 2.0 authentication to provide secure, permissioned access to your organization’s data. These integrations allow approved partners to take specific actions in Greenhouse on behalf of your organization.

#### In this article

  * Start the connection
  * Review requested permissions and log in
  * Choose an authorization method
  * Manage or revoke access



#### Start the connection

The connection process begins when the OAuth flow is launched. This may be initiated in two ways:

  * **From the partner’s product:** Most partners will include a button such as **Connect with Greenhouse** inside their application. Clicking this launches the OAuth flow.
  * **From the Greenhouse Integrations page:** Some integrations can be found by selecting **Integrations** from the top navigation bar, then searching for the partner in the marketplace.



**Note:** Not all integrations listed in the marketplace use Harvest v3. The partner determines where the connection starts and whether a Site Admin or a standard user should complete setup. Always follow the partner’s instructions.

#### Review requested permissions and log in

When the OAuth flow launches, Greenhouse displays the specific actions the partner integration is requesting permission to perform with your organization’s data.

After reviewing the requested permissions, **Log in to Greenhouse** with your credentials to continue.

#### Choose an authorization method

After logging in, you'll see the requested permissions again and a checkbox for how to authorize this integration.

There are two authorization methods:

  * **Authorize using a service account:** Creates an organization-level service user account that owns the authorization. The account has no username or password and persists until disconnected by a permissioned user. Actions appear in Greenhouse as performed by the service account.



**Note:** This option is available only if the authorizing user is a Site Admin.

  * **Authorize** _**without**_**a service account:** Links the authorization to the individual user’s account. Actions taken by the integration appear as if they were performed by that user.



We recommend confirming with the partner which authorization method is best for their integration.

#### Manage or revoke access

Once authorized, connected integrations appear on the **Connected Integrations** page. To access this page, click on the **Configure** icon  on your navigation bar, then click **Dev Center** on the left. 

Click **Connected integrations**. 

From here, you'll see all your OAuth-connected integrations and the following info:

  * **Integration name —** the name of the partner integration.
  * **Connected by —** the user or service account that authorized the integration.
  * **Connected on —** the date when the integration was connected.



From the Connected Integrations table, permissioned users can open the integration’s details page by clicking the **integration name** or selecting **View details** from the **ellipsis (…) menu**. The ellipsis menu may also include other available actions, such as **Disconnect** , depending on the integration.

On the view details page, users can:

  * Review integration information and authorized permissions.
  * View which account was used to connect the integration.
  * Disconnect the integration to revoke access.



**Note:** Disconnecting immediately revokes access, but the same user can reconnect later by repeating the OAuth flow.

# Bandana integration

[Bandana](http://bandana.com) is a job search platform built for modern recruiting. Our worker-centric product and extensive social channels make us one of the most trusted job boards in the US.

Bandana’s integration with Greenhouse Recruiting allows companies to directly post jobs from Greenhouse onto Bandana, and intake applications from Bandana into Greenhouse.

#### In this article

  * Send integration request to Bandana
    * Find your Job Board URL
    * Generate a job board API key 
    * Add Bandana as a Custom Source and create a Job Board Tracking Link
  * Use the Bandana integration with Greenhouse Recruiting
  * Additional resources



### Send integration request to Bandana

To make your open jobs available to Bandana, please submit your **job board URL, job board API key, and a custom job board tracking link here:**[bandana.com/b/greenhouse](http://bandana.com/b/greenhouse)**.** We will walk through how to obtain each of these items below

#### Find your Job Board URL

You can find your Job Board URL by navigating to the Job Board settings. (**Configure** > **Job Boards & Posts** > **Ellipsis** icon next to job board > **Edit Board Settings**) and scroll to the URL field.

[Click here](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/5888210160155) for a more detailed walkthrough of how to locate your job board URL.

#### Generate a job board API key

Next, you’ll need to create a Job Board API key for Bandana.

Follow the steps in [this article](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/13446638483355) and use the information below when creating your API key:

  * **API Type:** Job Board
  * **Partner:** Bandana or Unlisted vendor
  * **Description:** Bandana job board API key



#### Add Bandana as a Custom Source and create a Job Board Tracking Link

Follow the steps in [this article](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/200721664-Add-custom-source) to add “Bandana” as a custom source. 

Once you have created the custom source, follow [this article](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/201823760-Create-a-tracking-link-for-a-job-board) to generate a tracking link with the source as “Bandana.” This is the **custom job board tracking link** you should share with the Bandana integrations team.

**Once you have the board URL, API key, and customer job board tracking link, please submit it here:**[bandana.com/b/greenhouse](http://bandana.com/b/greenhouse)**.** If you have questions, email [integrations@bandana.com](mailto:integrations@bandana.com)**.**

### Use the Bandana integration with Greenhouse Recruiting

Once you have shared your job board URL with Bandana, your Greenhouse jobs will be automatically synced on Bandana’s search platform. Bandana also offers organic, free traffic, as well as sponsorship campaigns to boost your jobs to the right applicants. 

Sponsored jobs will appear first on all search surfaces and qualified applicants will be notified. Your Bandana campaign team will help you select and launch sponsorship campaigns to maximize job views and applications.

Once you have integrated fully, interested applicants can complete your job application directly on Bandana. Completed applications will be sent directly to your Greenhouse Recruiting organization. 

You will be able to see all applicants, with the source as ‘Bandana’ and their information in your Greenhouse Recruiting account.

### Additional resources

For additional information not covered here, reach out to [integrations@bandana.com](mailto:integrations@bandana.com). For information on pricing and job sponsorship information, please reach out to [business@bandana.com](mailto:business@bandana.com).

# Generate my referrer link

**Permissions:** \--

**Product tier:** Available for new subscription tiers (Core, Plus, and Pro)

Each user in Greenhouse Recruiting has access to their own unique referrer link, which is a URL associated with your personal account. This link can be shared with people you know. 

When someone applies to a job through your referrer link, you'll be credited as the source for the applicant. If your organization has a referral program, you may also be rewarded for applicants you refer.

**Note:** To generate referral links, your organization must have the setting enabled under Configure > Organization > Referral Program.

#### In this article

  * Generate your referrer link from your dashboard
  * Generate your referrer link from your account settings



### Generate your referrer link from your dashboard

The easiest way to generate your Referrer Link is from the **My Dashboard** page. Find the _Add a Referral_ section and use the dropdown to select a job or job board.

Once you select an option, your referral link will auto-populate in the next field. Click **Copy** to save the link to your clipboard.

Once you've copied the link to your clipboard, _Link copied_ will appear.

### Generate your referrer link from your account settings

You can also generate your referrer link from the _Account Settings_ page. To start, click on your name in the top right corner. Click **Account Settings** from the dropdown.

From the _Account Settings_ page, find the _Personal Information_ section. Click **My Referrer Link.**

The _Get Tracking Link_ window will allow you to select whether you would like to generate a tracking link for an entire job board or a specific job post.

Once you select an option, your referral link will auto-populate in one of the next fields. Click **Copy** to save the link to your clipboard.

Once you've copied the link to your clipboard, _Link copied_ will appear.

# Release Notes: September 2025

Greenhouse Software regularly releases new product features, updates, and improvements. You can stay up-to-date by following our [release notes](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/200929955) or checking out the [latest feature releases](https://www.greenhouse.com/greenhouse-latest-features) page.

#### This month's releases

  * Greenhouse Recruiting
  * Greenhouse Onboarding
  * Integrations
  * Bug fixes



### Greenhouse Recruiting

#### Country code on job posts

Job applications now include a country code picker for phone numbers, giving candidates a clearer, more consistent way to enter their contact details—whether applying through a job post or Quick Apply in MyGreenhouse. The selected country code is stored in Greenhouse Recruiting to support accurate, structured data. 

#### Improvements to calculated custom fields

Calculated fields can now reference other calculated fields, making it easier to build multi-step logic without duplicating work.

Offer fields also support more complex formulas, including multiple field references, fixed numbers, and repeated operators. This helps teams set up detailed compensation structures, such as salary breakdowns by pay frequency or region.

[Read more about calculated fields](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/31723991042075)

#### Updated names for AI features to improve clarity

We’ve renamed a few AI settings so they more clearly reflect what they do:

  * **Keyword suggestions** replaces Talent Filtering and Talent Rediscovery. It uses AI to suggest relevant filter keywords based on the job description or your input—making it faster to refine your search.

  * **Prospect response review** is the new name for GHSA Sentiment Analysis. It gives you AI-powered insights into candidate replies, helping you quickly gauge tone and intent while keeping you in control of the final decision.

  * **Scorecard summaries** now include a clearer description, highlighting how it brings together interview feedback, points of agreement or disagreement, and key quotes for your team.




#### New Connected integrations page

Users with developer permissions can now view a _Connected integrations_ page in the Dev Center. 

This early access release lists Harvest v3 Partner integrations that use OAuth and lays the groundwork for a centralized place to manage all of your organization’s integrations.

More integration types will be added to this page in future updates.

[Read more about connecting to Harvest v3 partner integrations.](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/41437121183899)

### Greenhouse Onboarding

#### Assign onboarding tasks to multiple people

Users can now assign the same onboarding task to more than one person. The task stays open until one team member completes it, helping reduce delays and making it easier for others to step in when needed.

[Read more about managing tasks.](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/4402108629787)

### Integrations

  * **Candidate sourcing** : [JobMinglr](https://integrations.greenhouse.com/partners/jobminglr) brings quality candidates to every role, so hiring teams spend less time on unqualified applicants.
  * **Candidate sourcing** : [Pin](https://integrations.greenhouse.com/partners/pin) automates sourcing and outreach, so teams can spend less time searching and more time connecting with the right candidates.
  * **Candidate testing** : [Codeaid's](https://integrations.greenhouse.com/partners/codeaid) AI Interviewer provides real-world coding assessments to measure the skills of developers and ML/AI engineers.
  * **Candidate testing** : [DigAI](https://integrations.greenhouse.com/partners/digai) generates dynamic interview questions, conducts interviews through audio and evaluates candidate performance by AI analysis.
  * **Other integrations** : [PerchPeek](https://integrations.greenhouse.com/partners/perchpeek) delivers exceptional relocation experiences for global mobility teams and their relocators at a fraction of traditional prices.
  * **Other integrations** : [CV-Transformer](https://integrations.greenhouse.com/partners/cv-transformer) transforms CVs into branded, recruiter-ready formats in seconds.
  * **Other integrations** : [Hire2Retire](https://integrations.greenhouse.com/partners/hire2retire) integrates HR with AD & Google Workspace to automate onboarding, role changes, RBAC and offboarding.



### Bug fixes

  * Fixed an issue that returned an error when users tried to send a personal self-schedule request email template.
  * Fixed an issue where custom fields were automatically rounding numerical values to two decimal points.
  * Fixed an issue where the old Job Notes field was still displaying after the job notes update last month.
  * Fixed an issue where the self-schedule window was not loading when there were too many email template options or custom fields.
  * Fixed an issue where users saw an error when trying to select a personal self-schedule email template.
  * Fixed an issue where the Mark as Hired date was automatically updating to the day before if the user was located in a different time zone.
  * Fixed an issue where migrated candidates were not receiving candidate surveys.

# Clinch integration

Clinch Talent is the first step in building a better talent network, by helping employers attract, identify, and really get to know passive candidates before they hit apply. Clinch leverages the proven practices of content marketing — helping you build better careers content and delivering key information on the candidates who engage with that content. This improved flow of information in the pre-application stage makes it much easier for both sides to figure out if they are a good fit.

Clinch's integration with Greenhouse Recruiting allows you to source, access, engage, and track candidates from Clinch.

#### In this article

  * Enable the Clinch integration
    * Create a Harvest API key
    * Find your job board token
    * Setup the integration on Clinch
    * (Optional) Create web hooks
  * Use the Clinch integration with Greenhouse Recruiting



### Create a Harvest API key for the Clinch integration

To enable the Greenhouse Recruiting / Clinch integration, you'll need to create a Harvest API key.

Follow the steps in [this article](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/5888163769883) to create the key, and verify that the credentials and permissions below are selected.

#### Credentials

In the _Create New Credential_ box, make the following selections:

  * **API type:** Harvest
  * **Partner:** Clinch (optional)
  * **Description:** Clinch Harvest API key



#### Permissions

Contact Clinch to verify the Harvest API Key permissions needed for your integration.

### Find your job board token

To make your job posts available to Clinch, you'll need to find and provide your Greenhouse Recruiting job board token.

You can find your job board URL by navigating to **Configure** > **Job Boards & Posts **> **Ellipsis** icon  next to your job board > **Edit Board Settings** , then scroll to the URL field.

Copy the token at the end of the URL for use in the next step.

[Check out this article](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/5888210160155) for a more detailed walkthrough of locating your job board token.

### Set up the integration on Clinch

With your API key and job board token copied, navigate to the integrations page on Clinch via **Settings** > **Integrations** , then click the **Greenhouse** logo.

Paste the API key and job board token in the available fields.

**Note** : Paste the job board token in the **Company code** field.

Next, type in your Greenhouse Recruiting account email in the **Default Team Member Email** field, and select a campaign and a template page associated with the campaign to use as a page template for the imported jobs.

When finished, click **Save**.

Click **Sync** to import your jobs from Greenhouse Recruiting.

### (Optional) Create web hooks

Once you have your API details saved in Clinch, you can also set up Greenhouse Recruiting web hooks to keep candidate statuses in sync between Clinch and Greenhouse Recruiting.

On Clinch, navigate to the [edit Greenhouse integration form](https://clinchtalent.com/admin/greenhouse_ats_integration/edit) and copy the **Webhook Secret Token** and the **Webhook URL** from the form. 

Next, follow the steps in [this article](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/5888163727003) to create your web hooks on Greenhouse Recruiting using the values below. You'll need to create three (3) separate web hooks for the Clinch integration.

#### Webhook 1: Candidate application

  * **Name** : Candidate application
  * **When** : Candidate has submitted application
  * **Endpoint URL** : The Webhook URL copied in Clinch
  * **Secret Key** : The Webhook Secret Token copied in Clinch



#### Webhook 2: Candidate stage change

  * **Name** : Candidate stage change
  * **When** : Candidate has changed stage
  * **Endpoint URL** : The Webhook URL copied in Clinch
  * **Secret Key** : The Webhook Secret Token copied in Clinch



#### Webhook 3: Candidate Rejection

  * **Name** : Candidate rejection
  * **When** : Candidate or Prospect has been rejected
  * **Endpoint URL** : The Webhook URL copied in Clinch
  * **Secret Key** : The Webhook Secret Token copied in Clinch



Once complete, Clinch will use the web hooks to maintain parity between candidate statuses in Clinch and in Greenhouse Recruiting.

### Use the Clinch integration with Greenhouse Recruiting

Once enabled, as soon as a job post is live on your Greenhouse Recruiting job board, Clinch will generate a new job page on the career site using the desired template for that job.

If distribution is enabled the job is also sent for indexing to Google and the main aggregators and added to the Career site map.

You can read more about using the Clinch integration on [Clinch FAQ](https://www.clinchtalent.com/faq/).
