<!-- source: https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/4405633343259-Redshift-vs-S3-for-Business-Intelligence-Connector -->

# Redshift vs. S3 for Business Intelligence Connector

**Permissions:** –

**Product tier:** Available for Plus and Pro subscription tiers

With [Business Intelligence Connector](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360017503272), your recruiting data can be delivered in nightly ETLs to your organization through Amazon Web Services (AWS) using Redshift or S3. Which method you use depends on your organization's processes and tech stack.

#### In this article

  * Redshift
  * S3



### Redshift

With Redshift, Greenhouse hosts the data in our Amazon Redshift instance and will provide your organization with credentials to access your data.

If you use Redshift, the data is already formatted in a relational database and prepared to be plugged directly into your data development tool. However, because Greenhouse maintains the database, you won't be able to control the location or format of the data.

Some organizations prefer Redshift for these reasons:

  * You aren't required to pay for your own storage solution. We'll host the data so you can retrieve it when needed.
  * You don't need internal technical resources to manage a Redshift instance.



**Note:** Redshift is not available for organizations on the EU silo or on [Silo: 101](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360056365191).

### S3

S3 is a cloud storage service provided by Amazon Web Services. When using an S3 bucket, your organization hosts and controls all the data in your own database. We'll deliver your data nightly in a _.csv_ to your S3 bucket. 

**Note:** The ._csv_ files can be easily transformed into a relational database using [Athena](https://aws.amazon.com/athena/?whats-new-cards.sort-by=item.additionalFields.postDateTime&whats-new-cards.sort-order=desc), another Amazon service. 

Some organizations prefer S3 for these reasons:

  * You can control the authentication credentials (username and password) for your data and grant Business Intelligence Connector permission to send new data.
  * Your organization needs a ._csv_ to manipulate your data.
  * Your organization is on the [EU silo or silo 101](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360056365191) and wants to use the Business Intelligence Connector. 



**Learn more**

[Enable Business Intelligence Connector](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/4405507275547)

[Business Intelligence Connector settings](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/4409350482843)
email-domain-verification-faq:
<!-- source: https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/11919501911835-Email-domain-verification-FAQ -->

# Email domain verification FAQ

**Permissions:** Users with "Can configure email settings" permission

**Product tier:** Available for new subscription tiers (Core, Plus, and Pro)

Greenhouse Recruiting allows you to send emails from within your account that will appear to the candidate as being sent from your organization's domain. This article answers frequently asked questions about [verifying your domain](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/11915120413211) to use in emails.

#### In this article

  * How does Greenhouse Recruiting send emails?
  * What's the difference between a root domain and a subdomain?
  * What's the difference between a domain registrar and a Domain Name Server (DNS) provider
  * How do I find my DNS provider?
  * How do I edit my DNS settings?
  * Why is `gh-mail` added to my domain?
  * My company won't let me use the `gh-mail` subdomain. What do I do?
  * How do I know if my domain has been verified?
  * What should I do if my domain isn't being verified?
  * Why aren't my emails being delivered?
  * I'm getting the error message "Heads up! It's unlikely this email will be delivered!" What should I do?
  * How do I remove my email domain from Greenhouse Recruiting?



**Note** : Work with your organization's IT team when configuring and verifying your email domain.

### How does Greenhouse Recruiting send emails?

Greenhouse Recruiting uses the third-party email provider [Mailgun](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360023438532) to send emails. By default, all originating in Greenhouse Recruiting are sent via Mailgun. This includes (but is not limited to) emails such as new user invitations, notifications, emails to candidates, and [@mention](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360013153651) messages between users.

As a part of the Greenhouse Recruiting implementation process, we ask all organizations to register their domain within the Greenhouse application and complete the [email verification process](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/11915120413211). This process registers your domain with Mailgun, which then generates DNS records (SPF, DKIM, and sometimes MX records) to be added to your DNS settings.

Greenhouse Recruiting also offers the option to send mail from your own server by setting up a [custom SMTP](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360002116131).

### What's the difference between a root domain and a subdomain?

A root domain is your primary main domain, which is purchased through a domain name provider and houses all the pages on your website. For example, the URL `omniva-corp.com` is a root domain.

A subdomain is a subsection of your root domain which, in a URL, comes before the root domain along with a period. For example, in the URL`support.omniva-corp.com`, `support` is the subdomain.

### What's the difference between a domain registrar and a Domain Name Server (DNS) provider?

A domain registrar is a service from which your purchase a domain. A Domain Name Server (DNS) provider is a service you use to host your domain. Some services provide both domain registration and domain hosting, so you may use the same service for both.

You can look up your domain registrar by searching for your domain name on [ICANN.org](https://lookup.icann.org/en).

### How do I find my DNS provider?

Common DNS providers include [Google](https://support.google.com/domains/answer/3290350?hl=en#zippy=%2Cadd-a-resource-record), [Cloudflare](https://developers.cloudflare.com/dns/manage-dns-records/how-to/create-dns-records/), and [GoDaddy](https://www.godaddy.com/help/manage-dns-records-680), but your organization may use a different one. If you don't know who your DNS provider is, we recommend reaching out to someone on your team.

We created the following message template to help you collect the info you need. Copy the message below and send it to a member of your team:
    
    
    Hello, I’m working on setting up our account with Greenhouse Recruiting, and I need to know what DNS provider we use. Do you know the answer, or do you know someone who would?

### How do I edit my DNS settings?

Find the area in your account where you can edit your DNS settings. The process of finding and navigating this section of your account will differ depending on the DNS provider you use.

**Tip:** Look for buttons or links like "Host Record," "New Record," or "Add Items to DNS."

If you need help locating your DNS settings, you may need to consult the DNS provider's support center or contact their support team.

Copy the message below and send it to your DNS provider's support team:
    
    
    Hello, I’m trying to update my DNS records to include TXT, MX and CNAME. Where can I go to edit these settings?

If you still need help after contacting your DNS provider's support team, reach out to the Greenhouse Recruiting [Technical Support](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/requests/new) team.

### Why is gh-mail added to my domain?

When you register a new root domain, you may encounter some situations that prevent or complicate the process of updating your DNS records. These include the following:

  * Your root domain may have already been registered with our email provider, [Mailgun](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360023438532)
  * You may have reached the limit of 10 DNS lookups of your root domain's SPF
  * Your IT team may have strict policies on adding new DNS records to your root domain



By adding the `gh-mail` subdomain to your root domain automatically, a new subdomain is created in your DNS records, avoiding the possibility of the above issues. In simple terms, using the `gh-mail` subdomain avoids common complications that impede your organization's ability to send emails reliably.

Using the `gh-mail` subdomain doesn't change the email experience for your users. They can send and receive messages through Greenhouse Recruiting from their standard email address.

### My company won't let me use the gh-mail subdomain. What do I do?

Some companies have a strict security, or DMARC, policy on their domain that prohibits using the `gh-mail` subdomain. In this case, your organization won't be able to send emails successfully with our standard process. Instead, you'll need to register your domain without the `gh-mail` subdomain.

To start, click the **Configure** icon > **Dev Center** >**Email Settings**.

If your domain is already registered with the `gh-mail` subdomain, remove the domain.

Add your domain again, this time with an exclamation point `!` before the domain name (For example, `!omniva-corp.com`.) The exclamation point tells Greenhouse Recruiting not to add the `gh-mail` subdomain.

When you finish, click **Register**. Follow the steps to [verify your email domain](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/11915120413211).

### How do I know if my domain has been verified?

**Note** : Email settings have moved to **Configure** > **Dev Center** > **Email Settings**

On the _Email Settings_ page in Greenhouse Recruiting, click **Check DNS Records Now**. When the icons in the table turn from ellipses  to check marks , your domain has been verified.

### What should I do if my domain isn't being verified?

If the table on your _Email Settings_ page shows ellipsis icons  instead of check mark icons , your domain records still need to be verified.

To start, we suggest you review the troubleshooting steps in our article [Why isn’t my domain name system (DNS) verified?](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/13646923428507)

If you still need help, reach out to the Greenhouse Recruiting [Technical Support](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/requests/new) team.

### Why aren't my emails being delivered?

Your Greenhouse Recruiting emails may not be sent in the following situations:

  * **Your domain hasn't been verified:** Domain registration is the first step in setting up your emails in Greenhouse Recruiting. If your domain hasn't been verified, you may receive an error message such as "Heads up! It's unlikely this email will be delivered!". Make sure to [verify your email domain](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/11915120413211) before sending any emails from your Greenhouse Recruiting account.
  * **Your organization has a strict DMARC policy:** Some companies have a strict security, or DMARC, policy on their domain that prohibits using the `gh-mail` subdomain. In this case, your organization won't be able to send emails successfully with our default process. Instead, you'll need to [register your domain without `gh-mail`](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/201111684-Email-domain-verification#h_01F88QTD7W1WAHF8RDMAQT31M7). 
  * **The recipient's email address is on our bounce list:** Mailgun may add an email address to its bounce list after numerous failed attempts to deliver mail. These failed attempts can be caused by the following:
    * An email being sent to an email address that hasn't been fully set up
    * Your organization rejecting the email from Mailgun
    * An unexpected error



Mailgun adding an email address to its bounce list is an effort to prevent potential abuse and protect your sender score. However, some email addresses may be added to the bounce list in error. If you suspect this is the case, reach out to the Greenhouse Recruiting [Technical Support](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/requests/new) team.

### I'm getting the error message "Heads up! It's unlikely this email will be delivered!" What should I do?

The error message "Heads up! It's unlikely this email will be delivered!" may display when sending an email in Greenhouse Recruiting if your email domain is not yet verified. Follow the steps to [verify your email domain](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/11915120413211).

### How do I remove my email domain from Greenhouse Recruiting?

In some cases, it may be necessary to remove a previously registered email domain from your Greenhouse Recruiting account.

To remove an email domain, click the **Configure** icon  on your navigation bar, select **Dev Center,** then **Email Settings** on the left. Click **Show verification details** to view your previously registered email domain, then click **Remove**.

# Skyvia integration

Skyvia is a universal SaaS data platform for quick and easy solving a broad set of data-related tasks with no coding: data integration, automating workflows, cloud data backup, building reports and dashboards, data management with SQL, CSV import/export, creating OData services, etc. It supports over 170 cloud applications and databases and requires no software except a web browser.

There’s no need for extensive technical knowledge, making it perfect for both technical and business users. It’s ranked as one of the Easiest To Use ETL Tools by G2 Crowd ratings and offers scalability and flexibility enough for any business needs. 

Among data integration scenarios, there are basic (Import, Synchronization, Replication) and complex (Data Flow and Control Flow). Apply powerful mapping settings to load and synchronize Discourse data with sources having different data structures and schedule integrations to execute automatically.

Skyvia’s integration with Greenhouse Recruiting allows data import, export, and synchronization with cloud applications and relational databases.

#### In this article

  * Create a Harvest API key
  * Create Skyvia connection
  * Get a User ID
  * Use the Skyvia integration with Greenhouse Recruiting
    * Scheduling integration
    * Data querying with Google Sheets Add-on
  * Additional resources



### Create a Harvest API key

To configure the Skyvia integration, you’ll need to create a Harvest API key. 

Follow the steps in [this article](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/5888163769883) to create the key and verify that the permissions below are selected when configuring the Skyvia integration. Be sure to copy the key as you will need to paste it in Skyvia in the next step.

#### **Credentials**

In the _Create New Credential_ box, make the following selections:

  * **API Type:** Harvest
  * **Partner:** Skyvia or Unlisted Vendor
  * **Description:** Skyvia Harvest API Key



#### **Permissions**

Verify that the following permissions are selected for the Skyvia integration: 

Select the Select All checkbox and click Save at the bottom of the page. 

### Create Skyvia connection

  1. In Skyvia, click **+NEW** in the top menu.
  2. On the left, click **Connection**.
  3. Select the Greenhouse from the list of pre-made connectors. 
  4. Enter your API Key to create a Skyvia connection to Greenhouse.



If you want to load data to Greenhouse and not just read data from Greenhouse, you also need to specify your User ID.

### Get a User ID

There’s a few ways to obtain your Greenhouse user ID. You can use the methods on this [Greenhouse support article](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/10765948752027-Find-your-Greenhouse-Recruiting-user-ID), or via one of the Skyvia tools — Query or Export. Both of these ways can be used even within the limits of the free pricing plan.

To get User IDs via [Query](https://docs.skyvia.com/query/), perform the following steps:

  1. Click **+NEW** in the top menu.
  2. Under Query, click **Builder**.
  3. Click **Select connection** on the left and select your Greenhouse connection.
  4. Scroll down the object list on the left till you see the Users object. Drag it to the Results pane.



After this, you can see your Greenhouse users’ data. Find the corresponding user in the table and copy the value from the Id column of the corresponding row.

Now, you can update a connection with Skyvia. In the Connection Editor, enter your API Key and User ID. Click **Save connection**. 

### Use the Skyvia integration with Greenhouse Recruiting

  * [Import ](https://docs.skyvia.com/data-integration/import/)Greenhouse data directly within major cloud and on-premise data sources.
  * Perform Greenhouse data [synchronization](https://docs.skyvia.com/data-integration/synchronization/) with various sources in both directions.
  * Import and [export CSV files](https://docs.skyvia.com/data-integration/export/) to/from Greenhouse in a convenient web-based user interface. 
  * [Powerful mapping settings](https://docs.skyvia.com/data-integration/common-package-features/mapping/index.html) allow loading and synchronizing Greenhouse data with sources having different data structures. 
  * [Replicate](https://docs.skyvia.com/data-integration/replication/) Greenhouse data to a relational database and maintain this database in an actual state.
  * [Schedule](https://docs.skyvia.com/data-integration/scheduling-packages-for-automatic-execution.html) Greenhouse integration operations, like Greenhouse import or Greenhouse export, etc., to execute it automatically.
  * Use the power of SQL to manage Greenhouse data via the Skyvia Query tool. Skyvia Query also includes a [Google Sheets Add-on](https://docs.skyvia.com/skyvia-query-google-sheets-add-on/) and an [Excel Add-in](https://docs.skyvia.com/skyvia-query-excel-add-in/) that allow Greenhouse export to Excel and Google Sheets with data refresh in one click.



### Scheduling integration

It’s possible to set up automatic integration of data between Greenhouse and other applications and databases using the **Schedule** option. It’s available in every tool of the Data Integration product.

  1. Open the integration scenario of your choice.
  2. Find the**Schedule** option in the upper-left corner of the screen and click on it.



  3. Define the exact time at which the integration must take place. Otherwise, set the interval for recurring data transfer. Skyvia allows for setting the 2-minute interval, which is the near-real-time integration.



  4. Click **Save**.



### Data querying with Google Sheets Add-on

Skyvia add-on for Google Sheets uses a powerful visual **Query Builder** that allows non-techs to craft and execute queries without SQL knowledge. Tech-savvy professionals can create queries using SQL syntax. 

  1. Open any document in your Google Sheets account.
  2. Go to **Extensions - > Add-ons -> Get add-ons**.
  3. Type **_Skyvia Query_** in the search bar.



  4. Click **Install** and proceed with setup instructions in the wizard.
  5. Once the Skyvia Query add-on is installed, go to **Extensions - > Skyvia Query -> Login**.



  6. Log into your Skyvia account or create a new one.
  7. Once the setup and login are completed, go to**Extensions - > Skyvia Query -> Query**.
  8. Select the workspace, Greenhouse connector, and the object to import. Specify the filtering and order criteria if needed. Click **Run** to populate the spreadsheet with the data from Greenhouse.



Now, you can apply Google Spreadsheet functionality to the loaded data.

### Additional resources

For additional information or troubleshooting not covered here, reach out to the Skyvia Support Team via [support@skyvia.com](mailto:support@skyvia.com) or visit the [support portal.](https://support.skyvia.com/portal/en/community/skyvia)

Skyvia documentation is available at <https://docs.skyvia.com/>

**Other resources**

  * [Skyvia case studies](https://skyvia.com/case-studies/)

  * [Mastering data integration - from definition to best practices](https://skyvia.com/learn/what-is-data-integration)

# HRIS Link for hired candidates

HRIS Link can automatically export hired candidates from Greenhouse Recruiting, allowing you to sync new hire information with your HRIS. This feature requires setup and development work to be completed by you or third-party developers.

#### In this article

  * Feature highlights
  * Get started



### Feature highlights

When candidates are [marked as hired](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/200242039-Mark-candidate-as-hired-with-offer-approvals-) in Greenhouse Recruiting, HRIS Link immediately delivers a payload containing candidate details to the SFTP server or S3 bucket you provide.

### Get started

First, decide whether you want to export new hires to an S3 bucket or an SFTP server, and whether you prefer PGP encryption. Once you've made these choices, reach out to your Greenhouse technical consultant to enable the feature. Then you're ready to dig in with the article [Set up HRIS Link for hired candidates](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/11758489369755).

When a candidate is marked as hired in Greenhouse Recruiting, we'll export a payload that includes the new hire's [application, candidate, job, offer, and opening details](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/11758489371419#h_01GNZ3E2TCE6R3CGZMP29TSSC6). Your team, or third-party developers, can transform the resulting data using middleware for use in your preferred HRIS.

**Note** : Each candidate who is marked as hired is exported using HRIS Link, even if the candidate was previously marked as hired on the same job. Each export will include a timestamp to differentiate hires.

It isn't currently possible to exclude certain offices, departments, jobs, or candidates from the HRIS Link export.

# Asana integration

**Permissions:** Owners

**Product tier:** Available to the Greenhouse Welcome and Greenhouse Onboarding subscription tiers

Asana is a web and mobile application designed to help teams organize, track, and manage their work. 

You can connect your organization's Asana board as a [third-party task system](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360022403771) in Greenhouse Onboarding to assign onboarding tasks to Asana. Tasks assigned to Asana will be automatically added as a card to your board and sent to relevant users via email.

#### In this article

  * Add Greenhouse Onboarding to an Asana project
  * Retrieve your Asana project email
  * Connect Asana to Greenhouse Onboarding
  * Additional resources



### Add Greenhouse Onboarding to an Asana project

Before you can send onboarding tasks to Asana, you'll need to share your Asana project with Greenhouse Onboarding.

To start, navigate to the Asana project that you want to connect with Greenhouse Onboarding.

Click **Share**.

In the _Share project_ dialog box, add `no-reply@mail.onboarding.greenhouse.io` to the **Invite with email** field.

Set the member permissions to **Editor**.

**Note:** Make sure that the **Notify them when new tasks are added to this project** checkbox stays unchecked.

When you're finished, click **Send**.

Greenhouse Onboarding has now been added as a member to your Asana project.

### Retrieve your Asana project email

Next, you'll need to retrieve your Asana project's email. This email will be used in Greenhouse Onboarding to set up the integration.

Click the **downward arrow** to the right of your project's name.

From the dropdown menu, select **Import** > **Email**.

Copy the **email address** from the _Add tasks by email_ dialog box.

### Connect Asana to Greenhouse Onboarding

Once you've copied your Asana project's email address, navigate to [Greenhouse Onboarding](https://onboarding.greenhouse.io/).

From your Greenhouse Onboarding homepage, navigate to **Settings** > **Company Info** > **3rd-Party Task Systems**.

On the  _3rd-Party Task Systems_ page, click **Add New**.

Give your new 3rd-party task system a **name** and select **Asana** from the **System** dropdown.

Paste your copied Asana email in the **Email Address** field.

Since your Greenhouse Onboarding tasks can include tokens (which may reveal personally identifiable information), you'll need to define which fields Asana can view.

Use the **Viewable Fields (Optional)** dropdown to select which fields Asana can view.

**Note:** If a task with a non-viewable token is assigned to Asana, Greenhouse Onboarding will block Asana from accessing the information. 

When you're finished, click **Save and Close**.

Your Asana project will be added as a 3rd-party task system to Greenhouse Onboarding and can now be assigned tasks.

**Note:** To connect multiple Asana boards to Greenhouse Onboarding, repeat the above steps for all Asana projects you want to connect.

### Additional resources

  * [3rd-party task systems overview](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360022403771)

# Rejection emails

**Permissions:** \--

**Product tier:** Available for new subscription tiers (Core, Plus, and Pro)

A rejection email is the official email sent to a candidate or prospect when they are marked as **Rejected** for a job. 

Greenhouse Recruiting provides your organization with a default version of this email. Additionally, your organization can edit the provided default, create multiple versions, or write your rejection emails ad hoc when rejecting a candidate or prospect.

#### In this article

  * Edit the default organization-wide rejection email
  * Create a new organization-wide rejection email
  * Create an ad hoc rejection email



### Edit the default organization-wide rejection email

**Note** : Only users with Site Admin level permissions or users with Job Admin level permissions with the additional user-specific permission **Can manage company email and social media templates** can edit the Greenhouse provided default version of the rejection email.

To start, navigate to the **Email Templates** configure page. (**Configure icon** > **Email Templates**)

From the _Email Templates_ page, find the _Organization-Wide Templates_ section. Then, click the **Edit icon** next to **Default Candidate Rejection**.

Edit the body of the email, then click **Save**.

The Default Candidate Rejection is now updated with your edits and will populate for the entire organization when selected during a candidate rejection.

### Create a new organization-wide rejection email

**Note** : Only users with Site Admin level permissions or users with Job Admin level permissions with the additional user-specific permission **Can manage company email and social media templates** can edit the Greenhouse provided default version of the rejection email.

In addition to the default rejection email, your organization can also create new rejection emails at the organizational level.

Navigate to the **Email Templates** configure page. (**Configure icon** > **Email Templates**)

From the _Email Templates_ page, go to the _Organization-Wide Templates_ section. Then, click **New**.

From the _Create an Email Template_ page, enter a **template name**. Then, select **Candidate Rejection** from the **Type** dropdown menu.

Next, select the **email address** the rejection email will come from and provide an **email subject line**. 

Edit the **body of the email** , then click **Save**.

When rejecting a candidate, this template will appear as an available option from the _Template_ dropdown menu.

### Create an ad hoc rejection email

When rejecting a candidate or prospect from a job, you can also create your own rejection email from the _Reject this Candidate/Prospect_ window. These messages are created per candidate/prospect and will not be stored as a template for future use.

**Note** : Users can edit any templates selected from the **Template** dropdown menu when creating an ad hoc email. Any edits made in the _Reject this Candidate/Prospect dialog box_ will not be saved to the template.

# FAQ: HRIS Link for hired candidates

HRIS Link allows you to export newly hired candidates from Greenhouse Recruiting to be synced with your preferred HRIS. This article provides answers to some frequently asked questions about HRIS Link.

#### In this article

  * How does HRIS Link export hired candidates?
  * What data is included in the payload for each hired candidate?
    * Sample payload
  * Is it possible to exclude offices, departments, jobs, or candidates from HRIS Link for hired candidates?
  * How do I import a hired candidate payload to my preferred HRIS?



#### How does HRIS Link export hired candidates?

When a candidate is marked as hired in Greenhouse Recruiting, HRIS Link will export a JSON or XML payload to the [SFTP server or S3 bucket you choose](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/11758489369755).

#### What data is included in the payload for each hired candidate?

HRIS Link will export the following details for each candidate who is marked as hired in Greenhouse Recruiting:

**Application details** | [Source](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/216902526)  
---|---  
[Referrer](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/201982560)  
[Custom application fields](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/115003544472)  
Application ID  
Resume and attachments  
Take home test  
**Candidate details** |  Candidate profile URL  
First name  
Last name  
Current job title  
[Private](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360039936051) (True or false)  
[Recruiter](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360016347712)  
[Coordinator](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360016347752)  
Can email? (Yes or no)  
Email address  
Phone number  
Mailing address  
Education  
Employment  
[Custom candidate fields](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/202609675)  
[Linked Greenhouse Recruiting user](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360020922752)  
Candidate ID  
**Job details** |  Job name  
Job open and close dates  
[Requisition ID](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360061697231)  
Office, office location and office ID  
Department and department ID  
[Custom job fields](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/202609855)  
**Offer details** |  Offer ID  
Offer creation and resolution dates  
Start date  
[Custom offer fields](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360024551831)  
Offer letter  
**Opening details** |  Opening ID  
[Opening](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360037953951) open and close dates  
Target start date  
[Custom opening fields](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360036370951)

# Text-Em-All integration

Text-Em-All is an effective phone broadcasting service that provides the option to send automated phone calls, text messages, and surveys on demand.

Greenhouse Recruiting's integration with Text-Em-All allows you to send broadcasts to your Greenhouse Recruiting contacts and candidates, all from within your Text-Em-All account.

#### In this article

  * Set up the Text-Em-All integration
    * Create a Harvest API key
    * Provide your API key to Text-Em-All and complete setup 
  * Use the Text-Em-All integration with Greenhouse Recruiting
    * Send a broadcast to candidates
    * Review results
    * Opt-in consent for Application-to-Person (A2P) messaging
  * Additional resources



### Set up the Text-Em-All integration 

#### Create a Harvest API key

To configure the Greenhouse Recruiting / Text-Em-All integration, you'll need to create a Harvest API key.

Follow the steps in [this article](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/5888163769883) to create the key, and verify that the credentials and permissions below are selected when configuring the Text-Em-All integration.

#### Credentials

In the _Create New Credential_ box, make the following selections:

  * **API type:** Harvest
  * **Partner:** Text-Em-All
  * **Description:** Text-Em-All Harvest API key



#### Permissions

Verify that the following permissions are selected for the Text-Em-All integration:

**Activity Feed**

  * All permissions



**Candidates**

  * GET: Retrieve Candidate
  * GET: List Candidates
  * POST: Add Candidate
  * POST: Add Note
  * POST: Add Attachment
  * POST: Add Attachment
  * POST: Add Attachment
  * POST: Add Employment
  * POST: Add E-mail



**Jobs**

  * GET: List Jobs
  * POST: Create a new job



**Users**

  * GET: List Users



When finished, click **Save**.

Your Harvest API key for the Greenhouse Recruiting / Text-Em-All integration is created and configured. Copy the Harvest API key to provide to Text-Em-All in the next step.

#### Provide your API key to Text-Em-All and complete setup 

Once you have the Harvest API key, log into your **Text-Em-All** account.

Then, navigate to your **S****ettings** and click **Integrations**.

From the _Integrations_ page, find Greenhouse and click **Connect**.

Using the pop-up window, enter your **Greenhouse User email** and your **Harvest API key**.

Click **Connect Me** to complete the connection.

### Use the Text-Em-All integration with Greenhouse Recruiting

#### Send a broadcast to candidates

To send a message to your candidates, **log into** your Text-Em-All account and click **Create Broadcast**.

Follow the steps as you normally would to create a Broadcast, and select **Greenhouse** as the designation.

Next, search for any **candidates** you have in Greenhouse Recruiting. You can search by any of the displayed criteria, including tags, if you need to find a custom list of people you tagged in Greenhouse Recruiting.

**Note** : Tags are a good way of saving searches in Greenhouse Recruiting and finding those searches in Text-Em-All to message a list of candidates simultaneously. To learn more about tagging candidates in Greenhouse Recruiting, click [here](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360027904392).

Once you find the contacts you wish to message, simply **add** them to your broadcast and continue.

#### Review results

Once your Broadcast goes out, Text-Em-All sends the results to Greenhouse Recruiting so you can easily see what happened when your message went out.

To view these results, navigate to the **candidate profile** and review their **Activity feed** where Text-Em-All posts the results.

You can also view the Broadcast details in their entirety in your Text-Em-All account.

#### Opt-in consent for Application-to-Person (A2P) messaging

Application-to-Person (A2P) messaging allows organizations to send messages to standard 10-digit long code (10DLC) phone numbers.

New texting regulations for A2P 10DLC require candidates expressly opt-in when applying for jobs in order to receive A2P communications. If a candidate opts-out, these messages will be blocked.

To obtain this opt-in consent in Greenhouse Recruiting, [create a custom application question](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360025222851) using Yes/No as the configured answer type and then, apply this question to your job posts in bulk. Once created, you can then [report on candidate application responses](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360001114992) to locate the consent status. 

To learn more on working with A2P 10DLC regulations in Greenhouse Recruiting, reach your Customer Success manager or [open a ticket](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/requests/new) with Greenhouse Technical Support.

### Additional resources

For additional information or troubleshooting not covered here, reach out to [support@text-em-all.com](mailto:support@text-em-all.com).

# Google Apps for SSO

**Permissions:** Basic users and above who can manage and configure SSO

**Product tier:** Available for new subscription tiers (Core, Plus, and Pro)

If your organization manages user access through Google Apps, you can easily set up Single Sign-On (SSO) to allow your users to log into Greenhouse Recruiting or Greenhouse Onboarding using their employee Google account.

**Note:** [Click here](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/210259723) for more information on Single Sign-On.

Once SSO is enabled, all users must log in through Google Apps and won't be able to use their previous username and password.

Logging in through Google Apps only changes the way a user logs in to Greenhouse Recruiting or Greenhouse Onboarding and doesn't change anything else associated with their account. In other words, if a user has an existing Greenhouse Recruiting or Greenhouse Onboarding account, they'll still be able to access their jobs, candidates, interviews, onboarding tasks, and other data as normal.

**Note:** If a new user has a Google Apps account, but not a Greenhouse Recruiting account, Greenhouse Recruiting will automatically create a Greenhouse user account the first time they sign in using Google Apps. By default, this account will be assigned Basic permissions. Site Admins can update these permissions on the **Configure** page.

#### In this article

  * Set up SSO for Greenhouse Recruiting
  * Set up SSO for Greenhouse Onboarding



### Set up SSO for Greenhouse Recruiting

**Note:** This process is based on Google's standard SSO setup steps, outlined [here](https://support.google.com/a/answer/6363766?hl=en.).

Log into Greenhouse Recruiting and copy your **SSO Assertion Consumer URL** in the Dev Center. _(**Configure** > **Dev Center** > **Single Sign-On** > **SSO Assertion Consumer URL**)_

In another tab, sign in to your Google Admin console and navigate to the _Web and mobile apps_ page. _(**Home** > **Apps** > **Web and mobile apps**)_

Click **Add app** at the top of the page and select **Add custom SAML app**.

Enter the **App name** and click **Continue**. If needed, you can enter an optional description and app icon on this page.

Enter the following information on the _Service Provider Details_ page:

  * **Entity ID:** greenhouse.io
  * **Assertion Consumer Service (ACS) URL:** The ACS URL previously copied from Greenhouse Recruiting
  * **Name ID format:** EMAIL
  * **Name ID:** Basic Information > Primary email



Map the following information on the _Attributes_ page and click **Finish**. The text must exactly match the text below (including capitalization) in order for the integration to work correctly

**Basic information** | **App attributes**  
---|---  
First name | User.FirstName  
Last name | User.LastName  
Primary email | NameID  
  
Select **Download Metadata** on the saved tile. 

Navigate back to the Dev Center in Greenhouse Recruiting and finish the Single Sign-On setup outlined in [this article](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360040753811).

Once you're finished, take the following steps:

  * Grant users access to Greenhouse Recruiting in your Google Admin Console under **User Access**  

  * Finish setup in Greenhouse Recruiting by completing the remaining fields in the Dev Center _(**Configure** > **Dev Center** > **Single Sign-On**)_
  * Finish overall SSO setup and move your integration to a hard-enabled state by following the steps in [this document](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360040753811)



**Note:** For troubleshooting guidance for common SAML errors, [click here](https://support.google.com/a/answer/6301076?hl=en).

### Set up SSO for Greenhouse Onboarding

#### Add Greenhouse Onboarding to Google Apps

Sign in to your Google Admin console and navigate to the _Web and mobile apps_ page. (**Home** > **Apps** > **Web and mobile apps**)

Click **Add app** at the top of the page and select **Add custom SAML app**.

Enter the **App name** and click **Continue**. If needed, you can enter an optional description and app icon on this page.

**Note:** We recommend using "Greenhouse Onboarding" for your app name.

Enter the following information on the _Service Provider Details_ page:

  * **Entity ID:**[app.parklet.co](http://app.parklet.co)
  * **Assertion Consumer Service (ACS) URL:** https://onboarding.greenhouse.io/saml/{Greenhouse Onboarding UID}/consume
  * **Name ID format:** EMAIL
  * **Name ID:** Basic Information > Primary email



**Note:** Owners can retrieve your organization's Entity ID and ACS URL directly in Greenhouse Onboarding. 

Navigate to **Settings** > **Data Flow** > **Single Sign-On** , then copy the values from the **SSO Assertion Consumer Service (ACS) URL** and **Entity ID/Issuer** fields.

Map the following information on the _Attributes_ page and click **Finish**. The text must exactly match the text below (including capitalization) in order for the integration to work correctly

**Basic information** | **App attributes**  
---|---  
First name | User.FirstName  
Last name | User.LastName  
Primary email | NameID  
  
Select **Download Metadata** on the saved tile. You'll use this metadata to complete setup in the next step.

#### Finish SAML configuration in Greenhouse Onboarding

Next, you'll finish SAML configuration directly in Greenhouse Onboarding.

Open Greenhouse Onboarding, then navigate to **Settings** >**Data Flow** >**Single Sign-On**.

On the  _Single Sign-On_ page, fill out the following fields with credentials from your Google metadata file:

  * Single Sign-On URL
  * Single Logout URL (optional)
  * IdP Certificate Fingerprint (SHA1 format)



Click **Save**.

Once you've saved your SSO information, [reach out to Greenhouse Technical Support](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/8921763177115) to finish setup and turn on your SAML configuration.

After you've finished setup in Greenhouse Onboarding, you'll need to grant users access to Greenhouse Onboarding in your Google Admin Console under **User Access**.

**Note:** For troubleshooting guidance for common SAML errors, [click here](https://support.google.com/a/answer/6301076?hl=en).

# Why can't I view private or hired candidates? 

Only users with the [permission](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360021050791) **Can create and view private candidates/prospects** can access a candidate profile marked as private.

**Example:** To limit user access to sensitive data, many organizations mark candidate profiles as private once those candidates are hired.

If you need to access private candidate profiles, contact your [In-House Contacts](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360021238012) to update your account. The permissions adjustment required will depend on your user type:

**Site Admins** : A Site Admin user requires the user-specific permission **Can create and view private candidates.**

**Note:** This permission gives the user access to view all private candidates for all jobs in your organization.

**Job Admins** : A Job Admin user must be assigned to the candidate's job with a [Job Admin level](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360039518131) that includes the permission **Can create and view private candidates**.

**Note:** This permission gives the user access to view all candidates marked as private on that job.

# Send (non-offer) documents to candidates in an Interview Plan

Sometimes, a candidate will need to sign a document before their offer stage and have the document attached to their profile in Greenhouse Recruiting.

To send non-offer documents through Greenhouse Recruiting, you can add the **Document Submission** stage to an Interview Plan. When a candidate enters the stage, an email containing an upload link can be sent so candidates can upload their signed files when they're finished. 

**Notes:**

  * To automate document submission email requests being sent, you can create a stage transition rule. To learn more, [click here.](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360053129752)
  * The Document Submission stage does not have any e-signature capabilities. However, you can use this stage to send candidates a needed document and provides them with a way to upload a completed file.
  * This stage should only be used for documents not related to a candidate's offer. [Click here](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/200485589) for more information on sending offer packets.

# MegaHR integration

Mega HR for Greenhouse adds our conversational AI hiring assistant, Megan, to your hiring process to help you save hundreds of hours managing your recruiting and hiring processes. Let her scour through your historical candidates to find the best fits for a new role and reach out to them to see if they’re interested and update their resumes. Integrate her into your hiring workflow to screen out pesky AI applicants, or short list the best fit. Or schedule interviews and take notes, even get approval for background checks and kick them off. You’ll also love that Megan is fully bi-directional! Stage changes, resume updates, feedback, interviewers, are all synced back into Greenhouse in real-time!

#### In this article

  * Create a Harvest API key
  * Configuring webhooks
  * Adding Megan (AI Agent) to Greenhouse
  * Use the integration
  * What Megan will Sync back to Greenhouse
  * Additional resources



### Create a Harvest API key

To configure the integration, you’ll need to create a Harvest API key.

Follow the steps in [this article](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/5888163769883) to create the key, and verify that the permissions below are selected when configuring the Mega HR integration.

#### Credentials

In the _Create New Credential_ box, make the following selections:

  * **API Type:** Harvest
  * **Partner:** Mega HR or Unlisted Vendor
  * **Description:** Mega HR Harvest API Key



Once your API key is created, be sure to share it with your Mega HR account manager. 💡 **If you don’t yet have a Mega HR account manager, just email** [**partner-support@mega.hr**](mailto:partner-support@mega.hr)**.**

#### Permissions

Verify that the following permissions are selected for the Mega HR integration

  * **Activity Feed**
    * Get: Retrieve Activity Feed


  * **Applications**
    * Get: Retrieve Application
    * Get: List Applications
    * Post: Advance Application
    * Post: Add Attachment to Application
    * Post: Move Application
    * Post: Reject Application
    * Post: Moves Application to Job
    * Post: Unreject Application


  * **Candidates**
    * Get: Retrieve Candidate
    * Get: List Candidates
    * Patch: Edit Candidate
    * Post: Add Note
    * Post: Add Attachment


  * **Departments**
    * Get: Retrieve Department
    * Get: List Departments​​
  * **Job Openings**
    * Get: List Openings For a Job


  * **Job Posts**
    * Get: List Job Posts
    * Get: Retrieve Job Post for Job
    * Get: List Job Posts for Job


  * **Jobs**
    * Get: Retrieve Job
    * Get: List Jobs
    * Get: Get hiring team


  * **Job Stages**
    * Get: List Job Stages for Job
    * Get: Retrieve Job Stage
    * Get: List Job Stages


  * **Offices**
    * Get: Retrieve Office
    * Get: List Offices


  * **Rejection Reasons**
    * Get: List Rejection Reasons
  * **Scheduled Interviews**


  * Post: Create a scheduled interview
  * Delete: Delete a scheduled interview
  * Patch: Update a scheduled interview


  * **Scorecards**
    * Get: Retrieve Application's Scorecard
    * Get: List Scorecards for Application


  * **User Roles**
    * Get: List User Roles


  * **Users**
    * Get: Retrieve User
    * Get: List Users
    * Get: List User Job Permissions
    * Patch: Enable User (SSO only)
    * Patch: Update User (SSO only)



### Configure webhooks

Webhooks allow changes from Greenhouse to update inside Mega HR instantly.

Follow the steps in [this article](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360005574531-Create-a-webhook) to create the necessary webhooks and keep your Mega HR integration in sync with Greenhouse. 💡 Each webhook will require an **Error Email Address** we recommend you use [partner-support@mega.hr](mailto:partner-support@mega.hr).

Verify that the following webhooks are configured for the Mega HR integration.

  * **Name** : A descriptive name for each webhook event. Most customers choose _‘Mega HR integration’_
  * You will use the same endpoint URL for each webhook but the **{COMPANYID}** needs to be replaced with the correct value. **This will be provided by your account manager.**
  * **Webhook Endpoint URL:**[https://integrations.mega.hr/v1/api/integrations/greenhouse/webhook/**{COMPANYID}**](https://integrations.mega.hr/v1/api/integrations/greenhouse/webhook/%7BCOMPANYID%7D)



Add the above Endpoint URL to the following Webhooks:

  * **Job Post Created**
  * **Job Post Updated**
  * **Job Created**
  * **Job Updated**
  * **Prospect Created**
  * **Applicant Updated**
  * **Candidate Applied**
  * **Candidate Updated**
  * **Candidate Deleted**
  * **Candidate Rejected**
  * **Candidate Unrejected**
  * **Candidate Stage Changed**



### Add Megan (AI Agent) to Greenhouse

What Megan (AI hiring assistant) has access to manage in Greenhouse is controlled by what jobs she is added as a Hiring Manager on.

Follow the steps in[ this article](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360027077811-Add-new-users) to invite [megan+COMPANYNAME@mega.hr](mailto:megan@mega.hr) to Greenhouse as a Job Admin.

**Note:** COMPANYNAME should be replaced with the full name of your company without any spaces. For example, for a company named Acme Corp, you could use [megan+acmecorp@mega.hr](mailto:megan+acmecorp@mega.hr). _If you have any questions on this, please contact your Mega HR Account Manager or email_[partner-support@mega.hr](mailto:partner-support@mega.hr) _._

You may choose to add her to all jobs, or select them individually but Megan **must be added as a Hiring Manager**.

Once the following steps have been completed, it’s time to Activate the Mega HR integration:

  * API key created and shared with your Mega HR account manager
  * Required Webhooks configured
  * Megan has been added to one or more jobs as a Hiring Manager



Your Mega HR account manager then initiates a sync with your Greenhouse company. Once that completes (1 min - 1 hour depending on how much data) you’re ready to go! 🚀

### Use the integration

  1. **Logging In** Now that your Mega HR integration has been activated you’re ready to login! Login here: <https://app.mega.hr/login>
  2. **The basics** We recommend you watch this [quick 90 second intro video](https://www.loom.com/share/7bc2d6e7360e4bb6be123481104df8df). Once you login you’ll land on the Home screen. If you’re a non-Greenhouse Admin, here you’ll see all the jobs you and Megan are Hiring Managers on. If you’re a Greenhouse Admin, you’ll see all the jobs Megan has access to.



On the right you'll see your Megan conversations. This is where you interact with Megan in natural language. Just click “New Conversation” to chat with her. Megan has access to many of the same candidate management features you have in Greenhouse and she can use those as tools to get work done for you. When she’s doing work for you, she’ll create a task. Those tasks will be linked inside the conversation as well as on the Home screen in the “AI Work History” section.

You’ll see a ✅ for tasks that are complete and a little spinner for those in progress. You can also click on them to get more detail.

  3. **Conversing with Megan** Megan is extremely powerful conversationally. Sure, she can handle quick tasks like telling you about applicant volume over the weekend or scheduling a meeting for you. But she’s also great at much more complex & time consuming tasks. Here’s an example of something she could take care of for you: “Hey Megan, would you please get a list of the top 50 candidates we have in the system who may be a good fit for this new Finance Manager job we have? Once you have the list, email them and see if they may be interested. If they are, ask them for an updated resume and add them to the Finance Manager job for me.” Yes, she’s pretty powerful. 💪🏼
  4. **Configuring Megan as part of a Job Workflow**



One of the other great timesavers is integrating Megan as part of your Job workflow. Here we have a Greenhouse Job along with all of the stages we have configured.

With Mega, each Stage in your Pipeline can be configured with AI automation, triggered when the applicant enters that stage. You configure those automations by hovering over the stage and clicking the gear icon in the top right of each stage. To continue with this, here we have the Application Review stage; the stage new applicants automatically enter after they’ve applied to a job. One common task would be to have her score applicants, share feedback and optionally advance or disqualify them.

Yes, all of that is configurable but you can do quite a bit more.

Maybe it’s important that each candidate has some particular skill that may not be 100% clear on their application. Well, that’s easy, just ask her (in natural language), to reach out to any applicants who look good, but she’s unsure if they have that important skill before completing her assessment. This is just one example of many ways you can inject Megan into your hiring process. Megan can schedule meetings, attend those meetings and take notes, get candidate consent to kick off background checks and so, so much more!

### What Megan will sync back to Greenhouse

Megan does a lot for you and she tries her best to make sure everything she does is synchronized back into Greenhouse.

Here we’ll cover what those things are:

**Candidate profile updates:**

  * Candidate profile updates, such as updated resumes



**Candidate notes:**

  * Feedback on candidates
  * Justifications for screening actions (advancing or disqualifying)
  * Interview summaries for meetings she’s been asked to attend:
    * Overview of questions asked & responses
    * General interview summary
    * Actions items/Takeaways
  * Clarity around why she did something when it was at the direction of another user.



**Candidate stage progression:**

  * When Megan moves a candidate to another stage
  * When a candidate is Hired or Rejected



**Copy Applicant to another job:**

  * When Megan copies a candidate to another job at the request of a user



**Interviews:**

  * When an interview is scheduled based on an Interview template that interview will be added to the candidate with the relevant details.
  * If an interview is scheduled in an adhoc fashion (e.g. outside the scope of an interview template), details around that meeting will be shared as a note on the candidate.
  * Cancelled interviews Megan is managing



**Interview Recordings:**

  * When Megan attends an interview she’s scheduled she will takes notes and share that feedback with the team in Greenhouse including the questions/responses, summary of the meeting, her assessment and any actionable items.
  * The video recording will be uploaded and added as an attached file marked “Private”.



**General updates:**

  * Megan will provide general status updates around things she’s doing through Candidate notes. e.g when she’s working to schedule a meeting.
  * If her conversation with a candidate leads to a question she can’t answer, she’ll escalate to the team.



### Additional resources

For additional information or troubleshooting not covered here, reach out to [partner-support@mega.hr](mailto:partner-support@mega.hr).

Also feel free to check out our [Greenhouse Integration Help Center](https://intercom.help/mega-hr/en/collections/14953968-greenhouse).

# JDP integration

JDP’s bi-directional integration with Greenhouse Recruiting allows you to easily initiate a pre-employment background check on candidates directly within Greenhouse with just a few clicks.

Once a background check is initiated, information entered into Greenhouse is pre-populated in the background check form. Then, an email is sent to the candidate to obtain any additional information and the consent to perform the background check.

With seamless access and an interactive workflow for managing background screening requirements, the solution offers a fast, simple, and intuitive user and applicant experience, allowing you to increase workforce productivity, reduce time-to-hire, and get more, high-quality hires.

#### In this article

  * Set up the JDP integration
    * Create a Harvest API key
    * Additional configuration to complete setup
  * Use the JDP integration
    * Add the JDP assessment to your interview plan
    * Create an integration service user (ISU)
    * Provide your credentials to JDP
  * Additional resources



### Set up the JDP integration

#### Create a Harvest API key

To configure the JDP integration, you’ll need to create a Harvest API key.

Follow the steps in [this article](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/5888163769883) to create the key, and verify that the permissions below are selected when configuring the JDP integration.

#### Credentials

In the _Create New Credential_ box, make the following selections:

  * **API Type:** Harvest
  * **Partner:** JDP or Unlisted Vendor
  * **Description:** JDP Harvest API Key



#### Permissions

Verify that the following permissions are selected for the JDP integration: 

**Applications**

  * GET: Retrieve Application
  * GET: List Applications
  * PATCH: Update Application
  * POST: Advance Application
  * POST: Move Application
  * POST: Reject Application



**Candidates**

  * GET: Retrieve Candidate
  * GET: List Candidates
  * PATCH: Edit Candidate
  * POST: Add Note



**Tags**

  * DELETE: Remove tag from Candidate
  * GET: List tags applied to Candidate
  * GET: List Candidate Tags
  * POST: Add New Candidate Tags
  * PUT: Add a candidate tag
  * DELETE: Remove Candidate Tags



**Custom Fields**

  * GET: Get custom fields



**Job Stages**

  * GET: Retrieve Job Stages
  * GET: List Job Stages
  * GET: List Job Stages for Job



**Jobs**

  * GET: Retrieve Job
  * GET: List Jobs



**Users**

  * GET: List Users



When finished, click **Save**.

Your Harvest API key for the Greenhouse Recruiting / JDP is configured. Copy your key to provide to JDP in a later step. 

#### Additional configuration to complete setup

**Create custom Job fields**

Next, in order to use the JDP integration, you'll need to [create three custom Job fields](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/202609855) in Greenhouse Recruiting.

To create these fields, navigate to **Configure** > **Custom** **Options** >**Jobs** and then, click **Add field**. Enter the following details to configure the new fields:

**Custom job field #1**

  * **Name** : _Background Check Package Name_
  * **Type** : Single Select
  * **Options** : Enter all the package names JDP has configured for your company.
  * Select both **Mark private** and **Required** check boxes



**Save** when finished.

Once done, an  _Immutable field key_ will be generated. You will need to provide this key to JDP.

**Custom job field #2**

You will now need to create a second custom job field to represent sub client names; this is optional and only created if the client has a parent and child accounts; similar to the other custom job field, follow these steps:

  * **Name** :, enter **Child Client Name**
  * **Type** : Single Select
  * **Options:** Enter either the name or code for all your accounts – do not mix names and codes – choose only one approach
  * Select the **Mark private** check box



**Save** when finished.

Once done, an  _Immutable field key_ will be generated. You will need to provide this key to JDP.

**Custom field option #3**

Last custom job field to create is the **Requestor Name** field.

  * **Field Name:** Job Order Requestors
  * **Type** : Single Select
  * **Options:** Enter the names of all users who will be submitting orders 
    * Format as _LastName, FirstName_
  * Select the **Mark private** check box



**Save** when finished.

Once done, an  _Immutable field key_ will be generated. You will need to provide this key to JDP.

To learn more about creating custom job fields, check out [this guide](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/202609855). 

### Use the JDP integration with Greenhouse Recruiting

#### Add the JDP assessment to your interview plan

After enabling the JDP integration, you'll need to add the 5 JDP Background check stages to your [job's interview plan](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/115002194903) to facilitate the background check ordering process. The 5 stages will need to be named exactly as shown.

**Note** : If your company utilizes [job templates](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360038222812) for creating new jobs, you'll want to update the template to include the JDP stages.

The **Background Check Package Name** field appears for the user to select a package from the list of choices we had created previously.

Now that the user is in the Interview plan section, click on the **Add Stage** button.

**Create** a new stage named _Background Check Requested_ and then, click **Add**. 

Repeat the above process to create the additional stages:

  * Background Check In-Process
  * Background Check Completed
  * Background Check Canceled
  * Background Check Error



#### Create an integration service user (ISU)

In order to send information from JDP to Greenhouse Recruiting using the Harvest API, JDP will need a [Greenhouse Recruiting user ID](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/4405511253659) to associate with the data. This user account must be a Site Admin, but does not require any additional user-specific permissions. Use the steps listed below to create a new user for this integration:

Click the **Configure** icon and then, select the _Users_ tab. Click **+New Users** and enter the email address for the API User; this user is purely for connection between Greenhouse and JDP. Provide this email address to JDP when created.

Select the **Assign** button for the **Site Admin** and enable all permissions that display.

**Save** when finished. 

#### Provide your credentials to JDP 

At this point, the JDP integration team will need to configure the integration within your JDP account. Please provide the following to your JDP implementation team contact(s):

  * Immutable Field Key(s)
  * ISU user email address
  * API Key



Send the above information to: [greenhouseintegrations@jdp.com](mailto:greenhouseintegrations@jdp.com).

Before moving on to finalize the set-up process, the JDP integration team will provide the following: 

  * Endpoint URL
  * Secret Key



Provide this information to your Greenhouse account executive and/or your Greenhouse implementation resource.

### Additional resources

For additional information or troubleshooting not covered here, reach out to[integrationsupport@jdp.com](mailto:integrationsupport@jdp.com).

# Redesign overview

**Permissions:** —

**Product tier:** Available for new subscription tiers (Core, Plus, and Pro)

The Greenhouse redesign simplifies how you interact with our applications by creating a consistent experience, guiding your organization with hiring best practices and accounting for the needs of all user types through [AA accessible standards](https://www.w3.org/WAI/fundamentals/accessibility-intro/).

With our new design, you can move through workflows more confidently and efficiently while accessing the most important content first.

Keep reading for details on the specific changes you can expect to see in your Greenhouse account and check out our [blog post](https://www.greenhouse.io/blog/greenhouse-app-redesign-to-improve-customer-experience) for more information on our design strategy.

#### In this article

  * New design
  * New navigation
    * Major changes
    * Other changes
  * Upcoming changes
  * Additional resources



### New design

We updated the look of Greenhouse Recruiting and Greenhouse Onboarding to reflect our brand better. Some of these changes include a new color palette, added white space and refreshed buttons.

We redesigned the buttons in the top right corner of the page, including replacing your name with your initials. You can continue to click on your initials to open a dropdown menu of account options.

### New navigation

We improved the naming and navigation of pages to make your workflows more consistent and organized.

After looking at the way people use Greenhouse Recruiting, we've simplified the navigation bar at the top of your page to show pages that our users access most. We've taken the lesser-used pages and moved them elsewhere in the application. See the bullet points below for more information on specific changes.

#### Major changes

  * **A new way to toggle between your accounts** : Click the dropdown arrow next to the logo in the top left corner to switch between Greenhouse Recruiting and Greenhouse Onboarding.  
  


Because of the new toggle, we removed the link to Greenhouse Onboarding from the dropdown under your initials.
  * **Easier access to your dashboard:** Clicking the Greenhouse logo now brings you back to your dashboard, which means we could remove it from the top navigation bar.
  * **Simpler navigation:** We removed the ellipses icon  and dropdown menu from the primary navigation bar and moved the dropdown links to new, more intuitive locations. 
    * We moved**CRM** , **Reports** and **Integrations** to the primary navigation bar.  
  


    * We removed the **Sourcing** overview page. You can continue to access Sourcing from each job by going to the **Job Dashboard** > **Sourcing**.
    * You can continue to access the _Approvals_ page by going to the _My Approvals_ section on the right side of the _My Dashboard_ page.  
  

    * We moved **Inclusion** to **Configure** > **Inclusion Tools**.
  * **Fewer button clicks to see internal jobs:** We removed the**Internal Job Board** from the dropdown under your initials. You can continue to access it from the _Helpful Links_ section on the right side of the _My Dashboard_ page.  
  





#### Other changes

  * **New account dropdown:** We replaced your name with your initials in the dropdown under your initials.
  * **Relocated job dashboard navigation:** We moved the _Job Dashboard_ navigation bar from the top of the page to the left side of the page.  
  




  * **More specific page names:** To reflect the features that have been added over the years, we've updated the name of the _Job Boards_ page to _Job Boards & Posts_.
  * **A new home for agencies:** We moved **Agencies** from the **Ellipses icon** > **Sourcing** > **Agencies** to **Configure** > **Agencies**.



### Upcoming changes

You might notice some areas of our application that haven't been updated with our new design. Our team is working on them! Stay tuned for information about the following features:

  * Mobile app



### Additional resources

For more information on why we made these changes, remember to read our [blog post](https://www.greenhouse.io/blog/greenhouse-app-redesign-to-improve-customer-experience)! For any other questions, please contact Technical Support.

# Cruit integration

Cruit is the job referral platform that turns employees and communities into the number one source of applicants. With the Cruit app, people can share jobs, track their referrals, and earn amazing rewards.

Cruit's integration with Greenhouse Recruiting allows many actions in Cruit to be automated without changing your existing workflows:

  * **Sync data from Greenhouse Recruiting** : The integration enables you to load job data directly from Greenhouse Recruiting to Cruit. You can easily manage your referable jobs in the Cruit dashboard, control which jobs should be referable, and edit other info such as rewards per interview stage, public referral rewards, and more.
  * **Referral status** : The integration allows your employees or public Cruiters to see the latest status of their referred candidates if those candidates have opted into showing this data, and allows you to create referrals based on past applications in Greenhouse Recruiting.



#### In this article

  * Set up the integration
    * Create a Harvest API key
    * Enable on Cruit
    * Create a custom source
  * Use the integration
  * Additional resources



### Set up the integration

#### Create a Harvest API key

First, create a Harvest API key in Greenhouse Recruiting. Follow the steps in [this article](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/5888163769883) to create the key, and copy the API key as you will need to enter it into Cruit in the next step. Verify that the permissions below are selected when configuring the API key:

In the _Create New Credential_ box, make the following selections:

  * **API type:** Harvest
  * **Partner:** Cruit or Unlisted Vendor
  * **Description** : Cruit Harvest API Key



Verify that the following permissions are selected for the Cruit integration:

**Job** **openings**

  * GET: List openings for a job



**Departments**

  * GET: List departments
  * GET: Retrieve department



**Users**

  * GET: List users
  * GET: Retrieve user



**Applications**

  * PATCH: Update application
  * POST: Advance application
  * POST: Add attachment to application
  * GET: Retrieve application
  * GET: List applications
  * PATCH: Update a rejected application's rejection reason



**Jobs**

  * GET: Get hiring team
  * GET: List jobs
  * GET: Retrieve job



**Candidates**

  * POST: Add note
  * POST: Add application
  * GET: List candidates
  * POST: Add candidate
  * POST: Add e-mail
  * PATCH: Edit candidate
  * GET: Retrieve candidate
  * POST: Add attachment



**Job posts**

  * GET: Retrieve job post for job
  * GET: List job posts for job
  * GET: List job posts



**Job** **stages**

  * GET: Retrieve job stage
  * GET: List job stages for job
  * GET: List job stages



**Offices**

  * GET: Retrieve office
  * GET: List offices



**Offers**

  * GET: List offers
  * GET: Retrieve offer
  * GET: Retrieve application's current offer
  * GET: List application's offers



**Tags**

  * PUT: Add a candidate tag
  * GET: List candidate tags
  * POST: Add new candidate tags
  * GET: List tags applied to candidate



**Sources**

  * GET: List sources



Copy your Harvest API key to a secure location for use in the next step.

#### Enable on Cruit

Next, [log into](https://cruit-backend-backup.herokuapp.com/api/v1/oauth/authenticate?response_type=code&client_id=1234567890&client_secret=secret&redirect_uri=https://cruit.work/auth/callback&state=1234567890&scope=read) your Cruit admin account. Click your profile icon at the top-right, then click **Settings**.

Click **ATS** on the left, then find _Connect with your ATS_.

Enter your Greenhouse Recruiting Harvest API key.

Next, enter a user ID for authenticating the integration. We recommend [creating an ISU](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/4405511253659) specifically for the integraiton, or using a key stakeholder your organization's referral program, such as the head of acquisition. You can learn more about finding Greenhouse Recruiting [user IDs here](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/10765948752027).

Enter the user ID and click **Update**.

Once complete, you can navigate to **Jobs** , and see all the available jobs loaded in directly from Greenhouse Recruiting to make referable.

#### Create a custom source

Finally, to optimize the quality of your experience with Cruit, create two custom sources in Greenhouse Recruiting. Follow the instructions [in this article](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/200721664) to create the custom sources, using the details below:

**Custom source 1**  
---  
**Name** | Cruit In-House  
**Sourcing strategy** | Prospecting  
**Custom source 2**  
---  
**Name** | Cruit Public  
**Sourcing strategy** | Prospecting  
  
These custom sources enable Greenhouse Recruiting to properly source candidates that come from different Cruit platforms. When candidates are assigned a source, you can easily filter and report on those candidates in Greenhouse Recruiting.

**Note** : If you only use one of Cruit's platforms, create a custom source for that platform.

### Use the integration

After enabling the integration, you can see your current open jobs in Cruit by navigating to **Jobs**.

You can manage whether your jobs are referable, and set rewards for each job individually, per hire, or per interview stage for maximum employee engagement.

When you receive candidates via referrals through Cruit, they sync to Greenhouse Recruiting and enter any regular workflows for candidates that you have already set up.

### Additional resources

For additional information or troubleshooting not covered here, use the chat widget in the bottom-right of the Cruit dashboard, or reach out to [steye@cruit.work](mailto:steye@cruit.work).

# Candidate self-scheduling setup

**Permissions: Site** **Admin** , and **Job** **Admin** who can email candidates / prospects

**Product tier:** Available for new subscription tiers (Core, Plus, and Pro)

**Note:** While only **Site** **Admin** , or **Job** **Admin** with the user-specific permission 'can email candidates / prospects,' can send self-schedule requests to candidates, all interviewers (including Basic users) need to complete the steps below to allow candidates to schedule interviews with them.

Candidate self-scheduling is simple to set up so you can benefit from more efficient scheduling in Greenhouse Recruiting.

You'll need to complete these steps before you [send a self-schedule request](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/4409534677915) or allow another user to send one on your behalf.

#### In this article

  * Connect your calendar to your Greenhouse Recruiting account
  * Connect your video conferencing tool
  * Grant access to your calendar
  * Create self-schedule email templates
  * Allow candidates to reschedule



### Connect your calendar to your Greenhouse Recruiting account

Interviewers will need to enable the Google Calendar or Outlook 365 integration to receive self-scheduling requests.

To connect your calendar to your Greenhouse Recruiting account, click **Integrations** on your navigation bar.

On the _Integrations_ page, search for**Google Calendar** or**Office 365** , and select **Connect** to integrate your calendar on Greenhouse Recruiting.

See the topics below for more information:

  * [Enable Google Calendar](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360021799232)
  * [Enable Outlook 365](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/115003943972)



### Connect your video conferencing tool

To automatically add a video conference to self-scheduled interviews, you'll also need to connect your video conferencing tool to your Greenhouse Recruiting account.

To connect your video conferencing tool, click **Integrations** on your navigation bar.

On the Integrations page, search for your preferred video conferencing tool like **Zoom** or **Google** **Meet** , and click **Connect** to connect your video conferencing tool.

For more information on each video scheduling integration, see the following:

  * [Zoom integration](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360042222612)
  * [Google Meet integration](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360058730452)
  * [Microsoft Teams integration](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360058730512)



**Note:** If your organization is using Zoom, this configuration only needs to be completed once for the organization. Google Meet and Microsoft Teams integrations will automatically occur when you connect your calendar.

### Grant access to your calendar

If you want another user to send self-schedule requests for interviews scheduled to **your calendar** on your behalf, you need to first grant that user permission to add and edit events on your calendar. 

To grant access to your calendar, follow the instructions for your calendar provider below. 

  * [Google: Share your calendar with someone](https://support.google.com/calendar/answer/37082?hl=en)
  * [Outlook 365: Share an Outlook calendar with other people](https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/office/share-an-outlook-calendar-with-other-people-353ed2c1-3ec5-449d-8c73-6931a0adab88)



When editing a [stage transition rule](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360053129752) that sends a self-schedule request, existing calendar selections are preserved to protect calendar access and privacy. If you don’t update the calendar field, the original selection will remain unchanged. If you make a change, you’ll select from your own calendar options and become the meeting organizer for the request.

**Note:** This step is only necessary if the interview is being scheduled to your calendar. If the interview is scheduled to a [shared calendar](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/12260890092955-Best-practices-Managing-Hiring-team-absences-#h_01GR74GZD43QKT6T0JM5YE5AXD), for example, the user only needs permission for that shared calendar.

### Create self-schedule email templates

**Note:** This setup can only be completed by **Site** **Admin** , or **Job** **Admin** with permission to email candidates / prospects.

While a default email template for self-scheduling requests is automatically included with your Greenhouse Recruiting account, you can create, modify, or add an attachment to additional self-scheduling request templates to be sent to candidates.

To create a self-schedule email template, click **Configure** from your navigation bar, then select**Email Templates** on the left.

**Note:** Self-schedule email templates must contain the `{{INTERVIEW_REQUEST_LINK}}` token. If the token isn't included, the candidate won't be able to complete a self-schedule request.

[Click here](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/115004020946) for more information on creating email templates.

### Allow candidates to reschedule

To let candidates reschedule self-scheduled interviews, go to **Configure** , then select **Permissions**. Scroll to **Scheduling** , then turn on "Allow candidates to reschedule self-scheduled interviews.

Once enabled, candidates can re-schedule interviews from their meeting invitation or reminder.

**Note:** Candidates can only book interviews scheduled at least 24 hours in advance. To reschedule interviews that are less than 24 hours in the future, candidates must contact their recruiter.
greenhouse-recruiting-glossary:
