# Employee ID login method for SSO

**Permissions: Basic** and above, who can manage SSO configuration

**Product tier:** Available to Pro subscription tier

Greenhouse Recruiting provides your team with the ability to log in via Single Sign-On (SSO). With SSO enabled, your users can access your organization’s Greenhouse Recruiting account through your Identity Provider (IdP) of choice. To learn more about enabling Single Sign-On, please click [here](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360040753811-Configure-Single-Sign-On-in-Greenhouse-Recruiting).

Greenhouse Recruiting uses email address as the default login method, but organizations with an Pro subscription can opt to use employee ID as the login method instead.

#### In this article

  * Employee ID login method requirements 
  * Employee ID login method rules 
  * Use cases for employee ID login method 



### Employee ID login method requirements

The following requirements apply to organizations using employee ID for the login method:

  * Your SSO must be configured to provide an employee ID.
  * The SAML response from your IdP must include an employee ID.



Before hard-enabling your SSO configuration, be sure to confirm the following:

  * All users in your IdP directory have an employee ID value.
  * Your SAML response for the Greenhouse Recruiting application contains the attribute User.EmployeeID.



### Employee ID login method rules

  * If there is not a User.EmployeeID attribute in the SAML response, or if there is no email address in the SAML response, the login attempt will fail.
  * If there is a User.EmployeeID attribute in the SAML response and the value in that attribute matches a user in Greenhouse Recruiting: 
    * If the email address in the SAML response exists in Greenhouse Recruiting on a user with an employee ID that matches the employee ID in the SAML response, the user will be logged into their existing account.
    * If the email address in the SAMLResponse does not exist in Greenhouse Recruiting, the user will be logged into their existing account with a matching employee ID, and the new email address will be added to the user.
    * If the email address in the SAML response matches a user in Greenhouse Recruiting that has a different employee ID than the employee ID in the SAML response, the login attempt will fail with the following error message: _Invalid SAML Response: employee ID does not match e-mail address.  
  
_
  * If there is a User.EmployeeID attribute in the SAML response and the value in that attribute does not match a user in Greenhouse Recruiting: 
    * If the email address in the SAML response also does not exist in Greenhouse Recruiting, a new user will be created with the employee ID and email address from the SAML response.
    * If the email address in the SAML response already exists in Greenhouse Recruiting: 
      * If the email address is on a Greenhouse Recruiting user with no employee ID, the user will be logged into their existing account with a matching email address, and the employee ID will be added to the user
      * If the email address in the SAML response matches a user in Greenhouse Recruiting that has a different employee ID than the employee ID in the SAML response, the login will fail with the error message: _Invalid SAML Response: employee ID does not match e-mail address._



### Use cases for employee ID login method

Organizations with a large number of Greenhouse Recruiting users sometimes prefer this method as a way to simplify user account management when email address changes occur.

**Example:** A user at your organization might change their first or last name and update their email address to reflect the change.  
  
If your organization uses the Email login method, when the user attempts to sign into Greenhouse Recruiting with the new email address, your IdP's SAML response will confirm the email address, but we will not see that email address associated with an existing Greenhouse Recruiting user account. As a result, we will create a new (duplicate) user account for that individual.  
  
If your organization uses the employee ID login method, we will check for the user's employee ID in the SAML response. If we receive an employee ID that is associated with an existing Greenhouse Recruiting user account, we will log the user into that account, as well as associate the updated email address with the existing user account.

# Celential.ai integration

Celential.ai offers a talent sourcing solution that builds strong pipelines of technical and sales candidates, ready to interview with your team.

Powered by AI (with humans in the loop), Celential.ai identifies candidates of the best mutual fit and sends them hyper-personalized outreach emails at scale.

# Identity verification setup

**Permissions:** Site Admin

Greenhouse identity verification helps your team focus on real, qualified candidates by reducing the risk of impersonation, duplicate profiles, and other forms of fraud. Identity verification works in tandem with our partner, CLEAR, to cross-check the information submitted to CLEAR against the candidate’s application.

#### In this article

  * Update permissions
  * GDPR compliance
  * Additional resources



### Enabling CLEAR identity verification requests across your organization

To set up or manage your settings for all Real Talent features, navigate to the Real Talent page and select the **Fraud** tab. _(**Configure** > **Real Talent** > **Fraud**) _

Click **Edit** and follow the instructions on the screen to enable identity verification. Then, choose the offices and departments that are eligible for verifications. 

**Tip:** When implementing identity verification for the first time, begin with a small group of users in a specific office or department to test your settings and workflows before expanding access across the organization.

### Update permissions

All Site Admins can send and view identity verification requests. 

Additionally, job admins can be given permission to update CLEAR verification requests. You can update a [job admin level](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360039518131) to add the following permissions to any Job Admin level:

  * **Can view identity verification requests:** Can view the results of an identity verification request
  * **Can request identity verification details:** Can initiate an identity verification request 



### GDPR compliance

If your organization is subject to GDPR, you can manage compliance through your data retention and candidate packet settings.

To manage the deletion of data, you can add or update a [data retention rule](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360002418112-Configure-a-data-retention-rule) and select identity verification under the _Real Talent_ section. Click **Save** to update the rule. 

To support candidate data access requests, identity verification can be added to [candidate packets](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360000916572).

# MyGreenhouse Dream Job

**Permissions:** Job admins

**Product tier:** Available to all product tiers

Each month, candidates using MyGreenhouse can mark one application as their Dream Job. This creates a strong, reliable signal that your team can use to prioritize candidates who are deeply engaged.

You don’t need to turn on any features to access Dream Job applications. They’re available automatically for organizations and candidates in app review.

#### In this article

  * [Overview](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/28688386131739#h_01JC6TBJTP8VCD2BRC08VRKAYX)
  * What Dream Jobs mean
  * Surfacing Dream Job candidates
  * Candidate Dream Job experience



#### Overview

Dream Job is a first-of-its-kind feature that allows job seekers to mark their application as their top pick, showing hiring teams their motivation for the role. Each month, candidates can mark one role they've applied to as their Dream Job making their application more visible to your recruiting team.

For your team, this signal makes it easier to spot:

  * Candidates who are actively engaged in their job search.
  * Applicants who are specifically enthusiastic about _your_ company and _this_ role.
  * Opportunities to respond faster to highly motivated candidates.



#### What Dream Jobs mean

Dream Jobs are a way for candidates to self-identify that they’re particularly interested in a role. This is different from a generic application. It’s a signal that combines intent, clarity, and focus.

Why it matters:

  * **It’s voluntary:** Candidates choose when and where to use it.

  * **It’s limited:** They can mark only one application per month as their Dream Job.

  * **It’s specific:** They’re telling you this is the role they’re most excited about—right now.




#### Surfacing Dream Job candidates

You can filter for Dream Job applicants during app review. First, go to the job that you're hiring for. Select "Priority candidates." Then you can easily review Dream Job applicants, internal candidates and employee referrals.

#### Candidate Dream Job experience

In MyGreenhouse, candidates can choose their Dream Job from the application itself, or from their task list.

They can select any active application, then click "Mark as Dream Job."

After marking their Dream Job, candidates must wait until the first of the month when Dream Jobs refresh to choose their next one. Dream Jobs can't be canceled or transferred to another role.

# Sourcing Automation campaign pool types

**Permissions:** Job Admins and above with CRM access and a Sourcing Automation seat

**Product tier:** Available for the Plus and Pro subscription tiers

When you [create a new campaign pool](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/5045604930843) in Greenhouse Sourcing Automation, you'll have the option to build one of the following campaign types:

  * **Engage** campaigns
  * **Nurture** campaigns



Use this guide to learn more about these campaign pool types and determine which type will best fit your sourcing needs.

#### In this article

  * Engage campaigns
  * Nurture campaigns
  * Frequently asked questions
  * Additional resources



### Engage campaigns

Use engage campaigns to quickly source and add prospects to active jobs at your organization. Engage campaigns run at a much faster pace than nurture campaigns, with emails delivered frequently to ensure you consistently engage prospects until your job is filled.

### Nurture campaigns

Nurture campaigns are designed to help you stay in front of prospects over a longer period of time, especially when you aren't actively hiring or don't have open jobs. If you have prospects that have shown interest but aren't yet ready to apply for your current jobs, you can also add them to a nurture campaign.

With nurture campaigns, you can also include [featured job post tokens](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/19649645052955) in your campaign messages. This allows you to automatically highlight your organization's featured external job posts, helping nurture prospects by keeping them informed of your latest job openings.

Nurture campaigns keep your brand top-of-mind and ensure your talent pipeline remains warm, with longer wait times between prospect emails.

### Frequently asked questions

#### Which campaign type should I use?

If you're actively looking to fill open roles at your organization, create an **engage campaign** to source and communicate with prospects more frequently.

If you have prospects that are interested, but not currently able to apply for open jobs, create a **nurture campaign** to maintain brand awareness and keep prospects in contact with you.

#### Are campaign messages delivered differently in nurture campaigns?

Yes. In general, engage campaigns run at a much faster pace than nurture campaigns. Wait times between steps are much longer in nurture campaigns, because you'll be reaching out to prospects less frequently than in engage campaigns.

Here's how wait times differ between engage and nurture campaigns:

**Campaign type** | **Minimum wait time, Step 1** | **Minimum wait time, Step 2 and beyond**  
---|---|---  
Engage | 10 minutes | 1 day  
Nurture | 7 days | 30 days  
  
#### Can I highlight my organization's featured job posts in both engage and nurture campaigns?

No, featured job post tokens are available for nurture campaigns only. Learn more about [adding featured job post tokens](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/19649645052955) to your organization's nurture campaigns.

### Additional resources

  * [Create and manage campaign pools](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/5045604930843)

When you're finished, click **Update**.

Your Harvest API key for the Greenhouse Recruiting / IntelliCorp integration is created and configured.

Provide your Harvest API key to your IntelliCorp onboarding team so they can set up the integration. The Harvest API key will be used to auto-populate information in the _Account_ and _Package_ Custom Job Fields you will set up later in the configuration process.

### Create the IntelliCorp web hooks in Greenhouse Recruiting

Click the **Configure** icon  on your navigation bar, and click **Dev Center** on the left. From the _Dev Center_ page, click **Web Hooks**. Click **Web** **Hooks** again.

Enter the following details in the _Create A New Web Hook_ page:

  * **Name:** You can name the webhook whatever makes sense for your organization. We suggest the following names for each webhook:



For test environment:_IntelliCorp Screening – Test_

For production environment:_IntelliCorp Screening Integration_

  * **When:** Candidate has changed stage
  * **Endpoint URL** :



For test environment: <https://stageapi.intellicorp.net/Greenhouse/CreateInvite>

For production environment: [https://api.intellicorp.net/Greenhouse/CreateInvite ](https://api.intellicorp.net/Greenhouse/CreateInvite%20)

  * **Secret Key:** Provided by Intellicorp
  * **Advanced settings**



**Basic Authorization Credentials:** The **username** and **password** provided by Intellicorp

**Note** : You will need to repeat this process twice to create two web hooks: one for your test environment, and one for your production environment.

When you're finished, select **Create Web Hook**.

That's it! Your Greenhouse account and IntelliCorp account can now talk to each other. These settings send data to Intellicorp when a candidate is moved between stages for a job.

### Verify offices are created in Greenhouse Recruiting

IntelliCorp uses the city, state, and country associated with an office to determine the position location, which is used by IntelliCorp for different tasks, including Adverse Action communication.

You will need to have offices defined in Greenhouse Recruiting to send the full information to Intellicorp. These options are selected from a standard list when setting up Greenhouse Recruiting.

Verify that the correct offices are created when setting up this integration.

To learn more about how to add a new office in Greenhouse Recruiting, [click here](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/115002226426).

### Create custom job fields

You will need to create the following two custom job fields to support the IntelliCorp integration:

  * **Account:** IntelliCorp Account
  * **Package:** IntelliCorp Package



After you set up the custom fields, you'll need to add them to each job requisition to send the information to Intellicorp.

To create new custom fields, click the **Configure** icon  on your navigation bar, then click **Custom Options** on the left.

Under the _Company Custom Fields_ section, click **Jobs**.

On the _Manage Job Fields_ page, click **Add Field**.

On the _New Job Field_ page, provide the following details:

  * **Field Name:**_Account_
  * **Type:** Single-select



Click **Save** at the bottom of the page when finished.

Repeat these steps to create a second custom job field using the following details:

  * **Field Name** : _Package_
  * **Type** : Single-select



The selection options for these Custom Job Fields will be added to your Greenhouse Recruiting account by IntelliCorp using the Harvest API key you configured previously.

### Create custom candidate field

The IntelliCorp integration requires one custom candidate field:

  * **Results:** To display IntelliCorp results in real-time on the candidate’s profile, results from multiple searches are displayed in this field



To create the custom candidate field, click the **Configure** icon  on your navigation bar, then click **Custom Options** on the left.

Under the _Company Custom Fields_ section, click **Candidates**.

On the _Manage Candidate Fields_ page, click **Add Field**.

On the _New Candidate Field_ page, provide the following details:

  * **Field Name** : _Results_
  * **Type** : Long textbox



Click **Save** at the bottom of the page when finished.

### Configure job requisitions

To use the IntelliCorp integration, you'll need to configure each job with the appropriate IntelliCorp options.

To configure a requisition, navigate to the Job Info panel (**Job** > **Job Setup** >**Job Info**).

Verify that an office, _Account_ , and _Package_ are selected for the job.

Repeat this process for each job where you intend to submit candidates to IntelliCorp background screening.

### Configure background screening stages

Follow the sections below to incorporate background check stages into your interview plan.

Open the interview plan (**Jobs** > select job > **Job Setup** > **Interview Plan**).

Click **Add Stage** in the top right corner of the page.

Select **Background Check** and click **Add**.

**Note:** If you're using a Secondary Background Check, you can repeat this process with the Intellicorp stage. If the stage doesn't exist, you can create it.

Click and drag the Background Check stage to the right location in your interview plan.

### (Optional) Complete setup for secondary background screenings

Secondary Background Screenings are an optional part of the integration that allows users to order more packages beyond the single one configured on each job.

To integrate secondary background screenings with Greenhouse Recruiting, complete the following steps:

Contact your Intellicorp representative ([support@intellicorp.net](mailto:support@intellicorp.net\))) to request your API key. Once you have received your API key, _[click here](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/requests/new)_ to open a ticket with Greenhouse Technical Support.

**Note** : Do not send the API key in this initial email. Wait until the Greenhouse Technical Support team provides a secure messaging link to send the API key.

Send your API Key to Greenhouse Technical Support using a [SendSafely link](https://www.sendsafely.com/howitworks/). Once sent, Greenhouse Technical Support will be notified of your response. Once the setup is complete, you'll receive an email confirmation from Greenhouse Technical Support.

**Note:** To verify your identity, Greenhouse Technical Support might request you provide a [Support Verification Code](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360022771952) before adding the API key to your organization's account.

### Initiate background screening

During the interview process, when the candidate is moved to the _Background Check_ stage, the candidate receives an email from IntelliCorp to complete their IntelliCorp profile for screening. This email includes consent and authorization steps.

Once the candidate completes their IntelliCorp profile, IntelliCorp automatically updates the custom fields in Greenhouse Recruiting like _Status_ , _Results_ , and _Last Update_. You can see this information on the **Details** tab of the candidate's profile.

### (Optional) Initiate secondary background screenings

When your organization is set up for a secondary background screening and a candidate is moved to the Secondary Background Check stage, the _Status_ and _Search Results_ will appear in the candidate’s _Results_ field. You can click Send Text to start a secondary background check.

Once you started the check, you can choose the specific package from the **Test** dropdown menu.

### Additional resources

For any information or troubleshooting not covered here, reach out to IntelliCorp Support at [support@intellicorp.net](mailto:support@intellicorp.net).

# Troubleshoot the Outlook 365 integration

**Permissions:** Job Admin and above

**Product tier:** Available for new subscription tiers (Core, Plus, and Pro)

Outlook 365 is part of Office 365, a cloud-based subscription service that allows your organization to create, communicate, and collaborate using Microsoft tools. Greenhouse Recruiting's integration with Outlook 365 lets you schedule, update, and delete interviews from calendars where you have the appropriate permissions.

If you're experiencing issues with the integration, a few troubleshooting steps can get you back on track.

#### In this article

  * Unable to set up the integration
  * Unable to send invites
  * Unable to schedule to a specific calendar
  * Unable to schedule to shared calendars
  * Error when scheduling private interviews



### Unable to set up the integration

#### Needs admin approval error

When enabling the Outlook 365 integration, people at organizations with more restrictive security policies might receive a prompt that requires an admin to approve before you can complete setup.

This error is caused when your organization turns off the Microsoft 365 setting that allows users to consent to access company data on their behalf.

To address this error, an Outlook 365 admin will need to set up the integration on their Greenhouse Recruiting account and select **Consent** **on behalf of your organization** on the OAuth2 grant screen.

Afterward, other users at your organization will be allowed to set up their own Outlook 365 integration in Greenhouse Recruiting.

### Unable to send invites

Sometimes you may not see the option to add video conferencing or click **Send invites** on the final scheduling step. This error typically indicates an incorrect setup with your default Greenhouse Recruiting scheduling calendar.

To correct the default scheduling calendar, navigate to a candidate profile that currently requires scheduling.

Click **Schedule** **Interview** on the candidate profile.

On the _Scheduling_ page, click the **Settings** icon at the top-right.

Ensure your _Calendar_ _Type_ is set to Outlook 365, and then your _Calendar_ _Name_ from the drop-down.

Click **Save**.

These settings will dictate the default scheduling calendar to be used when scheduling candidates on Greenhouse Recruiting.

Continue scheduling the candidate as normal.

### Unable to schedule to a specific calendar

When scheduling an interview, you may find that certain time blocks or days on an interviewer's calendar are unavailable. This can happen because of a setting in Outlook 365 that allows users to show their working location on their calendars. If an interviewer's status is set to **Working elsewhere** their calendar will block those days from being scheduled.

To resolve this, the calendar owner should change their status in Outlook 365 to **Free.** After the status is updated, the interview can be scheduled in Greenhouse.

### Unable to schedule to shared calendars

If you're unable to schedule to or see shared calendars or other shared resources, you may need to update some Outlook 365 settings.

To update your shared calendar permissions, log into the [Outlook365 web app](https://outlook.office.com/owa/).

**Note:** This issue can't be fixed on the desktop application.

Next, complete the following steps:

  * The calendar owner should update their sharing permissions to add the shared user.
  * The scheduling user should accept the calendar invitation.



**Note:** Both the calendar owner and the person who needs to schedule using the shared calendar will need to update these settings. To learn more, [click here.](https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/office/share-your-calendar-in-outlook-on-the-web-7ecef8ae-139c-40d9-bae2-a23977ee58d5)

#### Update sharing permissions

The owner of the shared calendar should right-click on the calendar to open the **Sharing Permissions**. For a shared mailbox, a user with access to manage the mailbox’s sharing permissions must open the shared mailbox directly.

The calendar owner should remove the user’s access to the calendar and then re-add the user’s access. The can edit permission is needed to schedule to a calendar via the integration.

#### Accept shared invite

The recipient user who wants to access the calendar in Greenhouse Recruiting must re-accept the shared calendar invitation through the web app.

After completing these steps, the user who accepts the invitation should see the shared calendar in Greenhouse Recruiting when scheduling.

### Error when scheduling private interviews

When scheduling a private interview on a shared Outlook 365 calendar, you may see an error message, or the interview may fail to sync without showing any error.

This happens because Outlook 365 requires a specific permission level (_Delegate access with permission to view private events_) to create private events on shared calendars. If you are not the owner of the shared calendar, you must have this delegate access. Without it, Outlook will prevent the event from being created.

To fix this issue, ask the calendar owner to update your permissions. Once your permissions are updated, try scheduling the private interview again in Greenhouse Recruiting.

**Learn more**

[Outlook 365 integration](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/115003943972)

[Outlook 365 integration security settings](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360049611992)

[Microsoft Teams integration](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360058730512)

# Manager access to employee profiles

**Permissions:** Managers

**Product tier:** Available for Greenhouse Onboarding and Greenhouse Welcome subscription tiers

Users assigned as a manager have access to view and manage their employees' profiles in Greenhouse Onboarding.

#### In this article

  * Access your employee's profile

    * Tasks tab
    * Documents tab
  * Additional resources



### Access your employee's profile

To access your employee's profile, click on their name under _My New Hires_ or enter their name in the **Search bar** at the top of your home page.

The header of their employee profile includes their name, profile picture, [pronouns and pronunciations](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/4564402907291), job title, department, start date, and work email. 

The employee's profile includes the following tabs:

  * Info tab
  * 30-day goals tab
  * Tasks tab
  * Documents tab



#### Info tab

On the Info tab, you'll find additional personal information for your employee and a list of your employee's direct reports (if they are assigned as a manager to other users).

**Note:** Managers have access to view or edit employee information based on permissions granted by your organization's Admin Owner. For example, managers may be able to view an employee's ethnicity but cannot edit it.

Any field that has a **private********icon** next to it indicates that this information is not viewable to other employees in your organization unless they have specified permissions granted by your Admin Owner.

Click **Edit** to add or make changes to the employee's information. Once finished, click **Save** at the top of the _Information dialog box_.

#### 30-day goals tab

Use the 30-day goals tab to configure and assign [onboarding goals for your new hire](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/9265626455067).

**Note:** Goals for new hires is currently running as a beta with opt-in participation. Please contact your Customer Success Manager to request access to this feature.

#### Tasks tab

The Tasks tab shows all [tasks](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360000525691) assigned to your employee. You'll also see tasks related to onboarding this employee that have been assigned to you as manager and other users in your organization (such as an onboarding coordinator).

**Note** : Owners can configure whether managers have view-only access or full edit access to their direct reports' onboarding tasks. Learn more about [setting manager access to tasks](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/16336320416155).

If you have access to edit your employees' tasks, click **Create a New Task** to create and assign a new task for your employee. Click **Add an Existing Task** to assign an existing task that your organization already created.

#### Documents tab

The Documents tab shows all [documents](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/216488683) and [e-signatures](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/115003695071) assigned to your employee by you or your organization. 

**Note** : Owners need to grant managers [permission to manage employee documents and signature requests](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360021729772) in order to view the Documents tab. E-Signature documents are only available for the Greenhouse Onboarding subscription tier.

Click **Add Document** or **Request Signature** to add a new document or send an e-signature request to your employee. 

Click the **ellipsis icon** to **Cancel** a signature request or **Download** a signed document. If your employee has completed multiple signatures, you can select **Download All** to download all available signed documents.

### Additional resources

  * [View and manage an employee profile](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/5759718119707)
  * [Admin access to employee profiles](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/13298757842587)

# Calyptus integration

**Calyptus.co** provides a suite of automated solutions designed to optimize recruiting operations. By seamlessly integrating with **Greenhouse** Recruiting, Calyptus enables users to streamline their hiring workflows, enhance data management, and improve overall efficiency in candidate and job management.

**Calyptus.co's** integration with **Greenhouse** Recruiting allows users to automatically sync candidate and job data, ensuring that all necessary information is up-to-date across both platforms. This integration simplifies workflows for recruiting teams by eliminating the need for manual data entry, improving accuracy, and saving valuable time.

#### In this article

  * Create a Harvest API key
  * Connect Greenhouse to your Calyptus profile 
  * Use the Calyptus integration with Greenhouse Recruiting
  * Additional resources



### Create a Harvest API key

To configure the **Calyptus** integration, you’ll need to create a Harvest API key.

Follow the steps in [this article](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/5888163769883) to create the key, and verify that the permissions below are selected when configuring the Calyptus integration.

#### **Credentials**

In the _Create New Credential_ box, make the following selections:

  * **API Type:** Harvest
  * **Partner:** Calyptus or Unlisted Vendor
  * **Description:** Calyptus Harvest API Key



#### **Permissions**

Verify that the following permissions are selected for the Calyptus integration:

  * **Candidates**
    * POST: Add Candidate
  * **Jobs**
    * GET: List Jobs
  * **Users**
    * GET: List Users



### Connect Greenhouse to your Calyptus profile

Follow these steps to connect Greenhouse to your Calyptus profile:

Log in to your Calyptus account.

Go to **Settings** > **Integration** tab. 

Click **Connect** on the Greenhouse section.

Enter the API Key in the **Add your API key to connect Greenhouse to your profile** window.

Click **Connect**. Your connection is now established, and Greenhouse is integrated with your Calyptus profile.

### Use the Calyptus integration with Greenhouse Recruiting

Once the integration setup is complete, you can begin leveraging the full benefits of Calyptus.co's seamless synchronization with Greenhouse Recruiting.

With the Calyptus integration, you can post Job Positions from Greenhouse into Calyptus, ensuring your data is in sync between the two systems

#### Manage candidate sync from Calyptus

In **Candidate Pool** , select the **Job Position Imported from Greenhouse** and contact the Candidate.

Once the Candidate is contacted you can navigate to Chats and sync the Candidate to Greenhouse by clicking **Send to ATS.**

#### Sync applicants from Calyptus

Additionally, the Candidate can be synced from Applicants by navigating to _Jobs_ in the menu on the left side of the page > clicking on **Job Position imported from Greenhouse** > opening the _Applications_ tab > clicking the Applicant > clicking **Send to ATS.**

__

__

### Additional resources

For additional information or troubleshooting not covered here:

  * Reach out to [support@calyptus.co ](mailto:support@calyptus.co%20)
  * Create a support ticket for Calyptus in [Discord](https://discord.com/channels/1130457754826461216/1130494069953528008/1130915378491572274).
  * Search the solution in [FAQs ](https://www.calyptus.co/employers-faq)section of the Calyptus [website](https://www.calyptus.co/).

# Release Notes: March 2026

Greenhouse Software regularly releases new product features, updates, and improvements. You can stay up-to-date by following our [release notes](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/200929955) or checking out the [latest feature releases](https://www.greenhouse.com/greenhouse-latest-features) page.

#### This month's releases

  * Greenhouse Recruiting
  * Integrations
  * Bug fixes



### Greenhouse Recruiting

#### Candidate profile: right panel improvements

We've updated the [candidate profile](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/30352015432987)'s right panel to make common actions quicker and more intuitive:

  * Buttons now include text labels, so each action is easier to identify without memorizing icons. 
  * A dedicated close button makes it easier to collapse the panel when more screen space is needed. 
  * Uploaded documents now display their file names, so reviewers can quickly identify the right file when multiple documents of the same type are on file.



#### Duplicate candidate tag improvements

The **Duplicate** tag is now a more reliable signal for recruiting teams. Historically, the **Duplicate** tag displayed whenever the candidate shared the same email or name as another record in your system, leading to many false positives if the candidate had a common name. 

Now, candidates will only be flagged as duplicate when they share the same email address, phone number, or LinkedIn profile URL, reducing noise and making the tag more useful for identifying profiles that need review. 

In addition to these changes, the tag's color and wording have been standardized across the candidate profile, Talent Matching, and Application Review for a more consistent experience.

#### Multi-calendar view in suggested interview times

Recruiters can now view multiple interviewer calendars at once when [suggesting times](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/13301025470875) for candidates. Instead of switching between calendars or leaving Greenhouse, they can see combined availability in a single view, making it faster and easier to find suitable time slots. This reduces scheduling back-and-forth, lowers the risk of conflicts, and helps teams move more quickly and confidently through interview coordination.

#### Hire Link for Workday® 

Greenhouse now offers an out-of-the-box integration with Workday® that automatically exports new hire data to Workday® to create pre-hire profiles and initiate the onboarding process.

Previously, recruiting teams had to manually transfer candidate data or invest in costly custom integration work to bridge the gap between hiring and onboarding. Hire Link for Workday® eliminates that gap for new hires, rehires, and internal transfers — bringing the full candidate-to-new-hire lifecycle into one connected experience.

For more information on getting Hire Link for Workday® for your organization, contact your account team. [Read more about Hire Link for Workday®](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/37059787892251).

#### MyGreenhouse Stages

Customers can now use MyGreenhouse Stages to map internal hiring stages to clear, candidate-friendly labels that job seekers can see directly in MyGreenhouse. Teams can group multiple internal stages into a single stage, add optional descriptions, apply mappings by department, preview the experience before publishing, and keep stage updates synced automatically as candidates move through the process. This gives organizations a simple way to make the hiring process feel more transparent, reduce uncertainty for job seekers, and cut down on status update follow-ups.

[Read more about MyGreenhouse Stages.](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/42201508536091-MyGreenhouse-Stages)

#### Harvest v3 API usage

You can now monitor Harvest v3 API activity directly in Greenhouse. View total request volume and success rates for the month, a daily breakdown of HTTP response codes to help identify error spikes, and a per-credential view showing which integrations are most active and how they're performing. All data is filterable by month, making it easier to compare activity over time and catch issues before they become incidents.

[Read more about viewing Harvest API usage.](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360029266032-Harvest-API-overview#view-api-usage)

#### Stage transitions when an application is created

Stage transition automations now run for candidates when their application is created, not just when they’re moved between stages. This ensures that configured actions—like sending forms or emails—aren’t missed for candidates entering Application Review or other stages. 

### Integrations

# Aquera ITSM Applications integration

**Note:** The Aquera ITSM application integration is specifically for Greenhouse Onboarding.

Aquera’s ITSM application integration with Greenhouse Onboarding allows organizations to scale complex data management by automating the service request creations in ITSM applications for new employees hired in the Greenhouse Onboarding application.

#### In this article

  * Create an Onboarding API Key
  * Use the Aquera Integration with Greenhouse Onboarding
    * Prerequisites
  * Configure the Greenhouse Onboarding Connector
    * Supported Resources and Operations
    * Configuration
  * Configure an ITSM Connector
    * Supported Resources and Operations
    * Configuration
  * Set Up the Aquera Workflow
  * Automate Service Request Creation
  * Additional resources



### Create an Onboarding API Key

To configure the Aquera integration, you will need to create an Onboarding API key. You must be an **Owner** in the Greenhouse Onboarding application to create the API key. 

Follow the steps in [this article](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360003470371) to create a Greenhouse Onboarding API key.

In the **Create a new API key** box, provide a name for the API key, and click **Create**. 

For further details, refer to the [Greenhouse documentation](https://developers.greenhouse.io/gho.html#authentication).

### Use the Aquera Integration with Greenhouse Onboarding

Use the Aquera Integration with Greenhouse Onboarding to automatically create new service requests in ServiceNow, which is an ITSM application when new employees are hired in the Greenhouse Onboarding application using Aquera's Workflows.

To integrate with the applications of your interest, check Aquera's [Application Catalog](https://www.aquera.com/applications.html).

The following is the Aquera Flow Map showing data flow from the Greenhouse Onboarding application to the ServiceNow application through Aquera's Workflows:  


With the Aquera Greenhouse Integration, you can import employees from the Greenhouse Onboarding application and create a service request in an ITSM application such as ServiceNow to allocate laptops to the new employees hired in the Greenhouse Onboarding application.

You are required to perform the following steps for the Aquera Greenhouse Integration:

  * [Prerequisites](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1sZoYg8QhGBDgYjrR9Fn8TsEUMPNF50twBbmI_LLqXco/edit#heading=h.tyjcwt)
  * [Configure the Greenhouse Onboarding Connector](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1sZoYg8QhGBDgYjrR9Fn8TsEUMPNF50twBbmI_LLqXco/edit#heading=h.1t3h5sf)
  * [Configure an ITSM Connector](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1sZoYg8QhGBDgYjrR9Fn8TsEUMPNF50twBbmI_LLqXco/edit#heading=h.17dp8vu)

  * [Automate Service Request Creation](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1sZoYg8QhGBDgYjrR9Fn8TsEUMPNF50twBbmI_LLqXco/edit#heading=h.1ksv4uv)



#### **Prerequisites**

The following are the prerequisites:

  * **Tenant Account in the Aquera Admin Portal:** You must have a tenant account in the Aquera admin portal. Visit [https://admin.aquera.io](https://admin.aquera.io/) and register to get a tenant account. Contact your Aquera account manager to get the Aquera tenant access.



**Note:** If your organization is in the EU region, use the following URL to register: <https://admin.eu.aquera.io/>

  * **Owner credentials to the Greenhouse Onboarding application:** You must have the credentials (username and password) of an Owner to log in to the Greenhouse Onboarding application. Contact the Greenhouse Onboarding administrator who will assign the **Owner** role to a user for API Management.
  * **API Key:** You must create an Onboarding API key as mentioned in the previous section for authenticating the API requests. The Greenhouse Onboarding connector leverages the Onboarding API to retrieve employees from the Greenhouse Onboarding application.



### Configure the Greenhouse Onboarding Connector

You need to configure the Greenhouse Onboarding connector in the Aquera Admin portal to retrieve employees from the Greenhouse Onboarding application.

#### Supported Resources and Operations

The following resource supported by the Greenhouse Onboarding connector is used for this integration:

**Employees**

  * Retrieve all employees
  * Retrieve information of an employee



#### Configuration

Perform the following steps to configure the Greenhouse Onboarding connector in the Aquera Admin portal:

  1. Log in to the Aquera Admin portal.
  2. Navigate to **Applications** and click **Add Application** in the Aquera Admin portal.
  3. Search for _Greenhouse Onboarding_ and click the _Greenhouse Onboarding_ icon.
  4. Enter the values for the following fields under the **Configuration** tab:



  * **Basic Details:**
    * **Display Name:** Enter a display name for your application.
    * **Description:** Enter a description for your application.
    * **Source Connection Type:** Select **Direct Connection****.**_  
_**Note:** This field is available only if you have access to Aquera's File Collection module.
    * **Source Owner:** Enter a valid email ID of the source owner(s).
    * **Subscribe error notification:** Select this checkbox to send notification emails to source owner(s) for any errors in the user data transactions.
    * **Pick your Protocol:** Select the protocol as SCIM to populate the fields in the Schema accordingly.
    * **Copy this URL:** This is the interface URL to the Greenhouse Onboarding connector. Copy this URL and paste it at the time of provisioning in the identity service provider.


  5. Click **Create** to create the Greenhouse Onboarding connector.



Refer to the [Greenhouse Onboarding Configuration Guide](https://support.aquera.com/hc/en-us/articles/360050540634) for detailed configurations and schema attributes.

#### Configure an ITSM Connector

You need to configure an ITSM connector in the Aquera Admin portal to create a service request in an ITSM application. Refer to the respective connector configuration guides in the [Aquera Help Center](https://support.aquera.com/hc/en-us/categories/115000284613-Connectors) for details on configuring an ITSM connector.

  * List all users

  * Edit information of a user
  * Activate/Deactivate a user
  * Delete a user



#### Configuration

Perform the following steps to configure the ServiceNow connector in the Aquera Admin portal:

  1. Log in to the Aquera Admin portal.
  2. Navigate to **Applications** and click **Add Application** on the Aquera Admin portal.
  3. Search for _ServiceNow_ and click the _ServiceNow_ icon.

     * **Basic Details:**

       * **Description:** Enter a description for your application.
       * **Tenant:** Enter the hostname of your ServiceNow application. For example, if your ServiceNow instance URL is **https:// aquera.service-now.com** , enter **aquera.service-now.com** as the tenant name.
       * **Source Connection Type:** Select **Direct Connection****.**  
**Note:** This field is available only if you have access to Aquera's File Collection module.
       * **Source Owner:** Enter a valid email ID of the source owner(s).
       * **Subscribe error notification:** Select this checkbox to send notification emails to source owner(s) for any errors in the user data transactions.

  5. Click **Create** to create the ServiceNow connector.



Refer to the [ServiceNow Configuration Guide](https://support.aquera.com/hc/en-us/articles/360048479854-ServiceNow-Configuration-Guide) for detailed configurations and schema attributes.

### Set Up the Aquera Workflow

# Tracking a candidate's source

**Permissions:** \--

**Product tier:** Available for new subscription tiers (Core, Plus, and Pro)

Tracking a candidate's source allows your organization to collect information on how a particular candidate entered your pipeline. Tracking a candidate's source provides additional context to the candidate's profile and allows you to [report](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/203940929) on candidate sources to analyze which sources are returning the highest-quality candidates. 

#### In this article

  * Tracking links and source tokens
  * Tracking candidate sources across job board integrations
    * Greenhouse-hosted job boards (Options 1 and 3)
    * Greenhouse Recruiting iFrame job board (Options 2 and 4)
    * API-driven job board (Option 5)
  * Troubleshooting missing sources



### Tracking links and source tokens

Greenhouse Recruiting tracks the source of your candidates using a [tracking link](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/216904366) that can be generated for a specific source. When you create a tracking link, you'll have to choose the source where you add the link. Then, when a candidate applies using the generated link, the source will automatically be added to their profile details.

A tracking link is made up of two parts: the **job board URL** and the **Source Token**. The Source Token is an automatically generated combination of letters and numbers used to identify the unique link. You can find a source token after the **gh_src=** part of the URL.

To make sure that the candidate's source is assigned correctly, make sure to include the full URL when posting the tracking link.

**Example:** When it's generated, a tracking link might look like this URL: _https://omniva-corp-careers.com/jobs?gh_src=abcdef_.

In this example, `omniva-corp-careers` is the name of the job board, while `gh_src=abcdef` is the unique token. 

### Tracking candidate sources across job board integrations

For most [job board types](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/200721644), if the Source Token is in the URL when the candidate applies, the source of the candidate will be pushed back into Greenhouse Recruiting. Specifically, this behavior occurs when you embed your application form in a Greenhouse iFrame or if you redirect candidates to <https://boards.greenhouse.io> to apply.

However, when using more advanced job board integrations, it is possible that your job board may remove the Source Token URL parameter when a candidate clicks the link and is redirected to the job board. 

To make sure this issue isn't occurring, select your tracking link and then verify that the `gh_src={TOKEN}` part of the URL is still intact. 

#### **Greenhouse-hosted job boards (Options 1 and 3)**

With Job Board Integration [Option 1](https://app.greenhouse.io/jobboard/integration/documentation/hosted_board_and_apps) and [Option 3](https://app.greenhouse.io/jobboard/integration/documentation/api_board_hosted_apps), candidates are redirected from your website to a Greenhouse-hosted application page to apply.

The URL of the Greenhouse-hosted application page will include the job board token (typically the name of your company) and the Job ID for the specific job.

For the candidate's source to be tracked correctly, the Source Token needs to be passed from your careers page URL to the URL of the application form on <https://boards.greenhouse.io>.

**Example:** If the Source Token is _abcdef_ , the full application page URL might look something like this: [https://boards.greenhouse.io/example/jobs/12345?gh_src=abcdef](https://boards.greenhouse.io/example/12345?gh_src=abcdef).

If the Source Token is not present in the application URL as in the example above, we recommend reaching out to your web development team.

Typically, this issue is caused when the Source Token is not being passed to the application URL when candidates click the link.

#### **Greenhouse Recruiting iFrame job board (Options 2 and 4)**

For customers who embed the application form in an iFrame on their own page using an [Option 2](https://app.greenhouse.io/jobboard/integration/documentation/embedded_board_and_apps) or an [Option 4](https://app.greenhouse.io/jobboard/integration/documentation/api_board_embedded_apps) job board, the Source Token will also need to be included in the URL of the application page.

**Example:** The URL of the application page for a job with ID _12345_ may look something like this: <https://example.com/jobs?gh_jid=12345>. In this case, the Job ID is included in the URL in the parameter `gh_jid={JOB_ID}`.

For Greenhouse to track the candidate’s Source, that URL also needs to contain the Source Token `gh_src={TOKEN}`.

**Example:** The full URL might look something like this: [https://example.com/jobs?gh_jid=12345&gh_src=abcdef](https://example.com/jobs?gh_jid=12345&gh_src=abcdef).

If the Source Token is not present in the application URL as in the example above, we recommend reaching out to your web development team.

If your application form is hosted on a different URL from your job board, first confirm that the Job Post URL has been set up correctly. You can read more about setting up Job Post URLs [here](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/214375866).

#### **API-driven job board (Option 5)**

If you have configured your own customized application form through the [Job Board API](https://developers.greenhouse.io/job-board.html) (in an Option 5 job board), the developers who created the application form will need to send the Source Token to Greenhouse in the **POST** Application request.

The Source Token should be included in the `mapped_url_token` parameter and should be sent to Greenhouse Recruiting along with the candidate’s application data.

Read more about building the API-driven application form [here](https://developers.greenhouse.io/job-board.html#submit-an-application).

### Troubleshooting missing sources

If you suspect that your candidates’ sources are not being tracked in Greenhouse Recruiting, try [generating a tracking link](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/216904366) and following the link in your browser to ensure that the Source Token is included in the URL of the application page.

If the Source Token is not present in the application URL, reach out to your development team as they typically have more insight on how your job board redirects to Greenhouse Recruiting.

**Example:** If a careers page is using a Greenhouse-hosted job board (_candidates are redirected to_ _<https://boards.greenhouse.io>__to apply_), when you click the link, the source token should still appear in the URL.

If the source token is displaying on the tracking link, but not the job board, you'll want to investigate how the pages are redirected.

If the source is missing from both the link and the job board, you'll want to make sure you correctly generated the link.

# Mailgun

**Permissions:** \--

**Product tier:** Available for new subscription tiers (Core, Plus, and Pro)

Mailgun is a third-party email provider Greenhouse Recruiting uses to send emails. All emails from Greenhouse are sent via Mailgun. This includes (but is not limited to) emails such as new user invitations, notifications, emails to candidates, and [@mention](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360013153651--mentions) messages between users.

As a part of the Greenhouse Recruiting implementation process, we ask all organizations to register their domain within the Greenhouse application and complete the [email verification process](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/201111684-Email-Verification). This process registers your domain with Mailgun, who in turn generates DNS records (SPF, DKIM, and sometimes MX records) to be added to your domain host.

The primary purpose of adding these records to your domain host is to expressly permit Greenhouse Recruiting (via Mailgun) to send emails on behalf of your domain, which helps prevent emails from going to spam.

All outbound emails from Greenhouse Recruiting are sent through Mailgun whether or not a domain is verified. Any emails sent through Greenhouse using our email provider from an unverified domain will be sent through outbound-mail.greenhouse.io instead of through your domain.

A flag will appear in the **from:** address of your emails that reads **via greenhouse.io**. Since the domain that emails are sent from do not match the domain in the **from:** address, these emails will likely go to spam.

The SPF, DKIM, and MX records are generated by Mailgun. However, the SPF record only permits emails to be sent from Greenhouse Recruiting's dedicated Mailgun IP addresses which we actively monitor. The SPF record does not permit emails to be sent from all Mailgun IP addresses. You can find a list of Greenhouse Recruiting's dedicated IP addresses [here](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360033429591).

# SmartDreamers integration

SmartDreamers offers Recruitment Marketing Automation Software to help your company reach and attract better candidates, faster. Greenhouse Recruiting’s integration with SmartDreamers allows your organization to seamlessly export open/active positions into SmartDreamers and receive candidates directly in Greenhouse Recruiting.

**Note** : All active jobs within Greenhouse will be automatically synchronized within SmartDreamers at a 5-minute interval, while all applicants will be imported into Greenhouse every 12 hours.

### Create a Harvest API key for the SmartDreamers integration

To configure the Greenhouse Recruiting / SmartDreamers integration, you'll need to create a Harvest API key.

Follow the steps in [this article](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/5888163769883) to create the key, and verify that the credentials and permissions below are selected when configuring the SmartDreamers integration.

# Anonymize resumes

**Permissions:** —

**Product tier:** Available for Pro subscription tiers

When scanning through hundreds of resumes in application review, it's easy for bias to creep in. Familiar information like a candidate's home town, links to social media profiles, or other identifying information promote mental shortcuts that result in snap decisions that are based on this surface-level information, rather than the candidate's skills and qualifications for the role.

Greenhouse's resume anonymization feature uses AI to assess a candidate's resume and blur certain pieces of identifying information to help improve your hiring practices.

For more information on how we use AI, check out our [blog](https://www.greenhouse.com/blog/embracing-ai-in-our-hiring-software).

#### In this article

  * Benefits of resume anonymization
  * Turn on resume anonymization for a job
  * How resume anonymization works
    * Anonymized resume information
  * Use resume anonymization
    * View an anonymized resume
    * Provide feedback on anonymization
    * Turn off resume anonymization for a job
  * Sources



### Benefits of resume anonymization

Resumes contain a lot of personal information about candidates, and hiring teams may experience bias without realizing it.

Many peer-reviewed studies have shown that hiring bias is reduced when candidates’ identifying information is concealed. Hiring teams have already seen these results with the [anonymization of take-home tests](https://www.greenhouse.com/guidance/how-anonymous-take-home-tests-mitigate-bias-and-improve-candidate-odds). 

Greenhouse Recruiting’s resume anonymization tool uses machine learning, a component of AI, to identify and anonymize candidates’ identifying information. This provides the following benefits:

  * Makes your hiring practice fairer and more equitable from the beginning
  * Helps you identify the most qualified candidates
  * Improves the candidate experience so they can feel confident applying through Greenhouse



### Turn on resume anonymization for a job

**Note:** Only Site Admins and Job Admins can make changes to a job's interview plan.

If resume anonymization is turned on for your organization, it can be turned on for a specific job by editing the Application Review stage of the interview plan:

  1. Open a job
  2. Click **Job Setup**
  3. Click **Interview Plan**
  4. Click the **Edit** icon next to Application Review
  5. Scroll to the bottom of the page, select the checkbox for resume anonymization, and click **Save**.



Anonymized resumes will become visible in the Application Review within 40 minutes. The time required for the tool to anonymize resumes varies depending on the number of applications the job has received.

### How resume anonymization works

**Note:** This feature is currently optimized for resumes written with Latin characters, and no candidate resumes were used in the training of our model.

Greenhouse Recruiting uses a proprietary machine-learning model to identify and conceal specific candidate data. The model breaks the candidate's resume into sections, which are then scanned for keywords, phrases, and other information that could identify the candidate. Our model uses state-of-the-art deep learning models that have been trained to work with the highest possible accuracy.

#### Anonymized resume information

Resume anonymization conceals candidate details that have the highest incidence of enabling bias. Studies show that this includes gender, photo, and related information.

**Example:** The presence of a candidate’s name on their resume can unintentionally influence an employer to assume the candidate’s gender. Other places the candidate’s name is used, such as in their email address, can have the same effect. Resume anonymization accounts for these factors to conceal the most relevant information.

The following pieces of information can be anonymized:

  * Name
  * Titles
  * Suffixes
  * Gender
  * Photo
  * Race/ethnicity/nationality
  * Marital status
  * Address
  * Email
  * Phone number
  * Links to social media profiles



While our model is highly precise, it's important to note it may not cover every part of the application review process. When your organization includes custom application questions, the applicant's responses could potentially disclose identifiable details. Additionally, if the resume includes a headshot with peripheral details like a company logo on clothing, these details might still be visible.

### Viewing anonymized resumes

#### Configure resume anonymization for your jobs

Go to **Jobs** and select one of your open jobs. Then, select **Job Setup** > **Interview Plan.** Resume anonymization can be turned on for two stages: Application Review and Hiring Manager Review. Click the **Edit** icon  next to the stage name and go to the _Additional Settings_ section. Add a checkmark to the box next to **Anonymize resumes in Application Review** , then select **Save** to enable resume anonymization.

#### View an anonymized resume

**Note:** Resume anonymization is currently available only for the following stages:

  * [Application Review](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/4401963991707)
  * [Hiring Manager Review](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/4402694472347)



When you're viewing the job dashboard, select the **Review Applications** button in the  _Pipeline_ tab.

This button will only appear if you're a recruiter or hiring manager on the hiring team and there are candidates to review.

You can also follow these steps to [access a resume for application review](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/4401963991707#h_01F9A9KV6BKX0H7DZ21AD3NHDS).

Recruiters and hiring managers can access a candidate’s full resume on their candidate profile.

#### Provide feedback on anonymization

Every anonymized resume includes the ability to leave feedback on the accuracy of the anonymization. Your feedback is crucial to the ongoing development of resume anonymization, and we encourage you to submit your thoughts.

#### Turn off resume anonymization for a job

To turn off resume anonymization for a specific job, go to the job’s Interview Plan page and uncheck the box next to**Anonymize resumes in Application Review**. Then, click **Save**.

### Sources

  1. Johnson, Stefanie K., and Jessica F. Kirk. 2020. “Research: To Reduce Gender Bias, Anonymize Job Applications.” Harvard Business Review. March 5, 2020. <https://hbr.org/2020/03/research-to-reduce-gender-bias-anonymize-job-applications>.
  2. A., Corinne, John F. Dovidio, Victoria L. Brescoll, Mark J. Graham, and Jo Handelsman. "Science Faculty’s Subtle Gender Biases Favor Male Students." Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences 109, no. 41 (2012): 16474-16479. Accessed December 11, 2023. <https://doi.org/10.1073/pnas.1211286109>.
  3. Ahmed, Ali, Mark Granberg, and Shantanu Khanna. "Gender Discrimination in Hiring: An Experimental Reexamination of the Swedish Case." PLoS ONE 16, no. 1 (2021). Accessed December 11, 2023. <https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pone.0245513>.

# Reimbi integration

This integration allows candidate data to be sent from Greenhouse Recruiting to Reimbi resulting in the candidate record being created in Reimbi. Upon receiving the required information via the integration Reimbi will send the candidate an email with Reimbi login instructions so that their expense report can be submitted and reimbursed.

In this article

  * Create a Harvest API key for the Reimbi integration
    * Credentials
    * Permissions
  * Add Harvest API Key to Reimbi
  * Retrieve Reimbi's Endpoint URL and Secret Key
  * Create a webhook
  * Create custom candidate fields in Greenhouse Recruiting
    * Field 1: Send to Reimbi
    * Field 2: Reimbi Reimbursement Policy
  * Use the Reimbi Integration with Greenhouse Recruiting
  * Additional support



### Create a Harvest API key for the Reimbi integration

To configure the Greenhouse Recruiting / Reimbi integration, you'll need to create a Harvest API key.

Follow the steps in [this article](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/5888163769883) to create the key, and verify that the credentials and permissions below are selected when configuring the Reimbi integration.

#### Credentials

In the _Create New Credential_ box, make the following selections:

  * **API type:** Harvest
  * **Partner:** Reimbi
  * **Description:** Reimbi Harvest API key



#### Permissions

Verify that the following permissions are selected for the Reimbi integration:

  * **Candidates**
    * GET: Retrieve Candidate
    * GET: List Candidates
  * **Jobs**
    * GET: Retrieve Job



### Add Harvest API Key to Reimbi

_**Note:** This step must be performed by a Reimbi user with Admin permissions._

  1. Log in to Reimbi, navigate to **Company Settings** , and click **Integrations**
  2. Turn the **Greenhouse integration** slider to **On**
  3. Enter your Harvest API Key
  4. Choose how you want the approver assigned to candidates sent via the Reimbi/Greenhouse Recruiting integration.
  5. Choose who will be the backup approver. If Reimbi can't assign the approver based on the information we receive from Greenhouse Recruiting (for example, the user doesn't exist), then this user will be assigned as the approver.
  6. Choose the default reimbursement policy that should be assigned to the candidate.
  7. Click **Update**.



### Retrieve Reimbi's Endpoint URL and Secret Key

From the same page in Reimbi (**Company Settings** > **Integrations**), retrieve the following pieces of information to be used in the next section.

  * Reimbi's Endpoint URL
  * Reimbi's Secret Key



To get these values, click **Generate Web Hook Secret Key and API URL**. On the next page, copy your Endpoint URL and Secret Key.

### Create a webhook

To integrate Reimbi with Greenhouse Recruiting, you'll need to create a webhook. Follow the steps in [this article](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/5888163727003) to create your webhook. Use the values listed below to configure the webhooks.

  * **Name:** _Reimbi integration_
  * **When:** Candidate or Prospect updated
  * **Endpoint URL:** The Endpoint URL copied from Reimbi
  * **Secret Key:** The Secret Key copied from Reimbi
  * **Disabled?:** No



### Create custom candidate fields in Greenhouse Recruiting

**Note:** Custom candidate fields can only be created by users with Job Admin level permissions with the additional user-specific permission **Can manage custom fields** , or by users with Site Admin level permissions.

The final step to successfully enabling the integration is to create a custom candidate field.

Follow the steps in [this article](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/202609675) and create a custom field with the following options:

#### Field 1: Send to Reimbi

  * **Name:** Send to Reimbi
  * **Type:** Yes/No



#### Field 2: Reimbi Reimbursement Policy

**Note:** This field is only required if you have more than one policy set up in Reimbi.

  * **Name:** Reimbi Reimbursement Policy
  * **Type:** Single Select
  * **Options:** Add the names of your organization's policies, one per line. These values can be found on the _Policies_ page in Reimbi.



### Use the Reimbi Integration with Greenhouse Recruiting

  1. Navigate to the _Details_ tab for a candidate in Greenhouse Recruiting.
  2. Select the policy in the **Reimbi Reimbursement Policy** field and click **Save**.
  3. Select **Yes** in the **Send to Reimbi** field and click **Save**.



The candidate's record will display as Invitation _Pending_ in Reimbi with the assigned policy. Additionally, the candidate will receive an email to help set up and submit expenses using their Reimbi account.

### Additional support

Contact [support@reimbi.com](mailto:support@reimbi.com) for troubleshooting assistance regarding the integration.

# BrightHire Screen integration

Brighthire Screen is an AI Interviewer that acts as an extension of your team, helping you handle high-volume inbound while uncovering more great talent.

The AI interviewer is able to confirm job candidate interest, skills, eligibility, employment history and availability via a web-based call.

Brighthire has designed Screen to be used by recruiting teams to assist them in their screening processes. Recruiting teams will be able to configure Screen in one of two ways. In each case, there is a human-in-the-loop.

  * **Summarization Only:** The AI Interviewer can pose questions and summarize candidate responses for recruiting teams to review. The interview screening agent will also provide recruiting teams with the source audio data and the transcript of the call. Recruiters will make their own decisions regarding which candidates to advance or decline.
  * **Evaluation and Scorecard:** The AI interviewer can pose questions and use candidate responses, as well as inferences it makes about candidate qualifications based on their responses, to compare a candidate's qualifications to pre-defined screening criteria and rank candidates based on their ability to meet screening criteria. The screening criteria is defined by the customer's recruiting team. BrightHire Screen will also provide recruiting teams with an evaluation summary, source audio data and the transcript of the call. At this point, recruiters will make their own decisions regarding which candidates to advance or decline.



BrightHire’s integration with Greenhouse Recruiting allows you to seamlessly add BrightHire’s assessment to a job's interview plan.

#### In this article

  * Enable the integration
  * Use the integration with Greenhouse Recruiting
  * Additional resources



### Enable the integration

Go to [this page](https://app.brighthire.ai/settings/greenhouse) in BrightHire and create a new “AI interviewer” API key.

Then, follow the steps in [this article](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/5888163696923) to work with Greenhouse Support and add the assessment stage in your interview plans.

Once you’ve set up your interview plans and configured your take home test, you’ll be able to send the test to candidates.

### Use the integration with Greenhouse Recruiting

Once the BrightHire integration is enabled for your organization, you will be able to add the BrightHire assessment as an interview stage.

You can send an assessment to a candidate by selecting the**Send Test** button next to the interview stage. The assessment instructions will be sent by BrightHire.

After it has been sent, an assessment’s status will display in Greenhouse Recruiting.

Once the candidate has submitted their test, the Interview Kit will contain a link to view the submitted test in the BrightHire application. 

To see a candidate’s results in BrightHire, click **View** **Report** .

You’ll be able to view a summary of the assessment, the candidate’s score and a quick snapshot of their strongest and weakest answers. For each question, you’ll be able to view a summary of the candidate’s response, the response score and a justification for why the candidate’s response received that score. You’ll also be able to access the interview transcript and audio.

### Additional resources

For additional information not covered here, reach out to [support@brighthire.ai](mailto:support@brighthire.ai).

# Why didn't the interview I scheduled show up in Greenhouse Recruiting?

If you scheduled an interview, but it didn't show up in Greenhouse Recruiting, this may be caused by a few different things:

  * Was your organization's [Greenhouse Recruiting calendar email address](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360050154551) included as a guest on the event?
  * Was the interview kit URL included in the body of the email?
  * Is the email address of your calendar the same as the email address associated with your Greenhouse Recruiting user account? 
  * Did you wait long enough for the interview to sync? In some cases, it can take up to an hour for the calendar events to reach us and appear on the candidate's profile.



If you're still having issues with the interview, reach out to [Greenhouse Technical Support](https://support.greenhouse.io/direct).

# Error message: "Heads up!  It's unlikely this email will be delivered!"

The error message "**Heads up! It's unlikely this email will be delivered!** " may display when trying to send an email on Greenhouse Recruiting if your email domain is not yet verified.

Your email domain must be verified on Greenhouse Recruiting in order to send emails successfully. Read more here: [Email domain verification](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/201111684).

Since Greenhouse Recruiting has not yet been authorized to send emails from your email domain, your emails may not reach its recipient successfully, and the error message may persist until your domain is verified. Your team can take the needed steps to verify your email domain by following the steps outlined here: [Email domain verification](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/201111684).

# We're rebranding.  How do we update all of our user email addresses?

If your organization is [rebranding](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360004238711) or has updated its email domain, the Greenhouse Technical Support team can assist you with updating all user email addresses in bulk.

#### In this article

  * How can I bulk update email addresses to a new domain?
  * How does the process work after I put in a request?
  * What do users need to do after their email address is updated?
  * Will these new emails be marked as Primary?
  * Additional resources



### How can I bulk update email addresses to a new domain?

Users with "Can configure email settings" permission can update email addresses for multiple users by using the bulk Email Migration Tool under **Configure** > **Dev Center** > **Email Settings** > **Bulk Email Migration Tool**.

To use this tool, you'll download a .csv of all users in your system, add new emails to the spreadsheet, and upload it. Once the migration is complete, the new addresses will be added as Secondary emails to all affected users.

Once a migration is complete, an email notification will be sent to the submitter's email.

### What do users need to do after their email address is updated?

After the bulk update is finished, each updated user will receive an email from Greenhouse to confirm their new email address.

**Note:** Email addresses can’t be marked as **Primary** until the new email address is verified. 

Users will need to click the links included in the confirmation email to verify the new email address to leverage communication features such as notifications, reminders, and interview kits within Greenhouse Recruiting.

However, this step isn't required to access Greenhouse Recruiting using the new email address or through [Single Sign-On (SSO).](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/210259723)

As long as the email address you attempt to log in with matches an email address on your account, you will be able to log in with that address. 

### Will these new emails be marked as Primary?

By default, the new email address will be added as a secondary email address on the user's account.

However, if you'd like to set the new emails as Primary for the updated users, include that information in your initial request.

If you elect to use this option, once a user verifies their new email address using the emailed verification link, it will automatically be set as the **Primary** address on their user account. This Is based on the settings you chose during the migration.

Once the new Primary email has been set, you can then manually remove the secondary email from your Account Settings if it's no longer needed.

To learn more about removing a secondary email from your account, [click here.](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360034879332)

**Note:** Users must click the link to verify their new email address within 24 hours of receipt. If a user doesn't click the link within 24 hours, a new link must be sent.

### Additional resources

  * [My company is rebranding - how do I change our domain?](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/115003083966)
  * [Best Practices: Rebranding](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360004238711)

# Endorsed integration

Endorsed is like having 1,000 AI clones of yourself to do sourcing and applicant review.

Forget filters, booleans, keyword search causing you to over-filter and miss the top candidates that aren’t keyword-stuffing their profiles. Endorsed instantly reads every profile in your market and ATS, surfaces the best talent, and blocks fraud before it reaches the interview table.

**Greenhouse Recruiting’s best-in-class integration with Endorsed lets you:**

  * Activate AI Sourcing – One click spins up a thousand virtual recruiters that scan the entire talent universe, score every prospect, and add up to 3× more great candidates into your shortlist.
  * Configure industry-leading AI to screen applicants on your unique criteria.
  * Score and rank candidates automatically—so the shortlist writes itself.
  * Create AI-powered knockout questions that shed unqualified applicants in seconds.
  * Perform deep research on every employer candidates worked at during applicant review so you never Google and Crunchbase search again.
  * Intelligently bulk-reject and stage-advance candidates, with every action mirrored back to Greenhouse in real time.
  * Trigger auto-personalized Greenhouse emails the moment candidates are advanced or rejected.
  * Sync jobs and applicants bi-directionally so recruiters always work from a single source of truth.
  * Shield every requisition with FraudShield. AI pattern recognition taps billions of signals to flag fakes, impostors, and embellished résumés before they waste interview slots.



**Results Teams See**

  * Up to 3× more qualified candidates in their shortlists.
  * Up to 74 % faster time-to-hire, driven by intelligent triaging and earlier access to stronger talent.
  * 2× increase in recruiter capacity as manual sourcing and applicant review demands evaporate.
  * Never wasting time interviewing fake candidates again.
