### Use the Endorsed integration with Greenhouse Recruiting

Once the integration is connected, Endorsed will sync actions taken in Endorsed to Greenhouse Recruiting. For example, when a user rejects a candidate on Endorsed, this action will be synced to Greenhouse with the credited user being the same user who took the action.

When you advance or reject candidates in Endorsed, these actions are automatically and immediately synced to Greenhouse.

The **Advancing** button in Endorsed will move the candidate to a specified stage, which is set up as a mandatory step for each job within Endorsed. Additionally, any automated emails configured in Greenhouse to send when candidates are advanced or rejected will also be triggered by these actions in Endorsed.

#### Sync jobs to Greenhouse Recruiting

To start using Endorsed with your Greenhouse ATS, you can take the following steps.

[Sign up](https://endorsed.ai/sign-up) and create an Endorsed account, or log into your existing account. 

Choose **Recruiting** as your Organization Type.

Click **Connect ATS Account** button. Occasionally, this button will take a few seconds to load.

Find Greenhouse in the ATS integration window. Select the Greenhouse integration. Do not select the Greenhouse - Job Boards API option, as that's used for a different setup. 

Click **Continue** to give Endorsed access to your Greenhouse account.

Paste in your Harvest API key and click **Submit**. 

Wait for the API connection to complete. This can take up to a minute.

Note: If your account is not able to connect to Greenhouse, contact Endorsed Support by clicking the button in the button right corner of your screen to start a live chat. 

When the connection is complete, you'll automatically be redirected to your **Jobs** page. After your first setup, Endorsed will need to sync with Greenhouse Recruiting to load the initial data. The time needed for this initial sync can differ for different customers, based on the number of jobs and candidates in your system.

If this sync takes longer than 24 hours, contact Endorsed support.

When the job sync is complete, your integration set up is complete.

### Additional resources

For any questions or further troubleshooting support, reach out to the Endorsed team at[support@endorsed.com](mailto:support@endorsed.com).

# Edit or deactivate a webhook

**Permissions:** Basic and above who can manage and configure webhooks

**Product tier:** Available for new subscription tiers (Core, Plus, and Pro)

A webhook is a simple notification system. When an event occurs in Greenhouse Recruiting, like when a candidate is hired, and a webhook is configured for the event, data about the event can be sent to a specified destination called an endpoint.

In some cases, you may need to edit an existing webhook to accommodate changes to the receiving endpoint.

**Tip:** Check out [Create a webhook](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360005574531) for steps to create a new webhook.

#### In this article

  * Edit a webhook
  * Deactivate a webhook
  * Delete a webhook



### Edit a webhook

To edit an existing webhook, click the **Configure** icon on your navigation bar then select **Dev** **Center** on the left.

Click **Web** **hooks**.

Click **webhooks** again on the next page.

Scroll to the _Edit webhook_ section to find your webhooks. Click the **Edit** icon beside your webhook.

You can update any configuration settings for the webhook and click **Update** when you're finished.

### Deactivate a webhook

Deactivating a webhook prevents the webhook from sending notifications, but it maintains the webhook's configuration for later use if needed.

To deactivate a webhook, scroll to the _Edit webhook_ section to find your webhook.

Click the **Edit** icon beside the webhook, and deactivate it by choosing **Yes**.

When finished, click **Update webhook**.

### Delete a webhook

Deleting a webhook completely removes the webhook and its configuration from your Greenhouse Recruiting account.

To delete an active or deactivated webhook, scroll to the _Edit webhook_ section to find your webhook.

Click the **Remove** icon beside the webhook to delete it.

Click **Ok** to confirm, and the webhook will be deleted.

**Note** : Deleted webhooks cannot be recovered.

# SeekOut integration

SeekOut is a passive candidate sourcing tool that allows you to easily move candidate records from SeekOut into Greenhouse Recruiting. 

SeekOut’s integration with Greenhouse Recruiting allows you to export candidate data from SeekOut and turn it into Greenhouse Recruiting candidate profiles, complete with contact information and work/education history. SeekOut candidate data can be sent to Greenhouse Recruiting as prospects or they can be attached to an existing job.

#### In this article

  * Create a Harvest API key
    * Credentials
    * Permissions
  * Create a webhook
  * Send candidate records from SeekOut to Greenhouse Recruiting
  * Additional resources



### Create a Harvest API key

To configure the SeekOut integration, you’ll need to create a Harvest API key.

Follow the steps in [this article](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/5888163769883) to create the key, and verify that the permissions below are selected when configuring SeekOut’s integration.

#### **Credentials**

In the _Create New Credential_ box, make the following selections:

  * **API Type:** Harvest
  * **Partner:** SeekOut or Unlisted Vendor 
  * **Description:** SeekOut Harvest API Key



#### **Permissions**

Verify that the following permissions are selected for the SeekOut integration:

  * Application 
    * Patch: Update Application

    * Post: Add New Candidate Tags

    * Get: Retrieve Job

  * Users 
    * Get: Retrieve User

  * Education 
    * Get: Get degrees
    * Get: Get disciplines
    * Get: Get schools
  * Job Openings 
    * Get: List Openings For a Job
  * Close Reasons 
    * Get: Get close reasons



### Create a webhook

To configure the SeekOut integration, you’ll need to create a job post deleted webhook.

Follow the steps in [this article](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360005574531-Create-a-web-hook) to create a job post deleted webhook using the details below:

  * **Name:** SeekOut Job Post Deleted
  * **When:** Job post deleted
  * **Endpoint URL:** Contact SeekOut ([support@seekout.com](mailto:support@seekout.com)) for URL endpoint
  * **Secret Key:** Contact SeekOut ([support@seekout.com](mailto:support@seekout.com)) for the secret key
  * **Error recipient email:** Contact SeekOut ([support@seekout.com](mailto:support@seekout.com)) for the recipient email
  * **Deactivated?:** No



### Send candidate records from SeekOut to Greenhouse Recruiting

Once the integration is configured, it's simple to move candidates from SeekOut into Greenhouse Recruiting.

From a SeekOut project, select the candidates you want to add to Greenhouse Recruiting by checking the box next to each candidate. Then click Export… and choose

Select the job and click **Export**.

By default, SeekOut will not export a candidate if they have already been exported from SeekOut. If you want the same candidate sent again you can check **Include previously exported candidate(s)**.

Within a few seconds, the candidates you have sourced in SeekOut will be visible in Greenhouse Recruiting.

### Additional resources

For information or troubleshooting assistance with this integration, contact SeekOut Support at [support@seekout.com](mailto:support@seekout.com).

# California Consumer Privacy Act (CCPA) overview

The California Consumer Privacy Act (“CCPA”) took effect on January 1, 2020. The CCPA was subsequently amended by the California Privacy Rights Act of 2020, often referred to as the CPRA.

The CCPA imposes several obligations on businesses that collect personal information from California consumers, and generally expands the rights of California consumers to include the right to (a) access their personal information; (b) request that their personal information be deleted; (c) to get information about the collection, sales, and disclosure of their personal information; and (d) to opt out of the sale of their personal information.

As of January 1, 2023, the CCPA applies to the personal information of a business’s California employees and job applicants.

“Personal information” is defined by the CCPA as “information that identifies, relates to, describes, is capable of being associated with, or could reasonably be linked, directly or indirectly, with a particular consumer.” The term “consumer” is defined more broadly in the CCPA than it is normally used in everyday parlance and includes not only a business’ individual customers, but also its employees and job applicants who are California residents, which is where Greenhouse comes in.

### CCPA FAQ

#### Does my company have to comply with the CCPA?

The CCPA applies to any “business,” which is a term of art under the CCPA that refers specifically to a for-profit company that (a) collects personal information (“PI”) of consumers; (b) determines the purposes and means of processing of the PI; (c) does business in California; and (d) meets one of the three additional criteria: (i) has annual gross revenues greater than $25 million, (ii) collects or shares PI from at least 50,000 California residents per year for commercial purposes, or (iii) derives at least 50% of its annual revenue from selling California consumers’ PI.

Obviously, Greenhouse cannot decide whether its customers are obligated to comply with the CCPA, as we have thousands of customers and it is a fact-specific determination. If you haven’t already, we encourage you to consult with your company’s own data privacy counsel in order to decide how your organization can best proceed under the law.

#### If the CCPA applies to my company, what are our obligations with respect to the data we collect to recruit and/or onboard our employees?

As of January 1, 2023, the aspects of the CCPA that currently apply to employee and applicant data include:

1) Businesses are required to provide employees and job applicants with a CCPA notice (see Section 100(b)) at the point that their personal information is collected that includes:

  * (a) The categories of personal information being collected; and
  * (b) The purposes for which each category of personal information will be used



2) A business’s employees and applicants are entitled to:

  * (a) Know what personal information the business has collected about them;
  * (b) Request that a business correct inaccurate information about them;
  * (c) Request that a business delete information about them (unless the business is required to keep the information);



3) A business’s employees and applicants have a private right of action under the CCPA (see Section 1798.150) _IF_ their personal data is disclosed or stolen as a result of the business’s violation of its duty to implement and maintain reasonable security practices and procedures to protect the personal information.

#### Where does Greenhouse come in?

With respect to our customers, Greenhouse is a “service provider” under the CCPA’s definition of that term; specifically, Greenhouse is a for-profit corporation that stores and processes California consumers’ personal information on behalf of our customers for a business purpose pursuant to a written contract that prohibits Greenhouse from using or disclosing the personal information for any purpose other than performing the services set forth in that contract.

Accordingly, the CCPA permits our customers to disclose personal information about its employees and applicants to Greenhouse (i.e. by allowing us to store and process it on the customer’s behalf) without requiring consent from the employees or applicants or giving them the opportunity to opt out.

To satisfy the CCPA notice requirement in (1) above, your company can simply include a link to its CCPA-compliant privacy policy in its job posts, which are highly customizable within your instance of our Greenhouse’s recruiting software. Similarly, if your company uses Greenhouse Onboarding, you can easily send the required notice to new hires through the application, just as you do other onboarding paperwork.

To help you comply with the CCPA’s requirements in (2) above, Greenhouse has built-in functionality that gives our customers the ability, at their option, to delete an applicant’s personal information or provide a “candidate packet” that contains all of an applicant’s personal information.

As for the CCPA’s requirement in (3) above regarding security practices and procedures, Greenhouse takes our obligation to keep our customers’ data safe and secure very seriously and we adhere to industry standard best practices, including maintaining SOC2, ISO27001, and ISO27701 certifications.

# Use a sandbox

**Permissions:** Basic and above

**Product tier:** Available to Pro subscription tier

A sandbox allows you to train new users, send test offers and emails, evaluate integrations, and more.

#### In this article

  * Use your sandbox
    * Add new users
    * Train new users
    * Test communications
    * Try new integrations
    * Test workflows
    * Test APIs



### Use your sandbox

Your sandbox is generated as an empty space allowing you to manually add fake data like mock jobs, candidates, or organizational data to test scenarios.

To use your sandbox, open a separate browser window from the one running your production Greenhouse Recruiting environment. We recommend using an incognito window.

Next, log in using your sandbox credentials.

**Tip** : If you don't have a user account in your organization's sandbox, reach out to a colleague [who can invite you](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360027077811-Add-new-users).

You can always tell whether you're in a sandbox or production environment by the marigold sandbox badge.

Once you log in, you can use your sandbox for a variety of scenarios.

#### Add new users

**Note** : To add new users to your sandbox, you need to be a Job Admin or Site Admin in the sandbox who [can invite new users to Greenhouse and reactivate deactivated users](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360027077811).

You can add an unlimited number of user accounts to your sandbox environment.

To add new users, log in to your sandbox environment and click **Configure****** > **Users**.

Click **\+ New** **users** and enter the user details.

To add users in bulk, click **Bulk** **import**.

**Note** : Your sandbox users must have a unique email address that is distinct from their production Greenhouse Recruiting accounts. Email addresses can't be shared across multiple Greenhouse Recruiting environments.

**Tip** : Add `+sandbox` to the end of your email, like `jen+sandbox@ymail.com`, to create a unique sandbox email address login.

Check out [Add new users](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360027077811-Add-new-users) to learn more about user management.

#### Train new users

Your sandbox offers a unique test environment for your new team members to interact with Greenhouse Recruiting without disturbing sensitive data like real jobs or candidates.

Check out these new user training resources to help get you started:

  * [Training new Greenhouse Recruiting users](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360044868992-Training-new-Greenhouse-Recruiting-users)
  * [Team training templates](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/sections/4405933096731-Training-resources-)
  * [Learn Greenhouse](https://learn.greenhouse.io/)



#### Send test communications

Use your sandbox to hone the look and feel of your organization's communications, like [offer templates](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/6459061824155), without disturbing your recruiting teams.

You can use your sandbox to create and send new [email templates](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/sections/360000690671-Email-templates), including [interviews](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/115002226746-Interview-kit-overview) and [scorecard reminders](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360047691292-Configure-a-scorecard-reminder-notification), as well as [offer letters](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/200485589-Generate-and-send-offer-letter). Use your sandbox to verify email content like images, videos, and links perform as expected.

#### Try new integrations

Greenhouse Recruiting has [over 400 unique integrations](https://www.greenhouse.com/integrations) with features like video interviewing, e-signatures, and candidate sourcing.

Use your sandbox to test new integrations and explore the most efficient workflows.

Check out a few of our customer-preferred integrations to help get you started:

  * [BambooHR](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/201177624-BambooHR-integration): BambooHR is the leading provider of tools that power the strategic evolution of HR in small-to-medium-sized businesses by tracking and managing essential employee information in an HRIS.
  * [Calendly](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360029649991-Calendly-integration): Impress top candidates and connect with them before anyone else with Calendly's automated scheduling.
  * [Checkr](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/204839386-Checkr-integration): Checkr powers the fastest, fairest background checks for businesses of all sizes. It's time to change the way you hire.
  * [Codility](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/202062659-Codility-integration): Gauge your developer candidates' real-life skills with deeply accurate CodeCheck assessments.
  * [Criteria Corp](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360045101352-Criteria-integration): World-leading video interviews and aptitude, personality, EI, risk, and skills tests that highlight every candidate's potential
  * [Docusign](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/205633569-Docusign-integration): Docusign helps businesses easily and securely sign, send, and manage documents in the cloud.



#### Test workflows

You can use your sandbox to test and build new configurations, such as [office and department structures](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360029179271-Offices-and-departments-overview), [custom options](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/10978274576667-Custom-options-overview), [permission policies](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/115002226606-Permission-policies-overview), [company goals](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/8382420999835-Company-goals), [inclusion tools](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360004910232-Diversity-Equity-and-Inclusion-DE-I-overview), and more. Since changes to organizational configurations can impact downstream integrations or reports, your sandbox offers a safe space to test changes before you deploy them to your production environment.

#### Test APIs

Sandboxes work with all [Greenhouse APIs](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/10568627186203-Greenhouse-API-overview), allowing you to test custom integrations, make sample requests, and ensure the payloads are what your development teams expect.

Follow these tips to test API with your sandbox successfully:

**Tip** : API keys aren't interchangeable between production and sandbox environments. You'll need to [generate a new API key](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/202842799-Generate-an-API-key-for-Greenhouse-Recruiting) in your sandbox before making any API requests.

**Tip** : Use the correct [job board token and job board URLs](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360020776251-Job-board-URL-for-Greenhouse-hosted-job-board) for your sandbox. These will be different from your production environment.

**Learn more**

[Sandbox overview](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/16904526959899)

[Sandbox FAQ](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/17057838106651)

# Troubleshoot a report

**Permissions:** Job Admin or above

**Product tier:** Available for new subscription tiers (Core, Plus, and Pro)

Greenhouse Recruiting offers a variety of tools to track and measure your hiring processes, including [essential reports](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360034704071-Essential-reports-overview), [report dashboards](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/4408761575963-Report-dashboards-overview), as well as [Report Builder](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360000954692-Report-Builder-overview) for customized reports. You can [save](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/115003218066-Save-a-report) and [email](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/115003338503-Email-a-report) your reports, or [schedule](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/115003711906-Schedule-recurring-report) reports to be shared on a regular basis.

Sometimes you may see unexpected data on a report or have trouble accessing or sharing a saved report. A few quick troubleshooting steps can help get you back on track.

#### In this article

  * Troubleshoot unexpected data
  * Troubleshoot missing data
  * [Troubleshoot Greenhouse Report Connector](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/4415874352411)
  * Unable to view or share a report
  * Report best practices



### Troubleshoot unexpected data

If you're seeing unexpected data on your report, the first thing to do is check your report filters. We recommend checking all of your filters, especially if you're comparing two different reports, as your filters determine the data that appears.

The date filter and the migrated candidates filter in particular often produce unexpected data.

Click **Filters and more** to adjust the filters on your report.

#### Is your date filter correct?

The date filter can cause unexpected data. Be sure the date is set to the time period that you want to review. Many essential reports include a default date filter, such as being set to the current quarter, or the previous week automatically. Adjust the date range to match your goal.

**Tip** : Essential reports may use different types of date filters. Check out [Which report should I use?](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/8837686136987-Which-report-should-I-use-) to understand the date filter on your specific report.

#### Are migrated candidates included in your report?

Migrated candidates are candidates whose applications were migrated from a previous ATS. Migrated candidates aren't included in our essential reports by default because we can't vouch for the integrity of the data from your prior ATS.

If you're running a report, but you aren't seeing a candidate you expect to see, check if you need to include the migrated candidates filter by clicking **Filters and more**.

### Troubleshoot missing data

If your report is missing data you expect to see, check your filters under **Filters** **and** **more**.

  * Is your report filtered to include the correct jobs?
  * Is your report filtered to the correct date?
  * Did you include migrated candidates, if necessary?
  * Is this the right report for your goal?



**Tip** : Check out [Which report should I use?](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/8837686136987-Which-report-should-I-use-) for help finding the right report.

If your filters are correct, user permissions or the permission policies set by your organization may be affecting the data you see.

#### User permissions

Reporting on Greenhouse Recruiting is dynamic, meaning you can only report on data that you have permission to view. If you aren't a Job Admin on a job, you won't be able to report on the job or its candidates.

Click your initials at the top-right of any page, then click **Account** **Settings**. Scroll to _Job Specific Roles_ to see which jobs you have permission to view. [Learn more about user permissions on Greenhouse Recruiting](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360039614171-User-permission-levels).

Does your report require a specific permission? [Check the permissions required for essential reports](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360034704071).

#### Permission policies

Organization-level permission policies may be affecting your report. For instance, the [Rejection reasons report](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/203941409-Rejection-reasons-report) benefits from the organization-level permission policy ‘Make rejection reason a required field on rejected candidates' being enabled, because if all rejected candidates have a rejection reason, you have more data to report on.

You can [learn more about permission policies here](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/115002226606-Permission-policies-overview), or reference the table below to find possible organization-level impacts on your reporting:

**Report** | **Permission policy** | **Impact**  
---|---|---  
[Rejection reasons report](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/203941409-Rejection-reasons-report) | Make rejection reason a required field on rejected candidates | This policy requires that your hiring team choose a rejection reason when rejecting candidates. Use this permission policy to improve data integrity on your reports.  
[New candidates by source report](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/204636125-New-candidates-by-source-report) | When creating a candidate, make "Source" a required field | This policy requires that your hiring team choose a source when manually adding a candidate. Use this permission policy to have more accurate source reports.  
[All jobs summary report](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/203940239-All-jobs-summary-report) | When creating a job, make "Office" a required field | This policy requires that your hiring team choose an office when creating a job. Use this permission policy to make office-level reporting more accurate.  
[All jobs summary report](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/203940239-All-jobs-summary-report) [Department summary report](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/203940739-Department-summary-report) | When creating a job, make "Department" a required field | This policy requires that your hiring team choose a department when creating a job. Use this permission policy to make department-level reporting more accurate.  
  
### Unable to view or share a report

You can email reports to colleagues, as well as schedule reports to be emailed on a regular basis.

However, emailed report URLs are only valid for 24 hours. After 24 hours, you'll receive an error message when trying to open the link.

If you are viewing a shared report within 24 hours, and you're still receiving an error message, it likely indicates that you don't have permission to view the report in Greenhouse Recruiting. You need to be Job Admin or above the view reports on jobs, and some reports have additional permission requirements. [Check the permissions required on your report](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360034704071-Essential-reports-overview).

### Best practices

If after troubleshooting you're still seeing unexpected data or missing data on your report, there are some [best practices](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/16772285562907) your organization should consider.

#### Accurate open dates

Inaccurate open dates can cause discrepancies in reports, particularly for the [Time to fill by job report](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/204635705). Make sure accurate open dates are maintained at the job and opening level. [Learn more](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/7992568877595#h_01GA6X3GBN0TVWGTZD151VW6EG).

#### Accurate application dates

If you add a candidate to Greenhouse Recruiting after you've already started considering them, [backdate their application date](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/17201325129371). Accurate application dates on candidate touchpoints ensure your pipeline reports have integrity. [Learn more](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/7992568877595#h_01GA503WWZENN0HHX2ZZXMHE1R).

#### Accurate offer dates

When hiring a candidate, double-check the opening you're hiring them against has the correct open date. Hires against inaccurate job and opening open dates can impact your [Time to fill by job report](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/204635705).

If the candidate's offer is updated in Greenhouse Recruiting on a different day than the actual offer was accepted or rejected, you should adjust those dates to reflect reality. Accurate offer dates will improve your organization's reporting. [Learn more](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/7992568877595#h_01GA5044XKC59KC7BRANW1ZJM2).

# ModernLoop integration

ModernLoop is an interview scheduling platform that automates coordination, reduces manual effort, and improves the candidate experience.

ModernLoop’s integration with Greenhouse Recruiting allows users to seamlessly sync candidate data, automate interview scheduling workflows, and manage interview logistics directly from ModernLoop.

#### In this article

  * Configure the ModernLoop integration
  * Use the ModernLoop integration
  * Additional resources



### Configure the ModernLoop integration

ModernLoop integrates with Greenhouse via the Harvest API, enabling reliable, real-time data syncing across your hiring workflows.

**Step 1:** Authorize the Greenhouse integration in ModernLoop at the organization level

  1. In ModernLoop, navigate to **Organization** **Settings → Organization → Integrations**  
****
  2. Click **Connect** next to **Greenhouse (Harvest V3 - OAuth)**  
****
  3. Enter your **service account email address (site admin)** and click**Log in to Greenhouse**  
****
  4. **Log in to Greenhouse** using your service account credentials
  5. Select **Authorize using a service account** , then click **Authorize**  
****
  6. Once complete, you'll be redirected back to ModernLoop.



**Step 2:** Authorize at the personal level (recommended)

To ensure scheduling actions are correctly attributed to you in Greenhouse reporting, connect your personal account as well:

  1. Navigate to **Your account → Personal Preferences**  
****
  2. Select the **Integrations** tab  
****
  3. Select **Connect** next to **Greenhouse**  

  4. Enter your email and click **Log in to Greenhouse**

****

  5. Leave "_Authorize using a service account_ " **UNCHECKED** , then click **Authorize**  
****  

  6. You’ll be redirected back to ModernLoop once complete.



### Use the ModernLoop integration

Once connected, ModernLoop and Greenhouse work together to streamline scheduling and provide full visibility into the interview process.

#### Install the ModernLoop Chrome Extension

To get started, install the ModernLoop Chrome Extension:

  1. In ModernLoop, navigate to **Your account → Personal Preferences**
  2. Select the **Integrations** tab
  3. Click **Connect** next to **Chrome Extension**  

  4. Return to Greenhouse and refresh the page



The ModernLoop extension will appear directly within Greenhouse, allowing you to take action without leaving the candidate profile.

#### Access ModernLoop from a candidate profile

From any candidate profile in Greenhouse, open the ModernLoop extension to:

  * View synced candidate details
  * Create and manage scheduling tasks
  * Launch scheduling workflows
  * Quickly navigate between ModernLoop and Greenhouse



#### Automatically Sync Candidate Information

ModernLoop automatically syncs key candidate data from Greenhouse, including:

  * Hiring team
  * Job and job stage
  * Candidate profile details



This ensures scheduling workflows always reflect the most up-to-date information. You can also navigate back to the candidate’s Greenhouse profile at any time.

#### Sync Candidate Availability

When a candidate submits availability through Greenhouse’s **Request Availability** feature, their availability is automatically reflected in ModernLoop.

This allows coordinators to immediately access submitted time slots and build interview schedules without manual entry

#### Sync job setup and interview plans

ModernLoop mirrors your Greenhouse interview configuration, including:

  * Interview stages
  * Interview types and durations
  * Associated scorecards



This eliminates duplicate setup and keeps both systems aligned.

#### Sync communications and activity back to Greenhouse

All scheduling activity in ModernLoop is logged in Greenhouse, including:

  * Candidate communications
  * Scheduled interviews and updates
  * Coordination notes and debrief activity



These updates are posted to the candidate’s **Activity Feed** in Greenhouse, giving your team full visibility into the scheduling process without needing to switch tools.

### Additional resources

For additional information or support, please contact:

**ModernLoop Support:**[ support@modernloop.io](mailto:support@modernloop.io)

**ModernLoop Help Center:**[ https://help.modernloop.io/](https://help.modernloop.io/)

# Docusign integration

[Docusign](https://www.docusign.com/) pioneered the development of cloud-based e-signature technology, helping organizations of all sizes securely connect and automate how they prepare, sign, act on, and manage digital agreements.

Greenhouse Recruiting's integration with Docusign allows your team to add specialized tokens to your created offer templates so candidate offer documents are efficiently generated and sent out for signature with ease.

**Tip** : The Docusign integration can be used by all organizations, regardless of your Docusign subscription tier. However, some Docusign functionality may be limited based on your Docusign subscription. Reach out to your Docusign account manager for questions on[ the appropriate plan](https://www.docusign.com/plans-and-pricing) for your team. To experience full integration functionality, Docusign recommends a Business Pro plan.

#### In this article

  * Enable the integration
    * Add Docusign tokens to offer document templates
  * Use the integration
    * Send an offer document with Docusign
    * Track signatures and access signed offer letters



### Enable the Docusign integration

Each team member at your organization who wants to use the integration needs to follow the setup instructions outlined in this article, including users who don't send documents but may need to sign them.

**Note** : The Docusign integration can't be set up at once for an entire organization.

To enable Docusign for your Greenhouse Recruiting account, click **Integrations** on your navigation bar, then search for and select **Docusign**. Click **Connect**.

Enter your Docusign credentials, then click **Accept** to grant Greenhouse Recruiting permission to access your Docusign account.

You'll be redirected back to Greenhouse Recruiting, where the integration will indicate it's connected.

**Note** : If you use SSO, you may be redirected to your authentication provider for Docusign. You need to be on the new version of SSO that Docusign supports. Send-on-behalf-of settings don't need to be configured within Docusign before enabling the integration and sending out offers.

#### Add Docusign tokens to offer document templates

After Docusign is enabled for your account, 8 additional offer document tokens will become available to include in any[ offer document templates](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/6459061824155):

  * `{{CANDIDATE_SIGNATURE}}`
  * `{{CANDIDATE_SIGNATURE_DATE}}`
  * `{{CANDIDATE_ADDRESS}}`
  * `{{CANDIDATE_INITIALS}}`
  * `{{COMPANY_SIGNATURE}}`
  * `{{COMPANY_SIGNATURE_DATE}}`
  * `{{COMPANY_SIGNER_NAME}}`
  * `{{COMPANY_SIGNER_JOB_TITLE}}`
  * `{{CANDIDATE_TEXT_INPUT#}} `
  * `{{CANDIDATE_LONG_TEXT_INPUT#}} `
  * `{{COMPANY_SIGNER_TEXT_INPUT#}} `
  * `{{COMPANY_SIGNER_LONG_TEXT_INPUT#}}`



**Note:** For multiple text inputs, you can use the same Docusign Tokens, but change the number in the token for each new group of text. For example, to add a second text input, use {{CANDIDATE_TEXT_INPUT2}}

The placement of your Docusign tokens on offer templates determines where electronic signatures, dates, and other details show up on the offer document.

**Note** : If your organization has existing [custom offer tokens](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/200871485) with the same name as any of the Docusign tokens, your custom offer token will take precedence, and the Docusign token will not work properly. You should consider [editing any matching custom offer tokens](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/19337788166683) if you intend to use the Docusign integration.

The Docusign integration originally launched with a single signature token, `{{SIGNATURE_DATE}}`. While we strongly recommend you update any existing offer document templates to use the new tokens, the legacy token `{{SIGNATURE_DATE}}` is still supported.

Use a document editor like Google Docs or Microsoft Word to edit your offer template and add the Docusign tokens as desired.

**Note** : Docusign tokens must be on their own line on offer templates to work correctly.

#### Example

After modifying offer templates to include the Docusign tokens, [re-upload the templates](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/6459061824155) to Greenhouse Recruiting.

**Note** : Job Admin need the user-specific permission 'Can manage offer templates' to modify existing offer templates, while Site Admin need the user-specific permission 'Can see private notes, salary info, manage offers, request approvals, and approve jobs/offers'. [Learn more](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360020849292) about user-specific permissions.

To upload offer templates, click the **Configure** icon  on your navigation bar, then select **Offer Templates** on the left. Click **\+ Upload New**.

Fill in the appropriate fields, and click **Choose File** to locate the offer template on your computer.

When finished, click **Save Template**.

Next, test the template the check your document for any unsupported tokens. Find the offer template and click **Test**.

If all tokens in the template are supported, the template status will read _Verified_.

**Note:** If an error occurs, confirm Docusign is enabled for your account. [Learn more](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/115003014126) about troubleshooting offer template tokens.

### Use the integration with Greenhouse Recruiting

#### Generate and send an offer document with Docusign

**Notes** :

  * The Docusign integration can only be used for candidates who are active in the offer stage in Greenhouse Recruiting. It's not possible to utilize Docusign with earlier stages in your interview plan. For additional documents that may require candidate review like NDAs, check out the [Forms](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360019478952) feature.
  * You can only send offer letters from your own email address.
  * If the offer document you've generated includes the `{{COMPANY_SIGNATURE}}` token, select the appropriate person to sign on behalf of your company using the **To User** field. Users with [job-based permissions assigned](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360040181991) on the job can be selected on the **To User** dropdown. If someone doesn't appear that you expect to see, [check their permissions](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360020855632).



After you [generated your offer document](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/200721744), click **Send with Docusign** under the offer details.

Finish the offer email and click **Preview on Docusign**.

On Docusign, you'll see your offer document tokens have populated signature fields. You can add additional fields, change the signing order, and modify interactions using the panel on the left.

Select the **Settings** icon at the top-right > **Edit** **Documents** to edit, add, and configure documents.

Select **Actions** at the top > **Edit** **Recipients** to edit the signing order.

Toggle **Set signing order** , then order the signers. Click **Done**.

You can also set expiration timers on the offer. Click **Actions** > **Advanced** **Options** to explore additional settings.

When you're ready to send the letter, click **Send.**

The offer document will be delivered to the recipients you chose. Docusign wraps documents in [envelopes](https://support.docusign.com/s/articles/000045001?language=en_US&rsc_301#:~:text=At%20DocuSign%2C%20an%20envelope%20is,signers%20will%20sign%20the%20documents.), which are digital containers holding one or more documents for sending, signing, and tracking your e-signature documents.

#### Track signatures and access signed offer letters

Once an offer document is sent with Docusign, you can check on the status of the document within Greenhouse Recruiting on the candidate's **Offer** **Details** tab.

Check out the table below more information on the offer status:

– | A dash indicates the offer document has been sent to the candidate by Docusign and is awaiting action from the candidate.  
---|---  
Pending | Pending indicates the candidate has reviewed the offer document sent by Docusign, but has not yet signed it.  
01/01/2024 | A date indicates the candidate or counter-signer has signed the offer document on this date.  
  
The person who sent the offer document will receive email notifications when all of the signatures have been collected.

After all signatures are collected, a fully signed letter will be uploaded to the candidate's profile and accessible on the candidate's **Details** tab under the _All Attachments_ section.

**Learn more**

[Troubleshoot Docusign](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/115002421126)

[Docusign FAQ](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/14659656686107)

# Rehire an employee in Greenhouse Onboarding

**Permissions:** Owner

**Product tier:** Available for Greenhouse Welcome and Greenhouse Onboarding subscription tiers

If a former employee has been rehired and is joining your organization again, you can rehire them in Greenhouse Onboarding and retrieve their original profile.

**Example:** An intern who worked for your organization last summer has now returned as a full-time employee! You can rehire this employee in Greenhouse Onboarding to reopen their employee profile.

#### In this article

  * How it works
  * Rehire an employee
  * Additional resources



### How it works

You can use the rehire flow if the former employee's original [employee profile](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/5759718119707) is still in Greenhouse Onboarding and their [employment status](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360045429531) is marked as **terminated**.

You'll use the Greenhouse Onboarding rehire flow to:

  * Avoid duplicate employee profiles
  * Clear out and update field values for the rehired employee
  * Update the employment status and start date
  * Assign a new onboarding plan to the rehired employee



**Note:** Only users with [Owner access](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360019575491) can rehire employees in Greenhouse Onboarding.

### Rehire an employee

To start the rehire process, navigate to your Greenhouse Onboarding homepage and [add a new hire](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360000683352).

On the _Add New Hire_ page, enter the former employee's **First Name** , **Last Name** , and the **Work Email** that was used to set up their original profile.

You don't need to fill out any other required fields.

**Tip:** You can find a terminated employee's original email in the **Info** tab of their employee profile. Terminated employee profiles are still available to search in Greenhouse Onboarding.

Next, click **Review Onboarding Plan**.

Greenhouse Onboarding will recognize the duplicate information and will ask you to confirm that you'd like to rehire the employee.

Click **Rehire Employee**.

From there, you can assign a new [onboarding plan](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360000508312-Onboarding-Plan-Overview) to the rehired employee.

### Additional resources

  * [Add a new hire and assign their onboarding plan](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360000683352)
  * [Terminate employees](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360000866892)

# Resend a take home test

**Permissions:** Site Admin, and Job admin who can email candidates/prospects

**Product tier:** Available for new subscription tiers (Core, Plus, and Pro)

Sometimes, a candidate will lose track of a take-home test email and need a new link for their test. You can quickly resend a take home test on the candidate's profile.

_**Note:** This article only applies to take home tests created through Greenhouse Recruiting. [Partner take home tests](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/201156035) cannot be resent._

#### In this article

  * Resend a take home test (test not submitted)
  * Resend a take home test (test submitted)



### Resend a take home test (test not submitted)

If a take home test has not been submitted by a candidate yet, the test can be resent directly Take Home Test stage on their candidate profile. Any unsubmitted take home tests will be located under the **Pending** tab.

Hover on the take home test and click Resend to restart the take home test email process for the candidate.

### Resend a take home test after a test has been submitted

If the candidate has submitted a completed a take home test already, or if a user has manually uploaded a completed test on the candidate's behalf, you won't be able to use the **Resend Test** button.

Instead, you'll need to manually create and resend the take home test to the candidate. You can do this by using the Email button in the top right corner of the candidate profile. 

Use the _Email_ window to write an email to the candidate. Replace the subject line and body with the content from the initial take home test email. If you want to use the existing take home test language, you can use the Activity Feed to find the copy-and-paste the information from the previous email.

However, when manually sending take home tests, you won't be able to re-use assessment links and should direct the candidate to send their completed test in an email reply.

Once the candidate's test is received, you'll need to manually [replace the submitted test file](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/115004494683) in the candidate profile.

# Rejection reason requirement

**Permissions:** Site Admin who can edit another user's advanced permissions

**Product tier:** Available for new subscription tiers (Core, Plus, and Pro)

A rejection reason is a configurable field when rejecting a candidate or prospect from a job and is categorized into three main types:

  * We rejected them
  * They Rejected us
  * None specified



By default, rejection reasons are **required** whenever a candidate and/or prospect is [rejected](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360025225732) in your organization. 

If your organization chooses not to enforce a required rejection reason, you can deactivate this requirement in your account settings. 

To begin, navigate to the **Permission Policies** configure page. (**Configure icon** > **Permissions Policies**). 

**Uncheck** the box  _When rejecting a candidate, make "Rejection Reason" a required field_

**Note** : If your organization has deactivated the rejection reason requirement and would like to enforce the requirement again, follow the above steps to add a check in the appropriate checkbox.

# Structured hiring: Candidate roundup

A candidate roundup meeting is held at the end of a structured hiring process so that you can make a hiring decision based on the process you just completed. A successful candidate roundup should accomplish three things:

  1. Decision on who you will extend an offer to
  2. Create a shortlist of actions required to make an offer
  3. Review the hiring process your team has just finished and learn how you can improve for next time.



The candidate roundup meeting provides a space for your hiring team to come together and systematically review the data gathered from the interview process and make a hiring decision. Prior to this meeting, confirm that all interviewer feedback is complete. 

When evaluating candidates, stick to the [scorecard attributes](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360003464191) rather than relying on summations or generalizations.

# Resume-Library integration

Resume-Library is America's fastest-growing job board offering flexible hiring packages. Users can post their jobs across 100+ specialist sites in Resume-Library's network, and search for over 13 million candidates from every industry nationwide.

Greenhouse Recruiting's integration with Resume-Library allows you to seamlessly search and view resumes in Resume-Library's database until you find the perfect match for your jobs. Once you have found the perfect candidate, simply unlock their resume and import their details straight into your Greenhouse Recruiting account! In this article, we will cover how to:

#### In this article

  * Create a Harvest API key for the Resume-Library integration
    * Credentials
    * Permissions
  * Use the Resume-Library integration with Greenhouse Recruiting
  * Additional resources



### Create a Harvest API key for the Resume-Library integration

To configure the Greenhouse Recruiting / Resume-Library integration, you'll need to create a Harvest API key.

Follow the steps in [this article](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/5888163769883) to create the key, and verify that the credentials and permissions below are selected when configuring the Resume-Library integration.

#### Credentials

In the _Create New Credential_ box, make the following selections:

  * **API Type** : Harvest
  * **Partner** : Resume-Library
  * **Description** : _Resume-Library Harvest API Key_



#### Permissions

Verify that the following permissions are selected for the Resume-Library integration:

**Candidates**

  * All permissions



**Sources**

  * All permissions



**User Roles**

  * All permissions



**Users**

  * All permissions



Please provide your Harvest API key to your Resume-Library onboarding team so they can set up the integration.

### Use the Resume-Library integration with Greenhouse Recruiting

Follow the following steps to use the integration:

  1. **Log into** your Resume-Library account and hover over the **cog** icon to surface the dropdown menu
  2. From the dropdown, select **Integrated Services**
  3. Locate _Greenhouse_ and switch the toggle to **On** , then click **Re-authenticate**
  4. Next, enter your **Harvest API key** created in Greenhouse Recruiting, and click **Authenticate**



Click **Search Resumes**. Enter your search criteria, then click **Search Resumes** again.

All matching candidates on Resume-Library are displayed in your search results.

To open a candidate's resume, click **Preview Resume**.

Once you find a candidate you like, click **Unlock Resume**.

**Note:** If you do not have any remaining credits on your account, you will be prompted to purchase more.

Once a candidate is unlocked, you can import their details to your Greenhouse Recruiting account.

To do this, click **ATS Import** and choose **Greenhouse** from the dropdown menu. Then, click **Import**.

To view the candidates in your Greenhouse Recruiting account, click **Candidates** in the navigation bar.

Next, expand the **Application Type** filter on the left-hand side and set the _Type_ dropdown to **Prospects only**.

Then, expand the **Source** filter and set the _Source_ dropdown to **Resume Library**.

This allows you to view a list of all candidates imported from Resume-Library.

**Note:** It may take up to five minutes for candidates to appear in Greenhouse Recruiting after exporting from Resume-Library.

For assistance setting up access to Resume-Library, call Resume-Library's team at 1-800-672-6706, or email [greenhouse@resume-library.com](mailto:greenhouse@resume-library.com).

# HRIS Link best practices

**Permissions:** **—**

**Product tier:** Available for Pro subscription tier with HRIS Link add-on

HRIS Link can programmatically sync updates from your HRIS to Greenhouse Recruiting for [jobs](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360058912031), [users](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360058975731), and [offices / departments](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360058975151). By adopting best practices when configuring HRIS Link, you can optimize the integration to work for your recruiting process.

#### In this article

  * Use structured custom field types
  * Sync custom field options with your HRIS
  * Plan out your job templates
  * Simplify your office and department structure
  * Create a dedicated HRIS Link user
  * Use report filters to optimize performance
  * Additional resources



### Use structured custom field types

We strongly recommend not using custom fields with field types _short textbox_ or _long textbox_. Instead, the structured field types below allow you to validate, filter, and report on Greenhouse Recruiting data more effectively:

  * Single-select
  * Multi-select
  * Date
  * Boolean
  * User
  * Currency
  * Number
  * Currency range
  * Number range



### Sync custom field options with your HRIS

We recommend implementing custom field options syncing for any single- or multi-select custom field that has a large number of options, or whose options change frequently over time. By syncing field options with an HRIS report, you can be assured any selectable fields in your HRIS also exist as field options in Greenhouse Recruiting.

For more information on custom field options syncing, check out this article: [Custom options sync overview](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360044483232).

### Plan out your job templates

When using HRIS Link for job imports, you should carefully plan out the job templates you'll use. If you opt to use multiple job templates, we recommend:

  * Limiting the number of job templates to fewer than 10;
  * Ensuring well-defined logic exists to automate the job template selection.



To help you decide how many job templates will best suit your organization, check out this article: [Decision guide: Template jobs](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360013450271).

### Simplify your office and department structure

In order to reduce the need for system maintenance, we recommend simplifying your organizational structure in Greenhouse Recruiting as much as possible. Strive for the fewest number of offices and departments. This allows for streamlining other configurations like:

  * User permissions
  * Job and offer approvals
  * Job board configurations
  * Dashboard and reporting filters
  * Custom field configurations
  * Email template and offer templates



For more details on the downstream impacts of your office / department structure, check out these articles: [Office and department-dependent workflows](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360029591631) and [Tiered offices and departments](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/211537106).

### Create a dedicated HRIS Link user

HRIS Link requires a Site Admin's user ID to work with Greenhouse Recruiting. We recommend creating a dedicated integration system user (ISU) called _HRIS Link_ , which ensures the user account is not linked to a specific individual. Check out this article to learn more about using ISUs with HRIS Link: [How to create a Greenhouse Recruiting integration system user (ISU) for HRIS Link](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360060056451).

### Use report filters to optimize performance

To ensure optimal performance, we recommend applying specific filters to the reports that drive each aspect of your HRIS Link integration. For a full list of filters, check out these articles: 

  * [Setup HRIS Link job import with job requisitions enabled](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/4403889907355)
  * [Setup HRIS Link job import without 'job requisitions' enabled](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/4403988430235)
  * [Setup HRIS Link office and department import](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360058921191)
  * [Setup HRIS Link user import](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360058479852)



### Additional resources

  * [Manage HRIS Link ISUs and reports](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/11006737633307)
  * [FAQ: Import jobs with HRIS Link](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360058731532)
  * [FAQ: HRIS Link office and department import](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360059152791)
  * [FAQ: HRIS Link user import](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360059153471)

# Troubleshoot the Docusign integration

If you encounter an error when sending offer letters with the Docusign integration, a few troubleshooting steps can help get you back on track.

#### In this article

  * Common errors
    * Re-connect your Docusign account
    * The envelope specified doesn't exist or you have no rights to it
    * System was unable to convert this document to a .pdf
    * This user is not the sender of the envelope
  * Full list of errors



### Common errors

#### Please re-connect your Docusign account and try again

To resolve this error, disconnect and reconnect the Docusign integration. This process refreshes your Docusign credentials.

To disconnect the Docusign integration, log in to Greenhouse Recruiting, and click **Integrations** on your navigation bar.

Scroll to the _Manage Integrations_ section and click **Docusign** > **Disconnect**.

A banner at the top of the page will confirm the integration has been disconnected.

Click **Connect** to re-enter your account credentials and refresh the integration.

**Tip** : Check out [Docusign integration](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/205633569) to access the full integration setup process.

After reconnecting the Docusign integration, return to the candidate profile and attempt to resend the offer.

If you continue to experience this error, [connect with Greenhouse Technical Support](https://support.greenhouse.io/direct).

#### The envelope specified either does not exist or you have no rights to it

There are a few possible causes of this error. Typically this error indicates that the person attempting to send the offer wasn't the original sender of the offer. If another Greenhouse Recruiting user previously created and sent the offer, only they can resend the updated offer.

The error can also result if the offer was sent more than 30 days ago, or if the offer itself has been deleted.

If these conditions don't match your scenario, [disconnect and reconnect the Docusign integration](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/205633569) and see if the issue persists.

If the error persists, reach out to [Docusign support](https://support.docusign.com/s/contactSupport?language=en_US).

#### System was unable to convert this document to a PDF

This error indicates that Docusign is unable to convert the offer file attempted into a PDF file. [Regenerate the offer documents](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/200485589) and attempt to send the offer with Docusign again.

If the error persists, [connect with Greenhouse Technical Support](https://support.greenhouse.io/direct).

#### This user is not the sender of the envelope. Only the sender of the envelope may perform this requested operation

Only the person who created the original offer can [replace it](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/201093394) with a new version. Other people who attempt to update or send a new offer will encounter this error.

If you receive an error, reach out to the original offer creator to have them [delete or replace the agreements](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/201093394).

You can also void the offer's envelope in Docusign directly. [Learn more](https://support.docusign.com/s/document-item?dscj_ft=https%253A%252F%252Fwww.google.com%252F%2C1682288924%2Chttps%253A%252F%252Fwww.docusign.co.uk%252Fblog%252Fquick-tip-setting-signing-order&dscj_lt=https%253A%252F%252Fwww.google.com%252F%2C1682288924%2Chttps%253A%252F%252Fwww.docusign.co.uk%252Fblog%252Fquick-tip-setting-signing-order&dscj_m=referringUrl%2Cts%2Ccu&language=en_US&rsc_301&_gl=1*ayw7d2*_ga*MTgyMzkwOTEwOS4xNjgyMjg4OTI2*_ga_1TZ7S9D6BQ*MTY4MjI4ODkyNS4xLjAuMTY4MjI4ODkyNS42MC4wLjA.&_ga=2.255427147.2123661385.1682288926-1823909109.1682288926&bundleId=oeq1643226594604&topicId=zyn1578456424164.html&_LANG=enus) from Docusign support.

### Full list of errors

If your error or scenario isn't listed here, you can [view a full list of errors](https://developers.docusign.com/docs/esign-rest-api/esign101/error-codes/) provided by Docusign support.

**Learn more**

[Docusign integration](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/205633569)

[Docusign FAQ](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/14659656686107)

# Create a tracking link for a job board

**Permissions:** Job Admin and above

**Product tier:** Available for new subscription tiers (Core, Plus, and Pro)

**Note** : A job board must be Live before you can create a tracking link.

Tracking links are unique URLs that allow your organization to track a candidate's source when they apply for a job. While your organization can create [tracking links for individual job posts](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/4405093302427), you can also create a tracking link for an entire job board.

**Example** : If your organization plans to share a job board through a marketing campaign, Greenhouse Recruiting recommends that you generate a tracking link for the job board so you can track the source for candidates entering your system via the campaign.

#### In this article

  * Create a tracking link for your job board via the Configure page



### Create a tracking link for your job board via the Configure page

Click the **Configure** icon  on your navigation bar and select **Job Board & Posts** on the left.

Find a job board on the subsequent  _Job Boards_ list and click the **Ellipsis** beside the job board name. Click **Tracking Link** from the dropdown.

Use the _Get a Tracking Link_ box to configure the _Who gets credit_ and _Source_ fields.

**Note:** Only people who have signed into Greenhouse Recruiting can be selected to receive credit. People who have a Greenhouse Recruiting account but have not signed into the platform will not appear as options in the _Who gets credit_ dropdown.

Click **Create Link** when finished.

A tracking link for the job board is generated in the provided field. **Copy** the tracking link and share it with the appropriate parties.

When the tracking link is added to the address field in a browser, the tracking link is updated and consists of two parts: the **job board URL** and the **Source Token**. The Source Token is an auto-generated combination of letters and numbers used to identify the unique link. You can find the source token after the **gh_src=** part of the URL. 

[Click here](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/216902526) to learn more about using the tracking link to track the candidate's source based on your job board integration. 

**Note:** If you are generating the link for an external / third-party job board, paste the tracking link wherever you are providing instructions as to where candidates should go to apply. Many external job boards have a special field for links to the application, but some may have only a free-text entry box where you will need to write your own text and then paste the link.

# Invite an agency recruiter to submit candidates

**Permissions:** Site Admin, and Job Admin who can invite and deactivate agency recruiters

**Product tier:** Available for new subscription tiers (Core, Plus, and Pro)

An [agency](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/201078255) must have at least one agency recruiter configured in your Greenhouse Recruiting account in order to submit job candidates through [Agencies](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/202924839). 

#### In this article

  * Invite an agency recruiter
  * Troubleshooting agency recruiter invites



### Invite an agency recruiter

**Note:** Multiple agency recruiters can use the same profile to submit candidates or prospects if a shared email address is used to create an agency recruiter profile in Greenhouse Recruiting.

In your Greenhouse Recruiting account, navigate to **Configure** > **Agencies**.

Click**Add recruiter**.

Select an existing agency from the **Agency** dropdown.

**Note:** If you haven't added the recruiting agency to your account yet, click **Create new agency** to add the agency first.

Enter the agency recruiter's **email** , then click **Create recruiter**.

Greenhouse Recruiting sends an invitation to the email address you've provided. Agency recruiters will use the link in their invitation email to set up an account in [Agencies](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/202924839) and begin submitting job candidates.

When an agency recruiter [submits a candidate](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/202924839-Guide-for-agency-recruiters-#h_f50e10bd-c1e9-4f05-8e4b-19ac51481988) in Agencies, the candidate's **Source** will be the agency and the candidate's **Referrer** will be the agency recruiter. 

### Troubleshooting agency recruiter invites

When inviting a new agency recruiter to your organization's Greenhouse Recruiting account, you could encounter an error stating the email address already exists or has been invited.

These types of error messages suggest the agency recruiter's email address might have previously been added to your organization's account or another Greenhouse customer's account [as a full user](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/115002713363) instead of as an agency recruiter.

**Note:** We don't recommend granting external individual access to your organization's Greenhouse Recruiting account as [a full user](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360027077811), but recognize external recruiters sometimes consult for specific requirements or overall systems for periods of time. 

In most cases, this error message means you need to request the agency recruiter provide an alternate email address to use for their agency recruiter profile, as the address they've provided is already used in the Greenhouse Recruiting system. An email address can be used only once across the entire Greenhouse Recruiting database, whether as a full user or as an agency recruiter.

[Click here](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/requests/new) to contact the Greenhouse Technical Support team for troubleshooting assistance regarding this error if needed.

# Add pay transparency to a job post

**Permissions:** Job Admin and above who can create, edit, and delete job posts

**Product tier:** Available for new subscription tiers (Core, Plus, and Pro)

Pay transparency rules are created by your Site Admin. When you select a rule during the [job post](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/sections/360000691932) configuration, then the required pay range fields appear. 

**Note:** Consult with your legal team if you have questions about local pay transparency laws and how it affects your organization.

#### In this article

  * Add pay transparency to a job post
  * Use pay transparency with the Job Board and/or Harvest API
    * Job Board API 
    * Harvest API
  * Troubleshooting guide
    * Rule synced to custom field with empty pay range
    * Rule no longer syncs with updates to custom field values
  * Additional resources



### Add pay transparency to a job post

Navigate to the _Post Details_ section and select a **rule(s)** from the _p_ _ay transparency_ dropdown. 

Key points to keep in mind:

  * The dropdown is unavailable if a rule hasn't been created yet
  * Rules pre-populate if your Site Admin configured the rule to auto-fill for this office. Click the **X** next to any rules that don't apply
  * Select **N/A** if pay transparency isn't required for this job post
  * Refer to the Troubleshooting guide if you receive an error once selecting a rule



Next, scroll down to the _pay transparency_ section. The description and title are configured by the Site Admin and can't be modified on this page. 

Select the **currency** from the dropdown and enter a **pay range**. This information may be pre-filled if your Site Admin linked the rule to a custom field. 

Navigate to the _Post Description_ section and **remove any pay details** that were manually added as needed.

When done, scroll to the bottom of the page and click **preview** to see how the job post appears for candidates.

Click **Save** to finalize your changes.

### Use pay transparency with the Job Board and/or Harvest API

#### Job Board API 

When using pay transparency rules, customers and partners utilizing the [Greenhouse Recruiting Job Board API](https://developers.greenhouse.io/job-board.html) will need to confirm the query parameters `pay_transparency` and/or `pay_input_ranges` in the [GET: Retrieve a job](https://developers.greenhouse.io/job-board.html#retrieve-a-job) endpoint have been set to `true` to return pay transparency data.

If a job post has pay transparency rules enabled, you or your developer team can add the query parameters `=true` to the end of the endpoint above to confirm pay transparency data is returned.

If a job post contains an introduction and / or conclusion, the entire description (introduction, pay transparency, post description, and conclusion) will be combined and appear in the existing [`content`](https://developers.greenhouse.io/harvest.html#get-retrieve-job-post-for-job) field.

#### Harvest API

For customers and partners using Greenhouse [Harvest API](developers.greenhouse.io/harvest.html), the following four endpoints will return pay transparency:

  * <https://developers.greenhouse.io/harvest.html#get-list-job-posts>
  * <https://developers.greenhouse.io/harvest.html#get-retrieve-job-post>
  * <https://developers.greenhouse.io/harvest.html#get-list-job-posts-for-job>
  * <https://developers.greenhouse.io/harvest.html#get-retrieve-job-post-for-job>



To obtain pay transparency details, add the query parameter `?full_content=true` to the end of the four endpoints above.

Adding this query parameter will return the entire description (introduction, job post, pay transparency, conclusion) in either the `content` field (for external posts) or the `internal_content` field (for internal posts).

[Click here](https://developers.greenhouse.io/harvest.html) to read more about using Greenhouse Harvest API.

### Troubleshooting guide

#### Rule synced to custom field with empty pay range

You'll receive an error message when you select a rule that's linked to a custom field with an empty pay range. Since your Site Admin marked this rule as uneditable on the job post, you'll need to update the pay range from the job itself. 

**Note:** The following troubleshooting can only be completed by Job Admins who **can edit job info**.

Follow these instructions to add a pay range to your job post:

  1. Open a **new tab**(to avoid losing your existing job post edits)
  2. Navigate to **Greenhouse Recruiting** > **Job** > **Job Setup** > **Job Info** or navigate to the job using your integration 
  3. Add the **pay range** to the custom field
  4. **S****ave** your changes
  5. Return to the **job post tab** from your browser
  6. Click the **X** next to the rule and **re-select** it from the dropdown  




The pay range added to the job is now synced with the pay transparency rule on the job post. 

Finish completing the section, Add pay transparency to a job post.

#### Rule no longer syncs with updates to custom field values

When your Site Admin links the rule to a custom field, any updates to the custom field values also sync with the pay range on the job post. 

However, the rule stops syncing with the custom field when you manually change the pay range on the job post.

Follow these steps to reset the link:

  1. Navigate to the **job post**
  2. Click the **X** next to the rule linked to the custom field and **re-select** it from the dropdown  

  3. **Save** the job post



The connection between the rule and the custom field is now restored. 

### Additional resources

  * [Configure pay transparency rules](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/10027759675931)
  * [Pay transparency overview](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/13304010418075)

# HR Cloud integration

HR Cloud is a leading developer of HR software & HRMS solutions for small- and medium-sized businesses that have high turnover. Founded in 2012, the HR Cloud HRIS empowers teams to easily onboard new hires, manage employee data, create a company social network, and support employee development.

Greenhouse Recruiting's integration with HR Cloud allows you to automatically move newly hired candidates from Greenhouse Recruiting to the HR Cloud system. In this article, we will cover:

#### In this article

  * Enable integration in HR Cloud
  * Create a webhook
  * Use the HR Cloud integration with Greenhouse Recruiting
  * Additional resources



### Enable integration in HR Cloud

Navigate to <https://corehr.hrcloud.com> and log in as an HR administrator role.

Click **Settings** in the left-hand panel.

From the _Settings_ page, navigate to the _Integrations_ panel and click **Greenhouse.io**.

Click the **toggle** next to _Greenhouse.io Integration_ so a checkmark appears.

Copy and save the **Endpoint URL** and **Secret key**. This information is used in the next step.

Next, click **Configure Greenhouse.io Web Hooks**. The page redirects to Greenhouse Recruiting. Follow the steps in the next section of this article to create the webhook. 

### Create a webhook

To integrate HR Cloud with Greenhouse Recruiting, you'll need to create a webhook. Follow the steps in [this article](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/5888163727003) to create your webhook. Use the values listed below to configure the webhooks.

  * **Name** : HR Cloud integration
  * **When** : Candidate has been hired
  * **Endpoint URL** : Enter the Endpoint URL copied from HR Cloud
  * **Secret Key** : Enter the Secret key copied from HR Cloud



If you want a user at your organization to be notified if the webhook encounters an error, enter the **user's email address** in the _Error recipient email_ field.

### Use the HR Cloud integration with Greenhouse Recruiting

The following fields are mapped automatically between Greenhouse Recruiting and HR Cloud:

Greenhouse field | HRC field  
---|---  
Offer salary | Salary  
Offer bonus | Bonus  
First name | First name  
Last name | Last name  
Candidate work phone | Work phone  
Candidate mobile | Mobile phone  
Job name | Position  
Job office | Location  
Job department | Department  
Offer employmenttype | Employment type  
Offer starts at | Start date  
  
### Additional resources

After using the integration, you may decide to share more information between Greenhouse Recruiting and HR Cloud.

If you would like additional information transferred when new hires are added to HR Cloud, please reach out to the HR Cloud Customer Success team at [support@hrcloud.com](mailto:support@hrcloud.com).

# Idealist integration

Idealist is a nonprofit organization that offers job and internship postings on its site. With a mission to help build a world where all people can lead free and dignified lives, the job board offers low-cost job listings for nonprofits, government agencies, social enterprises, and other social businesses.

Greenhouse Recruiting's integration with Idealist allows your organization to automatically post your jobs to the Idealist job board.

#### In this article

  * Find your job board token
  * Enable the Idealist integration
  * Use the Idealist integration with Greenhouse Recruiting



### Find your job board token

To make your job posts available to Idealist, you'll need to send your job board URL / job board token to Idealist.

You can find your job board URL by navigating to **Configure** > **Job Boards & Posts **> **Ellipsis** icon next to your job board > **Edit Board Settings** , then scroll to the URL field.

Once you have this URL, copy it to send to Idealist in the next step.

[Click here](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/5888210160155) for a more detailed walkthrough of locating your job board URL.

### Enable the Idealist integration

Next, contact Idealist by visiting their _Contact_ page or by emailing [support@idealist.org](mailto:support@idealist.org) to request they enable the Greenhouse Recruiting / Idealist integration with your organization's existing Idealist account.

  * Be sure to contact Idealist using an email address listed as an administrator on your organization's Idealist account.
  * Be sure to include your job board token in the message.



Once the Idealist team confirms the integration is complete, you'll be able to access the Greenhouse Recruiting menu within your organization's Idealist Dashboard!

### Use the Idealist integration with Greenhouse Recruiting

From the Idealist Dashboard, log into your Administrator account and click **Greenhouse** on the left.

The _Greenhouse Integration_ page allows you to manage how jobs are shared from your Greenhouse Recruiting job board with Idealist, as well as view all of your organization's jobs that are currently posted on Greenhouse Recruiting.

Click **Enable auto-publish** to post all job posts currently on your Greenhouse Recruiting job board to Idealist. Additionally, any future jobs you post to Greenhouse Recruiting will automatically be posted to Idealist.

**Note:** This option requires you to purchase [Job Credit Packs](https://help.idealist.org/s/article/job-and-internship-packs?language=en_US) from Idealist. Each job posted in this way will spend one (1) Credit.

To instead select which jobs you wish to import manually, do not enable the Auto-Publish option. Instead, click the checkbox next to the jobs you would like to import to Idealist and then click **Import Selected**. You will then input your invoice and payment information, and pay for these posts by credit card, check, or use of any Job Credits you have previously purchased.

**Note:** [Prices will vary](https://help.idealist.org/s/article/cost-to-post?language=en_US) depending on the type of organization you represent.

Once listings are live on the Idealist site, they cannot be edited via Greenhouse Recruiting. If you need to edit the listing on Idealist, please use the normal editing process for jobs on the Idealist website.

**Note:** Applicants for your jobs will be directed to the Greenhouse-hosted application to apply.
