# Release Notes: May 2024

Greenhouse Software regularly releases new product features, updates, and improvements. You can stay up to date by following our [release notes](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/200929955) or checking out the [latest feature releases](https://www.greenhouse.com/greenhouse-latest-features) page.

#### This month's releases

  * Greenhouse Recruiting
  * Integrations
  * Bug fixes



### Greenhouse Recruiting

#### AI-powered email generator

All customers now have access to email generator, an AI-assisted content generation tool to help you quickly create effective email content that keeps candidates engaged and informed throughout the hiring process. Email generator is available to create and modify email templates. [Read more here.](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/25618229870107)

#### Resume anonymization

Expert-tier customers can now hide identifying candidate information on resumes during Application Review. This feature, part of our Diversity, Equity, and Inclusion (DE&I) feature set, helps reduce unconscious bias in the hiring process. Learn more about [resume anonymization](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/19864880540827) in our article.

#### Automated permissions management

Increase efficiency and reduce manual work by setting up rules that automatically assign the right permissions to the right people. Read more about [automated permissions](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/22567258374171) in our article.

#### HRIS Link for ADP Workforce Now

HRIS Link for ADP is available to purchase for all Greenhouse Recruiting customers. This new connector is a partial platform integration that allows customers to import users and export new hires. This integration syncs critical HRIS data and workflows with easy setup and maintenance. Contact Greenhouse Customer Success for more information.

#### LinkedIn Apply Connect

The Greenhouse Recruiting integration with LinkedIn Apply Connect is available. The LinkedIn Apply Connect integration provides a fast and seamless experience for Greenhouse customers posting jobs to LinkedIn. [Read more here. ](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/17073067102747)

**Note:** Easy Apply is now part of the Apply Connect integration and will be deprecated by July 15, 2024. To continue using Easy Apply, organizations will need to enable LinkedIn Apply Connect in Greenhouse Recruiting.

#### New candidate profile enhancements

We've made the following updates to the new candidate profile:

  * Added more features to the All Stages view so users can get a holistic view of the candidate's full interview plan on one page.
  * Fixed issue where candidate availability couldn't be resent if it was already received.
  * Fixed an issue where the candidate availability requests weren't showing updated time zones.
  * Updated the Application Review and Hiring Manager review fields to show the bell icon when a user hasn't completed an assigned scorecard.
  * Updated Application Review to display any completed or pending reviews like a scheduled interview. 
  * Fixed issue where text in the side panel couldn't be copied using the right-click.
  * Fixed an issue where you couldn't filter by offices when requesting a candidate's availability.
  * Fixed an issue where rejection emails couldn't be sent if an external user was cc'd on the message.
  * Fixed an issue where users couldn't cc other users on outgoing emails.
  * Fixed an issue where some interviewers weren't being included as an option when scheduling Zoom emails on behalf of another user through an integrated Google calendar. 
  * Fixed an issue where answers to private custom fields could be accessed by Job Admins without the right permissions.
  * Fixed an issue where a Job Admins with the correct permissions couldn't add a rejected candidate as a prospect.
  * When adding a prospect, the office will not be automatically populated.
  * Updated the Application Details to include all responses from both active and inactive forms, addressing cases where a form is deleted and replaced with a new version. 
  * Fixed an issue where certain date fields had to be selected from the calendar and couldn't be typed in.
  * Fixed an issue where users couldn't download documents in the Adobe Acrobat Sign window.



**Note:** The new candidate profile is currently being rolled out to all customers, so the new experience may not yet be available for your organization. [Read more about the new candidate profile.](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/11957068130971)

#### Greenhouse Sourcing Automation enhancements

We made the following updates to the Greenhouse Sourcing Automation product: 

  * The "Owner" filter will be automatically automatically set to the current user.
  * Users can now copy a full campaign from within a campaign.
  * The Preview step button is now available directly on the page, instead of hidden in a menu.
  * Clicking the prospect name in the side panel takes you to their prospect profile, rather than just being text-only.
  * Private prospect information will be hidden from Job Admins who only have permission to manage unattached prospects.



#### Other changes

In addition to the changes outlined here, Greenhouse has released several smaller, but impactful changes across our product:

  * Email tokens can now be used in bulk email and bulk rejection emails.
  * Interview reminders will now remember your last setting, allowing you to select the checkbox once and have it selected by default for future jobs.
  * Custom sourcing strategies can be added.
  * Agency recruiters will be notified of potentially duplicate submissions if they submit a candidate whose email address matches a candidate or prospect in your system.
  * The agency configuration page now has a link to download a _.csv_ containing the full list of jobs and submissions for audit purposes.
  * Updated GPDR legal basis wording from "legitimate interest" to "legitimate interest or contract."
  * Updated Harvest API to include deactivated users in requests from Jobs endpoints.



### Integrations

  * **Other integrations** : [Integration.app](https://www.greenhouse.com/integrations/integration-app) is an IPaaS platform specializing in building embedded integrations with numerous SaaS Apps. 
  * **Optimization:**[Blue Saturn’s](https://www.greenhouse.com/integrations/blue-saturn) plug-in integrates directly with Greenhouse Recruiting and offers comprehensive analysis for 1000s of applicants in seconds.
  * **Optimization:** [Talent Llama’s](https://www.greenhouse.com/integrations/talent-llama) integration with Greenhouse Recruiting allows hiring teams to automatically import and invite candidates to take conversational screening interviews from any stage in the Greenhouse candidate pipeline.
  * **Reference check:** [Jointl](https://www.greenhouse.com/integrations/jointl) allows Greenhouse users to create and integrate custom pre-screening questionnaires, skills assessments, references, and background checks into any stage of their hiring process.



### Bug fixes

  * Fixed issue preventing self-service requests from being sent through stage transition rules.
  * Fixed an issue where transferring a candidate between jobs was resetting their email preferences. 
  * Fixed an issue where emails were not being matched correctly in quick select windows if the pasted text was formatted using capital letters.
  * Fixed issue where organizations with a large number of job posts saw significant lag when trying to create or update a custom field.
  * Fixed an issue where custom questions weren't appearing from the Indeed integration.
  * Fixed an issue where removing a rejection reason from an organization-wide sourcing role was causing an error.
  * Fixed an issue where approval information could be seen by Job Admins without the correct permissions.
  * Fixed an issue where private field options were displayed when creating a new opening.
  * Fixed an issue where the sandbox sync wrapper was not displaying on the new candidate profile.
  * Fixed an issue where candidates encountered an error when providing consent to for GDPR.
  * Fixed an issue where the Job Name / Requisition filter wasn't working creating jobs through the Workday integration.
  * Fixed occasional issues when trying to update a user's email through the Harvest API.
  * Fixed an issue where the Business Intelligence Connector used default data for the survey_builder_surveys table if the organization hadn't customizable candidate surveys.
  * Fixed the following issues in Greenhouse Onboarding: 
    * Custom field values weren't displaying correctly on the employee's profile.
    * Welcome Emails were still being sent an employee's personal email when they had a work email on file.
    * The signature request status wasn't updated when the counter signer was reassigned.
    * Added guardrails to e-signature templates to not allow more than 200 custom fields or custom field names longer than 250 characters.
    * Updated error message in Greenhouse Onboarding to be more helpful when trying to upload a video URL that is currently set to private.
    * Rehired employees showed an error if their emails were typed with a capital or lowercase letter that didn't exactly match their existing email.

# Configure structured education fields on job posts

**Permissions:** Site Admin, and Job Admin who can create, edit, and delete job posts

**Product tier:** Available for new subscription tiers (Core, Plus, and Pro)

Greenhouse Recruiting's structured education fields allow your organization to capture a candidate's relevant education history in a uniform format. By capturing a candidate's education history in a structured format, your organization can more easily and effectively search your candidate database.

Greenhouse Recruiting's structured education fields include the following:

  * School name
  * Degree
  * Discipline
  * Start year
  * Start month
  * End year
  * End month



#### In this article

  * Configure structured fields on job posts



**Note** : The configuration process outlined here is also applicable to users who are creating [new job posts for existing jobs](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360020285311-External-Job-Posts#existing) and / or creating [job posts as part of a new job](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360020285311-External-Job-Posts#new) configuration.

### Configure structured fields on job posts

To configure structured education fields on a job post, click**Jobs** on your navigation bar and select a job from the list.

Click **Job Setup** then click **Job Posts** on the left.

Click the **Edit** icon  beside the job post to be edited.

Scroll to _Basic Application Information_.

Under the _Education_ section, toggle the settings of the seven structured education fields to either of the following options:

**Required** : | The education field will be visible and will require a value before the candidate can successfully apply or be added to a job.  
---|---  
**Optional** : | The education field will be visible but will not need a value before the candidate can successfully apply or be added to a job.  
**Hidden** : | The education field will be hidden from the candidate and / or user adding a candidate to a job.  
  
**Note** : Available settings for the start month and end month structured education fields will follow the configuration of start year and end year, respectively. In other words, you can't make start month _required_ and start year _optional_.

When finished, click **Save** at the bottom of the page.

# Edit the 'Your next steps' email template

**Permissions:** Coordinators and Owners

**Product tier:** Available for Greenhouse Welcome and Greenhouse Onboarding subscription tiers

The ['Your next steps'__ email](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360020389692) is a follow-up email sent from Greenhouse Onboarding to a new hire after they've been assigned an [onboarding plan](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360000683352). In the email, new hires will receive a summary of who their manager is and which tasks need their attention.

**Note:** Learn how to [configure the delivery schedule](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360027921091) for the 'Your next steps' email.

Greenhouse Onboarding provides a default version of this email, but your organization can also customize the default email to [add multiple variations](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360020389692).

#### In this article

  * Edit the default 'Your next steps' email
  * Edit custom 'Your next steps' email variations
  * Additional resources



To begin, navigate to **Settings** > **Onboarding Plan** > **Emails**.

On the _Emails_ page, scroll to **Your next steps** to review your existing 'Your next steps' default email and variations.

### Edit the default 'Your next steps' email

To edit your organization's default 'Your next steps' email, hover over the email named **Default**. Click the **pencil icon** to begin editing.

**Note:** The default 'Your next steps' email is intended to work as a catch-all for new hires who haven't been assigned specific departments, locations, employment statuses, or other criteria.

As a result, the default email can't be deactivated or renamed. In addition, match rules for department, location, employment status, and other criteria can't be applied to the default email template.

Use the **Email Subject** and **Message** fields to update the subject line or email copy for your default 'Your next steps' email.

When you're done, click **Save and Close**.

New hires who do not have matching criteria for 'Your next steps' email variations will receive this default email.

### Edit custom 'Your next steps' email variations

**Note:** Learn how to [create a new variation](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360020389692) of the 'Your next steps' email.

You can also edit any of your organization's 'Your next steps' email variations. Hover over the email variation you want to edit, then click the **pencil icon**.

If you want to delete this email variation, click the **trash icon**.

From the email template editor, you can edit any of the following elements:

  * Enable or turn off email delivery
  * Template name
  * Email subject
  * Message
  * Match criteria



**Note:** Make sure each 'Your next steps' email variation has **match criteria** applied to filter for specific new hires. This ensures that the correct email variation will reach new hires with matching locations, departments, employment statuses, or other criteria.

When you're done, click **Save and Close**.

New hires who match the applied criteria will receive this 'Your next steps' email variation.

### Additional resources

  * ['Your next steps' email](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360020389692)
  * [Configure 'Your next steps' email delivery schedule](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360027921091)

# Job closed notification

**Permissions:** Job Admin and above

**Product tier:** Available for new subscription tiers (Core, Plus, and Pro)

[Job closed](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360025499691) notifications make it easy to keep your team informed when a job is no longer accepting applicants. Once set up, users added to the notification list will automatically receive an email when that specific job is closed.

To add users to this notification, click**Jobs** from the navigation bar and select a job from the list.

Click **Job Setup** from the listed panel options and navigate to **Notifications** on the left.

On the _Notifications_ page, scroll to **Job Closed** within the _Other Notifications_ section. Click **Configure.**

****

Click the _Participant(s)_ dropdown and select the appropriate user. You can select a user by name, or you can select the [Hiring Manager(s)](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360016572311) listed on the job's [Hiring Team](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/115002194983), the Candidate's Recruiter, and/or the Candidate's Coordinator.

Add as many users as you would like to receive this notification, then select **Save** when you're finished.

All selected users will receive an email when the job has been closed. The email includes the date the job was closed and its close reason.

**Note** : The user who closed the job will not receive an email notification.

To remove users from the list, navigate to the name of a user listed in the provided field and click **X** to the right of their name. **Save** when finished.

# Time to fill by job report

**Permissions:** Job Admin and above

**Product tier:** Available for new subscription tiers (Core, Plus, and Pro)

The Time to fill by job report helps your organization forecast the anticipated time it will take to hire a candidate for a role by displaying the length of time it took to hire other candidates.

By tracking your time to fill, your team can understand your organization's recruiting efficiency to ensure positions are filled promptly, providing a more effective hiring process.

**Note** : If your Time to fill report shows `0` days in the _Days to Hire_ column, it likely means a candidate was marked as hired on the same day that the job opening was marked as open.

**Tip** : Need help troubleshooting this report? Check out [Troubleshoot a report](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/13710986142107).

#### In this article

  * Time to fill by job report
    * Time to fill by job report filters
    * Time to fill by job calculation



### Time to fill by job report

To create a time to fill by job report, click **Reports** on your navigation bar.

Click **Essential** **Reports** on the left.

Scroll to the _Share Progress with Executives_ section and click **Time to fill by job**.

The time to fill by job report will generate.

The time to fill by job report will display the following information for all jobs included in the report:

  * Job
  * Requisition ID
  * Departments
  * Offices
  * Status
  * Opening ID

| 

  * Open date
  * Hired candidate
  * Offer date
  * Accepted date
  * Start date
  * Days to hire

  
---|---  
  
Days to hire is calculated as the time between the job opening's open date and the date that a candidate is marked as hired on the opening. Read more here: [How to maintain accurate hiring data](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/7992568877595#h_01GA7AW3A32S92ERFEYHSARJ3Z).

**Note** : The Time to fill by job report will include all jobs where you have at least Job Admin permission.

#### Time to fill by job report filters

Click **Filters and more** to apply filters to further refine your report.

The time to fill by job report can be filtered by the following:

  * Job
  * Job status
  * Department
  * Office
  * User
  * Hiring team role
  * Custom job field
  * Include migrated candidates



Click **Apply** after applying any filters.

To access the profile for either a job or candidate on the report, click the underlined link.

#### Time to fill by job calculation

The Time to fill calculation is measured as the time between the [opening's open date](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360027736012#h_c8049f79-949b-48a5-b77d-7a91319584f0) on a job and the [candidate's hire date](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/115005471286).

# Sales and transaction tax for Greenhouse customers

For more general accounting information, including details about payments, banking information, and vendor processes, see the [Greenhouse accounting overview](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/4411848172059).

Greenhouse reserves the right to assess sales and certain transactional taxes (“Taxes”) as required by local laws. Greenhouse fees are quoted and shown exclusive of taxes. Taxes are calculated based on your billing address and shown separately on your Greenhouse invoice, when applicable.

#### In this article

  * U.S. taxes
  * International taxes
  * Request an exemption
  * Update your tax information



### U.S. taxes

Greenhouse will assess taxes in the following U.S. jurisdictions, unless a tax exemption has been approved for your organization:

  * Arizona*
  * Colorado - Aurora
  * Colorado - Boulder
  * Colorado - Broomfield
  * Colorado - Colorado Springs
  * Colorado - Denver
  * Colorado - Englewood
  * Colorado - Greenwood Village
  * Colorado - Longmont
  * Colorado - Louisville
  * Connecticut
  * District of Columbia
  * Hawaii
  * Iowa
  * Illinois - Chicago**
  * Kentucky
  * Louisiana
  * Massachusetts
  * Maryland
  * New Mexico
  * New York
  * Ohio
  * Rhode Island
  * Pennsylvania
  * South Carolina
  * Tennessee
  * Texas
  * Utah
  * Vermont
  * Washington
  * West Virginia



_*Arizona Transaction Privilege Tax_

_**Chicago Lease Transaction Tax_

### International taxes

Greenhouse reserves the right to assess value added tax (“VAT”), goods and services tax (“GST”), or consumption tax. Additional details are listed below by your billing country.

#### Australia

Australian GST will not be added to your invoice. Customers with a billing address in Australia can provide their Business Number to be included on invoices. See the Update your tax information section below for more information.

#### Canada

**British Columbia**

British Columbia provincial sales tax (“PST”) will be added to invoices if your billing address is in British Columbia province. Customers can provide their PST ID to be included on invoices. See the Update your tax information section below for more information.

**Saskatchewan**

Saskatchewan provincial sales tax (“PST”) will be added to invoices if your billing address is in Saskatchewan province. Customers can provide their PST ID to be included on invoices. See the Update your tax information section below for more information.

#### European countries 

VAT will not be added to your invoice and is subject to the reverse charge mechanism. Customers with a billing address in the countries listed below can provide their VAT ID to be included on invoices. 

  * 27 European Union Member States
  * Norway
  * Switzerland
  * United Kingdom



See the Update your tax information section below for more information.

#### Japan

Japan Consumption Tax (“JCT”) will not be added to invoices. Customers with a billing address in Japan are responsible to self-assess and report JCT under the reverse charge mechanism in accordance with the Consumption Tax Act.

#### Mexico

Mexico VAT will not be added to your invoice. Customers with a billing address in Mexico can provide their RFC (Federal Taxpayers Register) to be included on invoices. See the Update your tax infomation section below for more information.

Customers with a billing address in Mexico are responsible to self-assess and report VAT under the reverse charge mechanism in accordance with the Value Added Tax law.

#### Philippines

Philippines VAT will not be added to your invoice. Customers with a billing address in the Philippines must provide their Tax Identification Number (TIN) to be included on invoices. See Update your tax information section below.

Customers with a billing address in the Philippines are responsible to self-assess and report VAT under the reverse charge mechanism in accordance with the Value Added Tax law.

#### South Africa

South Africa VAT will be added to your invoice if your billing address is in South Africa. Customers with a billing address in South Africa can provide their VAT ID to be included on invoices. See the Update your tax information section below for more information.

### Request an exemption

Customers eligible for U.S. Tax exemption are required to submit an official exemption certificate with their Greenhouse Invoice to [tax@greenhouse.io](mailto:tax@greenhouse.io).

### Update your tax information

Customers with a billing country that is listed above, other than the United States of America, you may add your valid Tax ID to be shown on future invoices on the Greenhouse App.

For detailed steps and supported Tax ID types, see [Billing page overview](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/30383521759259).

# TeamOhana integration

TeamOhana empowers fast-changing businesses to execute their strategic hiring plans on time and within budget by unifying data, people, and processes in a collaborative platform so they can achieve their business goals faster.

TeamOhana’s integration with Greenhouse Recruiting allows the following:

  * Creation of jobs and openings in Greenhouse from headcount in TeamOhana, autofilling internal and external job names and opening IDs for a reduction in manual data-entry
  * Association of approved and open headcount in TeamOhana with existing jobs and openings in Greenhouse, enabling the automation of hiring updates in a centralized platform viewable by all stakeholders
  * Visibility into offer details in real time, highlighting the budget vs the actual for each headcount and automatically reconciling costs so Finance doesn’t have to
  * Visibility into candidate name and email address, providing the data upon which TeamOhana matches new employee information from the HRIS to close out the headcount from the hiring plan



#### In this article

  * Set up the Greenhouse Recruiting / TeamOhana integration
    * Create a Harvest API key
    * Provide your API key credentials to TeamOhana and complete setup
  * Use the TeamOhana integration with Greenhouse Recruiting
    * Automate job and opening creation
    * Create new openings automatically
    * Link automatic job and hire updates 
  * Additional resources



### Set up the Greenhouse Recruiting / TeamOhana integration

#### Create a Harvest API key

To configure the Greenhouse Recruiting / TeamOhana integration, you’ll need to create a Harvest API key.

Follow the steps in [this article](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/5888163769883) to create the key, and verify that the permissions below are selected when configuring the TeamOhana integration.

#### Credentials

In the _Create New Credential_ box, make the following selections:

  * API Type: Harvest
  * Partner: TeamOhana or Unlisted Vendor
  * Description: TeamOhana Harvest API Key



#### Permissions

In order for TeamOhana to gain access to all relevant endpoints that are needed for the integration to run properly, please include the following permissions when you create your API key:

**Applications**

  * GET: Retrieve Application
  * GET: List Applications



**Candidates**

  * GET: Retrieve Candidate
  * GET: List Candidates



**Users**

  * GET: Retrieve User
  * GET: List Users



**Offers**

  * GET: List Application's Offers
  * GET: Retrieve Application's Current Offer
  * GET: Retrieve Offer
  * GET: List Offers



**Departments**

  * GET: Retrieve Department
  * GET: List Departments



**Custom Locations**

  * GET: Retrieve Custom Location for Job Board



**Jobs**

  * GET: Retrieve Job
  * GET: List Jobs
  * PATCH: Update Job
  * POST: Create a new job
  * GET: Get hiring team
  * POST: Add hiring team member
  * DELETE: Remove hiring team member
  * Put: Replace hiring team



**Job Posts**

  * GET: List Job Posts
  * GET: Retrieve Job Post for Job
  * GET: List Job Posts for Job
  * PATCH: Update job posts



**Job Stages**

  * GET: Retrieve Job Stage
  * GET: List Job Stages
  * GET: List Job Stages for Job



**Job Openings**

  * GET: List Openings For a Job
  * POST: Create openings
  * PATCH: Edit openings
  * DELETE: Delete openings



**Offices**

  * GET: Retrieve Office
  * GET: List Offices
  * POST: Create a new office
  * PATCH: Update an office



**User Roles**

  * GET: List User Roles



**Custom Fields**

  * GET: Get custom fields
  * POST: Create custom field
  * PATCH: Update custom field



**Custom Field Options**

  * GET: Custom field options
  * POST: Create custom field options
  * PATCH: Update custom field options



**Close Reasons**

  * GET: Get close reasons



**Save** when finished. Copy the Harvest API key to provide to TeamOhana in the next step.

#### Provide your API key credentials to TeamOhana and complete setup

After creating your API key, you'll be ready to connect your created credentials to TeamOhana.

**Note** : TeamOhana partners with [Merge](https://merge.dev/) to enable the Greenhouse Recruiting integration. You'll need to input your created API credentials into a Merge Link interface within your TeamOhana account.

To add your API key, navigate to TeamOhana and [log in as an Admin user](https://login.teamohana.us/u/login?state=hKFo2SBCd3lWYVhPbHRncUdvSzF0ck5HZ1B0WERNaldsQlhGMaFur3VuaXZlcnNhbC1sb2dpbqN0aWTZIEdrNDFNZlVCZXBEdVh3aTFrM0lUU1pnaVZpTF9lbDF6o2NpZNkgV2ZnZDVqZXc3dDRoa0VvSndUbHpRWWZhb3Bha3NTN3o). Next, click **Settings** > **Integrations**.

Locate and select **Link HRIS or ATS** > **Applicant Tracking System**. Click the Greenhouse logo and paste your key in the _Enter your Greenhouse API key_ field.

**Submit** when finished. The Greenhouse Recruiting / TeamOhana integration will be enabled for use. 

TeamOhana’s implementation team will work with you directly to collect information about your offers and offer fields to complete the integration setup.

### Use the TeamOhana integration with Greenhouse Recruiting

When the TeamOhana / Greenhouse Recruiting integration is enabled, you can automate new job creation in TeamOhana, as well as centralize all hiring and offer updates into one platform.

#### Automate job and openings creation

Once a headcount is approved for recruiting, users can automate the job and opening creation process.

  * On the headcount in TeamOhana, click on the **Hiring Details** tab, then ensure “ready to hire” is enabled
  * Select **Create job in Greenhouse**
  * Internal and External job names, as well as the Opening ID field, will all be autofilled. Complete the remaining fields (template job, department, office, and requisition ID) to create your Greenhouse job and opening
  * Once created, the new job and opening will automatically be linked to the headcount and all hiring updates for the opening will sync into TeamOhana



#### Create new openings automatically

If a headcount is approved for recruiting and a job already exists in Greenhouse, users can automate the opening creation process from TeamOhana

  * On the headcount in TeamOhana, click **Hiring Details** , then ensure _Ready to hire_ is enabled
  * Select the Greenhouse job from the dropdown menu and then under _Opening ID_ , click **Create opening in Greenhouse**
  * The opening ID will be autofilled with the headcount ID from TeamOhana. Verify that all information is correct, then click **Create**
  * Once the opening ID is created, it will autolink to the headcount and all hiring updates for the opening will sync into TeamOhana



#### Link automatic job and hire updates 

If a headcount is approved for recruiting and a job and opening already exist in Greenhouse, users will be able to link both with the headcount in TeamOhana to centralize all hiring updates

  * On the headcount in TeamOhana, click on the Hiring Details tab, then ensure _Ready to hire_ is enabled
  * Click on the dropdown menu under Job ID and select the job, then the opening, that should be linked to the headcount
  * Going forward all hiring updates for the opening will sync into TeamOhana



When an offer has been created for the opening in Greenhouse, all offer details will sync into TeamOhana, including candidate name, email address, offer start date, base salary, and more. When the candidate accepts the offer and they are marked as hired in Greenhouse, the headcount status will update to “Hired” in TeamOhana.

Finally, when the candidate is added to the company’s HRIS as a new employee, TeamOhana will recognize the match across ATS, HRIS, and hiring plan, and will link the new employee’s HRIS record to the headcount. The headcount status will then update to “closed.”

### Additional resources

If you’d like to learn more about TeamOhana, visit their website at [www.teamohana.com](http://www.teamohana.com).

For additional information not covered here, please reach out to Customer Success, TeamOhana at [success@teamohana.com](mailto:success@teamohana.com)

If you’d like to learn more or see a demo of TeamOhana, please reach out to: [sales@teamohana.com](mailto:%20sales@teamohana.com)

# Email GDPR information to candidates

**Permissions:** Site Admin

**Product tier:** Available for new subscription tiers (Core, Plus, and Pro)

**Note** : This article pertains to organizations who've selected legitimate interest or contract as the [legal basis for their GDPR configuration](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360042142612).

If you included a [GDPR notice on your job post](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360002594791), all applicants who applied through that specific job post will see your company's GDPR information displayed. However, if candidates, prospects, or referrals were entered into your system without having applied through a job post, either through a referral process, being manually added to your account, or submitted through an agency, those individuals never had the opportunity to review your GDPR notification.

By configuring data collection email rules _,_ your organization can automatically email a GDPR notification to candidates and / or prospects who entered into your system without having applied to a job post. These rules can be configured on a per-office basis.

#### In this article

  * Add data collection email rule
  * Configure GDPR email template
  * Greenhouse GDPR notice to unwitting prospects example



**Note** : Before continuing, we strongly advise that you speak with your legal counsel to draft the text of your email template to unwitting candidates, prospects, and referrals.

To begin configuring GDPR, click the **Configure** icon  on your navigation bar, then select **Privacy & Compliance** on the left.

Find the _General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR)_ section and click **Configure**.

### Add data collection email rule

From the GDPR page, navigate to the _Data Collection Email Rules_ panel and click **Add a Rule**.

Use the panel to select the offices that will be impacted by the rule and the recipients of the GDPR notification email.

Click **Save** when finished.

Candidates and / or prospects who are added to your system for the selected offices and match the configured recipient criteria will receive your organization's GDPR notification.

**Note** : If you manually add a candidate or prospect that matches the criteria you have specified in your data collection rule, then you will need to provide an email address for the candidate or prospect so they can be notified of your GDPR policy.

Repeat as necessary for other offices.

### Configure GDPR email template

From the Data Collection Email Rules panel, click **Configure GDPR Email Template** to create the email that will be sent to selected individuals.

From the _Edit Email Template_ page, input a name for the template, sender address, and subject heading for the email in the appropriate fields.

Draft the language that will be automatically sent to candidates whose data you are collecting from other sources.

**Note** : You should seek the advice of your legal counsel to prepare this text as it applies to your business. A Greenhouse example of an Article 14 notification is provided below to serve as a starting point, but Greenhouse cannot guarantee that this text will ensure GDPR compliance for your company.

When you have finished, click **Save**.

### Greenhouse GDPR notice to unwitting prospects example

**Note:** You should seek the advice of your legal counsel to prepare this text as it applies to your business. What follows is an example of an Article 14 notification. Greenhouse cannot guarantee that this text will ensure GDPR compliance for your company

This email is to notify you that personal data about you has been collected by `[CONTROLLER]` (“Controller”), which is located at `[ADDRESS]` and can be contacted by emailing `[EMAIL]`, because Controller wishes to evaluate your candidacy for employment at Controller. Your personal data was either obtained from publicly available sources (e.g. LinkedIn) or provided to Controller by someone who referred you for potential employment. Controller’s data protection officer is `[DPO NAME]`, who can be contacted at `[CONTACT INFORMATION]`. Your personal data will be processed who can be contacted at `[CONTACT INFORMATION]`. Your personal data will be processed for the purposes of managing Controller’s recruitment related activities, which include setting up and conducting interviews and tests for applicants, evaluating and assessing the results thereto, and as is otherwise needed in the recruitment and hiring processes. Such processing is legally permissible under Art. 6(1)(f) of Regulation (EU) 2016/679 (General Data Protection Regulation) as necessary for the purposes of the legitimate interests pursued by the Controller, which are the solicitation, evaluation, and selection of applicants for employment.

Your personal data has been shared with Greenhouse Software, Inc., a cloud services provider located in the United States of America and engaged by Controller to help manage its recruitment and hiring process on Controller’s behalf. Accordingly, if you are located outside of the United States, your personal data has been transferred to the United States. Because the European Union Commission has determined that United States data privacy laws do not ensure an adequate level of protection for personal data collected from EU data subjects, the transfer was subject to appropriate additional safeguards under [either the standard contractual clauses or the Privacy Shield]. You can obtain a copy of the standard contractual clauses by contacting us at [example@yourcompany.com](mailto:example@yourcompany.com).

Your personal data will be retained by Controller as long as Controller determines it is necessary to evaluate your application for employment. Under the GDPR, you have the right to request access to your personal data, to request that your personal data be rectified or erased, and to request that processing of your personal data be restricted. You also have to right to data portability. In addition, you may lodge a complaint with an EU supervisory authority.

# Set your preferred meeting times

**Permissions:** —

**Product tier:** Available for new subscription tiers (Core, Plus, and Pro)

In addition to your working hours, you can set preferred meeting times to help your team schedule interviews at times that work best for you. Adding preferred meeting times gives your team more context about your availability without blocking off your calendar completely.

To set your preferred meeting times, click your initials in the top right hand corner of any page of Greenhouse.

Click **Working hours**.

Scroll to the**Preferred meeting times** section and check the box to show the calendar.

Click and drag to add availability. Greenhouse doesn’t set preferred meeting times by default.

Your preferred meeting times must fall within your working hours. If you haven’t customized your working hours, they’ll default to 9 AM – 5 PM.

When your team uses [automated scheduling](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/36255269371419), all suggested times—including those outside your preferred meeting hours—appear in chronological order. Times outside your preferred hours are marked as a conflict, but remain available to select.

The more preferred times you add, the easier it is for your team to find options that work for you. To give an even fuller picture of your availability, you can also mark specific times as “available” or “busy” when setting your [interview availability.](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/28929396249115)

# RepScout AI Integration

RepScout provides AI-powered interviews and assessments, reducing your time investment in qualifying a pool of candidates. Recruitment managers focus on the key target criteria in an ideal candidate, and we handle running and analysing the interviews and assessments directly with the candidate.

Our primary focus is voice-based assessments, making the platform ideal for companies hiring for roles with a strong communications component.

RepScout’s integration with Greenhouse Recruiting allows you to seamlessly add a range of RepScout assessments to a job's interview plan.

#### In this article

  * Enable the RepScout integration
  * Use the RepScout integration with Greenhouse Recruiting
  * Additional resources



### Enable the RepScout integration

You’ll first need an account with RepScout. To sign up, head over to our [sign-up page](https://app.repscout.ai/sign-up) \- we offer a range of different plans as well as a free trial. When logged into your RepScout account, head to _**company-settings - > integrations**_ and click ‘Generate Key’.

Once you have your API key, follow the steps in [this article](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/5888163696923) to complete the setup in Greenhouse.

### Use the RepScout integration with Greenhouse Recruiting

Once the RepScout integration is enabled for your organization, you will be able to add the RepScout assessment as an interview stage.

Follow the steps in [this article](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/5888163696923) to add the assessment stage to your interview plans. 

Once you’ve set up your interview plans and configured your take-home test, you’ll be able to send the test to candidates.

You can send an assessment to a candidate by selecting the**Send Test** button next to the interview stage.

When you send a test in Greenhouse Recruiting, the instructions are sent by RepScout. An email will be sent to the candidate with a link to start the test. This must be completed within 90 days.

After it has been sent, the assessment’s status will display in Greenhouse Recruiting.

#### The Test

RepScout offers the ability to conduct a series of different tests in series. Typically, this may take the form of an interview followed by another industry-specific assessment, i.e. mock cold-call.

The test style sits between a human-led interview and a static text-prompted test. So it remains dynamic, whilst not pretending to be a real human interaction. There’s the option to record the candidate’s video or audio.

Once the candidate has submitted their test, the ‘Interview Kit’ will contain a link to view the submitted test in the RepScout application. 

To see a candidate’s results in RepScout, click **View** **Report**.

RepScout's report view displays a detailed breakdown of the criteria defined by the recruiter for each assessment, along with an overarching results summary. The screenshot below shows the summary tab, which is currently selected. Here, the results of two assessments - a Q&A interview and a mock call role-play - are laid out.

#### RepScout Pricing

To send RepScout assessments, a paid account with sufficient credit is required. Details on our paid plans are available here: <https://repscout.ai/pricing>.

#### RepScout’s Ethical Framework

RepScout prioritizes fairness and inclusion in its evaluation methods. To achieve this, we implement skills-based hiring alongside consistent evaluation standards for every applicant. We ensure transparency and openness in our AI algorithms by offering thorough explanations of each evaluated criterion.

We strive for continuous improvement of our processes and decision-making by gathering regular feedback, ensuring our results are both consistent and aligned with RepScout’s ethical values.

### Additional resources

For additional information not covered here, reach out to [info@repscout.ai](mailto:info@repscout.ai). Alternatively, you can take a look at our [FAQs page](https://repscout.ai/faqs).

Learn how to log in to your Greenhouse Onboarding or Greenhouse Welcome account.

**Note:** If your organization uses single sign-on and you need to log in to Greenhouse Onboarding before your start date, you can [request a magic link](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/207507453) to access your account.

# AdaptiLab integration

AdaptiLab has built a technical screening tool for machine learning and data science to help hiring managers evaluate candidates at the top of their funnels.

The product generates preliminary interviews that test technical coding ability for the core competencies: data preprocessing, data analysis, algorithms, model development, general machine learning, and automatically provides a graded score report for each candidate. 

Greenhouse Recruiting's integration with AdaptiLab allows you to seamlessly add AdaptiLab’s assessment to a job's interview plan.

#### In this article

  * Set up the AdaptiLab integration
  * Use the AdaptiLab integration with Greenhouse Recruiting
  * Additional resources



### Set up the AdaptiLab integration

To enable the integration, follow the steps in [this article](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/5888163696923) to retrieve your API key from your AdaptiLab representative and set up the assessment stage in your interview plans.

Once you've set up your interview plans and configured your take-home test, you'll be able to send the test to candidates.

### Use the AdaptiLab integration with Greenhouse Recruiting

# User-specific permissions for Job Admins

**Permissions:** —

**Product tier:** Available for new subscription tiers (Core, Plus, and Pro)

User-specific permissions are extra permissions granted to a user in addition to those included in that user's permission level (Basic, Job Admin, Site Admin). In this article, we will cover the different user-specific permissions associated with the Job Admin permission level.

  * Job Admin user-specific permissions overview
  * Job Admin user-specific permissions detailed descriptions
    * Can create new jobs and request job approvals
    * Can manage unattached prospects 
    * Can create job stage names
  * Additional resources



### Job Admin user-specific permissions overview

Users who are assigned the Job Admin permission level can be assigned the following optional user-specific permissions:

Permission | Description  
---|---  
Can create new jobs and request job approvals |  When granted, this permission allows the user to [create a job](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/200668380-Create-a-New-Job), which can be accessed from the **Add** button on the navigation bar. Click here to learn more about this permission.  
Can invite new users to Greenhouse and reactive disabled users | This permission allows the user some control over who to invite into your Greenhouse Recruiting account and gives the user the ability to [re-enable user accounts that were deactivated previously](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/115004494583).  
Can manage custom fields |  [Custom fields](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360001421452-System-Default-Fields-vs-Custom-Fields) can be created to house additional information for Candidates, Jobs, Offers, or your Referral Questionnaire. Site Admins can always manage custom fields; this permission allows Job Admins the ability to create, make changes to, and remove custom fields for your entire organization.   
Can manage company metadata | Similar to custom fields, metadata includes information that appears in dropdown menus throughout Greenhouse, like Referrers, Rejection Reasons, Sources, and Tags.  
Can manage company email and social media templates | If you have a Job Admin who manages your templates, you can allow them to make changes to organization-wide [email templates](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/sections/360000690671-Templates) and company social media templates that will be accessible to all of the users in your Greenhouse Recruiting account.  
Can manage unattached prospects | A [prospect is considered unattached](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/206729066)**** if they have been added to Greenhouse Recruiting without being assigned to a specific job. This permission allows the user to add unattached prospects to jobs or convert them to candidates. This permission does not allow the user to view information under the _Private_ tab on prospect profiles. Click here to learn more about this permission.  
Can create new job stage names | This permission allows your organization to control who has the ability to create new job stage names on Interview Plans. Ideally, this permission will help reduce erroneous or duplicate job stages that will need to be cleaned up later. Click here to learn more about this permission.  
Can invite and deactivate agency recruiters | This permission allows the user to [invite/deactivate agency recruiters](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/200666389-). If granted, users will find additional functionality on the agency management page.   
Can manage offer templates | This permission allows the user to upload new offer templates, test offer tokens, rename offer templates, and download or delete offer templates.  
Can create and manage scheduling links | This permission allows the user to create, edit, deactivate, and reactivate scheduling links for coordinating meetings with potential hires inside or outside of Greenhouse. [Click here](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/34270522324763) to learn more.  
  
### Job Admin user-specific permissions detailed descriptions

#### Can create new jobs and request job approvals

When granting a user this permission, you must select a [default Job Admin role](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360040467451) for new jobs this user creates. Options include Job Admin: Private and Job Admin: Standard.

You also have the option to limit job creation to specific departments and offices. If selected, these options would allow the user to only create new jobs within chosen departments or offices.

_**Tip:** Limiting job creation by department or office can help avoid confusion in organizations with many departments or offices. Consider using these permissions to align Job Admins with the teams or geographic areas they work with most._

#### Can manage unattached prospects

This user-specific permission allows users to view and manage unattached prospects. A prospect is considered unattached if they have been added to Greenhouse Recruiting without being assigned to a specific job.

_**Note:** Prospects added to a department or office, but not a job, are still considered unattached._

Job Admin users with this permission assigned will be able to complete the following actions on unattached prospects:

  * Add prospect to jobs as a prospect where the user has Job Admin permissions
  * Convert prospect to a candidate on jobs where the user has Job Admin permissions



Job Admin users with this permission assigned will have the following visibility on profiles that include an unattached prospect process:

  * **Activity Feed** : Users can view Activity Feed data for the prospect’s profile. The Activity Feed might include information related to jobs where the user does not have Job Admin permissions. This can include activities such as stage changes, form requests, emails, and notes. Users will **not** see submitted scorecard information for jobs where the user does not have Job Admin permissions.
  * **Notes** : Users can view public notes added to the prospect’s profile from the _Make a Note_ box.



#### Can create job stage names

This user-specific permission gives your organization tighter control over your Interview Plans by limiting which users can create new stage names. Without this permission, Job Admins won't be able to create new stage names and will only be able to select stages from a preexisting list.

Limiting which users can create new stage names helps prevent the creation of multiple stages that represent the same step in your Interview Plans, making reporting across multiple jobs a cleaner process.

### Additional resources

For more information about the user-specific permissions for the other permission levels, click the links below: 

  * [Permissions for Basic users](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360020860672)
  * [User-specific permissions for Site Admins](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360021113491)

# Deactivate a user

**Permissions:** Site Admin

**Product tier:** Available for new subscription tiers (Core, Plus, and Pro)

In order to preserve your organization's historical data, you are unable to completely delete users from your Greenhouse Recruiting account. Rather than deleting users, Greenhouse Recruiting allows your organization to deactivate a user account so the user can no longer access your system or be assigned any responsibilities.

#### In this article

  * Deactivate a user
  * What happens to a deactivated user's historical data?



### Deactivate a user

**Note** : [Click here](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/200521489-How-do-I-disable-multiple-users-at-the-same-time-) for information on how to deactivate multiple user accounts at the same time.

__

# Time in stage goal attainment report

**Permissions:** Job Admin and above

**Product tier:** Available for new subscription tiers (Core, Plus, and Pro)

The time in stage [company goal](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/8382420999835) represents the ideal time between when a candidate is moved into a stage and when they exit the stage. Use the time in stage goal attainment report to track progress on this goal.

**Note** : The time in stage goal **does not** include time spent in the Application Review or Hiring Manager Review stages, as candidates typically spend much less time in these stages.

#### In this article

  * View time in stage goal attainment report
    * Time in stage goal attainment report visualization
  * Apply report filters
  * Additional resources



### View time in stage goal attainment report

To create a time in stage goal attainment report, click **Reports** on your dashboard's navigation bar.

On the  _Reports_ page, click **Essential****reports**.

Select **Time in Stage Goal Attainment** from the  _Understand Goal and Attainment Metrics****_ section.

Your time in stage goal attainment report will generate.

Your report will display attainment percentages for your entire organization in a visualization. Below this visual chart, you'll find a breakdown of attainment percentages for individual users or departments (depending on the report filters you've applied) in a table.

Attainment percentages are relative to the [target value your organization set for this goal](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/8382420999835) and the time period you've selected as a filter for your report columns. Each percentage is calculated by the total number of actions completed on time (based on the target value you've set) over the total number of actions overall for your specified time period.

**For example:** You've set your time in stage goal report to display your attainment levels per week. Each percentage represents the number of times you've moved candidates to the next stage within your target **divided by** the total number of times you've moved candidates between stages (whether on time or not) for that week.

**Note:** Credit for the time in stage goal will accrue to the Greenhouse Recruiting user who moves the candidate to and from an interview stage.

#### Time in stage goal attainment report visualization

The time in stage goal attainment report presents your organization's attainment levels in a line chart. The attainment percentage is displayed on the _y_ -axis and the time period is displayed on the _x_ -axis.

You can hover over each point in the visualization for additional details.

This visualization will adjust each time you apply new filters from the **Filters and more** dropdown.

### Apply report filters

Click **Filters and more** to apply filters and further refine your report.

You can use the following filters on your time in stage goal attainment report:

  * **Rows** – select whether to display attainment levels for users or departments
  * **Columns** – select whether to display attainment levels per week, month, or quarter
  * **Activity date** – view goal attainment for a specific date range
  * **User or department filter** – view goal attainment for specific users or departments



**Note:** Activity date is set to the last 180 days by default. To optimize performance, company goals data is only available for the last 365 days.

Click **Apply** to add your selected filters and adjust your report.

### Additional resources

  * [Report on goals](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/8383632617755)
  * [Time to schedule available candidate goal attainment report](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/9166289363739)
  * [Time to approve offer goal attainment report](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/9166643653403)
  * [Time to submit scorecards goal attainment report](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/7507124760347)
  * [Time to review applications goal attainment report](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/10061338502171)

# Set application limits for job posts

**Permissions:** Site Admins

**Product tier:** Available for the Pro subscription tier

A high volume of applications can put stress on even very structured and efficient hiring processes. Application limit rules help you limit the amount of repeat applications your job posts get, so your team can focus on reviewing applications from qualified and interested candidates.

#### In this article

  * Video walkthrough
  * Create a new application limit rule
  * Delete a rule
  * Rule conflict resolution
  * Cases where application rules won't apply



### Video walkthrough

### Create a new application limit rule

Before getting started, turn on [auto-merge](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/208063316) if it's not already on for your organization. To enable auto-merge, click the **Configure** > on your navigation bar and then click **Organization** on the left. From the _Organization_ page, toggle the button next to _Auto-Merge Candidates_ to **ON.**

To add a new rule, click **Configure** > **Job Boards & Posts**.

Click **Create rule.**

First, give a descriptive name to your new rule.

Choose which department or departments the rule will apply to. The rule will limit repeat applications for all jobs within those departments.

There are two ways you can restrict applications: Limiting by frequency, and preventing rejected candidates from reapplying to jobs they've already been rejected from.

To restrict by frequency, check the box labeled _Restrict applications over a period of time_ , enter the number of applications a candidate can submit, and then enter the number of days they have to submit those applications.

Within the same rule, you can also prevent rejected candidates from reapplying to the same job they have already been rejected from. Specify the number of days that must pass before a rejected candidate can submit another application.

When candidates submit applications that break your rules, their applications will be automatically moved to the "rejected" category and marked as "blocked by auto reject rule."

To send a rejection email to rejected candidates, check the box labeled _Send a rejection email to affected candidates_. Then, choose the email template you want to use and set the timing for when the email should be sent.

### Delete a rule

Find the rule you'd like to delete on the Application limit rules page and click on the rule's name. Then, navigate to the bottom of the page and click **Delete rule**.

### Rule conflict resolution

In cases where two rules seem like they may apply to a job and conflict, Greenhouse Recruiting will choose the most granular rule.

**Example:** If you have a rule that applies to the Sales department and a rule that applies to Sales Operations, which is a sub-department of Sales, Greenhouse Recruiting will choose the rule that applies to Sales Operations.

### Cases where application limit rules won't apply

Applications added to Greenhouse Recruiting through any of these methods won't be affected by application limit rules:

  * Referrals
  * Internal candidates
  * Agency submissions
  * Applications added using the [Greenhouse Recruiting Chrome extensions](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/4947637389083)
  * Prospect applications
  * Anonymized candidates
  * Applications created using [Harvest API](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360029266032) or Ingestion API

# View candidate survey results

**Permissions:** Job Admin and above

**Product tier:** Available for new subscription tiers (Core, Plus, and Pro)

The [candidate survey](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360029861512) captures feedback that can be used to evaluate and strategically improve the experience you offer to candidates. In this article, we'll cover how to view aggregated responses to your candidate survey. 

**Note:** All candidate data is **anonymized** for compliance purposes and to reduce unconscious bias in the hiring process. Your organization's Greenhouse Recruiting users can only view anonymized candidate data. In addition, Greenhouse Technical Support cannot access candidate data unless given explicit consent by your organization.

#### In this article

  * View candidate survey results
    * Benchmarking data
  * Report filters
  * View candidate comments
  * Additional resources



### View candidate survey results

To view candidate survey results, click **Reports** from your navigation bar.

From the Reports Overview page, click **Essential** **Reports**.

On the _Essential Reports_ page, scroll to the _Share Progress with Executives_ section and click **Candidate** **Surveys**.

**Note:** The candidate surveys report includes data for all jobs where you have appropriate permissions.

Your survey questions and the response data are displayed.

#### 

#### Benchmarking data

Benchmarking data is the average response to a question based on candidate survey results across all jobs and organizations using the survey.

Benchmarked data is shown in the _Customer Avg._ row under default survey questions.

Benchmarked data isn't available for custom questions that your organization may have [added](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/19605214290331). 

### Report filters

Using the filter panel, the report can be filtered by _submission date, department, and office_.

In order to maintain anonymity, the report cannot be filtered by job since it is possible to deduce candidate feedback with this level of granularity.

### View candidate comments 

Candidates have the option to provide a comment in response to survey questions. Candidate comments aren't viewable inside Greenhouse Recruiting, but you can view them by exporting the report to a spreadsheet.

Click the **Download** icon  in the upper right-hand corner to export the report to a spreadsheet. A spreadsheet of the report will be downloaded with the accompanying comments.

# Greenhouse Recruiting Chrome extension for Sourcing Automation

**Permissions:** Job Admin and above with CRM access and a Sourcing Automation seat

**Product tier:** Available for new subscription tiers (Core, Plus, and Pro)

**Note:** This article is for users with a Sourcing Automation seat. [Click here](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/8304229988635) to learn how to use the Greenhouse Recruiting Chrome extension with CRM access only.

The [Greenhouse Recruiting Chrome extension](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/8302339682843) is a browser plugin that allows your organization to add prospects to your Greenhouse CRM from a website, resume, or manually through the plugin without leaving your current workflow.

For organizations with a Sourcing Automation seat, the extension also has the ability to discover a prospect's email address when parsing their information from select websites. With [lookup credits](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/6018927588635), recruiters can accelerate their outreach initiative and improve response rates through enriched and accurate contact data.

#### In this article

  * Step 1: Install and open the extension
  * Step 2: Locate duplicate prospects
  * Step 3: Add a prospect to the Greenhouse Recruiting Chrome extension
    * Add a prospect from AngelList
    * Add a prospect from GitHub
    * Add a prospect from Indeed
    * Add a prospect from LinkedIn
    * Add a prospect with their resume
    * Add a prospect manually
  * Step 4: Upload your prospect to Greenhouse Recruiting
    * Check for duplicate profiles
    * Perform a phone number lookup
    * Update your prospect's details
    * Set your prospect's pool and source
    * Set your prospect's recruiter and job
    * Provide additional details (optional)
    * Upload your prospect
  * Step 5: Review your uploaded prospect
    * View your prospect's profile in Greenhouse Recruiting
    * Personalize your prospect's first campaign email
    * Manually complete your first task
    * Complete your first InMail task
  * Security FAQs
  * Additional resources



### Step 1: Install and open the extension

If you haven't already, [install the Greenhouse Recruiting extension](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/8302339682843) from the Chrome Web Store. Make sure to **pin** the extension to your browser for easy access.

Once it's installed, open the extension when you're ready to add prospects to Greenhouse Recruiting. Click the Greenhouse Recruiting **extension icon** from your extensions menu.

### Step 2: Locate duplicate prospects

When parsing a prospect's information from AngelList, Github, and Indeed, highlight the prospect's **name** or **email address** to check for duplicates within Greenhouse Recruiting. The extension checks your campaign pools for duplicates that match one of the following details: first and last name, email, phone number, or LinkedIn URL. These duplicate checks always use all four details and are separate from the [Duplicate tag configuration](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/49207850415003-Configure-the-Duplicate-tag) used for candidate profiles in Greenhouse Recruiting.

If a duplicate isn't found, click **Prefill** to add their information to the extension. 

**Note:** If the highlight feature doesn't work, confirm that the extension has access to website data.

Right-click your pinned Greenhouse Recruiting extension, then select **Manage Extension** from the dropdown. Scroll to _Site access_ and **toggle** to automatically allow access.

Now that you've checked for duplicates, continue adding your prospect to the extension as detailed in Step 3.

### Step 3: Add a prospect to the Greenhouse Recruiting Chrome extension

**Note:** Sourcing Automation users with LinkedIn Recruiter can upload multiple prospects in bulk through the extension. [Learn more](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/21803036511259).

You can add prospects to the Greenhouse Recruiting Chrome extension using the following methods:

  * Add a prospect from AngelList
  * Add a prospect from GitHub
  * Add a prospect from Indeed
  * Add a prospect from LinkedIn
  * Add a prospect using their resume
  * Add a prospect manually



**Note:** An email address is required if [GDPR](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360061849112) rules are enabled for your organization. 

#### Add a prospect from AngelList

Navigate to the **Source** tab from your AngelList homepage.

Select a **search** option from the **Starred** tab or the **All Searches** tab. You can also select **New Search** to create a query.

Click the **Greenhouse** button on your prospect's AngelList profile, then click **Continue** in the Greenhouse Recruiting extension.

**Note:** The Greenhouse button won't be available if a prospect has no name on their AngelList profile. For example, some prospects elect to display their job title instead of their name.

The extension parses an available **first name** , **last name** , and **company** from your prospect's AngelList profile.

**Email lookups for AngelList prospects**

Greenhouse will perform an [email lookup](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/6018927588635) when you add a profile without an email to the extension. The extension will prioritize lookups for personal or work emails based on the priority settings you've configured in [Sourcing Automation account settings](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/5769727776795).

If the extension finds multiple emails that match your lookup priority settings, you can select which email address will be added to Greenhouse Recruiting.

If the extension doesn't find an email address during lookup, the email field will remain blank.

Now that you've added an AngelList prospect, finish uploading their information to Greenhouse Recruiting.

#### Add a prospect from GitHub

Navigate to GitHub and open your prospect's profile.

Click **Greenhouse Recruiting** from your prospect's GitHub profile _,_ then click **Continue** within the extension.

The extension will parse an available **first name** , **last name** , **email address** , and **company** from your prospect's GitHub profile.

**Email lookups for GitHub prospects**

The Greenhouse extension will perform an [email lookup](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/6018927588635) for your prospect's **personal** email address if one isn't available on their GitHub profile. Review your [Sourcing Automation account settings](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/5769727776795) to confirm you've selected **personal email addresses** as your lookup priority.

If the extension doesn't find an email, the email field will remain blank.

Now that you've added a GitHub prospect, finish uploading their information to Greenhouse Recruiting.

#### Add a prospect from Indeed

Navigate to [Indeed for Employers](https://resumes.indeed.com/).

Use the **search panel** to find prospects. You can apply filters to refine your search as needed.

Select a **prospect** from the search results to preview their profile.

Once you've selected a prospect, click their **name** to open their profile in a new tab.

Click the **Greenhouse** icon to add their information to the Greenhouse Recruiting Chrome extension.

The extension will parse an available **first name** , **last name** , and **company** from Indeed.

**Email lookups for Indeed prospects**

Greenhouse will perform an [email lookup](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/6018927588635) when you add a profile without an email to the extension. The extension will prioritize lookups for personal or work emails based on the priority settings you've configured in [Sourcing Automation account settings](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/5769727776795).

If the extension finds multiple emails that match your lookup priority settings, you can select which email address will be added to Greenhouse Recruiting.

If the extension doesn't find an email address during lookup, the email field will remain blank.

Now that you've added an Indeed prospect, finish uploading their information to Greenhouse Recruiting.

#### Add a prospect from LinkedIn

You can [add a prospect from LinkedIn](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/16445656895131) to the Greenhouse Recruiting Chrome extension by saving the prospect's profile as a PDF and uploading it to the extension.

The Greenhouse Recruiting Chrome extension will check for duplicate prospects in your Sourcing Automation campaigns and provide details on any potential duplicates. In addition, you can perform a manual [email lookup](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/6018927588635) to locate your prospect's email.

**Note:** Check out [this resource](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/16445656895131) for full instructions on adding LinkedIn prospects to the Greenhouse Recruiting Chrome extension.

Once you've added a prospect from LinkedIn, finish uploading their information to Greenhouse Recruiting.

#### Add a prospect with their resume

You can add a prospect to the Greenhouse Recruiting Chrome extension by uploading their resume.

**Drag and drop** a resume into the extension or click **Upload resume** to import the document from your files. Greenhouse will parse the resume to fill out your prospect's details.

Now you've added this prospect, finish uploading their information to Greenhouse Recruiting.

#### Add a prospect manually

Manually enter the prospect's available information. 

Once added, click **Continue** and finish uploading their information to Greenhouse Recruiting.

### Step 4: Upload your prospect to Greenhouse Recruiting

#### Check for duplicate profiles

Once you've added a prospect to the extension and clicked **Continue** , the extension allows you to do a final check for duplicate profiles. The extension checks your campaign pools for duplicates using any of these details: first and last name, email, phone number, or LinkedIn URL. The criteria used here are fixed and do not change if you update your [Duplicate tag configuration](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/49207850415003-Configure-the-Duplicate-tag) in the Greenhouse Recruiting web app.

A warning appears if the prospect is a potential duplicate. Click **View duplicate** to open the existing prospect's profile in Greenhouse Recruiting. 

#### Perform a phone number lookup

Click **Lookup** next to the phone icon to perform a lookup for your prospect's phone number.

**Note:** Phone lookups are **turned off** by default. A user with Site Admin access will need to give your organization [access to phone lookups](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/20827297488667) in **Configure** >**Sourcing Automation**.

#### Update your prospect's details

Click the **pencil icon** to make any additional edits to your prospect's personal information. Click **Done** at the top of the page once your edits are complete.

#### Set your prospect's pool and source

Select a **Pool** and **Source** for your prospect.

You can select from either prospect pools or campaign pools. If you select a campaign pool, any prefilled data you configured in the [campaign pool settings](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/5045604930843) tab auto-populates in the extension.

#### Set your prospect's recruiter and job

Select the applicable **Recruiter** and **Job** for this prospect.

#### Provide additional details (optional)

Click **Edit additional details** to add any of the following information for your prospect:

  * Coordinator
  * Department
  * Office
  * Prospect owner
  * Tags
  * Website
  * LinkedIn URL
  * Social media
  * Address
  * Notes



#### Upload your prospect

Once you've filled out the above details, click **Upload prospect** when you're ready to send this prospect to Greenhouse Recruiting.

### Step 5: Review your uploaded prospect

#### View your prospect's profile in Greenhouse Recruiting

Once successfully uploaded, click **View profile** to see your prospect's profile in Greenhouse Recruiting. Their profile will indicate that the prospect was created with the extension.

Click **Upload next prospect** to return to the extension and add new prospects.

**Note** : If a prospect is added to an active campaign pool, they'll receive automated emails at the cadence configured during [campaign pool ](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/5045604930843)setup and the schedule you've configured in settings.

#### Personalize your prospect's first campaign email

If you added this prospect to a campaign pool, you can personalize your prospect's first campaign email within the extension.

Add your personalized message to the email body field and click **Send personalized message**.

**Note:** Message personalization within the extension isn't available if the prospect is missing information needed to fill in any tokens. Click **View profile** to add the information to the prospect's profile, then [complete personalization](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/5285464148379) within your campaign pool.

#### Manually complete your first task

If the first step in your campaign pool is a manual task, you can mark it as complete within the extension.

Complete your manual task, then click **Mark as complete**. The extension will automatically update this step in your campaign pool and move your prospect to the second step.

#### Complete your first InMail task

If the first step in your campaign pool is an InMail task, you can manually complete it within the Chrome extension.

**Note:** Connect your LinkedIn RSC account to Sourcing Automation to use this feature. You'll be reminded to connect your account within the extension if you haven't already.

**Copy your InMail message** from the extension, then manually send this message to your new prospect on LinkedIn. 

Once you've finished messaging your prospect on LinkedIn, click **Mark as complete** in the extension.

The extension will automatically update this step in your campaign pool and move your prospect to the second step.

### Security FAQs

#### Which Google permissions does Sourcing Automation request through the extension?

The Greenhouse Recruiting Chrome extension requests the following permissions:

**Permission** | **Description**  
---|---  
Cookies | Uses cookies to authenticate you as a user and ensure you're logged in to Greenhouse to successfully save data.  
webRequest | Detects when you've downloaded a resume from LinkedIn to automatically parse it in the extension.  
Storage | Uses storage to manage your preference of Greenhouse Recruiting domains and keep a reference to the extension's pop-up window.  
System.display | Adjusts your browser's display size so that the extension is correctly positioned beside your main Chrome window.  
Tabs | Uses the URL of your current browser tab to prefill some extension fields and streamline your experience.  
Host permission | Helps the extension more easily read data from target websites and send that data back to Greenhouse.  
  
### Additional resources

  * [Bulk upload prospects with the Greenhouse Recruiting Chrome extension](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/21803036511259)
  * [Sourcing Automation overview](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/5131929423643)
  * [Manage prospects in a campaign pool](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/5285464148379)
