# I use Google Calendar to schedule and can't edit the interview for a candidate

To edit the interview scheduled with the Google Calendar integration, you must have one of the following things:

  * You must be the original scheduler of the interview.
  * You must have "manage/edit" access to the calendar that the event was scheduled on.



These permissions are based on your Google/Gmail account, and not related to your user permissions in Greenhouse Recruiting.

In other words, if another user scheduled an interview, it was likely scheduled on their personal work calendar associated with their specific Google account, which other users can't modify unless they're given specific permissions.

### Best practices

If your organization wants to have multiple users modify a Google calendar, we typically suggest creating a shared calendar in Google and granting manage/edit access to all the users responsible for scheduling. Using a shared calendar ensures that multiple people can update interviews if the original scheduler is unavailable. [Click here](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360022161532-Create-Shared-Calendar-Google-Calendar-) for more information on creating a shared calendar.

# Time to review applications goal attainment report

**Permissions:** Job Admin and above

**Product tier:** Available for new subscription tiers (Core, Plus, and Pro)

The time to review applications goal is a [company goal](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/8382420999835) that represents the ideal time between when a candidate submits an application and when that candidate is advanced to the next stage or rejected during the Application Review stage or Hiring Manager Review stage.

Use the time to review applications goal attainment report to track your organization's progress on this goal.

**Note:** Credit for this goal goes to the job's assigned [recruiter](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360016347712) during the Application Review stage and the assigned [hiring manager](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360016572311) during the Hiring Manager Review stage. Attainment for this goal occurs when a recruiter or hiring manager moves a candidate to the next stage, rejects a candidate, or leaves feedback for the candidate.

#### In this article

  * View time to review applications goal attainment report
    * Time to review applications goal attainment report visualization
  * Apply report filters
  * Additional resources



### View time to review applications goal attainment report

To create a time to review applications goal attainment report, click **Reports** on your dashboard's navigation bar.

On the  _Reports_ page, click **Essential reports**.

Select **Time to Review Applications Goal Attainment** from the  _Understand Goal and Attainment Metrics****_ section.

Your time to review applications goal attainment report will generate.

Your report will display attainment percentages for your entire organization in a visualization. Below this visual chart, you'll find a breakdown of attainment percentages for individual users or departments (depending on the report filters you've applied) in a table.

Attainment percentages are relative to the [target value your organization set for this goal](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/8382420999835) and the time period you've selected as a filter for your report columns. Each percentage is calculated by the total number of actions completed on time (based on the target value you've set) over the total number of actions overall for your filtered time period.

**For example:** You've set your time to review applications goal report to display your attainment levels per week. Each percentage represents the number of times hiring managers or recruiters reviewed applications within your target **divided by** the total number of times they reviewed applications (whether on time or not) for that week.

#### Time to review applications goal attainment report visualization

The time to review applications report presents your organization's attainment levels in a line chart. The attainment percentage is displayed on the  _y_ -axis and the time period is displayed on the  _x_ -axis.

You can hover over each point in the visualization for additional details.

This visualization will adjust each time you apply new filters from the **Filters and more** dropdown.

### Apply report filters

Click **Filters and more** to apply filters and further refine your report.

You can use the following filters on your time to review applications goal report:

  * **Rows** – select whether to display attainment levels for users or departments
  * **Columns** – select whether to display attainment levels per week, month, or quarter
  * **Activity date** – view goal attainment for a specific date range
  * **User or department filter** – view goal attainment for specific users or departments



**Note:** Activity date is set to the last 180 days by default. To optimize performance, company goals data is only available for the last 365 days.

Click **Apply** to add your selected filters and adjust your report.

### Additional resources

  * [Report on goals](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/8383632617755)
  * [Time to schedule available candidate goal attainment report](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/9166289363739)

# JobsForHer integration

JobsForHer is India's largest career platform to accelerate women's careers. Incepted in 2015, JobsForHer connects over 2.2 million job aspirants registered on the platform to 7500+ companies across the country.

JobsForHer's vision is to enable women to achieve their full potential by helping them to start, restart and rise in their careers. JobsForHer caters to the three largest cohorts of women professionals: women returnees, women in tech, women in leadership, and JobsForHer is expanding their reach to women starters.

JobsForHer's integration with Greenhouse Recruiting allows you to sync job details from Greenhouse Recruiting to your JobsForHer job listing page to allow candidates to apply.

#### In this article

  * Enable the JobsForHer integration
    * Locate your job board URL 
    * Create a job board API key
    * Create custom job fields
  * Use the JobsForHer integration with Greenhouse Recruiting
  * Additional resources



### Enable the JobsForHer integration

#### Locate your job board URL

To make your open jobs available to JobsForHer, you'll need to send your job board URL.

You can find your Job Board URL by navigating to **Configure** > **Job Boards & Posts** > **Ellipsis** icon next to job board > **Edit Board Settings,** then scroll to the URL field.

Copy this URL. You'll send it to JobsForHer in the next step.

[Click here](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/5888210160155) for a more detailed walkthrough of how to locate your job board URL.

#### Create a job board API key

Follow the steps in [this article](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/5888210160155) and use the information below when creating your API key:

  * **API Type:** Job Board
  * **Description:** JobsForHer Job Board API Key



Copy your API key and the job board URL from the previous step and reach out to [admin@jobsforher.com](mailto:admin@jobsforher.com) to enable the integration.

### Create custom job fields

Next, you'll need to create six (6) [custom job fields](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/202609855) in Greenhouse Recruiting in order for your jobs to successfully post on JobsForHer.

To create a custom job field, click the **Configure** icon  on your navigation bar, then click **Custom** **Options**.

Click **Jobs**.

Click **Add** **Field** to create a new custom job field.

Create six (6) custom job fields with the following configurations:

**Name** | **Type**  
---|---  
minimum_experience | Number  
maximum_experience | Number  
functional_area |  Multi-select **Note** : You should add your own options for the multi-select values. Reach out to JobsForHer for assistance configuring these options.  
industry |  Multi-select **Note** : You should add your own options for the multi-select values. Reach out to JobsForHer for assistance configuring these options.  
job_type |  Multi-select **Note** : You should add your own options for the multi-select values. Reach out to JobsForHer for assistance configuring these options.  
description | Long text  
  
**Note** : To learn more about creating custom job fields, check out [Add a custom job field](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/202609855).

Once complete, the custom job fields will appear on your JobsForHer job posts.

**Example**

### Use the JobsForHer integration with Greenhouse Recruiting

Once enabled, the JobsForHer integration will sync jobs from Greenhouse Recruiting to the [JobsForHer website](https://www.jobsforher.com/jobs) within six days of activation.

When candidates apply for your jobs, you'll be able to see application details on your JobsForHer [employer dashboard](https://www.jobsforher.com/employer/jobs/job-application) with the registered email id and password.

### Additional resources

For additional information not covered here, reach out to JobsForHer at [admin@jobsforher.com](mailto:admin@jobsforher.com).

# U.S. Standard demographic questions

**Permissions:** Site Admin

**Product tier:** Available for new subscription tiers (Core, Plus, and Pro)

Designed as an alternative to the federally-approved [EEOC questionnaire](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/205278605), standard demographic question sets are part of Greenhouse Recruiting's [Inclusion](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/sections/4405932901019-Inclusion) offerings, allowing teams to collect self-reported demographic data when candidates apply.

This optional set of six pre-configured demographic questions were developed by a team of [Diversity, Equity, and Inclusion (DE&I) ](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360004910232)experts, for customers looking to utilize a standardized, more inclusive way of capturing data to improve their team's overall DE&I reporting.

Using standard demographic questions, your team can better understand your hiring pipeline to make more confident and informed hiring decisions, uncovering any potential biases along the way.

#### In this article

  * Configure standard demographic questions
    * Enable standard demographic questions 
    * Enable standard demographic questions for job posts and/or candidate surveys
    * Review and edit U.S. standard demographic questions  

      * Edit external description
      * Review standard demographic questions and answer options
  * Add standard demographic questions to a job post
  * Add standard demographic questions to the candidate survey
  * Report on standard demographic questions
  * Standard demographic question best practices



**Note:** This question set is based on Greenhouse's own practices to collect demographic information for U.S.-based applicants. This question set does not replace the standard EEOC questions for companies that are required by law to report on candidate demographic data.

Please consult with your company’s own legal counsel before enabling this question set, as there are risks inherent to collecting demographic data where it is not required to do so, and Greenhouse disclaims any legal responsibility for the wording of the questions themselves.

In addition, Greenhouse will not be responsible for any liability that may arise out of your use of this question set.

### Configure standard demographic questions

#### Enable standard demographic questions

To turn on standard demographic questions for your organization, click **Configure** in the top-right corner of your dashboard, then select **Inclusion Tools.**

Locate the **U.S. Standard Demographic Questions** by scrolling down to the _Demographic Question Sets_ section on the _Configure Inclusion Tools_ tab.

**Toggle** to activate. 

A green checkmark will confirm the feature is **On.**

#### Enable standard demographic questions for job posts and/or candidate surveys

After activating standard demographic questions, scroll to the **Add demographic questions to** section directly below to allow your team to add the questions to your job posts or candidate surveys.

**Toggle** to enable an option.

**Note:** The ability to configure U.S. Standard Demographic Questions on [candidate surveys](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360029861512) and access those results in reporting is available to organizations subscribed to our [Expert tier](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360047194191). Customers on other subscription tiers will not see this option. 

After enabling demographic questions for your candidate surveys and/or job posts, you'll need to add the questions to your job posts to ensure candidates can access the sets when applying. [Click here](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360014863312) to learn more. 

#### Review and edit U.S. standard demographic questions

Standard demographic question sets are designed to promote [structured DE&I reporting](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360004985331). For this reason, your team won't have the ability to edit the set's title, questions or answers.

Team members can, however, edit the _External description_ for your questions. This description will appear as a section header on job posts where the standard demographic question sets have been configured to appear.

#### Edit external description

To edit the external description, click on **U.S. Standard Demographic Questions** from the _Configure Inclusion Tools_ page.

Scroll to the _External Description_ text box, then edit the text.

**Save** when finished.

#### Review standard demographic questions and answer options

Standard demographic questions and their configured answer options are viewable from the _Edit U.S. Standard Demographic Questions_ page. By design, standard demographic questions cannot be edited.

If your team is interested in creating customized demographic questions and answer options, [click here](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360004588971).

U.S. standard demographic question | Answer options  
---|---  
**How would you describe your gender identity? (mark all that apply)** |  Man Non-binary Woman I prefer to self-describe I don't wish to answer  
**How would you describe your racial/ethnic background? (mark all that apply)** |  Black or of African descent East Asian Hispanic, Latinx or of Spanish Origin Indigenous, American Indian or Alaska Native Middle Eastern or North African Native Hawaiian or Pacific Islander South Asian Southeast Asian White or European I prefer to self-describe I don't wish to answer  
**How would you describe your sexual orientation? (mark all that apply)** |  Asexual Bisexual and/or pansexual Gay Heterosexual Lesbian Queer I prefer to self-describe I don't wish to answer  
**Do you identify as transgender?** |  Yes No I prefer to self-describe I don't wish to answer  
**Do you have a disability or chronic condition (physical, visual, auditory, cognitive, mental, emotional, or other) that substantially limits one or more of your major life activities, including mobility, communication (seeing, hearing, speaking), and learning?** |  Yes No I prefer to self-describe I don't wish to answer  
**Are you a veteran or active member of the United States Armed Forces?** |  I am a veteran or active member No, I am not a veteran or active member I prefer to self-describe I don't wish to answer  
  
### Add standard demographic questions to a job post

Ensure **Job Posts** are toggled on for your organization on the _Configure Inclusion tools_ page.

Then, go to the _Job Posts_ page for a job. _(Job > **Job Setup** > **Job Posts**)_

Click the **Edit** icon  next to a job post.

On the _Edit Your Job Post_ page, scroll down to the _Settings_ section. Click the checkbox next to **Include Demographic Questions** , then select **U.S. Standard Demographic Questions** from the dropdown.

**Note:** Expert tier customers may have previously created custom demographic questions that are similar in name to Greenhouse Recruiting's U.S. standard demographic questions. To avoid confusion, we recommend renaming any existing question sets to better differentiate between question sets when selecting an option from the dropdown.

Scroll to the bottom of the page, then click **Preview** to see what your changes will look like on the live job post.

When you finish making changes, click **Save**.

### Add standard demographic questions to the candidate survey

**Note:** This option is only available for customers with an Pro subscription. 

Make sure to first [configure the **Candidate Survey**](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/202040375) your organization. Then, make sure the toggle is set to On on the _Configure Inclusion_ tools page.

**Note:** If a candidate has already completed the standard demographic question set in a job post, they won't receive the question set with the candidate survey.

### Report on standard demographic questions

#### Essential report

The [Standard demographic data report](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/7987759577243) displays details on the number of applicants and number of hires for a particular demographic answer.

**Note:** All candidate demographic data is **anonymized** for compliance purposes and to reduce unconscious bias in the hiring process. Your organization's Greenhouse Recruiting users can only view anonymized candidate demographic data. In addition, Greenhouse Technical Support cannot access candidate demographic data unless given explicit consent by your organization.

**Note:** To protect candidate anonymity, in categories where less than five candidates have been hired, the standard demographic data report will show `<5` instead of an exact number.

#### Other reports

The [Pipeline by demographic report](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360007254531), [Sourcing by demographic report](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360017457032) and [Candidate surveys by demographic report](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360018063972) also include the standard demographic questions as a filter option. In addition, standard demographic questions will appear in [Business Intelligence Connector](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360017503272) reports.

**Note:** These reports are only available for Expert tier customers.

### Standard demographic question best practices

[Click here](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/8292714720667) for more information on using demographic reporting.

# Here’s how Tray.io leverages recruitment analytics to put people first

Leveraging data to drive decision-making has benefited hundreds of industries, companies and teams over the last decade. But what about those areas of business where data has traditionally been hard to come by – such as within talent teams? Can businesses really measure the human element of hiring?

The answer is a [strong yes](https://www.greenhouse.io/guidance/structured-hiring-101-4). Being a data-driven talent team really comes down to embracing a structured hiring process. With structured hiring in place, companies gain recruitment analytics – valuable, data-driven feedback that allows them to iterate and improve on what works (and reduce what doesn’t). This consistent data feedback loop serves as the foundation for great hiring practices, driving better business outcomes and setting companies up for success year after year.

One such company, Greenhouse customer [Tray.io](https://tray.io/), has been leading the charge in structured hiring and seeing their success pay off in a big way. We sat down with Michael Kieran, Head of Talent at Tray.io, to discuss what structured hiring means to his team – and how data-driven decision-making via recruitment analytics elevates the human side of hiring.

### To start, can you give us a bit of background on Tray.io?

**Michael:** We're in the enterprise automation space – in other words, we help cloud apps talk to each other. It’s a pretty exciting time for us as an industry because there are more cloud apps now than ever before, providing us with more opportunities to help the businesses we serve. Ultimately, our goal at Tray.io is to make people’s lives easier and make a positive impact on the world through tech.

For example, we recently had an organic food distributor in the UK that needed help keeping up with demand, so we used our product to create an entirely different supply chain that works really well for them and their existing systems. That’s just one recent example, but there are so many opportunities right now for us to make a real difference. We’re ready to do that because we have the people to make it all happen.

### Let’s dive deeper into the people element of your business. As Head of Talent, what’s your team’s philosophy when it comes to hiring?

**Michael:** I think the number one reason people love getting up and going to work at Tray.io is the people that they're going to work with. We've got the best people in the world and the best team in the world, and that powers everything we do for our customers. We make people's lives easier and enable the creation of workplace superheroes – in essence, we empower people to think bigger and achieve more at work. That’s why great hiring is vital to the success of our business.

When we bring new hires on board at Tray.io, unanimous but indifferent is not what we are looking for – in other words, we want a strong yes! To get that strong yes, [we use Greenhouse scorecards](https://www.greenhouse.io/blog/the-hiring-mindset-series-how-to-implement-candidate-scorecard-adoption) and the data from those scorecards to drive our decision-making and reduce bias. Does the candidate display empathy? How does the candidate approach problem-solving? Do they think collaboratively? We look to our Greenhouse scorecards to measure the human element of every hire and use data to back up our decisions. Once we get those strong yes scores across the board, we can get excited about the candidate and really advocate for them to become a part of our team.

"We look to our Greenhouse scorecards to measure the human element of every hire."  
Michael Kieran, Head of Talent at Tray.io

### Has 2020 impacted the way you think about hiring at all?

**Michael:** This year has been a challenging one for many businesses, ours included. Our hiring plans match our growing business landscape, our customers' success – and empowering our customers to succeed is within our control. We strategically decided to continue hiring throughout this year so that we don’t lose our momentum – we’re keeping our foot on the gas. Ultimately, the uncertainty of 2020 is an opportunity to emphasize one of our key priorities: [hiring quality](https://www.greenhouse.io/guidance/recruiter-agility-building-a-strong-hiring-foundation-when-youre-not-hiring). It’s made us think even more critically about how we build the team, using data to drive our decisions while maintaining the human experience of hiring.

### Can you expand on that? Let’s explore some specific ways in which you structure your hiring at Tray.io in 2020.

**Michael:** We started by rethinking the typical interview process and building out candidate cohorts; in other words, we began moving candidates through the hiring process within the same timeline, rather than starting each candidate out on separate timelines (which could range from two to four weeks of difference in some cases).

Then, based on our structured hiring scorecards from Greenhouse, we evaluate the candidates and move the top 25% of the cohort to the next hiring stage. Yes, waiting until we can get all candidates into the same timeline adds a bit more time to the process – but by slowing it down and having the ability to look at the [data in an unbiased](https://www.greenhouse.io/guidance/reduce-bias-when-automating-high-volume-applications) way, it’s easier to evaluate which candidate would be our top choice for the role. Each cohort round ends with a debrief for us to discuss the top candidates all in the same day and really address the diversity and strengths of each individual. We also use calibration reports to weigh our scoring after every interview, benefitting our candidates.

### How do you get leadership alignment on these new hiring processes?

**Michael:** Our senior leadership at Tray.io has fully embraced Greenhouse scorecards to make hiring a data-driven process. When we're only putting forward a small number of people for a final stage, it becomes very easy for them to dive a little bit deeper and read every single scorecard to understand why each candidate would be a good fit. It’s important to have these really thoughtful conversations with leaders and be able to say with certainty, “This is somebody who we know, based on our structured hiring processes, is the best person available.”

We want to be able to go to bat for each and every hire. All our hires should have a strong yes from the recruiting team – powered by the data – and confirmed with another strong yes from our leadership team. By [taking bias out of the equation](https://www.greenhouse.io/blog/how-unconscious-bias-affects-employee-experience-and-how-to-reduce-it) and really looking at the results of our processes, we’re able to get the best of both worlds: a data-driven process powered by the human element.

### It’s great to hear that your team is seeing these positive results from structured hiring. Have you seen any benefits when it comes to candidate experience?

**Michael:** Absolutely. It’s been especially beneficial for us when it comes to expectation-setting with candidates. Yes, we’re [slowing down our processes ](https://www.greenhouse.io/blog/adapting-hiring-slowdown-guide)at this time, but we don’t want to create a situation that goes on for longer than the candidate expects. We’ve gotten really good at communicating the timeline up front. That allows candidates to manage their options properly, as well as do the research they need to be confident when choosing us.

### What has been the key to your hiring success?

**Michael:** We’re able to make data-driven decisions on what excellence means to us when it comes to hiring. That has really accelerated this year. We’re leaning into the structured hiring process and using all the tools available through Greenhouse in order to make that happen.

Scorecard responses have been better and more complete than ever before. Our employees now know that when they want to champion someone, they need to document it exceptionally well. The quality of our scorecard notes, details, attributes and more has gone up substantially over time. Executives especially are really looking to understand what's happening with candidates and how they move through our process. Ultimately, that’s how we’re using data to put people first.

**Learn how to improve leadership alignment, optimize the candidate experience and reduce bias in your hiring process with [Greenhouse recruiting and structured hiring](https://www.greenhouse.io/recruiting).**

_Michael Kieran is the Head of Talent at_[Tray.io](http://tray.io/) _, a hypergrowth enterprise automation platform that helps people do more, faster by connecting cloud applications.__Prior to Tray.io, Michael lead Recruiting for Duo Security, a company that many credit to democratizing security by focusing on user-friendly, intuitive experiences while ushering in the era of zero trust networks_.

# CreativeGuild integration

CreativeGuild is the global company directory and job board from [CreativeMornings](https://creativemornings.com/). It is a place to hire and get hired, show off your work and unique company culture, and make new connections with creatives around the world. CreativeGuild members gain access to unlimited job postings on their global job board.

Greenhouse Recruiting’s integration with CreativeGuild allows Greenhouse users to amplify their hiring efforts by syncing their jobs directly to their global job board. A unique benefit for Greenhouse users is that you can sync your job boards directly so that any edits you make to postings in Greenhouse Recruiting will be reflected in CreativeGuild. In this article, we will cover how to sync your organization's Greenhouse job board with CreativeGuild.

### Integrate CreateGuild with Greenhouse Recruiting

To start, become a CreativeGuild company member by visiting [www.creativemornings.com/join](http://www.creativemornings.com/join).

Once you are a company member, log into your **CreativeMornings account** and visit your company page via the _dropdown menu_ in the upper right-hand corner.

Select **Create Job Post** on your company page.

Instead of manually entering a single job posting on the subsequent page, select**Sync Job Board**.

Enter your **Greenhouse job board URL** and click **Save**.

Your posts automatically begin to populate on both your company page and CreativeGuild's global job board.

Integration candidates who click on jobs through your CreativeGuild company page, or the global job board, are redirected to your original job post with a UTM tag in the URL referencing CreativeGuild.

# Re-trigger job approval stage request

**Permissions:** Site Admin who can see private notes, salary info, manage offers, request approval, and approve jobs / offers, and Job Admin who can view and edit job fields and approve / request approval on jobs

**Product tier:** Available for new subscription tiers (Core, Plus, and Pro)

A job approval process allows your organization to configure a flow whereby a secondary person must review and approve the details of a job in Greenhouse Recruiting before candidate recruitment and / or offer creation can begin.

Since an approval process is intended to provide accurate job details to the approver, changes to a job's details can trigger a second re-approval process while the initial approval process is underway. In this article, we'll cover the impacts of re-triggering job approval on one-stage and two-stage job approvals.

For more information on the difference between one-stage and two-stage job approval flows, [click here](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360025756071-One-Stage-vs-Two-Stage-Job-Approvals).

**Note** : In the case of a two-stage job approval process, the second-stage approval process can be triggered even after full approval.

#### In this article

  * One-stage job approvals
  * Two-stage job approvals



### One-stage job approvals

With a one-stage job approval flow enabled, any newly created job is opened in a _Draft_ job status instead of being immediately available for candidate recruitment. People configured to be job approvers are notified that the new job is pending approval.

While a job is pending approval, changes to the following job details will re-trigger another email to notify the approver of the changes and request approval:

  * Requisition ID
  * Openings
  * Opening IDs
  * Department
  * Employment type



### 

The original approval notification email requesting approval will be voided and the new re-triggered email will allow the approver to reject or approve the job.

### Two-stage job approvals

With a two-stage job approval flow enabled, any newly created job is opened in a _Draft_ status instead of being immediately available for candidate recruitment. Once the final person approves the job, it'll be opened for candidate recruitment as _Open (Approval Pending)_.

Unlike a one-stage job approval, a two-stage job approval requires a second approval process to generate an offer for a candidate. We've outlined the various approval states a job can be in and what changes to specific job details can trigger:

#### Before first-stage approval received

If a job is still awaiting first-stage approval, the job status is _Draft_. This means the designated approver for the job has yet to approve the job for candidate recruitment.

Any changes to the following fields re-trigger the approval request email to begin candidate recruitment:

  * Requisition ID
  * Openings
  * Opening IDs
  * Department
  * Employment type



#### Between first-stage and second-stage approvals

If a job has been approved for candidate recruitment but not yet approved for the second stage (generating offers), the job status is _Open (Approval Pending)_.

Any changes to the following fields re-trigger the approval request email to begin candidate recruitment:

  * Requisition ID
  * Openings
  * Opening IDs
  * Department
  * Employment type



#### After second-stage approval received

If a job has received approval to start creating offers for candidates the job is considered fully open and the job status is _Open_.

Any changes to the following fields re-trigger the second-stage approval only:

  * Requisition ID
  * Openings
  * Opening IDs
  * Department
  * Employment type



**Note** : To re-trigger the first stage approval email (such as approval to start recruiting) in this scenario, the job must be set to _Draft_ mode, have its job details changed, and then be re-submitted for approval.

# Talent Finder

**Permissions:** Job Admins or above, with access to CRM and prospects

**Product tier:** Available for new subscription tiers (Core, Plus, and Pro)

**Note:** For most customers, Talent Finder has been replaced by Talent Rediscovery. [Click here to learn more.](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/30184390692379)

Greenhouse CRM's Talent Finder feature allows your organization to tap into the various groups of talent cultivated through your sourcing and recruitment efforts for any job. Using this feature, your organization can jumpstart sourcing for a job, and infuse your current pipeline with candidates who previously made it to the Offer and Face-to-face milestones in other jobs.

#### In this article

  * Navigate to Talent Finder
  * Find prospects with Talent Finder
  * Filter candidates by rejection reason
  * Include prospects from a prospect pool
  * Build your own search



### Navigate to Talent Finder

Talent Finder can be found on any open job's dashboard. To launch Talent Finder, click **Find Prospects** in the _Prospecting_ panel.

**Note:** Talent Finder is only available for open jobs.

### Find prospects with Talent Finder

By default, Talent Finder filters candidates by the **Department** and **Office** of the selected job.

To remove or change these defaults, or to apply additional filters by **Job** or **Tags** , click the **Edit** icon  and select new values from the dropdown menu.

When you're finished, click **Save** to update the list.

Talent Finder allows you to quickly search for candidates who reached the **Offer** or **Face-to-face** milestones for the filters configured above.

**Note:** Talent Finder only displays candidates across the Offer and Face-to-face milestones.

To quickly view the list of defined candidates, click the number link on the right side of the table.

### Filter candidates by rejection reason

To further filter the list of candidates in the Offer or Face-to-face milestone, click the **Edit** icon  and choose a rejection reason from the dropdown menu.

Select a **Rejection Reason** and click **Save.**

### Include prospects from a prospect pool

In addition to previous candidates from Offer and Face-to-Face milestones, Talent Finder allows your organization to quickly access the prospect pools you have configured in [CRM](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360022793612).

You can select an existing prospect pool from the dropdown menu. When you're finished, click **Save** to update the list.

### Build your own search

Your organization can also build your own custom search by clicking **Build Your Own Search**. When you click this button, you'll be navigated to the _Candidates_ page with all the page filters (including prospect pools and rejection reasons) automatically applied.

# Restrict job creation to template jobs for all Job Admins 

**Permissions:** Site Admin who can edit another user's advanced permissions

**Product tier:** Available for new subscription tiers (Core, Plus, and Pro)

A [template job](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360038222812) is a template that includes the key components for most of the jobs your organization will open. Users with the appropriate permissions to create a new job can use this template as a starting point when creating a new job. Alternatively, if your organization wants to exert more control over the jobs your users can create, you can restrict new job creation to only those based on template jobs.

This article will cover how to restrict users with Job Admin level permissions so that they can only create new jobs based on template jobs. 

**Note** : To create new jobs based only on templates, users with Job Admin level permissions will still need the user-specific permission **Can create new jobs and request job approvals**. 

Go to the _Permissions Policies_ page. _(__**Configure** icon  > **Permission Policies**)_

Navigate to the  _Job Admins_ section and uncheck the box inline with**Allow Job Admins to create or copy non-template jobs during job creation**.

**Note** : By default, this box is checked so Job Admins who can create new jobs can create non-template jobs.

Job Admins who can create new jobs can now only create new jobs that are based on template jobs where you have given them at least Job Admin level permissions. 

Users will be directed to the _Copy an Existing Job_ page when they try to create a new job. The _Copy an Existing Job_ page will be filtered to show jobs marked as a template only.

**Note** : It is important to remember that you will still need to assign Job Admin level access to users for template jobs. By doing this, Greenhouse Recruiting can accurately show the templates a user can access during the job creation process

# Scheduling for Daylight Saving Time

**Permissions:** \--

**Product tier:** Available for new subscription tiers (Core, Plus, and Pro)

Greenhouse Recruiting automatically adjusts to account for the beginning and end of Daylight Saving Time (DST).

If you are scheduling interviews that will occur / [emails that will be sent](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/202817609) after the beginning or end of DST, you do not need to make any manual adjustments to account for the time change. 

**Example:** If _before_ DST starts, you are scheduling an interview that will occur at 2:00 p.m. the day _after_ DST starts, you should schedule the interview for 2:00 p.m. When DST begins, Greenhouse Recruiting will not move the interview ahead to 3:00 p.m. The interview will remain scheduled for 2:00 p.m. as intended.

# Prospect owner

**Permissions:** Job Admin and above with access to CRM and prospects

**Product tier:** Available for new subscription tiers (Core, Plus, and Pro)

The prospect owner feature allows your organization to configure a user in charge of managing the relationship with a specific prospect.

#### In this article

  * Prospect owner overview
  * Assign prospect owner
  * Assign prospect owner in bulk



### Prospect owner overview

Configured per prospect application (i.e. a prospect with multiple applications can have multiple prospect owners), prospect owners are given access to the specific prospect process for the prospect.

By selecting a specific user for the prospect owner role, your organization can retroactively assess the performance of a [sourcer](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360016347852-Hiring-Team-Role-Sourcer) (or a user with a similar task) who was initially responsible for the prospect. Use reports such as the [prospect conversion report ](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/115002427623-Prospect-Conversion-Report)and [prospecting activity report ](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/204636785-Prospecting-Activity-Report)to measure the performance of your sourcing team and answer questions such as _how many prospects owned by a specific sourcer were converted to candidates?_

### Assign prospect owner

**Note** : Prospect owner roles can be assigned to users without a CRM user license. However, users without a CRM user license cannot edit the prospect owner field.

You can assign or update a prospect owner by navigating to their profile and clicking **Edit** in the main panel.

Select a user from the pop-up menu and click **Save**. They'll be assigned as the new prospect owner.

### Assign prospect owner in bulk

A prospect owner can be assigned to multiple prospects using the Greenhouse Recruiting bulk action feature.

Click**Candidates** from your navigation bar and expand the **Application Type** filter on the left.

Select **Prospects only** from the _Type_ dropdown.

Click **Bulk Actions** at the top-right.

Select the prospects who will have a new prospect owner assigned through the bulk action by clicking the checkbox to the left of their name.

When finished, click **Edit Selected**.

Click **Edit Prospect Owner**.

Select a user to be the prospect owner for these prospects and click **Save**.

# Zinc integration

Zinc offers automated reference and background checks, helping customers put scalable process checks in place so deeper candidate insights are gleaned. 

Greenhouse Recruiting's integration with Zinc allows you to leverage background checks within your interview plans.

#### In this article

  * Retrieve your API key from Zinc
  * Enable the Zinc integration
  * Use the Zinc integration with Greenhouse Recruiting
    * Send and review the test
    * Additional options
  * Additional resources



### Retrieve your API key from Zinc

To retrieve your API key from Zinc, log into your Zinc account and select your name at the bottom of your Zinc profile.

Click **Generate API key**.

Click **Copy.** You'll enter the copied API key into Greenhouse Recruiting in the next step.

### Enable the Zinc integration

Once you've retrieved your API key, follow the steps in [this article](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/5888163696923) to add the assessment stage in your interview plans. Once you’ve set up your interview plans and configured your take home test, you’ll be able to send the test to candidates.

**Note** : Don't send the API key in this initial email. Greenhouse Technical Support will respond with a [SendSafely link](https://www.sendsafely.com/howitworks/) for you to securely share your API key.

Once Greenhouse Technical Support receives your API key via SendSafely, we'll email you to confirm that your API key has been set up in your account and that your integration is enabled.

**Note:** To verify your identity, Greenhouse Technical Support might request you provide a [support verification code](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360022771952) before adding the API key to your organization's account.

### Use the Zinc integration with Greenhouse Recruiting

Once the integration is enabled, add the Zinc background check by first navigating to a job dashboard and click the **Job** **Setup** tab. Select **Interview** **Plan** from the listed options. 

Click **Add Stage** to search and select the Zinc background check from the list.

Configure the interview stage placement, then click **Edit** on the interview kit to select the correct test and assign graders to review the assessment.

#### Send and review test

When a candidate enters the stage with a Zinc background check, your team can click **Send** **Test** to send the assessment to your candidates. 

When you send a test from Greenhouse Recruiting, the interview instructions actually are sent by Zinc.

The graders will be notified and can view a link to their submission directly from the scorecard in Greenhouse Recruiting.

**Note:** If you want to automate assessments being sent to your candidates, [create a stage transition rule](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360053129752).

Once [configured](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360048178672), assessments will be triggered to send automatically after a candidate moves into the partner assessment stage. 

#### Additional options

**Custom branding:** If you wish to add custom branding to your candidate’s journeys please contact your Zinc account manager.

**Edit your reference questions:** If you wish to edit the questions asked in references, you can do so from your questions page in Zinc. You can also enter company values and things you want Zinc to analyze across your checks.

**Build your background check packages:** If you wish to change the background checks shown in the Greenhouse Recruiting packages please contact your Zinc account manager.

### Additional resources

For additional questions or for integration troubleshooting, reach out to [contact@zincwork.com](mailto:contact@zincwork.com).

**Permissions:** Site Admin, and Job Admin who can manage custom fields

Offer sections allow your organization to create conditional language for custom offer field options. This conditional language can be used to build and customize offer letters based on selections made when generating a candidate offer.

<!-- source: https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360025499691-Close-a-job -->

# Close a job

**Permissions: Site Admin** and **Job Admin** , who can edit job info

**Product tier:** Available for new subscription tiers (Core, Plus, and Pro)

Closing a job preserves all the configurations made on the job while restricting users from adding candidates to the job, visiting the job dashboard, and submitting scorecards to the job. Additionally, this action un-publishes the job's job posts from all of your organization's job boards.

There are many [reasons to close a job](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/213351483-Close-Reasons-for-Job-Openings):

  * Making the necessary new headcount or backfill hires
  * The job is placed on hold while your organization priorities other roles
  * Your organization has implemented a hiring freeze
  * The job is temporarily not being filled 



_**Note** : All active candidates will remain active on a closed job. We suggest your organization reject these candidates or move them to another job._

To close a job, click the **Jobs** tab from the navigation bar and select a job from the subsequent list. Click **Job Setup** and navigate to **Job Info**.

From the _Job Info_ page, hover over _Job Status_ and click the **Edit** icon .

Select **Closed** from the dropdown menu. Click **Save**.

Note: 

If the job has any pending offers, a dialog box will ask if you wish to **Mark Candidates as Hired** before closing the job. Click a candidate name to review their application without closing the job. Alternatively, click **Cancel** to dismiss the close job action, or click **Continue** to move forward with the close job action. 

If the job does not have any pending offers, or if you click **Continue** in the dialog box discussed above, a subsequent dialogue box will ask you to confirm the decision to close the job. Select a [**Close Reason**](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/213351483) from the dropdown menu and click **Save.**

The job will be closed and users can no longer add candidates to the job, visit the job dashboard, or submit scorecards for the job.

_**Note:** An interviewer with an outstanding scorecard for a closed job will encounter an error page if they click the Interview Kit URL provided to them. The job must be re-opened for the interviewer to access and submit their scorecard. _

To learn how to search for and re-open a job after closing, review the following articles: 

  * [Search for Closed Jobs](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/115002711983)
  * [Re-open Job](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360025208872)

# New referrals notification

**Permissions:** Job Admin and above

**Product tier:** Available for new subscription tiers (Core, Plus, and Pro)

Configuring a referral notification list allows your organization to automate internal communication to select team members when a job [receives a new referral](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/201982560). Once configured, any user added to the referral notification list will receive an email notification per new referral made for the job. 

#### In this article:

  * Configure new referrals notification on a job
  * Remove users from new referrals notifications



### Configure new referrals notification on a job

To begin new referral notification setup, click**Jobs** from the navigation bar and select a job from the subsequent list.

Click **Job Setup** from the listed panel options and navigate to **Notifications** on the left.

On the _Notifications_ page, scroll to **New Referrals** within the _Candidate Notifications_ section. Click **Configure.**

**Note** : The text of the email notification for new referrals cannot be edited.

To add users to the notification list for new referrals, click the _Participant(s)_ dropdown and select the appropriate user. You can select a user by name, or you can select the [Hiring Manager(s)](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360016572311) listed on the job's [Hiring Team](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/115002194983), the Candidate's Recruiter, and/or the Candidate's Coordinator.

**Note** : Only users who have appropriate [job-based permissions assigned](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360040181991) will populate in the dropdown menu.

Repeat as necessary for other users who should be notified when the job receives a new referral. **Save** when finished.

All selected users will receive an email for every new referral on the job with relevant contact and application information.

**Note** : Site Admins who enable the new referrals notification will also get all email notifications for [prospect referrals with no jobs](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/206729066). This cannot be adjusted.

### Remove users from notification list for referrals

To remove users from the new referral notification list, navigate to the name of a user listed in the provided field and click **X** to the right of their name.

Repeat as necessary for other users. **Save** when finished.

# Manager form

**Permissions:** Managers

**Product tier:** Available to Greenhouse Welcome and Greenhouse Onboarding subscription tiers

When a new hire is onboarded, there are various logistical pieces of information that their manager needs to provide for a successful onboarding. For example, the following questions would require input from an onboarding employee's manager:

  * What kind of software should be ordered for the new hire?
  * Which distribution lists should the new hire be added to?
  * What kind of computer equipment needs to be ordered for the employee?
  * Should the new hire be given a company credit card?
  * Who will the new employee's mentor be?



The **manager form** combines these types of questions in one place, giving managers quick and easy access to fill out important fields for their incoming new hires. This article covers how to configure the form for your organization's managers and what managers can expect to receive.

#### In this article

  * Configure the manager form
  * Fill out the manager form
  * Additional resources



### Configure the manager form

Manager forms are created from a combination of employee fields that managers have been granted access to edit. This access is based on permissions set by Owners in **Settings** >**Permissions** >**Manager Additional Access**.

**Note:** [Manager access](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360021729772) to employees' fields can only be configured by users with [Owner access](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360019575491).

Any employee field enabled under the **Can Edit for Direct Reports** column will be included in the manager form. Learn more about [configuring manager additional access](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360021729772).

### Fill out the manager form

When a user is assigned to the **Manager** role for a new hire, they'll be notified by email to provide more information about their new hire.

In the email notification, click **Fill Out Information**.

The manager will be redirected to the **Info tab** on their new hire's [employee profile](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/13298081921179), where they can enter any additional information required for their employee.

# VidReferencing by VidCruiter integration

VidCruiter offers Automated Reference Checking which can be integrated directly within Greenhouse. Greenhouse Recruiting's integration with VidCruiter allows you to seamlessly add VidCruiter's Reference Checking Assessment to a job's interview plan. In this article, we will cover how to:

#### In this article

  * Enable the VidCruiter integration with Greenhouse Recruiting
  * Add VidCruiter stage to job’s interview plan
  * Configure the VidCruiter stage
  * Send and review the test



### Enable the VidCruiter integration with Greenhouse Recruiting

To start, contact your VidCruiter representative ([csm@vidcruiter.com](mailto:csm@vidcruiter.com)) to receive your **API key**. Once you've received your API key, fill out the form at [www.greenhouse.io/asksupport](http://support.greenhouse.io/direct) or _[click here](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/requests/new)_ to open a ticket.

**Note** : Do not send the API key in this initial email.

The Greenhouse Technical Support team will respond with a [SendSafely link](https://www.sendsafely.com/howitworks/) for you to enter your API key. A notification is sent to the Greenhouse Technical Support team after you've entered your API key, and they will email you to confirm that your API key has been set up in your account and your integration is enabled.

**Note:** To verify your identity, the Greenhouse Technical Support team might request you provide a [Support Verification Code](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360022771952) before adding the API key to your organization's account.

### Add VidCruiter stage to job’s interview plan

Once the Greenhouse/VidCruiter integration is enabled for your organization, you can add the VidCruiter Reference Check Assessment as an interview stage.

To do this for an existing job, navigate to the _Job setup page_ (**Jobs****Job Name** **Job Setup** in the _left-side navigation bar_).

From the _Job Setup_ page, navigate to the**Interview Plan** tab and click **Add Stage**.

From the _Add Stage_ window, select the **VidCruiter** stage.

When finished, click **Add**.

### Configure the VidCruiter stage

Once the stage has been added to the job's interview plan, click the **pencil icon** to edit the VidCruiter step.

Use the provided dropdown menu to choose **assessments** that you have previously set up in VidCruiter.

Next, assign at least one **Greenhouse user** to grade/review submitted assessments.

Click **Save** at the bottom of the page when done.

**Note** : All configurations of the assessment itself, including the email template, needs to be done in VidCruiter.

### Send and review the test

When candidates are moved into the VidCruiter interview stage, Greenhouse displays a **Send Test** link.

Click the **link** within the Interview Kit to view the submitted test within the VidCruiter platform.

# Fortay integration

Building a high-performing company culture is one of the most important priorities for the leaders of any organization. Fortay provides a holistic, data-driven toolset that enables you to scale or evolve your company’s culture, as well as track and improve employee engagement.

With Fortay, you can screen candidates for relative team fit, and unlike psychometric (persona) based solutions, Fortay focuses on the collective beliefs and values of your best employees.

Greenhouse Recruiting's integration with Fortay allows you to seamlessly add an assessment to your interview pipeline.

#### In this article

  * Set up the Fortay Integration
    * Create a Harvest API key
    * Provide your API credentials to Fortay
    * Configure an Integration service user (ISU) and complete setup
  * Use the Fortay integration with Greenhouse Recruiting
    * Add the Fortay assessment to your interview plan
    * View candidate results
  * Additional resources



### Set up the Fortay Integration

To enable the integration, refer the steps in [this article](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/5888163696923) to retrieve your API key from your Fortay representative and set up the assessment stage on your job's interview plans.

Once you've enabled the integration and set up your take-home test, you'll be able to send the test to candidates in Greenhouse Recruiting.

#### Create a Harvest API key

To begin setup, you’ll need to create a Harvest API key.

Follow the steps in [this article](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/5888163769883) to create the key, and verify that the permissions below are selected when configuring the Fortay integration.

#### Credentials

In the _Create New Credential_ box, make the following selections:

  * **API Type:** Harvest
  * **Partner:** Fortay or _Unlisted Vendor_
  * **Description:** Fortay Harvest API Key



#### Permissions

Verify that the following permissions are selected for the Fortay integration:

**Applications**

  * DELETE: Delete application
  * GET: Retrieve application
  * GET: List applications
  * PATCH: Update application
  * POST: Advance application
  * POST: Move application
  * POST: Reject application
  * POST: Moves application to job
  * POST: Unreject application
  * POST: Hire application
  * POST: Add attachment to application
  * PATCH: Update a rejected application's rejection reason
  * PATCH: Convert a prospect



**Candidates**

  * DELETE: Delete candidate
  * GET: Retrieve candidate
  * GET: List candidates
  * PATCH: Edit candidate
  * POST: Add candidate
  * POST: Add attachment
  * POST: Add application
  * PUT: Anonymize candidate
  * POST: Add note
  * PUT: Merge two candidates
  * POST: Add education
  * DELETE: Delete education
  * POST: Add employment
  * DELETE: Delete employment
  * POST: Add E-mail
  * POST: Add prospect



When finished, click **Save**.

Your Harvest API key for the Fortay integration is created and configured. Copy the Harvest API key to provide to Fortay in the next step.

**Note** : If additional assistance is needed to configure your API credentials, contact [support@fortay.co](mailto:support@fortay.co).

#### Provide your API credentials to Fortay

After configuring your API credentials, you'll need to provide the key to Fortay. 

Navigate to your Fortay account and from the _Manage_ drop-down menu, select **Integrations**.

On the _Integrations_ page, paste the copied key in the _API key from Greenhouse_ field and then, click **Save**.

Next, click **Click to Show** to reveal the Fortay API key to provide to Greenhouse support to enable the Fortay assessment stage. This key will continue to be accessible using the _Integrations_ page.

**Note** : Do NOT click on _Generate New Token_ unless instructed by Fortay support.

#### Configure an Integration service user (ISU) and complete setup

To allow the Fortay integration the transfer of candidate documents, a user is required for auditing purposes. Follow the steps in [this article](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360027077811-Add-new-users) to create a new user or follow the steps below. 

Navigate to **Configure** > **Users** and select or create a user. Ensure the selected user is [assigned as a Site Admin](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360040189391). 

On the _Edit User_ page, copy the 10-digit sequence in the URL. 

Navigate back to Fortay and then, enter the 10-digit sequence in the _Site Admin ID_ field. **Save** when finished. 

### Use the Fortay integration with Greenhouse Recruiting

#### Add the Fortay assessment to your interview plan

Once the Fortay integration is enabled for your organization, you can [add the Fortay assessment](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/5888163696923-Set-up-an-assessment-API-integration#h_01G2SYAVKVRQ27Z9HP1RV73WXC) as an interview stage on your jobs in Greenhouse Recruiting.

As a best practice, Fortay recommends that the Fortay assessment be positioned as early as possible in the candidate interview process.

When candidates are in the stage, you can send an assessment to a candidate by selecting**Send Test** on their candidate profile next to the interview stage.

**Note** : When you send a test, the assessment and instructions are sent by Fortay and not Greenhouse Recruiting.

#### View candidate results 

You can confirm the candidate has received the Fortay assessment on the _Candidate Invitations_ page in Fortay. The _Source_ in Fortay will indicate Greenhouse ATS.

In Greenhouse Recruiting, the “View Report” within the candidate interview kit will link to the candidate results on Fortay where you will be able to view the detailed results and responses.

A PDF copy of the candidate's results will be accessible via Greenhouse under the **Details** tab of the profile or the **Cover Letter** tab in the Interview kit per the screenshot below.

### Additional resources

For additional information on the integration not covered here, reach out to [support@fortay.co](mailto:support@fortay.co).

# Career.Place integration

Career.Place is an anonymous candidate screening tool that removes bias from hiring. It completely eliminates resumes and any candidate identifying information from the screening process and replaces them with a step-by-step evaluation funnel easily configured by the employer.

The evaluation funnel can include basic requirement questions, trait assessments, scenarios and pre-recorded video interviews. Only those qualified advance through each step of the funnel.

Greenhouse Recruiting's integration with Career.Place allows you to seamlessly add Career.Place’s anonymous candidate screening process to a job's interview plan.

#### In this article

  * Set up the Career.Place integration
  * Use the Career.Place integration
  * Additional resources



### Set up the Career.Place integration

To enable the integration, follow the steps in [this article](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/5888163696923) to retrieve your API key from your Career.Place representative and set up the assessment stage in your interview plans.

Once you've set up your interview plans and configured your take-home test, you'll be able to send the test to candidates.

### Use the Career.Place integration

#### Send and review an assessment

Once the Career.Place integration is enabled for your organization, you will be able to add the Career.Place assessment as an interview stage.

You can send an assessment to a candidate by selecting the**Send Test** button next to the interview stage.

After it has been sent, an assessment's status will display in Greenhouse Recruiting.

#### Review assessment results

Once the candidate has submitted their test, the Interview Kit will contain a link to view the submitted test in the Career.Place application.

To see a candidate's results in Career.Place, click **View Report**.

Based on the associated job configuration in Career.Place, candidates will complete up to four stages:

  * Criteria
  * Assessments
  * Homework
  * Video Interview



If the associated job in Career.Place is configured with Homework and/or Video Interview stages, the appropriate user (Recruiter or Hiring Manager) will need to review the submitted candidate responses, rate them, and provide a disposition on whether the candidate’s responses are a fit or not for the organization.

Candidates are returned to Greenhouse Recruiting as either qualified with a score of 100 or not qualified with a score of 0. When a candidate becomes disqualified in Career.Place, their status is updated in Greenhouse Recruiting immediately. For a candidate to be shown as qualified in Greenhouse Recruiting, the Recruiter or Hiring Manager will need to “Unlock” the candidate in Career.Place.

### Additional resources

For additional information not covered here, reach out to [support@career.place](mailto:support@career.place).

**Product tier:** Available to all product tiers

Sharing updates in MyGreenhouse helps candidates stay organized and understand what’s next while giving your team a more transparent, branded candidate experience with no manual effort.

When you choose to share updates, you can decide whether candidates see application statuses, tasks, or both.

#### In this article

#### Overview

When candidates apply for Greenhouse-hosted jobs, their application details are automatically added to their MyGreenhouse account. When you share updates, they'll see any tasks you've assigned and whether their applications are active or inactive.

Turn the toggle "On." Your changes will be automatically saved.

#### Tasks

Tasks give candidates one place to see and complete important steps in the hiring process, so nothing gets missed. When you share tasks, requests you send from Greenhouse automatically appear in the candidate’s account. This helps candidates stay on track without extra follow-up from your team. 

In MyGreenhouse, candidates can:

  * Share their availability
  * Self-schedule interviews
  * Complete emailed tests
  * Fill out forms
  * Complete candidate experience surveys



#### Turn on tasks

Turn the toggle "On." Your changes will be automatically saved.

# Email best practices

Your users and candidates need to receive your emails in order to keep your hiring goals on track, but sometimes email deliverability issues can get in the way.

To ensure your emails have the best chance of reaching their intended recipients, follow the best practices listed below.

#### In this article

  * Email setup
    * Verify your email domain
    * Allowlist our mail providers' IP addresses
  * Email content
    * Add an email signature
    * Avoid spam triggers
    * Mix up your email content
    * Lengthen your emails
  * Email strategy
    * Avoid bulk emailing
    * Replace outdated candidate email addresses
    * Test your email deliverability



### Email setup

#### Verify your email domain

Greenhouse Recruiting sends emails on your organization's behalf using a third-party mail server.

Since spammers have been known to use similar methods to imitate legitimate email addresses, some mail providers may block emails from Greenhouse or mark them as spam.

To prevent this, be sure to [verify your domain](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/201111684) in your organization's account. This informs mail providers that you've given us permission to send emails on your behalf, which will reduce the chance of your emails being blocked or marked as spam.

#### Allowlist our mail providers' IP addresses

Allowlisting is a process in which you permit, or "allow," certain applications to run. This allows the application to bypass typical security measures and prevent it from being blocked.

You may need to add our [mail providers' IP addresses](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360033429591) to your organization's allowlist. Contact your IT team for help.

### Email content

#### Add an email signature

Emails that include a signature, or sign-off, are less likely to be marked as spam. You can [add and edit an email signature](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/203800669) in your Greenhouse Recruiting account that will automatically be added to your outgoing emails.

#### Avoid spam triggers

Email providers associate certain words and phrases with a higher likelihood of spam. If these are detected in your email, your email may be marked as spam.

Common spam triggers in the hiring industry include:

  * **References to earnings:** "Be your own boss," "Fast cash," "Potential earnings," etc.
  * **References to remote work:** "Home-based," "Online opportunity," "Work while you sleep," etc.
  * **References to personal finances:** "Social security number," "Your income," "Debt," etc.



#### Mix up your email content

Sending multiple identical emails over a short period of time may result in your future emails being marked as spam. Consider adding variety to the body of your emails using [tokens](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360007039771) or other information.

#### Lengthen your emails

Short emails, especially those that include links, are more likely to be marked as spam. If you find that a specific email template is consistently being marked as spam, consider adding more content to the body of the template.

### Email strategy

#### Avoid bulk emailing

Email recipients are more likely to mark an email as spam when the email isn't personally directed at them. While email templates sent to individuals can be personalized with a variety of tokens, the token options for [bulk email](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360050950892) templates are limited. This prevents bulk emails from being as personalized as possible and increases the risk of the recipient marking the bulk email as spam.

For this reason, we encourage you to use the bulk emailing feature only in special circumstances.

#### Replace outdated candidate email addresses

You might sometimes receive a "failed to send" email after attempting to email an invalid address. Continuing to send emails to an invalid email address increases the likelihood of your future emails being marked as spam.

If it's indicated that a candidate's email is invalid, be sure to let me know using another contact method. You can replace the outdated address with a new address in the candidate's profile.

### Test your email deliverability

After following the best practices outlined above, you can check your email deliverability score using a free tool like [Mail Tester](https://www.mail-tester.com/). The test results provide a score out of 10, along with recommended areas of improvement.

**Job Stages**

    * GET: Retrieve Job Stage
    * GET: List Job Stages for Job
    * GET: List Job Stages



When finished, click **Save**.

Your Harvest API key for the Coderbyte integration is created and configured. Copy the Harvest API key to provide to Coderbyte in a later step.

#### Create an integration service user

To update a candidate's status in Greenhouse Recruiting, you'll need to provide Coderbyte with a user who will make the updates.

The user associated with this ID will be listed as the user who provided updates to these values on behalf of Coderbyte. [Create a new service user](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/4405511253659-Create-an-ISU-for-an-integration) with the following details:

  * **Email address:** Use any email address (example: coderbyteintegration@YOURCOMPANY.com)
  * **Permission** : [Site Admin](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360040189391)



Once you created the user, follow [these steps](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/10765948752027-Find-your-user-ID) to obtain the ID of that user.

#### Provide your API credentials to Coderbyte

Next, you'll need to add your API credentials to Coderbyte. To start, [navigate to Coderbyte](https://coderbyte.com/organizations?redirDashboard=true) and **Log in**.

Select **Settings** -> **ATS**. Under the Greenhouse Recruiting logo, click **Connect**.

On the next screen you will be prompted to enter the **Harvest API Key** and **User ID** that you just created.

Once you enter the information, click **Connect**.

#### Create a webhook and finish setup

To leverage the full capability of Coderbyte with Greenhouse Recruiting, you’ll need to create a webhook. Follow the steps in [this article](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/5888163727003) to create your webhook.

After connecting Greenhouse Recruiting to Coderbyte, you should be presented with an instruction for setting a webhook:

These values are secret and unique to your account. Use them to configure the webhook in Greenhouse Recruiting:

  * **Name:** A descriptive name for your integration. Most customers choose ‘Coderbyte integration’
  * **When** : Candidate has changed stage
  * **Endpoint URL:** The Endpoint URL provided by Coderbyte in the _Endpoint URL_ field
  * **Secret Key:** The Secret Key provided by Coderbyte in the _Secret key_ field



### Use the Coderbyte integration with Greenhouse Recruiting

You can navigate to the Workflows page in Coderbyte to configure your recruiting automation.

You can now create Workflows that automatically send assessment invites or move candidates to the next stage after a successful interview.

### Additional resources

For additional information or troubleshooting not covered here, reach out to [integrations@coderbyte.com](mailto:integrations@coderbyte.com) and [https://help.coderbyte.com](https://help.coderbyte.com/).
