# Greenhouse Recruiting browser support

Greenhouse Software's browser support policy outlines our commitment to ensure our application works and performs as intended on the various web browsers and devices your organization may use to access our applications. Greenhouse Software supports a variety of browsers and operating systems across three tiers:

#### In this article

  * Fully supported browsers
  * Partiallly support browsers
  * Unsupported browsers



### 

### Fully support browsers

If a web browser is fully supported, Greenhouse Software will ensure that our application is both functional and performs as expected on these browsers. Fully supported browsers are tested as part of the regular QA process. Below are the web browsers that are fully supported by Greenhouse Software:

**Note** : For supported versions, **current major version minus two** means that Greenhouse Software will provide full support for the most recent major version of the browser and the previous two versions of the browser (i.e. if Chrome 80 is the most recent web browser, we will support Chrome 80, 79, and 78).

**Browser** | **Supported Version** | **End of Life**  
---|---|---  
Chrome | Current major version minus two |   
Edge | Current major version minus two |   
Firefox | Current major version minus two |   
Firefox Extended Support Release (ESR) | Current major version minus two |   
Safari | 12+  | Newer version of MacOS is bundled with a new version of Safari   
  
### 

### Partial support

If a web browser is partially supported, Greenhouse Software will ensure that our application is functional on these browsers. Minor visual/UI defects will not be addressed so long as they do not impede functionality. Partially supported browsers are not part of the regular QA process. Below are the web browsers that are partially supported by Greenhouse Software:

**Browser** | **Supported Version** | **End of Life**  
---|---|---  
Internet Explorer  | 11  | [Lifecycle policy](https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/lifecycle/faq/internet-explorer-microsoft-edge)  
  
**Note** : Greenhouse Software will always support the recommended browser for the latest version of Windows. Presently, that browser is Microsoft Edge on Windows 10. Internet Explorer 11 is the last version of Internet Explorer that will ever be supported by Microsoft, and as such is the last version that we will partially support. Microsoft recommends Microsoft Edge instead of IE11 on Windows 10+.  
  
[Microsoft has announced it will end support for Internet Explorer 11](https://techcommunity.microsoft.com/t5/windows-it-pro-blog/internet-explorer-11-desktop-app-retirement-faq/ba-p/2366549) on February 14, 2023. Greenhouse Software will stop supporting Internet Explorer 11 on the same date.

### 

### Unsupported browsers

If a web browser is unsupported, Greenhouse Software will not ensure that Greenhouse Recruiting is functional on these browsers. Any browser that is not listed in fully supported or partially supported is not supported at this time.

# LinkedIn RSC+ integration

Linkedin’s RSC+ integration with Greenhouse Recruiting allows users to keep ATS data seamlessly aligned across systems. [RSC+](https://www.linkedin.com/help/recruiter/answer/a8052001) continuously pulls data from your ATS (Applicant Tracking System), ensuring your candidate, job, and application information on LinkedIn Recruiter is always up-to-date and consistent for your hiring team. This free upgrade to your Recruiter System Connect (RSC) experience strengthens your ATS connection so you can see more complete candidate records (e.g., resumes, phone numbers) in the flow of work - saving your team from switching platforms. This improved data quality powers LinkedIn Talent Solutions features like Connected Projects and ATS-enabled Reporting, making your hiring workflow smoother. While RSC+ gives LinkedIn access to more data, the way LinkedIn processes, handles, and stores that data remains unchanged from standard Recruiter System Connect.

#### In this article

  * Enable the RSC+ integration
  * Use the RSC+ integration
  * Additional resources



### Enable the RSC+ integration

  1. As a pre-requisite you will need to configure [Recruiter System Connect ](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/115005678103-LinkedIn-Recruiter-System-Connect-RSC-integration)in Greenhouse and must be both 1) a LinkedIn Recruiter Admin, 2) a Greenhouse Site Admin 
  2. In LinkedIn Recruiter, navigate to ‘Product Settings’  

  3. On the left nav, select the ‘Manage Integrations’ tab. If you do not see this tab, Recruiter System Connect has not been activated. Please follow steps [here](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/115005678103-LinkedIn-Recruiter-System-Connect-RSC-integration) to complete onboarding.



  4. Navigate to your Greenhouse application, and click “Authorize” next to “RSC+”



  5. Review the data scope and permissions, and click “Login into ATS”



  6. In the Greenhouse login popup, enter your ATS admin credentials, and click “Log in to Greenhouse”. If necessary, complete any additional login steps using your Site admin or Greenhouse ISU credentials



  7. Select “Authorize using a service account” to ensure that the connection remains even after you leave the company. 



  8. Once complete, you will be redirected back to the LinkedIn Recruiter authentication screen and see the confirmation notice:



### **Use the RSC+ integration**

To initiate [RSC+](https://www.linkedin.com/help/recruiter/answer/a8052001), you will need to configure [Recruiter System Connect.](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/115005678103-LinkedIn-Recruiter-System-Connect-RSC-integration) Once RSC+ has been enabled through Recruiter System Connect, and data has successfully synced, recruiters can begin using LinkedIn Recruiter and Greenhouse together in a more seamless way. See [here ](https://www.linkedin.com/help/recruiter/answer/a8052001)for more details about how RSC+ works. 

For non-Hiring Assistant customers, it unlocks value through [ATS-enabled Reporting](https://www.linkedin.com/help/recruiter/answer/a500012), which shows how activity on LinkedIn results in hiring outcomes in the ATS. 

For Hiring Assistant customers, it unlocks value through [Connected Projects,](https://www.linkedin.com/help/recruiter/answer/a8074536) allowing Hiring Assistant to evaluate applicants from the ATS alongside those sourced from LinkedIn (including resume data for Hiring Assistant). These capabilities help maintain consistent, accurate data across systems and give recruiters a more complete view of candidates without extra manual steps. 

#### Using Connected Projects 

**Important:** Must have RSC+ enabled and an active Hiring Assistant license

  1. Navigate to the ‘Projects’ tab > Select ‘Connect ATS job requisitions’



  2. For each Job requisition that has been synced by your ATS, map to the correct Recruiter project. Recruiter projects will be suggested automatically if there is a strong match.



  3. Click ‘Connect project’ 



  4. Review project details and where, applicable, determine if you would like to Enable Hiring Assistant on this project. Note: Hiring Assistant must be enabled on your Connected Project to evaluate applicants with AI, and additional steps are required after clicking “Connect” to kick off applicant evaluation.



  5. Click ‘Create Project’.



  6. Review your Hiring Assistant qualifications. These qualifications will be automatically generated using information from your connected job requisition, and you can edit them on the screen below.  

  7. Ask Hiring Assistant to start applicant evaluation by selecting “Start sourcing and applicant evaluation” or typing “start applicant evaluation” into the chat box  

  8. View your applicants within the “Applicants” tab of your hiring project. Once Hiring Assistant evaluation has been started, evaluations will automatically appear. Note that if you have a large volume of applicants, it will take time (up to a few hours for >1000 applicants) for them all to sync into your connected project and be evaluated by Hiring Assistant. You can refresh the experience to see the latest results.  

  9. Once applicants are evaluated, you can view their Hiring Assistant evaluation on their profile.



#### Filter using Hiring Assistant Evaluations

**Filtering from the “Candidates” tab**

  1. Under the “Candidates” tab, click the “Profile Details” field and select “Custom Field.”



  2. Select “LinkedIn Hiring Assistant Evaluation.”



  3. Filter for “Top Fit”, “Might be a fit” and “Might not be a fit” applicants based on Hiring Assistant evaluation results.



**Filtering from the “Jobs” tab**

  1. Select Job where Hiring Assistant has been enabled



  2. Under “Pipeline”, click “Review Applications”



  3. In the top right corner, select “Filter talent”



  4. In the “filters” section, select “Add custom field”



  5. Select “LinkedIn Hiring Assistant Evaluation”



  6. In the search bar, select evaluation value



#### View Hiring Assistant Evaluations in RSC Profile Widget

Hiring Assistant evaluations will automatically show in a matched candidate’s RSC Profile Widget to users with a Hiring Assistant license:

Users can click to view the full evaluation summary

### Additional resources

For additional information not covered here, reach out to [ltsatsintegrations@linkedin.com](mailto:ltsatsintegrations@linkedin.com).

# Wedge integration

**Permissions: Job Admin** and above

**Product tier:** Available for new subscription tiers (Core, Plus, and Pro)

You can meet more candidates in less time with Wedge. Wedge makes screening candidates a breeze by allowing candidates to record interviews and recruiters to review them on their own time. Wedge gives you the power to customize your interviews and invite as many candidates as you'd like, making scheduling headaches a thing of the past.

Greenhouse Recruiting's integration with Wedge allows you to seamlessly add Wedge one-way interviews to a job's interview plan.

### In this article:

  * Enable the Greenhouse Recruiting / Wedge integration
  * Add Wedge stage to an interview plan
  * Set up the assessment on the Wedge stage
  * Send and review a Wedge

  * Additional resources



### Enable the Greenhouse Recruiting / Wedge integration

To enable the integration, follow the instructions below to get your Wedge API Key:

  1. Login to your Wedge account.
  2. Click **Settings** on the top navigation bar.
  3. Click the **Integrations** tab.
  4. Click **Connect Integration**.
  5. Copy your API token/key to a secure location.



Once you have your API token/key copied, [click here](https://support.greenhouse.io/direct) to open a ticket with Greenhouse Technical Support. 

**Note** : Do not send your API key in the initial ticket. Greenhouse Technical Support will respond with a [SendSafely](https://www.sendsafely.com/about/) link for you to securely share the API key.

Greenhouse Technical Support will respond in the ticket with a SendSafely link for you to securely share the API key. Greenhouse Technical Support may ask you to verify your identity using a [verification code](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360022771952).

Once Greenhouse Technical Support has received your API key and enabled the integration, they will send a confirmation email to you.

### Add Wedge stage to an interview plan

Once the Greenhouse Recruiting / Wedge integration is enabled for your organization, you'll be able to add the Wedge assessment as an interview stage.

To add a stage to an existing job, navigate to the job (**All Jobs** >**Job Name**), and click the **Job Setup** tab.

Select **Interview Plan** on the left, then click **Add Stage**.

Select the Wedge stage on the next window. When you're finished, click **Add** to apply the stage to the job's interview plan.

### Set up the assessment on the Wedge stage

After the Wedge stage has been added to your job's interview plan, you'll need to add the assessment to the stage.

To add the assessment, click **Edit Take Home Test** on the Wedge stage.

Choose the assessments from the dropdown menu. The available options are based on the assessments you configured in Wedge. Assign at least one Greenhouse Recruiting user to review submitted assessments.

When you're finished, click **Save**.

**Note** : All configuration for the assessment (including the email template) will need to be done in Wedge. [Click here for instructions on setting up jobs in Wedge](https://help.wedgehr.com/en/collections/3026760-organizations#jobs).

### Send and review a Wedge

When candidates are moved into the Wedge interview stage, Greenhouse will display a **Send Test** link.

**Note** : When you send a Wedge from inside Greenhouse Recruiting, the interview instructions will be sent by Wedge.

After it has been sent, an assessment's status will display in Greenhouse Recruiting.

Once the candidate has submitted their interview, you'll receive an email notification for the completed Wedge.

Additionally, the interview kit in Greenhouse Recruiting will contain a link to view the submitted Wedge interview on the Wedge application.

Click **View Report** to see the candidate's results in Wedge.

You will be taken to the Wedge platform to review the submitted interview.

### Additional resources

  * Check out the [Wedge Help Center](https://help.wedgehr.com/en/)!
  * Wedge offers 24/7 in-app chat via their chat widget.
  * If candidates have any issues submitting their interview, they also have access to 24/7 in-app chat from Wedge.



For additional information not covered here, reach out to Wedge Support at [support@wedgehr.com](mailto:support@wedgehr.com).

# How do I turn off email notifications for user permission changes?

User permissions can be updated from two locations:

  * The _User Permissions_ page for an individual user
  * A job's _Hiring Team_ page



If you update a user's permissions from the _User Permissions_ page and don't want a notification email sent to the user, uncheck the **Notify user of new permissions via email** box at the bottom of the page before saving.

# Juro integration

Juro is a contract management software that allows your organization to quickly and easily manage electronic signatures on contracts.

Greenhouse Recruiting's integration with Juro ensures a seamless process for data transfer between the two platforms.

#### In this article

  * Configure user setup permissions in Greenhouse Recruiting
  * Create Harvest API key for the Greenhouse Recruiting / Juro integration
  * Create webhook in Greenhouse Recruiting
  * Map Greenhouse Recruiting fields to Juro templates
  * Use the Greenhouse Recruiting / Juro integration



### Configure user setup permissions in Greenhouse Recruiting

In order to enable the Greenhouse Recruiting / Juro integration, you will need the following developer permissions:

  * Can manage ALL organization’s API Credentials
  * Can manage and configure web hooks



Contact a Greenhouse Recruiting user in your organization with **Site Admin** level permissions with the additional user-specific permission **Can edit another user's advanced permissions** to apply the developer permissions to your account.

Have the user with Site Admin level permissions edit your user account's permissions by navigating to the **Configure** icon  > **Users** > **Your Name**.

The user with Site Admin level permissions should navigate to the _User-Specific Permissions_ panel on your user page and expand the _Developer Permissions_ dropdown.

Select **Can manage ALL organization’s API Credentials** and **Can manage and configure web hooks** so a check is in each checkbox. When finished, click **Save**.

Repeat as necessary for any other user that should have access to set up the integration.

### Create Harvest API key for the Greenhouse Recruiting / Juro integration

To create a Harvest API key for the integration, click the **Configure** icon  then select **Dev Center** on the left.

From the _Dev Center_ page, click **API Credential Management**.

From the _API Credential Management_ page, click **Create New API Key** to generate the API key for Juro.

In the _Create New Credential_ box, make the following selections:

  * **API Type** : Harvest
  * **Partner** : Juro
  * **Description** : Juro Harvest API Key



When finished, click **Manage Permissions** to generate the Harvest API key and automatically assign it the appropriate permissions required by Juro.

In the subsequent box, click **Copy** to save your API key to your clipboard. Store the API key in a secure location to provide to Juro in the next step. Click **I have stored the API Key** once you have copied and saved the key.

**Note:** You cannot access the full API key again after clicking **I have stored the API Key**. If you lose your API key and need to access it later, you must create a new API key, provide it to Juro, and then revoke access to the original key.

On the next page, confirm the following permissions are assigned to your new API key:

**Applications**

  * GET: Retrieve Application
  * POST: Add Attachment to Application



**Candidates**

  * GET: Retrieve Candidate



**Custom Field Options**

  * GET: Custom field options



**Custom Fields**

  * GET: Get custom fields



**Jobs**

**Users**

  * GET: List Users



If any of the permissions above are not checked, place a check in the box next to the appropriate permission. Click **Save** when finished.

Your Harvest API key for the Greenhouse Recruiting / Juro integration is created and configured.

Open a new browser tab and navigate to your Juro account. From your Juro account, click **Settings** > **Integrations**. Navigate to **Greenhouse** and click **Connect**.

### Create webhook in Greenhouse Recruiting

**N****ote:** Before creating your webhook in Greenhouse Recruiting, you must paste the API key generated in the previous step into Juro, and define a secret key. Juro will then give you a webhook URL which you can use, along with your defined secret key, to create a webhook in Greenhouse Recruiting.

With Juro’s endpoint URL and secret key copied, you are ready to finish enabling the Greenhouse Recruiting / Juro integration.

To create a webhook for the integration, click the **Configure** icon  on your navigation bar and then click **Dev Center** on the left. From the _Dev Center_ page, click **Web Hooks**.

Click **Web Hooks** on the next page.

On the _Create A New Web Hook_ page, provide the following details:

  * **Error recipient email** : Provide a contact email address for error notifications
  * **Disabled?** : No



When finished, click **Create Web hook**.

That's it! Your Greenhouse account and Juro account can now talk to each other. These settings dictate how the Juro webhook works once you transition a candidate into the appropriate application stage for a given job.

### Map Greenhouse Recruiting fields to Juro templates

As part of the Greenhouse Recruiting / Juro integration, you'll want to map Greenhouse Recruiting offer fields to Juro templates.

From the _New Offer Field_ page, enter the following details:

# Assign or edit focus attributes on a scorecard

**Permissions:** Site Admin, and Job Admin who can create new jobs and request job approvals

**Product tier:** Available for new subscription tiers (Core, Plus, and Pro)

It would be very difficult to evaluate every attribute on a scorecard for every interview conducted. Instead of covering all attributes in every interview, Greenhouse Recruiting suggests that your interviewers focus on different key attributes that when considered holistically provide a complete portrait of the candidate.

**Note:** For more information on scorecard best practices, [click here](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360003500291-Best-Practices-Creating-a-Scorecard). 

Greenhouse Recruiting's Focus Attributes feature allows your organization to select and emphasize which attributes interviewers should focus on during their respective interviews. See the following sections for more information:

#### In this article

  * Assign focus attributes for a new job
  * Assign or edit focus attributes for an existing job
  * Assign or edit focus attributes for interviews



### Assign focus attributes for a new job

**Note** : Assigning focus attributes during the new job creation process requires that your organization has **Interview Plan** enabled as a step in the [job setup flow](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/204923599-Configure-Job-Setup-Flow).

To start, click the **Add** icon  at the top of the page and click **Create a Job**.

Fill out the information on the _Job Info_ tab, then click **Create Job & Continue**.

Continue through the job setup steps until you reach the _Interview Plan_ tab.

**Note:** Depending on whether you are working from a sample template, blank template, or a [custom job template](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360006876232-Best-Practices-Template-Job), the _Interview Plan_ tab page or may not have pre-populated stages in your interview pipeline.

Click the **Edit** icon  next to the stage you want to add a focus attribute to.

On the next page, find the _Focus Attributes_ section. Attributes populated here are synced from the [scorecard stage of the job setup](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/115002194863).

Select attributes that you want the interviewer to focus on during this particular interview. When you finish, click **Save** at the bottom of the page.

**Tip:** You can also [link focus attributes to specific interview questions](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/115002276366).

Repeat as needed for any additional scorecards. 

Interviewers assigned to this interview kit will see the selected focus attributes in the _Attributes_ section top of their scorecard. You can view the rest of the scorecard attributes for the interview kit by clicking**Show additional attributes**. 

### Assign or edit focus attributes for existing jobs

**Note** : Users with Job Admin level permissions do not need the user-specific permission**Can create new jobs and request job approvals** to edit focus attributes on existing jobs.

Clicks on the **Jobs** tab at the top of the page. On the _All Jobs_ page, click on the job you want to edit.

Go to the _Interview Plan_ page. _(**Job Dashboard** > **Job Setup** > **Interview Plan**)_

Click the **Edit** icon  next to the stage you want to edit focus attributes for.

On the next page, find the _Focus Attributes_ section. Attributes populated here are synced from the [scorecard stage of the job setup](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/115002194863).

Select attributes that you want the interviewer to focus on during this particular interview. When you finish, click **Save** at the bottom of the page.

### Assign or edit focus attributes for interviews

To easily assign, edit and view focus attributes for interviews and stages, go to the job's _Scorecard_ page. _(**Job Dashboard** > **Job Setup** > **Scorecard**)_

Scroll to the bottom of the page and find the _Focus attributes per interview_ section.

__

The numbers in the first row of each column show how many focus attributes are selected for that interview stage. The numbers in the first column of each row show how many stages contain the specific focus attribute.

If you have many interviews, you can view the focus attributes in a larger window by clicking **Expand** in the top right corner of the section.

Click the checkbox next to an attribute to assign or remove it from an interview stage. When you finish, click **Save**.

**Note:** If a focus attribute is associated with a custom question, it can't be updated in the _Focus attributes per interview_ section until you unlink it from the custom question.

# Affintus integration

Improve the quality of every hire and virtually eliminate hiring mistakes using the Affintus pre-hire assessment. Learn about each job seeker's strengths in 19 different work dimensions as well as how each candidate's strengths compare to the unique success requirements of your job.

Greenhouse Recruiting’s integration with Affintus allows hiring teams to send assessments to candidates, receive and review individual results, and view all candidates ranked by fit per job.

#### In this article

  * Create a Harvest API key for the Affintus integration
    * Credentials
    * Permissions
  * Enable the Greenhouse Recruiting / Affintus integration
  * Add Affintus stage to a job's interview plan
    * Initial setup of Affintus
    * Add assessment state to Greenhouse Recruiting jobs
    * Configure the Affintus stage
  * Use the Affintus integration
    * Send and review an Affintus test
    * Review and interpret results
    * See all candidates within a job RANKED by the quality of fit
  * Additional support



### Create a Harvest API key for the Affintus integration

To configure the Greenhouse Recruiting / Affintus integration, you'll need to create a Harvest API key.

Follow the steps in [this article](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/5888163769883) to create the key, and verify that the credentials and permissions below are selected when configuring the Affintus integration.

#### Credentials

In the _Create New Credential_ box, make the following selections:

  * **API Type:** Harvest
  * **Partner:** Affintus
  * **Description:** _Affintus Harvest API Key_



#### Permissions

Verify that the following permissions are selected for the Affintus integration:

  * **Applications**
    * Select all
  * **Candidates**
    * Select all
  * **Custom Fields**
    * Select all
  * **Custom Field Options**
    * Select all



Your Harvest API key for the Greenhouse Recruiting / Affintus integration is created and configured. Provide the Harvest API key to your Affintus onboarding team so they can enable the integration.

### **Enable the Greenhouse Recruiting / Affintus integration**

To start, contact your Affintus representative to request your API key. Once you have received your API key, _[click here](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/requests/new)_ to open a ticket with the Greenhouse Technical Support team.

**Note:** Do not send the API key in this initial email.

The Greenhouse Technical Support team will respond with a [SendSafely link](https://www.sendsafely.com/howitworks/) for you to enter your API key. A notification will be sent to the Greenhouse Technical Support team after you have entered your API key and they will email you to confirm that your API key has been set up in your account and your integration is enabled.

**Note:** To verify your identity, the Greenhouse Technical Support team might request you provide a [Support Verification Code](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360022771952) before adding the API key to your organization's account.

### Add Affintus stage to a job's interview plan

#### Initial setup of Affintus

The first time you use Affintus to evaluate a job, you will need to send a job description (as an attachment or link) to [support@affintus.com](mailto:support@affintus.com). Each _Test Name_ aligns with a specific job type, but can be used across multiple positions with the same responsibilities (for example, a Sales Representative position in multiple cities).

Affintus will then populate the _Test Name_ dropdown list for you to select the appropriate assessment. Your system should update within a few hours and Affintus will notify you once you are able to continue job setup.

#### Add assessment state to Greenhouse Recruiting jobs

Once the Greenhouse Recruiting / Affintus integration is enabled for your organization, you can add the Affintus assessment as an Interview stage.

[When you're adding a new stage to an interview plan](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/115002194903), the Affintus stage will display in the list. Select this stage and add it to the interview plan.

#### Configure the Affintus stage

Once the stage has been added to the job's interview plan, click **Edit** and select the correct **Test Name** from the list.

**Note:** The options in this list are based on your setup in Affintus.

__

Select the appropriate assessment and assign at least one Greenhouse Recruiting user to review submitted Affintus assessment responses. When you're finished, click **Save**.

Click and drag the Affintus stage immediately after **Application Review**.

Complete job setup as normal.

### Use the Affintus integration

Affintus integration with Greenhouse Recruiting was designed for ease of use. Affintus Customer Service will handle all initial setup so you can manage everything within Greenhouse Recruiting — no additional system to learn or password to remember.

#### Send and review an Affintus test

When a candidate enters the Affintus Stage, you can invite them to complete Affintus by clicking **Send Test**.

If not already populated, select the appropriate test from the dropdown menu and designate the grader. Click **Send Test**.

Once the candidate has completed the assessment, the grader is notified and the results show up in the Workflow.

**Note:** Candidates only need to complete the assessment once and the questionnaire is the same for all positions. The matching formula is different for each job so the match results may vary. If you send the assessment to a candidate who has already completed it, the results will automatically be returned to the new record without any interaction with the candidate.

#### Review and interpret results

Affintus is designed to be easy to understand. Decide to proceed with the candidate by looking at their overall match.

Applicants align with the job at three separate levels:

Icon | Result | Recommendation  
---|---|---  
Green (circle) | Strong Match | Affintus recommends moving to interview  
Yellow (triangle) | Moderate Match | Proceed with caution if no Green candidates  
Grey (square) | Weak Match | Affintus does not recommend hiring  
  
The Overall Match can be found at the top of the report:

Dig deeper into a candidate’s alignment with each of the 19 Dimensions throughout the report.

The final section of the report includes Behavioral Interview Questions unique to each candidate based on their results. These questions are designed to get deeper insight into areas where the candidate did not fall into the desired range of that dimension.

#### See all candidates within a job RANKED by the quality of fit

Access all candidates for a job via the “Review All Candidate Matches” button on the top right of every candidate’s Job Match report.

Candidates will show up in order of best fit. Each candidate’s Job Match Report can be accessed by clicking on their name.

### Additional support

For personal assistance, schedule a time with Affintus here:  
<https://app.hubspot.com/meetings/ryanaffintus/affintus-support>

Contact [support@affintus.com](mailto:support@affintus.com) for troubleshooting assistance regarding the integration.

# ZipRecruiter integration

**Permissions:** Site Admin

**Product tier:** Available for new subscription tiers (Core, Plus, and Pro)

ZipRecruiter connects employers and candidates with its wide-reaching network of over 100 partner job sites. ZipRecruiter's integration with Greenhouse Recruiting allows your organization to easily harness the power of this network to attract high-quality candidates to your open jobs.

**Note** : Beginning April 24, 2023, ZipRecruiter will add pay range estimates to job posts that don't have pay ranges on them. To avoid automatic pay range estimates on third-party job boards, use Greenhouse Recruiting [pay transparency](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/13304010418075) to add pay ranges to your job posts.

#### In this article

  * ZipRecruiter Premium and organic job posts
  * Enable the ZipRecruiter integration
  * Enable the ZipRecruiter integration on additional job boards
  * Data shared with ZipRecruiter
  * Additional resources



### ZipRecruiter Premium and organic job posts

The ZipRecruiter integration is available for all organizations. If your organization doesn't have a ZipRecruiter Premium subscription, the integration creates free organic ZipRecruiter job posts on your behalf.

Organizations with a ZipRecruiter Premium subscription benefit from the following features:

  * Unlimited number of US-based jobs promoted continuously on ZipRecruiter and over 100 partner job sites
  * Job posts populate in social feeds and search results
  * ZipRecruiter's Smart Matching technology proactively suggests your jobs to qualified candidates via email



If your organization doesn't have a ZipRecruiter Premium subscription currently, reach out to ZipRecruiter by [email](mailto:greenhouse.concierge@ziprecruiter.com) or by phone at 1-855-624-1136 to see if you're eligible for a special discount.

### Enable the ZipRecruiter integration

To set up the ZipRecruiter integration, you first need to enable it on one of your [job boards](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360031374411).

Click the **Configure** icon on your navigation bar, then select **Job Board & Posts **on the left.

Click the **Ellipsis** icon next to your job board, then select **Edit Board Settings** from the dropdown.

Click **Set** **up** in the _Allow candidates to apply directly from ZipRecruiter_ section.

To use the integration, you need to agree to the ZipRecruiter policies. This ensures that your job information can be shared on ZipRecruiter. The policy window provides a brief overview of the data shared with ZipRecruiter. For more information, refer to Data shared with ZipRecruiter below.

Select the checkbox to agree to the policy and click **Set up** when you're finished.

**Note** : The next window requests optional information and is only necessary if you want to learn more about ZipRecruiter Premium.

If you don't want to learn more about ZipRecruiter Premium, you can skip entering contact details, and click the **X** icon at the top-right to dismiss the box.

**Note:** Organizations that enable Greenhouse Recruiting's integration with ZipRecruiter for the first time and do not have an existing ZipRecruiter Premium membership may be eligible for a special promotion through ZipRecruiter. To learn if you are eligible, provide your contact information or contact ZipRecruiter directly by [email](mailto:greenhouse.concierge@ziprecruiter.com) or by phone at 1-855-624-1136.

When finished, click **Save** at the bottom of the page.

The ZipRecruiter integration is now enabled for your organization on the job board.

### Enable the ZipRecruiter integration on additional job boards

After you've enabled the integration on one job board using the above steps, you can enable it on other job boards using a simpler set of steps.

Navigate to a job board and [edit it](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360031374411) via the **Configure** icon on your navigation bar, then select **Job Board & Posts **on the left. Click the **Ellipsis **icon next to your job board, then select **Edit Board Settings** from the dropdown.

Scroll to the _Allow candidates to apply directly from ZipRecruiter_ section and click **Yes**.

Click **Save** at the bottom of the page.

The ZipRecruiter integration is now enabled for your job board.

### Data shared with ZipRecruiter

In order to enable Greenhouse Recruiting's integration with ZipRecruiter, we must collect and share certain data about your organization with ZipRecruiter.

Data shared with ZipRecruiter | Purpose  
---|---  
Contact data |  The following information will be requested from the user who enables the integration for your Greenhouse Recruiting account and shared with ZipRecruiter:

  * Name
  * Email
  * Phone number

Sharing this information is optional. If provided, ZipRecruiter might reach out via these contact details to discuss paid ZipRecruiter features.  
Job post information | Greenhouse Recruiting will automatically share job post information with ZipRecruiter for every job board where the ZipRecruiter integration is enabled. This information will be used by ZipRecruiter to populate job posts on their site and over 100 partner job sites.  
Job board API keys |  Greenhouse Recruiting will automatically share a Job Board API Key for every job board where the ZipRecruiter integration is enabled. This data allows candidates to apply directly from ZipRecruiter and its partner job sites. **Note** : Candidates who apply through the ZipRecruiter integration (either directly from ZipRecruiter or its partner job sites) are assigned ZipRecruiter as a [source](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/115003931231-Sourcing-The-Basics-).  
Candidate stage and application status |  For every candidate that enters your Greenhouse Recruiting account through the ZipRecruiter integration (either directly from ZipRecruiter or its partner job sites), we will share the stage and application status of these candidates with ZipRecruiter. We share this information to utilize ZipRecruiter's Smart Matching technology. As ZipRecruiter collects information about how far their candidates are progressing through your job's interview plan they can subsequently reach out to other candidates who may be a good match.  
  
### Additional resources

For questions about ZipRecruiter, including eligibility for a ZipRecruiter Premium discount, contact ZipRecruiter by [email](mailto:greenhouse.concierge@ziprecruiter.com) or by phone at 1-855-624-1136.

# Paylocity integration

Paylocity offers intuitive, easy-to-use HR and payroll software that helps automate and streamline processes, attract and retain talent, and build culture and connections with employees. Paylocity accompanies its clients on the journey to create great workplaces to help employees achieve their best.

Paylocity's integration with Greenhouse Recruiting seamlessly imports newly hired candidates from Greenhouse Recruiting into Paylocity.

#### In this article

  * Set up the integration
    * Before you start
    * Create a webhook
  * Use the integration
    * Integration field mapping
  * Additional resources



### Set up the integration

#### Before you start

Before setting up the Paylocity integration, you must first purchase the Greenhouse integration in Paylocity's Marketplace. Once an integration agreement is in place with Paylocity and a partner integration resource is assigned, Paylocity will provide the details to create the webhook. 

You can [reach out to your Paylocity account manager](mailto:service@paylocity.com) to clarify any contract requirements.

**Note** : For this webhook to be created, first confirm that your organization's Paylocity contract includes an integration agreement. Paylocity's partner resources will provide you with the information needed to create a webhook in Greenhouse Recruiting.

To integrate Paylocity with Greenhouse Recruiting, create a webhook. Follow the steps in [this article](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/5888163727003) to create your webhook. Use the values listed below to configure the webhook:

  * **Secret Key** : Your Paylocity company ID. This will be provided by Paylocity.
  * **Advanced Settings** : The username and password will be provided by Paylocity on a per-customer basis.



### Use the integration with Greenhouse Recruiting

Once enabled, the Greenhouse Recruiting webhook will send new employee information to Paylocity's Onboarding module where the employee can be added to an onboarding event.

# Auto-advance

**Permissions:** Site Admin, and Job Admin who can create, edit and delete job posts

**Product tier:** Available for Plus and Pro subscription tiers

With auto-advance, your organization can set up application rules so that, based on an applicant's answer to a question, they will be automatically advanced to a specified stage in your Interview Plan.

### In this article:

  * Create custom job post question
  * Create auto-advance application rule
  * Additional resources



### Create custom job post question

Before creating an auto-advance application rule, your organization needs to create a custom job post question with a response that will auto-advance the applicant. The directions that follow detail how to add a custom question to an existing job post.

**Note:** Auto-advance application rules can only be configured for the following custom job post question types: 

  * Yes/No
  * Single Select
  * Multi Select



Click**Jobs** from the navigation bar and select a job from the subsequent list.

From the _Job Dashboard_ , click **Job Setup** and then select **Job Posts** on the left.

From the _Job Posts_ page, click the **Edit** icon  beside the name of the job post. Navigate to the subsequent page to the _Custom Application Questions_ section. **Click Add Custom Question**.

Input your question in the appropriate field and choose either **Yes/No** , **Single Select** , or **Multi Select** from the _Answer type_ field. Fill in response choices in the _Options_ field if appropriate. When you have finished, click **Add**.

When you have returned to the _Edit Your Job Post_ page, scroll to the bottom and click **Preview**. Review your job post from the _Preview_ screen and click **Save**. Your custom job post question is now saved.

### Create auto-advance application rule

With the custom job post question created, you can now assign an auto-advance application rule to a response. From the _Job Posts_ page, click **# rules** or **Manage Rules** under the _Application Rules_ column.

From the _Rules_ page, you can edit, delete, and add new rules. To edit an existing rule, click the **Edit** icon . To remove an existing rule, click the **Delete** icon . To create a new application rule, click **Add a Rule**.

**Note:** The workflow to add an application rule includes [Nudges](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360004923452#h_4df465a2-8199-48ee-bd08-a56e6421b0a3) that help remind users to configure automated processes thoughtfully. We encourage your team to configure application rules based on need-to-have qualifications that are directly relevant to the role. This ensures candidates from non-traditional professional backgrounds receive fair consideration, and avoids job post questions about personality characteristics, individual interests, or personal background. By focusing your questions this way, your roles are more likely to attract a diverse and uniquely qualified pool of candidates.

From the _Add a Rule_ dialog box, select your job post question and the candidate response that should trigger the application rule.

**Note:** OR Conditions allow you to select more than one candidate response for a given auto-advance rule. For example, in the image below, candidates who have either 3-5 years or 5-8 years experience will be automatically advanced to the Hiring Manager Review stage. Application rules also support AND Conditions, which allow you to base an application rule on the candidate's responses to multiple custom job post questions.  
  
To learn more about using AND/OR conditions in application rules, [click here](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/203105595#h_01ECK29NWK2JRM6Y82N69ZSEAB).

Check the box next to **Auto-Advance** , then use the _Advance to:_ dropdown to select which stage candidates should be moved to if their response triggers the application rule.

**Note:** When configuring an auto-advance application rule, all stages in the job's Interview Plan are selectable except for the first stage (typically this is **Application Review** , but can be renamed by your internal team). Candidates who apply to the job are added to the first stage automatically, so an auto-advance rule that moves candidates to this first stage would be nonfunctional.

You can also auto-tag candidates at the same time an auto-advance rule is applied by checking the box next to **Tag** and following the prompts to assign a candidate tag. [Click here](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360000060551) to learn more about auto-tag.

Click **Save** when finished.

Candidates who respond to the question with any of the defined answers will now be auto-advanced to the appropriate stage, and any relevant candidate notifications, stage change notifications, or web hooks your team has configured will be triggered.

**Note:** If a candidate auto-advances to a stage that has an email-based [stage transition rule](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360048178672) configured, the email is sent by the user who created the auto-advance rule. The Activity Feed entry logging the action also is attributed to the user who created the auto-advance rule. For more information, click [here](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/11976912882075).

### Additional resources

To learn more about application rules, please review the articles linked below:

  * [Application rules overview](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/203105595)
  * [Auto-tag](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360000060551)
  * [Auto-reject](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360000653472)

# HackerRank Interview integration

HackerRank Interview is an integration between Greenhouse Recruiting and HackerRank that gives you access to live paired code exercises.

To use HackerRank's other assessments, your organization will also need to set up the [HackerRank Assessment](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/201178044) integration.

#### In this article

  * Set up HackerRank interview
    * Generate a HackerRank API key
    * Finish setup in Greenhouse Recruiting
    * Harvest API key
      * Configure API key in Greenhouse
      * Find your user ID
      * Enter information into HackerRank
  * Send a live coding link



### Set up HackerRank interview

Each user who plans to use HackerRank Interview must set up the integration for their account. However, these different connections can all use the same API key.

**Note:** You need a HackerRank Recruiter user account to send tests. HackerRank Developer accounts can't be used with the HackerRank integration.

#### Generate a HackerRank API key

A HackerRank account administrator can generate a global API key and share it with other recruiters at your organization. This API key will need to have the Recruiter and Company Admin permissions in HackerRank get to full access to your assessments.

Admins can generate the key under the integration settings ([Log in ](https://www.hackerrank.com/access-account/)> **Settings** > **Integrations**)

Find Greenhouse Recruiting and click **Configure**.

Click **Generate an API token** to save the key to your clipboard.

**Note** : After generating the HackerRank global API key, securely store this key. Every new user will need to enter the global API key into their individual Greenhouse Recruiting user accounts.

#### Finish setup in Greenhouse Recruiting

Log in to your Greenhouse Recruiting account and click **Integrations** on your navigation bar.

Find HackerRank in the integrations search bar. Click **Connect**.

Paste your HackerRank API key, and click **Save**.

### Harvest API key

If you already set up the Harvest API as part of the [HackerRank Assessment](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/201178044) integration, you can skip these steps.

HackerRank also uses the Harvest API to send information to Greenhouse. You'll need to [create a Harvest API key](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/5888163769883), [retrieve your user ID](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/10765948752027), and add both items to the **Greenhouse Integration Settings** page in HackerRank.

#### Configure API key in Greenhouse

To create your Harvest API key, follow the steps in [this article](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/5888163769883). Use the following permissions and credentials when setting up the integration.

**Credentials**

In the _Create New Credential_ box, make the following selections:

  * **API Type:** Harvest
  * **Partner:** HackerRank
  * **Description:** HackerRank Harvest API Key



**Permissions**

Make sure the following permissions are selected when configuring your API key.

  * **Candidates**
    * Post: Add Candidates
    * Post: Add Attachment
    * Post: Add Note
  * **Tags**
    * Get: List tags applied to candidate
    * Get: List Candidate Tags
    * Post: Add New Candidate Tags
    * Put: Add a candidate tag
  * **Users**
    * Get: Retrieve User
    * Get: List Users
  * **Custom Fields**
    * Get: Get custom fields
    * Post: Create custom field
    * Patch: Update custom field



#### Find your user ID

To retrieve your user ID, follow the steps in [this article](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/10765948752027).

#### Enter information into HackerRank

Once you have your Harvest API key and user ID, you can enter them in the **Greenhouse Integration Settings** page in HackerRank.

### Send a live coding link

When you schedule an interview and have the HackerRank Interview integration, a link will be available anytime you add a new stage. You can copy and paste this link into the interview description so it will be automatically sent to your hiring team.

This link will not be automatically sent to the candidate. To make sure the candidate has access to the link before their CodePair session, either send this link to the candidate manually or include it in their [take-home test email](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/200734889).

When it's time for the live exercise, the interviewer and candidate can both log into the HackerRank platform and conduct the exercise. The interviewer can then complete their assessment using the Greenhouse Recruiting [scorecard](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/4414777492891).

Once a session is finished, your team can use the same link to access a recording of the session.

# Submit referrals

**Permissions: Basic** , **Job Admin** , or **Site Admin**

**Product tier:** Available for new subscription tiers (Core, Plus, and Pro)

Referrals from your organization's existing employees can be a powerful source for strong candidates.

#### In this article

  * Submit a referral
  * View submitted referrals
  * Questions about submitted referrals



### Submit a referral

If your organization has enabled referrals, most users can submit a referral by scrolling to the _Add a Referral_ section of their dashboard.

However, if you're a job admin or a Site Admin, you can submit a referral directly from the navigation bar.

It is not possible to refer a prospect, so choose a job for your referral. If you think they might be good for several different jobs, simply choose one and write a note to the Recruiter outlining the other jobs as well. The Recruiter can then assess your referral's information and make sure they end up in the best job or jobs.

**Note:** A user can make a referral to any job with a live external job post, as well as to any job where they have been assigned permissions. This means a Basic user can submit referrals only to jobs which have a live external job post, while a Job Admin user can submit a referral to any of their assigned jobs (as well as to any job with a live external job post). Because Site Admins users have access to all jobs, a Site Admin can submit a referral to any job in your Greenhouse Recruiting account.

When selecting a job, the job name will be the primary job post name on the job under **Job** **Setup** > **Job** **Posts**.

**Note** : If you would prefer that users submit referrals by internal job name, rather than external primary job post name, you'll need to reach out to a Site Admin to edit your Permission Policies. Have the Site Admin select **Configure** (gear icon), then choose **Permission** **Policies** from the left. Find and check the permission policy **When adding a referral, surface the internal job name instead of the primary job post name**.

When submitting a referral, be sure to complete the fields under the _Details_ section to provide background about your relationship with the referral.

When finished, click **Add this referral** at the bottom of the page.

If you have checked **Follow referral** under the _Name & Company _section, you will receive notifications when/if your referral is moved to a different stage or has their status changed

### View submitted referrals

You can check the status of your referrals by viewing the _My Referrals_ panel on your Dashboard.

### Questions about submitted referrals

Every organization has unique internal processes for referrals, so your organization's internal HR/recruiting team is best equipped to answer questions about your submitted referrals. For additional information, visit [Referrals FAQ](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/12320251521435).

### Additional resources

  * [Generate my referrer link](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/200721674)

# Betts Connect integration

The Betts Connect platform is a talent marketplace for Sales, Marketing, and Customer Success roles. Accelerate your growth by attracting top talent from this carefully curated list of candidates that are looking for their next career move.

Greenhouse Recruiting’s integration with Betts Connect allows you to find and pitch candidates in the Connect marketplace and seamlessly push interested candidates to Greenhouse Recruiting to follow your standard interview and hiring process. As a candidate moves through the job workflow in Greenhouse Recruiting, updates are automatically reflected back to Betts Connect.

### Create a Harvest API key for Betts Connect integration

### Set up Betts Connect webhook

  * **Secret Key:** Paste the Secret Key copied from Betts Connect



#### Webhook 5: Candidate or Prospect unrejected

  * **Name:** We suggest _Betts Connect: Candidate or Prospect unrejected  
_
  * **When:** Be sure to select the right webhook so that the webhook fires at the appropriate event in Greenhouse [Candidate or Prospect unrejected]
  * **Endpoint URL:** Paste the Endpoint URL copied from Betts Connect
  * **Secret Key:** Paste the Secret Key copied from Betts Connect



#### Webhook 6: Offer created

  * **Name:** We suggest _Betts Connect: Offer created_

  * **Endpoint URL:** Paste the Endpoint URL copied from Betts Connect
  * **Secret Key:** Paste the Secret Key copied from Betts Connect



#### Webhook 7: Offer updated

### Use the Greenhouse Recruiting / Betts Connect Integration

# Custom options FAQ

**Permissions:** Site Admin and Job Admin who can manage custom fields

**Product tier:** Available for new subscription tiers (Core, Plus, and Pro)

[Custom options](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/10978274576667) allow your organization to capture custom data related to your jobs, offers, applications, and candidates in Greenhouse Recruiting.

We've collected answers to a few commonly asked questions about custom options.

#### In this article

  * Can I edit custom fields?
  * What happens when I delete a custom field or custom metadata?
  * What is a custom options sync?



#### Can I edit custom fields?

Yes, you can edit your custom fields after you've created them. Learn more about editing custom fields below.

**Note:** You can't edit a custom field's Field Type. To change the Field Type after you've created a custom field, you'll need to delete the custom field and create a new one with the correct Field Type.

#### What happens when I archive a custom field or custom metadata?

When you archive a **custom field** , that field will no longer appear for new applications, jobs, candidates, openings, or offers. The field and associated data will no longer appear in reports.

If an existing entity has data associated with a deleted custom field, that data will remain after the field is deleted. You'll need to manually delete this data at the application, job, candidate, opening, or offer level to completely remove it.

**Note:** Archived fields can be restored on the Custom Options page.

When you archive **custom metadata** , the metadata is permanently removed from all candidates, jobs, reports, and other associated entities.

Use the below resources to learn more about deleting custom fields and metadata.

#### What is a custom options sync?

Organizations that have enabled an HRIS integration with Greenhouse Recruiting can set up a [custom options sync](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360002158492). This is a per-field integration that helps you sync the list of options available for a custom field in Greenhouse Recruiting with the list of available options for a corresponding field in your HRIS.

**Learn more**

[Custom options overview](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/10978274576667)

# Structured hiring: Interview kit creation

In order to confidently assess a candidate on required attributes, your hiring team needs to create insightful interview questions for the interview kit. In this article, we will cover the purpose and question types in an interview kit, how to create interview kits in Greenhouse, and provide some additional resources to help you get started. 

### Purpose and Question Types

An interview kit allows your interviewers to remain consistent across candidate interviews and provides a consistent framework for assessing candidates. By having this consistency, your hiring team will have better data for making hiring decisions at the end of the process. Likewise, the interview kit alleviates the stress imposed on interviewers to ask questions on the spot. Since the interview kit provides the questions that need to be asked, interviewers can focus on evaluating the responses instead of coming up with the next question. 

Different attributes are also tested best by different types of questions. We've taken the opportunity to divide these questions into 4 types that you might consider incorporating into your interview kit.

### Create Interview Kits in Greenhouse Recruiting

Additionally, you can learn more about using Interview Kits to evaluate candidates [here](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/115002226826-VIDEO-Using-Interview-Kits).

Check out the side of this article for a downloadable worksheet to help your team craft insightful questions for the Interview Kit.

# Approved to start recruiting notification

**Permissions:** Site Admin who can see private notes, salary info, manage offers, request approval, and approve jobs / offers, and Job Admin who can view and edit private job fields and approve / request approval on jobs

**Product tier:** Available for new subscription tiers (Core, Plus, and Pro)

Configuring a notification list for a completed job approval allows your organization to automate internal communication to select team members when a job is approved for candidate recruitment.

#### In this article

  * Add users to the notification list for completed job approval
  * Remove users from the notification list for completed job approval
  * Notification list for completed two-stage job approvals



### Add users to the notification list for completed job approval

To add users to the notification list for completed job approval, click**Jobs** on your navigation bar and select a job from the list.

Click**Job Setup** and navigate to **Notifications** on the left.

Scroll to the _Approval Notifications_ section and click **Configure** beside _Approved to Start Recruiting_.

**Note** : The text of the email notification indicating a job has been approved cannot be edited.

By default, the user who initially requested the job approval is the only user who automatically receives a notification when the job is approved to start candidate recruitment.

Click the _Participants_ dropdown and select the appropriate person. You can select a person by name, or you can select the [hiring managers](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360016572311) listed on the job's hiring team.

**Note** : Only users who have appropriate permissions on the job populate in the dropdown.

Repeat as necessary for other users who should be notified when the job is approved to start recruiting. When finished, click **Save**.

### Remove users from the notification list for completed job approval

To remove users from the notification list for when a job is approved for candidate recruitment, navigate to the name of a user listed in the _Participants_ dropdown and click **X** to the right of their name.

Repeat as necessary for other users and click **Save** when finished.

### Notification list for completed two-stage job approvals

For organizations using a[ two-stage approval process](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360025756071-One-Stage-vs-Two-Stage-Job-Approvals) for a job, the following users are notified when the first stage of the process is complete:

  * Users added to the approved to start recruiting notification list
  * User who initially requested the first-stage job approval
  * Users configured as approvers for the second-stage



When the second stage of the approval process is complete, the user who initially requested the approval is automatically notified. It is not possible to have additional users notified when the second stage of approvals is completed.

# Scorecard visibility options

**Permissions:** —

**Product tier:** Available for new subscription tiers (Core, Plus, and Pro)

Adjusting the visibility settings for your scorecards allows you to decide under what circumstances an interviewer can access another interviewer's submitted scorecard.

You have three options: **Never** , **Always** , and **Only after submitting their own**.

This setting can be configured at the organizational level (**Configure** > **Permission Policies** > _Interviewers)_ and at the Job Admin level (**Configure** > **Permission Policies > **_Job Admins_ > **See and manage Job Admin levels**).

### Scorecard visibility options

#### Never

Interviewers will never be able to see scorecards submitted by other interviewers. Only the interviewer's own scorecard will show up in the _Scorecards_ section of the candidate profile.

This gives individual interviewers the most privacy by limiting the number of people who can view their submitted scorecards.

#### Always

Interviewers will always be able to scorecards submitted by other interviewers. [All submitted scorecards](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/115005415966) will show up in the _Scorecards_ section of the candidate profile.

#### Only after submitting their own

Interviewers will only be able to see scorecards submitted by other interviewers after they've submitted their own scorecard.

This option prevents interviewers from being influenced by others' scorecards before they've finished their own, which can introduce bias.

**Example:** Imagine that Deidre has finished her interview but hasn't completed her scorecard yet. Deidre has access to other interviewers' scorecards. She looks at Carl's submitted scorecard and sees that he gave the candidate poor feedback.  
  
Deidre had a positive impression of the candidate after her interview, but now she's having second thoughts. When she fills out her scorecard, she changes her overall recommendation from "Yes" to "No Decision."

In this example, Deidre was biased by Carl's scorecard, which caused her to give the candidate poorer feedback on her own scorecard despite her positive interview experience.

# Qualifi integration

Qualifi allows our customers to pre-record interview questions and invite candidates to take their phone interview on their own schedule. Qualifi will invite candidates to complete their interview via SMS and/or email when a candidate moves to the Qualifi stage in the interview process.

Greenhouse Recruiting's integration with Qualifi allows you to seamlessly add Qualifi’s assessment to a job's interview plan.

#### In this article

  * Enable the Greenhouse Recruiting/Qualifi integration
  * Add the Qualifi stage to an interview plan
  * Set up the assessment in the Qualifi stage
  * Send and review a test
  * Additional support



### Enable the Greenhouse Recruiting/Qualifi integration

To begin the integration, contact your Qualifi representative ([service@qualifi.hr](mailto:service@qualifi.hr)) to request an API key for your integration. Once you have received your API key, [click here](https://support.greenhouse.io/direct) to open a ticket with Greenhouse Technical Support.

**Note** : Do not send your API key in unencrypted communication (such as email and support tickets). If they are needed for setup, Greenhouse Technical Support will provide a secure way to send your API keys.

Wait for a confirmation email from Greenhouse Technical Support. You may be required to verify your account before you can proceed.

If they need your API key, the Greenhouse Technical Support team will provide a [SendSafely link](https://www.sendsafely.com/howitworks/) where you can enter your API key. Once Greenhouse Technical Support has been notified that you’ve entered your API key, they will send a confirmation email.

### Add the Qualifi stage to an interview plan

Once the Greenhouse Recruiting/Qualifi integration is enabled for your organization, you will be able to add the Qualifi assessment as an Interview stage.

To add a stage to an existing job, navigate to a job (**All Jobs >Job Name**) and click **Job Setup** tab.

Select **Interview Plan** on the left side of the page and click **\+ Add a Stage**.

Select the Qualifi stage on the next window. When you’re finished, click **Add** to apply the stage to the job's interview plan.

### Set up the assessment in the Qualifi stage

After the stage has been added to the job's interview plan, you’ll need to add the assessment to the stage. To add the assessment, click **Edit Take Home Test**.

Choose the assessments from the dropdown menu. These options are based on the jobs you configured in Qualifi.

Assign at least one Greenhouse Recruiting user to grade/review submitted assessments. When you’re finished, click **Save**.

**Note** : All configuration for the assessment (including the email template) will need to be done in Qualifi.

### Send and review a test

When candidates are moved into the Qualifi interview stage, Greenhouse will display a **Send Test** link.

**Note** : When you send a partner assessment from inside Greenhouse Recruiting, the interview instructions will still be sent by Qualifi.

After it has been sent, an assessment’s status will display in Greenhouse Recruiting.

Once the candidate has submitted their test, the Interview Kit will contain a link to view the submitted test in the Qualifi application.

Click **View Report** to see the candidate’s results in Qualifi.

### Additional support

Please contact [service@qualifi.hr](mailto:service@qualifi.hr) for additional support regarding this integration.

# Sync offices and departments from an external system

**Permissions:** Site Admin

**Product tier:** Available for new subscription tiers (Core, Plus, and Pro)

It's possible to add new offices and departments using Greenhouse Recruiting's [Harvest API](developers.greenhouse.io/harvest.html). However, offices and departments are organization-level fields that can be tied to permissions, approval chains, jobs, custom fields, template jobs, and more. Due to these dependencies, there are some limitations on how offices and departments can be updated through Harvest API.

For more information on these dependencies, check out: [Office and department-dependent workflows](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360029591631).

#### In this article

  * Sync offices and departments from an external system
  * Limitations



### Sync offices and departments from an external system

You can add new offices and departments as a parent or child office or department with the following API endpoints:

  * [POST: Add department](https://developers.greenhouse.io/harvest.html#post-add-department)
  * [POST: Add office](https://developers.greenhouse.io/harvest.html#post-add-office)



**Note** : If you're importing these values from an HCM or other third-party system, we recommend including an [External ID](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360027394072-office-and-department-External-ID) value.

If you're adding a child office or department, you'll need to specify the Greenhouse Recruiting parent office or department ID in the "parent_id" field. You can use the `external_id` querystring parameter on [GET: List offices](https://developers.greenhouse.io/harvest.html#get-list-offices) and [GET: List departments](https://developers.greenhouse.io/harvest.html#get-list-departments) to retrieve the Greenhouse Recruiting office or department ID that's required for your POST requests.

**Example** :
    
    
    curl -X POST \  
     https://harvest.greenhouse.io/v1/departments \  
     -H 'Authorization: Basic ***********************' \  
     -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \  
     -H 'On-Behalf-Of: 642569' \  
     -d '{  
     "name": "NewChilddepartment",  
     "parent_id": 45819,  
     "external_id": "ABC123"  
    }'  
     

Update existing office names, locations, or external IDs, and existing department names or external IDs via the following endpoints:

  * [PATCH: Edit office](https://developers.greenhouse.io/harvest.html#patch-edit-office)
  * [PATCH: Edit department](https://developers.greenhouse.io/harvest.html#patch-edit-department)



You'll need to use the Greenhouse Recruiting office or department ID in the HTTP request in order to specify the appropriate office / department to update. 

**Example** : The following call would update the office with the Greenhouse Recruiting ID 63683.
    
    
    curl -X PATCH \  
     https://harvest.greenhouse.io/v1/offices/63683 \  
     -H 'Authorization: Basic ***********************' \  
     -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \  
     -H 'on-behalf-of: 642569' \  
     -d '{  
     "name": "Updated office Name",  
     "location": "New York, NY",  
     "external_id": "ABC123456"  
    }'

### Limitations

The following actions are not possible using Harvest API:

  * **Removing offices or departments** – We do not recommend this in general for the purpose of preserving historical job data.
  * **Updating office or department hierarchy** – For example, you can't make a subordinate office a parent office by using Harvest API.
