# Application review stage

**Permissions:** Job Admin or above

**Product tier:** Available for new subscription tiers (Core, Plus, and Pro)

Application review is a unique stage that is automatically added as the first stage in every job's [interview plan](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/115002194903). The Application Review stage provides a streamlined process for a job's [Recruiter](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360016347712) to screen every new applicant for a given job, then advance or reject each application. 

#### In this article

Start reviewing applications

Application review features 

Additional resources

### Start reviewing applications

When you have applications ready for review, a link will appear on your dashboard in the  _Applications to Review_ section. You can start by reviewing candidates who are referrals, internal applicants, agency submissions, or Dream Job applicants by clicking **Review priority**.

This link will only appear if you're a recruiter on the hiring team and the job has candidates in the application review stage, or if you're the Hiring Manager and candidates are in the Hiring Manager Review stage. 

Additionally, you can review on a specific job's dashboard by selecting the _Pipeline_ tab and selecting **Review Applications** beneath _Application Review_ on the right side of the page.

Finally, you can review a specific subset of candidates on the _Candidates_ tab using Bulk Actions. [Click here](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/115003558531) for more information.

### Application review features 

In this section, we'll cover the information and actions available within the Application Review workflow.

See the following sections for more information:

  * Candidate name
  * Advance or reject a candidate
  * Leave feedback for a candidate
  * View candidate details
  * View or download a candidate's documents
  * Custom application questions
  * [Fraud report](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/42738009117467)
  * Application history 
  * View candidate roundup
  * Keyboard shortcuts



**Note:** Depending on your [user permissions](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360020855632) and the information available for the candidate, you might not see every section listed below. For example, if the candidate wasn't submitted by an agency recruiter, you won't see the **Agency questions** panel. 

#### 

#### Candidate name

The top of the page shows the candidate's name and any applied [candidate tags](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360027904392), and provides the ability to add and remove tags. This section indicates if the candidate is a _referral_ , an _internal candidate_ , or marked as a potential _Duplicate_. If the candidate is a referral, hover over the  _Referral_ label to view the related referral questions and responses.

When a candidate has the _Duplicate_ tag, it means Greenhouse has found another profile that matches on at least one of your duplicate tagging criteria (name, email, phone number, or LinkedIn URL). The exact checks depend on how a Site Admin [configured duplicate tagging](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/49207850415003-Configure-the-Duplicate-tag). 

Where available, you can click the **Duplicate** tag to review and merge duplicate profiles.

#### Advance or reject a candidate

When you review a candidate's application, you can Advance or Reject them based on how you'd like to move them in the pipeline. _Advance_  _or_ _Reject_ a candidate (user permissions permitting).

  * Clicking **Advance** moves the candidate to the next stage in the interview plan. If your organization has configured any [Stage Transition rules](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360053129752), they could be triggered by this action.
  * Clicking **Reject** launches the rejection workflow, prompting you to select a [rejection reason](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/207305363), provide responses to your organization's custom [rejection questions](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360025028252), and send or schedule a [rejection email](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360025603151) to the candidate. 



You won't be able to Advance or Reject candidates if don't have the proper user permissions.

To move to the next candidate without advancing or rejecting the current candidate, click the **greater than** icon  at the top right. 

[Click here](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360025225732) to learn more about rejecting a candidate.

#### Leave feedback

You can quickly record scorecard feedback for a candidate using the **Leave Feedback** button. All scorecard feedback is recorded in the  _Feedback_ section of the candidate's profile.

You can send a notification to another member of the hiring team by using [@mentioning](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360013153651) in this field.

**Note:** Your scorecards are visible to all recruiters, hiring managers, and other users with permission to view the candidate or role. Notes recorded here are considered public notes.

If another member of the hiring team had previously left scorecard feedback on the candidate, it will also display during the application review.

#### Candidate details

The  _Candidate Details_ panel provides in-depth information about the candidate and their application:

  * Applied date
  * Job post applied through
  * [Source](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/115003931231)
  * Credited to
  * URLs for personal websites, portfolios, and social media accounts
  * Any tags for the candidate



For additional candidate actions, click the **Ellipsis** icon . You'll be able to see specific actions based on your user permissions:

  * Merge the candidate record with another record in your organization
  * [Transfer candidate](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360031249311) to a different job
  * Send an email to a candidate to directly from application review
  * Reject as [spam](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/205094045): Mark the application as spam and automatically reject future applications associated with this candidate's email address



#### View or download a candidate's documents

If the candidate included documents with their application, or if a member of your team added [attachments to the candidate's profile](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/202815509), they appear here. This can include a resume, a cover letter, and/or other documents, with each document labeled to match the file type selected on the candidate's profile. View the documents directly in app, or click the download icon next to the file name to store and view locally. 

#### Custom application questions

If the candidate responded to custom application questions through a job post or [job post request email](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360002568971), the questions and responses appear here. 

#### Fraud report

The fraud report section displays key details from the candidate’s fraud report. If a report hasn’t been run yet, users with permission can generate one directly from this section to review potential risk signals before moving the candidate forward.

You must be a Site Admin or be assigned the Job Admin permission to view fraud reports to see this information.

#### Application history 

The  _Application History_ section provides an overview of other jobs the candidate has applied to. This includes jobs the candidate applied to historically and those the candidate might be active on currently. If your permissions allow, you can view scorecards submitted for the candidate on those jobs as well.

You must either be a Site Admin or be assigned Job Admin permissions on the candidate's other jobs to see their application history. 

#### Agency questions

If the candidate was submitted by an agency recruiter, [custom agency questions](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360040318592) and responses are surfaced in this section. If the candidate was not submitted by an agency recruiter, this panel does not appear. 

#### View candidate roundup

When you're finished reviewing candidates, click **I'm done, view candidate roundup** at the bottom-right of the page for an overview of candidates advanced, rejected, or not-actioned during your review session.

Click the link on the  _Advanced for role_ tile to view a filtered list of candidates advanced during your review session.

You can click the **X** icon in the top-right corner to return to the  _Job Dashboard_ page. 

#### Keyboard shortcuts

You can use the following keyboard shortcuts to quickly move through applications in your queue without touching the mouse. 

You can open this menu by pressing the question mark (?) key on your keyboard.

### Additional resources

To learn more about reviewing candidate applications, see the following articles: 

  * [Hiring manager review stage](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/4402694472347)
  * [Bulk application review](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/115003558531)

# Configure the new job setup flow

**Permissions:** Site Admin

**Product tier:** Available for new subscription tiers (Core, Plus, and Pro)

When people create new jobs at your organization, they'll be presented with a standardized job setup flow in Greenhouse Recruiting. You can customize the steps of the job setup flow to best suit your organization's needs.

#### In this article

  * Configure the new job setup flow



### Configure the new job setup flow

To configure the new job setup flow for your organization, click the **Configure** icon __on your navigation bar, then click**Custom Options** on the left.

Click **Configure Job Setup Flow**.

Next, check the box beside the steps you want to include in the job setup flow. The steps you select will appear to all users who create new jobs.

**Note:** The Job Info step is required.

**Note** : The [Forms](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360019478952) step is only available to Advanced and Pro subscription customers.

Check out the chart below for more information on each of the available steps:

**Job info** | Use this step to set the job's department, office, and more. The job info step includes basic information about the job, like its internal name (or the way it appears to your employees), requisition ID and opening IDs, along with any custom [job](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/202609855) or [opening](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360036370951) fields you have configured.  
---|---  
**Hiring team** | Use this step to determine who will be a part of the job's [hiring team](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/115002194983). You can assign both roles (like hiring manager, recruiter) and permissions (like Job Admin) to the job.  
**Job insights** |  Use this step to gain valuable insights into how your job might perform based on how similar jobs performed in the past. You can see at-a-glance information to set expectations for operations, finance, and recruiting teams. You'll see job insights that include:

  * Total applicants
  * Top sources
  * Pipeline history
  * Offers created

Read more here: [Job insights overview](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/10280036917275)  
**Job kickoff** | Use this step to construct the job kickoff form to be sent to the hiring manager. Job kickoff is an essential step of structured hiring that empowers recruiters and hiring managers to collaborate and align on key objectives. Use the form to brainstorm sourcing strategies, scorecard attributes, and more.  
**Scorecard** | Each job should have a standard set of criteria that each candidate is compared against. Use this step to setup the scorecard that will be used to evaluate candidates on the job. [Click here](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360003500291) to learn more about configuring a well-rounded scorecard.  
**Interview plan** | Use this step to create a consistent interview process for candidates to go through: set stages, expected interviews, and interview kits to prepare interviewers to collect useful feedback. Learn more about creating useful interview plans [here](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/115002194903).  
**Approvals** | Use this step to assign approvers that should be required to sign off on a job opening or offers being created. Read more here: [Configure job approvals](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360062257351) and [Offer approval overview](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360035625832).  
**Job post** | Use this step to determine how your job post will look. Also known as an application page, this is the candidate-facing part of the job setup flow. Here you'll determine the best way to market the job's responsibilities, perks, and benefits.  
**Forms** | Use this step to configure any [forms](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360019478952) that will be used on the job. Forms are candidate-facing requests for information. Common use cases include NDAs and post-application questions.  
**Email notifications** | Use this step to configure email notifications for users to be informed of progress on the job. Read more here: [Available email notifications](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/201368340).  
**Sourcing plan** | Use this step to assign sourcing tasks, such as the agencies, third-party job boards, or other sourcing strategies you'll tackle. Read more here: [Best practices: Sourcing strategies](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360004175751).  
  
When finished, click **Save**.

Any new jobs will now include the setup steps you selected!

# Business Intelligence Connector data model

**Permissions:** —

**Product tier:** Available for Plus and Pro subscription tiers

Business Intelligence Connector delivers a nightly ETL of your organization's Greenhouse Recruiting or Greenhouse Onboarding data. The data model relies on three main keys, on which other tables and columns are mapped.

#### In this article

  * Overview
    * Candidate-level data
    * Application-level data
    * Job-level data
    * Process and applicant tracking data
    * Other tables



### Overview

There are three main keys in Business Intelligence Connector data:

**Candidates** | A candidate is a person who can submit any number of applications for any number of jobs, meaning they can apply to one job many times, or to many jobs at different times. A candidate is represented in the model by `candidate_id`.  
---|---  
**Applications** | Only one application can be submitted for a single job. This information is summarized in the `application_jobs` table. A single candidate might have multiple applications. Additionally, there is a boolean dimension named `prospect` on the `applications` table which indicates whether an application is an actual application on a job, or is a prospect application. An application is represented in the model by `application_id`.  
**Jobs** | A job is a role with one or more openings. A job is represented in the model by `job_id`.  
  
#### Candidate-level data

Candidates in the [`candidates`](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360001892012#Candidate) table can be associated with the following candidate-level tables using `candidate_id` as a key:

#### One-to-many relationships

  * `candidate_custom_fields`
  * `candidate_email_addresses`
  * `candidate_mailing_addresses`
  * `candidate_phone_numbers`
  * `candidate_tags`
  * `educations`
  * `employments`
  * `referral_question_custom_fields`



#### Application-level data

Applications in the [`applications`](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360001892012#Application) table can be associated with the following application-level tables using `application_id` as a key:

#### One-to-one relationships

  * `eeoc_responses`



#### One-to-many relationships

  * `application_custom_fields`
  * `application_question_answers`
  * `rejection_question_custom_fields`



#### Job-level data

Jobs in the [`jobs`](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360001892012#Job) table can be associated with the following job-level tables using `job_id` as a key:

#### One-to-many relationships

  * `hiring_team`
  * `job_custom_fields`
  * `job_posts`
  * `job_snapshots`
  * `jobs_attributes`
  * `jobs_departments`
  * `jobs_interviews`
  * `jobs_offices`
  * `jobs_stages`
  * `openings`
  * `stage_snapshots`



#### Process and applicant tracking data

As applications move through the hiring pipeline, [process and applicant tracking data](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360001892012#Process) is generated for each application ID.

**Process** | **Representation**  
---|---  
Stages | The `application_stages` table represents each stage on a job that an application has or could be in, along with the enter and exit times for each stage. `Null` is represented on stages that applications have not yet entered.  
Interviews | The `scheduled_interviews` table represents each interview that is scheduled in Greenhouse Recruiting. The `interviewers` and `interviewer_tags` tables represent the Greenhouse users assigned to the interview. The `scorecards`, `scorecard_question_answers`, and `scorecards_attributes` tables represent each scorecard that each interviewer submits.  
Offers | The `offers` and `offer_custom_fields` tables represent the details of any offer that is generated for an application.  
  
#### Other tables

There are a few other tables that are not keyed to candidates, applications, or jobs:

#### User-level tables

  * [`users`](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360001892012#Usage)
  * [`user_actions`](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360001892012#Usage)
  * [`greenhouse_usages`](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360001892012#Usage)



#### Standalone tables

  * [`organizations`](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360001892012#h_01H91NC639J911BNWGD6R77FPF)
  * [`candidate_surveys`](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360001892012#h_01H91NC639J911BNWGD6R77FPF)



Every other data table is a simple mapping table that maps an ID to the name of the item represented. For example, the `attributes` table maps an attribute ID to the name of the attribute.

**Tip** : For more detailed information on all the tables, check out [Guide to Business Intelligence Connector tables](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360001892012).

**Learn more**

[Business Intelligence Connector schema](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/12373826600603)

[Guide to Business Intelligence Connector](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360001892012)

# Custom integrations overview

While Greenhouse offers [over 400 official partner integrations](http://greenhouse.io/integrations), a custom integration is an integration that seeks to do something our standing integrations can't accomplish while still making use of Greenhouse's available APIs.

Custom integrations leverage our APIs to use or transform data in your organization's Greenhouse instance, resulting in candidate and job updates, custom take home tests, background checks, HRIS parity between platforms, and other powerful capabilities.

#### In this article

  * Create a custom integration



### Create a custom integration

You can leverage one or a combination of [Greenhouse APIs](https://developers.greenhouse.io) to post, update, and extract data in Greenhouse Recruiting or Greenhouse Onboarding, while Greenhouse [web hooks](https://developers.greenhouse.io/webhooks.html) can be used to integrate a third-party system based on real-time triggers or events such as candidate hires.

Combining API endpoints and web hooks can result in a powerful integration that responds to and syncs data in real-time.

**Tip** : Check out [Greenhouse API overview](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/10568627186203) for more information on our APIs.

When integrating your Greenhouse Recruiting instance with a third-party system, you'll need to cover a few basics.

  * **You'll need a middleware platform** such as Mulesoft, Boomi, or Workato to transpose data from the third-party into a format that can be understood by Greenhouse APIs.
  * **You'll need a developer** to build and maintain the adapter layer through the middleware platform.
  * **You'll need a mapping schema** to define how fields from the third-party application map to Greenhouse Recruiting.



With these necessities in hand, you can begin to build out your integration! There are a few ways to create a custom integration, from Greenhouse-inspired to Greenhouse-designed.

#### Fully custom-built integration

A fully custom-built integration is an integration that is designed, built, and maintained by your internal team. Common fully custom-built integrations include HRIS integrations and other system-parity integrations.

#### Third-party integration

With third-party integrations, the integration is built and maintained by a third-party integrator. Sometimes third-party integrators will offer design assistance with the integration, but this would be up to the statement of work that your team agrees on with the third-party integrator. Common third-party integrations include background check and assessment integrations, candidate offer integrations, and more.

#### Greenhouse Professional Services + a system integrator

If you want the best-in-class design for your custom integration, you can leverage Greenhouse's Professional Services to help design your custom integration. Greenhouse Professional Services ensure that best practices for Greenhouse Recruiting and your organization's hiring maturity are considered. The build of the integration would be completed either by an internal team member at your organization or by a third-party system integrator. Common Greenhouse Professional Services integrations include HRIS integrations.

Interested in learning more about Greenhouse Professional Services? Reach out to your Greenhouse Account Manager!

# BarRaiser Assessment integration

BarRaiser Assessment uses a smart interviewing platform, data-driven analytics, and support from hundreds of experts from leading companies around the world to make the interviewing process smarter and more effective.

Its proprietary AI generates a normalized BarRaiser Global Score (BGS TM) – an industry-acclaimed benchmark of candidates' true potential based on 200+ data points throughout the interview.

The integration will allow human resource professionals who use Greenhouse's platform to seamlessly interview on the BarRaiser Assessment platform.

#### In this article

  * Set up the BarRaiser Assessment integration
    * Generate a BarRaiser Assessment API key
    * Provide your key to Greenhouse Recruiting and finish setup
  * Use the BarRaiser Assessment integration with Greenhouse Recruiting
    * Add the BarRaiser Assessment stage to the job's interview plan
    * Configure the BarRaiser Assessment interview stage
    * Send and review the test
  * Additional resources



### Set up the BarRaiser Assessment integration

#### Generate a BarRaiser Assessment API key

To enable the BarRaiser Assessment integration, [navigate to BarRaiser](https://app.barraiser.com/login) and **Log In**.

In the left-hand panel, click **Integrations** > **Generate API key**.

Once the API key is generated, copy the key.

#### Provide your key to Greenhouse Recruiting and finish setup

Follow the steps in [this article](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/5888163696923) to provide your BarRaiser Assessment API key to Greenhouse Recruiting and set up the assessment stage in your interview plans.

Once you've set up your interview plans and configured your take-home test, you'll be able to send the test to candidates.

### Use the BarRaiser Assessment integration with Greenhouse Recruiting

#### Add the BarRaiser Assessment stage to the job's interview plan

Once the BarRaiser Assessment integration is enabled for your organization, you will be able to [add the BarRaiser Assessment assessment as an interview stage](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/21338859258267).

To do this for an existing job, navigate to a job (**Jobs** > **Job** > **Job Dashboard**) and then, click **Job Setup**. On _Job Setup_ , select **Interview Plan** on the left-hand panel. Then, click **+Add stage**.

From the _Add Stage_ dialog box, select the BarRaiser Assessment stage.

When finished, click **Add** to apply the stage to the job's interview plan.

#### Configure the BarRaiser Assessment interview stage

Once the stage has been added to the job's interview plan, click **Edit Interview**.

On the _Edit BarRaiser Assessment Interview Kit_ page, use the provided dropdown menu to choose from the assessments you have previously set up in BarRaiser Assessment.

Select the appropriate assessment and assign at least one Greenhouse Recruiting user to grade/review submitted assessments.

Once all the edits are done scroll down on the page and click **Save**.

**Note:** Keep in mind that all configuration of the assessment itself, as well as the email template, will be completed by your BarRaiser Assessment Account Manager.

#### Send and review the test

When candidates are moved into the BarRaiser Assessment interview stage, Greenhouse Recruiting will display a _Send Test_ link on their candidate profile.

**Note:** When you send a test from Greenhouse Recruiting, the interview instructions actually are sent by BarRaiser Assessment.

The status of the assessment will be viewable in Greenhouse Recruiting.

Once the candidate has submitted their test, their greenhouse activity feed will contain a link to view the submitted test on BarRaiser Assessment's platform. Click on the BarRaiser Assessment Button enclosed in the golden border.

Click on the link to see the candidate’s results in the BarRaiser Assessment score report.

### Additional resources

For additional information not covered here, reach out to [support@barraiser.com](mailto:support@barraiser.com) or log onto your [BarRaiser partner portal](https://app.barraiser.com/partner) for further assistance.

# Dropbox Sign integration

**Note:** The Dropbox Sign for Greenhouse integration requires a **paid subscription**. Shake IT can provide packaged subscriptions including Signatures and the integration. Before you follow the installation steps, please contact [sales@shakeit.ai](mailto:sales@shakeit.ai) for subscription options and a quote.

Dropbox Sign for Greenhouse is an integration provided by Shake It. Dropbox Sign for Greenhouse Recruiting simplifies your offer process by allowing users to generate and send out offer letters to candidates in just a few clicks.

The Dropbox Sign integration with Greenhouse Recruiting simplifies the candidate signature process.

#### In this article

  * Enable the Dropbox Sign integration
  * Create an ISU
  * Create a Harvest API key
  * Create a webhook
  * Create custom offer fields
  * Create an offer document with text tags
  * Use the Dropbox Sign integration with Greenhouse Recruiting
  * Additional resources



### Enable the Dropbox Sign integration

#### Create a Dropbox Sign API key and client app

**Note:** This step is only required if using your own Dropbox Sign account. If using the shared or dedicated subscription provisioned by Shake IT, Shake IT will provide the client id and secret.

The integration to Dropbox Sign can be configured in a variety of ways, depending on your subscription plan type:

  * Track signatures at the individual user level within a team 

  * Track signatures at the team level using a single user account 

  * Track signatures at the company level using an API key 




Reach out to Shake IT if you are unsure of what you need or to understand more about your account.

#### Track Signatures at the individual User level with a team (Recommended)

If you wish to track signature requests at an individual user (within a team) or are using a user-based Dropbox Sign subscription, perform the following steps:

  1. Login to Dropbox Sign with an admin or developer account that has access to that team
  2. Browse to API settings
  3. Click the "Create app" button under the "API apps" section
  4. Use the following settings: 
     * Choose a unique name: "Dropbox Sign for Greenhouse"
     * example.com: "shakeit.ai"
     * Event callback: <https://greenhouse.shakeit.ai/api/signed>
     * Optionally update branding
     * Check: Enable OAuth for this app
     * OAuth Callback URL: [https://greenhouse.shakeit.ai](https://greenhouse.shakeit.ai/)
  5. Click the "Create Application" button



**Note:** Copy the Client ID and OAuth Secret and store them somewhere safe. You will need these values later.

#### Track Signatures at the Company Level[​](https://greenhouse.shakeit.ai/docs/setup-guide/configure-dropbox-sign#track-signatures-at-the-company-level)

If using a Dropbox Sign API plan, signatures can be tracked at a company level or an individual user level. If you wish to track signature requests at a company level, perform the following steps:

  1. Login to Dropbox Sign with the account that will be used to track the signature requests
  2. Browse to API settings
  3. Click the "Create app" button under the "API apps" section
  4. Use the following settings: 
     * Choose a unique name: "Dropbox Sign for Greenhouse"
     * example.com: "shakeit.ai"
     * Event callback: <https://greenhouse.shakeit.ai/api/signed>
     * Optionally update branding
  5. Click the "Create Application" button



**Note:** Copy the Client ID and store it somewhere safe. You will need this value later.

Next, an API Key must be generated. If a valid API Key already exists, copy this value. If not, perform the following:

  1. Browse to API settings
  2. Click the "Generate key" button under the "API key" section
  3. Give the key a name, such as Greenhouse



**Note:** Copy the API key value and store it somewhere safe. You will need this value later.

### Create an ISU

An integration system user (ISU) is required in order to use the integration. Follow the steps in [this article](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/4405511253659-Create-an-ISU-for-an-integration) to create an ISU and assign Site Admin permission with 'Can see private notes, salary info, and manage offers.'

### Create a Harvest API key

To configure the Dropbox Sign integration, you’ll need to create a Harvest API key.

Follow the steps in [this article](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/5888163769883) to create the key, and verify that the permissions below are selected when configuring the Dropbox Sign integration.

#### Credentials

In the _Create New Credential_ box, make the following selections:

  * **API Type:** Harvest
  * **Partner:** Dropbox Sign
  * **Description:** Dropbox Sign Harvest API Key



#### Permissions

Verify that the following permissions are selected for the Dropbox Sign integration:

  * **Applications**
    * **POST:** Add Attachment to Application
  * **Approvals**
    * **GET:** List Approval Flows For Job
  * **Candidates**
    * **GET:** Retrieve Candidate
    * **POST:** Add Note
  * **Custom Fields**
    * **POST:** Create Custom Field
    * **GET:** Get Custom Fields
  * **Offers**
    * **GET:** Retrieve Offer
    * **PATCH:** Update Application’s Current Offer
  * **Custom Fields Options**
    * **GET:** Custom Field Options
    * **POST:** Create Custom Field Options
  * **Users**
    * **GET:** Retrieve User



### Create a webhook

Next, you’ll need to create a webhook. Follow the steps in [this article](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/5888163727003) to create your webhook. Use the values listed below to configure the webhook:

  * **Name:** Dropbox Sign for Greenhouse Offer Updated
  * **When:** Offer Updated
  * **Endpoint URL:** https://greenhouse.shakeit.ai/api/created/embedded
  * **Secret Key:** Generate a random 12-digit secret key



Note: Copy the secret key and store it somewhere safe. You will need this value later.

### Create custom offer fields

In order for the Dropbox Sign integration to work, you'll need to create custom offer fields in Greenhouse Recruiting. Follow the steps in [this article](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360024551831-Add-a-custom-offer-field) to create the custom offer fields listed below.

**Required Fields**

**Name** | **Field Type** | Options | Notes  
---|---|---|---  
Send to Dropbox Sign | Single select | 

  * \--
  * Send
  * Re-send
  * Cancel and re-send
  * Pull Dropbox Sign templates
  * Authenticate Dropbox Sign

### Create an offer document with text tags

### Use the Dropbox Sign integration with Greenhouse Recruiting

#### Offer Conditions

The Dropbox Sign for Greenhouse functionality is tied to the Offer Update action. To send an offer for signature, the following conditions must first be met:

  * The Candidate is in the Offer Stage
  * The Offer has been approved (if using an approval workflow)
  * Either an Offer Document has been generated or a Dropbox Sign Template has been selected



#### Authenticate User[​](https://greenhouse.shakeit.ai/docs/user-guide/#authenticate-user)

If using an API Key, there is no need for authentication. Continue to the next step.

If using the individual or single user based integration, the user must authenticate before sending a request. Depending on your configuration, this is either a one-time process for one user or a one-time process for each individual user.

  1. Select a Candidate and move to the Offer Stage if needed
  2. Select "Update" under the "Offer Details" section



  3. Select the "Authenticate Dropbox Sign" option under the "Send to Dropbox Sign" field



****

  4. Press the "Save" button
  5. Wait 5 seconds and refresh the browser window
  6. An authentication link has been added to the Dropbox Sign Url field on the Offer



  7. Visit this URL and authenticate to Dropbox Sign.  


**Note:** Each user must have an account in Dropbox Sign to login. Please be sure each user has received an invite to join your subscription and has created their account.

  8. Accept the prompt to finish linking the Dropbox Sign account to Greenhouse



  9. A success message is displayed. Close the browser tab and refresh the Offer to start using the integration.



#### Send for Signature[​](https://greenhouse.shakeit.ai/docs/user-guide/#send-for-signature)

Before sending for signature, ensure the Offer meets the conditions listed in the Offer Conditions section above.

Once ready, follow the steps below:

  1. Browse to the candidate and update the existing Offer
  2. Update the Send to Dropbox Sign field to "Send" and press Save
  3. Wait 5 seconds and refresh the browser window
  4. A Dropbox Sign link has been added to the Dropbox Sign Url field on the Offer
  5. Click on the link. This open the Dropbox Sign Embedded Requesting tool, which contains a 3-step wizard.
  6. On the first step, ensure the appropriate signers are selected. You may add any additional signers needed. Click Next.  
  




  7. On the second step, ensure the signature locations are in the correct location. You can also add additional documents for review if needed. Click Next.



  8. On the final step, add any desired CC recipients, a Document Title, and an optional message that will send with the document. Click Send for Signature.



  9. The requested signers will receive email notifications to complete the process



#### Cancel and Resend Signature Request[​](https://greenhouse.shakeit.ai/docs/user-guide/#cancel-and-re-send-signature-request)

A signature request can be cancelled after the request email has been sent and before all parties have signed.

To cancel and resend a request:

  1. View the Offer
  2. Regenerate the documents as needed
  3. Update the Offer
  4. Update the Send to Dropbox Sign field to "Cancel and re-send" and press Save
  5. Wait 5 seconds and refresh the browser window
  6. At this point the previous request has been cancelled and a new Dropbox Sign link has been added to the Dropbox Sign Url field on the Offer
  7. If you do not wish to send a new request, you can Update the offer and clear this URL
  8. If you do want to send a new request, click on the link and progress through the wizard using the same process as above



**Review Signed Offer Letter**[**​**](https://greenhouse.shakeit.ai/docs/user-guide/#review-signed-offer-letter)

Once all parties have signed, the executed offer document will appear under Offer Documents for download and viewing:

### Additional resources

For additional information not covered here, see <https://greenhouse.shakeit.ai/docs/> or reach out to [dbsc.support@shakeit.ai.](mailto:dbsc.support@shakeit.ai)

Pricing is based on the number of signature requests processed via the integration, so please provide an anticipated number of signature requests per annum initiated from Greenhouse Recruiting. Packaging the Greenhouse integration and Dropbox Sign subscription together via Shake IT is the most cost-effective plan.

# Move prospects to another pool and stage in bulk 

**Permissions:** Job Admins and above with access to CRM who can advance candidates/prospects

**Product tier:** Available for new subscription tiers (Core, Plus, and Pro)

Prospect pools (and their subsequent stages) enable your organization to organize, track, and manage outreach efforts for [prospects](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/200670155) within Greenhouse CRM.

In this article, we will cover moving prospects assigned within an existing prospect pool or stage to a differing one.

**Note:** To learn more on configuring prospect pools and stages, click [here](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360024904051).

Select prospects to include in this bulk action by clicking the checkboxes next to the individual prospect profile.

Click **Edit Selected** when finished.

Click **Move to Another Pool and Stage.**

Using the subsequent dialogue box, fill in the updated prospect **Pool** and/or **Prospect Stage** fields.

When finished, click **Save** and the selected prospects will be added to the updated prospect pool and stage.

# Assign or change a user's permission level

**Permissions:** Site Admin, and Job Admin who can add users to their assigned jobs 

**Product tier:** Available for new subscription tiers (Core, Plus, and Pro)

You may need to edit a user's permission level, such as changing a user from a Site Admin to a Job Admin, or from a Basic user to a Job Admin.

#### In this article

  * Edit a user permission level 
  * Impacts of removing user permissions
    * Hiring team roles 
    * Candidate/Prospect Recruiter or Coordinator assignment
    * Notifications
    * Approvals



### Edit a user permission level 

**Note:** Downgrading a user's permission level will impact a user's access to jobs, which can affect notifications the user has enabled, as well as carry job- and candidate-level implications. For more information about the potential impacts of downgrading a user's permission level, please review the impacts of removing user permissions section of this article.

To edit a user's assigned permission level, click the **Configure****icon** in your navigation bar, then select **Users** from the left-side panel.

Click the **name of the user** whose permission level you wish to edit.

On the _Edit User_ page, navigate to the _Permissions_ panel and click **Reassign permission**. 

Click **Assign** next to the new user permission level.

**Note:** When assigning a user as a Job Admin, you must add them to a job in order for the changes to save. [Click here](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360040181991) to learn more about assigning job-based permissions.  
  
Additionally, you can only assign a user a permission level that has no greater permissions than what you have on that job. This means a Job Admin user editing another user's permission level cannot assign that user as a Site Admin, nor can they assign the user a Job Admin level which includes permission stripes not included in the assigning user's own Job Admin level. 

As a next step, you might choose to assign user-specific permissions or job-based permissions to the user. To learn more about assigning these permissions, see the following articles: 

  * [User-specific permissions overview](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360021050791)
  * [Assign job-based permission](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360040181991)



### Impacts of removing user permissions

Downgrading or removing user permissions will impact a user's access to jobs, which can affect notifications the user has enabled, as well as carry job- and candidate-level implications. 

**Example:** As a Site Admin, a user has access to all of your organization's jobs, and can be assigned Hiring Team roles for any of those jobs. If the user is downgraded to a Job Admin user type, they will have access only to jobs where they are explicitly granted Job Admin permissions.  
  
Let's say a Site Admin user, John, was configured as a Recruiter on the Mid-Market Account Manager job, but later was downgraded to a Job Admin. After John was changed to a Job Admin, he was not assigned a Job Admin level on the Mid-Market Account Manager job. As a result, John will be removed from the job's Hiring Team, and will not be able to access the candidates where he was assigned as the Recruiter. John's name will appear with a strikethrough on the job's Hiring Team page, as well as on the candidate's profile > Details tab > Recruiter field. Any notifications for the job configured to be sent to a candidate's assigned Recruiter will no longer be sent to John. 

There are four locations where a user will be preserved when they are removed from a job where they had responsibilities: 

  * Hiring team roles 
  * Candidate/Prospect Recruiter or Coordinator assignment
  * Notifications
  * Approvals (available for Plus and Pro subscription tiers)



#### Hiring team roles 

**When a user’s permission on a job is removed** : If the user was marked as _Responsible_ for new applications as a Recruiter or Coordinator, their ownership of that process is removed. 

They remain visible on that job with a strikethrough across their name to indicate they no longer have permissions on that job.

A user with a Hiring Team role on a job but no permission on the job will not be able to access the job or see tasks associated with it.

**If that user is given permissions to the job again** : The strikethrough disappears, and the user is able to access the job. However, they will not automatically be set as responsible for new applications again.

#### Candidate/Prospect Recruiter or Coordinator assignment

**When a user’s permission on a job the candidate is attached to is removed** : Removed users will still show up on the candidate's **Details** tab with a strikethrough across their name, but they will not be able to view candidates for this job. Any tasks or notifications associated with this candidate and job will not show up on that user’s Dashboard or the user's  _My Tasks_ widget.

**If that user is given permissions to the job again** : The strikethrough will disappear and the user will be able to access the candidate. Historic tasks or notifications will be visible again.

#### Notifications

**When a user’s permission on a job is removed** : The user is removed as a recipient from the notification panel and will not receive any further communication. 

**If that user is given permissions to the job again** : The recipient is added as a _participant_ to the notification panel and will receive email communication. 

#### Approvals

**When a user’s permission on a job is removed** : Removed users will still show up on the _Approvals_ page for each job or the  _Offer Details_ page for each candidate with a strikethrough across their name. However, these users will not receive any emails when approval is requested, and they will not see these pending approvals on their **Approvals** tab.

**If that user is given permissions to the job again** : The strikethrough will disappear, any outstanding approvals will show up on the user's **Approvals** tab, and any new approvals requested will be sent via email.

# JustCall integration

JustCall is a cloud-based phone system tailored to meet the needs of businesses, especially recruiting teams, sales, and support. Designed for both in-house recruiters and third-party talent acquisition firms, JustCall streamlines communication, making it easy to connect with candidates and clients. Its seamless integrations with CRM platforms, Helpdesk tools, Slack, Intercom, and Zapier simplify workflows, saving valuable time. Recruiters can effortlessly schedule calls, follow up with candidates, and ensure no opportunity is missed. With AI-powered features, JustCall boosts productivity, automates repetitive tasks, and provides actionable insights—all accessible on web, desktop, and mobile devices.

The JustCall integration with Greenhouse Recruiting offers the following features:

  * All candidates in your Greenhouse account are automatically synced as contacts in JustCall.
  * You can access candidate profiles and previous conversations instantly by clicking the contact badge during calls.
  * Call or text candidates directly from Greenhouse with ease—no screen-switching needed! Simply install the JustCall Chrome Extension for seamless click-to-dial functionality and you can simply pin it to your browser to handle incoming calls without opening JustCall.
  * Automatically logs all calls (incoming, outgoing, missed, voicemail) and texts (incoming and outgoing) in Greenhouse, capturing details like call duration, agent info, notes, AI-generated summaries, voicemail recordings, and SMS content—all neatly saved as Notes and linked to the respective candidate for seamless tracking.
  * Use any JustCall Dialer—Web, Chrome Extension, Desktop, or Mobile Apps (iOS and Android)—to call or text, with all activities synced and logged in real-time to your Greenhouse account.



#### In this article

  * Create a Harvest API key
  * Enter Your API Credentials in JustCall to Complete Setup
  * Use JustCall's Dialer with Greenhouse
  * Use JustCall's Sales Dialer with Greenhouse
  * Download JustCall Chrome Extension
  * Additional resources



### Create a Harvest API key

To configure the JustCall integration, you’ll need to create a Harvest API key.

Follow the steps in [this article](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/5888163769883) to create the key, and verify that the permissions below are selected when configuring the JustCall integration.

#### Credentials

In the Create New Credential box, make the following selections:

  * **API Type:** Harvest
  * **Partner:** JustCall or Unlisted Vendor
  * **Description:** JustCall Harvest API Key



#### **Permissions**

Verify that the following permissions are selected for the JustCall integration:

  * **Candidates**
    * Get: Retrieve Candidate
    * Get: List Candidates
    * Patch: Edit Candidate
    * Post: Add Candidate
    * Post: Add Note
  * **Users**
    * Get: Retrieve User
    * Get: List Users



### Enter Your API Credentials in JustCall to Complete Setup

With your Harvest API key copied from Greenhouse Recruiting, you're ready to enable the JustCall integration.

Login to your respective [JustCall](https://justcall.io/login) account.

From the JustCall **Dashboard** , select**Integrations** in the left-hand menu bar.

On the **Integrations** page, navigate to the **CRM and Helpdesk Tools** tab and search for Greenhouse.

Click **+Integrate** button in the left corner of the Greenhouse integration box.

In the **Connect your Greenhouse Account with JustCall** dialog box, fill in the following fields:

  1. **Greenhouse API Key:** Paste the Greenhouse Harvest API Key saved from your Greenhouse account
  2. **Greenhouse URL:** Add your Greenhouse account URL appearing at the top of your browser.
  3. **Greenhouse Email Address:** enter the Email ID with which you are logged into the Greenhouse account.



Click on the **Integrate** button at the bottom of the **Connect your Greenhouse Account with JustCall** dialog box.

**Note:** After setting up the integration, review your team’s mapping. For users with matching email IDs in JustCall and Greenhouse, the mapping is automatically handled. For others, you can manually select the appropriate email ID from the dropdown menu.

### Use JustCall's Dialer with Greenhouse

Once the JustCall and Greenhouse integration is successfully set up, you can effortlessly call or text candidates directly from Greenhouse without switching between screens. Follow the steps below to make a phone call or send a text message.

#### Making a Phone Call

Log into Greenhouse, and navigate to the candidate's profile by selecting the job they applied for and then clicking their name in the candidate list.

On the candidate’s details panel (typically on the right-hand side), find the candidate’s phone number listed under the **Phone number** section.

Click on the phone icon next to the candidate’s phone number.

Click on the phone icon next to the candidate’s phone number and Greenhouse will use the JustCall dialer to place the call.

During the call, relevant details like call duration and call ID will be displayed.

The system logs the following information automatically:

  * **Call ID:** A unique identifier for the call.
  * **Call Duration:** Recorded in HH:MM:SS format.
  * **Date & Time:** When the call was made.
  * **Called On:** Candidate's contact number.
  * **Called Via:** The assigned sales or recruiting line.
  * **Call Recording:** The complete recording of the call is available.



After the call you add additional notes or tags, if applicable.

#### Sending a Text Message

Similar to Making a Phone Call, on the candidate’s details panel (typically on the right-hand side), find the candidate’s phone number listed under the **Phone number** section.

Click on the text icon next to the candidate’s phone number.

Click on the text icon next to the candidate’s phone number and Greenhouse will use the JustCall dialer to send the text.

### Use JustCall's Sales Dialer with Greenhouse

From the JustCall **Dashboard** , select**Sales Dialer** in the left-hand menu bar.

Click **\+ Create Campaign** button in the **Sales Dialer** left-hand menu bar.

**Tip:** Customize your campaign by giving it a specific name. To do this, simply click the **Edit Name** icon located next to the **New Campaign** title.

On the **New Campaign** page, begin by choosing the most suitable dialing mode for your outreach campaign.

The following options are available:

  * **Dialing Preferences**
  * **Dialing Mode**



**Tip:** You can click **Learn more** under each mode for detailed explanations.

After choosing the desired Dialing Mode, click the **Next** button on the top right corner of the **New Campaign** page to proceed to the contact step.

Choose **Greenhouse** as an option to proceed to add the contacts you wish to include in your campaign.

### Configure the Greenhouse integration

Next, you’re required to configure the Greenhouse integration.

Select the **Greenhouse account** from the drop-down menu list.

**Select Entity** from the drop-down menu.

The following options are available:

  * **Candidates**
  * **Prospects**



#### Candidates

If you choose **Candidates** as an option for **Select Entity:**

  * In the **Select Job** option, you will see the list of all open jobs present in your integrated Greenhouse account. You can select the job from the drop-down for which you would like to fetch candidates.
  * In the **Select Stage** option, you can select the stages from the drop-down for which you'd like to import candidates. Note that if you leave this field empty, candidates from all stages will be imported.



#### Prospects

If you choose **Prospects** as an option for **Select Entity:**

  * In the **Select Job** option, you will see the list of all open jobs present in your integrated Greenhouse account. You can select the job from the drop-down for which you would like to fetch prospects.
  * The **Select Pool** and **Select Owner** fields allow you to filter prospects based on specific criteria. Note that JustCall will only retrieve prospects who belong to a selected prospect pool and have one of the specified users assigned as their owner in Greenhouse. If these fields are left blank, all prospects associated with the job will be fetched.



#### Finish setup

After adding the desired contacts, click the **Next** button on the top right corner of the **New Campaign** page to proceed to the review mapping.

Next, you’re required to map Sales Dialer fields with Greenhouse fields.

The following options are available for you:

  * **Sales Dialer Fields:** These are the fields in Sales Dialer where you want the data to go.
  * **Greenhouse Fields:** These are the fields in your CRM that contain the data you want to import.
  * **Mapped Status:** A green checkmark indicates a successful mapping. A red triangle means the field is not mapped yet.



To map a field:

  1. Click the dropdown menu under the **Greenhouse Field** column for the corresponding field from your CRM.
  2. The mapped status should change to a green checkmark. 

Note that by default, the following fields are mapped between Sales Dialer and Greenhouse - Phone Number, Name, Email, and Address. To import additional data into Sales Dialer custom fields, you are required to map fields between Sales Dialer and Greenhouse.




Next, customize how your contacts are imported, including the country code, and click the **Next** button on the top right corner of the **New Campaign** page to proceed with your campaign.

You can configure your **Campaign Settings** and **Assign Members** to your team, as per your requirements.

Once you're done, click **Finish Setup** on the top right corner of the **New Campaign** page.

### Download JustCall Chrome Extension

You can either search for and download the [JustCall Chrome Extension from the Google Chrome Web Store](https://justcall.io/crx) or download it directly from the JustCall Dashboard bar.

From the JustCall **Dashboard** bar, click the **Download Apps** icon in the top right corner.

Next, choose **Chrome** from the given options.

In the **JustCall - Click To Calls for CRM Tools** page, click **Add to Chrome** button in the top right corner.

On the confirmation pop-up, review the data the JustCall extension will access and click **Add extension**.

Next, you'll be directed to a page where you can choose your input and output devices and perform a test. To ensure you are able to make and receive calls from this Chrome browser, please allow the microphone permissions. (check the permissions popup coming out of the address bar).

After installing the extension, go back to the Candidate's profile in Greenhouse and refresh the page. This will ensure the Click to Call and Text icons appear and are ready to use. If the icons do not appear, it indicates an issue with the integration.

Integrating JustCall with Greenhouse Recruiting streamlines your recruitment process, making communication with candidates more efficient and seamless. With automatic syncing of candidate information, easy access to profiles during calls, and the ability to log calls and texts directly in Greenhouse, your team can save time and improve productivity. Whether you're using JustCall Dialer or Sales Dialer to manage candidate outreach, the integration ensures all activities are logged and tracked in real-time. By following the steps in this guide, you'll be able to easily set up and use the JustCall integration, empowering your team to enhance recruitment workflows and improve overall efficiency.

**How will calls made from Sales Dialer be logged in Greenhouse?**

Calls made from Sales Dialer would be logged against the candidates or prospects on Greenhouse as an activity feed Notes, similar to the calls that are made from JustCall.

### Additional resources

Need more info? Check out the help articles linked below:

  * [What can the JustCall integration with Greenhouse do?](https://help.justcall.io/en/articles/9286592-what-can-the-justcall-integration-with-greenhouse-do)
  * [How to set up Greenhouse integration with JustCall?](https://help.justcall.io/en/articles/9374573-how-to-set-up-greenhouse-integration-with-justcall)
  * [How to Integrate and use JustCall's Sales Dialer with Greenhouse?](https://help.justcall.io/en/articles/9812924-how-to-integrate-and-use-justcall-s-sales-dialer-with-greenhouse)



If you run into any issues, drop us a line at [help@justcall.io](mailto:help@justcall.io).

# Add a custom job field

**Permissions:** Site Admin, and Job Admin who can manage custom fields

**Product tier:** Available for new subscription tiers (Core, Plus, and Pro)

Job fields refer to the various pieces of information that can be filled out for every job your organization creates, and allow you to capture this data in a standardized format. By default, every new job includes the following job fields:

  * Internal job name
  * Department
  * Office
  * Number of openings
  * Employment type



**Note** : Employment type is a custom job field that can be enabled by request.

In addition to the default job fields, your organization can create custom job fields to capture relevant information about jobs. 

To create a custom job field, click the **Configure** icon  on your navigation bar, then click **Custom** **Options**.

Click **Jobs**.

Click the **Add Field** button to create a new custom job field, or click on an existing field to edit that field. 

Customize the new job field. Every custom job field requires a _Field Name_ and  _Field Type_.

**Note** : Once a custom job field is created, the field type cannot be changed.

  * To use the value of the field in email and offer document templates, select Create new email token and enter the token name in the provided field. 
  * To restrict access to the field to only users with one of the following permission levels, check the box next to Mark Private. 
    * Job Admin with the permission stripe Can view and edit private job fields and approve/request approval on jobs, or 
    * Site Admin with the user-specific permission Can see private notes, salary info, manage offers, request approvals, and approve jobs/offers
  * To require users to complete a field before they can proceed to the next step, check the box next to required.
  * If you have an approval workflow where jobs must be approved before they are opened, and you would like changes to this field to trigger re-approval when the job is in **Draft** or **Closed** status, check the box next to Changes to this field require reapproval.
  * To expose the field in the Job Board API, check the box next to Expose in Job Board API.



**Note** : The **Changes to this field require reapproval** setting only applies when a job is in **Draft** or **Closed** status. If a job is **Open** , changes to this field can be made without triggering reapproval.

When finished, click **Save** at the bottom of the page. 

In addition to viewing and managing these custom fields via **Job Setup** >**Job Info** , any custom fields you add to jobs will be included in the [all jobs summary report](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/203940239-).

# Greenhouse training guide for hiring managers and recruiters

#### Congratulations on starting your journey with Greenhouse!

We've designed a training guide that will help introduce Greenhouse Recruiting to people at your organization who will act as hiring managers and recruiters in the hiring software.

Click the link below to access the template, then select **Make** **a** **copy** to customize and edit the slides as needed:

# Internal job board overview

Alongside your [external job board](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360062032092), your organization can host an internal job board to post positions available to your internal network of employees. You can use iFrames to add your job board to your company's [internal site](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/articles/211233903) or host your job board on Greenhouse.   
  
By default, your organization's internal job board is hosted by Greenhouse Recruiting and is accessible to all users from within Greenhouse Recruiting. Employees must be logged in to Greenhouse to [access](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/200913945) Greenhouse-hosted internal job boards.

For each [job post](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/217267766), your organization can choose to post to the external job board, the internal job board, or both. You can also [edit](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/200521739) the board to include a logo or descriptions unique to your internal job board.

**Note** : Organizations can have only one internal job board, and the internal job board cannot be deleted.

# Greenhouse Gmail add-on

**Permissions:** **—**

**Product tier:** Available for new subscription tiers (Core, Plus, and Pro)

The Greenhouse Gmail add-on allows you to do the following:

  * View candidate profile details directly in a Gmail-hosted inbox when you are viewing an email from the candidate
  * Export candidate email messages from a Gmail-hosted inbox to the candidate's profile in Greenhouse Recruiting



The Greenhouse Gmail add-on scans the headers of an email message for email addresses that match candidates in your Greenhouse Recruiting account. If a match is identified between an email address and a Greenhouse Recruiting candidate profile, details about the candidate populate in the add-on panel on the right side of the page.

Details include the matched candidate's name, contact information, the job(s) with which the candidate is associated, and a link to view the candidate's profile in Greenhouse Recruiting. The panel also includes an option to export the candidate's email message to their Greenhouse Recruiting profile.

**Note:** This add-on can be used by organizations who use Google's email service, Gmail. Additionally, the add-on is limited to the following data gathering and sharing: 

  * The add-on doesn't bulk-gather data. No information is shared with non-Greenhouse servers or third parties
  * If a user clicks the Greenhouse Recruiting icon to open the add-on, the add-on reviews the content of that specific email
  * If a user does not click the Greenhouse Recruiting icon, the add-on looks only at email addresses on the message



#### In this article

  * Install and authorize the Greenhouse Gmail add-on
  * Use the Greenhouse Gmail add-on



### Install and authorize the Greenhouse Gmail add-on

To install the Greenhouse Gmail add-on, follow the steps below, or [click here](https://workspace.google.com/marketplace/app/greenhouse/250187532019) to navigate directly to the Google Workspace Marketplace.

Next, navigate to your Gmail account and click the **Settings** icon  in the top-right corner. In the dropdown, click **See all settings**.

Click **Add-ons** , then click **Manage** in the _Installed add-ons_ panel.

Use the search bar at the top of the _Google Workspace Marketplace_ window to search for _Greenhouse Gmail add-on_. Click the **Greenhouse** tile.

Click **Install** , then follow the installation and authentication prompts to approve the add-on for your Gmail account. The install process includes granting the application permission to view your email messages and settings, to run as an add-on, and so on. You might be prompted to provide your Gmail account credentials during this process.

When you finish authorizing the add-on, a confirmation window confirms a successful installation. To begin using the Greenhouse Gmail add-on right away, click **Done** and reload your Gmail window.

### Use the Greenhouse Gmail add-on

To use the Greenhouse Gmail add-on, open an email message or conversation from a candidate and click the Greenhouse Recruiting icon to expand the Greenhouse Gmail add-on panel.

If the add-on doesn't find any matches between the email addresses scanned in the message header and your Greenhouse Recruiting account, the panel on the right will indicate no match was found.

**Note:** If you receive an email that doesn't match an existing candidate and you want to create a new candidate profile, forward the email to Greenhouse Recruiting via Maildrop. [Click here](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/201990630) to learn more.

If a match is found between email addresses in the message and a candidate in your Greenhouse Recruiting account, the candidate's details appear in the Greenhouse Gmail add-on panel. Use the details on the right to review the job the candidate is associated with, or click **View Profile** to navigate directly to the candidate's Greenhouse Recruiting profile.

#### Export an email to Greenhouse Recruiting

To export the candidate's email message to Greenhouse Recruiting, click **Export Email** beneath the message you wish to export. A footer at the bottom of the Greenhouse Gmail add-on panel confirms when the message has been exported successfully.

Exported emails appear on the candidate's Greenhouse Recruiting profile under the **Activity Feed** tab.

# Add an interview question to an interview kit

**Permissions:** Site Admin, and Job Admin who can edit interview plans

**Product tier:** Available for new subscription tiers (Core, Plus, and Pro)

Interview kits are used by interviewers to prepare for their interviews, record their assessments and evaluate candidates on scorecards. In addition to structured categories and attributes, interview kits can also contain custom interview questions that interviewers ask candidates. In this article, we will cover how to add an interview question to an interview kit for an existing job. 

Navigate to a specific job by clicking**Jobs** from the navigation bar and selecting a job from the subsequent list. 

Go to the _Interview Plan_ page. _(**Job Setup** > **Interview Plan**)_

Click **Edit** next to the interview kit you want to update.

From the _Edit interview kit_ page, go to the _Interview Questions_ panel. Click **Add**.

Use the subsequent  _Add Interview Question_ dialog box to create the new interview question.

**What is your question?** | Enter your interview question.  
---|---  
**Select an answer type** |  _**Note:** If you choose Single Select or Multi Select, provide each possible response on a separate line in the **Options** field._  
**Required** | Check this box to mark the question as required for interviewers.  
**Tag attributes to focus on** |  Select one or more scorecard attributes to be associated with the interview question. Tagged attributes appear directly next to the associated interview question on the candidate scorecard, helping interviewers recognize which attribute to assess for. _**Note:** Linking an attribute to an interview question automatically makes it a [focus attribute](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360018399451) for the interview._  
  
Click **Add** when finished.

Interview questions support rich text formatting, like bold, italics, quotes, and lists, so you can add nuance and clarity for interviewers.

Repeat these steps to add additional interview questions as needed. When you finish, click **Save** at the bottom of the page _._

# Tonkean integration

Tonkean empowers your operations teams with an adaptive, no-code platform to optimize your unique mix of processes, people, and systems. Tonkean helps companies connect their systems, orchestrate their processes, and more specifically coordinate the people who are an integral part of these processes.

Greenhouse Recruiting’s integration with Tonkean allows you to create/deactivate Greenhouse Recruiting accounts along with taking all of the traditional actions you’d be able to take within Greenhouse Recruiting.

#### In this article

  * Create a Harvest API key for the Tonkean integration
  * Use the Tonkean integration with Greenhouse Recruiting
  * Additional resources



### Create a Harvest API key for the Tonkean integration

To configure the Greenhouse Recruiting / Tonkean integration, you'll need to create a Harvest API key.

Follow the steps in [this article](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/5888163769883) to create the key, and verify that the credentials and permissions below are selected when configuring the Tonkean integration.

#### Credentials

In the _Create New Credential_ box, make the following selections:

  * **API type:** Harvest
  * **Partner:** Tonkean
  * **Description:** Tonkean Harvest API key



#### Permissions

Verify that the following permissions are selected for the Tonkean integration:

  * For all cases involving provisioning and deprovisioning user accounts, select all permissions under **Users**.
  * If you intend to update other Greenhouse Recruiting entities (**User Roles** , **Jobs** , **Scorecards** , etc.) make sure those boxes are selected so Tonkean has write access to Greenhouse Recruiting.



If you have questions about which permissions to grant your Harvest API key, reach out to Tonkean.

### Use the Tonkean integration with Greenhouse Recruiting

A great example of how you can utilze the Greenhouse Recruiting / Tonkean integration is for account provisioning/deprovisioning. An example could be when a user is created in the _Recruiting_ Okta Group, you want to automatically create a Greenhouse Recruiting account for that user.

Using the _Create User_ action, you simply need to put in the Okta fields of the user (first name, last name, email address).

**Note:** It is important that you are updating/creating data on behalf of a Greenhouse Recruiting user who has the correct permissions to create accounts. Specifically, you need that user’s unique Greenhouse Recruiting user ID (which can be found on the Users page within Greenhouse Recruiting, extracting it from the URL of their profile).  
  
Once you have the user ID, input the ID in the last field, **Create On Behalf Of** , to complete the process.

### Additional resources

For additional information not covered here, reach out to [support@tonkean.com](mailto:support@tonkean.com).

# Create a new offer and re-trigger offer approval

**Permissions:** Site Admin who can see private notes and salary info, manage offers, request approval, and approve jobs/offers, and Job Admin who can view and edit offers and approve/request approval on offers

**Product tier:** Available for new subscription tiers (Core, Plus, and Pro)

Editing specified fields in a [created offer](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/201165300-Request-Offer-Approval) creates a new offer version and restarts the offer approval process for the job.

In this article, we will provide an overview of how to create a new offer version, which fields create a new offer version, and the implications of editing these unique fields.

#### In this article

  * Edit existing offer to create new offer version
    * Request approval for new offer version 
  * General considerations



### Edit existing offer to create new offer version

**Note** : Creating a new offer version and re-triggering the offer approval process voids the original offer and any associated approvals already issued.

To edit an existing offer, navigate to a candidate's profile who already has an offer created (which may or may not be in the process of an offer approval) and go to the **Offer** stage.

Scroll down to the bottom of the offer details and click **Update**.

Update the offer fields on the pop-up window. Updating a field with the **Refresh** icon will create a new offer version.

**Note** : Editing fields without the  icon won't create a new offer version or re-trigger the offer approval process.

Click **Save** when finished.

### Request approval for new offer version 

To request approval and re-trigger the offer approval process for the new offer version, click **Request Approval.**

Users configured as offer approvers for the job are notified via email that their approval is required for the new offer version.

### General considerations

  * It's not possible to remove older offer versions without removing the newest offer version first. 
  * To remove an existing offer version, click Delete at the bottom of the **Offer details** section

# Sova Assessments integration

Sova is an award-winning online assessment platform that guarantees fair, equitable outcomes from assessments without compromising on anything else. Sova is the only recruitment software application that balances relevant and engaging content for candidates, with absolute fairness and accuracy.

# Expensify integration

Greenhouse Recruiting's integration with Expensify allows you to automatically send candidates from Greenhouse to Expensify for easy reimbursement of out-of-pocket expenses. To link your accounts, log into Expensify.com as a Policy Admin to get started. 

#### In this article

  * Create a webhook
  * Use the Expensify integration with Greenhouse Recruiting
  * Additional resources



### Create a webhook

To integrate Expensify with Greenhouse Recruiting, you'll need to create a webhook. Follow the steps in [this article](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/5888163727003) to create your webhook. Use the values listed below to configure the webhooks.

  * **Name** : Expensify integration
  * **When** : Candidate or prospect updated
  * **Endpoint URL** : The Endpoint URL provided by Expensify
  * **Secret Key** : The Secret Key provided by Expensify



### Create a custom candidate field

In Greenhouse, select **Configure** > **Custom Options** > **Custom Company Fields** > **Candidates**.

Click **Add Field** at the top of the page.

Name field “Invite to Expensify” and select type “**Yes/No** ”.

Click **Save**.

That's it! Your Greenhouse account and Expensify account can now talk to each other.

### Use the Expensify integration with Greenhouse Recruiting

Log into Greenhouse and go to any candidate’s Details tab. Make sure the Email field is filled in and optionally, select the Recruiter field.

To send this candidate to Expensify, toggle the Invite to Expensify field to Yes and click Save.

In Expensify, navigate to Admin > Policies > [your policy] > People.

The candidate you just sent to Expensify will be listed here. If the Recruiter field was filled in in Greenhouse, the candidate will already be configured to submit reports to that recruiter.

The Candidate will be guided through how to set up their Expensify account and submit their receipts for reimbursement.

### Additional resources

If you run into any trouble establishing or using the integration, please first visit our Greenhouse ExpensifyDocs page by going to <https://docs.expensify.com/> and searching for Greenhouse. If you still need assistance or have any questions, please reach out to [help@expensify.com](mailto:help@expensify.com) or use our in-app messenger.

# Add custom source

**Permissions:** Job Admins who can manage company metadata, and Site Admins

**Product tier:** Available for new subscription tiers (Core, Plus, and Pro)

By default, Greenhouse Recruiting comes with more than 180 sources configured for your organization. Additionally, your organization can add to this list with specific custom sources. This article covers how to add a custom source to this list.

Click the **Configure** icon in the upper right-hand corner and select **Custom Options** from the left-hand panel.

On the subsequent page, click **Sources** under the _Company Metadata_ section.

On the _Manage Sources_ page, click the **Create New Source** button.

Use the subsequent dialog box to select a [sourcing strategy](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360004175751) and provide a name for the source.

Click **Create Source** when finished.

**Note** : Every custom source must be associated with a sourcing strategy. You can add [additional sourcing strategies](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/25550517997467) in Custom Options.

Your newly created source will appear under the _Sources_ list.

Your new source also will be added to dropdown menus for tracking links and on the candidate's **Details** tab. To learn more on how to create a tracking link to your custom source, visit: [Create a Tracking Link for a Single Job Post](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/4405093302427)
