# Release Notes: July 2024

Greenhouse Software regularly releases new product features, updates, and improvements. You can stay up to date by following our [release notes](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/200929955) or checking out the [latest feature releases](https://www.greenhouse.com/greenhouse-latest-features) page.

#### This month's releases

  * Greenhouse Recruiting
  * Business Intelligence Connector
  * Integrations
  * Bug fixes



### Greenhouse Recruiting

#### Summer packaged release

Greenhouse launched its summer packaged release, dedicated to helping you save time while still making inclusive hiring decisions

You can read more about everything in the release in [our blog post](https://www.greenhouse.com/blog/greenhouse-summer-2024-new-releases-help-you-save-time-while-still-making-inclusive-hiring-decisions), or keep up with the [latest feature releases](https://www.greenhouse.com/greenhouse-latest-features?utm_source=greenhouse-employees&utm_medium=database-email&utm_campaign=CUS-0723-Q3Packagedrelease) on our website.

#### External job board UI updates

Released a completely overhauled experience for external job boards to allow organizations easier control over job board styling and functionality:

  * Streamlined, no-code customization options for job board layout, colors, fonts, and buttons. 
  * Options to add 'New' tags to recent job posts
  * Redesigned configuration page
  * WCAG 2.0AA accessibility



[Read more here](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/18996861758363)

**Note:** New styling options are only available for job board options 1-4.

#### New essential reports for scheduling activity

A new essential report, Scheduling Activity, provides organizations with a high-level view of interviews created, scheduled, pending, or completed in a specific time range.

#### Reschedule self-scheduled interviews

A new setting has been added under Configure > Permissions that allows candidates to reschedule self-scheduled interviews up to 24 hours before the scheduled interview time.

Once the setting is turned on, add the {{INTERVIEW_RESCHEDULE_LINK}} token to the [Candidate Interview Confirmation](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/115002573326) template to give candidates access to the new link.

**Note:** Candidate self-scheduling is only available to Advanced and Expert tier customers.

#### Parent/child relationship in Openings custom fields

Expert-tier customers can add dependencies to custom Opening fields (similar to [parent child relationships](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360038889992) in Offer fields) to help streamline their workflows and only show specific the most relevant fields when opening a job. 

#### New DocuSign Tokens

The following tokens have been added to the [DocuSign integration](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/205633569) and can be used in templates:

  * Single-line text inputs for candidates
  * Single-line text inputs for company counter signers
  * Long text inputs for candidates
  * Long text inputs for company countersigners



#### Other changes

  * Overhauled the [Webhook Log](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/11647402997275) page to add better search and filtering so it's easier to locate, diagnose, and fix webhook issues.
  * Added a new "Can manage unattached prospects" permission for job admins so organizations can take greater control over their prospect permissions. 
  * Added an organization setting under **Configure** > **Permissions** to include an interviewer's title when scheduling interviews. 
  * Added two new settings under **Configure** > **Organization** to allow organizations to deactivate users' ability to submit referrals or generate referral links. 
  * Users can now select multiple options when creating permission rules.



#### Candidate profile updates

As part of our continuing rollout of the new candidate profile, we've made the following updates and fixes in the new experience:

  * Added an Agency tag to the profile header
  * Improved alerts across the candidate profile 
    * Moved "time in stage" alerts within the stages panel 
    * Updated the appearance and verbiage of alert text in the All Stages view
    * Added Duplicate Candidate alert to the header that can be clicked to address the duplicate record
  * Removed inactive Agency Recruiter accounts as options in dropdown menus
  * Tooltip text can now be highlighted for copy/paste
  * Updated dropdown menus across the candidate profile to allow users to fully scroll all options without having to narrow the search with the text field
  * Updated the styling for buttons in the candidate rejection window to reduce the risk of sending unintended rejection emails 
  * Added a blank Opening ID field when the candidate is hired
  * Improved self-schedule windows to include all steps on a single page
  * Updated behavior of submitted candidate forms to include any added links in the submitted form response, instead of under the Websites section of the right panel.
  * Updated take-home test emails so any email address can be typed in the 'To' field.



Over the past month, we've also released the following fixes to the new experience:

  * Fixed an issue where opening a Calendly email wouldn't include users entered in the CC field of the template
  * Fixed an issue where jobs couldn't be copied if used a self-schedule request with a user who had disconnected their calendar 
  * Fixed an issue where users couldn't transfer hired candidates
  * Fixed an issue where completed prospect post questions weren't being shown on the new candidate profile
  * Fixed an issue dates on the candidate profile were displaying as one day earlier than the date selected
  * Fixed an issue where users couldn't modify the Sent On field for the offer after the candidate was marked as hired
  * Fixed an issue with Zenefits integration where trying to export candidates using the button in the header was showing an error
  * Fixed an issue where long stage or form names in the right panel were pushing the edit button off the page
  * Fixed an issue where removing and re-adding a grader to a take-home test would add a new stage instead of adding the grader to the existing test.
  * Fixed where custom rejection fields when a candidate was rejected in any stage, rather than the option stage that was chosen when setting up the custom field.
  * Fixed an issue where resizing a window across a page would remove any unsaved values



### Business Intelligence Connector

A new update for the Business Intelligence Connector will be released today, July 26, 2024. [Read more here.](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/27488664121371)

### Integrations

  * **Candidate sourcing:** [Jobzyn](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/26523052773019) is a next-generation recruiting platform, centered around employer branding and AI solutions.
  * **Candidate testing:** [Hallo](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/27277402055579) is an AI-powered language assessment platform that evaluates the proficiency levels of your applicants according to CEFR standards.
  * **Candidate testing:** [Personality Insights](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/26325561277595) has a simple integration with Greenhouse that adds an automated DISC personality assessment system. 
  * **Free job posts:** [The Hub](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/26523377421723) is the biggest recruitment platform for startups and scale-ups in the Nordics, with more than 1500 daily applications and over 500k talents in their talent base.
  * **Free job posts:** [X Hiring](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/25140309418267) allows your organization to post for free to X and reach millions of relevant candidates or become a Verified Organization to enhance your hiring capabilities.
  * **HRIS and onboarding:** [Lattice’s](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/26683626219163) integration with Greenhouse Recruiting allows for mutual Greenhouse and Lattice customers to seamlessly transfer hired candidates from Greenhouse to Lattice.
  * **Optimization:** [Covey](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/26684264799771) helps teams focus on the best candidates in their hiring pipeline with plain-language AI resume screening and outreach.



### Bug fixes

  * Organizations using the old candidate profile encountered an error attaching documents to Adobe eSignature requests. 
  * Fixed an issue where a user was receiving automated alerts about a pending approval request, even though the job was already approved
  * LinkedIn Apply Connect: 
    * Fixed an issue where offline job posts were displaying a "job was not found" error under the LinkedIn Status
    * Fixed an issue where users couldn't enter their Company URL once Apply Connect or enable Easy Apply when using the new job board interface
    * Fixed syncing with LinkedIn Apply Connect fully remove pending job posts if the job is deleted in Greenhouse while the post is being processed by LinkedIn
    * Updated how Greenhouse handles syncing with LinkedIn so that multiple notes are added to the job when the LinkedIn sync fails
  * Corrected an issue where lookup credit balances weren't displaying under the Sourcing Automation Settings 
  * Fixed an issue where adding attachments to Adobe eSignature agreements through email template attachments was showing an error
  * Fixed an issue where the GDPR banner wasn't showing immediately in the candidate profile when the candidate manually denied consent
  * Fixed an issue where GDPR banners weren't displaying the retention date when an organization changed their legal basis to explicit consent
  * Fixed issues with sandbox sync: 
    * Harvest API keys will be correctly retained in sandboxes so they don't have to be recreated after every sync
    * Offer letter templates will now be correctly synced
  * Fixed an issue where multiple webhook events were being logged whenever a candidate was merged
  * Fixed an issue where inactive custom offer field options were still available in the dropdown menus on offers
  * Updated error messages when uploading templates with an invalid token be more helpful
  * Fixed formatting issues on an error message in Greenhouse Onboarding.

In an effort to improve our suite of products, Greenhouse Software regularly releases new product features, updates, and improvements. Stay up-to-date with what's new at Greenhouse by **Following** our [Release Notes](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/sections/360000710732-Release-Notes).

### **Greenhouse Recruiting**

  * We updated the  _All Users_ page and individual  _User Permission_ pages to ensure using type-to-search filters the  _Interviewer Tags_ dropdown menu as expected .

  * We fixed an offer exceptions bug that caused the salary field in the  _Offer Details_ dialog box to default to a currency type of USD, rather than inheriting the currency type of the tracked custom job field.

# AI Screened integration

AI Screened streamlines applicant screening with Ryan, an AI recruiter who reviews resumes, conducts phone screens, and manages candidate comms 24/7 so you can meet your best potential hires, right away.

AI Screened’s integration with Greenhouse Recruiting allows you to seamlessly add Ryan’s assessment to a job's interview plan.

#### In this article

  * Enable the AI Screened integration
  * Use the AI Screened integration with Greenhouse Recruiting
  * Frequently asked questions
  * Additional resources



### Enable the AI Screened integration

You will need an AI Screened API key to connect the integration. To obtain this key, first, create an AI Screened account [here](https://screened.io/get-started/). 

Once your account is created, log in to your account and click ‘Settings’ on the left side. Then scroll down to the Integrations section and click ‘Connect Greenhouse’ to generate an API key. 

On the next screen, you will receive an AI Screened API key to copy and save. Keep this API Key somewhere safe as it will not be shown again. 

Then, follow the steps in [this article](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/5888163696923) to add the AI Screened assessment stage in your interview plans in Greenhouse.

After Greenhouse has activated the AI Screened integration, log in to the AI Screened application again and add your Job Description. Common document file types, including .pdf, .docx, .doc, .rtf, and .txt can be uploaded.

The AI Screened application will assess the job description. Once the JD is uploaded, it’s time to teach your AI Recruiter, Ryan, about an ideal candidate’s specific skills that he can use to screen resumes for who to reach out to. You’ll do this by highlighting two things: Must Haves and Nice to Haves.

#### Adding Must Have skills for resume screening

These are non-negotiables. If a candidate doesn’t meet these requirements, they don’t qualify to move forward. For example, if you’re hiring for a NodeJS developer and the candidate’s resume doesn’t mention any JavaScript or NodeJS experience, they will be disqualified.

We recommend you start with only listing things your candidates absolutely must have. At a minimum you need 2 Must Haves. It’s good to start with only that. You can always add on more later to refine your shortlist.

#### Adding Nice to Have Skills for resume screening

These are the extra skills or experiences that would be great to have, but aren’t dealbreakers. Ryan will prioritize candidates who meet most of your Nice to Haves, but he won’t rule someone out if they don’t tick every box.

Once you’ve set up your interview plans and configured your take-home test, you’ll be able to send the test to candidates to have them screened for your role.

### Use the AI Screened integration with Greenhouse Recruiting

Once the AI Screened integration is enabled for your organization, you will be able to add the AI Screened assessment as an interview stage.

Edit your Interview Plan, select Add Stage, and select the AI Screened stage. Position this stage near the beginning of your interview plan.

#### Calibrate your Resume Screening Scorecard

When you add a new role to AI Screened, we recommend calibrating your resume screening scorecard with a few sample profiles. By default, our integration will only screen candidate resumes and your AI Recruiter, Ryan, will not reach out to candidates.

To calibrate your scorecard, follow the steps below to send your test to a few sample profiles. The test results for the resume screening will sync back to Greenhouse within a minute. You may also conveniently review all results on the AI Screened application. 

If you wish to revise your scorecard at this point, go back to the AI Screened application and edit the scorecard. It’s helpful to do a few rounds of calibration until you feel your resume screening scorecard is shortlisting the right candidates for interview from your sample batch.

Once you feel comfortable with the calibration results, go to your job on the AI Screened application and click ‘Outreach’ and enable screen calling from your job settings. 

Simply click the option to do additional shortlisting with screen calls.

After you have saved your changes to the outreach setting for your role, Ryan will proceed to schedule interviews for selected candidates from your calibration. (You can read more about that process further below)

Note: After outreach is enabled for a job, test results for candidates will be updated on Greenhouse only after Ryan’s job is done. This means you will receive the results after the candidate completes the interview unless the profile fails resume screening.

#### Screening candidates

In Greenhouse Recruiting, under the Candidates tab, move candidates to the AI Screened stage using Bulk Actions. Initiate a screening assessment by clicking Send Test.

Choose the role for which you are assessing and select the member of your team who will grade the results of AI Screened’s assessment.

After clicking **Send Test** , AI Screened will assess the resume fit for the role based on the criteria you configured during setup on the AI Screened application.

At this point one of two things will happen:

  * **If outreach is disabled for the role, or if the candidate fails resume screening:** You will receive test results within a minute explaining why the candidate is unsuitable for the role. These candidates will not be contacted by AI Screened.
  * **For candidates who meet the majority of your criteria:** Ryan, our AI recruiter, will initiate contact via email to schedule a screening call. This call is designed to further evaluate the candidate’s suitability for the role. These instructions are actually sent by Ryan at AI Screened who will communicate with your candidate as your AI recruiter.



With outreach enabled, a candidate’s assessment status will be marked as 'pending' in Greenhouse Recruiting until they complete the screening call with AI Screened. This typically takes 1-3 days, depending on candidate availability.

Once the candidate has completed the screen call, the Interview Kit will contain a link to view the results in the AI Screened application.

To see a candidate’s results in AI Screened, click View Report.

### Frequently asked questions

#### How do I set up a new role to screen for in the AI Screened application?

Before you begin using AI Screened with Greenhouse Recruiting, log in to the AI Screened application and add a role with a job description.

After the job description has been processed, AI Screened will suggest criteria to assess the candidates. Select criteria suggestions that are important to your organization for this role, or add skills that are required.

#### What is the screening process like?

At a high level, AI Screened’s process follows a structured process to review resumes with a scorecard, interview candidates on their experience and fit, and help answer questions / coordinate all the steps in between.

It all starts when candidate resumes will be first assessed for fit based on the criteria you’ve established on the AI Screened application.

If a candidate’s assessment results determine they are a poor fit for the role, immediate feedback will be returned to your grader, including an email summary and a detailed evaluation in the AI Screened application. In this situation, the candidate will not receive any communication from AI Screened.

For candidates with a strong or potential match to the criteria, Ryan, the AI recruiter from AI Screened, will email the candidate to schedule a screening call at a convenient time. (This typically occurs within 1-3 days, depending on the candidate.)

On the phone call, Ryan will cover relevant experience, problem-solving, and behavioral attributes. The call takes from 15 to 30 minutes, depending on the candidate.

**Note:** Customizable screen call assessments ranging from technical skill evaluations to in-depth behavioral interviews are also available on certain pricing plans. Please [contact AI Screened](https://screened.io/contact)

Afterwards, the candidate’s performance will be assessed by AI Screened’s mindful AI designed to recommend fair, neutral assessments. The grader assigned in Greenhouse Recruiting will be notified of the results, including objective, detailed feedback about the candidate’s qualities that matter most to your organization.

#### How do candidates communicate with Ryan?

For candidates who pass the resume screening, Ryan manages all the screening stage candidate communication by email.

Correspondence includes scheduling the screening call, answering questions for candidates, follow-ups if left pending too long, handovers to the next round, rejections, and reminders.

Think of Ryan like an extension of your recruiting team capable of communicating at scale to ensure no candidate at the screening stage is overlooked.

#### What does a screen call sound like?

You can listen to call samples from [AI Screened’s AI recruiter](https://screened.io/#call-samples) or reach out to [help@screened.io](https://help@screened.io) to try a screen call demonstration.

#### Can you assess a candidate without a resume?

Not at this time. Candidates sent to AI Screened without a resume will be assessed as ‘not a fit’ at the resume screening step, as there are no qualifications, skills, or experience that can be screened. Please [reach out to AI Screened](https://screened.io/contact) if you have a use case for screening candidates without resumes.

### Additional resources

For assistance with this integration, [reach out to the AI Screened application team](https://screened.io/contact).

# Guide to Business Intelligence Connector

**Permissions:** —

**Product tier:** Available for Plus and Pro subscription tiers

Business Intelligence Connector delivers a daily ETL of your organization's Greenhouse Recruiting and Greenhouse Onboarding data, dating from the time of your environment's creation. The data is comprehensive. This article provides a guide to the data, with a brief description of each table and what each row represents, as well as what to expect for each column.

**Tip** : Use your browser's Find feature (CMD + F on Mac | CTRL + F on Windows) to search for the data point you're interested in, like "custom candidate fields."

#### In this article

  * Application data
  * Candidate data
  * Candidate PII data
  * Demographic data
  * Greenhouse Onboarding data
  * Greenhouse Sourcing Automation data
  * Job data
  * Offer data
  * Organization data
  * Process data
  * Usage data



### Application data

#### The applications table

The `applications` table represents a snapshot of application data. Each row represents the latest status of a single application.

**Note** : This table doesn't contain any historical records.

**Column** | **What to know**  
---|---  
`id` | The application ID. This appears as `application_id` on other tables.  
`candidate_id` | The candidate ID.  
`coordinator` | The [coordinator's](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360016347752) name.  
`coordinator_id` | The candidate's [coordinator's](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360016347752) ID. A candidate might not have the same coordinator assigned to the hiring team of the candidate's job if their application has been [added to another job](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/115002867346) or if their profile has been [merged](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/208063316).  
`applied_at` | The date and time the candidate applied, like `2024-01-31 06:00:00.000`. Timestamps are in Coordinated Universal Time (UTC).  
`status` | The application's current status and is one of `active`, `converted`, `rejected`, or `hired`. Converted applications represent prospect applications that were [converted](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360025848912) to candidate applications.  
`prospect` | Boolean. Results are either `true` or `false`, indicating whether the application is for a [prospect](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/200670155).  
`stage_id` | The [stage](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/115002194903) ID of the application.  
`source_id` | The [source](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/115003931231) ID for the application.  
`recruiter` | The [recruiter's](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360016347712) name.  
`recruiter_id` | The candidate's [recruiter's](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360016347712) ID. A candidate might not have the same recruiter assigned to the hiring team of the candidate's job if their application has been [added to another job](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/115002867346) or if their profile has been [merged](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/208063316).  
`referrer_id` | The [referrer](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/201982560) ID for the application. This appears as '[Who Gets Credit](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/20713686421147)' on the application under Details > Source & Responsibility.  
`rejected_at` | The date and time the application was rejected, if applicable, like `2024-01-31 06:00:00.000`. Timestamps are in Coordinated Universal Time (UTC).  
`rejected_by_id` | The [user ID](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/10765948752027) of the person who rejected the application, if applicable.  
`rejection_reason_id` | The [rejection reason](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/207305363) ID for a rejected application, if applicable.  
`pipeline_percent` | The percentage that an application has advanced through a job's [stages](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/115002194903), not including the application's current stage. For an application in a job's first stage, the pipeline percent is `0`. For an application in a job's last stage, the pipeline percent is `{number of stages} - 1 / {number of stages}`. For a hired application, the pipeline percent is `[NULL]`. For prospects, the pipeline percent is `0`.  
`migrated` | Boolean. Results are either `true` or `false`, indicating whether the application was migrated from a different ATS.  
`rejected_by` | The name of the Greenhouse Recruiting user who rejected the application, if applicable.  
`stage_name` | The application's current [stage](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360000767191) name.  
`job_post_id` | The [job post](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360020285311) ID associated with the application.  
`prospect_pool` | The name of the [prospect pool](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360024904051), for prospect applications.

Data isn't collected for candidates who didn't respond to questions on the job post or didn't receive a request to respond to the questions afterward.

**Column** | **What to know**  
---|---  
`application_id` | The application ID.  
`status` | The EEOC response status and is one of `responded` or `pending response`.  
`race` | The application response to the [EEOC questions](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/205278605) `Are you Hispanic/Latino?` and `Please identify your race`.  
`gender` | The application response to the [EEOC question](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/205278605) `Gender`.  
`disability_status` | The application response to the [EEOC question](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/205278605) `Disability Status`.  
`veteran_status` | The application response to the [EEOC question](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/205278605) `Veteran Status`.  
`submitted_at` | The date and time the EEOC response was submitted, like `2024-01-31 06:00:00.000`. Timestamps are in Coordinated Universal Time (UTC).  
`organization_id` | Your organization's unique Greenhouse Recruiting ID.

### Greenhouse Sourcing Automation (GHSA) data

Greenhouse Sourcing Automation (GHSA) data helps subscribers analyze how their team connects with and converts prospects.

#### The GHSA actions table

The `gsha_actions` table captures each interaction a prospect has with your outreach. You can also distinguish between manual and AI-assigned sentiments like _interested_ or _bad fit_.

**Column** | **What to know**  
---|---  
`id` | The GHSA action ID.  
`application_id` | The application’s ID.  
`campaign_detail_id` | The campaign detail's ID.  
`verb` | The type of action was taken on the prospect: `viewed` , `visited` , `replied`, `messaged` , `booked`, `bounced`, `unsubscribed` , `reply_removed` , `booked_removed`, `sentiment_updated`, `sentiment_removed`  
`created_at` | The date and time the tag was created for the prospect, like `2024-01-31 06:00:00.000`. Timestamps are in Coordinated Universal Time (UTC).  
`manual_user_id` |  The Greenhouse Recruiting [user ID](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/10765948752027) for custom application fields with user field types.  
`auto_assigned` | Boolean. Results are either true or false. True indicates that a sentiment has been auto-assigned to a prospect.  
`sentiment` | The sentiment assigned to a prospect: `interested`, `not interested`, `bad fit`, `wrong contact`, `timing`, `bad data`  
`organization_id` | Your organization's unique Greenhouse Recruiting organization ID.  
  
#### The GHSA campaign pool performance table

The `gsha_campaign_pools` table breaks down the structure, type (engage or nurture), and timing of your campaigns. You can also track which users created and managed each campaign pool.

**Column** | **What to know**  
---|---  
`id` | The GHSA campaign pool ID.  
`prospect_pool_id` | The GHSA prospect pool ID.  
`campaign_detail_id` | The GHSA campaign pool ID.  
`user_id` | The Greenhouse Recruiting user ID for GHSA campaign pools.  
`campaign_type` | Your campaign type: `nurture` or `engage`  
`created_at` | The date and time the campaign pool was created, like `2024-01-31 06:00:00.000`. Timestamps are in Coordinated Universal Time (UTC).  
`updated_at` | The date and time the campaign pool was updated, like `2024-01-31 06:00:00.000`. Timestamps are in Coordinated Universal Time (UTC).  
`organization_id` | Your organization's unique Greenhouse Recruiting organization ID.  
  
#### The GHSA message activity table

Understand your delivery and engagement metrics using the `ghsa_messages` table. This table includes timestamps for when a message was sent, viewed, replied to, or clicked, which gives you visibility into every step of a prospect’s journey.  


**Column** | **What to know**  
---|---  
`id` | The Greenhouse Recruiting user ID for GHSA messages.  
`campaign_step_id` | The campaign step’s ID.  
`campaign_detail_id` | The GHSA campaign pool ID.  
`application_id` | The application’s ID.  
`requires_personalization` | Indicates that a GHSA message requires personalization.  
`created_at` | The date and time the message l was created, like `2024-01-31 06:00:00.000`. Timestamps are in Coordinated Universal Time (UTC).  
`sent_at` | The date and time the message was sent to the prospect, like `2024-01-31 06:00:00.000`. Timestamps are in Coordinated Universal Time (UTC).  
`viewed_at` | The date and time the message was viewed by the prosepect, like `2024-01-31 06:00:00.000`. Timestamps are in Coordinated Universal Time (UTC).  
`visited_at` |  The date and time a link in the message was visited by the prospect, like `2024-01-31 06:00:00.000`. Timestamps are in Coordinated Universal Time (UTC). If the message doesn't have a `viewed_at` value when the prospect clicks this link, `viewed_at` will inherit the `visited_at` date and time.  
`replied_at` |  The date and time the prospect replied to a message, like `2024-01-31 06:00:00.000`. Timestamps are in Coordinated Universal Time (UTC). If the message doesn't have a `viewed_at` value when the prospect replies to the message, `viewed_at` will inherit the `replied_at` date and time.  
`organization_id` | Your organization's unique Greenhouse Recruiting organization ID.  
  
#### The GHSA outreach steps table

The `ghsa_campaign_steps` table allows you to audit campaign design. See subject lines, message content, delays between steps, and whether a step used personalization, AI contribution, or a Gmail aliases.

**Column** | **What to know**  
---|---  
`id` | The Greenhouse Recruiting user ID for campaign steps.  
`campaign_detail_id` | The GHSA campaign detail ID.  
`step_number` | Where a selected step appears in a campaign’s sequence of steps: 1, 2, 3 etc.  
`sent_on_behalf_of_user_id` | The step sender’s ID, if different from the campaign owner.  
`subject` | The campaign step’s message.  
`wait_days` | The length of time your campaign pool will pause before automatically moving to the next step (note: 0 means 10 minutes)  
`gmail_sent_as` | The name and address of the Gmail alias, if using.  
`ai_contribution_status ` | The status of an AI-generated step: `created` or `approved`  
`requires_personalization` |  Boolean. Results are either `true` or `false`. True indicates that step requires personalization.  
`step_type` | The step type: `task` or `message`  
`task_type` | The task type: `manual` or `inmail`  
`organization_id` | Your organization's unique Greenhouse Recruiting organization ID.

Understand lookup activity with the `ghsa_lookups` table. See when your team searched for work or personal email addresses and whether a lookup was successful.

**Column** | **What to know**  
---|---

#### The audit log table

The `audit_log` table represents a list of [audit log](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/15074318933275) results in Greenhouse Recruiting. Each row represents a single audit log result.

**Note** : Audit log is only available to Pro subscription tier.

**Column** | **What to know**  
---|---  
`request_id` | The ID of the [audit log](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/15074318933275) request, which can be used to link an [event](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/15076048557723) and its resulting changes across multiple audit log results.  
`request_type` | The type of request.  
`performer_meta` | The name and Greenhouse Recruiting email address of the person who performed the change or the exact type of API key that performed the event.  
`performer_id` | The Greenhouse Recruiting user ID of the person who performed the change, or the API key name if performed via Greenhouse API.  
`performer_ip_address` | The IP address of the performer of the change.  
`performer_type` | The performer type and is one of `user`, `api_key`, or `greenhouse_internal`.  
`event_time` | The date and time the event occurred, like `2024-01-31 06:00:00.000`. Timestamps are in Coordinated Universal Time (UTC).  
`event_target_type` | The type of [event](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/15076048557723) that occurred.  
`event_type` | The type of event that occured and is one of `data_change_update`, `data_change_create`, `data_change_destroy`, `harvest_access`, or `action`. `action` event types are defined in the [audit log glossary](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/15076048557723).  
`event_target_id` | The ID of the element that was created, edited, or accessed. This may be blank if the action doesn't target one particular ID.

For scorecards submitted before this date, `created_at` and `submitted_at` hold the same value. For submission time, use the `submitted_at` column.  **Note:** Prior to May 28, 2026, this value was overwritten on submission to match `submitted_at`. # Best practices: Write an effective job description

**Permissions:** **—**

**Product tier:** Available for new subscription tiers (Core, Plus, and Pro)

Job descriptions are a crucial part of attracting quality candidates. The more aligned your job description is to your company’s unique culture, the more you are differentiating your job from the other thousands of options out there. It is one of the first windows into what a career might look like at your company, and the goal of it is to both inform candidates and excite them enough to apply.

### Here are 5 things to consider when writing a job description:

#### Job title

The job title is the first piece of information that will introduce the job to the candidate, so make sure it attracts the appropriate audience. You will want to consider what your title might mean in the context of other companies -- for example, an “Account Manager” can be a pure sales role at one company or a pure customer success role at another. It is also important to make sure your title isn’t too specific -- for example, the title “Site Reliability Engineer” makes sense within the context of Greenhouse’s engineering team, but we’ve externally marketed the role as “DevOps Engineer,” as this is a more common title held by those qualified for our position. The key is to make the title relatable and broad enough that you aren’t turning away people who would be a good fit. At Greenhouse, we also like A/B testing titles through our multiple job posts feature to see which titles generate more qualified candidates.

#### Description

This section contains the meat of the job description. Typically, the description is outlined in 1) a high-level blurb that includes who the role is reporting to and what team the position is on and 2) bullet points that outline the responsibilities of the job. Instead of listing what your ideal candidate will do, we encourage you to focus on what they will accomplish. Through this approach, candidates have a more exciting, goal-oriented view of what they’ll be tasked to fulfill.

#### Qualifications

The qualifications are usually presented as a list of the hard skills a candidate needs in order to be considered for the role. Typically, these are the things you can learn from a resume - anything from previous work experience to required certifications or degrees to familiarity with certain technology stacks. At Greenhouse, our Recruiting team takes an open-minded approach, given that so much of someone’s success in a role is not only based on years of experience or certifications but also the ability and desire to learn. 

#### Voice

Now that you have the content of your job description created, check your voice or tone. Does it reflect your company culture, and is it consistent throughout your job description? At Greenhouse, we favor an authentic, jargon-free and “human” voice for our job descriptions, but more corporate environments might adopt a formal tone to match their environment.

#### Company Info

Finally, most employers will conclude their job description with a brief description of their company culture to further provide insight into a day-in-the-life-of. This can include anything from benefits, perks, an EEO / diversity statement, and awards your company has accrued. This section should be consistent across all full-time job postings.

# Sinta integration

Sinta streamlines your hiring process by syncing effortlessly with the tools your team uses every day, like Slack and Greenhouse. It boosts your recruiting efficiency through smart notifications, timely feedback reminders, and actionable alerts, all within Slack. This not only shaves hours off your schedule but also brings the kind of precision and consistency you need to make smarter hiring choices and knock out bias.

Sinta’s integration with Greenhouse Recruiting allows information to flow smoothly right where you need it—into your favorite messaging platforms. It ensures that candidate details, interview stages, and updates are mirrored back and forth seamlessly between your systems. This means your alerts and reminders are always spot on, helping you keep your hiring process on track and turbo-charged for both speed and accuracy.

#### In this article

  * Create a Harvest API key
  * Provide your Harvest API key to Sinta
  * Add your sub-domain and Harvest API Key
  * Use the Sinta integration with Greenhouse Recruiting
  * Additional resources



### Create a Harvest API key

To configure the Sinta integration, you’ll need to create a Harvest API key. 

Follow the steps in [this article](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/5888163769883) to create the key, and verify that the permissions below are selected when configuring the Sinta integration. Be sure to copy the API key as you will need to paste it in Sinta during the next step.

#### **Credentials**

In the _Create New Credential_ box, make the following selections:

  * **API Type:** Harvest
  * **Partner:** Sinta or Unlisted Vendor
  * **Description:** Sinta Harvest API Key



#### **Permissions**

Verify that the following permissions are selected for the Sinta integration: 

  * **Applications**
    * All permissions
  * **Candidates**
    * All permissions
  * **Jobs**
    * All permissions
  * **Scheduled Interviews**
    * All permissions
  * **Users**
    * All permissions



### Provide your Harvest API key to Sinta

In Sinta, head to the ‘Integrations’ section in the left-hand navigation bar

Select ‘Integrate’ to the right of Greenhouse

### Add your sub-domain and Harvest API Key

# Structured hiring: Interview planning

The Interview Planning step of a structured hiring process is typically combined with the [Scorecard Definitions](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360007247412) step. Together, they define the criteria being measured and the interviewing strategy to evaluate these attributes. In this article, we will cover the goals of the Interview Planning step and provide a video that will demonstrate how to develop this plan in Greenhouse. 

### Interview Planning Goals and Strategies

When devising the interview plan for the role, consider the answers to the three questions below:

**_What are you testing for_**? Use the 90 and 365 definitions of success discussed at the [Role kick-off meeting](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360007247092#%E2%80%9Cobjectives%E2%80%9D) and your Scorecard Definitions to define testable attributes. Boil down the list of attributes to mutually exclusive and collectively exhaustive need-to-haves

_**When should we test?**_ Aim to design a process that is complete but operationally efficient. Our suggestion is to test deal-breakers early on in the process and test attributes that require further explanation later.

**_Who should test it?_** Use the Interview Planning step to figure out the key stakeholders of the role and who should perform these interviews. 

By answering these questions (and others like it) you should essentially be achieving 4 main goals during the interview process:

  1. Uncover candidates' relevant experiences and capabilities
  2. Measure candidates against the same framework
  3. Deliver a consistent candidate experience
  4. Get participation from the right internal stakeholders 



**Previous** : [Scorecard Definitions ](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360007247412)

**Next** : [Interview Kit Creation](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360007490711)

# Sourcing by demographic report

**Permissions:** Job Admin and above who can see demographic reports

**Product tier:** Available for new subscription tiers (Core, Plus, and Pro)

Regularly collecting and tracking demographic data allows your organization to recognize where you are sourcing diverse candidates. The sourcing by demographic report aggregates candidate responses to [standard](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/7541739987355), [custom](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360004588971), or [EEOC](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/205278605) demographic questions asked across enabled job posts. 

To learn more about how you can create and enable custom demographic questions on job posts, [click here](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360004588971).

**Note:** All candidate demographic data is **anonymized** for compliance purposes and to reduce unconscious bias in the hiring process. Your organization's Greenhouse Recruiting users can only view anonymized candidate demographic data. In addition, Greenhouse Technical Support cannot access candidate demographic data unless given explicit consent by your organization.

#### In this article

  * Demographic
  * Sourcing strategy
  * Total candidates by source



**Note** : To best maintain the anonymity of applicants, responses that receive less than five responses will display`< 5`in the report results.  
The sourcing by demographic report results will only show jobs where you are a Job Admin who has permission to view demographic reports.

You can organize the report to display [U.S. standard](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/7541739987355), [custom demographic](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360004588971), or [EEOC](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/205278605) question set using the **Use data from** filter under **Filters and more**.

  * Job
  * Job status

  * Office
  * User
  * Hiring team role
  * Custom job field
  * Use data from EEOC, standard, or custom demographic questions
  * Date applied
  * Include migrated candidates



Click **Apply** after applying any filters.

**Note** : By default, the date applied for the report is set to the current year.

# Edit stages and interviews in bulk

**Permissions:** Site Admin who can bulk edit jobs

**Product tier:** Available for new subscription tiers (Core, Plus, and Pro)

Editing stages and interviews across multiple jobs in your organization is a great way to ensure that stages and interviews are aligned and can save plenty of time as your organization refines its hiring process. Before your organization decides to make any changes to stages and/or interviews in bulk, it is important to know that there is potential to overwrite a lot of the work your organization has done.

Exercise caution before editing stages and interviews in bulk. Some things to keep in mind as you move forward are:

The changes you make will not be saved until you have actually clicked the **Save** **Changes** button.

This is good news because it means you can click **Cancel** at any time if you decide to abandon the changes you have been working on. It could also be bad news if you navigate away from the page before clicking **Save Changes**.

Renaming stages and interviews is not the same as syncing them.

When you want to make sure that stages and interviews are added or synced to all selected jobs, be sure to use **Add to all** and **Sync interview kits**. You will be able to keep track of what has been added to all or synced during your session because those stages and interviews will be highlighted in green.

Below you can find additional resources to help you understand the bulk edit stages and interview features.

  * [Edit scorecards in bulk](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/201993099)

# Best practices: Template jobs

**Permissions:** Site Admin

**Product tier:** Available for new subscription tiers (Core, Plus, and Pro)

In Greenhouse Recruiting, template jobs include the key components for most of the jobs your organization will open. By reducing the manual need of entering repetitive information, such as desired candidate attributes or common interview questions, template jobs can help streamline your job creation process. 

Below, we'll cover some best practices for your team to consider when creating template jobs.

#### In this article

  * Using job templates
    * Job info
    * Job kickoff
    * Scorecard
    * Interview plan
    * Hiring team
    * Job post
  * Reporting
  * Additional resources



### Using job templates

The number of templates you create will depend on the size of your organization and the differences between pipelines per department. If each department or hiring manager has a unique component to each interview, it may be worth creating a template just for those instances.

Regardless of how many template jobs your organization creates, every template should include basic information captured for every job.

Using the components listed below, consider the following best practices when configuring your job template: 

#### Job info

**Internal job name** |  A name indicating that the job is a template job (you'll want to provide additional detail if you have multiple templates). **Example** : [TEMPLATE] Sales Engineer  
---|---  
**Set as a template** | Be sure to check the box to make the job a template so it is selectable in the future.  
**Department** |  Add the template job to the appropriate department.  
**Custom fields** |  Enter any information that you want to pre-populate.  
**Optional information for interviews** |  If you'd like to add more context regarding the template, or information about the format for other others to follow, enter it here.  
  
#### Job kickoff

A **job kickoff** is an essential step in the structured hiring process. During this time the recruiter and the hiring manager align on the goals of the hiring process and collaborate to define the scorecard and interview plan for the job.

[Learn more](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/4416516263707) about setting up the job kickoff form.

#### Scorecard

Add scorecard categories that are relevant for all jobs such as the following:

  * Requirements (e.g. "Fits our salary range" or "Based locally")
  * Company attributes
  * Qualifications
  * Department attributes



Add example characteristics to help your team brainstorm skills they should include.

**Example** :

#### Interview plan

[Define](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/204923599) a basic interview pipeline with stages that all jobs will most likely include (such as application review, phone screen, face-to-face, and offer).

Customize the interview kits for interviews that will happen across all jobs. Check out the recommendations below:

  * **Phone screen** – Add custom questions (questions the interviewer will ask) and select focus attributes for topics that are covered on all phone screens (such as tell me about yourself, desired salary range, and availability to begin work).
  * **Culture fit** – Add custom questions and select focus attributes for the traits that represent your company culture.
  * **Other interviews** – If you have any interviews with standard questions and criteria that you're evaluating, add them to the interview kit.



**Example** :

#### Hiring team

Grant [Job Admin](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360039518131) permission to all users who should have access to copy the template to create a new job.

#### Job post

**Description** | If there is consistent messaging about your company, benefits, or other information, include it in the description box.  
---|---  
**How candidates apply for this job** | Select _Optional_ or _Required_ on all basic information fields, and add custom questions that should appear on all applications.  
**Settings** |  Determine standard settings.  
  
Once you've configured all the steps in the job creation process for your template job, click **Finish**.

After you click Finish, the status of your template job depends on the following:

If your organization has an [approval process for new jobs](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360062257351), your template job is saved in _Draft_ status until it's approved.

If your organization does not have an approval process, your new job is automatically set to the status _Open_.

### Reporting

You can exclude template jobs when running [reports](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/203940239) on Greenhouse Recruiting. To exclude your template jobs when running a report, expand **Filters and more** at the top of the report, navigate to the **Job Filter** section, and click **Change Filter**. In the subsequent box, uncheck the box next to **Include template jobs**.

### Additional resources

  * [Creating and using template jobs](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360038222812)

# Deel integration

Greenhouse Recruiting’s integration with Deel allows users to streamline their hiring and onboarding process, and customize data mapping to ensure data accuracy between both platforms. 

In this article

  * Create a Harvest API key for the Deel integration
    * Credentials
    * Permissions
  * Create custom fields in Greenhouse Recruiting for the Deel integration
  * Retrieve Deel’s Endpoint URL and Secret Key to set up webhooks
  * Create a webhook
  * Finish setup in Deel
  * Use the Deel Integration with Greenhouse Recruiting
  * Additional resources



### Create a Harvest API key for the Deel integration

To configure the Greenhouse Recruiting / Deel integration, you'll need to create a Harvest API key.

Follow the steps in [this article](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/5888163769883) to create the key, and verify that the credentials and permissions below are selected when configuring the Deel integration.

#### Credentials

In the _Create New Credential_ box, make the following selections:

  * **API Type:** Harvest
  * **Partner:** Deel
  * **Description:** Deel Harvest API Key



#### Permissions

Verify that the following permissions are selected for the Deel integration:

**Applications**

  * **GET:** Retrieve Application



**Candidates**

  * **GET::** Retrieve Candidate



**Offers**

  * **GET:** Retrieve Offer



**Jobs**

  * **GET:** Retrieve Job



**Custom Fields**

  * **GET:** Custom fields



### Create custom fields in Greenhouse Recruiting for the Deel integration

To configure the Deel integration, you'll need to create some custom fields in Greenhouse Recruiting. Following the steps in [this article](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360024551831), create a custom offer field using the following criteria:

  * **Name:** Hire remotely using Deel?
  * **Description:** Select Deel contract type. It can be Fixed, Pay As You Go, Milestone, or Employee (via EOR)
  * **Type:** Single select
  * **Options:**  

    * Deel Fixed
    * Deel Milestone
    * Deel Pay As You Go Time
    * Deel Pay As You Go Milestone
    * Deel EOR



You can copy and paste the single select options and the field name from the Deel platform when setting up the connection to ensure the exact wording from the field name and single select field options are being utilized. 

### Retrieve Deel’s Endpoint URL and Secret Key to set up webhooks

Deel’s integration with Greenhouse relies on certain webhooks to be configured. For this to happen, you will need to get 2 key pieces of information:

  * Deel’s Endpoint URL
  * Deel’s Secret Key



This information can be retrieved from the Deel integrations directly in your client admin.

Click on integrations, and locate Greenhouse in the list.

Click **Connect.**

Enter the API key you have saved from Greenhouse Recruiting.

**Note:** Deel recommends securely storing your key as they do not store this key within their platform. 

Click **Connect** to get check the integration.

If the integration is successful, the **Deel URL** and **Secret Key** will display. Copy this information for the next section.

### Create a webhook

To integrate Deel with Greenhouse Recruiting, you'll need to create a webhook. Follow the steps in [this article](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/5888163727003) to create your webhook. Use the values listed below to configure the webhook:

  * **Name:** A descriptive name for the integration. Most customers choose "Deel Integration"
  * **When** : The time that the event will be sent to Deel. Select the following options for this integration:
    * Offer Deleted
    * Offer Updated
    * Offer Created
  * **Endpoint URL** : The Endpoint URL shown on the Deel instruction page in the previous section
  * **Secret Key** : The Secret Key shown in the Deel instruction page in the previous section



### Finish setup in Deel

With Deel’s endpoint URL and Secret Key copied into the 3 webhooks, and your Greenhouse user permissions enabled, you are ready to enable the Greenhouse/Deel integration.

Navigate back to Deel and click **Connect**.

Deel will verify that webhooks have been enabled. Once the connection is verified, you'll be able to access to the candidate list and customization settings for your integration.

### Use the Deel Integration with Greenhouse Recruiting

Once the integration is complete, the hiring process will be tidier by allowing you to push candidate data from Greenhouse into Deel for onboarding, improve coordination within hiring teams, and reduce data entry.

  * During the integration setup, the client can select a box in the job offer in Greenhouse saying 'Hire through Deel?
  * When a candidate has accepted the job offer, the client can 'Mark them as hired' in Greenhouse. This will push the candidate through to the Deel platform.
  * If a client has set up email notifications, then the linked email will let them know a candidate has been pushed to Deel.
  * They can go to I**ntegrations** > **Greenhouse** > **Candidates** and click **'Onboard [Employee] in Deel'.** This will bring them into the relevant contract creation flow with their pre-populated information available in the contract already based on the custom fields they have set up.
  * 


### Additional resources 

For additional help, click the **Information** or **Setup** tabs inside the Deel platform to see more configurations you can apply to your integration. The integration and support are free to Deel clients. Please contact customer service directly within the platform if you have any other questions.

You may also submit a Deel support ticket for troubleshooting assistance regarding the integration: [integrations@deel.com](mailto:integrations@deel.com).

# Set manager access to view or edit employee tasks

**Permissions:** Owners and Coordinators

**Product tier:** Available for Greenhouse Onboarding and Greenhouse Welcome tiers

Owners and Coordinators in Greenhouse Onboarding can grant managers one of the following permissions related to their employees' [onboarding tasks](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360000525691):

  * View-only permissions
  * Edit permissions



This gives you the freedom to determine whether managers in your organization can edit tasks assigned to their new hires and direct reports.

#### In this article

  * Assign managers access to view tasks
  * Assign managers access to edit tasks



### Assign managers access to view tasks

From your Greenhouse Onboarding homepage, navigate to **Settings** > **Data Flow** > **Permissions**.

On the  _Permissions_ page, scroll to the **Default Access** section.

Click **Edit** next to **Manager Additional Access**.

On the  _Manager Additional Access_ page, mark the **Can only view the tasks that have been assigned to direct reports**.

With this permission enabled, managers can view all assigned tasks in their direct reports' [employee profiles](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/13298081921179).

Managers with this permission won't be able to edit employee tasks that were created by another user.

**Note:** With view-only permissions enabled, managers can still edit any tasks they personally created for their direct reports. They won't have permission to edit other tasks, such as organization-wide tasks created by Owners or Coordinators.

### Assign managers access to edit tasks

From your Greenhouse Onboarding homepage, navigate to **Settings** > **Data Flow** > **Permissions**.

On the  _Permissions_ page, scroll to the **Default Access** section.

Click **Edit** next to **Manager Additional Access**.

On the  _Manager Additional Access_ page, mark the **Can view and edit the tasks that have been assigned to direct reports**.

With this permission enabled, managers can view and edit any onboarding tasks from their direct reports' [employee profiles](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/13298081921179).

# Connect Domo to Business Intelligence Connector

**Permissions:** –

**Product tier:** Available for Plus and Pro subscription tiers

Domo is a cloud-based business management suite that integrates with multiple data sources, including spreadsheets, databases, social media, and any existing cloud-based or on-premise software solution.  
If Domo is your preferred business intelligence tool, your organization can connect the tool using Redshift to pull all of your data and perform advanced data analytics with Business Intelligence Connector.

#### In this article

  * Business Intelligence Connector setup
  * Domo setup



### Business Intelligence Connector setup

To get started, check out the article [Enable Business Intelligence Connector](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/4405507275547) for instructions on setup in Greenhouse Recruiting.

**Note** : Greenhouse Recruiting has already allowlisted [Domo's IP addresses](https://knowledge.domo.com/Connect/Connecting_to_Data_with_Connectors/General_Guide_to_Connecting_with_Connectors/Whitelisting_IP_Addresses_for_Connectors) so your organization can easily access Redshift via Domo.

### Domo setup

After you've set up Business Intelligence Connector on Greenhouse Recruiting, you can configure Domo to pull data with Redshift.

Navigate to your Domo account and click the **+** in the upper right corner.

Select **Data** from the dropdown menu.

Click **Database** and then select **Amazon Redshift**.

Click **Get the Data**.

Enter the following information in the appropriate fields using the information presented when setting up Business Intelligence Connector on Greenhouse Recruiting:

**Field name** | **Input**  
---|---  
JDBC Driver | Select the latest driver.  
Host | Enter the host shown during [Business Intelligence Connector setup](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/4405507275547) in Greenhouse Recruiting.  
Database | Enter the database shown during [Business Intelligence Connector setup](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/4405507275547) in Greenhouse Recruiting.  
Username | Enter the username shown during [Business Intelligence Connector setup](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/4405507275547) in Greenhouse Recruiting.  
Password | Enter the password shown during [Business Intelligence Connector setup](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/4405507275547) in Greenhouse Recruiting.  
Certificate Format | Select _No Certificate - Please use Default Certificate_  
  
When finished, click **Connect**.

**Tip** : If you experience trouble with setup, check out solutions to some [common connection errors](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/4405638883867-Common-errors-when-connecting-to-Business-Intelligence-Connector).

If you experience any issues with Domo, contact Domo directly for assistance.

# Default Job Admin levels

**Permissions:** Site Admin, and Job Admin who can add users to their assigned jobs

**Product tier:** Available for new subscription tiers (Core, Plus, and Pro)

Job Admin levels are defined sets of permissions that are granted to Job Admin users on a per-job basis. Greenhouse Recruiting provides all organizations with two default Job Admin levels:

  * Job Admin: Standard
  * Job Admin: Private



With these default Job Admin levels, you can assign a Job Admin user a specific permission set based on the level of access and visibility the user needs on that particular job.

**Note:** Organizations with an Advanced or Pro subscription can customize Job Admin levels, including adding or removing permission stripes from the default Job Admin levels, deleting the default levels entirely, and/ or creating new Job Admin levels.

For more information about creating custom Job Admin levels, click [here](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/207813806). 

#### In this article:

Job Admin levels overview

Job Admin: Private versus Job Admin: Standard

Moving candidates between jobs

Audit users with specified Job Admin level

Additional resources

### Job Admin levels overview

Greenhouse Recruiting includes three base [user permission levels](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360039614171): Basic, Job Admin, and Site Admin.

Users belonging to the same permission level generally will be able to complete the same actions, although some variances might occur based on the [user-specific permissions](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360021050791) assigned to an individual. 

**Note:** To learn more on the configurable actions each user permission level can take for users on the Advanced or Pro subscription tier, click [here](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/210957383).

Users assigned to the Job Admin user permission level can only access jobs to which they are explicitly assigned.

When you assign a Job Admin user to a job, you also must choose which Job Admin level (Job Admin: Standard or Job Admin: Private) the user should have on that particular job, as the level permissions define what actions the user can take on the job based on their level of involvement in the job's hiring process. 

To learn more about the Job Admin user type and use cases for assigning this user type, click [here](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360039614171-User-Permission-Levels-Overview#h_8c5c89da-263f-4223-9c1f-dd05af9de815).

### Job Admin: Private versus Job Admin: Standard

Managing user access to private candidate information is tricky — you need to ensure your users have all the information they need to make an informed decision without over-sharing, which can be a tough line to walk. Moreover, blanket user permission levels can be problematic if Job Admins require access to private data for only certain jobs (e.g. a recruiter is involved with salary negotiations for one job, but you would not want them to see this information for a candidate on their own level or higher).

The Job Admin: Private level allows your organization to designate the jobs where a user can access private candidate data, without giving them that visibility on all jobs to which they are assigned.

On jobs where they are assigned the Job Admin: Private level, a user has the following permissions for all candidates on the job by default:

  * Can view and edit candidates and prospects
  * Can edit job info
  * Can delete jobs
  * Can create, edit, and delete job posts
  * Can change job posts status
  * Can edit forms
  * Can configure scorecard attributes
  * Can view candidate scorecards submitted by other users (always)
  * Can edit interview plans
  * Can edit hiring teams
  * Can advance candidates / prospects
  * Can email candidates / prospects
  * Can add and remove users to their assigned jobs
  * Can create, edit, and delete Stage Transition rules (Advanced and Expert subscriptions only)
  * Can view and edit private candidate and application fields
  * Can view and create private notes
  * Can view and edit private job fields and approve/request approval on jobs*
  * Can view and edit offers and approve/request approval on offers*



**Note:** The [job approval](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360025756071) and [offer approval](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360035625832) features are included in the Plus and Pro subscription tiers only. Users assigned to the Job Admin: Private level at organizations with an Core subscription tier are unable to request approvals for or approve jobs/offers.

On jobs where they are assigned to the Job Admin: Standard level, a user has the following permissions by default:

  * Can view and edit candidates and prospects
  * Can edit job info
  * Can delete jobs
  * Can create, edit, and delete job posts
  * Can change job posts status
  * Can edit forms
  * Can configure scorecard attributes
  * Can view candidate scorecards submitted by other users (always)
  * Can edit interview plans
  * Can edit hiring teams
  * Can advance candidates / prospects
  * Can reject candidates / prospects
  * Can email candidates / prospects
  * Can add and remove users to their assigned jobs
  * Can create, edit, and delete Stage Transition rules (Advanced and Expert subscriptions only)



All Job Admin users always have the following default permissions on each job where they're assigned any level of Job Admin permissions:

  * Can see the job's Dashboard, pipeline, and reports
  * Can see all candidates on the job
  * Can add and edit candidates and referrals
  * Can be assigned Hiring Team roles



### Moving candidates between jobs

A Job Admin will be able to move a candidate only to another job where they have permissions that are the **same level or lower** , but not higher (i.e. a Job Admin: Standard cannot move a candidate to a job where they are a Job Admin: Private).

For example, if a Job Admin: Standard was allowed to move a candidate to a job where they are a Job Admin: Private, the user would gain access to all the private information on the moved profile.

Regardless of whether the intent is malicious or accidental, allowing this action could show an employee a new hire in their role is making more money than they do themselves, or that they are at the bottom end of the salary band for the job. They could find out sensitive details about a new hire's health or family situation that were meant to be kept between the Hiring Team and the candidate, or even read a negative comment that an interviewer mentioned on their scorecard.

Because these incidents represent some of the worst-case scenarios for your users and Hiring Team, Greenhouse Recruiting imposes some restrictions on Job Admins moving candidates between jobs. 

### Audit users with specified Job Admin level

Go to the _Users_ page._(**Configure** icon  > **Users**)_

On the  _Users_ page, click **Export to Excel**. 

An  _.xlsx_ file containing all your users will be downloaded to your computer. Find the  _Job Admin: Private_ column to determine on how many jobs each user has been assigned to the Job Admin: Private level. 

### Additional resources

For more information about Job Admin levels, please see the following articles: 

  * [Job Admin levels and permission stripes](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360039518131)
  * [Create custom Job Admin level](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/207813806)
  * [Assign job-based permission](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360040181991)

# Equal Employment Opportunity Commission (EEOC) report

**Permissions:** Site Admin with the user-specific permission Can see EEOC and demographic reports

**Product tier:** Available for new subscription tiers (Core, Plus, and Pro)

The Equal Employment Opportunity Commission (EEOC) questionnaire is a set of federally-approved questions about race, gender, veteran status, and disability status.

Greenhouse Recruiting's EEOC report allows your organization to view an anonymized report of this data to see how many total and hired candidates fall into each category.

**Tip** : Need help troubleshooting this report? Check out [Troubleshoot a report](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/13710986142107).

#### In this article

  * Equal Employment Opportunity Commission (EEOC) report
  * EEOC report filters



### EEOC report

**Note** : It is not possible to associate responses to EEOC questions with individual candidate applications. All candidate demographic data is **anonymized** for compliance purposes and to reduce unconscious bias in the hiring process. Your organization's Greenhouse Recruiting users can only view anonymized candidate demographic data. In addition, Greenhouse Technical Support cannot access candidate demographic data unless given explicit consent by your organization.

To create an Equal Employment Opportunity Commission (EEOC) report, click **Reports** on your navigation bar and select **Essentials Library**. 

Click the **Reports** tab, scroll to the _Run Your Own Analysis_ section, and click **EEOC**.

**Note** : In order to generate an EEOC report, you must be a Site Admin with the [user-specific permission](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360021050791) Can see EEOC and demographic reports.

The EEOC report will generate.

The EEOC report will display the total number of applicants and the total number of hires per demographic. The following demographics are represented in the [EEOC questionnaire](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360031720371):

**Race**

  * American Indian or Alaskan Native
  * Asian
  * Black or African America
  * Hispanic or Latino
  * White
  * Native Hawaiian or Other Pacific Islander
  * Two or More Races
  * Decline to Self Identify



**Gender**

  * Male
  * Female
  * Decline to Self Identify



**Veteran Status**

  * I am not a protected veteran
  * I identify as one or more of the classifications of a protected veteran
  * I don't wish to answer



**Disability status**

  * Yes, I have a disability or have a history / record of having a disability
  * No, I don't have a disability or a history / record of having a disability
  * I don't wish to answer



**Note** : Applicant responses to EEOC questions will never tie directly back to candidates or applications _._

### EEOC report filters

Click **Filters and more** to apply filters to further refine your report.

The EEOC report can be filtered by the following:

  * Job
  * Job status
  * Department
  * Office
  * User
  * Hiring team role
  * Custom job field
  * Date applied
  * Stage
  * Rejection reason
  * Include migrated candidates



**Note** : When you filter the EEOC report by stage, the report will display all applicants who are currently in the current stage. Since this filter will only include candidates who completed a current state, the hired column will always display as zero, because they were moved into the offer process but never moved out of the hired stage.

Click **Apply** after applying any filters to your report.

**Note** : By default, the date applied filter is set to the current year.

# Application Review Nudge

**Permissions:** Site Admin

**Product tier:** Available for new subscription tiers (Core, Plus, and Pro)

In this article, we will cover the Application Review inclusion nudge that, when [activated](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360004974491), helps your organization maintain inclusive and diverse practices while reviewing applications. Working with our partners at Paradigm and our academic advisory board, Greenhouse has provided the copy for the behavioral nudge. 

**Nudges** are timely reminders that help modify behaviors by helping employees remember to engage in efforts to disrupt bias and promote inclusion. To learn more about bias-reducing behavior, [click here](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360004923452).

### Add Inclusion Nudge during Application Review

When this toggle is enabled, a non-intrusive nudge display to recruiters and hiring managers during application review. This prompt will encourage users to consider diversity in real-time when reviewing applications. 

When nudges are enabled, recruiters and hiring managers will see an additional panel when reviewing applications that reminds them to rely less on snap judgments and encourage the reviewer to consider the attributes outlined for the role.

### Report Builder

Report Builder is an additional reporting tool on Greenhouse Recruiting with increased flexibility to organize your data into easily digestible views. You can customize the metrics that you're tracking and organize the data across jobs, offices, departments, timeframes, or other filters within your reports.

You can also use customizable pipeline reports to track the historical and current health of your interview pipeline and explore your recruiting activity for each stage of the process.

Check out these resources for more information:

  * [Report Builder overview](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360000954692-Report-Builder-Overview)
  * [Create a custom report using Report Builder](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360050317592)
  * [Report Builder template guide](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360050783391)
  * [Report Builder filter guide](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360050783451)
  * [Report metrics](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360000955592-Glossary-Report-Metrics)



### Greenhouse Report Connector

With Greenhouse Report Connector, we've enhanced your ability to analyze essential reports data with a tool that combines the power and customization of a spreadsheet in a simple and seamless Google Sheets add-on.

With this integration, you can easily import Greenhouse Recruiting reports to Google Sheets, refresh your reports in real-time directly from your workbook, build and manipulate dashboards, charts, and graphs, and combine reports to perform complex analyses.

Since Report Connector uses existing reports in Greenhouse Recruiting, once you build and save a custom report, the data within remains live and up-to-date in Google Sheets.

Check out these resources for more information:

  * [Greenhouse Report Connector toolkit](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/115003728551-Toolkit-Greenhouse-Report-Connector)
  * [Set up Greenhouse Report Connector](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/115001875646-Set-Up-Greenhouse-Report-Connector-)



### Business Intelligence Connector

Business Intelligence Connector is a data analysis add-on to the Greenhouse Recruiting platform that allows you to retrieve your organization's data in a format that can be readily plugged into a business intelligence tool for advanced reporting and data analysis.

For customers with Business Intelligence Connector, Greenhouse Recruiting transfers your data to Amazon Redshift at the end of every day. Your organization can then connect your in-house business intelligence tool to Amazon Redshift to pull your data for analysis.

Check out these resources for more information:

  * [Business Intelligence Connector overview](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360017503272)
  * [Guide to Business Intelligence Connector](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360001892012-Guide-to-BI-Connector-Greenhouse-Analytics-Tables)
  * [Business Intelligence Connector data model](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360001905032-BI-Connector-Greenhouse-Analytics-Data-Model)



**Tip** : With Business Intelligence Connector, we recommend relying on an internal data analyst at your organization who is knowledgeable about business intelligence tools.
