# Set your interview availability

**Permissions:** —

**Product tier:** Available for new subscription tiers (Core, Plus, and Pro)

Scheduling a meeting can be challenging when juggling multiple busy calendars. Make it easier for your team to plan important hiring meetings, like interviews, by marking certain recurring events on your calendar as _Available_. This signals that those time slots are open for scheduling.

Give your team a holistic view of when you're available by [setting your working hours and time zone](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/28299067084315) as well.

To set up your availability, click your initials in the top right-hand corner of any page of Greenhouse.

Click **Interview availability** on the left side panel.

To set your availability, connect your calendar to Greenhouse if you haven’t done so already.

Use the primary email for the calendar you want to connect. Greenhouse can’t pull events from email aliases or subaddresses.

After connecting your calendar, you'll see a list of your recurring events displayed on the screen. By default, all events are marked as _Busy_.

When an event is set to _Busy,_ anyone scheduling an interview or other hiring meeting will see that time slot as unavailable.

If you have flexible events on your calendar, or events you can skip to attend an interview, check the box next to the event name. Then, click **Set Status** and select **Set as Available** from the menu.

Events marked as _Available_ create time slots your team can use to schedule interviews.

An event's status is automatically saved whenever you make a change.

**Note:** Greenhouse does not have access to write information to your connected calendar or calendar integration. Changing the status of events with this feature will not impact how they appear outside of Greenhouse.

# Welcome to the Jungle integration

Welcome To The Jungle curates job opportunities so candidates can find more sustainable career paths. Welcome To The Jungle explores exciting new ways of working, sharing first-hand advice, and building tools for companies who believe work can and should be different.

Greenhouse Recruiting’s integration with Welcome To The Jungle allows you to synchronize job offers between your ATS and your Welcome To The Jungle profile.

#### In this article

  * Obtain job board token
  * Create a Harvest API key for the Welcome to the Jungle integration

    * Permissions
  * Use the Welcome to the Jungle integration with Greenhouse Recruiting
  * Additional support



### Obtain job board token

You can find your Job Board token on the Job Board configuration page. _(**Configure** > **Dev Center** >**Configuring your job board** >**Your Board Token**)_

Copy the token and provide it to the Welcome To The Jungle team.

### Create a Harvest API key for the Welcome to the Jungle integration

To configure the Greenhouse Recruiting / Welcome to the Jungle integration, you'll need to create a Harvest API key.

Follow the steps in [this article](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/5888163769883) to create the key, and verify that the credentials and permissions below are selected when configuring the Welcome to the Jungle integration.

  * **API type:** Harvest
  * **Partner:** Welcome to the Jungle (optional)
  * **Description:** Welcome to the Jungle Harvest API key



#### Permissions

Verify that the following permissions are selected for the Welcome to the Jungle integration:

  * Job Posts

# Climb the hiring maturity curve by evaluating your hiring process

There’s a curve that companies climb as they improve their hiring process – we call it the Greenhouse Hiring Maturity curve. This curve answers the questions we hear most frequently in working with thousands of companies, including:

  * How are we doing?
  * What are we doing that’s better or worse than everyone else?
  * What could we do to get better?



There’s no easy way for talent teams to compare themselves to their peers, so they mostly have only a vague idea of how they can improve.

We’ve observed so many teams get stuck in the weeds doing the tactical work of making today’s hires. They’re so busy executing on urgent activities that they don’t have the time or capacity to create an effective process. Yet true, transformational success only comes when you take the time to step back and figure out how to build new, lasting capabilities.

To understand how to get better at hiring, it's worthwhile to see where your company currently exists on the Greenhouse Hiring Maturity curve. Even if you’re not actively hiring right now, becoming great at hiring will help you bring in top talent tomorrow and beyond so you can better achieve your business goals.

In this post, we'll walk through the four stages we see companies go through with their hiring process and the characteristics of each one:

First, a caveat: Placing a company into one of these Hiring Maturity curve stages is just the beginning. The goal here is for the entire organization to become better and more effective at hiring over time. Different parts of an organization typically mature at different rates. It’s also possible for an organization to be mature in one discipline, like candidate experience, while lagging in another, such as operational rigor. Keeping that in mind, here are general characteristics of the four different stages of the Hiring Maturity curve.

### Chaotic

If you’ve worked at a few different companies, you’ve probably come across a chaotic hiring situation. It is most easily identified by a mistrust between the recruiters and their business partners. The recruiters feel they aren’t getting the support they need and just get orders handed down to them from above. The hiring managers don’t have confidence in the recruiters, so they work around the system, frequently bringing in their own agencies and finding their own candidates. There’s usually a lot of the “blame game” going on as everyone points fingers at each other, and very little real or accurate data that speaks to the candidate pipeline or hiring performance. These organizations are the ones that pop up in horror stories on Glassdoor about terrible interviewing experiences. It’s important to recognize that this state of affairs has nothing to do with the size of the company, or even whether a company has an ATS. It’s all about how recruiting is viewed and supported within the business.

### Inconsistent

The usual way a company gets out of the Chaotic stage is by lucking into a really great individual recruiter. Through force of will, such an individual is able to bend the organization to work together and actually make a bunch of hires. These recruiters are heroes and almost always greatly appreciated by their internal partners. BUT, it’s a fragile situation. If – OK, when – that individual leaves the company (or even takes vacation), the whole thing collapses back into chaos. And when you try to scale, these folks inevitably get burned out. The truth is, there still isn’t a repeatable, predictable hiring process and the Inconsistent stage is a vulnerable place to live. It’s also the most common stage we see companies in when they are just starting to use Greenhouse. They’ve realized that the way forward isn’t through more heroes but through the application of a consistent process.

### Systematic

Companies often see the fragility of the Inconsistent stage and institute real processes to graduate to Systematic. In that stage, when new people join the company, they go through standard training in how to participate in the hiring process. The recruiting process is supported by technology that then generates high quality data that can be used to understand what’s actually going on. Another characteristic of the Systematic stage is that consistency develops across the organization as each team is held accountable for working in the same way rather than just inventing processes on their own.

### Strategic

Once a company reaches the Systematic state, for the first time, they can aspire to the Strategic level. That’s where recruiting becomes a competitive advantage for the company. There is a differentiated candidate experience, data is used to drive continuous improvement, structured hiring is used to drive consistent, unbiased decisions, and pools of high quality candidates (internal, referrals, silver medallists, etc.) are leveraged over widespread and random outreach. Another key transition is when the relationship between hiring managers and recruiters can be characterized by true partnership, with collaboration around role kickoffs, mutual accountability and a shared understanding of progress.

While only a small proportion of companies actually make it all the way to the Strategic stage, they are the ones who write the best blog posts and make everyone else feel terribly insecure. The key is to figure out where you are today and what will get you to the next logical steps, even if you still have a ways to go to get to the very top.

### Build a strong hiring process today to prepare for whatever tomorrow brings

Perhaps you’re in a phase of low or slow hiring, or hiring isn’t an immediate business priority. This time presents an opportunity to do the important foundational work to build a structured, repeatable and scalable hiring process. Also, you can focus on getting everyone in the company aligned on the importance of hiring. A low-volume hiring period is the perfect time to do the planning and developing work to prepare your business for an eventual hiring uptick.

By focusing on improving key areas of your hiring strategy now, you’ll be ready to hit the ground running when the situation changes. Using our Hiring Maturity methodology, you can improve your hiring performance and identify areas of opportunity, no matter what phase of hiring you’re in.

[Take the Hiring Maturity assessment](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/4404786088091) to see where you are on the curve – and how to move up.

* * *

_**  
This article was co-written by Jon Stross and Rosa Gandler.**_

_[Jon Stross](https://www.greenhouse.io/guidance/buying-an-ats-everything-you-need-to-know#entry:73012:url) is the President and Co-Founder of Greenhouse. At Greenhouse, Jon drives the product strategy and works closely with customers and partners to build a platform that improves recruiting performance. Before founding Greenhouse, Jon served as the GM for BabyCenter.com and was responsible for the global rollout of the business._

Now, she focuses on making the customer success team as strategic as possible with streamlined, efficient processes._

# ADP Workforce Now integration FAQ

**Permissions:** Owners

**Product tier:** Available for Greenhouse Onboarding

This article answers frequently asked questions related to the ADP Workforce Now integration with Greenhouse Onboarding.

#### In this article

  * Frequently asked questions
    * How does the integration work?
    * What information is required for the integration?
    * What additional information can I sync from Greenhouse Onboarding to ADP?
    * Can I set up additional fields to sync between the systems?
    * Can the integration manage documents?
    * Is the integration compatible with ADP e-verify or electronic I-9s?
    * How can I notify specific people when someone is added to ADP using the integration?
    * I have a custom template built to onboard employees in Workforce Now. Can the new hires from Greenhouse Onboarding be onboarded using this template?
    * I have employees based in two or more states. When new hires are synced, does the integration reflect their different locations in the State Worked In field?
    * Can the integration sync new hires based outside of the US?
    * Does the org structure in Greenhouse need to mirror the org structure in ADP?
    * What's the best way to test the integration before going live?
  * Additional resources



### Frequently asked questions

#### How does the integration work?

The Greenhouse Onboarding/ADP Workforce Now integration allows you to collect essential information from new hires in Greenhouse Onboarding and then create a new in-progress profile in ADP.

You can choose which employees are pushed over to ADP.

#### What information is required for the integration?

The following new hire information is required on their Greenhouse Onboarding profile in order to successfully create an ADP account:

  * Birthday
  * Legal Name
  * Start Date
  * Work Email



If you are using a custom template, we will send all supported fields over to ADP.

#### What additional information can I sync from Greenhouse Onboarding to ADP?

**A–D**

  * Business Fax
  * Business Landline
  * Business Mobile
  * Business Pager
  * Business Unit
  * Company Code
  * Compensation Type
  * Cost Center
  * Daily Pay Rate
  * Department



**E–H**

  * Eligibility Classification
  * Ethnicity
  * Federal Tax Filing Marital Status
  * File Number
  * FLSA Status
  * Gender
  * Government Id Type
  * Home Phone
  * Hourly Pay Rate



**J–L**

  * Job Title
  * Legal Address - Address Line 1
  * Legal Address - Address Line 2
  * Legal Address - Address Line 3
  * Legal Address - City
  * Legal Address - Country
  * Legal Address - Postal Code
  * Legal Address - State / Territory
  * Lived in State
  * Location



**M–P**

  * Marital Status
  * National Identifier
  * Onboarding Template
  * Pay Frequency
  * Personal Email
  * Personal Fax
  * Personal Landline
  * Personal Mobile
  * Personal Pager
  * Preferred First Name



**R–S**

  * Race
  * Reason for Hire
  * Salary
  * Social Security Number (SSN) / Government ID
  * State Tax Filing Marital Status
  * SUI/SDI Tax Code



**T–W**

  * Tax ID Type
  * Worked in State
  * Worked-In Country
  * Worker Category



#### Can I set up additional fields to sync between the systems?

Fields that are not listed above **cannot** be synced between the systems. This means the integration cannot sync fields such as emergency contact, manager, or other custom fields.

#### Can the integration manage documents?

No, the integration cannot manage documents.

#### Is the integration compatible with ADP e-verify or electronic I-9s?

Yes, the integration adds a pending hire, allowing you to launch the e-verify solution in ADP or an electronic I-9.

#### How can I notify specific people when someone is added to ADP using the integration?

The integration processes new hires using any template you wish to select. If you want to adjust email notifications on that template, please reach out to your ADP representative.

#### I have a custom template built to onboard employees in Workforce Now. Can the new hires from Greenhouse Onboarding be onboarded using this template?

Yes, new hires are processed by any template you wish to choose.

#### I have employees based in two or more states. When new hires are synced, does the integration reflect their different locations in the _State Worked In_ field?

Yes. The integration allows you to select the State Worked In for all new hires added to ADP.

#### Can the integration sync new hires based outside of the US?

Yes, the integration supports new hires outside the US, but only for customers using ADP Workforce Now in the US. If your ADP account is based outside the US, this integration is not compatible.

#### Does the org structure in Greenhouse need to mirror the org structure in ADP?

No, your org structure in Greenhouse Onboarding doesn't need to mirror the org structure in ADP.

Please reach out to your **Customer Success Manager (CSM)** for more information. 

#### What's the best way to test the integration before going live?

Please reach out to your **Customer Success Manager (CSM)** who can lead a testing session with you and your team.

### Additional resources

Learn more about integrating ADP Workforce Now with your Greenhouse Onboarding account:

  * [HRIS Link for ADP Workforce Now](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/34374327140763/)
  * [Sync data using ADP Workforce Now validation tables](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/212342466)

# Syft integration

Syft, a tool by Kitsune Studio, parses your candidate applications and job descriptions to automatically rank in order how well suited a candidate is for a role. In addition, it allows you to reduce bias in the recruiting process through candidate name redaction and allows use of fine-grained filter criteria to query your candidate data-set.

Syft's integration with Greenhouse Recruiting allows recruiters and hiring managers to:

  * Hire faster with more confidence
  * Reduce bias in the review process
  * Match candidates against other candidates, rather than a job description



#### In this article

  * Set up the Syft integration
    * Create a Harvest API key
    * Download the Syft Chrome extension
  * Use the Syft integration with Greenhouse Recruiting
    * Activate Syft
    * Upload candidates
    * Review candidates
  * Additional resources



### Set up the Syft integration

#### Create a Harvest API key

To configure the Syft integration, you’ll need to create a Harvest API key.

Follow the steps in [this article](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/5888163769883) to create the key, and verify that the permissions below are selected when configuring the Syft integration.

#### Credentials

In the _Create New Credential_ box, make the following selections:

  * **API Type:** Harvest
  * **Partner:** Syft or Unlisted Vendor
  * **Description:** Syft Harvest API Key



#### Permissions

Verify that the following permissions are selected for the Syft integration:

**Job Openings**

  * GET: List openings for a job



**Users**

  * Get: List User Job Permissions
  * Get: List Users
  * Get: Retrieve User
  * Get: List User Future Job Permissions



**Applications**

  * Get: Retrieve Application
  * Get: List Applications
  * Post: Move application



**Jobs**

  * Get: Get hiring team
  * Get: List Jobs
  * Get: Retrieve Job



**Candidates**

  * Get: List Candidates
  * Get: Retrieve Candidate



**Job Posts**

  * Get: Retrieve Job Post for Job
  * Get: List Job Posts for Job
  * Get: List Job Posts



**Job Stages**

  * Get: Retrieve Job Stage
  * Get: List Job Stages for Job
  * Get: List Job Stages



**Tags**

  * All Permissions



**User Roles**

  * Get: List User Roles



When finished, click **Save**.

Your Harvest API key for the Greenhouse Recruiting / Syft integration is created and configured. Copy the API key to provide to Syft in a later step.

#### Download the Syft Chrome extension

Syft is accessible through your Chrome-based browser via browser extension. Extensions are official packages that you can install security in your browser.

To utilize the Syft Integration, you must first [download the Syft Chrome extension](https://chrome.google.com/webstore/detail/syft/hipnmkhpcpbhaafhjhokiehhbmacaenm). 

Once installed, [Sign up](https://www.syft.cc/) or **Log in** to complete the integration setup. 

### Use the Syft integration with Greenhouse Recruiting

#### Activate Syft

Once you’ve installed the Syft extension, you will be automatically logged in to Syft. As a next step, you'll need to paste your created API key details into the extension to activate Syft.

To start, navigate to a job (**Jobs** > **select a job** > **Job Dashboard**). The Syft launcher will display in the bottom right hand corner of your screen.

**Note:** If the Syft launcher isn't shown, refresh your browser window.

Click the Syft launcher and you'll be prompted to enter your API key.

Enter your Harvest API key credentials here and then, click **Authorize**.

#### Upload candidates for analysis

To use the Syft integration, navigate to a job dashboard and then, click the **Syft launcher** located on the bottom right. Syft will then start uploading candidates and the job description for analysis.

When finished, the launcher will say _Syfting is complete_.

#### Review uploaded candidates

Next, to review qualified candidates, click the launcher to load the Syft interface.

Syft will have automatically parsed your job description, and filled in the filter criteria necessary to find candidates that match against your job.

**Note:** Updating any of the filter definitions will automatically update the candidate results list.

By default, candidate names are hidden to help reduce bias. To turn this feature off, toggle **Hide candidate name** at the top of the Syft interface. 

Use the _Find Candidates_ search to search for a specific candidate. To view a candidate in detail, click the**double-arrow**. This will load the candidate detail screen where you can see the breakdown of our ranking, as well as the candidates’ CV.

Once you’ve found a candidate you would like to move forward in the process, either click **Tag** in the main candidates search screen or scroll to the bottom of the candidate detail page and click **Tag in ATS**. 

Upon closure of the main Syft interface, Syft will automatically apply a _Syfted_ tag and update your candidate list accordingly.

You can then [filter for Syfted candidates](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360043184152) in Greenhouse Recruiting using the **Profile Details** >**Candidate tag** filters on the _Candidates_ tab. 

### Additional resources

For additional information or troubleshooting not covered here, reach out to [help@syft.cc](mailto:help@syft.cc).

# Offer forecast FAQ 

**Permissions:** Job Admin and above  
  
**Product tier:** Available for new subscription tiers (Core, Plus, and Pro)

Offer forecast uses machine learning from the recruiting process to make a prediction for each job about when an offer might be accepted and when a new hire's start date might begin. Use offer forecast to hone your recruiting pipeline, communicate timelines, and engage your team towards a goal.

We’ve collected answers to a few commonly asked questions about offer forecast.

#### In this article

  * How does offer forecast work?
  * Why does offer forecast still say it's generating a forecast?
  * How do I change the target start date?
  * How does offer forecast handle multiple openings on a job?
  * How do evergreen jobs work with offer forecast?
  * Who can see offer forecasts?
  * Can you reset an offer forecast?
  * What range is predicted for acceptance and start dates?
  * Can I deactivate offer forecast?
  * Can I report on offer forecast predictions?
  * Why doesn't offer forecast provide a start date prediction for organizations with accounts in the European Union?



#### How does offer forecast work?

Offer forecast is powered by a machine learning model called LightGBM or Light Gradient Boosting Machine. This model is trained on input variables from filled jobs to derive an output called time to hire. Some of the data used to train the model include the following:

  * Number of candidates in each milestone
  * Steps in the hiring plan
  * Months an organization has been using Greenhouse Recruiting
  * Days a job has been open
  * Days since a job was last updated
  * Offer status, if any
  * Average hiring speed
  * Time to hire from previous jobs
  * Lots of other things



Learn more about [how it works](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360002797252).

#### Why does offer forecast still say it's generating a forecast?

Because there hasn't been enough activity in the recruiting process for the forecast to generate.

#### How do I change the target start date?

On the offer forecast widget, click **Set target date** to choose a target start date for your new hire. You can also set a target start date on the opening under **Job** **Setup** > **Job** **Info**.

**Note** : Only Job Admins [who can edit job info ](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360020855632)can set target start dates.

#### How does offer forecast handle multiple openings on a job?

Offer forecast will share a forecast for one opening at a time. When jobs have multiple openings, offer forecast shares a forecast for the opening with the soonest target start date. When this opening is closed or filled, the forecast will move to the next open opening with the soonest target start date.

#### How do evergreen jobs work with offer forecast?

Evergreen jobs, or pipeline jobs, are jobs that temporarily hold candidates until they’re moved to a hiring job. When you transfer a candidate to another job, the forecast will not transfer with them.

#### Who can see offer forecasts?

A Job Admin assigned to a job will see offer forecasts. However, only Job Admins who can edit job info will be able to [set the target start date](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/19573002102299). 

#### Can you reset an offer forecast?

You can't.

#### What range is predicted for acceptance and start dates?

Offer forecast will share a prediction with a static range from 2 to 6 weeks.

**Note** : The start date prediction is not available for organizations with accounts in Silo 101. [Learn](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/20536912019867)[ m](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/20536912019867)[ore](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/20536912019867).

#### Can I deactivate offer forecast?

It isn’t possible to deactivate offer forecast.

#### Can I report on offer forecast predictions?

We don't store historical predictions over time in Greenhouse Recruiting. As a result, offer forecast data doesn’t appear in any reports. 

#### Why doesn't offer forecast provide a start date prediction for organizations with accounts in the European Union?

Offer forecast is based on US standards, which typically involve a fixed 2-week lead time from the moment an employee accepts a role to the actual start date. However, in the EU, the lead time for employee onboarding is often variable and can vary significantly.

Start date predictions in offer forecast are designed to be most effective in scenarios where a fixed 2-week lead time is the norm, making it less suitable for regions with diverse lead time requirements.

The same functionality as the US version is offered, except the widget will not include a start date prediction. The widget will only include a predicted offer acceptance date and target start date.

[Learn more on using offer forecast in the EU](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/20536912019867). 

**Learn more**

[Offer forecast overview](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/115005312666)

[How offer forecast works](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360002797252)

[Use offer forecast](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/18710896459163)

# IP addresses for email delivery

An essential step to ensuring your internal users receive automated emails, @mentions, and other messages from Greenhouse Recruiting is by allowlisting our email providers' dedicated IP addresses.

When the IP addresses are allowlisted, your internal email server will know the emails are safe to route to your internal users, which will reduce the likelihood of your [internal emails being routed to the Spam folder](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/13639450575899).

In this article, we'll cover which IP addresses should be added to your organization's allowlist to support successful email delivery.

#### In this article

  * IP address list
  * Frequently asked questions



### IP address list

Greenhouse Recruiting's mail provider, Mailgun, sends emails from the IP addresses listed below. Add them to your organization's allowlist to ensure successful mail delivery. 

  * 69.72.40.93
  * 69.72.40.94
  * 69.72.40.95
  * 69.72.40.96
  * 69.72.40.97
  * 69.72.40.98
  * 69.72.40.99
  * 69.72.47.205
  * 185.250.239.190
  * 185.250.239.148
  * 185.250.239.168
  * 198.244.59.30
  * 198.244.59.33
  * 198.244.59.35



**Fallback IP addresses**

In rare cases of service disruption, Mailgun may send Greenhouse Recruiting emails from a different set of IP addresses. This list is a dedicated set of IP addresses that are used across all Mailgun customers in exceptional circumstances (such as a server outage). You can add the following IP addresses to your allowlist to ensure email delivery in these circumstances.

  * 198.61.254.21
  * 209.61.151.249
  * 209.61.151.251
  * 209.61.151.236



### Frequently asked questions

#### How do we allowlist IP addresses?

Your IT Team will manage this for you. Please forward this article to your IT team for assistance.

#### Why does Greenhouse require so many IP addresses to be allowlisted?

Greenhouse maintains a list of IP addresses that we use actively to send email, as well as some additional IP addresses that we have on reserve in case we ever need to move traffic to a new IP address on short notice. We recommend you allowlist the entire list of IP addresses so your team will be prepared if we ever need to shift traffic between IP addresses. Additionally, we recommend allowlisting both sets of the IP addresses above, as we will continue to use both sets of IP addresses until the new set of IP addresses are warmed up, and the original IP addresses can be deprecated.

#### Are there any security concerns with allowlisting these IP addresses?

These IP addresses are all dedicated to Greenhouse’s Mailgun account, meaning no other platforms outside of Greenhouse Recruiting can use these IP addresses to send email.

As these IP addresses belong to Greenhouse’s Mailgun instance, allowlisting these IP addresses will not affect emails to your internal users from any other Mailgun customer or service, other than Greenhouse. Additionally, allowlisting these IP addresses will not grant Greenhouse or any other Mailgun customers visibility into your company email inboxes.

# One-stage versus two-stage job approvals

**Permissions:** Site Admins who can create and override default approval flows

**Product tier:** Available for new subscription tiers (Core, Plus, and Pro)

Job approvals are beneficial for organizations that want more control and oversight before opening a job for candidate recruiting. Once an approval flow is configured, initially opening a job will set it in **Draft** mode and requires authorization from selected users before they can be **Opened** for candidate recruitment.

When you [set up a new job approval flow](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360062257351) in Greenhouse Recruiting, you can choose between one-stage and two-stage approval processes. See the sections below for more information on the specific workflows. 

In this article

One-stage job approvals

Two-stage job approvals

### One-stage job approvals

With one-stage job approvals, any newly created job will open as a **Draft** instead of being immediately available for candidate recruitment. Users configured to be job approvers will be notified that the new job is pending approval.

* Number of approvers is dependent on how approvals are configured

**Note** : There can be multiple approvers assigned to an approval flow and can be configured sequentially or non-sequentially in. Additionally, approvers can be assigned by office or department. 

Once the final necessary user approves the job, it will be opened for candidate recruitment with no other limitations on what can be done to it. Candidates can be hired immediately and any changes to Department, Openings, Custom Fields, etc. will **never** trigger re-approval.

[Click here](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360025478652) for more information on how to configure one-stage job approvals for your organization.

### Two-stage job approvals

With a two-stage job approval flow enabled, any newly created job will open as a **Draft** instead of being immediately available for candidate recruitment. Once the final user approves the job, it will be opened for candidate recruitment as**Open (Approval Pending)**. However, unlike a one-stage job approval, a two-stage job approval requires a second approval process to generate an offer for a candidate.

* Number of approvers is dependent on how approvals are configured

**Note:** There can be multiple approvers assigned to an approval flow and can be configured sequentially or non-sequentially. Additionally, approvers can be assigned by office or department. 

Any major changes to the job after the second stage approval is received will restart the second stage of approvals from the beginning.

Updates to **Department** , **Openings** , **Custom Fields** , and other fields must be made on the job’s **Approvals** tab and will send a new approval email to the second-stage approvers. This process ensures that the job's details are always accurate and aligned throughout your organization.

**Note:** Organizations who are serious about using openings as the system of record should always set up two-stage job approvals for their roles.

[Click here](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360025776391) for more information on how to configure two-stage job approvals for your organization.

# Creating and using template jobs

**Permissions:** Site Admin

**Product tier:** Available for new subscription tiers (Core, Plus, and Pro)

A template job is a template that includes the key components for most of the jobs your organization will open. Subsequently, members of your team can decide to use the template as a starting point when creating new job or be [limited to only using templates](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360039093852) when creating a new job.

In this article, we will cover how to create a new template job from the new job creation flow. 

_**Note** : [Click here](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360006876232) for more information on how to best configure and organize template jobs for your organization._

#### In this article

Creating a template job

Marking an existing job as a template job

### Creating a template job

Click the **Add** button at the top of the page and select **Create a Job** from the dropdown menu.

From the subsequent page, select either **Copy an Existing Job** , **Sample Job,** or **Blank Job**.

From the **Job Info** page of the job setup flow, click the checkbox next to **Set as a Template**. 

Fill in the _Internal Job Name_ field, as this is required to create both a template and a job. Any other required fields in the template's details and openings may be left blank for the template job. However, when a job is created from this template, these fields will become required and must be filled in for that job.

When finished, proceed to create the new job as normal. 

After the job is created, a **Template Job** tag will appear next to the job name.

### Marking an existing job as a template job

To mark an existing job as a template job, open the **Job Info** tab in the job. (**Jobs** > Select job from list > **Job Setup** > **Job Info**)

Click the **Template Job** toggle in the top right corner of the**Job Info** page.

When a job is marked as a template job, a label will display next to the job name.

_**Note** : Template jobs and confidential jobs are mutually exclusive. You cannot mark a confidential job as a template job._

# ERIN integration

ERIN App is a smart employee referral software that allows employees to easily source the highest quality candidates for their employers as quickly as possible. Referrals are a great way for hiring teams to increase the number of applicants, hire more quickly, and increase the tenure of those hires. Referrals are also the ideal way to reduce recruitment costs by turning your employees into an insourced recruiting team.

Greenhouse Recruiting's integration with ERIN allows jobs to be cloned automatically from Greenhouse Recruiting upon creation and closed upon expiration of the position. In this article, we will cover how to:

#### In this article

  * Obtain the job board URL in Greenhouse Recruiting
  * Generate a job board API key
  * Use the ERIN integration with Greenhouse Recruiting



### Obtain the job board URL in Greenhouse Recruiting

To make your open jobs available to ERIN, you'll need to send your job board URL.

You can find your Job Board URL by navigating to the Job Board settings. (**Configure** **Job Boards Posts** **Ellipsis** icon next to job board **Edit Board Settings**) and scroll to the URL field.

Once you have this URL, send it to ERIN.

[Click here](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/5888210160155) for a more detailed walkthrough of locating your job board URL.

### Generate a job board API key

Next, you'll need to create a Job Board API key for ERIN.

Follow the steps in [this article](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/5888210160155) and use the information below when creating your API key:

  * **API type:** Job Board
  * **Description:**_ERIN Job Board API key_



### Use the ERIN integration with Greenhouse Recruiting

ERIN will handle the Greenhouse Recruiting / ERIN integration once the Job Board API key has been generated and submitted to the ERIN team. Users can view, update, and manage the integration settings at the bottom of the _Settings_ page in ERIN (app.erinapp.com/settings), but it is recommended the ERIN support team handles the management of the integration.

With the Greenhouse Recruiting / ERIN integration, you can post open jobs to ERIN and export candidates to Greenhouse Recruiting.

# Send campaign pool emails on behalf of an email alias

**Permissions:** Site Admin who can edit another user's advanced permissions (to turn on the feature), Job Admin and above with a Sourcing Automation seat (to send campaign pool emails on behalf of an email alias)

**Product tier:** Available for new subscription tiers (Core, Plus, and Pro)

With Greenhouse Sourcing Automation, you can send step emails for your campaign pools on behalf of an email alias. This helps your organization improve recruiting efficiency and save Sourcing Automation seats, as recruiters can share one email alias to send and receive prospect emails.

Using email aliases in your campaign pools can also increase response rates from prospects, who may respond more to emails coming from a hiring manager, executive, or other recognizable person.

**Note:** Sending on behalf of email aliases is available for Google-based email accounts only. Email aliases from other email service providers are not supported at this time.

#### In this article

  * Allow users to send campaign steps with an email alias
  * Configure an email alias
    * Email alias requirements
    * Create an email alias in Gmail
    * Set up reply tracking
  * Use an email alias to send campaign pool emails
  * Additional resources



### Allow users to send campaign steps with an email alias

A Sourcing Automation admin must enable all users in your organization to send campaign emails through an email alias.

Navigate to **Configure** > **Sourcing Automation**.

On the _Sourcing Automation_ page, scroll to _General settings_.

Mark the checkbox to **Allow Gmail aliases when sending a campaign step**.

Once this permission is turned on, all users with a Sourcing Automation seat will have the option to send campaign emails on behalf of an email alias when [creating campaign pool steps](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/5045604930843).

### Configure an email alias

#### Email alias requirements

Before you can send campaign pool emails on behalf of an email alias, your email alias must meet the following requirements:

  * Uses Gmail: Google is the only supported email service provider for sending Sourcing Automation emails on behalf of an email alias.
  * Does not have a separate inbox: Replies from prospects to your email alias should go into your primary email address instead of a separate inbox. Replies to prospect messages should be set to send on behalf of your email alias. These settings allow Sourcing Automation to track replies properly.



Follow the steps outlined below to make sure your email alias meets these requirements.

**Note:** Email aliases that use a separate inbox and require password verification are not supported in Sourcing Automation.

#### Create an email alias in Gmail

First, create an email alias in Gmail. Sourcing Automation only supports sending on behalf of Gmail aliases at this time.

**Step 1**

Ask your Google Workspace admin to create an email alias under your existing Gmail account.

**Note:** Send this [Google resource](https://support.google.com/a/answer/33327?hl=en) to your Google Workspace admin if they need help creating Gmail aliases for other users.

**Step 2**

Add the alias created by your Google Workspace admin to your existing Gmail account. Follow the steps in this [Google resource](https://support.google.com/mail/answer/22370) to learn how to add your new alias.

#### Set up reply tracking in Gmail

Once you've added your new email alias, set up reply tracking in Gmail. This allows you to send replies to prospects through your new email alias and allows Sourcing Automation to track prospect replies correctly.

In Gmail, navigate to **Settings** >**See all settings** , then click the **Accounts** tab.

Scroll to the **Send mail as:** section of the  _Accounts_ page.

Select the option to **Reply from the same address the message was sent to**.

### Use an email alias to send campaign pool steps

Once you've met the above requirements and your Sourcing Automation admin has allowed the use of email aliases, you can start sending campaign step emails on behalf of an email alias.

When you [create or edit a campaign step](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/5045604930843), use the **From** dropdown to select your email alias as the step sender.

### Additional resources

  * [Send on behalf of permission management](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/13830810020763)
  * [Create and manage campaign pools](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/5045604930843)
  * [Email authentication for Sourcing Automation](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/5131512808091)

# Trace integration

Trace Headcount is the workforce planning platform of choice for some of the best-run companies. Trace helps finance, talent, HR, and management collaborate on headcount planning and related workflows. Trace allows businesses to operate more efficiently by eliminating busy-work and keeping everyone aligned.

Trace’s workforce planning platform provides the following core capabilities: headcount planning, position management, org charts & workforce views, headcount analytics, budget management, and recruiting ops automation.

Trace’s integration with Greenhouse Recruiting enables the following recruiting automation:

  * Streamline the creation of jobs in Trace. Auto-populate job fields from approved and open positions in Trace, then sync to create a new Job. Reduce manual data-entry and improve accuracy. Manage the job in Greenhouse from there. 
  * Automate the creation of job openings in Trace. Associate approved and open positions in Trace with existing Jobs synced from Greenhouse, then sync to create a new opening. Reduce manual data-entry and improve accuracy. Manage the opening in Greenhouse from there.
  * Provide visibility and automate headcount reconciliations. Greenhouse sends Trace information such as opening status and candidate name. Trace gives teams visibility into hiring performance and automatically fills open positions with new employees. 



#### In this article

  * Enable the Greenhouse Recruiting / Trace integration
    * Create a Harvest API key for the Trace integration
    * Configure an integration user
    * Retrieve the integration user ID
    * Evaluate custom fields in Greenhouse Recruiting
    * Provide your API key credentials to Trace
  * Use the Trace integration with Greenhouse Recruiting
  * Additional resources



### Enable the Greenhouse Recruiting / Trace integration 

#### Create a Harvest API key for the Trace integration

To configure the Greenhouse Recruiting / Trace integration, you’ll need to create a Harvest API key.

Follow the steps in [this article](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/5888163769883) to create the key, and verify that the permissions below are selected when configuring the Trace integration.

#### Credentials

In the _Create New Credential_ box, make the following selections:

  * **API Type:** Harvest
  * **Partner:** Trace or Unlisted Vendor
  * **Description:** Trace Harvest API Key



#### Permissions

Verify that the following permissions are selected for the Trace integration:

**Applications**

  * GET: List Applications



**Candidates**

  * GET: List Candidates



**Users**

  * GET: List Users



**Departments**

  * GET: List Departments



**Jobs**

  * GET: List Jobs
  * PATCH: Update Job
  * POST: Create a new job
  * POST: Add hiring team member



**Job Openings**

  * GET: List Openings For a Job
  * POST: Create openings
  * PATCH: Edit openings



**Offices**

  * GET: List Offices



**Custom Fields**

  * GET: Get custom fields



**Custom Fields Options**

  * GET: Custom field options



**Close Reasons**

  * GET:Get close reasons



When finished, click **Save**.

Your Harvest API key for the Greenhouse Recruiting / Trace integration is created and configured.

Copy the Harvest API key to provide to Trace in the last step.

#### Configure an integration user in Greenhouse Recruiting

**Note** : Prior to completing setup, Trace recommends creating an integration system user (ISU) to associate with partner updates. Rather than requiring a specific user at your organization to authenticate an integration, which could cause downstream errors if the person loses permissions or cannot access Greenhouse Recruiting, an ISU allows you to create a solid infrastructure for your organization's integration needs. [Learn more](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/4405511253659).

In addition to a Harvest API key, the Trace integration requires a _Greenhouse User ID_ to create jobs and openings.

**Option 1**(_recommended_): **Create a new integration system user (ISU)**

To best track activities performed by the integration, it is recommended that you create a new user within Greenhouse Recruiting. Follow the steps in [this Greenhouse article](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360027077811-Add-new-users) to create the user.

  * The user’s email can be anything; consider **trace-integrations@** for easy identification.
  * The interviewer tags should be left blank.
  * For the account permissions, assign the **Site Admin** permission level and select the following [user-specific permissions](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360021113491): 
    * _Create and view private candidates_
    * _See private notes, salary info, manage offers, request approval, and approve jobs/offers_



**Option 2: Use a generic user**

Alternatively, a generic user, such as **recruiting@** , can be used for your Trace integration. You should refrain from using a specific person, such as sally@, to avoid the integration breaking after someone leaves the organization.

To reuse an existing user, you must ensure they have the same permissions mentioned in Option 1. Follow the steps in [this Greenhouse article](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360020849292-Add-user-specific-permissions) to manage a user’s permissions.

  * For the account permissions, assign the **Site Admin** permission level and select the following [user-specific permissions](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360021113491): 
    * _Create and view private candidates_
    * _See private notes, salary info, manage offers, request approval, and approve jobs/offers_



#### Retrieve the integration user ID

After configuring your integration user for the Trace / Greenhouse Recruiting integration, you'll need to [retrieve the user ID](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/10765948752027) for the user account. 

Click the **Configure** icon  on your navigation bar and then, click the **Users** tab from the left-hand panel.

Click **Export to Excel**.

A spreadsheet will be downloaded to your computer. Open the Excel file and locate the user ID in the **User ID** column.

#### Evaluate custom fields in Greenhouse Recruiting

When Trace creates a [job and/or job opening](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/4402057774747) within Greenhouse Recruiting, you can automatically use data that has been reviewed and approved within Trace. Created [custom fields](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/10978274576667) in Greenhouse are mapped to their related fields within Trace to do this effectively.

At a minimum, the custom fields need to be added as either a [custom job field](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/202609855) or a [custom opening field](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360036370951). The more fields mapped between Trace and Greenhouse Recruiting, the less manual work will be required.

To view or add custom fields, click the **Configure** icon on your navigation bar, then click **Custom Options**.

For the Trace integration, select either **Jobs** or **Openings** from the listed options to add or review the created fields. 

When reviewing your custom fields, you'll see the configured _Field type_ , _Options_ , _Immutable field key_ and other details that will sync within Trace.

**Save** when finished. 

#### Provide your API key credentials to Trace

After creating your API key, integration user, and custom fields to be mapped, you will be ready to connect your created credentials within Trace to begin syncing.

Provide the following details to Trace:

  * **Harvest API Key**(shared securely; here is [a tool to help](https://share.doppler.com/))
  * **Greenhouse User****ID**



Trace will work with you to use the additional information regarding the Greenhouse Recruiting [custom fields](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/10978274576667) and will complete the integration setup. 

### Use the Trace integration with Greenhouse Recruiting

Once the Trace / Greenhouse Recruiting integration is enabled, you can plan, request, and automate new job creation in Trace. Once a position is approved for recruiting, users can automate the Job creation process.

  * On the Trace Position, select **Create a new Greenhouse job**
  * The Job form will pre-populate with accurate data and allow users to input other required or custom fields from Greenhouse Recruiting
  * Once saved, select **Sync to ATS** to send the new Job to Greenhouse



**Note** : Creating a Job from Trace will also create an [opening](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/4402057774747) for that job in Greenhouse Recruiting. The Trace Position will be associated with the Job and Opening.

When approved Positions in Trace are opened for Jobs that already exist in Greenhouse, you can associate the Position with a Job and automate the Opening creation process.

  * Identify the position from the Trace Headcount Table or Position form.
  * Select the **Greenhouse Job** on the Position.
  * Once saved, select **“Sync to ATS”** to create a new Opening for the Job in Greenhouse Recruiting.



Once a Position has been associated with an Opening, it will sync the **Opening Status** to give visibility to hiring progress.

When the Opening has been filled, Trace will receive the candidate's name and mark the position as filled. Candidates will sync to Trace from the HR system, and will be automatically assigned as an employee to their Position.

### Additional resources

If you’d like to learn more about Trace, visit their website at [www.tracehq.com](http://www.tracehq.com). If you’d like to visit the help center for Trace’s integration with Greenhouse, see the [Integrations](https://help.tracehq.com/hc/en-us/sections/360012972811-Integrations) section of the [Trace Support](https://help.tracehq.com/hc/en-us) center.

For additional information not covered here, please reach out to:

Katherine Mitchell

Customer Success Lead, Trace

[katherine@tracehq.com](mailto:katherine@tracehq.com)

If you’d like to learn more or see a demo of Trace Headcount, please reach out to:

Matt Gonzalez

# Interview kit overview

**Permissions:** Job Admin and above

**Product tier:** Available for new subscription tiers (Core, Plus, and Pro)

The interview kit provides your interviewers with everything they need to successfully prepare for and conduct an interview with a candidate. A well-composed interview kit will contain everything an interviewer needs to execute a focused, purposeful interview, and provide the hiring team with the information that they can use to make a decision about whether or not to advance the candidate.

#### In this article

  * Interview kit overview
  * Create an interview kit for a new job
  * Access an interview kit for an existing job
  * Edit an interview kit  

    * Add focus attributes
    * Add interview prep
    * Add interview questions



### Interview kit overview

An interview kit allows your interviewers to remain consistent across candidate interviews and provides a consistent framework for assessing candidates. By having this consistency, your hiring team will collect better data for making hiring decisions at the end of the process. Likewise, the interview kit alleviates the stress imposed on interviewers to ask questions on the spot. Since the interview kit provides the questions that need to be asked, interviewers can focus on evaluating the responses instead of coming up with the next question.

To learn more about interview kit best practices, please [click here](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360007490711-Structured-Hiring-Interview-Kit-Creation).

### Create an interview kit for a new job

_**Note** : In the following section, users with **Job Admin** level permissions will need the additional user-specific permission **Can create new jobs and request job approvals**. _

To access the interview kit for a new job, navigate to the **Add** icon in the upper right-hand corner and select **Create a Job** from the dropdown menu.

_**Note** : Configuring interview kits during the new job creation process requires that your organization has **Interview Plan** enabled as a step in the [job setup flow](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/204923599-Configure-Job-Setup-Flow)._

Follow the on-screen instructions to create a new job and provide job details. When finished, click **Create Job & Continue**.

[Configure your scorecard](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/115002194863) and click**Next** to reach the _Interview Plan_ configuration __ page.

Depending on whether you are working from a sample template, blank template, or a [custom job template](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360006876232-Best-Practices-Template-Job), the _Interview Plan_ configuration page may or may not have pre-populated stages in your interview pipeline.

To access the interview kit for a specific interview, hover over the interview kit and click either the **Edit** icon  to make changes, or the **Delete** icon  to remove the interview kit from the interview plan entirely.

Edit the interview kit as needed.

### Access an interview kit for an existing job

If your organization's hiring team needs to edit an interview kit for an existing job, navigate to the job profile (**All Jobs** >**Job Name**) and click **Job Setup** from the job page navigation bar. From the  _Job Setup_ page, navigate to **Interview Plan** on the left-hand panel.

From the _Interview Plan_ page, hover over the interview kit you wish to edit and click the **Edit** icon .

Edit the interview kit as needed.

### Edit an interview kit

An interview kit is comprised of three major elements:

  * Focus attributes
  * Interview questions
  * Interview prep



In this section, we will briefly cover the purpose of each element. When you have finished editing the interview kit, click **Save** at the bottom of the page.

#### Add focus attributes

The focus attributes feature allows your organization to select and emphasize which attributes interviewers should focus on during their respective interviews. This helps direct interviewers to focus specifically on certain traits and alleviates interviewer pressure to cover all listed attributes. Interviewers will see the Interview Kit's selected focus attributes grouped at the top of their scorecard. All other Scorecard Attributes for the Interview Kit will be listed below the _Focus Attributes_ section. 

To make a scorecard attribute a focus attribute, place a check beside the name of the attribute. For more information about focus attributes, [click here](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360018399451-Focus-Attributes-on-Scorecards#edit%C2%A0).

#### Add interview questions 

[Interview questions](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/115002276366) allow your organization to guide the actual interview by suggesting or requiring certain questions to be asked. Use the window to list out questions you would like the interviewer to ask during the interview. The questions will be listed for the interviewer.

#### Add interview prep 

The interview prep panel allows you to provide context, directions, and suggestions for interviewers that they can reference during the interview. Use the provided space to communicate any pertinent information or general guidelines you want your interviewers to be aware of. Additionally, provide an estimated interview time so interviewers can budget appropriately.

_**Note:** Tagging an attribute to focus on automatically marks that attribute as a focus attribute for the interview._

# Set up Entra Active Directory (Entra AD) with Greenhouse Onboarding

**Permissions:** Owners

**Product tier:** Available for Greenhouse Onboarding and Greenhouse Welcome subscription tiers

Entra Active Directory (Entra AD) is Microsoft’s cloud-based identity and access management service. You can set up single sign-on (SSO) with Entra AD to authenticate users logging in to Greenhouse Onboarding and Greenhouse Welcome.

For information on setting up Entra AD SSO for Greenhouse Recruiting, [click here](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360004745971).

#### In this article

  * Enter your SSO credentials in Greenhouse Onboarding
  * Connect Greenhouse Onboarding in your Entra AD platform
    * Create a new Enterprise application in Entra AD
    * Edit SAML configuration, user attributes, & claims in Entra AD
    * Assign users to Greenhouse Onboarding in Entra AD



### Enter your SSO credentials in Greenhouse Onboarding

Before you can connect Greenhouse Onboarding with Entra AD, you'll need to provide the following identity provider details:

  * Single Sign-On URL
  * IdP Certificate Fingerprint (in SHA1 format)
  * Single Logout URL (optional)



**Note:** Your Single Log-out (SLO) URL is only needed if your organization wants to use SLO requests with your SAML provider.

Open Greenhouse Onboarding and navigate to **Settings** > **Data Flow** > **Single Sign-On**.

On the _Single Sign-On_ page, enter your SSO URL, IdP certificate fingerprint, and single logout URL in their corresponding fields.

Mark the checkbox above the Save button to indicate that your organization **uses Entra AD as an Identity Provider**.

Click **Save**.

When you're finished, reach out to [Greenhouse Technical Support](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/8921763177115) to turn on your SAML configuration setup.

Before closing Greenhouse Onboarding, copy your organization's **SSO Assertion Consumer URL** and **Entity ID/Issuer** from the  _Single Sign-On_ page. You'll need these details later during Entra AD setup.

### Connect Greenhouse Onboarding in your Entra AD platform

Once you've set up your SAML configuration in Greenhouse Onboarding, it's time to set up the integration in Entra AD. Follow the below steps to connect Greenhouse Onboarding in Entra AD.

#### Create a new Enterprise application in Entra AD

**Note:** Do not use the pre-configured Greenhouse tile on the Entra marketplace. Create a custom tile for your new Greenhouse Onboarding setup. 

Navigate to the Entra AD platform and click **All applications** on the left panel.

Click the **\+ New application** tab on the _All applications_ page. 

Select **Create your own application** and configure the following settings:

  * Enter **Greenhouse Onboarding** under **What's the name of your app?**
  * Under **What are you looking to do with your** **application?** , select **Integrate any other application you don't find in the gallery (Non-gallery)**



Name the application **Greenhouse Onboarding**. 

Click **Single sign-on** on the  _Greenhouse Onboarding application integration_ page.

Click the **SAML** tile to enable Single Sign-On on the next page. 

#### Edit SAML configuration, user attributes, & claims in Entra AD

Next, you will need to edit your Basic SAML Configuration and User Attributes & Claims.

Click the **Edit** icon to edit the Basic SAML Configuration. 

In the Basic SAML Configuration panel, enter the below information:

  * **Identifier (Entity ID):** Enter your Entity ID/Issuer from Greenhouse Onboarding, app.parklet.co
  * **Reply URL (Assertion Consumer Services URL):** Enter your SSO Assertion Consumer URL from Greenhouse Onboarding, https://onboarding.greenhouse.io/saml/{uid}/consume 
    * The bracketed section includes your Greenhouse Onboarding unique identifier (UID).
  * **Sign-on URL:** Leave this field blank



**Note:** If you are using the pre-configured marketplace tile, the Sign-on URL cannot be left blank. To complete the setup, create a new custom tile for the Greenhouse setup. 

Click **Save** when finished.

#### Assign users to Greenhouse Onboarding in Entra AD

In the Entra portal, open the applications view and navigate to the directory view.

Navigate to **Enterprise applications** in the left panel and click **All applications**.

In the applications list, select the **Greenhouse Onboarding** application you created above.

In the left menu, click **Users and groups**.

Click the **+** **Add user** button.

Click the **Users** option and select your desired users. 

After you select the users, choose a role. 

Click **Select** button on **Users and groups** window.

Click **Assign** button on **Add Assignment** window.

# DISA integration

DISA allows you to send background screening requests directly to job applicants, students, or even volunteers, rather than having to input applicant information yourself. DISA is built right into your client ordering module featuring an electronic consent form and all of the following benefits.

Greenhouse Recruiting's integration with DISA allows you to send DISA assessments to candidates within Greenhouse Recruiting.

#### In this article

  * Retrieve DISA endpoint URL and secret key
  * Enable the DISA integration
    * Create a webhook
    * Create custom candidate fields
    * Create custom job fields
  * Use the DISA integration with Greenhouse Recruiting



### Retrieve DISA endpoint URL and secret key

Before enabling the DISA integration, Greenhouse Recruiting will need two pieces of information:

  * DISA endpoint URL
  * DISA secret key



To retrieve this information, reach out to your DISA customer success manager.

### Enable the DISA integration

#### Create a webhook

To integrate DISA with Greenhouse Recruiting, you'll need to create a webhook. Follow the steps in [this article](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/5888163727003) to create your webhook. Use the values listed below to configure the webhooks.

  * **Name:** DISA integration
  * **When:** Candidate has changed stage
  * **Endpoint URL:** The Endpoint URL provided by DISA
  * **Secret Key:** The Secret Key provided by DISA
  * **Username:** Secret Key received from the DISA



When finished, click **Create Webhook**.

That's it! Your DISA integration is enabled.

#### Create custom candidate fields

To create custom candidate fields for the integration, click **Configure** > **Custom** **Fields** > **Candidates**. Then select **Add Field**.

Create separate custom candidate fields for each of the following:

**Field name** | **Field type**  
---|---  
Background Check Status | Short Textbox  
Background Check Result | URL  
Background Check Completed Date | Short Textbox  
  
[Check out this article for detailed instructions on creating custom candidate fields.](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/202609675)

### Create custom job fields

To create custom candidate fields, click **Configure** > **Custom Fields** > **Jobs**. Then select **Add Field**.

Create separate custom job fields for each of the following:

**Field name** | **Field type** | **Options** | **Required**  
---|---|---|---  
Background Check Package | Single Select | List all available packages on individual lines | Yes  
Background Check Location | Single Select | List all available locations on individual lines | Yes  
  
[Check out this article for detailed instructions on creating custom job fields.](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/202609855)

This configuration allows you to select the background check package and location necessary to complete the background check. In order to use the integration, it's necessary to select the package and location for each job in Greenhouse Recruiting.

### Use the DISA integration with Greenhouse Recruiting

#### Add DISA to your job's interview plan

Once the integration is enabled for your organization, you'll be able to add DISA as an interview stage.

To do this for an existing job, navigate to your job (**Jobs** > **Job Name**) and click **Job Setup** > **Interview Plan**.

Click**\+ Add a Stage**. Select the **DISA****** stage.

When finished, click **Add**.

Hover over the stage to click **Edit** , then select the background check and assign reviewers for the assessment.

#### Send and review the background check

When candidates are moved into the DISA interview stage, Greenhouse Recruiting will display a **Send Test** link on their candidate profile.

**Note:** When you send a background check request from Greenhouse Recruiting, the instructions are actually sent by DISA.

When sending the background check, provide the candidate's email and select which question profile applies to the job the candidate is applying for.

Click **Send Test** , and the candidate will receive an email to initiate the background check process.

Once the candidate completes the request, the report will be available for viewing within Greenhouse Recruiting on the candidate profile.

On the candidate scorecard / interview kit, click **View Report** to be taken to DISA for full results.

# Scorecard feedback report

**Permissions:** Job Admin and above

**Product tier:** Available for new subscription tiers (Core, Plus, and Pro)

Reports such as the [interviewer calibration report](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/203941429) and the [interviewer engagement report](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/203941439) give your organization a great overview of how your hiring teams are performing. However, when your organization needs more granular data about your interview process, the scorecard feedback report offers all the data you need to analyze any impactful trends.

The scorecard feedback report can help your organization investigate how a candidate's ratings changed at different points in the interview process, how certain interviewers tend to rate candidates in different stages, or even which jobs have the highest and lowest pass / fail rates.

**Tip** : Need help troubleshooting this report? Check out [Troubleshoot a report](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/13710986142107).

#### In this article

  * Scorecard feedback report
  * Scorecard feedback report filters



### Scorecard feedback report

To create a scorecard feedback report, click **Reports** on your navigation bar.

Click **Essential reports** on the left.

Scroll to the _Run Your Own Analysis_ section and click **Scorecard** **Feedback**.

The scorecard feedback report will generate.

The report will display information for the following:

  * Candidate name
  * Job
  * Requisition ID
  * Department
  * Candidate status
  * Current stage
  * Interview
  * Scheduled date
  * Scorecard submission date
  * Interviewer name
  * Scorecard outcome



By default, the report displays scorecard feedback for the past week.

### Scorecard feedback report filters

Click**Filters and more** to apply filters to further refine your report.

The scorecard feedback report can be filtered by the following:

  * Job
  * Job status
  * Department
  * Office
  * User
  * Hiring team role
  * Custom job field
  * Scorecard date
  * Stage



**Note:** Sorting the report by application review will only show scorecards that were filled out in this stage (which is uncommon), not an overall pass / reject rate.

Click **Apply** after applying any filters.
view-and-manage-an-employee-profile:

# View and manage an employee profile

**Permissions:** Employees and above

**Product tier:** Available for Greenhouse Welcome and Greenhouse Onboarding tiers

This article outlines how to view and manage an employee's profile in Greenhouse Onboarding as an employee, manager, admin, or user with custom access. Click [here](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/4536840067611) to learn how to edit your personal employee profile. 

**Note** : Your view of the employee's profile may look different depending on the permissions granted by your organization's Admin Owner.  
  
For example, coordinators who are __ assigned as a manager to other employees will have more access to the employee profile than users with manager access only. Click [here](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360018891992) to learn more about user permissions in Greenhouse Onboarding. 

#### In this article

  * Employee access
  * Manager access
  * Admin access
  * Custom access
  * Additional resources



### Employee access

To help foster engagement and connection in your organization, you are able to view basic information about other employees.

To access a coworker's profile, enter their name in the **Search box** located at the top of your home page. Click the resulting **employee** from the dropdown that appears.

The header of their employee profile includes their name, profile picture, [pronouns and pronunciations](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/4564402907291), job title, department, start date, and work email. 

This page also displays additional personal information, their manager, and a list of the employee's direct reports if they are assigned as a manager to other employees. 

**Note** : Access to employee information varies depending on what your Admin Owner makes viewable to different users in your organization.

### Manager access

Users assigned as a manager can view their employees' profiles, set up new hire goals, and manage employee tasks and documents.

Learn more about [manager access to employee profiles](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/13298081921179) in Greenhouse Onboarding.

### Admin access

Admins in Greenhouse Onboarding can view profiles for employees across your organization, update employee profile admin settings, manage employee goals, tasks, and documents, and monitor email activity. 

Learn more about [admin access to employee profiles](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/13298757842587) in Greenhouse Onboarding.

### Custom access

[Custom access](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360019516351) is a set of specialized permissions granted to users by your organization's Admin Owner. Your view of an employee's profile will depend on how your custom permissions are configured.

**Example** : If you are an employee's mentor and given access to view and edit tasks assigned to current employees, you'll see the Tasks tab on the employee's profile.

To access a coworker's profile, enter their name in the **Search box** located at the top of your home page. Click the resulting **employee** from the dropdown that appears.

The header includes basic information about the employee such as their name, profile picture, [pronouns and pronunciations](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/4564402907291), job title, department, start date, and work email. 

Based on your custom permissions, the employee's profile will include the following tabs:

  * Info tab
  * Tasks tab
  * Documents tab
  * Integrations tab
  * Email activity tab



#### Info tab

On the Info tab, you'll find additional personal information for the employee, details about their manager, and a list of their direct reports if the employee is assigned as a manager to other users.

Click **Edit** to add or make changes to the employee's information. Click **Save** when you're finished editing.

**Note** : The Edit button is only available if your organization grants you edit access to employee fields.

#### Tasks tab

The Tasks tab shows all [tasks](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360000525691) assigned to the employee, their manager, and other users in the organization, such as their Onboarding Coordinator.

**Note** : The Tasks tab is visible to [custom users](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360019516351) granted access to view and edit tasks by your organization's Admin Owner.

#### Documents tab

The Documents tab shows all [documents](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/216488683) and [e-signatures](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/115003695071) assigned to the employee.

**Note** : The Documents tab is visible to [custom users](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360019516351) who have access to manage employee documents and signature requests. [E-Signature](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/115003695071) documents are available for the Greenhouse Onboarding subscription tier. 

Click **Add Document** to assign a new document to this employee. Click **Request Signature** to send an e-signature request to this employee.

#### Integrations tab

The Integrations tab allows you to export an employee's information to the third-party integrations you've set up with Greenhouse Onboarding.

**Note:** The Integrations tab is visible to [custom users](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360019516351) who've been granted access by your organization's Admin Owner.

Click **Export** next to the third-party integration where you'd like to send this employee's details. You can also review the information and values that have already been sent to this integration.

#### Email activity tab

Use the Email activity tab to review all email notifications from Greenhouse Onboarding that have been sent to this employee.

**Note:** The Email activity tab is only visible to [custom users](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360019516351) who've been granted access by your organization's Admin Owner.

### Additional resources

  * [Manager access to employee profiles](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/13298081921179)
  * [Admin access to employee profiles](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/13298757842587)
