# Manage pay transparency rules and reporting

**Permissions:** Site Admin

**Product tier:** Available for new subscription tiers (Core, Plus, and Pro)

Pay transparency helps your organization take a step toward pay equity by standardizing how salary ranges display on job posts.

During the creation process, you can assign the rule to an office and provide an optional description that appears on the job post.

Job Admins are then prompted to enter a required pay range during the job post configuration. Alternatively, you can link the rule to a custom job field that'll sync the pay range on the job with the pay transparency rule. This increases efficiency and limits errors by streamlining the work for your Job Admins. 

**Note:** Consult with your legal team if you have questions about local pay transparency laws and how it affects your organization, including recommended messaging to add to the job post.

#### In this article

  * Create a rule
  * Edit a rule
    * Edit the pay input details
    * Delete a rule
  * Reporting
  * Frequently asked questions
  * Additional resources



### Create a rule

New pay transparency rules are created on the _Privacy & Compliance _page (**Configure icon** > **Privacy & Compliance**)

Scroll to the _Pay transparency_ section and click **Configure**.

Next, click **Create a rule**.

Complete the following steps to create a pay transparency rule:

  1. Name the rule
  2. Select an office (optional)
  3. Enter the pay input details
  4. Preview the rule



#### Name the rule

Enter an internal **name** in the text field for the rule that's specific to the location (For example, "Remote - Eastcoast"). 

While you can create unlimited rules, each rule must have a unique name. 

#### Select an office (optional)

Choose an [**office(s)**](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/115002226426) from the dropdown menu if you want the rule to auto-populate on new job posts based in the correlating office. 

**Note:** Job Admins need to manually add pay transparency rules to existing job posts. 

#### Enter the pay input details

Add a **d****escription** and**title**. These details can only be modified on this page and can't be updated from the job post.

**Tip:** Consult with your legal team as needed for suggested language to add to the description. 

Check the box **link value to job custom field** and select a **custom field** from the dropdown if you want to sync the pay details on the job with the pay transparency rule. 

**Note:** Only [custom job fields](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/202609855) with a _currency range_ appear in the dropdown. 

When you select this option, you can also elect to **mark the value as not editable on the job post**. This ensures updates to the pay range are done from a single source using the custom field. 

Next, create additional pay inputs as needed by clicking **Add another pay input**. 

#### Preview the rule

Click **Preview rule** to see what the rule looks like during the job post configuration, and what candidates see on the job post. Please note that this is a preview only. The currency and pay range can only be added during the job post configuration. 

Click **Save changes** when done.

### Edit a rule

To edit a rule, navigate to **Configure** **icon** > **Privacy & Compliance**.

Scroll to the _Pay transparency_ section and click **Configure**.

Click the **Pencil** icon  next to a rule.

Use the following actions to edit the rule:

  * Edit the pay input details
  * Delete a rule



#### Edit the pay input details

You can edit the **name** , which **office(s)** the rule applies to, and the **pay input details** including the description, title, and whether the value is linked to a custom job field. 

Please keep the following in mind as you make changes:

Change type | Note  
---|---  
Office | When you remove an office, the rule remains intact on existing job posts in that office. Job Admins and above can manually remove the rule from the job post.   
Link to custom field  |  When you _mark the values as not editable_ , the rule overrides the existing pay range on the job post and replaces it with the custom field data. However, the values on the job post aren’t overridden if the custom field is empty.  ****Example:** **Your Job Admin selects a rule and enters $60K - $75K in the pay range, but this differs from the $65K - $80K pay range listed in the custom job field.  
  
You later update the rule to make the value uneditable on the job post. This setting overrides the existing data and updates the job post to $65K - $80K since this value is connected to the custom field.  
  
Create additional pay inputs as needed by clicking **Add another pay input**. 

Click **Preview rule** to view your edits. Then, **save** your changes when done.

#### Delete a rule

Deleting a pay transparency rule removes the pay details and descriptions from job posts where the rule is applied. Additionally, the deleted rule can't be applied to future job posts.

**Note:** Deleting a pay transparency rule can't be undone.

To proceed, scroll to the bottom of the page and click **Delete rule**.

Click **Delete** from the popup window to confirm the changes.

### Reporting

You can audit live job posts with pay transparency enabled across your organization using a CSV report. 

To access the report, navigate to _Job Boards & Posts_. (**Configure icon** > **Job Boards & Posts**)

Click **Download pay transparency report**. 

The report provides the following information:

  * Offices
  * Department
  * Job board type (Internal or external)
  * Job board status
  * Job ID
  * Job name
  * Job post ID
  * Job post name
  * Job post status
  * Job post location
  * EEOC questions status
  * Demographic question set selection
  * Pay transparency rule ID
  * Pay range ID
  * Pay range name
  * Pay range min and max
  * Currency
  * Date last edited



### Frequently asked questions

**Are updates required to the Job Board API?**

All job board options support pay transparency functionality by default and don't require manual configuration.

Pay details, including the description and range, appear in the [`content` field](https://developers.greenhouse.io/job-board.html#retrieve-a-job) of the Job Board API.

**Are pay transparency rules applied to job posts automatically?**

Pay transparency rules only auto-populate on _new job posts_ when you assign the rule to an office. 

Job Admins need to manually apply rules to existing [external](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/115002791566) / [internal](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/9625883146907) job posts.

**I'm hiring for multiple positions with different salaries in the same office. How should I set up the rule?**

The following options are available:

  * Option one: **Create separate rules for each position**. You can create unlimited rules, but each rule must have a unique name
  * Option two: **Create one rule with multiple pay inputs**. With this option, all pay input details for each position are visible to candidates



### Additional resources

  * [Add pay transparency to a job post](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/10028084062491)
  * [Pay transparency overview](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/13304010418075)

# Who can view the private notes option on candidate scorecards? 

Users with either of the following permissions see the private notes option when filling out a scorecard for a candidate:

  * Job Admin with the permission stripe **Can view and create private notes**
  * Site Admin with the user-specific permission **Can see private notes and salary info, manage offers, request approval, and approve jobs/offers**

If you submit private notes on a candidate scorecard, those notes are visible only to other users with one of the two permission levels outlined above.

# Edit custom opening field

**Permissions:** Site Admin, and Job Admin who can manage custom fields

**Product tier:** Available for new subscription tiers (Core, Plus, and Pro)

A custom opening field allows your organization to record select information on a per opening basis rather than for the entire job. Recording information per opening basis can be useful if you plan to hire multiple candidates of varying attributes, such as experience and location, against the same hiring plan and need to capture information specific to the opening. [Click here](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360036372071) for more information. 

This article covers how to edit an existing custom opening field for your organization.

To begin, navigate to the **Custom Options** configure page. (**Configure** > **Custom Options**). 

Click **Openings** under  _Company Custom Fields_. 

The _Custom Fields: Openings_ page lists all of your organization's custom opening fields. Click the **custom opening field** you wish to edit. 

Edit the details of the custom opening field. Refer to the following table for additional information:

**Name** | **Description**  
---|---  
Field Name | The name of the field.  
Description | Provide any additional context, direction, and/or summary of this custom opening field.  
Only show for openings made in these offices | If this custom opening field should only be available for certain offices in your organization, select those offices from the dropdown menu. If none are selected, the custom opening field will default to all offices.   
Only show for openings made in these departments | If this custom opening field should only be available for certain departments in your organization, select those departments from the dropdown menu. If none are selected, the custom opening field will default to all departments.   
Mark Private |  Field can only be viewed by users with one of the following permission levels:

  * Job Admin who **Can view and edit private job fields and approve/request approval on jobs** , or 
  * Site Admin who **Can see private notes, salary info, manage offers, request approval, and approve jobs/offers**

  
Required | Makes the custom opening field a required field when creating any new opening.  
Changes to this field require reapproval  | When checked, changes to the custom opening field re-trigger any job approval flows your organization has configured.   
  
**Note** : The **Field Type** cannot be changed once the field is created. 

Once you are done, click **Save** at the bottom of the page to confirm your edits.

# Edit custom referral question

**Permissions:** Job Admins, who can manage custom fields, and Site Admins

**Product tier:** Available for new subscription tiers (Core, Plus, and Pro)

Referral questions enable your organization to capture structured data for referrals made by your existing employees. In addition to Greenhouse Recruiting provided default questions, your organization can [add new custom referral questions](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/202610325). In this article, we will cover how to edit a custom referral question. 

Navigate to the **Custom Options** page. (**Configure** icon > **Custom Options**)

Click **Referral Questions**.

From the _Custom Fields: Referral Questions_ page, click the custom referral question you wish to edit. 

On the subsequent page, edit the custom referral question. The following fields will be available:

**Field Name** | **Details**  
---|---  
Field | Input the name or question for this custom referral question  
Description | Input an optional description for the field. Values input here will appear when a user hovers over the tooltip icon to the right of Field  
Type |  The format of the question, such as a text box, single select, or multi-select. **Note** : Once a Custom Referral Question has been **Saved** , the question Type can no longer be edited.  
Required | If checked, the user must respond to this custom referral question to successfully submit a referral.  
Placeholder | This value will initially load in the empty field (_i.e. Select an option_)  
Immutable Field Key |  A key is generated when a custom field is created. It enables downstream systems (_e.g. HRIS systems_) to detect the presence of Greenhouse custom fields during an export. **Note** : The Immutable Field Key cannot be edited.  
  
Click **Save** at the bottom of the page when finished.

**Note:** New referral questions are added to the bottom of the list of referral questions, and will appear in this same order on the _Add a Referral_ page. To learn how to reorder referral questions, click [here](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/202610325-Add-Custom-Referral-Question#h_5ef9b010-b0f1-4b4d-92d9-311848513366).

# Reactivate a deactivated user 

**Permissions:** Site Admin, and Job Admin who can invite new users to Greenhouse and reactivate deactivated users and add and remove users to their assigned jobs

**Product tier:** Available for new subscription tiers (Core, Plus, and Pro)

In order to preserve your organization's historical data, you are unable to completely delete users from your Greenhouse account. Rather than deleting users, Greenhouse Recruiting allows your organization to deactivate their accounts so they can no longer access your system or be assigned any responsibilities.

#### In this article

  * Reactivate a deactivated user
  * Reactivated user's historical data and invitation email



### Reactivate a deactivated user

To find the user's profile, navigate to the _Users_ page. _(**Configure** > **Users**)_

From the filters panel, click the _User Status_ dropdown and select **Deactivated.**

Once the list is filtered, click the deactivated user who will be reactivated.

**Note:** You can only reactivate users who had the same permission levels or lower than you at the time of their deactivation. For example, a user with Job Admin level permissions is unable to reactivate a user who had Site Admin level permissions when they were deactivated.

Click **Activate User** on the _Edit User_ page.

### Reactivated user's historical data and invitation email

If the user was deactivated before accepting their Greenhouse Recruiting invitation, you must resend the invitation email before they can log in. This applies even if they are active in your account.

However, if the user had already created an account before being deactivated, they can log in using their username and password. 

When a user is deactivated, their data is preserved in Greenhouse Recruiting. If a user is reactivated, the data will display as normal.

**Note:** Interviewer tags and Employee ID will be restored based on the data assigned to the user at the time of the deactivation.

# Ducknowl Export integration

Ducknowl is a talent screening and assessment platform that makes the hiring process faster and smarter. Recruiters and HR teams spend a lot of time screening candidates for jobs, yet still the best candidates do not come to the surface. Ducknowl Export solves your screening problem.

The Ducknowl platform allows you to conduct resume screening, video screening and skill assessment of applicants from one dashboard, reducing the necessary screening time. With inbuilt features like resume sorting, keyword matching, video screening, skill test, proxy prevention, and results sharing, Ducknowl enables recruiters to make data-driven hiring decisions using all candidate information stored on one platform.

Greenhouse Recruiting’s integration with Ducknowl allows users to pull candidates' resumes, names, and emails, from Greenhouse to Ducknowl so recruiters can start the screening process quickly.

#### In this article

  * Create a Harvest API key for the Ducknowl Export integration
  * Use the Ducknowl Export integration with Greenhouse Recruiting
  * Additional resources



### Create a Harvest API key for the Ducknowl Export integration

To configure the Greenhouse Recruiting / Ducknowl integration, you'll need to create a Harvest API key.

Follow the steps in [this article](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/5888163769883) to create the key, and verify that the credentials and permissions below are selected when configuring the Ducknowl integration.

#### Credentials

In the _Create New Credential_ box, make the following selections:

  * **API type:** Harvest
  * **Partner:** Ducknowl Export
  * **Description:** Ducknowl Export Harvest API key



#### Permissions

Verify that the following permissions are selected for the Ducknowl integration:

**Activity Feed**

  * All permissions



**Applications**

  * All permissions



**Candidates**

  * All permissions



**Close Reasons**

  * All permissions



**Custom Field Options**

  * All permissions



**Job Openings**

  * All permissions



**Job Posts**

  * All permissions



**Job Stages**

  * All permissions



**Jobs**

  * All permissions



**Offers**

  * All permissions



**Rejection Reasons**

  * All permissions



**Scheduled Interviews**

  * All permissions



**Scorecards**

  * All permissions



**User Roles**

  * All permissions



When finished, click **Save**.

Your Harvest API key for the Greenhouse Recruiting / Ducknowl Export integration is created and configured. 

### Use the Ducknowl Export integration with Greenhouse Recruiting

Using [the same Ducknowl profile logged in](https://app.ducknowl.com/) under when integrating Greenhouse Recruiting with Ducknowl export, click your name in the top-right hand and select **Recruiters View**.

_Recruiter View_ displays a list of jobs you have created. If the job you want to pull resumes for is not in the list, then create the job by clicking add job and follow the steps provided. If/once job is created, click on it.

To connect this job with a specific job posting on Greenhouse and pull resumes specific to this job, click on the edit option displayed with a pencil icon near the job title.

The ATS link can be found on your Greenhouse Recruiting account. Click **All Jobs** in your Greenhouse Recruiting account and select the specific job in Greenhouse Recruiting you want to pull resumes for. Once you have selected the specific job posting, copy the URL link from the address bar. This is the link you can paste in the _ATS Link_ field described in the previous step.

Click **Saves Changes** and Ducknowl will pull all resumes from Greenhouse Recruiting for the job posting you have linked.

For additional information or support reach out to [vikram@ducknowl.com](mailto:vikram@ducknowl.com) or [corey@ducknowl.com](mailto:corey@ducknowl.com).

# Edit interview kits in bulk

**Permissions:** Site Admin who can bulk edit job posts

**Product tier:** Available for new subscription tiers (Core, Plus, and Pro)

As your organization refines its hiring process over time, it's possible to find that multiple departments are creating similar interview kits. This article covers how to edit interview kits across multiple jobs using the bulk edit feature.

Interview kits are within job stages. Click [here](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/203303195) if you would like to learn how to edit job stages in bulk. 

#### In this article

  * Edit interview kits
    * Edit interview kit names
    * Add new interview
    * Remove interview kit
    * Sync interview kits
    * Add existing interview kit to another job
    * Reorder interviews



### Edit interview kits

To edit interview kits in bulk, click **Jobs** in the navigation bar at the top of your Greenhouse Recruiting. 

Add a **checkmark** next to each job you'd like to edit or use the **checkbox in the header** to Select all jobs. 

When finished, click**Stages/Interviews**.

On the next page, you can perform the following actions across all jobs included in the interview kit bulk edit: 

  * Edit interview kit names
  * Add a new interview
  * Remove an interview kit
  * Sync interview kits
  * Add existing interview kit to another job
  * Reorder interviews



Once you have made all of your changes, click **Save Changes** at the top of the page. 

**Note** : Each interview references how many jobs you selected for bulk edit include that specific interview kit. Since interview kits are within an interview stage, this number will never exceed the number of stages in a job. For example, the **stage**  _Hiring Manager Review_ is in 6 out of 21 jobs. Of those 6 jobs, the **interview kit**  _Hiring Manager Application Review_ appears in 5 of them.   


#### Edit interview kit names

Click on the interview kit within a stage and rename the interview. 

Once renamed, click the **checkmark** to save your changes. Repeat this process for every interview kit you would like to edit. 

#### Add a new interview

To add a new interview to a stage, navigate to a stage and select **+interview**.

Use the _Add Interview_ dialog box, to either:

  * Create a brand new interview using the provided text field
  * Select an interview from the pre-populated list
  * Copy an interview from another job



**Note** : Users can only copy interviews from jobs where they currently have **Job Admin** level permissions or above. 

When finished, click **Add**. Repeat this process for every interview kit you would like to edit. 

#### Remove an interview kit

Hover over an interview and click the **ellipses** icon. 

**Note:** The _Remove from all_ button under the  _Stage_ name**** is for the job stage, **not** the interview kit within the stage. Click here to learn how to bulk edit [job stages](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/203303195). 

Next, select **Remove from all** from the dropdown menu. 

Click **Remove this interview** to confirm the action. 

Repeat this process for every interview kit you would like to edit. 

#### Sync interview kits

If every job included in the bulk edit has the same Interview in the same Stage, you can sync all the Interview Kits for that Interview so they are the same.

**Note** : Scheduled interviews are not deleted unless an interview kit is removed from a job. If an interview kit is updated or replaced, scheduled interviews will remain scheduled with the updated interview kit.

Hover over an interview kit and click the **ellipses icon**. 

Select **Sync interview kits** from the dropdown menu. 

Using the dialog box, select a **single job** whose interview kit will act as the template for all the jobs included in the bulk edit. 

Click **Sync Interview Kits** when finished. 

Repeat this process for every interview kit you would like to edit. 

#### Add existing interview kit to another job

If an interview only exists for some jobs in the bulk edit, you can add the interview to all selected jobs 

**Note** : Scheduled interviews are not deleted unless an interview kit is removed from a job. If an interview kit is updated or replaced, scheduled interviews will remain scheduled with the updated interview kit.

Hover over the interview kit and click the **ellipses** icon. 

Select **Add to all + Sync interview kits** from the dropdown menu.

Using the dialog box, select a **single job** whose interview kit will act as the template for all the jobs included in the bulk edit. 

Click **Sync Interview Kits** when finished. 

Repeat this process for every interview kit you would like to edit. 

#### Reorder interviews

Interview kits can be reordered when there are multiple interview kits in a stage. 

**Drag and drop** an interview kit to reorder the list for all jobs in the bulk edit. 

**Note** : This action only reorders the interview kit within the job stage. Click [here](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/203303195) to learn how to reorder job stages.

# Create a stage transition rule

**Permissions:** Site Admin, and Job Admin who can create, edit, and delete stage transition rules

**Product tier:** Available for new subscription tiers (Core, Plus, and Pro)

[Stage transition rules](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360053129752) allow you to configure candidate-related actions that occur immediately when any member of your team moves a candidate to a specified stage, or when the candidate enters a stage. 

#### In this article

  * Create a new stage transition rule
  * Stage transition rule icon
  * Trigger a stage transition rule
  * Delay or cancel a stage transition rule
  * Additional resources



### Create a new stage transition rule

Click**Jobs** from the navigation bar and select a job from the list.

Click the **Job Setup** tab and select **Stage Transitions** from the left-side menu.

Click **Create a rule**.

On the next page, enter the following details for the new rule:

#### Stage

The stage where the rule is triggered.

For details on available stage transition rules visit [Stage transition rules overview](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360053129752).

**Note** : Rules applied to the Application Review stage trigger when a candidate is moved into Application Review or when a candidate is added directly to that stage (for example, when applying or being created in that stage).

#### Then...

The action that occurs when the rule is applied.

In the _Action_ dropdown, select the [stage transition rule](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360053129752) to be triggered when a candidate enters the specified stage. The available types of rules are based on the selection you made in the _Stage_ dropdown.

**Note:** Selecting **Send Calendly request** populates additional dropdown menus for **Calendly Interviewer** and **Calendly Event Type**. [Click here](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360029649991) to learn more about scheduling through Calendly.

#### User credited with this action

Select the user who should be logged in the candidate's Activity Feed as executing the action (for example, the user logged as sending the availability request email).

If no user is specified or the selected user isn’t available, Greenhouse assigns credit using the following order:

  * The user who moved the candidate

  * The application’s recruiter

  * The hiring manager

  * The oldest Site Admin in your organization




While this user's name is logged in the Activity Feed, you can still configure the email itself to be sent from a [global email address](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/205759545) (see the **From** section below).

**Note:** You can configure the action to be credited to either yourself or to the user who moved the candidate. You cannot configure the action to be credited to another specific user.

#### Template (optional)

The [email template](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/115002573326) used for candidate emails sent by this rule.

The available templates are based on the [type of rule](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360053129752) you selected. For example, configuring a candidate email rule allows you to choose only from _Candidate Email_ templates.

#### From

The email address from which the automated emails should be sent.

You can choose to send the emails from a verified global email address, or from the email address of the user committing the action by selecting the `{{MY_EMAIL_ADDRESS}}` token. If this token is used, the user taking the action must have a verified email address.

#### Subject

The subject line for the automated email.

If you chose a template, this field will be completed automatically. If you did not choose a template, enter a subject line in the field.

#### Body

The body text for the automated email.

If you chose a template, this information will be filled in automatically. If you want to enter custom text or edit the email body, you can do so in this field.

#### When to send

The timing of the email or request.

Once you select a delay, you'll need to choose the specific time that the message is sent. For information on canceling a pending communication, review the section on delaying or canceling a stage transition rule.

Once all details are provided, click **Save** at the bottom of the page.

Your stage transition rule is configured and appears in the job's _Stage Rules_ list.

Repeat these steps as needed to add stage transition rules to additional stages in the job's interview plan.

### Stage transition rule icon

When a stage transition is applied to a stage, a lightning bolt icon is displayed next to the stage name.

### Trigger a stage transition rule

Once your stage transition rule is configured, it is triggered when a candidate enters the specified stage.

**Note** : Stage transition rules trigger when a candidate enters a stage, including when they are moved into the stage or added directly to it (for example, when applying or being created in that stage).

When a stage transition rule is applied, an update will be added to their [activity feed.](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360037386272) A note will also be added if a stage transition rule isn't able to run.

**Note** : For Greenhouse Recruiting to execute a stage transition rule, the candidate must have a valid email address provided and cannot be marked as _Do Not Email_. For more information, click [here](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/11972148311451).

### Delay or cancel a stage transition rule

When you create a new stage transition rule, you can add a buffer to the action by choosing a time from the **When to send** dropdown menu.

**Note:** If a candidate is moved out of the specified stage before the rule is scheduled to run, the rule will not run.

If a rule has triggered, but the action hasn't yet happened, you can cancel it by navigating to the **Pending** tab of the _Tasks_ section in the candidate profile and clicking **Cancel**.

### Additional resources

To learn more about stage transition rules, check out the following articles:

  * [Stage transition rules overview](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360053129752)
  * [Edit stage transition rule](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360048337832)
  * [Delete stage transition rule](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360048335732)
  * [Copy stage transition rule](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360052425952)

# Delete an opening

**Permissions:** Site Admin, and Job Admin who can delete jobs

**Product tier:** Available for new subscription tiers (Core, Plus, and Pro)

A job must have one opening for every candidate you wish to hire for the role. In some cases though, your team might end up with more openings on a job than you ultimately end up needing. For example, a user might have created additional openings unintentionally, or your approved headcount might be adjusted internally.

**Note:** An opening can be deleted from a job only if the opening is both closed and non-filled (that is, the opening does not have active or hired candidates associated with it).

To delete an opening, navigate to the job where you wish to delete one or more openings by selecting **Jobs** from your navigation bar, then select a job from the list.

From the job's _Dashboard_ , click the **Job Info** tab.

From the _Job Info_ page, scroll down to the _Openings_ panel and click**Manage Openings**.

From the subsequent box, hover over the opening you wish to delete and click the **Ellipsis** icon . Click **Delete** in the dropdown.

**Note:** Deleting an opening is a permanent action that cannot be undone. Deleting an opening will result in the loss of all associated data, which can impact reporting.

**Note** : If your job has [two-stage approvals](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360025776391), you'll need to manage openings from **Job** **Setup** > **Approvals** > **Edit Job & Openings**.

Confirm you wish to delete the opening by clicking **Delete Opening** in the subsequent box.

The opening and any associated data will be deleted immediately.

# Jobtrees integration

Streamline hiring with Greenhouse Recruiting's Integration with Jobtrees. This integration allows you to simplify posting jobs, sourcing top talent, managing applications and communicating status updates by integrating the following features with Greenhouse Recruiting:

  * Post your jobs on Jobtrees.com
  * Collect and consolidate applicant data
  * Identify the most suitable candidates based on your job criteria
  * Automatically update candidates on their status



By leveraging this integration, recruiters can efficiently find and engage with the best talent while only paying for results, not traffic.

#### In this article

  * Set up a Jobtrees account
  * Retrieve user ID
  * Create a Harvest API key
  * Add demographic questions with the Job Board API key
  * Complete your Jobtrees account setup
  * Create a custom job field
  * Create a webhook
  * Use the Jobtrees integration with Greenhouse Recruiting
  * Additional resources



### Set up a Jobtrees account

To set up this integration, you'll first need a Jobstrees account. This profile includes company-specific date and payment information, as well as information needed to link your Jobtrees account to Greenhouse Recruiting.

After you create this account, most of your Jobtrees information can be updated directly within Greenhouse. Only payment and budget information must be managed directly in Jobtrees.

To set up your account, navigate to Jobtrees' employer page at <https://www.jobtrees.com/post-a-job>.

Click **Start Hiring Now** or **Sign-Up** to launch the register screen.

Register with your email address or use a social sign-in to create your Jobtrees user account.

After completing the registration steps and are logged in, you should be directed to the employer registration page. If this page doesn't automatically open, navigate to <https://www.jobtrees.com/employer-setup>.

Enter the basic employer information (Company Logo, Company Name, No of Employees and Phone Number), click the **Enable a software integration connection (ex Greenhouse)** check box, and click **Save and continue**.

Next, you'll need to enter some information created in Greenhouse to complete your integration. Keep this page open and follow the steps below to create a Harvest API key, retrieve your user IDs, and retrieve your optional Job Board API key.

### Retrieve user ID

Jobtrees will need a Greenhouse Recruiting user ID to associate with updates and changes created by the integration.

Click the **Configure** icon  on your navigation bar and then click **Users** on the left.

Click **Export to Excel**.

A spreadsheet will be downloaded to your computer. Open the Excel file and locate the user ID in the **User ID** column.

Copy the User ID from the spreadsheet and paste in the User ID field on your Jobtrees employer company details page.

### Create a Harvest API key

To configure the Jobtrees integration, you’ll need to create a Harvest API key.

Follow the steps in [this article](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/5888163769883) to create the key, and verify that the permissions below are selected when configuring the Jobtrees integration.

#### **Credentials**

In the _Create New Credential_ box, make the following selections:

  * **API Type:** Harvest
  * **Partner:** Jobtrees or Unlisted Vendor
  * **Description:** Jobtrees Harvest API Key



#### **Permissions**

Verify that the following permissions are selected for the Jobtrees:

  * Select All



Paste the API key in the Harvest API Key field on your Jobtrees employer company details page.

### Add demographic questions with the Job Board API key

If you have demographic questions included as part of your application process, providing a Job Board API key allows us to connect to your job board and retrieve those questions for your applicants.

To enable this feature in Jobtrees, select **Enable demographic info** and follow the steps below to create a job board API key in Greenhouse.

To create a Job Board API key, follow the steps in [this article](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/5888210160155) and use the information below when creating your API key:

  * **API Type:** Job Board
  * **Partner:** Jobtrees or Unlisted vendor
  * **Description:** Jobtrees job board API key



[Click here](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/13446638483355-Create-a-job-board-API-key-for-an-integration) for more detailed information on setting up a job board API key for a partner.

Once it's created, paste the copied Job Board API Key into the designated field on <https://www.jobtrees.com/employer-setup>

### Complete your Jobtrees account setup

Once the steps above are complete, finish the budget and payment details sections with the required info and click **Update**.

**Note:** Secret Key & Additional HTTP Headers are available as part of your Jobtrees setup and are used to create webhooks in the next steps in the integration.

### Create a custom job field

Next, in order to use the Jobtrees integration, you'll need to create a custom Jobs field in Greenhouse Recruiting.

To create a custom Jobs field, click the **Configure** icon  on your navigation bar, then click **Custom** **Options** on the left.

Click Jobs.

Click **Add field** , and enter the following details to configure the new field:

  * **Name** : Publish On Jobtrees
  * **Type** : Yes/No
  * **Description:** Determine whether to list this job on Jobtrees. Select "Yes" to publish or "No" to exclude. (Paste this or a similar description into the ‘Description (optional)’ field)



### Create a webhook

To integrate Jobtrees with Greenhouse Recruiting, you’ll need to create 7 webhooks. Follow the steps in [this article](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/5888163727003) to create your webhook. Use the values listed below to configure the webhook:

**Webhook 1: Job Updated**

  * **Name** : Job_Update
  * **When** : Job updated
  * **Endpoint URL:** The Endpoint URL provided by Jobtrees [https://api.jobtrees.com/job-postings/greenhouse/job ](https://api.jobtrees.com/job-postings/greenhouse/job%C2%A0)
  * **Secret Key:** The Secret Key provided by Jobtrees <https://www.jobtrees.com/employer-company-details>



**Webhook 2: Job Created**

  * **Name** : Job_Create
  * **When** : Job created
  * **Endpoint URL:** The Endpoint URL provided by Jobtrees <https://api.jobtrees.com/job-postings/greenhouse/job>
  * **Secret Key:** The Secret Key provided by Jobtrees <https://www.jobtrees.com/employer-company-details>



**Webhook 3: Job Post Created**

  * **Name** : JobPost_Create
  * **When** : Job post created
  * **Endpoint URL:** The Endpoint URL provided by Jobtrees <https://api.jobtrees.com/job-postings/greenhouse/job>
  * **Secret Key:** The Secret Key provided by Jobtrees <https://www.jobtrees.com/employer-company-details>



**Webhook 4: Candidate Stage Change**

  * **Name** : Candidate_Stage_Change
  * **When** : Candidate has changed stage
  * **Endpoint URL:** The Endpoint URL provided by Jobtrees <https://api.jobtrees.com/job-postings/greenhouse/job>
  * **Secret Key:** The Secret Key provided by Jobtrees <https://www.jobtrees.com/employer-company-details>



**Webhook 5: Job Delete**

  * **Name** : Job_Delete
  * **When** : Job Deleted
  * **Endpoint URL:** The Endpoint URL provided by Jobtrees <https://api.jobtrees.com/job-postings/greenhouse/job>
  * **Secret Key:** The Secret Key provided by Jobtrees <https://www.jobtrees.com/employer-company-details>



**Webhook 6: JobPost Update**

  * **Name** : JobPost_Update
  * **When** : Job Post Updated
  * **Endpoint URL:** The Endpoint URL provided by Jobtrees <https://api.jobtrees.com/job-postings/greenhouse/job>
  * **Secret Key:** The Secret Key provided by Jobtrees <https://www.jobtrees.com/employer-company-details>



**Webhook 7: Candidate Reject**

  * **Name** : Candidate_Reject
  * **When** : Candidate or prospect rejected
  * **Endpoint URL:** The Endpoint URL provided by Jobtrees <https://api.jobtrees.com/job-postings/greenhouse/job>
  * **Secret Key:** The Secret Key provided by Jobtrees <https://www.jobtrees.com/employer-company-details>



**Note:** For each webhook, click on ‘Advanced settings…’ link further down in the webhook set-up page to see an “Additional HTTP Headers” box and paste the Additional HTTP Headers value from the Jobtrees employer set-up page here ensuring that the words “Employer ID” are included before the number (this will automatically happen if you use the copy function on the Jobtrees page).

The Additional HTTP Headers’ value is available on the Employer’s Company Details page. <https://www.jobtrees.com/employer-company-details>

Leave the maximum attempt value as defaulted and click the ‘Create Webhook’ button

**Reminder:** The Endpoint URL, Secret Key and Additional HTTP Headers are the same values for all Webhooks, The value for the Secret Key and Additional HTTP Headers is on the Jobtrees Employer Company Details page.

### Use the Jobtrees integration with Greenhouse Recruiting

**Seamless Job listing Integration**

Upon completing the one-time integration steps above, with a couple additional clicks, you will be able to choose which jobs you post to Jobtrees to gain access to our talented and focused group of job seekers. Aligned with your set budget, Jobtrees will highlight your active roles as they are relevant to our job seekers and seamlessly integrate applicants into your Greenhouse instance. Any updates you make to your job postings on Greenhouse automatically flow through to what’s shown on Jobtrees. As you close roles or remove them from active recruiting, they’ll be removed from Jobtrees as well so only the active listings you have shared will appear on the site.

**How your jobs get added, updated, and removed on Jobtrees**

Jobtrees will pull in new and updated job postings from your Greenhouse portal live (within seconds) and show those updates on Jobtrees including removing any closed or paused postings.

Jobtrees uses the following indicators from your Greenhouse instance when performing updates:

  * Publish on Jobtrees set to “Yes” 
    * This is the population of jobs they evaluate for update
    * If this is changed to “No”, the job will be removed from Jobtrees
  * The job ID 
    * If this is new, they will create a new job on the Jobtrees site
    * If the job ID already exists on Jobtrees, they will evaluate it for any updates to posting information or status and flow those updates thorough
  * The partner’s job budget 
    * If there is budget unspent within the budget period (either at the job level or overall based on the partner’s selection) the job will appear on Jobtrees
    * If there is not budget available, the job will not be shown until there are new funds added or the next budget period is reached



**Interacting directly on Jobtrees**

As part of the integration set-up you will need to create a Jobtrees account for your business on Jobtrees. You can choose to leverage the Jobtrees interface to review candidate data but with the exception on updates to payment info, budgets and viewing candidate eval scores, everything can be done in your Greenhouse environment. The data flows seamlessly between the two instances eliminating the need to duplicate or miss tasks across the two systems.

### Additional resources

For additional information or troubleshooting not covered here, please reach out to [employerportal@jobtrees.com](mailto:employerportal@jobtrees.com)

# Tiered offices and departments 

**Permissions:** Site Admin

**Product tier:** Available for Plus and Pro subscription tiers

Greenhouse Recruiting's tiered offices and departments feature allow your organization to express the exact department or office structure you need to support offices all over the world, multiple brands within one Greenhouse account, or departments and sub-departments.

#### **Flat vs tiered organization structure**

In a flat organizational structure, all departments and offices are structured on a single level. For example, a flat organizational structure would have offices in Boston and New York with no overlap. Users must be assigned specific permissions for each office location.

A tiered organizational structure can set the two offices under a larger umbrella called "Northeast." By assigning user permissions to the "Northeast" tier (rather than individual offices), the user's permissions can grow and scale with the individual workings of each office.

Tiering can also be applied to departments across the organization. For example, Product and Engineering departments may be united under a larger "R&D" group.

With this flat structure, it may be simpler to conceptualize your organization during the initial stages of using Greenhouse Recruiting, but over time, will be limiting as your organization grows.

Using a tiered structure makes it easier for organizations can generate overarching reports, easily configure the correct permissions across their organization, or effectively distinguish large sections of the recruiting organization from each other.

#### In this article

  * Office and department creation
  * Job board and APIs
  * Permissions
  * Approvals
  * Reports



### Office and department creation / deletion

While the process of adding new offices and departments in your organization is exactly the same as a non-tiered, flat organizational structure, users will find an added dropdown menu to select whether the newly created office or department should be subordinated to an existing office / department.

Once created, the office or department will be nested under the selected parent office or department and can be accessed by expanding the parent item.

In the example above, Berlin is a sub-ordinate office of the EMEA office.

### Job board and APIs

No matter what [style of job board integration](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/200721644-Integrate-Job-Board-Overview) you use, updating your organization to use tiered departments or offices will adjust how things look on your job board. For organizations using the Greenhouse-hosted board or an iframe on an external career site, you will see a series of indents that distinguish departments and sub-departments with indents.

If a specific department does not have any nested departments **AND** does not have any jobs, it will be hidden on the job board.

As an example, let's imagine the below structure represents our departments and tiered sub-departments:

#### Business 

  * Accounting 
  * Legal 
  * Sales 



#### Success

  * Technical Support 
  * Customer Enablement 



#### R&D

  * Product Engineering



— Solutions Engineering

— Team Delta

  * Security & IT



If there were no jobs in Accounting, Legal, or Sales, Business would also be removed from the board. If Product Engineering has one job while Team Delta and Solutions Engineering were both empty, the two empty sub-departments will disappear while Product Engineering will remain as-is.

For organizations using any of the API-driven job boards, you'll want to have your web development team take a look at the documentation on our [Developers Resources](https://developers.greenhouse.io/job-board.html) to ensure that moving a department underneath another one does not inadvertently remove it from your job board altogether.

Our APIs support listing out departments and sub-departments (and offices and sub-offices), so your team will also be able to recreate a nested structure directly in Greenhouse Recruiting if that's something you are interested in.

### Permissions

The tiered office / department structure still allows your organization to assign permissions to all future jobs in a specific department and office combination, but there may be more situations where a job may simultaneously be affected by two different rules. As an example, let's imagine the below structure represents our tiered offices and departments:

#### Departments

**R &D**

  * Product Engineering



— Team Delta

— Solutions Engineering

#### Offices

**USA**

  * Northeast



— Boston

  * Northwest



— Seattle

A single user could be configured to be a Job Admin: Recruiter on all Team Delta roles in Boston AND a Job Admin: Hiring Manager on all Product Engineering jobs in the Northeast. In this case, the more _department-specific_ of the two rules (Team Delta + Boston) will win out. But in the case of an equivalent tie, like R&D + Boston vs. R&D + Seattle, the higher of the two job permissions (Job Admin: Standard) will be granted.

Now, in the unlikely event of an _even more specific_ scenario where the two roles are both Job Admins with the same number of permission stripes, the older of the two permissions will be granted. We recommend that you are as specific as possible when setting up permission rules.

### Approvals

Approvals have always suffered from a tiered structure, since you could set up an approval rule that covers all Boston jobs and another one that covers all R&D jobs. In this case, an R&D job in Boston would defer to the department rule, since departments are _typically_ smaller and thus more specific than offices.

In regards to approvals, we follow a similar pattern as with permissions.

#### Departments

**R &D**

  * Infrastructure



— Site Reliability Engineer

#### Offices

**USA**

  * California



— Los Angeles

  * Northwest



— Seattle

An approval process for a Site Reliability Engineer in Los Angeles will always win out over all Infrastructure roles in California. In the case of a tie, the more specific Department will win out, so Site Reliability Engineer in USA will always be assigned over R&D jobs in Los Angeles.

When adjusting your default approvals, it may be helpful to think about who the fallback approvers should be at each of the high levels before assigning approvers to more specific combos. Assigning someone as the approver on All Future Jobs will ensure that every job opened will always have an approver, even if no department and office is selected. From there, you might set an additional fallback for all USA jobs and another for all R&D jobs to ensure that someone else will always be added as an approver should the job creator select the wrong department or office during the job setup process.

### Reports

Most reports will continue to function exactly as they would in a flat organization structure, but can be filtered to show data for individual subordinate offices and departments you select. 

If we take the same tree as earlier:

#### Business

  * Accounting
  * Legal
  * Sales



#### R&D

  * Product Engineering



— Team Delta

— Solutions Engineering

— Technical Support

  * Success



— Activations

— Customer Enablement

— Learning Experience

The numbers in R&D can be further refined to encompass specific subordinate departments for Success, such as Activations and Customer Enablement, when reviewing [essential reports](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360034704071) or [creating custom reports using Report Builder](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360050317592).

These figures offer a great overview of all your business units, allowing you to gain insights into the individual performance of each tier within your organization.

**Note** : Individual sub-departments and offices can only be filtered when the parent office or department is NOT selected.

# Consider integration

Consider uses active matching technology to surface the best possible candidates no matter where they live on the web. Online resumes, social profiles, code repositories (GitHub), and online publications (scientific and academic journals) contain a universe of passive candidates that Consider can search.

Greenhouse Recruiting's integration with Consider allows users to source, access, engage, and track candidates from Consider. Based on your job postings, Consider’s algorithms create constantly improving matches, eliminating the repetitive and tedious work of boolean searching, surfacing only the most relevant candidates from the universe of profiles.

Instantly review diverse candidates, generate references and referrals from your network through Slack, and review the best-matching profiles from the stock of resumes who have already expressed interest in working with you.

#### In this article

  * Create a Harvest API key for the Consider integration
    * Credentials
    * Permissions
  * Enable the Consider source
  * Finish integration setup in Consider 
  * Use the Greenhouse Recruiting / Consider integration 
    * Add candidates to Greenhouse Recruiting from Consider
    * Review projects in Consider
  * Additional support



### Create a Harvest API key for the Consider integration

To configure the Greenhouse Recruiting / Consider integration, you'll need to create a Harvest API key.

Follow the steps in [this article](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/5888163769883) to create the key, and verify that the credentials and permissions below are selected when configuring the Consider integration.

#### Credentials

In the _Create New Credential_ box, make the following selections:

  * **API type:** Harvest
  * **Partner:** Consider (optional)
  * **Description:** Consider Harvest API key



#### Permissions

Verify that the following permissions are selected for the Consider integration:

  * Candidates: 
    * All permissions
  * Tags: 
    * Get: List tags applied to candidate
    * Get: List Candidate Tags
    * Post: Add New Candidate Tags
    * Put: Add a candidate tag
  * Job Posts: 
    * GET: List Job Posts
    * GET: Retrieve Job Post for Job
    * GET: List Job Posts for Job
  * Jobs:   

    * GET: Retrieve Job
    * GET: List Jobs
  * Sources: 
    * GET: List Sources
  * Users: 
    * GET: Retrieve User
    * GET: List Users



When you're finished, click **Save** at the bottom of the page.

Your Harvest API key for the Greenhouse Recruiting / Consider integration is created and configured. Provide your Harvest API key to your Consider onboarding team so they can set up the integration.

### Enable the Consider source

After your API key is configured, you'll need to enable Consider under your Sources. You can configure your Sources under the _Configure_ tab. _(**Configure** > **Custom Options** > Company Metadata > **Sources**)_

Scroll down to the Consider integration and turn on the toggle.

### Finish integration setup in Consider

Before completing this step, ensure your Harvest API key for the Greenhouse Recruiting / Consider integration is created and configured with correct permissions, as well as provided to your Consider onboarding team.

To configure the integration, you must authenticate Greenhouse Recruiting from Consider. To do this, sign in to Consider and then choose any project that you are a member of. In the project, open the **In progress** tab and click **Export**. Next, click the **Sign in with Greenhouse** link .

Next, you will authorize Consider to use your Greenhouse Recruiting account. Enter the credentials used to access Greenhouse Recruiting, then click **Next Step**.

On the subsequent page, click **Authorize**.

When authorization is successful, you will see a success message.

Return to your Consider project to export candidates to Greenhouse. You will not be required to sign into Greenhouse the next time you want to export, unless you are signed out.

### Use the Greenhouse Recruiting / Consider integration

#### Add candidates to Greenhouse Recruiting from Consider

To automatically export candidates from any Consider project to the corresponding Greenhouse Recruiting job, open the **Summary** tab and click on the **Greenhouse** section in the left-side navigation.

Select a Greenhouse job to export candidates and click **Enable automatic exports.**

To export candidates manually from any Consider project to corresponding Greenhouse Recruiting job, open the **In progress** tab and click on **Export** to open the export dialog.

Select an existing job in Greenhouse Recruiting for this export and click **Export**

Consider will send the following information to Greenhouse Recruiting:

  * Candidate name
  * Candidate email add ress(es) (if available)
  * The Greenhouse Recruiting job with which the candidate should be associated
  * Web links like the candidate's website URL, LinkedIn URL, GitHub URL, or Twitter URL
  * Email of the candidate's referrer (if available)
  * Candidate's current company
  * Candidate's current title



The candidate's source in Greenhouse Recruiting will be set to _Consider_.

#### Review projects in Consider

Sign in to Consider at <https://consider.com/login> and navigate to **Projects**. Review the automatically created companion Consider projects for job openings in Greenhouse Recruiting. From any project, you can now export Consider-sourced profiles to Greenhouse Recruiting. You can find matches for your job search from resumes already in Greenhouse Recruiting.

Visit [consider.com](http://consider.com) for more details.

### Additional support

For troubleshooting assistance with the Greenhouse Recruiting / Consider integration, contact the Consider support team at [support@consider.com](mailto:support@consider.com).

# Finch integration

Finch offers a unified API for trusted applications to securely access employment and candidate data on behalf of employers from leading payroll providers, HR information systems, and applicant tracking systems.

Greenhouse Recruiting’s integration with Finch allows Greenhouse Recruiting customers to authenticate access and share Greenhouse Recruiting data with trusted applications through the Finch API. As an example, some learning or onboarding management systems may request your Greenhouse Recruiting candidate data from within their platform to automatically issue trainings to new hires.

#### In this article

  * Create a Harvest API key for the Finch integration
  * Use the Finch integration with Greenhouse Recruiting
  * Additional resources



### Create a Harvest API key for the Finch integration

To configure the Greenhouse Recruiting / Finch integration, you’ll need to create a Harvest API key. 

Follow the steps in [this article](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/5888163769883) to create the key, and verify that the permissions below are selected when configuring the Finch integration.

#### Credentials

In the _Create New Credential_ box, make the following selections:

  * **API Type:** Harvest
  * **Partner:** Finch (optional)
  * **Description** : “Developer” Harvest API Key (Note: the Finch screen’s instructions will specify the exact Developer name. See the note box below for an example.)



#### Permissions

Verify that the following permissions are selected for the Finch integration: 

**Candidates**

  * List Candidates
  * Retrieve Candidate



**Applications**

  * List Applications
  * Retrieve Application



**Job Posts**

  * List Job Posts



**Offer**

  * List Offer
  * Retrieve Offer



**Note** : These permissions may change depending on how much data access the application has requested. We have listed the maximum number of permissions above, but the Finch screen’s instructions will list the exact permissions you should select.

In the example below, the permissions are listed in step 3.

### Use the Finch integration with Greenhouse Recruiting

Finch typically shows up as part of the onboarding or setup process within your favorite application. For example, some learning or onboarding management systems may request your Greenhouse Recruiting candidate data from within their platform to automatically issue trainings to new hires.

When you’re ready to start syncing data from Greenhouse Recruiting to your application, the Finch screen will pop up, typically in your application’s dashboard.

In this screen, Finch displays several pages before asking you to share an API token.

First, you'll see information on Finch’s security practices.

Then, Finch shows exactly what data the application is requesting access to. The application has access to request all or a subset of job, offer, candidate, and application data. If you have any questions on the data scopes shown, please reach out to your application’s support team as they can share more information.

On the _Select your provider_ page, click **Greenhouse**.

Finally, you’ll see instructions on how to create an API token within Greenhouse Recruiting.

These instructions cover: 

  * What permissions you need to create a Harvest API token
  * How to create that API token
  * Which permissions to set, depending on what data the application is requesting access to



Just follow those instructions and click **Sign In** to create and share that API token with Finch.

Your application will then be able to retrieve automated, real-time data from your Greenhouse Recruiting system directly and securely. 

### Additional resources

For additional information not covered here, please reach out to your application’s support team as they will directly support Greenhouse Recruiting customers through the troubleshooting process.

For example, if your onboarding or learning management solution is requesting your Greenhouse Recruiting data through Finch, their support team is the best point of contact.

# Greenhouse identity verification overview

**Permissions:** —

**Product tier:** Available for Plus and Pro subscription tiers

Greenhouse identity verification helps your team focus on real, qualified candidates by reducing the risk of impersonation, duplicate profiles, and other forms of fraud. It’s part of Real Talent, a set of tools designed to block spam and spot suspicious behaviors. Identity verification works in tandem with our partner, CLEAR, to cross-check the information submitted to CLEAR against the candidate’s application.

#### In this article

  * Real Talent
  * How Greenhouse helps verify a candidate's identity
  * About CLEAR verification



### Real Talent

Identity verification is one part of Real Talent, a broader fraud and spam prevention solution. Real Talent takes a multifaceted approach to help recruiters focus on real, qualified candidates during the hiring process.

Real Talent also includes:

  * **Talent Matching** : Helps recruiters quickly identify candidates that closely meet the requirements of the job.
  * **Fraud Detection:** Flags suspicious patterns like mismatched location and IP, invalid contact info, or unusual network activity.
  * **Spam blocklist** : Your organization can block IP addresses and email domains that contribute to spam.



Together, these tools give your team more confidence in who you’re engaging with and reduce manual effort during the review process.

### How Greenhouse helps verify a candidate's identity

Greenhouse helps verify a candidate’s identity by cross-checking their application details against the information returned through the identity verification request. We compare fields like last name, email address, and phone number to spot inconsistencies. This check happens automatically once a candidate completes identity verification in MyGreenhouse.

Even small mismatches, like an unexpected email address or phone number, can signal potential fraud or impersonation. These results appear in the candidate profile and can help recruiters decide on next steps.

### About CLEAR verification

CLEAR is a secure, third-party identity platform integrated directly into Greenhouse. Candidates complete verification with CLEAR through MyGreenhouse. CLEAR runs over 60 security signals, including:

  * Government ID authentication
  * Selfie check with liveness detection
  * Device and network metadata



Once verified, candidates are marked as CLEAR verified for the stage in which verification was completed. You can search and filter candidates by verified status.

CLEAR does not store candidate data in Greenhouse. All identity information remains with CLEAR.

### Additional resources

  * [Operational readiness guide: Identity verification policy](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/44684268111643)
  * [Send an identity verification request with CLEAR](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/40893011137179)
  * [Identity verification setup](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/45125816892187)
  * [Failed CLEAR identity verification requests](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/40921076478491)
  * [Identity verification with CLEAR - Security & Privacy FAQ](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/44242404870811)

# Release Notes: October 2024

Greenhouse Software regularly releases new product features, updates, and improvements. You can stay up-to-date by following our [release notes](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/200929955) or checking out the [latest feature releases](https://www.greenhouse.com/greenhouse-latest-features) page.

#### This month's releases

  * Greenhouse Recruiting
  * CRM
  * Business Intelligence Connector
  * Sandbox Sync
  * Integrations
  * Bug fixes



### Greenhouse Recruiting

#### Featured job posts

Job posts can now be marked as "featured" so that they're highlighted at the top of your job board to bring the attention of candidates to specific openings at your organization. [Read more here.](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/30254867842587)

**Note:** Featured job posts are only available if you're using the [new job board customization options](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/18996861758363).

#### Internal job board embedding

Your organization can easily host and embed internal job boards on other sites - like a company site or your intranet - using an iFrame, allowing you to easily highlight internal job boards in the resources that are most referenced by your team. [Read more about job board embedding here.](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/211233903-Host-internal-job-board-outside-of-Greenhouse)

**Note:** Internal job board embedding is only available if you're using the [new job board customization options](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/18996861758363).

#### Command palette

Command Palette is a reimagined way to navigate Greenhouse Recruiting, placing all your search results in one place. In addition to candidates and jobs, the Command Palette can be used to search based on phone number, or find specific pages listed on the Configure page.

Command Palette can be accessed anywhere in the app using the keyboard shortcut **Command (⌘) + K** on Apple devices, **Ctrl + K** on Windows, or by clicking the search bar at the top of your page.

#### Archiving and restoring custom fields

All tiers now have access to a refreshed custom field page, including the ability to archive and restore custom fields. When a field is archived, you can’t change old values or add new ones for future candidates, jobs, or prospects. This keeps users from entering data in outdated or unused fields, but allows you to reference the previously-entered data on individual candidates and jobs.

Archived fields won't be included in reports, but are still available through the Harvest API and Business Intelligence Connector.

#### Dependent job and opening custom fields 

Expert tier customers can now add dependencies to job and opening custom fields to better manage structured data across your organization. [Read more here.](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360038889992)

#### Bulk team hiring updates

Advanced and Expert tiers can now update the assigned hiring team for multiple jobs at once under the Bulk Actions menu on the All Candidates page. [Read more here.](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/29787420693659)

#### Candidate profile enhancements

In the past month, we've released a number of new features and changes to the candidate profile:

**Keyboard shortcuts**

Use keyboard shortcuts to quickly perform important actions on the candidate profile. The keyboard shortcut menu can be accessed by pressing **Shift+/**.

**Pinned notes**

Important notes can now be pinned in the right panel so they always display at the top of the list. This allows your team to keep relevant information handy, even when lots of communication is occuring. We've also added filtering, allowing you to filter by pinned notes, visibility, note creator, and job association.

**Private mode**

Added a toggle to switch the candidate profile to **Private mode.** When in private mode, certain sensitive or private data is hidden, allowing you to share your screen when conducting an interview roundup or reviewing scorecards, without the risk of other participants unintentionally seeing sensitive information, like private notes.

**More information in the main panel**

Improved the view of the main panel to show all interview stages at a glance so it is easily referencable across the candidate's hiring plan. Stages now include more details about the candidate's availability.

In addition to these changes, we've also made a number of small updates to improve the readability of the page:

  * The **Reject** , **Move stage** , and **Mark as hired** buttons have moved from the main panel to the header.
  * The header now minimizes when scrolling to display more of the main panel.
  * Tasks have moved from the main panel to the right panel in the _Alerts_ section.



Read more about the redesigned candidate profile [here](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/30352015432987).

#### Other changes

In addition to the changes outlined above, we made the following updates to Greenhouse Recruiting this month.

  * Added a column to the Scheduling Activity Report for rescheduled interviews. 
  * Added rescheduled interviews and declined interviews as options in the Report Builder.
  * Added Resume Anonymization Status as a filter on the Report Builder so organizations can better analyze the impact of resume anonymization on your hiring process.
  * Added a city and radius filter to Talent Filtering for organizations that are currently using those settings in candidate search.
  * Improved resume parsing services for non-English languages, including Korean, Simplified Chinese, Japanese, Russian, and Dutch.



### CRM

CRM events can now be duplicated, meaning you can create a new event from an existing event, rather than starting from scratch. 

### Business Intelligence Connector

We released a new schema for the Business Intelligence Connector on October 18, 2024. [Read more here.](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/29303125452699)

### Sandbox Sync

This month, we released some updates to sandbox sync. With these enhancements, the following settings will now be synced between your production and sandbox accounts:

  * Application limits
  * Job post custom application questions & rules
  * Configurable candidate surveys
  * AI tools
  * Automated permission rules.



Additionally, the following settings will be retained after each sync to reduce the amount of time required to set up your sandbox for testing:

  * Users
  * User settings
  * Job board settings
  * Dev Center Single sign-on (SSO) setup
  * Verified email domains.



[Read more about sandbox sync here.](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/14111892585627)

### Integrations

  * **Candidate testing:** [Chattyhiring](https://www.greenhouse.com/integrations/chattyhiring) runs AI interviews, and evaluates and shortlists candidates so that you can spend more time talking to the right candidates.
  * **Candidate testing:** [Trading Interview](https://www.greenhouse.com/integrations/trading-interview) seamlessly incorporates assessments into your interviews, enabling a more comprehensive evaluation of candidates’ quantitative skills.
  * **Free job posts:** Nexxt offers free organic job postings to help companies reach millions of job seekers across Nexxt.com and its family of niche sites.
  * **Optimization:** [AI Screened](https://www.greenhouse.com/integrations/ai-screened) is an AI recruiter, Ryan, that reviews resumes, conducts phone screen calls, and handles all candidate comms.
  * **Other integrations:** [Caro](https://www.greenhouse.com/integrations/caro) helps Talent, People, and Finance teams with headcount planning and talent capacity management.
  * **Other integrations:** [Sync2Hire](https://www.greenhouse.com/integrations/sync2hire) makes it easy to bring all post-application communications into a collaborative environment. 



### Bug fixes

  * Fixed an issue where the rejection modal was unresponsive when rejecting candidates on template jobs.
  * Fixed an issue that prevented users from updating graders for take-home tests.
  * Fixed an issue where manually created Outlook events added the organizer as an attendee.
  * Fixed an issue where using the shortcut **Cmd+Z** in the text editor invalidated email template tokens.
  * Fixed an issue where keyboard shortcuts for the Command Palette prevented users from scrolling using the arrow keys.

# Interviewer visibility into the candidate profile

In Greenhouse Recruiting, users of all permission levels can be [scheduled to interview](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360050744912) candidates moving throughout your interview pipeline.

Unlike scheduling, however, access and visibility into the candidate profile for interviewed candidates is determined by the [permission level assigned](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360039614171) to your interviewers. 

For example, scheduling an interview for a user with **Job Admin** or **Site Admin** permissions will grant them access to their assigned scorecard, the interviewed candidate's profile, as well as, different points of access within the profile based on the job-based permissions allowed by their permission level.

Scheduling an interview for a user with **Basic** permissions will grant them access to the following information for the candidate where they are scheduled:

  * Public contact information
  * Attachments (resume and cover letter)
  * Assigned scorecard



Basic users will not have access to attachments marked **Admin Only** or **Private**.

**Note:** A candidate's profile in Greenhouse Recruiting houses [each individual application](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/115004506466) a candidate has submitted across your posted jobs.

If access and visibility to candidate applications stored within an interviewed candidate profile differs across your assigned jobs, [check your job-based permissions](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360020855632) to determine expected visibility settings. 

If your organization allows interviewers without job-based permissions to see other users' completed scorecard (either **Always** or **After submitting their own**), a link will appear on the right side of the interview kit and completed scorecard.

If applicable, click **View Scorecards** to see previously submitted scorecards.

This link will allow interviewers without job-based permissions to click into and view other scorecards without accessing the candidate's profile.

**Note:** Basic users will not be able to access the candidate's profile to view scorecards or access the full list of candidates on the job. To learn more on adjusting scorecard visibility settings for users without job-based permissions, [click here](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/115002226606).

# Add a custom demographic question set to a job post

**Permissions:** Site Admin, and Job Admin who can create, edit, and delete job posts

**Product tier:** Available for new subscription tiers (Core, Plus, and Pro)

Custom demographic data through Greenhouse Recruiting's DE&I feature set can be captured via job post using the [custom demographic question set](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360039535731) feature. In this article, we will cover how to do the following for existing job(s) in your organization:

#### In this article

  * Enable a custom demographic question set on a single job post
  * Enable a custom demographic question set on job posts in bulk



**Note** : This article assumes that your organization has configured one or more custom demographic question sets and enabled them to be included in job posts. [Click here](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360039535731) to learn more.

Once enabled, all responses will be reported in the [Pipeline by Demographic](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360007254531) report.

### Enable a custom demographic question set on single a job post

Once custom demographic question sets are [created](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360039535731) for your organization, these question sets can be enabled on a per job basis.

To enable a question set, navigate to a specific job by clicking **All Jobs** on the navigation bar and selecting a job from the list.

Click **Job Setup** on the job's navigation bar and select **Job Posts** from the left-hand panel.

Click the **Edit** icon inline with the job post you would like to edit.

From the Edit Your Job Post page, navigate to the _Settings_ panel and click the checkbox next to **Include Custom Demographic Questions**.

Use the provided dropdown menu to select a custom demographic question set.

When finished, click **Save** to confirm the change.

Your custom demographic question set will be added to this job's job post.

### Enable a custom demographic question set on job posts in bulk

**Note** : Bulk editing job posts is only available to Advanced and Pro subscription tier customers.

Once custom demographic question sets are [created](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360039535731) for your organization, these question sets can be enabled in bulk across multiple job post at once.

To enable a question set on multiple job posts, navigate to **All Jobs** on the navigation bar and checkbox the jobs on whose job posts you wish to enable custom demographic question sets.

At the top beside _Edit_ , click **External Job Posts**.

On the _Editing External Job Posts_ page, click the **Settings** tab.

Under the Settings tab, select **Ellipsis** beside _Custom demographic questions in the application form_.

Next, select **Enable for all job posts**.

On the pop-up, select the custom demographic question set you wish to enable for the selected job posts.

Click **Done**.

Once complete, click **Save and Exit** to apply your changes.

Your selected job posts will now automatically show the custom demographic question set you chose.

# Create and edit social templates

**Permissions:** Job Admins, who can manage company email and social media templates, and Site Admins

**Product tier:** Available for new subscription tiers (Core, Plus, and Pro)

To help employees stay on brand when sharing jobs via their social networks, you may want to customize your organization's social media templates.

Site Admins and Job Admins with the user-specific permission **Can manage company email and social media templates** can create and edit templates for organization-wide use, as well as manage their own personal social media templates. Job Admins without the noted user-specific permission can create and edit personal social media templates only.
