# Schedule an interview manually

**Permissions:** Job Admin or above

**Product tier:** Available for new subscription tiers (Core, Plus, and Pro)

You can schedule interviews for a candidate directly from their profile. Manual scheduling gives you control to choose specific times, review availability, and adjust details as needed. If your organization also uses [automated scheduling](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/36255269371419), you can switch between the two methods depending on what works best for a given interview.

After you select a time, Greenhouse will guide you through the remaining steps, including sending interviewer invites and confirming details with the candidate.

#### In this article

  * Create an interview schedule
  * Configure and send interviewer invites
  * Enable candidate calendar events
  * Send the candidate interview confirmation email
  * Additional resources



### Create an interview schedule

All scheduling information is located on the **Stages** tab of the candidate profile. You can use this section to help create an interview schedule that works for both the candidate and the interviewer.

In a multi-interview stage, you can schedule multiple interviews quickly by clicking **Schedule All**.

When you schedule an interview, a calendar will open in a new tab.

The left panel includes interview information, like the interviewer's name, additional candidate information, or resources.

The calendar in the center of the page is used to pick the specific interview time.

Use the scheduling panel on the left to enter a date and time manually, or double-click the calendar view on the right to create a new event.

When you assign a user to an interview, their availability appears in the interview column on the calendar. If enabled by your organization, you can also add a location or resource in the left panel to show its availability on the calendar.

If you clicked **Schedule All** to book multiple interviews, selecting a time for the first interview automatically creates chronological placeholders for the others. You can adjust any interview time by entering a new time in the scheduling panel.

If a candidate completed an availability request, their selected times will appear. Grey times are outside their availability; white times match their submitted preferences.

Click the **Settings** icon in the top right to change the calendar type or name. This lets you schedule to a shared calendar or view times in a specific time zone.

The **Calendar name** dropdown lists the calendars you can create events on. When you schedule an interview and send invitations, the selected calendar appears on the invite for interviewers.

Any of the candidate's details can be found in the left panel by hovering over the icon next to their name.

Once you have completed the necessary fields for the selected interviews, click **Customize details** at the top right of the page. 

### Configure and send interviewer invites

The _Send Calendar Invite to Interviewers_ page allows you to configure interviewer invites and add any video interviewing options. 

**Note:** Interview times selected in the previous step are not sent to the interviewers' calendars until the steps below are completed. If you exit the scheduling process before sending the invites, the interviews will not be scheduled. 

The  _Schedule Summary_ panel on the right displays the finalized interview schedule. Add a _Location_ and _Video Conferencing_ in the right panel.

To use video interviews, your organization must have set up a video interviewing integration, such as [Zoom](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360042222612).

If any of the interview details listed in the  _Schedule Summary_ panel require updating, click **Back to calendar** at the top right to return to the _Scheduling_ page.

If you are scheduling multiple interviews, you can use the same email template for all calendar invites, or create individual invites for each interview. The option to _Use the same email template for all interviews_ is selected by default.

You can customize invite emails manually or use an alternative template by unchecking the box next to _Use the same email template for all calendar invites_.

**Note:** Because the information populated by email tokens is unique to each interviewer, if you use the same email template for all interviewer invitations, email tokens will not be added in the interviewer invite preview, but will show up when the interviewer gets the email in their inbox.

When you're ready, click **Schedule interviews.** If you're using Google Calendar or Outlook to schedule your interviews, click **Open in Google** or **Download .ics File** to send the interviewer invitation and complete the scheduling process. 

The invitations are sent to the interviewer through their calendars. The scheduled interviews will appear on the candidate's profile momentarily. 

**Note:** Candidates can be added to calendar events by turning on the setting Send candidate calendar events via connected calendar integration under **Configure** > **Permissions** > **Scheduling**.

### Send the candidate interview confirmation email

By default, candidates are not included in the calendar event created through the scheduling process outlined above, although this can be changed in system settings.

If your organization hasn't enabled candidate events, notify the candidate by sending a [candidate interview confirmation email](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360015975112) once the interview is scheduled internally.

From the candidate's profile, click **Send Interview Confirmation** under the stage where you have scheduled the interviews. 

In the  _Availability_ dialog window, select the appropriate _Candidate Interview Confirmation_ email template and make any necessary changes to the body of the email. When finished, click **Send Email** to send the confirmation to the candidate. 

### Additional resources

To learn more about scheduling in Greenhouse Recruiting, including details regarding specific calendar integrations and scheduling across time zones, see the following Support Center resources: 

  * [Calendly](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360029649991)
  * [Google Calendar](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360021799232)

# Office and department dependent workflows

The purpose of this guide is to help your team understand the role of offices and departments within your organization configuration. Office and department values have many dependencies in Greenhouse Recruiting, so we recommend evaluating how these entities should be organized to fit your recruiting team's operational needs. Your organization configuration can impact the following areas:

  * User permissions
  * Job and offer approvals
  * Job board configuration
  * Dashboard and reporting filters
  * Custom field configurations
  * Email template and offer template configurations



If you still have any questions about the right office and department structure for your organization after reviewing this guide, reach out to your customer success representative.

**Note** : If you are building an integration to import jobs to Greenhouse from a third-party system and are interested in syncing office and department values through this integration as well, please [click here](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360029625351) for more information.

### How offices and departments are used in Greenhouse Recruiting

#### User permissions

Users can be assigned access to future jobs by office or department.

**Note** : If a job's office or department is assigned or updated after the job is created, users with future permission to jobs in the requisite office or department will be applied accordingly.

#### Approval flows

Organizations with an Advanced or Pro subscription can configure default approval flows to open new jobs and extend offers by office or department.

**Note** : Office and department-specific approval chains will only be applied if the job is assigned to the requisite office or department at the time the job is created. If the office or department is changed or added to the job after it is created, the requisite approval flow will need to be applied manually on the job's approval page.

#### Job posts on job board

If your organization is using a [job board hosted by Greenhouse Recruiting](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/200721644-Integrate-Job-Board-Overview) (option 1) or has your Greenhouse Recruiting job board [embedded on your careers page](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/200721644-Integrate-Job-Board-Overview#%E2%80%9C2%E2%80%9D) (option 2), the jobs will be organized by your offices and departments.

Your web team can only implement an alternative organization of job posts on your site if implementing an API driven job board ([option 3, option 4, or option 5](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/200721644-Integrate-Job-Board-Overview#%E2%80%9C3%E2%80%9D)).

Please reach out to your internal web development team or third-party website developer if you are unsure of which option your team is currently using or plans to use.

#### Report and dashboard filters

Jobs can be sorted by office and / or department in reports and on the Job and Candidate search dashboards.

#### Offer templates

Organizations with an Advanced or Pro subscription can make Offer Templates available only to candidates on jobs assigned to certain offices or departments.

#### Custom job and offer fields

Organizations with an Advanced or Pro subscription can configure custom job fields to appear only on jobs assigned to selected offices or departments. Similarly, custom offer fields can be configured to only appear on Offer forms for candidates on jobs assigned to selected offices or departments

#### Email templates

Organizations with an Advanced or Pro subscription can configure email templates so they are only available to be sent to candidates on jobs assigned to selected offices.

# Gusto integration

Greenhouse Recruiting's integration with Gusto allows your company to import candidate information from Greenhouse into Gusto with a quick one-time setup.

#### In this article

  * Enable the Gusto integration
    * Configure user setup permissions in Greenhouse Recruiting
    * Create a Harvest API key for the Gusto integration
    * Provide Harvest API key to Gusto
  * Use the Gusto integration
    * Import candidates to Gusto
  * Additional resources



### Enable the Gusto integration

#### Create a Harvest API key for the Gusto integration

To configure the Greenhouse Recruiting / Gusto integration, you'll need to create a Harvest API key.

Follow the steps in [this article](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/5888163769883) to create the key, and verify that the credentials and permissions below are selected when configuring the Gusto integration.

#### Credentials

In the _Create New Credential_ box, make the following selections:

  * **API type:** Harvest
  * **Partner:** Gusto
  * **Description:** Gusto Harvest API key



#### Permissions

Verify that the following permissions are selected for the Gusto integration:

**Applications**

  * Select all



**Candidates**

  * Select all



**Users**

  * Select all



**EEOC**

  * Select all



**Offers**

  * Select all



**Custom fields**

  * Select all



When finished, click **Save**.

Your Harvest API key for the Greenhouse Recruiting / Gusto integration is created and configured. Copy the Harvest API key to provide to Gusto in the next step.

#### Provide Harvest API key to Gusto

With your Harvest API key copied, navigate to the App Directory in your Gusto account. Search for **Greenhouse** and click the app.

Click **Connect** and paste the API key in the input area.

Click **Continue to setup** to finalize the integration.

### Use the Gusto integration

#### Import candidates to Gusto

When you're ready to import a candidate to Gusto, head to the **Hiring** tab, and click **Hire a new person**.

Select the **Import** option.

Choose a candidate from your list of Greenhouse Recruiting candidates, and select how you would like to bring them on to Gusto. When ready, click **Continue**.

After you've finished the next steps, you can find this candidate by navigating back to **Hiring** to proceed with the onboarding process.

Data sync between Gusto and Greenhouse:

  * Email
  * First name
  * Job Title (if the job title exists in your Gusto account)
  * Last name
  * Offer letter
  * Phone
  * Start date



### Additional resources

For additional information or troubleshooting not covered here, reach out to [Gusto](https://support.gusto.com/article/115266364100000).

# RecruitBot integration

RecruitBot uses machine learning to understand your hiring preferences and discover your ideal candidates, then gets them to engage with you by automating conversations with best-in-class email marketing tools. By making sure you only review the most promising candidates, RecruitBot will transform the quantity and quality of candidates you interview, all while saving you a ton of time. Through our integration with Greenhouse, you'll easily be able to sync actions between the two platforms.

#### In this article

  * Create a Harvest API key for the RecruitBot integration
    * Credentials
    * Permissions
  * Provide Harvest API key to RecruitBot
  * Integration Features



### Create a Harvest API key for the RecruitBot integration

To configure the Greenhouse Recruiting / RecruitBot integration, you'll need to create a Harvest API key.

Follow the steps in [this article](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/5888163769883) to create the key, and verify that the credentials and permissions below are selected when configuring the RecruitBot integration.

#### Credentials

In the _Create New Credential_ box, make the following selections:

  * **API type:** Harvest
  * **Partner:** RecruitBot
  * **Description:** RecruitBot Harvest API key



#### Permissions

Verify that the following permissions are selected for the RecruitBot integration:

**Applications**

  * GET: Retrieve Application
  * GET: List Applications
  * PATCH: Update Applications
  * POST: Advance Application
  * POST: Move Application
  * POST: Reject Application
  * POST: Moves Application to Job
  * POST: Unreject Application



**Candidates**

  * All permissions



**Custom Field Options**

  * GET: Custom Field Options



**Email Templates**

  * All permissions



**Job Stages**

  * All permissions



**Jobs**

  * GET: Retrieve Job
  * GET: List Jobs



**Rejection Reasons**

  * All permissions



**Tags**

  * All permissions



**Users**

  * All permissions



### Provide Harvest API key to RecruitBot

Once your API key is copied, navigate to your **RecruitBot account** and click on your **account name** in the upper right-hand corner. Then, click **Company Settings** from the dropdown menu. 

On the next page, input your copied **Greenhouse API key** into the appropriate field. Select a user for updates (typically, this is your Greenhouse Admin).

Next, map your Greenhouse stages to RecruitBot. Whichever Greenhouse stages your organization uses should be set as **To Review,** and all others should be set to **Reach Out**.

Select the positions for which you'd like to use RecruitBot. Click **Link Positions** when done.

Navigate to the **positions** tab at the _top of the RecruitBot toolbar_ , which reveals the positions you've decided to associate with RecruitBot.

Click on the **applicable position** , and RecruitBot automatically downloads each resume from Greenhouse that you've associated with this position. You can then proceed to use RecruitBot and enjoy all of its deeper interactions with your Greenhouse interface.

### Integration Features

RecruitBot intelligently integrates with Greenhouse, leading to functionality that might seem obvious.

The following are some examples:

  * Export all candidates you source in RecruitBot into Greenhouse, to manage the rest of your funnel
  * Understand which candidates you've already reached out to in Greenhouse, so you don't double message
  * Improve RecruitBot's understanding of your ideal candidate by analyzing your Greenhouse interviewing decisions

# Enable EEOC questionnaire on job post

**Permissions:** Site Admin, and Job Admin who can create, edit, and delete job posts

**Product tier:** Available for new subscription tiers (Core, Plus, and Pro)

The EEOC questionnaire is a set of federally-approved questions about race, gender, veteran status, and disability status. The questions included in this voluntary questionnaire are un-editable because they were carefully crafted to comply with relevant regulations. The EEOC questionnaire is enabled on a per-job post basis and in this article we will cover how to enable the questionnaire on an existing job post for a job.

To enable the EEOC questionnaire on a job post, click the**Jobs** tab from your navigation bar and then select a job.

Click **Job Setup** and navigate to **Job Posts** on the left. Find your job post and click the **Edit** icon  beside it.

From the _Edit Your Job Post_ page, navigate to the Settings section and check the box to enable the **Include EEOC Questions**. 

Click **Preview** to view the EEOC questionnaire that's included on the job posts when candidates apply. 

When done, scroll to the bottom of the page and click **Save**. 

**Note** : It isn't possible to edit the text of the EEOC questionnaire. Read more [here](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/205278605).

# SEEK Ad Sync integration

Ad Sync is SEEK's newest effortless job posting solution, enabling you to post quality job ads to SEEK using a feed from Greenhouse. It automates the ad posting process while giving you control and flexibility.

You can:

  * Mandate ad selection rules to centrally manage your budget
  * Post quality ads by leveraging SEEK's AI to pre-fill job ad fields
  * Manage branding across all SEEK ads or per sub brand



#### Who can access this solution?

As an automated posting solution, it's designed for organizations managing standardized, always-on roles at scale, where consistency and efficiency across large recruitment teams matters most.

To be eligible for the early access release, you must:

  * Be a large enterprise customer with high-volume, continuous recruitment needs, with a dedicated SEEK Account Manager, who can work with you to ensure it's the right fit for your business and guide you through the onboarding
  * Operate out of the following markets: Australia, New Zealand, Singapore, Hong Kong, or Malaysia



To enable the SEEK Ad Sync integration, first contact your SEEK Account Manager to activate it for your account. 

#### In this article

Enable the Greenhouse Recruiting / SEEK Ad Sync integration

Use the SEEK Ad Sync integration with Greenhouse Recruiting

Additional resources

### Enable the Greenhouse Recruiting / SEEK Ad Sync integration

Once that's completed, navigate to Greenhouse and click the **Configure** icon on your navigation bar, then click **Job Boards & Posts** on the left.

Click the **Ellipsis** icon beside your job board and select **Edit Board Settings** from the dropdown.

Scroll to _Allow candidates to apply directly from "SEEK Ad Sync"_ , check the box, and click **Save**.

#### Setting rules

In SEEK, rules are set using the following:

  * Role Title and/or
  * Location and/or
  * Salary – Note: if pay transparency rules are not used on the job post, salary will not be sent to SEEK; Instead, SEEK will use market data to assign a salary based on similar job ads.



#### Managing spend

As Ad Sync is automatic, spend visibility is critical. SEEK provides tools and support to help customers track it:

  * Monthly or weekly spend reports, automatically emailed to Greenhouse customers
  * On-demand insights via SEEK's Analytics tool



### Use the SEEK Ad Sync integration with Greenhouse Recruiting

Once enabled, ads are posted to SEEK via this process:

**Editing ads**

Customers can edit their job ads in two ways:

  1. Update the job post in Greenhouse; edits will be delivered to SEEK via XML feed every 2 - 3 hours
  2. Edit the job ad in their SEEK Advertiser Account (Note: This will break the link between the requisition and the job ad, and any changes made to the requisition will not be updated via the XML feed integration. Best practice is option 1!)



### Additional resources

For additional information or SEEK troubleshooting not covered here, contact your [SEEK account manager](https://talent.seek.com.au/contactus).

# Error when adding notes during application review

If you encounter an error when attempting to submit a scorecard for a candidate's application during [application review](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/4401963991707), the application review stage may not have any interviews in the interview plan.

You can update the job's interview plan by following these steps:

  1. Locate the job that the candidate is applying for
  2. Open the Interview Plan (Job's dashboard > Job Setup > Interview Plan)
  3. Confirm if there is an interview within the App Review stage



If there's no interview listed under the application review stage in the job's interview plan, then add an interview stage. You should now be able to review the candidate's application.

If the issue continues, contact Greenhouse Technical Support.

# Time to hire by candidate report

**Permissions:** Job Admin and above

**Product tier:** Available for new subscription tiers (Core, Plus, and Pro)

The perfect complement to the [Time to fill by job](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/204635705-What-is-the-Time-to-Hire-per-Job-report-How-do-I-use-it-) report, the Time to hire by candidate report lets you assess how long each of your hired candidates spent in the interview process,  highlighting areas where potential improvements can be made to streamline and expedite hiring.

Use this report to compare lead times for candidates in different jobs, between different recruiters, and against any personal goals your organization has set.

**Tip** : Need help troubleshooting this report? Check out [Troubleshoot a report](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/13710986142107).

#### In this article

  * Time to hire by candidate report
    * Time to hire by candidate report filters
    * Time to hire by candidate calculation



### Time to hire by candidate report

To create a Time to hire by candidate report, click **Reports** on your navigation bar.

Click **Essential** **reports** on the left.

Scroll to the _Share Progress with Executives_ section and click **Time to Hire**.

The Time to hire by candidate report will generate.

**Note** : By default, the Time to hire by candidate report will show all open jobs on which you have the [appropriate permissions](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360020855632).

The Time to hire by candidate report will display information for the following:

  * Hired candidate name
  * Job
  * Source
  * Requisition ID
  * Opening ID
  * Application date
  * Offer date
  * Accepted date
  * Days to offer



#### Time to hire by candidate report filters

Click **Filters and more** to apply filters to further refine your report.

The Time to hire by candidate report can be filtered by the following:

  * Job
  * Job status
  * Department
  * Office
  * User
  * Hiring team role
  * Custom job field
  * Include migrated candidates



Click **Apply** after applying any filters to your report.

#### Time to hire by candidate calculation

**Note** : The Time to Hire calculation within the essential report is based on the [created offer date](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/200721744), the Time to Hire calculation in Report dashboards is based on the [candidate hire date](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/115005471286).

The time to hire is measured as the time candidates spend in the hiring process, specifically the difference between the [candidate's application date](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/17201325129371) on a job and the [candidate's offer date](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/200721744).

# Use buffer time during scheduling

**Permissions:** Job Admins

**Product tier:** Available for new subscription tiers (Core, Plus, and Pro)

Back-to-back interviews can lead to delays, stress, and missed context. Buffer time creates intentional gaps between interviews, giving interviewers time to prepare, wrap up notes, and transition between meetings.

**Note:** Buffer times only appear in Greenhouse. They aren’t added as events to your external calendar.

#### In this article

  * Add buffer time to a scheduling link
  * Add buffer time to a self-schedule request
  * Buffer time in automated scheduling
    * Edit the interview plan
    * Seeing suggestions and viewing the calendar



### Add buffer time to a scheduling link

Navigate to your scheduling links by clicking your initials in the top right-hand corner of any page of Greenhouse. Click **Scheduling links** on the left side panel.

Create a new link, or edit an existing one.

To add buffer time, click the checkbox for _Add buffer time around meetings._ From the dropdown, select how many minutes of buffer time you need before or after the interview, or both.

In order to prevent back-to-back meetings, the selected buffer time will be applied to any meeting booked with the link. Only time slots that can accomodate this buffer time will be shown on the calendar when the recipient is scheduling using the link.

### Add buffer time to a self-schedule request

Buffer time can also be added to a [self-schedule request](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/4409534677915) to protect interviewers from back-to-back meetings.

When sending a self-schedule request, scroll to the _Add buffer time around this interview_ checkbox underneath the calendar settings.

Choose how much buffer time you need before, after, or on either end of the interview.

The candidate will only be able to select times from the calendar that account for buffer time.

### Buffer time in automated scheduling

Once buffer time has been configured on the interview plan, it’s applied throughout the [automated scheduling](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/36255269371419) experience. Suggested times reflect the buffer set before and after each interview, helping you avoid back-to-back scheduling.

#### Edit the interview plan

Navigate to the job’s interview plan and locate the interview you want to update. Hover over the interview, then click the pencil icon to edit it.

Scroll to the _Additional settings_ section and select **Add buffer time to this interview**.

Choose how much time to set aside before and after the interview, then click **Save**.

You can also add buffer time when creating a job.

When you copy a job or create one from a template, any configured buffer time is automatically applied to the new job.

#### Seeing suggestions and viewing the calendar

When buffer time is enabled, suggested times automatically account for the buffer set on the interview.

If a suggested time doesn’t fully accommodate buffer time or overlaps with another interview’s buffer, it’s flagged so you can review it before scheduling.

On the calendar, events appear extended to reflect the buffer time before and after the interview. This helps you understand the full time commitment at a glance. Buffer time does not create separate events on an interviewer’s external calendar.

When buffer time overlaps with another event on the calendar, the buffer may not be visible. Instead, the name of the existing event will be shown. This helps prioritize visibility into scheduled events while still indicating that buffer time can’t be fully applied.

When you move an interview on the calendar, its buffer time moves with it. Previously scheduled interviews keep their original buffer time. These also appear on the calendar view for visibility.

**Note** : Buffer time may be flagged as a conflict, but it doesn’t block scheduling. You can still drag and drop an interview over another interview’s buffer time.

# Change your new hire’s start date

**Permissions:** Owners, Coordinators, and Managers who can edit the Start Date field for direct reports

**Product tier:** Available for Greenhouse Welcome and Greenhouse Onboarding subscription tiers

If a new hire's start date changes after they've been added to Greenhouse Onboarding, you can manually update their start date in their employee profile.

**Note:** When a new hire's start date is updated in Greenhouse Recruiting, the changes will be [sent automatically to Greenhouse Onboarding for approval](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/13387377390875#:~:text=the%20above%20field-,Accept%20or%20dismiss%20new%20hire%20changes,-You%20can%20use).

#### In this article

# Assign custom access to the new hire report

**Permissions:** Owners

**Product tier:** Available for Greenhouse Onboarding and Greenhouse Welcome subscription tiers

[Owners](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360019575491) can configure which users have access to view your organization's new hires in Greenhouse Onboarding or Greenhouse Welcome.

Create custom access roles with the **Can access the new hire report** permission stripe and assign this role to allow specific users to view new hire details in the [new hire report](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/12134213304475).

#### In this article

  * Add new hire permissions to a custom role
  * Assign users to a custom role with new hire permissions
    * Define rules to view new hires
  * Additional resources



### Add new hire permissions to a custom role

To get started, you'll need to configure a new or existing custom role with permission to manage new hires.

From the Greenhouse Onboarding homepage, navigate to **Settings** > **Data Flow** > **Permissions**.

In the  _Custom Access_ panel, click an existing custom access role to edit its permissions.

You can also click **Create New** to [create a new custom role](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360019516351). Give your new role a **Name** , then click **Save and Close** to begin editing this role's permissions.

Navigate to the **Settings** tab in your custom access role.

Under  _Permissions_ , mark the checkbox **Can access the new hire report**.

Your changes are saved automatically.

Any user who's assigned this custom role will now have access to view new hires in the [new hire report](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/12134213304475). In the next step, you can limit access to manage specific new hires based on the rules that you define for each user assigned to this role.

### Assign users to a custom role with new hire permissions

Next, assign permission to manage new hires to specific users in your organization. You can also add rules to define which new hires can be viewed by users with this role.

Navigate to the **Users** tab for your custom role, then click **Add User**.

Under the **Add user(s)** field, use the dropdown menu to select each user in your organization that you'd like to assign to this custom role.

**Note:** You can add multiple users simultaneously during this step. Be aware that adding multiple users at once will give them all the same [match rules](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/15542886274075-Assign-custom-access-to-see-and-edit-tasks#h_01H0P2HJRYBBPTGN3TQN5JNFX0), which are defined below. If you need custom users to have different rules for managing new hires, add them one at a time or in batches.

#### Define rules to view new hires

Use any of the following fields to define which new hires this custom access user can see in the new hires report:

  * **Department matches** – view new hires from specific departments
  * **Location matches** – view new hires from specific locations
  * **Employment Status matches** – view new hires with specific employment statuses
  * **Other Criteria matches** – view new hires tagged with [other criteria](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360000863252)



**Example:** You'd like to give **two Marketing managers** a custom access role with permission to view new hires in the **Marketing** department and based in **Los Angeles**.

Select the two managers' **names** from the **Add user(s)** menu.

Select **Marketing** from the **Department matches** menu.

Select **Los Angeles** from the **Location matches** menu.

Once you save, these two managers will be able to see new hires from the Marketing department who are based in Los Angeles.

Click **Save and Close**. Repeat the process of adding users and defining their specific access rules as needed.

Once you're finished, custom access users will be able to see new hires that meet their role's match rules in the [new hire report](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/12134213304475).

### Additional resources

  * [New hire report](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/12134213304475)
  * [Custom access roles](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360019516351)

# Nametag integration

[Nametag](https://getnametag.com/) is an identity verification platform that helps organizations securely verify identities and prevent fraud. As AI-generated and fraudulent applications become more common, Nametag helps recruiting teams confirm that candidates are who they claim to be while reducing compliance risk.

Nametag’s integration with Greenhouse Recruiting allows users to initiate identity verification for candidates at key stages in the hiring process and track verification results directly within Greenhouse.

#### In this article

  * Configure the Nametag integration
  * Set up for each job
  * Scaling this setup across jobs
  * How Nametag updates candidate data in Greenhouse
  * Use the Nametag integration
  * Additional resources



### Configure the Nametag integration

#### Prerequisites

Before setting up the integration, ensure you have:

  1. An active **Nametag account**
  2. **Site Admin permissions** in Greenhouse



In this section, you’ll connect Nametag to Greenhouse through OAuth authorization and complete the setup to enable identity verification as part of your hiring process.

#### Connect Nametag to Greenhouse

In the **Nametag Console** , navigate to **Configure**. In the left sidebar, click **Integrations**. Click **Add Integration** and select **Greenhouse**.

Click **Connect to Greenhouse**.

You will be redirected to **Greenhouse** to complete the OAuth authorization flow.

Review the requested permissions and click **Authorize**.

After authorization is complete and you are redirected back to Nametag, the integration will be connected.

#### Create the candidate email template

To enable candidates to complete identity verification, create an email template in Greenhouse that includes the Nametag verification link.

**Create the email template**

In **Greenhouse** , navigate to **Configure**. In the left sidebar, click **Email Templates**.

Click either**Create a New Organization-Wide Template** or**Create a New Template.**

****

  1. Configure the template with the following settings:
     * **Type:** Candidate Email
     * **Body:** Include the Nametag verification link generated in the Nametag Console



**Recommended Candidate Email Template**

**Subject:** Complete your identity verification for your application

**Body:**

Hello {{CANDIDATE_FIRST_NAME}},

As part of our hiring process at {{COMPANY}}, we ask candidates to complete a secure identity verification. The verification is powered by Nametag and typically takes less than a minute to complete.

This helps us confirm that applicants are who they claim to be, protecting both candidates and our organization throughout the interview process.

You'll be prompted for:

\- A government-issued photo ID

\- A live selfie to confirm your identity

To begin, use the secure link below:

VERIFICATION_LINK

If you have any questions or run into issues, feel free to reach out to our recruiting team.

Thank you,

{{COMPANY}} Recruiting Team

**Note:** VERIFICATION_LINK is not a Greenhouse placeholder. Replace this with the verification link generated in the Nametag console

### Set up for each job

Complete these steps for each job where you want to use Nametag verification.

#### Create a Nametag verification stage

  1. In **Greenhouse** , navigate to **Jobs** and select a job.



  2. Click **Job Setup**.



  3. Click **Interview Plan**.



  4. Add a new stage named **Nametag Verification**.



You can place this stage anywhere in your hiring pipeline depending on your workflow.

#### Configure an automatic email trigger (recommended)

To streamline the process, configure Greenhouse to automatically send the verification email when a candidate enters the Nametag Verification stage.

  1. In **Greenhouse** , navigate to **Jobs**.
  2. Select the job where the **Nametag Verification** stage was added.
  3. Click **Job Setup**.
  4. Click **Stage Transitions**.
  5. Click **Create a New Rule**.



  6. Configure the rule:
     * **Stage:** Nametag Verification
     * **Action:** Email Candidate
     * **Template:** Select the email template created in Step 2



### Scaling this setup across jobs

Once you’ve configured Nametag verification for a job, you can reuse this setup across other jobs:

  * **Use a job template (recommended)** Create a Greenhouse job template that includes the Nametag Verification stage and email trigger. This allows you to skip Steps 3 and 4 for all new jobs created from the template. [Learn more about creating job templates in Greenhouse](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360038222812-Creating-and-using-template-jobs)
  * **Copy from an existing job** Copy an existing job’s interview plan to reuse the same setup.
  * **For existing jobs** Complete Steps 3 and 4 for each job individually.



### How Nametag updates candidate data in Greenhouse

Nametag uses Greenhouse APIs to update candidate application data when verification events occur, ensuring that verification results are reflected in real time

  * Creating and updating custom fields for verification data
  * Adding notes with verification results
  * Optionally moving candidates to the next stage



Nametag does not overwrite existing candidate profile data.

#### Custom fields created by Nametag

Nametag creates the following custom fields to store and display verification data on the candidate’s application in Greenhouse.

**Field** | **Description**  
---|---  
**Verification Status (Nametag)** | The current verification result  
**Verified Legal Name (Nametag)** | The verified legal name from the identity document  
**Name Match Result (Nametag)** | Indicates whether the name provided in Greenhouse matches the name on the verified identity document  
**Verification Details Link (Nametag)** | A link to the detailed verification results in the Nametag console  
**Verified GPS Location (Nametag)** | The GPS location captured during verification  
**Request ID (Nametag)** | The unique identifier for the verification request  
  
#### Application notes added by Nametag

Nametag adds notes to the candidate’s application to provide a clear verification timeline.

Notes may be added for the following verification events:

  * Verified
  * Not Verified
  * Review in Progress
  * Appeal Rejected
  * Confirmed Fraud



Nametag updates the candidate’s application in Greenhouse when key events occur during the identity verification process.

#### Auto-Move candidates after successful verification

You can configure Nametag to automatically move candidates to the **next interview stage in Greenhouse** after a successful verification.

When enabled, Nametag will advance the candidate to the next stage after the verification result is **Verified** and the legal name matches the candidate’s name.

Nametag will only move the candidate if their current stage is **Nametag Verification**. If the candidate has already been moved to another stage by a recruiter, Nametag will not modify the candidate’s stage.

### Use the Nametag integration

After completing setup, you can use the Nametag integration to verify candidate identities within your hiring workflow.

#### Identity verification workflow in Greenhouse

Verification is triggered when a candidate enters the **Nametag Verification** stage in Greenhouse and receives the verification email, either automatically (if configured) or manually.

  1. A candidate progresses through the hiring pipeline in Greenhouse.
  2. The candidate enters the **Nametag Verification** stage.



  3. Greenhouse sends the verification email using the configured template.
  4. The candidate completes identity verification through Nametag.
  5. Nametag processes the verification and determines the result.
  6. Nametag updates the candidate’s application in Greenhouse:
     * Updates custom fields
     * Adds a note with verification details



  7. If enabled, Nametag automatically moves the candidate to the next stage after successful verification.



**Common scenario: verifying a candidate before interviews**

  1. Recruiter moves candidate to Nametag Verification stage.
  2. Candidate receives a verification email.
  3. Candidate completes verification.
  4. Recruiter reviews verification status in Greenhouse.
  5. Candidate proceeds to the next stage if verified.



#### Removing the integration

You can disconnect the Greenhouse integration at any time from the Nametag Console.

To remove the integration:

1\. In the **Nametag Console** , go to **Configure**.

2\. In the left sidebar, select **Integrations**.

3\. Locate the **Greenhouse** **integration**.

4\. Click **Remove**.

Once removed:

  * Nametag will no longer access Greenhouse data
  * Verification results will no longer be sent to Greenhouse
  * Existing data in Greenhouse will remain unchanged



If you want to use the integration again, you will need to set it up again by following the setup steps.

### Additional resources

For additional information not covered here, reach out to [support@nametag.co](mailto:support@nametag.co).

Nametag Greenhouse integration documentation: <https://getnametag.com/docs/greenhouse-integration/>

#### FAQs

**What permissions does Nametag require?**

Nametag requests only the minimum permissions required to support identity verification workflows. This includes permissions to read candidate and application data, list and create custom fields, update application fields, add notes to applications, and move candidates between stages. It also reads interview stage configuration to determine the correct next stage when Auto-Move is enabled.

**Does Nametag overwrite candidate data?**

No. Nametag only adds verification-related data to the application.

**Can candidates be automatically advanced?**

Yes. If Auto-Move is enabled, candidates are moved to the next stage after successful verification, as long as they are still in the Nametag Verification stage and the verified legal name matches the name on the Greenhouse candidate profile.

# Individual goals over time report

**Permissions:** Job Admin and above

**Product tier:** Available for new subscription tiers (Core, Plus, and Pro)

[Individual goals](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/8381830669979) are crucial to hiring efficiency as they drive accountability and promote a vision for individual contributors to attain. The individual goals over time report allows you to track progress on your individual goals.

#### In this article

  * View individual goals over time report
    * Individual goals over time report visualization
  * Apply report filters



### View individual goals over time report

To create an individual goals over time report, click **Reports** on your dashboard's navigation bar.

On the _Reports_ page, click **Essential** **reports** from the left panel.

Select **Individual Goals Over Time** from the  _Understand Goal and Attainment Metrics_ section.

The individual goals over time report will generate.

Use **Filters and more** to select the goal you'd like to report on.

**Example:**

If you have a goal of adding 10 candidates per week, you'd want to set the filters to the following to report on your progress:

  * **Activity type** : Candidates added
  * **Frequency** : Weekly
  * **User filter** : You



The individual goals time report will display the following information:

  * Actual (your performance)
  * Target (your goal)
  * Completion (attainment percentage towards your goal)



#### Individual goals over time report visualization

The individual goals over time report displays your target and actual individual goals attainment in a line chart.

Activity is displayed on the _y_ -axis and the date is displayed on the _x_ -axis. Your target value is represented by a dotted line on the _y_ -axis.

You can hover over each point in the visualization for additional details.

This visualization will adjust each time you apply new filters from the **Filters and more** dropdown.

### Apply report filters

Click **Filters and more** to apply filters and further refine your report.

The individual goals over time report can be filtered by the following:

  * Activity date
  * Activity type
  * Frequency (daily, weekly, monthly)
  * Users



Click **Apply** to add your selected filters and adjust your report visualization.

# Journeyfront integration

Journeyfront uses the latest advances in predictive analytics, psychometric assessments, and machine learning algorithms to improve the accuracy of hiring and get more people into jobs where they will thrive.

Greenhouse Recruiting's integration with Journeyfront uses a brief assessment to evaluate the traits of your employees to create a model of the ideal hire, including attributes such as interests, values, competencies, and personality. Candidate assessments are measured against this data, so you can better predict performance and the likelihood of turnover.

In this article

  * Create a Harvest API key for the Journeyfront integration
    * Credentials
    * Permissions
  * Share User ID with Journeyfront
  * Create a webhook
  * Add a custom job field
  * Create Journeyfront interview stages
    * Configure Journeyfront interview stages
  * Test the integration
  * Additional support



### Create a Harvest API key for the Journeyfront integration

To configure the Greenhouse Recruiting / Journeyfront integration, you'll need to create a Harvest API key.

Follow the steps in [this article](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/5888163769883) to create the key, and verify that the credentials and permissions below are selected when configuring the Journeyfront integration.

#### Credentials

In the _Create New Credential_ box, make the following selections:

  * **API type:** Harvest
  * **Partner:** Journeyfront
  * **Description:** Journeyfront Harvest API key



#### Permissions

  * **Applications**
    * GET: Retrieve Application
    * PATCH: Update Application
    * POST: Advance Application
    * POST: Add Attachment to Application



### Share User ID with Journeyfront

In order for Journeyfront to make automatic updates in Greenhouse Recruiting, Journeyfront will need the user ID of an existing Greenhouse user in your organization, or the user ID for a Greenhouse Recruiting user account that is created specifically for Journeyfront.

To find a user ID, [export your user list](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/200521129) and retrieve the value from the **User ID** column.

Share the User ID with your Journeyfront representative.

### Create a webhook

To integrate Journeyfront with Greenhouse Recruiting, you'll need to create a webhook. Follow the steps in [this article](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/5888163727003) to create your webhook. Use the values listed below to configure the webhooks.

  * **Name** : Journeyfront Assessment Invite
  * **When** : Candidate has submitted application
  * **Endpoint URL** : Update the URL to include your organization's account name: 
    * Webhook for test environment: 
      * <https://api-stage.journeyfront.com/v1/assessment_invite/?account={account}>
    * Webhook for production environment: 
      * <https://api.journeyfront.com/v1/assessment_invite/?account={account}>
  * **Secret key** : Enter the secret key provided to you by Journeyfront
  * **Error recipient email** : [integrations@journeyfront.com](mailto:integrations@journeyfront.com)
  * **Advanced Settings**
    * **Maximum attempts:** 4
    * **Disabled?** No



### Add a custom job field

Some information for this integration must be stored in a custom job field. [Create a new custom field](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/202609855) using the following options:

  * **Field name:** _Journeyfront Assessment Link_
  * **Description:** _Unique Journeyfront assessment link for each job req_
  * **Type:** Short textbox



**Note:** Enter the field name exactly as specified above for the integration to work properly.

### Create Journeyfront interview stages

Two unique stages must be created for each job that will be administering Journeyfront assessments. [Create two interview stages with the following names:](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/115002194903)

  * **Stage 1:** Journeyfront Assessment Sent
  * **Stage 2:** Journeyfront Assessment Complete



**Note:** Place these stages directly after Application Review if you'd like the candidates to automatically get an email when they apply for a job.

### Configure Journeyfront interview stages

After they're created, you'll need to add the correct JourneyFront Assessment link to each job stage. Each job will have a unique link for candidates, provided by Journeyfront.

Log into your Journeyfront account and click **Hire.** Click the name of the SmartReq you want to link to in Greenhouse Recruiting and navigate to **Actions** > **Invite Applicants**. Copy the invitation link.

Return to Greenhouse Recruiting and modify the job you want to integrate. Paste the URL in the _Journeyfront Assessment Link_ custom job field.

Click **Save**.

Repeat these steps for each job req on which you wish to send Journeyfront assessments.

### Test the integration

Add a test candidate to a job with a Journeyfront assessment, using an email address that is different than the email address for your Greenhouse Recruiting account.

When you move the candidate to the _Journeyfront Assessment Sent_ stage, check the inbox for the email address and verify that the test candidate received an email from Journeyfront inviting the candidate to take the assessments.

If needed, you can select this link and complete the Journeyfront Assessments. After a short delay (10 minutes) the candidate's completed assessment will display in Greenhouse Recruiting. Additionally, the candidate should be automatically moved to the Journeyfront Assessment Complete stage.

Make sure the Journeyfront fields have been filled with values and click the Journeyfront scorecard to ensure the values are displaying correctly.

### Additional support

Contact [support@journeyfront.com](mailto:support@journeyfront.com) for troubleshooting assistance regarding the integration.

# Wonderlic Select integration

With over 80+ years of experience in providing objective candidate insights that predict only the most successful fits for your open positions, Wonderlic is the pioneer of pre-employment assessments. 

Through validated scientific research and award-winning expertise for i/o psychology, AI-technology, and machine learning, Wonderlic identifies top talent who showcase the cognitive ability, personality and motivation needed to succeed in your roles through whole-person, multi-measure assessments. 

Robust insights into what candidates can do, will do, and want to do are all gained using Wonderlic's pre-hire assessment tool, WonScore, allowing your team to move quickly on the candidates most likely to be successful. 

Greenhouse Recruiting's integration with Wonderlic allows you to seamlessly add the Wonderlic Select assessment stage to a job's interview plan.

  * Additional resources

  * All permissions

Once the candidate has submitted their test, the Interview Kit will contain a link and access code to view the submitted test in the Wonscore application.

Click **View** **Report** and use the Access Code provided to see the candidate’s results in Wonscore.

### Additional resources

# Screenloop integration

Greenhouse Recruiting’s integration with Screenloop brings data and benchmarks to every step of your hiring process. This enables your talent teams to track, analyse, and compare candidates' experience across teams, regions, and the entire recruitment process.

Screenloop supports Greenhouse as an ATS provider. Once the integration is set up and enabled, your organization will be able to automatically synchronize job positions, candidates, interview information and more!

#### In this article

  * Configure user setup permissions in Greenhouse Recruiting
  * Install Greenhouse within Screenloop
  * Setup Greenhouse and Screenloop
    * Create a Screenloop service user in Greenhouse
    * Retrieve the user ID for the Screenloop user within Greenhouse
    * Retrieve the Instance URL from your Screenloop user within Greenhouse
    * Create a Harvest API key for the Greenhouse Recruiting / Screenloop integration
    * Finalize the setup
  * Use the Screenloop integration with Greenhouse Recruiting
  * Support



### Configure user setup permissions in Greenhouse Recruiting

In order to create a user who can integrate Screenloop with Greenhouse, you will need the developer permission, **Can m****anage ALL organization’s API Credentials**.

Contact a Greenhouse user in your organization with **Site Admin** level permissions, including the additional user-specific permission **Can edit another user's advanced permissions** to apply the API credential management permission to your account. 

The Site Admin can edit the permissions for your user account by navigating to **Configure** > **Users** > **Your Name**.

### Install Greenhouse within Screenloop

To perform the following steps, you need to have **site administrator** permissions.

  1. Sign in to the[ ](https://app.screenloop.com/)[Screenloop web portal](https://app.screenloop.com/)
  2. Click **Organization Settings** at the bottom of the navigation panel on the left
  3. Click **Integrations** in the pop-up panel on the left
  4. Click **Connect** with the Greenhouse integration



Keep the _Greenhouse integration form_ within Screenloop open. Open a new tab in your browser and follow the remaining Greenhouse setup steps in this article. As you complete the steps within Greenhouse, you'll use the information to fill out the _Greenhouse integration form_ in Screenloop. 

Reach out to[ ](https://app.screenloop.com/support)[Screenloop's support](https://app.screenloop.com/support) if you experience any technical issues. 

### Setup Greenhouse and Screenloop

#### Create a Screenloop service user in Greenhouse

To begin, navigate to the **User** configure page (**Configure** > **Users**). Then, click **\+ New Users**.

Type in **< your-company-name>@greenhouse.screenloop.com** in the _Enter user emails_ field. 

Next, **a****ssign** **Site Admin** permissions in the  _Set permissions_ panel. 

**Uncheck** the _Send invitation email_ box and do not add interviewer tags.

Click **Save** when done. 

#### Retrieve the user ID for the Screenloop user within Greenhouse

You'll need the Site Admin user ID of the Screenloop user within Greenhouse in order to setup the integration. 

To identify the user ID, navigate to the **User** configure page within Greenhouse. (**Configure > Users > Screenloop User**)

**Tip:** Quickly locate the user by searching by their email, **< your-company-name>@greenhouse.screenloop.com**, in the _Filter Users_ search bar. 

Once located, click on the **Screenloop user's name**. 

The **user ID** is the numeric string of numbers in the _URL_.

**Copy** the user ID, then return to the Screenloop tab in your browser and **paste** the user ID in the designated field. 

#### Retrieve the Instance URL from your Screenloop user within Greenhouse

The next field to complete on the Screenloop integration screen is the Instance URL.

Within Greenhouse, copy the **host URL** (for example, app3.greenhouse.io) and **paste** the host URL into the **Instance URL**  _input box_ in the Greenhouse Integration page on Screenloop.

#### Create a Harvest API key for the Greenhouse Recruiting / Screenloop integration

**Note:** To generate an API key, you must have the developer permission **Can manage ALL organization's API Credentials.**

To create a Harvest API key for the integration, click on the **Configure** icon in the top right corner of your Greenhouse Recruiting. 

Navigate to**Dev Center** on the left-sidepanel. From the _Dev Center_ page, click **API Credential Management**.

From the _API Credential Management_ page, click**Create New API Key** to generate the API key for Screenloop.

In the _Create New Credential_ dialog box, make the following selections:

  * **API Type** : Harvest
  * **Partner** : Screenloop
  * **Description** : _Screenloop_



When finished, click **Manage Permissions** to generate the Harvest API key.

On the next page, click **Copy** to save your API key to your clipboard. Store it in a secure place because it will be used later on in the integration setup. 

Click **I have stored the API Key** once you have copied and saved the key.

**Note:** Make sure to store the API key in a secure location to provide to the partner in the next step.

Each key is unique, and for security purposes, you won’t be able to view it after it has been generated on this window.

If you lose the API key, you’ll need to generate a new one and provide it to the partner.

On the _Manage API Key Permissions_ page, **select ALL** permissions.

When finished, click **Save**.

Finally, navigate to your Screenloop tab and input the **API key** in the Screenloop Integration page under _API Token_.

#### Finalize the setup

After ensuring all the fields are completed successfully, click **Submit.**

Once successful, you'll see the message,  _Greenhouse integration successfully updated!_

To get the most out of Screenloop, platform users should install the Screenloop Chrome Extension[ ](https://chrome.google.com/webstore/detail/screenloop/gdpkbebflcgjacfhhekofebajjacgidj?hl=en-US)[here](https://chrome.google.com/webstore/detail/screenloop/gdpkbebflcgjacfhhekofebajjacgidj?hl=en-US).

### Use the Screenloop integration with Greenhouse Recruiting

The Screenloop integration provides the full context when filling out your scorecard by offering you a full view of your interviews, allowing you access to the interview video and transcript, and all the documented notes. 

On the _candidate’s activity feed_ , we also post a link of the interview recording for easy access and storage within Greenhouse.

### Support

You can reach the Screenloop team via email at [support@screenloop.com](support@screenloop.com). The Help Center page is also available [here](https://help.screenloop.com/en/articles/5469959-setup-greenhouse-for-screenloop).[ ](https://app.screenloop.com/support)

# Enabling teams guide

****

### Set your team up for structured hiring success

**Train your organization on structured hiring and establish a process for ongoing adoption.**

Greenhouse has worked with thousands of leading companies, so we’ve been able to identify the most effective ways to introduce Greenhouse and drive adoption of structured hiring processes across your organization.

Here are the most common launch tactics our customers swear by:

  * Referral programs – launch or promote existing [incentive-based programs](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360004175751-Best-Practices-Sourcing-Strategies#%E2%80%9C3%E2%80%9D)
  * Executive sponsorship – announce Greenhouse at company-wide meetings to [promote awareness](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/115003739232-Greenhouse-Roll-Out-Toolkit-Start-Here-)
  * Training – conduct in-product training, led by experts at the company, or let teams learn at their own pace with our [Customer education page,](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/sections/9405519602587-Customer-education-) featuring the latest on-demand tutorials and live training events
  * You can also learn more about our [Strategic training offering](https://www.greenhouse.io/blog/strategic-training-by-greenhouse) from our Professional Services team
  * Activation – use posters, flyers and newsletters to help spread the word there’s a new tool in town



Follow these four steps to build a plan for establishing company-wide structured hiring training and adoption.

### Here’s the plan

  * **Create permission guidelines**
  * **Launch or refresh your referral program**
  * **Organize a Greenhouse rollout plan**
  * **Build a culture of great hiring**



# Step 1

### Create permission guidelines

Here’s what you need to keep in mind when setting up Greenhouse permissions. 

**Be intentional about who receives admin permissions**

Because they have the highest level of access in Greenhouse, limit the number of Site Admins and ensure they’re enabled to support a strong candidate experience.

  * Advanced/Expert tier only: Use [custom user fields](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/7987443593499-Manage-custom-user-fields) to further specify how you categorize and assign your user permissions 
  * Learn how to set up permissions in three easy steps with [this short video](https://greenhouse-software.wistia.com/medias/8y9jnr1bbe):



**– Get familiar with user permission settings**

**– Review permission resources with your team** to get aligned on how permissions work in Greenhouse

**– Outline user responsibilities and roles** to determine who needs access to key data in your organization and apply your permissions

**Catch up on our permissions resources**

  * Watch the [Learn Greenhouse course](https://learn.greenhouse.io/understand-and-apply-permissions-in-greenhouse) on applying permissions in Greenhouse to help identify the best permission structure for your organization
  * Check out our [live training calendar](https://learn.greenhouse.io/calendar) for upcoming offerings on permission training
  * Keep these resources handy when determining user permissions: [user-specific permissions overview](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360021050791-User-Specific-Permissions-Overview) and [user permission levels](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360039614171-User-permission-levels)  
  




**Create permissions documentation**

This will make it easier for your team to assign the correct permissions to new users as you continue to grow. Getting it right is essential to ensure data integrity, avoid confusion on your teams and ultimately create the best experience for all. 

**Create an offboarding process to remove access**  
Have a structure in place for removing access to Greenhouse for team members that leave your organization.

Take a look at [this Learn Greenhouse course](https://learn.greenhouse.io/understand-and-apply-permissions-in-greenhouse) on understanding applying permissions in Greenhouse to identify the best permission structure for your organization.

# Step 2

###  Launch or refresh your referral program

[Employee referrals](https://www.greenhouse.io/blog/making-the-case-for-employee-referral-programs) are the best source for quality talent leads as they generally cost less to hire, perform better and stay longer than externally sourced candidates. Check out [these five steps for building a strong referral program](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1w5PV5eD2H5umeMtNt25UY8fILUBx33Xe/view) at your company and share [this Learn Greenhouse course](https://learn.greenhouse.io/interviews-and-referrals/863612) with your employees to ensure they understand how to submit referrals.

Operationally, you’ll want to make sure your referral program has been properly configured with the [relevant questions](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/202610325-Add-a-custom-referral-question) and keeps employees informed with an [up-to-date referral page](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/205162775-How-do-I-inform-users-about-our-company-s-referral-program-).

Enhance your referral program using integrations with several [referral sourcing partners](https://www.greenhouse.io/integrations?category=sourcing-parent&q=&page=1)that Greenhouse offers to help you create effective and efficient programs.

# Step 3

###  Organize a Greenhouse rollout plan

We’ve gathered the templates our most successful customers use to launch Greenhouse and get their teams’ buy-in. 

**Permission level** | **Tasks** | **Announcement emails** | **Training guidance**  
---|---|---|---  
**Basic**  
(all employees) |  Submit and track referrals Share jobs on social media Access internal job board   
(available in Recruiting Advanced and Recruiting Expert) |  [Greenhouse rollout launch day email template ](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/21216751399579) [Greenhouse overview video](https://greenhouse-software.wistia.com/medias/amvjec84q4) |  [Basic user training template ](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/201981500-PRESENTATION-PPT-Greenhouse-101-for-Basic-Users) [Learn Greenhouse – Submit referrals](https://learn.greenhouse.io/interviews-and-referrals/863612) [Post jobs to social media](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/115002226806-Post-jobs-to-social-media-from-Greenhouse-Recruiting)   
[Making referrals video](https://learn.greenhouse.io/interviews-and-referrals?next=%2Finterviews-and-referrals%2F863612)  
  
|  Conduct interviews  
  
Submit scorecards |  |  [Interviewer training template](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/201981520-Greenhouse-training-guide-for-interviewers) DE&I interviewer features  Tip: Ensure an inclusive interview experience for candidates by collecting each candidate’s name pronunciation and personal pronouns and reviewing inclusion nudges  Tip: Conduct a 30-minute company-led training Tip: Be sure to check our [customer education page](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/sections/9405519602587-Customer-education-) for the latest live trainings  
**Job admin**  
(hiring managers, coordinators, recruiters) |  Interviewer + Company-specific workflows   
(creating jobs, requesting approvals, advancing candidates, etc.) |  Same as above |  [Job admin/hiring manager training template](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/201981530-Greenhouse-training-guide-for-hiring-managers-and-recruiters) Tip: Conduct a 40–65-minute company-led training   
Tip: Check our [customer education page](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/sections/9405519602587-Customer-education-) for the latest live trainings  
  
**Site admin** |  Everything |  Same as above |  [Greenhouse training guide for Site Admin](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/8167950201115-Greenhouse-training-guide-for-Site-Admin)  
  
# Step 4

### Build a culture of great hiring

Once you’ve rolled out Greenhouse, it’s important to continually reinforce structured hiring processes to keep them top-of-mind for everyone at your organization. Here are a few of the top ways our customers drive cultures of great hiring. 

**Keep communication consistent**

Consistent and ongoing communication is key to ensuring everyone stays on track. Keep your team engaged throughout the hiring process with notifications, such as:  


  * Live role announcements for interviewers and hiring managers
  * Pipeline updates for hiring managers and stakeholders
  * Recruiting updates for key stakeholders



Check out these [email templates](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/115003739232-Greenhouse-rollout-toolkit-Start-here) to start communicating with your hiring team.

**Track ongoing progress**

At Greenhouse, our average time-to-hire – from role creation to offer acceptance – is between eight and 12 weeks. This timing can vary, but we measure our performance and effectiveness against diligent responsibilities, expectations and deadlines set with each person involved in the hiring process. 

While your company’s hiring process is unique and timelines may vary, it’s important that those timelines are established and then communicated throughout the organization. We’ve mapped out the Greenhouse recruiting workflow here for context. 

**Train new hires on Greenhouse**

Make sure that structured hiring with Greenhouse remains a company-wide priority by including training in your new hire onboarding process. Here are a few handy Greenhouse training templates for some of the most common roles:   


  * [New admin training](https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1z8ZM7QOaH50Qfx-vhs6wVqTyYuw59bMzpgwyllll_8A/edit#gid=224541986)
  * [Hiring manager training](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/201981530-PRESENTATION-PPT-Greenhouse-101-for-Hiring-Managers)
  * [Interviewer training](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/201981520-PRESENTATION-PPT-Greenhouse-101-for-Interviewers)  




Check out our [customer education page](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/sections/9405519602587-Customer-education-) for the latest on-demand tutorials and live training events.

# Sourcer integration

Sourcer helps companies scale up their hiring strategies with comprehensive sourcing and recruiting solutions.

Sourcer’s integration with Greenhouse Recruiting allows talent acquisition teams to seamlessly integrate Sourcer into their existing candidate pipeline by exporting the jobs from Greenhouse to Sourcer and uploading new candidates from Sourcer to Greenhouse. Any updates made to candidate applications on Sourcer reflect in your Greenhouse account and vice versa, keeping both platforms in sync with real-time status of jobs and candidates.

In this article

  * Create a Harvest API key
  * Add your API key to Sourcer
  * Create a custom Job field (optional)
  * Create webhooks
  * Setting up On-Behalf-Of user in Sourcer
  * Setting up job imports from Greenhouse
  * Setting up candidate uploads to Greenhouse
  * Use the Sourcer integration with Greenhouse Recruiting
  * Additional resources



### Create a Harvest API key

To configure the Sourcer integration, you’ll need to create a Harvest API key.

Follow the steps in [this article](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/5888163769883) to create the key, and verify that the permissions below are selected when configuring the Sourcer integration.

#### **Credentials**

In the _Create New Credential_ box, make the following selections:

  * **API Type** : Harvest
  * **Partner** : Sourcer or Unlisted Vendor
  * **Description** : Sourcer Harvest API Key



#### **Permissions**

Verify that the following permissions are selected for the Sourcer integration:

  * **Activity Feed**
    * All permissions
  * **Applications**
    * All permissions
  * **Candidates**
    * DELETE: Delete Candidate
    * GET: Retrieve Candidate
    * GET: List Candidates
    * PATCH: Edit Candidate
    * POST: Add Candidate
    * POST: Add E-mail
    * POST: Add Note
    * POST: Add Attachment
    * POST: Add Application
    * POST: Add Education
    * POST: Add Employment
    * POST: Add Prospect
  * **Close Reasons**
    * All permissions
  * **Job Posts**
    * GET: List Job Posts
    * GET: Retrieve Job Post for Job
    * GET: List Job Posts for Job
  * **Jobs**
    * GET: Retrieve Job
    * GET: List Jobs
  * **Job Stages**
    * All permissions
  * **Offers**
    * All permissions
  * **Rejection Reasons**
    * All permissions
  * **Scheduled Interviews**
    * GET: List Interviews for Application
    * GET: Retrieve Interview
    * GET: List Interviews
  * **Users**
    * GET: List Users
    * GET: Retrieve User



### Add your API key to Sourcer

Add your Greenhouse API Key in Sourcer and click Connect to establish the connection between your Sourcer and Greenhouse accounts.

### Create a custom Job field (optional)

If you prefer to automatically import all open jobs from Greenhouse into your Sourcer account, you can skip this section. If you prefer to pick which Greenhouse jobs should be imported into your Sourcer account, follow the instructions below to allow Greenhouse users to specify whether a job should be sent to Sourcer. You will also need to select the **Import selected jobs from Greenhouse** setting on the Settings page after the initial connection has been established.

To create a custom Job field, click the **Configure** icon  on your navigation bar, then click **Custom** **Options** on the left.

Click **Jobs**.

Click **Add field** , and enter the following details to configure the new field:

  * **Name** : Send job to Sourcer?
  * **Type** : Yes/No



### Create webhooks

To integrate Sourcer with Greenhouse Recruiting, you’ll need to create 12 webhooks.

Follow the steps in [this article](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/5888163727003) to create each webhook. Use the values listed below to configure the webhook:

  * **Name** : A descriptive name for your integration. Most customers choose ‘Sourcer integration - <event name>’
  * **When** : Create a separate webhook for each event: 
    * Job created
    * Job updated
    * Job deleted
    * Job post created
    * Candidate or prospect rejected
    * Candidate or prospect unrejected
    * Candidate has changed stage
    * Candidate has been hired
    * Candidate has been unhired
    * Delete candidate
    * Delete application
    * Offer created
  * **Endpoint URL** : The Endpoint URL provided by Sourcer
  * **Secret Key** : The Secret Key provided by Sourcer



#### **Setting up On-Behalf-Of user in Sourcer**

Select a Greenhouse user for Sourcer to assign as the **On-Behalf-Of** user. Note that candidate ownership will be assigned to the corresponding Greenhouse job owner regardless of the chosen On-Behalf-Of user.

#### **Setting up job imports from Greenhouse**

If you prefer to automatically import all open jobs from Greenhouse into your Sourcer account, select **Import all open jobs from Greenhouse** setting. If you prefer for your recruiters to select which Greenhouse jobs should be imported into your Sourcer account, select the **Import selected jobs from Greenhouse** setting. You will also need to create the custom field on Greenhouse to select the specific jobs to be imported into Sourcer.

#### **Setting up candidate uploads to Greenhouse**

If you prefer to automatically upload all submitted candidates to the corresponding jobs in Greenhouse, select **Automatically upload all candidates on submission** setting. If you prefer to manually upload only handpicked candidates to the corresponding jobs, select **Manually upload selected candidates only** setting. If you prefer to configure the interview stage at which the candidates would be automatically uploaded to Greenhouse, select **Automatically upload all candidates upon reaching a preset stage** setting, then select the specific stage of the interview process from **Interview Stage to Upload to ATS** dropdown.

### Use the Sourcer integration with Greenhouse Recruiting

Once a candidate has been uploaded to Greenhouse, any stage changes will be reflected in Sourcer, ensuring your Sourcer account stays as up-to-date as possible.

Any candidates from your Sourcer account that were submitted to jobs that were not linked to Greenhouse jobs will be uploaded as prospects.

To ensure there are no duplicate candidates uploaded to Greenhouse, Sourcer checks for existing candidates prior to uploading new candidates by comparing existing email addresses in your Greenhouse account to those found by Sourcer.

### Additional resources

For additional information or troubleshooting not covered here, reach out to Sourcer at [support@sourcer.com](mailto:support@sourcer.com).

# Goals report dashboard

**Permissions:** Job Admins and above

**Product tier:** Available for new subscription tiers (Core, Plus, and Pro)

The Goals report dashboard offers a one-stop, at-a-glance view into how your organization's [company goals](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/8382420999835) are progressing over time. Use this dashboard to monitor your goal attainment levels quickly and gain actionable insights for your hiring strategies.

#### In this article

### View goals report dashboard

To view the Goals report, click **Reports** on your navigation bar.

Click **Essential****library** on the left.

Click the **Dashboards** tab and then choose **Goals**.

On the Goals dashboard page, you'll find widgets that display your attainment percentage for each company goal over the period of time you've selected as a filter. Scroll to check out available widgets or adjust filters to narrow your dashboard results.

**Note:** Attainment percentages are calculated as the number of actions completed on time (based on your organization's [target value](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/8382420999835)) divided by the total number of actions taken during the last 90 days (or the time period you've selected as your filter).

Click on a widget's title to view the [full report](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/8383632617755) for each company goal.

### Available widgets

Use the following dashboard widgets to learn more about your organization's progress on company goals.

#### Time in stage attainment

Use this widget to see your organization's current attainment of the [time in stage](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/9964759087899) company goal.

#### Time to approve offers attainment

Use this widget to measure your organization's current attainment of the [time to approve offers](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/9166643653403) company goal.

#### Time to review applications attainment

Use this widget to measure your organization's current attainment of the [time to review applications](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/10061338502171) company goal.

#### Time to schedule available candidates attainment

Use this widget to measure your organization's current attainment of the [time to schedule available candidates](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/9166289363739) company goal.

#### Time to submit scorecards attainment

Use this widget to measure your organization's current attainment of the [time to submit scorecards](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/7507124760347) company goal.

### Filter dashboard

You can use the following filters to adjust your dashboard's results and quickly find the company goal metrics you need.

#### Last 90 days

By default, this filter will show you goal attainment metrics for the last 90 days. You can also select from a variety of different date ranges or create a custom date range for your filter.
