# Built for Teams integration

Greenhouse Recruiting’s integration with Built for Teams allows you to easily import your job requisitions from Greenhouse directly into your Built for Teams account. This integration, combined with the Built for Teams position management module, allows you to connect requisitions to open positions in Built for Teams.

#### In this article

  * Create a Harvest API key for the Greenhouse Recruiting / Built for Teams integration
  * Enable the Built for Teams integration
  * Use the Built for Teams integration with Greenhouse Recruiting
  * Additional resources



### Create a Harvest API key for the Greenhouse Recruiting / Built for Teams integration

To configure the Greenhouse Recruiting / Built for Teams integration, you'll need to create a Harvest API key.

Follow the steps in [this article](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/5888163769883) to create the key, and verify that the credentials and permissions below are selected when configuring the Built for Teams integration.

#### Credentials

In the _Create New Credential_ box, make the following selections:

  * **API type:** Harvest
  * **Partner:** Built for Teams (optional)
  * **Description:** Built for Teams Harvest API Key



#### Permissions

Verify that the following permissions are selected for the Built for Teams integration:

**Jobs**

  * Get: List Jobs



When finished, click **Save**.

Your Harvest API key for the Greenhouse Recruiting / Built for Teams integration is created and configured. You will need to enter this key into the Built for Teams interface in the next step to complete the setup.

### Enable the Built for Teams integration

To enable the Built for Teams integration, login to your Built for Teams account and navigate to **Settings** > **Integrations**.

Click the **Greenhouse** hyperlink in the list of integrations.

Paste in your Harvest API key from the previous step, and click **Connect**.

### Use the Built for Teams integration with Greenhouse Recruiting

After successfully enabling the integration, your data will be imported automatically from Greenhouse Recruiting, and daily automatic imports will be enabled.

#### Manually import job requisition data from Greenhouse Recruiting

You may also initiate a manual import from Greenhouse Recruiting at any time from the Job Requisitions page in Built for Teams.

To manually enable an import, navigate to **Positions** >**Job Requisitions.**

Click **Import**.

Once the import is complete, click **View Job Requisitions**.

#### Connect job requisitions to positions in Built for Teams

To connect job requisitions to positions in Built for Teams, navigate to **Positions > Job Requisitions **in Built for Teams. You can find the requisition you would like to connect to a position by filtering the list by the status of the requisition. You can also find requisitions using the search field. To see more details about a requisition, click the job requisition name or job requisition number.

Click **Connect Position** in the Position ID column.

Enter the title or position ID of the existing position, or click **Add New Position** to create a new position.

When finished, click **Save**.

#### Configure automatic imports

With the Built for Teams integration, imports are enabled by default. However, you can configure the frequency and notifications for automatic imports.

Navigate to **Settings > Imports** in Built for Teams. Click **Edit** beside the _Greenhouse Import Settings_ section.

In the _Enable Automatic Imports_ field, click **Yes**. Select your desired import frequency, and enter an email address where the system can send a notification email each time the automated import process completes.

When finished, click **Save**.

#### Deactivate automatic imports

Automatic imports are enabled by default. To deactivate automatic imports, navigate to **Settings** > **Imports** in Built for Teams. Click **Edit** beside the _Greenhouse Import Settings_ section.

In the _Enable Automatic Imports_ field, click **No**.

#### Deactivate the Built for Teams integration

To deactivate the Built for Teams integration, navigate to **Settings** > **Integrations** in Built for Teams.

Click **Greenhouse** in the list of integrations, and then click **Deactivate**.

Click **OK**.

**Note** : After you've disconnected the Built for Teams integration, you will no longer be able to view or edit the data in the job requisitions table, and no future imports from Greenhouse Recruiting will take place.

### Additional resources

For troubleshooting or additional information not covered here, check out the Built for Teams [Knowledge Base](https://support.builtforteams.com/en/) or reach out to [support@builtforteams.com](mailto:support@builtforteams.com).

# Business Intelligence Connector update: May 28, 2026

We are updating the Business Intelligence Connector on **May 28, 2026**.

This update does not include a schema change, but you can still [find and download the latest schema here](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/12373826600603-Business-Intelligence-Connector-schema).

### Overview of changes

#### Behavioral change to `created_at` in the scorecards table

Previously, when a scorecard was submitted, the `created_at` timestamp in the `scorecards` table was overwritten to match the submission time. As a result, `created_at` and `submitted_at` held the same value.

After this update, `created_at` will reflect the time the scorecard record was originally created (when the interviewer started the draft), and will no longer be overwritten on submission. The `submitted_at` column, introduced in April 2022, will continue to capture the time the scorecard was submitted.

  * **Before this change:** `created_at` = submission time (same as `submitted_at`)
  * **After this change:** `created_at` = time the scorecard draft was started; `submitted_at` = time the scorecard was submitted



**Note:** This is a back-end behavioral change only. No columns have been added, removed, or renamed in the BIC schema. However, the values in `created_at` for future scorecard submissions will differ from historical values, which were set to match submission time.

### Required action

If your reports, dashboards, or queries use `scorecards.created_at` as a proxy for scorecard submission time, update them to reference `scorecards.submitted_at` instead.

No action is required if your reports use `submitted_at` already, or if they use `created_at` for its intended purpose (record creation time).

# Landing.jobs integration

Landing.jobs is a tech recruitment marketplace dedicated to matchmaking top tech professionals with curated job offers from top employers. With a chronic tech skills shortage across the globe, high-caliber candidates are in high demand and yet are still lost in the noise of generic job boards or overlooked by recruitment agencies that lack increasingly complex sector knowledge.

Greenhouse Recruiting's integration with Landing.jobs allows you to source, access, engage, and track candidates from Landing.jobs.

#### In this article

  * Enable the Landing.jobs integration
  * Use the Landing.jobs integration
    * Add candidates to Greenhouse Recruiting
    * Track Greenhouse Recruiting candidates in Landing.jobs
  * Additional resources



### Enable the Landing.jobs integration

To enable the integration, log into Landing.jobs.

Go to your company profile page and click the **Integrations** tab.

Find the Greenhouse tile and click **Connect.**

Enter your Greenhouse email address and password and click **Authorize**.

You'll see a success message at the top of the page confirming that the integration is live.

The Greenhouse tile on your Integrations page will also now have a **Disconnect** button.

### Use the Landing.jobs integration

#### Add candidates to Greenhouse Recruiting

On your dashboard, you’ll be able to select a job in Landing.jobs and pair it with a job in Greenhouse Recruiting.

Open the job in Landing.jobs.

On the Job dashboard, click **Pair with Greenhouse** in the top right corner of the page.

You'll now see the list of all of your Greenhouse Recruiting jobs. Select the job that you'd like to pair with Landing.jobs and click **Pair**.

Enable the **Automatically export candidates** checkbox to receive Landing.jobs candidates automatically in your Greenhouse Recruiting account. This way, when Landing.jobs completes reviewing a candidate, you won't need to sign in to Landing.jobs to manually export them.

If you would prefer to manually export candidates from Landing.jobs to Greenhouse, untick the **Automatically export candidates** box.Then, follow the steps below for each candidate you'd like to export to Greenhouse:

Open the candidate's application in Landing.jobs and click **More.**

Click **Export to Greenhouse.**

#### Track Greenhouse Recruiting candidates in Landing.jobs

You'll also be able to track a candidate's Greenhouse Recruiting status within Landing.jobs.

On the Application screen, find the **Greenhouse application status** tile and click **Sync.** This will update the Landing.jobs record with the current state of the application in Greenhouse Recruiting.

### Additional resources

If you have questions or need additional support using this integration, reach out to Landing.jobs at [wegotyourback@Landing.Jobs](mailto:wegotyourback@Landing.Jobs).

# Talenthub integration

Talenthub.io provides a platform that lets you gather candidate feedback throughout the recruitment process and help you extract insights with which to build exceptional candidate experiences.

Greenhouse Recruiting's integration with Talenthub.io allows you to automatically gather data from your candidates as they proceed through your recruitment process.

#### In this article

  * Create a Harvest API key for the Talenthub integration
  * Retrieve Talenthub endpoint URL and secret key
  * Create webhooks for the Talenthub integration
  * Use the Talenthub integration with Greenhouse Recruiting
  * Additional resources



### Create a Harvest API key for the Talenthub integration

To configure the Greenhouse Recruiting / Talenthub integration, you'll need to create a Harvest API key.

Follow the steps in [this article](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/5888163769883) to create the key, and verify that the credentials and permissions below are selected when configuring the Talenthub integration.

#### Credentials

In the _Create New Credential_ box, make the following selections:

  * **API type:** Harvest
  * **Partner:** Talenthub
  * **Description:** Talenthub Harvest API key



#### Permissions

Verify that the following permissions are selected for the Talenthub integration:

To create a Harvest API key for the integration, click on the **Configure** icon  in the upper right-han

**Applications**

  * GET: Retrieve application



**Candidates**

  * GET: Retrieve candidate



**Custom Fields**

  * GET: Get custom fields



**Job Posts**

  * GET: List job posts



**Job Stages**

  * GET: Retrieve job stage
  * GET: List job stages
  * GET: List job stages for job



**Jobs**

  * GET: Retrieve job
  * GET: Get hiring team



**Offers**

  * Get: Retrieve application's current offer



**Scheduled Interviews**

  * GET: List interviews for application



**Scorecards**

  * GET: List scorecards for application



**Tags**

  * GET: List tags applied to candidate



**Users**

  * GET: Retrieve user



**Sources**

  * GET: List sources



When finished, click **Update**.

Your Harvest API key for the Greenhouse Recruiting / Talenthub.io integration is created and configured.

Provide your Harvest API key to your Talenthub.io Customer Success Representative so they can begin setting up the integration.

### Retrieve Talenthub endpoint URL and secret key

Before setting up your webhooks, Greenhouse Recruiting will need two pieces of information:

  * Talenthub.io's Endpoint URLs
  * Talenthub.io's Secret Key



You should be provided with this information by your Talenthub.io Customer Success Representative once you have sent them the API key.

### Create webhooks for the Talenthub integration

To integrate Talenthub with Greenhouse Recruiting, you'll need to create a webhook. Follow the steps in [this article](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/5888163727003) to create your webhook. Use the values listed below to configure the four webhooks.

  * **Name** : A descriptive name for your integration. Most customers choose 'Talenthub integration'
  * **When** : You will need to create a webhook for each of the following triggers:  
  

    * Candidate has submitted application
    * Candidate has been hired
    * Candidate has changed stage
    * Candidate or Prospect rejected
  * **Endpoint URL** : The Endpoint URL provided by Talenthub CSM team. They will provide you with a different URL for each of the triggers mentioned above.
  * **Secret Key** : The Secret Key provided by Talenthub. This value will be the same for all four webhooks.
  * **Error recipient email** : This is the email address that will be alerted when some error occurs in the webhooks. You can choose whether you want to forward this to yourself, one of your internal teams or to Talenthub at [thdev+greenhouse.alerts@talenthub.io](mailto:thdev+greenhouse.alerts@talenthub.io).



When finished, click **Create Web hook**.

Repeat this process until you've created a webhook for each of the four triggers listed above.

That's it! Your Greenhouse account and Talenthub.io account can now talk to each other.

Please reach out to your Talenthub.io Customer Success Representative with the good news so they can activate the integration and start sending out surveys.

### Use the Talenthub integration with Greenhouse Recruiting

Once the integration is enabled, you can proceed with your normal recruitment workflow, and the Talenthub.io platform will automatically send out relevant surveys to your candidates as they proceed through that workflow.

Your Talenthub.io Customer Success representative will have ensured that the integration is set up to survey the recruitment stages which matter most to you.

Depending on your needs, this could simply mean following the usual stages of application, interview, hire and rejection, but it could also include setups like onboarding surveys, hiring manager surveys, rejection-reason or department-specific surveys. We even offer a widget which can be used to collect input from your career page!

There's a multitude of survey templates available to ensure that you can collect relevant information for many different topics to help you get started.

Once we have collected some replies, you can log into the Talenthub.io platform and start analyzing your strengths and areas for improvement.

Talenthub.io also supports the use of custom variables to help enrich your survey responses with data from your Greenhouse Harvest API. This allows you to make use of Greenhouse data to filter, group and segment data within the Talenthub.io analytics platform.

Please speak to your Customer Success Representative to have them help work out the right setup for you.

Click the links below to get more information about how you can use Talenthub.io to bring your candidate experience to new levels:

If you are in need of any troubleshooting assistance regarding the integration, please contact your Talenthub.io Customer Success Representative.

# Pronouns and pronunciations overview

**Permissions:** Employees and above

**Product tier:** Available for Greenhouse Welcome and Greenhouse Onboarding subscription tiers

Inclusion matters for both the candidate experience and the new hire experience. Candidates have the option to include their [pronouns](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360055919252) and [name pronunciation](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360048410072) during the interview process in Greenhouse Recruiting. Once a candidate is marked as hired, their pronouns and pronunciations are automatically sent to Greenhouse Onboarding to foster an inclusive onboarding process.

# Maintain accurate hiring data

Inaccurate hiring data can cause frustration and confusion when running reports, and it can be overwhelming to try to correct bad information after it becomes apparent. But hiring doesn't have to be a headache – your organization can employ a few best practices to drive data integrity and resolve inaccurate hiring data.

#### In this article

  * Jobs and openings
  * Candidate records
  * Offers
  * How to audit for inaccurate hire data



### Jobs and openings

#### Open dates

Inaccurate open dates can cause discrepancies in reports, particularly for the time to hire report. Make sure accurate open dates are maintained at the job and opening level.

To confirm your job's open date, navigate to **Job** **Setup** > **Job** **Info** and view your job's open date. Click **Edit** icon to adjust the date if necessary.

To confirm openings' open dates on a job, navigate to Job Setup > **Approvals** > and scroll to _Openings_ to review your openings' open dates. Click **Manage** **Openings** to adjust the dates if necessary.

Finally, when hiring a candidate, double-check the opening you're hiring them against has the correct open date!

**Note** : If you add a candidate to Greenhouse Recruiting who was hired prior to the date on which you're adding them, be sure to adjust the open date of 1) the job, 2) the opening, and 3) the hired date on the offer. If you only adjust the latter, your reports could show `0` days to hire for the candidate.

#### Transfers

Some larger organizations may maintain [evergreen](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360000891392) or pipeline requisitions, for which they transfer hired candidates to a hire requisition. In these cases, it's important that your hire requisition show accurate open dates on 1) the job, 2) the opening, and 3) the hire date on the offer.

### Candidate records

Accurate candidate records ensure activity and hiring reports reflect reliable information.

If you add a candidate to Greenhouse Recruiting after you've already started considering them, backdate their application date.

To backdate an application date, navigate to the candidate profile (**Candidates** page > select or search for the candidate), and hover over the _Application_ _Review_ stage.

Click the **Edit** icon beside the _Applied On_ date.

Update the _Application_ _Date_ to the date you began considering them for the job.

### Offers

Each time you hire a candidate for a role, make sure you're resolving the offer by clicking **Mark** **Candidate** **as** **Hired** on the candidate profile under _Offer_ _Details_.

When hiring a candidate, double-check the opening you're hiring them against has the correct open date.

If the candidate's offer is updated in Greenhouse Recruiting on a different day than the actual offer was accepted or rejected, you should adjust those dates to reflect reality.

Navigate to the candidate profile (**Candidates** > Select or search for candidate), and click _Offer_ _Details_.

Ensure the dates on the offer are correct, or click the **Edit** icon to adjust the dates.

**Note** : It is possible to re-trigger [offer approval flows](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360035625832) if your organization has opted for changes to the start date to trigger a new offer version.

### How to audit for inaccurate hire data

There are a few different reports in Greenhouse Recruiting that can be helpful for finding inaccurate hiring data. Check out the table below to learn which report may be useful for you:

**Report** | **Look out for**  
---|---  
[Time to fill by job report](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/204635705) | If your time to hire report shows `0` days in the _Days to Hire_ column, it likely means a candidate was marked as hired on the same day that the job opening was marked as open.  
[Offer activity report](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/204635925) | If your offer activity report shows any offers on the _Outstanding Offers_ column, some candidate offers haven't been marked as accepted or rejected.  
[Time to hire by candidate report](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/203940469) | If your hiring speed per candidate report shows `0` days in the _Days to Offer_ column, it likely means a candidate was marked as hired on the same day that the job opening was marked as open.

# Web hook initiated job import integration

**Permissions: —**

**Product tier:** Available for new subscription tiers (Core, Plus, and Pro)

Access the latest version of Harvest API documentation at [**harvestdocs.greenhouse.io**](http://harvestdocs.greenhouse.io).  
  
Harvest API v1 and v2 will be deprecated and unavailable after August 31, 2026. Please make sure that your existing custom integrations use the latest version of Harvest (v3) by this date and any new integrations are developed with the latest version of Harvest API.

In some cases, your organization may need to initiate job creation in Greenhouse Recruiting and subsequently update the Greenhouse Recruiting job with information that is hosted in an HRIS.

This article outlines the workflow and API requests needed in order to update a job in Greenhouse Recruiting and import certain job information from an external HRIS by utilizing Greenhouse Recruiting's '[job created](https://developers.greenhouse.io/webhooks.html#job-created)' webhook and the [Greenhouse Harvest API](https://harvestdocs.greenhouse.io/).

#### In this article

  * Web hook initiated job import workflow
  * Web hook initiated job import diagram
  * Technical workflow: Catch the 'job created' webhook
  * Update or add custom job field values to existing jobs
  * Additional resources



### Web hook initiated job import workflow

When building a jobs integration between an HRIS and Greenhouse Recruiting, your organization may find that the HRIS is the source of truth for key data associated with particular roles, but doesn’t account for position/requisition creation and/or approval.

In these situations, your team may need to initiate job creation in Greenhouse Recruiting, and subsequently update the Greenhouse Recruiting job with information that is hosted in the HRIS.

In order to accomplish this goal, we recommend utilizing the '[job created](https://developers.greenhouse.io/webhooks.html#job-created)' webhook and the Harvest API endpoint [`PATCH: Update job`.](https://harvestdocs.greenhouse.io/reference/patch_v3-jobs-id)

#### Workflow:

1\. Create a job in Greenhouse Recruiting.

2\. Enter the job code, job profile, and/or level (whatever serves as the key identifier for the job attributes in the HRIS) on the Greenhouse Recruiting job.

**Note** : In this article we’ll refer to the job code, job profile, and/or level as the "HRIS Job Code."

3\. The integration will receive the '[job created](https://developers.greenhouse.io/webhooks.html#job-created)' webhook.

4\. The integration will use the HRIS Job Code to retrieve job information from the external system (HRIS/HCM).

5\. The integration will then update the Greenhouse Recruiting job with information from the HRIS.

Read more here.

### Web hook initiated job import diagram

### Technical workflow: Catch the 'job created' webhook

The '[job created](https://developers.greenhouse.io/webhooks.html#job-created)' webhook will send a payload of job data, including the HRIS Job Code, as soon as a job is created in Greenhouse Recruiting. This can then be used to gather the job information associated with that HRIS Job Code values in the HRIS. 

1\. Configure the '[job created](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360005574531-Enable-a-webhook)' webhook to send to the webhook listener in the integration layer/middleware.

2\. Catch the '[job created](https://developers.greenhouse.io/webhooks.html#job-created)' webhook in the integration layer.

**Example**
    
    
     { 
    
       "action": "job_created", 
       "payload": { 
         "job": { 
           "id": 371417, 
           "name": "Software Engineer", 
           "requisition_id": null, 
           "notes": "Looking for the best!", 
           "confidential": false, 
           "job_post_id": 2154, 
           "status": "open", 
           "created_at": "2016-10-20T18:16:32Z", 
           "opened_at": "2016-10-20T18:16:32Z", 
           "closed_at": null, 
           "custom_fields": { 
               >"job_code": { 
               "name": "JobCode", 
               "type": "single_select", 
               "value": “R101” 
               } 
             } 
           } 
         } 
       } 
     } 

3\. After catching the 'job created' webhook, the integration will use the HRIS Job Code value included in the webhook payload to retrieve the appropriate data from the HRIS (e.g. salary range, cost center, and other attributes associated with said Job Code in the HRIS). The integration should also store the Greenhouse Recruiting job ID included in the webhook.

4\. Once the HRIS attribute values associated with HRIS Job Code are retrieved, the integration should use the stored Greenhouse Recruiting job ID in an API request to update the Greenhouse job’s corresponding custom field values.

### Update or add default/custom job field values to existing jobs

Using the webhook initiated job import integration workflow, you may need to add or update default and custom job field values on existing jobs.

To make a PATCH request to update custom job field values:

1\. Use the Harvest API endpoint [`GET: List Custom Fields`](https://harvestdocs.greenhouse.io/reference/get_v3-custom-fields) to retrieve all custom job field name keys and available option values for single and multi-select fields.

**Note** : Any single or multi-select field values must match an available field option name or ID in Greenhouse exactly for the PATCH to be successful. 

2\. Once you have retrieved all custom job field name keys and available option values for single and multi-select fields, use the [`PATCH: Update job`](https://harvestdocs.greenhouse.io/reference/patch_v3-jobs-id) request to PATCH an existing job's custom field values.

3\. If you would like to incorporate updates to HRIS Job Code attributes so that any updates in the HRIS push over to the relevant Greenhouse Recruiting jobs, you may want to incorporate a scheduled cadence to check for updates, for example at the end of each day.

A.) Use the Harvest API endpoint [`GET: List Jobs`](https://harvestdocs.greenhouse.io/reference/get_v3-jobs) for all open or draft jobs in Greenhouse Recruiting, and store the Greenhouse Recruiting job ID and HRIS Job Code value.

B.) Cycle through each HRIS Job Code to retrieve the latest corresponding HRIS attribute values.

C.) For each HRIS Job Code, cycle through each Greenhouse Recruiting job with its respective HRIS Job Code value and use the Harvest API endpoint [`PATCH: Update Job` ](https://harvestdocs.greenhouse.io/reference/patch_v3-jobs-id)to overwrite the values that exist in Greenhouse Recruiting with the latest information from the HRIS.

### Additional resources

  * [Create a webhook](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360005574531-Enable-a-webhook)
  * [Harvest API overview](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360029266032-How-to-Establish-API-connectivity)
  * [Custom options sync overview](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360044483232-Custom-options-sync-overview)

# Candidate and prospect filters

**Permissions:** Job Admin who can view and edit candidates and prospects and above

**Product tier:** Available for new subscription tiers (Core, Plus, and Pro)

The _Candidates_ page includes a variety of filters that can be used to adjust the list of displayed candidate and prospect applications to make it easier to view specific sets of candidates, like those in prospect pools, with outstanding scheduling tasks, or assigned to a specific recruiter.

**Note:** The Candidates page displays individual candidate and prospect applications, and not individual candidate/prospect profiles. If a single candidate has applied to more than one job or a single prospect is in multiple pools, that person will appear on the Candidates page once per application, regardless of if those applications are associated with the same profile.

#### In this article

  * Use candidate filters
    * Apply candidate filter
    * Remove candidate filter
  * Available candidate filters
  * Additional resources



### Use candidate filters

To begin, click**Candidates** from the navigation bar.

You will be directed to the _Candidates_ page, which allows you to view a complete list of all applications that have been submitted to your organization. By default, the _Candidates_ page shows all active candidate applications on open jobs. The candidate filters on the left-hand panel can be used to edit or expand your search, such as to include prospects, rejected applications, or closed jobs.

#### Apply candidate filter

To apply a candidate filter, click the applicable section to expand.

Locate the filter you wish to apply and click the dropdown to select an option.

**Note:** Some filters use a checkbox or date range instead of a dropdown menu. See below for more guidance on the available filters.

The selected filter will be reflected at the top of the page, and the list of applications will adjust automatically to account for the filter.

Repeat this process to apply as many filters as necessary to adjust the list of applications.

**Note:** More than one option can be selected from a given filter. For example, if you wish to search for active, rejected, and hired candidate applications on open jobs, select each application status one at a time from the Profile Details > Status filter. Each filter will appear at the top of the All Candidates page as it is selected.

#### Remove candidate filter

To remove a candidate filter, locate the filter at the top of the _Candidates_ page and click the **X** to the right of the filters.

The filter will be removed, and the list of applications will adjust automatically to reflect the change.

### Available candidate filters

#### Application type

**Filter** | **Description**  
---|---  
**Type** |  The type of applications to be displayed. Options: Candidates only, Prospects only, Candidates + Prospects. **Note:** The 'Prospects only' and 'Candidates + Prospects' filters require the Prospect feature or CRM.  
**Exclude migrated candidates** | Checking this box removes applications migrated to Greenhouse Recruiting from your previous ATS during a data transfer, if applicable.  
**Prospects on No Jobs** |  Checking this box includes [unattached prospects](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/206729066) in your results. **Note:** This filter cannot be used if the Type filter is set to Candidates Only.  
  
#### Jobs

**Filter** | **Description**  
---|---  
**Filter By Job** | Display applications only for the selected jobs. This filter includes options to filter jobs by status (open, closed, draft), department, office, and more.  
**Stage** | Display applications currently in a specified stage.  
**Reached Milestone** | Display applications that reached or surpassed the selected [Milestone](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/208319943).  
**Job Post Submitted** | Display applications submitted through a specified job post.  
**To be sent** | Display applications for candidates who did not apply through your job board and have not been sent a [job post request email](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360002568971).  
**Pending submission** | Display applications for candidates who did not apply through your job board and have been sent a job post request email, but have not filled out the job post request yet.  
**Form and Form Status** | Display applications based on a specified form and the status of that form for the application (to be sent, pending submission, submitted).  
  
#### CRM

**Note:** CRM filters are available only for organizations with the Prospects and/or CRM features.

**Filter** | **Description**  
---|---  
**Prospect Pool** | Display prospect processes in a specified Prospect Pool.  
**Prospect Pool Stage** | Display prospect processes in a specified [Prospect Pool Stage](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360024904051).  
**Prospect Owner** | Display prospect processes assigned to a specified [Prospect Owner](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/115002698026).  
**Event** | Display prospect processes added through a specified [Event](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/115005216943).  
**Last Touchpoint** |  Display prospect processes based on the date of their most recently recorded [Touchpoint](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360020298312). **Note:** This touchpoint is only available for Expert tier customers.  
  
#### Profile details

**Filter** | **Description**  
---|---  
**Custom Field and Search Custom Field** | Display applications whose candidate profiles or applications include a specified response to a selected custom field. Filterable custom fields include [custom agency questions](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360040318592), [custom application fields](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/115003544472), [custom candidate fields](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/202609675), [custom offer fields](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360024551831), and [custom referral questions](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/202610325).  
**Candidate Tag** | Display applications whose candidate profiles include a specified [candidate tag](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360004149852).  
**Status** | Display applications based on the status associated with their application (active, rejected, hired, converted).  
**Rejection Reason** |  Display applications based on their rejection reason. **Note:** Be sure to first filter for applications with a **rejected** status when using this filter.  
**Data privacy and consent status** | The status of the candidate's data consent, based on the data retention rules that the candidate is eligible for.  
**Last Activity** | Display applications whose most recent profile activity occurred on or after a specified date, or during a specified date range.  
**Applied On** | Display applications that were submitted on or after a specified date, or during a specified date range.  
**Hired On** | Display applications that were marked as hired on or after a specified date, or during a specified date range.  
**Show potential duplicates** | Checking this box shows applications where two candidate profiles match on at least one of your [duplicate tagging criteria](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/49207850415003-Configure-the-Duplicate-tag) (name, email address, phone number, or LinkedIn profile URL). Identifying potential duplicates can help your team decide when to [merge candidate profiles](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/115004506466).  
  
#### Verification Status

**Filter** | **Description**  
---|---  
Current stage | The candidate's [identity verification](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/40966215931291) status based on the candidate's current stage.   
  
#### Fraud Status

**Filter** | **Description**  
---|---  
**Exclude potential fraud** | Don't show candidates who were flagged as potential fraud using [Fraud Detection](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/42738009117467).  
  
#### Source

**Filter** | **Description**  
---|---  
**Source** | Display applications based on the associated [source](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/115003931231).  
**Credited To** | Display applications based on the associated referrer or "who gets credit."  
  
#### Responsibility

**Filter** | **Description**  
---|---  
**Recruiter** | Display applications based on the recruiter associated with their candidate profile.  
**Coordinator** | Display applications based on the coordinator associated with their candidate profile.  
**Who I'm Following** | Checking this box displays applications only for candidates you are following.  
  
#### Pipeline tasks

**Filter** | **Description**  
---|---  
**Needs Decision** | Checking this box filters applications where all interview/scorecard/review tasks for the current stage have been completed, and the application is due to be advanced or rejected.  
**All Interviews** | Checking this box automatically checks all of the following boxes: To Be Scheduled, Scheduled, Scorecards Due, Completed Scorecards.  
**To Be Scheduled** | Checking this box filters applications with an outstanding scheduling task.  
**Scheduled** | Checking this box filters applications with upcoming scheduled interviews.  
**Scorecards Due** | Checking this box filters applications with scorecards due.  
**Completed Scorecards** | Checking this box filters applications that have had scorecards submitted for the current stage.  
**Interview Date** |  Filter applications with an interview scheduled on or after a specified date, or during a specified date range. **Note:** This filter reviews interviews scheduled for the application's current stage only.  
**Availability Status** | Filter applications based on the status of their availability for their current interview stage (not requested, requested, received, confirmation sent).  
**Test Status** |  Filter applications based on the status of their take-home test (to be sent, waiting, graded). **Note:** This filter reviews the test status for the application's current stage only.  
**Test Score** |  Filter applications based on their exact test score or test score range. **Note:** This filter reviews the test score for the application's current stage only.  
**Offer** | Filter applications based on offer status (to be created, created, to be sent, sent).  
  
#### Education

**Filter** | **Description**  
---|---  
School Name | Filter applications based on the candidate-provided school name.  
Degree | Filter applications based on the candidate-provided degree.  
Discipline | Filter applications based on the candidate-provided discipline.  
Education Start | Filter applications based on the candidate-provided education start date.  
Education End | Filter applications based on the candidate-provided education end date.  
Most Recent Education Only | Checking this box ignores older education information for candidates who have provided more than one education entry; only the most recent education information will be searched by other Education filters.

__

# Collect candidate demographic data

Collecting candidate demographic data allows you to make more confident, informed hiring decisions that lead to a more inclusive hiring process. Greenhouse offers multiple ways to collect candidate demographic data.

**Note:** This article includes general recommendations for using each collection method. We encourage you to work with your legal team to review the use cases for each method and pick the right option for your organization.

#### In this article

  * Choose a data collection method  

    * U.S. standard demographic questions
    * Custom demographic questions
    * Equal Employment Opportunity Commission (EEOC) questions
  * Combine data collection methods
    * Standard demographic questions + custom demographic questions
    * EEOC + custom demographic questions
    * EEOC + standard demographic questions



### Choose a data collection method

#### U.S. standard demographic questions

[Standard demographic questions](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/7541739987355) include pre-made, best-practice survey questions for customers based on Greenhouse's own practices to collect demographic information for U.S.-based applicants. You can also add the question set to your candidate survey.

Standard demographic questions allow organizations that have jobs in the U.S. to collect consistent candidate data.

#### Custom demographic questions

[Custom demographic questions](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360004588971) allow you to address your organization's specific needs with personalized demographic questions and answers. You can also add the question set to your candidate survey.

Custom demographic questions are only available for Expert tier customers. Those with an Pro subscription can also utilize detailed [demographic reports ](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/sections/360002478831-Inclusion-reports)that provide a view of job activity by demographic group.

#### Equal Employment Opportunity Commission (EEOC) questions

The [EEOC questionnaire](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/205278605) is a set of federally-approved questions about race, gender, veteran status, and disability status.

The EEOC survey and reporting functionality are intended to be used by Greenhouse customers who are government contractors or federal entities. We recommend you only utilize these features only if your organization fits that criteria.

If you do not fit these criteria and are using the EEOC report to gather demographic data without the appropriate level of DE&I reporting, it could represent a risk to your organization. Speak with your legal counsel to better understand the benefits and risks of accessing and reviewing this type of information.

**Note:** Neither the standard demographic question set nor the custom demographic question set replaces the standard EEOC questions for companies that are required by law to report on candidate demographic data. Please consult with your company’s own legal counsel before enabling this question set, as there are risks inherent to collecting demographic data where it is not required to do so, and Greenhouse disclaims any legal responsibility for the wording of the questions themselves. In addition, Greenhouse will not be responsible for any liability that may arise out of your use of this question set.

### Combine data collection methods

#### Standard demographic questions + custom demographic questions

While you can only have one or the other on a job post, you can use them with different job posts.

**Example:** Imagine your organization has some job posts located in the U.S. and others located internationally. You can combine demographic question sets by using standard demographic questions on your U.S.-based job posts and custom demographic questions on your other job posts.

#### EEOC + custom demographic questions

If you want to collect information beyond what you can collect with EEOC, you can use custom demographic questions to do so. Job applications with both questions enabled will show your custom demographic question set followed by the EEOC questionnaire.

#### EEOC + standard demographic questions

While it is possible to combine these two, we don't generally recommend it because there may be overlap in the questions which can cause unnecessary extra data.

**Note:** All in-app candidate demographic data is **anonymized** for compliance purposes and to reduce unconscious bias in the hiring process. Your organization's Greenhouse Recruiting users can only view anonymized candidate demographic data. In addition, Greenhouse Technical Support cannot access candidate demographic data unless given explicit consent by your organization.

### Candidate's consent to collect demographic data

A checkbox to collect the candidate's consent for demographic data collection will display on job and prospect posts under certain circumstances, based on your GDPR configuration:

  * **Job posts:**
    * The job post is associated with an office using a GDPR data retention rule
    * The job uses either US Standard Demographic Questions or customer demographic questions
  * **Prospect posts**
    * The prospect post uses either US Standard Demographic Questions or customer demographic questions
    * Your organization has an "All Offices" data retention rule



This checkbox is required and will be displayed in addition to any [GDPR data consent checkboxes](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360042142612).

# Permission levels overview

**Permissions:** —

**Product tier:** Available for new subscription tiers (Core, Plus, and Pro)

Every user added to Greenhouse Recruiting is assigned to one of three user permission levels: Basic, Job Admin or Site Admin.

The user permission level assigned provides general parameters for what access, abilities, and responsibilities a user has within Greenhouse Recruiting. The user permission level is assigned when a user is first added to Greenhouse Recruiting but can be edited later.

Once a user is assigned to a user permission level, additional user-specific permissions can be granted to individual users as needed. User-specific permissions are additional permissions assigned to users who may need to perform tasks that fall beyond their user permission level and are a key component to customizing each user's Greenhouse Recruiting access to fit your team's needs.

**Note** : Only a Site Admin with the permission **Can edit another user's advanced permissions** can edit user-specific permissions.

#### In this article

  * User permission level: Basic
  * User permission level: Job Admin
  * User permission level: Site Admin
  * Additional resources



### User permission level: Basic

The Basic user permission level allows the most limited visibility in Greenhouse Recruiting and should be assigned to individuals who do not participate in recruiting tasks.

Only the **My Dashboard** view is available to Basic users. From the _My Dashboard_ page, Basic users can do the following:

  * Submit referrals and review previously submitted referrals
  * Share jobs to social media (LinkedIn, Twitter, or create unique tracking links to post manually elsewhere)
  * Access your company's internal job board



### User permission level: Job Admin

The Job Admin user permission level allows users to be assigned recruiting tasks on a per-job basis. Users assigned to this permission level have additional information and access available on jobs to which they are assigned. Job Admins cannot access any information on jobs they aren't assigned to. Any employee in your organization who is responsible for recruiting tasks on at least one job should be configured with the Job Admin permission level.

To learn more about assigning a Job Admin user to a specific job, click [here](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360040181991).

Job Admins are users who are stakeholders in the interview plans for specific jobs. This might include Hiring Managers, Recruiters, Coordinators, and other individuals who should have high visibility into a given interview plan or candidate pipeline. A user cannot be assigned to a Hiring Team unless they have a Job Admin or Site Admin user permission level. To learn more about Hiring Team roles, click [here](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/115002194983).

Users have the following visibility and access available on jobs where they are assigned Job Admin user permissions:

  * Can see the job's Dashboard, pipeline, and reports
  * Can be assigned Hiring Team roles



Every time a user is assigned to a job as a Job Admin, your team must also decide what Job Admin permission level to grant the user on that particular role. Assigning a user to a role as a Job Admin allows the user to see that job, while the specific Job Admin permission level selected for the user defines what actions the user can take on the job.

Job Admin permission levels allow your team to specify the exact access a Job Admin should have on a given role. A Hiring Manager and a Recruiter might need different access to a job.

**Example:** Your team might want the Hiring Manager to be able to advance candidates to the next stage, but only the Recruiter should be able to edit the external job post.

Job Admin permission levels allow you to make those distinctions and grant users only the level of access they require for their role on a job. To learn more about the unique permissions that can be configured for Job Admins, [click here](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360039518131).

**Note:** Organizations with an Core subscription can assign users as **Job Admin: Standard** or **Job Admin: Private** ; these Job Admin permission levels cannot be customized. Organizations with a Plus or Pro subscription can customize the permissions assigned to **Job Admin: Standard** and **Job Admin: Private** , as well as [create custom Job Admin permission levels](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/207813806).

### User permission level: Site Admin

Site Admins have the highest level of access, with the ability to make changes that impact your entire company's Greenhouse Recruiting configuration. Accordingly, we encourage your team to assign individuals to the Site Admin user permission level sparingly.

Site Admins can do the following:

  * View and edit all jobs
  * Run all reports
  * View and edit candidates (to view private candidates, a Site Admin will need the user-specific permission **Can create and view private candidates**)
  * Manage custom fields
  * Manage company metadata such as Sources, Rejection Reasons, and Candidate Tags
  * Manage the _Organization s_ ettings page
  * Manage unattached prospects



### Additional resources

To learn about user permission levels and other types of permissions in Greenhouse Recruiting, please review the following articles:

  * [Permission policies overview](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/115002226606)
  * [User-specific permissions overview](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360021050791)
  * [User permissions grid](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/210957383)

# Edit choreographed introduction templates

**Permissions:** Owners and Coordinators

**Product tier:** Available for Greenhouse Welcome and Greenhouse Onboarding subscription tiers

Choreographed introductions help your onboarding team notify employees about the latest group of new hires who've joined your organization, giving employees a chance to learn more about their new teammates.

Greenhouse Onboarding provides four default templates to get you started, and you can create custom choreographed introduction templates. You can edit or delete default or custom choreographed introduction templates at any time.

#### In this article

  * Edit choreographed introductions email template
  * Delete choreographed introductions email template



### Edit a choreographed introduction template

From your Greenhouse Onboarding homepage, navigate to **Settings** > **Onboarding Plan** > **Emails**.

On the  _Emails_ page, scroll to  _Choreographed introductions_.

Hover over the template you want to edit, then click the **pencil** icon.

On the _Choreographed introductions template_ page, you can edit any of the following elements for your template's setup or email content:

**Template setup**

  * Template name
  * Template description
  * New hire cohort criteria
  * Email template schedule



**Email content**

  * Recipient
  * Subject line
  * Email body
  * New hire details



**Note:** Learn more about configuring your choreographed introduction's [template setup and email content](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360049052771).

Click **Preview** to review how your changes will appear to employees receiving this email.

When you're ready, click **Save and exit** to apply your changes.

### Delete a choreographed introduction template

**Note:** Deleting a choreographed introduction template is permanent and can't be undone. We recommend [turning off your template](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360048564072) to stop delivering emails instead of deleting your template. This allows you to save the template's content in case your organization ever needs to use it in the future.

On the  _Emails_ page, scroll to  _Choreographed introductions_.

Hover over the template you want to delete, then click the **trash can** icon.

Click **Delete** to confirm you want to remove this template.

Emails scheduled by this template will stop sending immediately once you delete it.

### Additional resources

  * [Choreographed introduction emails](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360048564092)
  * [Create choreographed introduction templates](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360049052771)
  * [Deactivate delivery for choreographed introductions](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360048564072)

# CRM overview

**Permissions:** **—**

**Product tier:** Available for new subscription tiers (Core, Plus, and Pro)

Greenhouse Recruiting's CRM feature allows your organization to build and nurture its most valuable asset — your talent network. With an organized and steady talent pipeline, your organization can stay a step ahead when the hiring opportunity arises. 

CRM provides various tools to help your organization find, add, organize, and engage with prospects to suit your sourcing needs.

#### In this article

  * CRM video overview
  * Add prospects
  * Organize and search your prospects
  * Group your prospects
  * Take action on prospects



**Note:** Greenhouse CRM is available to all subscription tiers. However, only Job Admins or above with CRM Access can use the features below. This access is granted by Greenhouse or the CRM contact in your organization. Some specific features may only be available to higher subscription tiers. Check out the specific support articles for a more detailed view of the permissions and subscription tiers for a specific feature. Click [here](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/4411120566299) to learn more about CRM permissions. 

### CRM video overview

### Add prospects

Creating and cultivating a talent database can be inefficient and challenging when your data lives across multiple systems. Regardless of how your organization sources prospects, Greenhouse CRM has a tool to help you quickly and easily import their information into your Greenhouse Recruiting account.

Whether you have been communicating with a prospect via email or maintaining a list of prospects on a spreadsheet, you can easily import this data into a centralized location with a few clicks using the following Greenhouse Recruiting features:

  * Greenhouse Recruiting Chrome extension
  * Maildrop
  * Bulk import prospects from a spreadsheet
  * Start a new prospect process for rejected candidates
  * Prospect post
  * LinkedIn RSC integration
  * Sourcing integration partners



#### [Greenhouse Recruiting Chrome extension](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/4947637389083)

Bring the power of CRM to where you are working. Once installed, the Greenhouse Recruiting Chrome extension allows your organization to add prospects to your Greenhouse CRM from a website, resume, or manually through the plugin without leaving your current workflow. 

For customers with a [Sourcing Automation](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/5131929423643) seat, the extension also retrieves accurate prospect contact information using state-of-the-art algorithms and multiple data sources.

Read more about the Greenhouse Recruiting Chrome extension [here](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/4947637389083).

#### [Maildrop](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/201990630)

Easily create prospects directly from your email. Use this feature to import 1 or multiple prospects into Greenhouse Recruiting by emailing their resume to a Maildrop address. This feature can save your team precious time when dealing with a large volume of resumes from a resume book, career fair, or another event.

Read more about Maildrop [here](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/201990630).

#### [Bulk import prospects from a spreadsheet](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/203871039)

If you collect prospect information from other sites in a spreadsheet and want to import them quickly into your Greenhouse account, our bulk import feature allows you to bulk upload hundreds of prospects in one workflow. We also support additional information you want to include, like custom fields, jobs, pools, stages, etc.

Read more about bulk importing [here.](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/203871039)

#### [Start a new prospect process for rejected candidates](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360026133251)

Chances are you already have great talent in your Greenhouse Recruiting database! Sourcing from past candidates cuts down on external sourcing time and is free. When closing a job, figure out which candidates in the pipeline could be a fit for your organization in the future and convert them into prospects. 

Read more about converting a candidate to a prospect [here](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360026133251).

#### [Prospect post](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360026554031)

A prospect post is a unique type of post on your organization's career page that is not linked to any specific job. It allows prospects to express general interest in applying to roles at your company who do not see current listings applicable to their skill set. These posts can be linked to specific [prospect pools](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360024904051) to help keep your prospects organized in Greenhouse CRM.

Read more about prospect posts [here](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360026554031).

#### [LinkedIn RSC integration](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/115005678103)

LinkedIn Recruiter System Connect (RSC) is an integration that allows you to seamlessly source and manage prospect and candidate information across Greenhouse and LinkedIn Recruiter all on one platform. When enabled, your organization can export the prospect directly to available jobs in your Greenhouse account.

Read more about LinkedIn RSC [here](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/115005678563).

#### [Sourcing integration partners](https://www.greenhouse.io/partners)

We offer over 80 integrations with sourcing partners across the industry. Get creative in your candidate sourcing efforts by searching proprietary databases, boosting employee referrals, and managing a fleet of agencies.

Check out our partners [here](https://www.greenhouse.io/partners).

### Organize and search your prospects

Prospecting is a high-volume job, but it's not helpful to have thousands of prospects in your Greenhouse Recruiting account if you cannot segment and find those prospects again. We provide multiple tools to help your organization categorize prospects, so it's easy to capture their information and find them in the future. Don't waste your existing relationships or start your internal prospect searches from scratch!

Check out the following tools to organize and search for your prospects:

  * Assign a prospect owner
  * Record sources
  * Add candidate tags to prospects
  * Use custom candidate fields
  * Outbound sourcing eBook



#### [Assign a prospect owner](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/115002698026)

Prospect owners identify the team member in your organization responsible for the prospect. This structure provides clear accountability and can help your organization report exceptional and/or underperforming team members.

Read more about prospect owners [here](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/115002698026).

#### [Record sources](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/115003931231)

Where are your prospects coming from? Which ones are converting to candidates? Which ones are making it farthest in the pipeline? Arguably the most important data point for analyzing your prospect database. Report on your sources to understand which sources are giving you the most high-quality candidates, and stop investing in those sources that are underperforming.

Read more about sourcing basics [here](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/115003931231).

#### [Add candidate tags to prospects](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360004149852)

Tags allow your organization to capture prospect data and quickly categorize prospects so you can search for them later.

Read more about candidate tags [here](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360004149852).

#### [Use custom candidate fields](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/202609675)

Use custom fields to capture prospect data not covered by Greenhouse's default fields. By leveraging custom fields, your organization can analyze the specific details you care about and use them to categorize and/or search for these prospects later.

Read more about custom fields [here](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/202609675).

#### [Outbound sourcing eBook](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/6183619224603)

In today’s competitive talent landscape, you’re probably looking for new and effective ways to create and structure your email outreach to discover, connect and engage with prospective candidates. That’s why we’ve compiled a list of best practices and templates to help you build an optimal outbound sourcing strategy for your company. We’ll walk you through how to craft compelling sourcing emails, from the subject line down to the signature.

[Click here](https://www.greenhouse.io/guidance/outbound-sourcing-best-practices-for-talent-leaders) to learn more about our Outbound sourcing eBook and how to receive your copy.

### Group your prospects

Organizing prospects into groups based on select criteria allows your organization to coordinate workflows for similar prospects. When a new job is approved for candidate recruitment, these groupings can be a quick and productive way to find talent for your organization.

#### [Prospect pools and stages](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360024904051)

A prospect pool (and its subsequent stages) is a feature in Greenhouse CRM that enables your organization to organize prospects sourced online, at events, and/or from other job pipelines into a single manageable group so you can track and plan outreach efforts. By default, prospects are added to the "Uncategorized Prospects" pool which can be configured on the Organization settings page.

Read more about prospect pools and stages [here](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360024904051).

### Take action on prospects

With your prospects' data organized, use the following features to nurture these prospect relationships:

  * Campaign pools
  * Pool and stage reminders
  * Talent Finder



#### [Campaign pools](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/5045604930843)

Users with a [Sourcing Automation](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/5131929423643) seat can add prospects to campaign pools that send automated email sequences to the prospects. When developing your outbound sourcing strategy, email is one of the most familiar, reputable, and effective approaches to communicating with prospective candidates. Since top prospects likely receive several emails daily, they can distinguish between high-quality, targeted emails and spam emails.

With an engaging email outreach, you can build an optimal outbound sourcing strategy that sets you up for success. 

Learn more about how to build a campaign pool [here](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/5045604930843). 

#### [Pool and stage reminders](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360020137872)

Managing the next steps for multiple prospects across different pools and stages can be challenging when those pools and stages have different workflows, timeframes for next steps, etc. Access these reminders directly from your Dashboard and stay on top of next steps for a group of prospects.

Read more about pool and stage reminders [here](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360020137872).

#### [Talent Rediscovery](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/articles/30184390692379)

Greenhouse CRM's Talent Rediscovery feature allows your organization to tap into the various groups of talent cultivated through your sourcing and recruitment efforts for any job. Using this feature, your organization can jumpstart sourcing for a job, infuse your current pipeline with a group of silver-medal candidates, and more.

Read more about Talent Rediscovery [here](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/articles/30184390692379).

<!-- source: https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360059153471-FAQ-HRIS-Link-for-Workday-user-import -->

# FAQ: HRIS Link for Workday®️  user import

**Permissions:** —

**Product tier:** Available for Pro subscription tier with HRIS Link add-on

#### In this article

  * Does a new user account created by HRIS Link trigger an email notification to that employee?
  * Can I manage user permissions with HRIS Link?
  * Does HRIS Link user import support required custom fields?
  * Can I assign users to offices or departments?
  * Can I assign users custom user fields?
  * How does HRIS Link work with SSO?
  * Can I use nested groups on my user import report?
  * Can I ask Greenhouse Technical Support for assistance troubleshooting HRIS Link errors?



#### Does a new user account created by HRIS Link trigger an email notification to that employee?

HRIS Link does allow organizations to send out invitation emails when the integration creates user profiles. For more information, refer to the user import report specifications [here](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360058479852).

#### Can I manage user permissions with HRIS Link?

No. HRIS Link creates, enables, deactivates, and updates user account details. HRIS Link doesn't assign permissions to users. New users created by HRIS Link are assigned [basic permissions](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360039614171-User-permission-levels-overview#h_113563b1-d2cd-464a-84d1-83bc885dc416).

#### Does HRIS Link user import support required custom fields?

HRIS Link user import supports required custom fields, if the custom field is marked required on the user import report. If a required custom field has a `NULL` value on the report, you'll receive an [error](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360059987811).

#### Can I assign users to offices or departments?

Yes, HRIS Link supports assigning users to offices or departments.

#### Can I assign users custom user fields?

Yes, HRIS Link supports assigning users [custom user fields](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/7626796336283). HRIS Link supports single-select, multi-select, yes / no, or user field types on custom user fields. Read more here: [Setup HRIS Link user import > Add custom user fields to your report](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360058479852#h_01GESZ151VGM7AAG1WCWWNW8AM).

#### How does HRIS Link work with single sign-on (SSO)?

SSO is the primary mechanism that controls employees' access to Greenhouse. While deactivating an employee's SSO account _does_ prevent them from logging into Greenhouse Recruiting, it won't deactivate their Greenhouse Recruiting account entirely. The user could still appear throughout Greenhouse Recruiting, such as in hiring team assignments. By deactivating user accounts via HRIS Link, you ensure inactive employees are not selectable throughout Greenhouse Recruiting.

#### Can I use nested groups on my user import report?

No, HRIS Link doesn’t recognize nested groups on your report. Your entity structure should be flat, with just the in-app name, reference_ID, or external_ID displayed.

#### Can I ask Greenhouse Technical Support for assistance troubleshooting HRIS Link errors?

Yes, Greenhouse Technical Support can assist with troubleshooting HRIS Link errors! If you're unable to resolve an issue using the [Support Center](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360059987811), you can open a ticket Greenhouse Technical Support by clicking [here](https://support.greenhouse.io/direct). Be sure to include the following details in your ticket:

  * The workflow ID (found in the error notification)
  * Details on the issue

# Manage onboarding fields

**Permissions:** Owner

**Product tier:** Available for Greenhouse Welcome and Greenhouse Onboarding subscription tiers

Fields help you collect information from new hires during onboarding and organize details related to your employees. You can also [configure permissions](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/sections/4405706385051-Onboarding-permissions) to give specific users or roles access to view and manage different employee fields.

[Owners](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360019575491) can add new fields, edit existing fields, set validation rules, and delete fields at any time.

#### In this article

  * Add a field
  * Edit a field
  * Add field validation
  * Move a field
  * Delete a field
  * Additional resources



### Add a field

**Note:** New fields cannot be added to the **Basic Information** field group.

From your Greenhouse Onboarding homepage, navigate to **Settings** > **Company Info** > **Fields**.

You can add fields to any [field group](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360002782332) other than the Basic Information field group.

Navigate to the field group, then select **Add Field** from the dropdown.

On the _Add New Field_ page, you'll create your new field, determine the type of information collected by this field, and set rules for which new hires will fill out this field.

Set up the following elements for your new field:

**Field element** | **Description**  
---|---  
Display name | The name that Greenhouse Onboarding users will see when filling out your new field.  
Field type |  Determines the type of information collected in this field. The field type can't be changed after a field is created. Select one of the following:

  * Short textbox
  * Long textbox
  * Single select
  * Multi select
  * Contact field
  * Date field
  * Coworker field
  * Address field
  * Masked field

  
Help text | (Optional) Provide descriptive text to help users fill out your field.  
Validation type | For short textbox fields, set a format rule to control how new hires enter data into this field. See Add field validation for details on available validation types.  
Selection options | If your new field uses the single select or multi select field type, add options for your new hires to select from when they fill out this field. For example, if your field asks for a new hire's favorite color, include each color as a selection option.  
Field group | The [field group](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360002782332) where this field will be placed on the **Fields** page in _Settings_.  
Greenhouse Recruiting field | If you've integrated your Greenhouse Onboarding account with Greenhouse Recruiting, you can [map your new field](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/208314493) to a corresponding field in Greenhouse Recruiting. This allows you to pull relevant candidate information into Greenhouse Onboarding when the candidate is hired.  
Required for new hires and/or managers | Mark this checkbox to require new hires or their managers to fill out this field during the onboarding process.  
Rules |  Set rules to determine which new hires will be able to see and fill out this field during their welcome experience. You can apply rules based on the following criteria:

  * Department
  * Location
  * Employment status
  * Other criteria

  
  
When you're finished, click **Save**.

### Edit a field

Click on any existing field from the _Fields_ page to edit it.

On the _Edit Field_ page, update any of the following elements:

  * Display name
  * Help text
  * Validation type (short textbox fields only)
  * Selection options (if the field type is single select or multi select)
  * Field group
  * Greenhouse Recruiting field
  * Required for new hires and/or managers
  * Rules (any field outside of Basic Information)



**Note:** The **field type** can't be changed during editing.

### Add field validation

Field validation lets you control the format of information that new hires enter into a short textbox field. When a validation rule is set, new hires receive real-time feedback if they enter data in the wrong format — for example, entering letters in a field that requires numbers only.

To set a validation rule, open any short textbox field from the _Fields_ page. In the **Validation Type** dropdown, select one of the following options:

**Validation type** | **Description**  
---|---  
None | No validation is applied. New hires can enter any value into this field.  
Custom regex | Enter a custom regular expression to define your own format requirements — for example, for employee IDs, cost center codes, or other organization-specific formats.  
Email address | Requires the entry to match a valid email address format.  
Letters only | Restricts input to letters only.  
Numbers only | Restricts input to digits only.  
National tax identity |  Requires the entry to match a country-specific tax ID format. Select from the following supported countries:

  * United States: Social Security Number (SSN)
