# Free job posts on Indeed

**Permissions:** Site Admin and Job Admin who can create, edit and delete job posts

**Product tier:** Available for new subscription tiers (Core, Plus, and Pro)

With Greenhouse Recruiting, you can create free job posts on Indeed with your live external job posts.

As of November 2025, **all** new clients will be reviewed by Indeed's Trust & Safety team. New clients will not automatically see their jobs on Indeed’s search results until reviewed by the Trust & Safety team. Upon review, the Trust & Safety team will determine the visibility level of those jobs. This may cause some delays to jobs going live.

**Actionable Tips & Resources**

  * **Proactive Review:** We highly recommend you review your jobs with Indeed's Trust & Safety standards in mind. Following the guidelines increases the chance of passing their reviews.
  * **Need Assistance?** If you have specific questions about potential fraudulent behavior or job visibility, please **contact your dedicated Indeed Client Success representative** directly. They can be reached through your employer dashboard or by calling [**1-800-475-4361**](tel:18004754361).
  * **Additional Resources:**
    * [Job Posting Best Practices](https://indeedinc.my.site.com/employerSupport1/s/article/203134734?language=en_US)
    * [General Job Posting Guidelines](https://indeedinc.my.site.com/employerSupport1/s/article/115005915763?language=en_US)
    * [Applicant Tracking System (ATS) Guidelines](https://docs.indeed.com/ats-guidelines)



_**Disclaimer:** Jobs that do not meet Indeed standards may be subject to review and require additional information. Listings that prove misleading, compromise the job seeker experience or those which Indeed are not convinced represent a “real” job may be removed from search results altogether._

#### In this article

  * Set up the Indeed integration
  * Publish a free job post on Indeed
    * Candidate source for Indeed
    * Indeed salary estimates



### Set up the Indeed integration

**Note:** You need to be a Site Admin in order to set up the Indeed integration.

To set up the Indeed integration, log in to Greenhouse Recruiting and navigate to **Configure** > **Job** **Boards** > then scroll to _Global Partner Settings_.

Enter a company email address for _Indeed job feed company email_. If your company has an Indeed account, use the company email address associated with your Indeed account. If you don't have an Indeed account, use any email address from your company email domain.

**Note** : To authenticate job posts and avoid spam, Indeed requires a company email address. This email address is used to validate your organization's job posts and is not used for any other purpose.

When finished, click **Submit**.

### Publish a free job post on Indeed

Once the Indeed integration is set up, you can publish a free job post to Indeed. Click**Jobs** on your navigation bar, then select a job from the list.

Click **Job Setup** > **Job** **Posts** , then [add a new job post](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360020285311) or click the **Edit** icon beside the job post you wish to edit.

First, ensure there's a location for your job post. Begin typing a location for Indeed to associate with the job and select the location from the dropdown. This location will appear on your job post. You can add one or more locations to a single job post. 

Next, select your work type: 

  * In person
  * Hybrid
  * Remote



If you're posting a remote job, flexible job, or job with multiple locations, add **Searchable locations**. You can add up to seven Searchable locations per job post. These are separate from the main **Location** field used for your Greenhouse-hosted job post. When job seekers search by location on Indeed, your job post can be surfaced in the results. Searchable locations don’t appear on your job post. 

Scroll to the _Publish to free job boards_ section.

Place a checkbox next to **Indeed** , then click **Save.**

**Notes:**

  * For remote roles, searchable locations can be added at the city or country level. Country-only locations are allowed only for remote roles. Statewide remote isn’t currently supported. To post a nationwide remote role, set **Work type** to **Remote** and add the country in **Searchable locations**.
  * It can take up to 48 hours for new job posts or updates to appear on Indeed. Because Indeed offers [sponsored posts](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360027973431) for better positioning on their site, it isn't possible to repost a job ad in Greenhouse Recruiting to generate a new ad on Indeed. Taking the post down and then reactivating it, or closing and reopening the job will simply re-post the stale job instead of creating a new one.
  * [Beginning April 1, 2023](https://indeed.force.com/employerSupport1/s/article/Policy-Personally-Identifiable-Information-PII?language=en_US), Indeed will not allow job post questions that seek personally identifiable information (PII) like full birthdates, driver's license numbers, or social security numbers from applicants. If your job post includes a custom question requesting PII, the job post will be removed from Indeed, and your Indeed account may experience restricted functionality. Reach out to your Indeed representative for more information.



### Candidate source for Indeed job posts

When a candidate applies using a free job post on Indeed, by default their source is listed as _Responded to an ad on Indeed_.

### Indeed salaries

If you post a job to Indeed and don't include salary information, Indeed will automatically include an estimated salary. For more information about this feature, contact Indeed's customer support.

If pay transparency is enabled in Greenhouse and you've included a pay range for your post, your job's salary range will be added to your Indeed post. Learn more about [pay transparency.](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/10028084062491)

Alternatively, add a salary range to your Greenhouse job post description, and it will be included on your Indeed job post.

# Create custom tokens for email and offer templates

**Permissions:** Site Admin, and Job Admin who can manage custom fields

**Product tier:** Available for new subscription tiers (Core, Plus, and Pro)

When creating or editing [custom fields](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360001421452), you have the option to create a token for each custom field.

These tokens can be added to email or offer templates to pull in information specific to the job, candidate profile, or application.

#### In this article

  * Create a custom token for email and offer templates
  * Considerations when using custom tokens in email templates
  * Find out which fields are available in a template
  * List of email templates that can use custom tokens



### Create a custom token for email and offer templates

To create a custom token for an email and offer template, click the **Configure** icon  in the upper right corner, and then click **Custom Options** in the left-hand panel

From the  _Custom Options_ page, navigate to the  _Company Custom Fields_ section.

Click either **Candidates** , **Jobs** , or **Offers** depending on the type of custom field for which you intend to create a custom token.

**Note:** Custom offer tokens can be used only in offer templates and in [email templates](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/115004020946) created in the **My Templates** section.

Custom offer tokens cannot be used in email templates created in the **Organization-Wide Templates** section.

If the field hasn't been created yet, use the following links to learn how to create the custom field: 

  * [Add custom candidate field](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/202609675)
  * [Add custom job field](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/202609855)
  * [Add custom offer field](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360024551831)



**Note:** Organizations with Advanced or Pro subscription tiers also can create custom tokens using [custom application fields](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/115003544472). 

On the subsequent page, click the field name for an existing field to modify it. If you want to add a new field instead, click **Add** **Field**.

On the _Edit Custom Field_ page, check the box next to  _Create new email token (optional)_. Edit the token name if needed. 

When finished, click **Save**.

### Considerations when using custom tokens in email templates

#### Job field token

When used in an email template, a **non-private** [custom job field](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/202609855) token will populate even if the recipient does not have permission to access the field in Greenhouse Recruiting.

A **private** custom job field token will populate in an email [only if the recipient has the appropriate permissions](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360020855632) in Greenhouse Recruiting to view the private field.

#### Offer field token

Custom offer field tokens can be used only in [email templates](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/115004020946) that you create in your _My Templates_ section (_Configure > Email Templates_).

Custom offer field tokens cannot be used in _Organization-Wide Templates_.

### Find out which fields are available in a template

Once you define a custom email token, it will display in the tokens section at the top of the email template. You can see a full list of available tokens in this box.

### List of email templates that can use custom tokens

You can use custom tokens in any of the following email types:

  * [Agency email](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360037580392)
  * [Calendly email](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360029649991)
  * Candidate availability request
  * Candidate email
  * [Candidate interview confirmation](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360015975112)
  * Candidate referral receipt
  * Candidate rejection
  * [Candidate self-schedule request](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/4409526364443)
  * [EEOC request](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/210382923)
  * Extending offer
  * Interviewer invite
  * [Job post request](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360002568971)
  * Scorecard due
  * Team email 



**Note:** Custom offer tokens can be used only in offer templates and in [email templates](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/115004020946) created in the **My Templates** section.

Custom offer tokens cannot be used in email templates created in the **Organization-Wide Templates** section.

# Find template job IDs for a custom HRIS integration

Access the latest version of Harvest API documentation at [**harvestdocs.greenhouse.io**](http://harvestdocs.greenhouse.io).  
  
Harvest API v1 and v2 will be deprecated and unavailable after August 31, 2026. Please make sure that your existing custom integrations use the latest version of Harvest (v3) by this date and any new integrations are developed with the latest version of Harvest API.

This article is intended for people who are currently working on an HRIS integration and need to extract Greenhouse Recruiting job IDs from your [template jobs](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360038222812). Once your organization has created template jobs in Greenhouse Recruiting, you can extract the job IDs in a few different ways – either in-app in Greenhouse Recruiting or programmatically by using Greenhouse Recruiting's [Harvest API](https://harvestdocs.greenhouse.io/).

#### In this article

  * Retrieve a job ID in Greenhouse Recruiting
  * Retrieve multiple job IDs in Greenhouse Recruiting
  * Retrieve job IDs programmatically using Harvest API



### Retrieve a job ID in Greenhouse Recruiting

To retrieve an individual job ID in-app in Greenhouse Recruiting, select **All Jobs** from your navigation bar, and find the template job in your list of jobs. Click the job and note the URL shown in your browser – the job ID is the last numerical string on the URL.

**Example** : The Greenhouse Recruiting job URL structure is https://app2.greenhouse.io/sdash/`{JOB_ID}`. In the example below, the job ID is **1234567890**.

### Retrieve multiple job IDs in Greenhouse Recruiting

To retrieve multiple job IDs in-app in Greenhouse Recruiting, select **All** **Jobs** from your navigation bar. Select **Filter** to apply any necessary filters, and be sure to check **Show only template jobs**.

Check the box to select all resulting jobs in your list.

Click Bulk Actions and choose **Download stage by job report**.

The resulting report includes a list of all Greenhouse Recruiting template jobs along with the corresponding job ID in column B.

### Retrieve job IDs programmatically using Harvest API

Teams building a custom integration can retrieve job IDs programmatically using Greenhouse Recruiting’s [Harvest API](https://harvestdocs.greenhouse.io/).

To obtain job ID values needed for the template_job_id, reference the [`GET: List Jobs endpoint`](https://harvestdocs.greenhouse.io/reference/get_v3-jobs) in the Harvest API documentation.

Refer to the Harvest API documentation for current endpoint behavior, response structure, and filtering options.

# Assign a data protection officer (DPO)

**Product tier:** Available for new subscription tiers (Core, Plus, and Pro)

According to Article 37 of the [General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR)](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360001636492), any organization that controls or processes data may be required to designate a data protection officer (DPO) as a point of contact for the organization.

Click **Contacts** on the left.

Click **Edit** beside Data Protection Officer.

In the _Edit Data Protection Officer_ window, choose a user from the **Users** dropdown. Then click **Save**.

Your selected user will be assigned as your organization's data protection officer.

**Note** : Only Site Admin can manage GDPR information like the data protection officer (DPO).

# SV Academy integration

**Permissions: Job Admin** or higher

**Product tier:** Available for new subscription tiers (Core, Plus, and Pro)

SV Academy is a sales and customer success training school, helping underrepresented groups access new career opportunities in customer-facing roles at high-growth companies. SV Academy graduates consistently perform at the highest level, overachieving quotas, earning promotions faster, and leading their respective teams. Partner employers can find rigorously trained and vetted talent for their revenue-generating teams while supporting the mission of increasing economic and career opportunities for people of color, women, those with lower socioeconomic backgrounds, LGBTQ+, and anyone else who doesn’t have the privilege of an established network and easy access to growth-oriented careers.

Greenhouse Recruiting’s integration with SV Academy allows for a quick and simple transfer of candidate information from the SV Academy Employer Portal to Greenhouse Recruiting, enabling you to streamline your recruiting process for SV Academy graduates.

#### In this article

  * Create an Ingestion API key for the SV Academy integration
  * Enable the integration in SV Academy
  * Use the Greenhouse Recruiting / SV Academy integration
    * Jobs and Job IDs
    * Add Candidates
  * Troubleshooting and additional resources



### Create an Ingestion API key for the SV Academy integration

To integrate with SV Academy, you'll need to create an Ingestion API key and provide it to SV Academy.

Follow the steps in [this article](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/5888200444571) for more information on creating an Ingestion API key. Once the key is created, provide it to SV Academy so they can set up the integration with Greenhouse Recruiting.

### Enable the integration in SV Academy

Once you have created the Partner API key, you’ll need to copy/paste the full API key into your company profile on SV Academy.

In SV Academy, from your [company profile](https://hire.sv.academy/company-profile), navigate to the **Internal Information** tab. Click **Edit** in the top-right corner.

At the bottom of the page, find the _Greenhouse API Key_ field. Paste the Greenhouse Partner API key in this box, then click **Save** at the top-right corner of the page.

### Use the Greenhouse Recruiting / SV Academy integration

#### Jobs and Job IDs

If you would like to have candidates assigned to a specific job at the time of importing, you will need to add the job ID to your company profile.

  * In SV Academy, on your [company profile](https://hire.sv.academy/company-profile), navigate to the **Internal Information** tab. Click **Edit** in the top-right corner.
  * At the bottom of the page, find the fields labeled _Greenhouse SDR Job ID_ and _Greenhouse CSA Job ID_. Add the desired Greenhouse job IDs to these fields.
  * To find a Greenhouse job ID, navigate to the job in Greenhouse and observe the resulting URL. 

For example: app.greenhouse.io/dash/**12345** , where _12345_ is the job ID.




**Note** : If you don’t want candidates added to a specific job, leave the job ID fields blank on your company profile. The integration will then add the profile as a [prospect](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/200670155), with no job assigned.

#### Add Candidates

To add a candidate to Greenhouse Recruiting, navigate to a candidate profile in SV Academy and click **Add to Greenhouse** at the top of the page.

On the next page, select your company in the dropdown, then click **Save**.

The candidate will appear in Greenhouse Recruiting within a few minutes.

### Troubleshooting and additional resources

If a candidate is not appearing after adding them from SV Academy, follow these tips:

**Make sure your job ID is correct**

The job ID can be found at the end of the URL of the job when viewing it in your Greenhouse Recruiting account (read more here). The job ID is different from the Requisition or Opening ID in Greenhouse Recruiting. If in doubt, leave the job ID field blank on your company profile, as you can always assign the candidate to a job after importing them to Greenhouse Recruiting.

**Make sure your user email is correct**

Your email login for the SV Academy portal must match your user email address in Greenhouse Recruiting. If it doesn’t, reach out to SV Academy so your login can be adjusted to match.

**Additional support**

For questions or assistance not covered here, reach out to SV Academy at [hire@sv.academy](mailto:hire@sv.academy).

# Emails routed to Gmail's Promotions tab

**Tip:** Emails sent from a Greenhouse domain (such as [no-reply@greenhouse.io](mailto:no-reply@greenhouse.io)) are more likely to be flagged as promotional messages by Gmail's algorithms. We strongly recommend sending emails from a [verified email domain](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/201111684) (such as @yourcompany.com) for the best likelihood of Gmail directing your messages to the recipient's Primary inbox tab.

Despite our best efforts, sometimes emails sent from Greenhouse Recruiting are not delivered where we expected. This can occur for a variety of reasons, including an email address landing on our [bounce list](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/115004508883), the recipient's email provider flagging the message as spam, or the recipient's email provider routing the message to a location other than the inbox.

If a user or candidate reports not receiving an email message you sent them, we recommend the following as an early troubleshooting step:

  * Ask if the recipient uses a Gmail-hosted email account and, if so,
  * Request the recipient check their _Promotions_ tab for the missing messages



**Note** : Messages routed to the **Promotions** tab are not as marked as spam or considered to be spam by Google. Gmail uses a specified **Spam** folder for messages identified as spam.

The Promotions tab is a function of [Gmail's tabbed inbox feature](https://support.google.com/a/users/answer/9282731?hl=en). Tabbed inboxes help users maintain a clean inbox view by segmenting it into tabs and routing certain messages out of the Primary tab. Gmail considers each tab to be part of the recipient's inbox. Users with tabbed inboxes enabled might be checking only their default inbox view, the Primary tab, and overlooking messages routed into other tabs.

Gmail uses unique filtering algorithms to determine where to route incoming emails for users who have enabled the tabbed inboxes feature. This filtering is managed by Gmail and cannot be managed from within Greenhouse Recruiting.

To learn more about tabbed inboxes, please review the following Google blog post: [Making Gmail's tabbed inbox work better for you](https://cloud.google.com/blog/products/gmail/how-gmail-sorts-your-email-based-on-your-preferences).

While messages routed to the Promotions tab are not considered spam, we still recommend having a recipient check their Spam folder if they cannot locate messages you sent them. If you determine your team's messages are landing in recipient Spam folders regularly, we recommend reviewing our [Email Best Practices](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/207273143) article to learn more about improving email deliverability.

# Send an interview confirmation email with Google Calendar

**Permissions:** Job Admin and above

**Product tier:** Available for new subscription tiers (Core, Plus, and Pro)

Candidates aren't automatically notified of interviews created in Greenhouse Recruiting. Once an interview is scheduled, confirm the date and time with the candidate by sending an interview confirmation email.

#### In this article

  * Send interview confirmation email
    * Included calendar files



### Send interview confirmation email

After an interview is scheduled, you can send the interview confirmation by clicking the button on the **Stages** tab of their profile.

By default, the email uses the **Candidate Interview Confirmation Message**[email template](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/115002573326), but you can edit the email in the pop-up window.

To set a [candidate interview reminder](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/17435302491547), check the box next to _Send interview reminder 24 hours before the scheduled interview._

When finished, click **Send Email**.

#### Included calendar files

Calendar files allow candidates to add a scheduled interview to their calendar via a downloadable _.ics_ file. By default, Greenhouse Recruiting includes the calendar files in the interview confirmation email. You can uncheck the box **Include** **calendar** **files** to remove the ._ics_ file.

**Note** : If all of the scheduled interviews are back-to-back with no gaps in between, one calendar file will be attached with the start time of the first interview and the end time of the last one. If there are gaps, multiple files will be added, although Greenhouse will attempt to consolidate them where possible.

You can adjust the name of the calendar files by clicking the **Ellipses** icon and choosing **Rename**.

Once an interview confirmation email is sent, the calendar files will be added as an attachment to the email. The calendar file display varies with each calendar and email client. However, typically the candidate will need to manually download and add the ._ics_ file to their calendar.

The body of the email will also display the calendar file details so the candidate is prepared with the interview information.

**Note:** Calendar files aren't linked to updates to scheduled interviews in Greenhouse Recruiting, so if you make a change to the date, time, or details of an interview, you need to manually send the candidate an updated interview confirmation email.

# Troubleshoot the Calendly integration

If you're using the [Calendly integration](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360029649991), but your interviews aren't syncing to Greenhouse Recruiting, a few troubleshooting steps can help get you back on track.

#### In this article

  * Did you add a Calendly link to your scheduling email?
  * Is there a Calendly link in your email signature?



### Did you add a Calendly link to your scheduling email?

The Calendly link is automatically generated when you send the _Schedule with Calendly_ email, so you don't need to add a Calendly link to the email manually. 

If add an additional link, the candidate may have used that link to schedule. This means the interview will successfully appear on your calendar, but it won't sync to the candidate's profile in Greenhouse Recruiting.

**Tip** : If an interview isn't syncing, delete it from your calendar and [send a new _Schedule with Calendly_ email.](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360029649991) It's not possible to sync an interview to Greenhouse Recruiting if it was scheduled using your personal Calendly.

### Is there a Calendly link in your email signature?

The Calendly link will be automatically generated when you send the _Schedule with Calendly_ email. If any other Calendly links are in your email body, the candidate may schedule with the wrong one, and as a result, the event will appear on your personal calendar but may not sync to Greenhouse Recruiting.

Confirm that your [email signature in Greenhouse Recruiting](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/203800669) doesn't include a Calendly link. If it does, update your signature to remove the link.

If you've confirmed there isn't an additional link in your email body and your event still isn't syncing, reach out to [Greenhouse Technical Support](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360058320292).

**Learn more**

[Calendly integration](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360029649991)

[Calendly and Microsoft Teams](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360052219651)

# Following candidates and prospects: Email notifications about candidate or prospect

**Permissions:** Job Admins who can view or edit candidates or above

**Product tier:** Available for new subscription tiers (Core, Plus, and Pro)

With the follow candidate or prospect feature, a user can elect to receive email notifications every time a specific candidate or prospect is **moved to a new stage or rejected** from a job. Users who follow a candidate or prospect will also receive email notifications if they are transferred to a job where the user has permissions.

#### In this article

  * Follow a candidate or prospect 
  * Unfollow a candidate or prospect 
  * Filter by followed candidates or prospects 



**Note** : To deactivate the ability for users to follow candidates/prospects, please contact your Customer Success Manager.

### Follow a candidate or prospect

To follow a candidate or prospect, navigate to their profile in Greenhouse Recruiting by selecting or searching for them on the **Candidates** page or the **Job > Candidates** tab.

From the candidate's or prospect's profile, click **Follow** under the ellipses menu. 

The candidate or prospect is now followed and the user will receive an email notification when the candidate or prospect is moved to a new stage, rejected from the job, or moved to a job where the user has permissions. The user will receive an email indicating these changes, for example:

**Note** : For privacy reasons, Greenhouse Recruiting will not send a notification to followers when the candidate is moved to the Offer Stage or is marked as hired.

### Unfollow a candidate or prospect

To unfollow a candidate or prospect and no longer receive email notifications about their progress, navigate to a candidate's or prospect's profile. Click the three dots at the top of their profile and select **Unfollow candidate**.

### Filter by followed candidates or prospects

To quickly view a list of all candidates and/or prospects being followed, navigate to the _People I'm Following_ panel on **My** **Dashboard**.

For a complete list of all candidates and prospects being followed, click the **People I'm Following** to expand the results.

You'll be directed to the **Candidates** search page, filtered by the candidates and prospects currently being followed. Use the provided filter panel to apply any additional criteria to the populated list.

# Evergreen jobs and HRIS integrations

Evergreen jobs are positions that frequently need to be filled and require a constant pipeline of qualified candidates for hire. If you're integrating Greenhouse Recruiting with your HRIS, you may run into a couple of issues managing evergreen jobs in your HRIS:

  * Your HRIS may allow you to map multiple openings to one job, but it may not allow you to update the number of openings after the job has been created. This means when you fill the available openings with hires, you'd have to create a new job.
  * Or your HRIS may require you to map multiple openings to one job, so an individual job must be created each time an evergreen position is filled.



The workflows below can help you maximize Greenhouse Recruiting features and keep data in your HRIS clean.

#### In this article

  * Create a pipeline job in Greenhouse Recruiting
    * Pipeline job setup
    * Candidate management
    * Reporting (optional)
  * Manage job positions with multiple openings
  * Add positions to open requisitions in your HRIS



### Create a pipeline job in Greenhouse Recruiting

If your HRIS doesn't allow you to update openings or map multiple openings to a job, you can manually create a pipeline job in Greenhouse Recruiting. This pipeline job won't be linked to a corresponding position in your HRIS, but you should continue to create and push approved positions over from your HRIS via integration. Each position or requisition that comes over from your HRIS will map to a distinct Greenhouse Recruiting job, and you'll want to manually move candidates over from the pipeline job to these integrated jobs when you are ready to extend an offer.

This solution allows you to receive an ongoing stream of candidates from a job board post, which you can use to collect and process candidates for evergreen positions but gives your recruiters a single place to manage and interview candidates inside of Greenhouse Recruiting.

#### Pipeline job setup

Create a job in Greenhouse Recruiting that's clearly labeled as a pipeline job. Ensure your pipeline job has a exact same [interview plan](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/115002194903) (including capitalization) as your non-pipeline, distinct positions, except with the offer stage which should signal to users to transfer the candidate to a non-pipeline position.

**Note** : If requisition ID is a required field in Greenhouse Recruiting, use a value that won't link to a position or requisition in your HRIS, like PIPELINE_1.

Imagine you have an evergreen job in Greenhouse Recruiting called Pipeline - Software Engineer I, with 4 interview stages, including a unique last offer stage you've renamed to _Transfer candidate to non-pipeline job_.

Your non-pipeline jobs like Software Engineer I should have a generally matching interview plan structure, except with a real offer stage.

#### Pipeline job

#### Non-pipeline job

#### Candidate management

Manage candidates and conduct the interview process as normal on the pipeline job, but stop before you create an offer and hire candidates. When you identify a qualified candidate and would like to extend an offer, [ transfer the candidate ](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360031249311-Transfer-Candidate-to-a-Different-Job) to the appropriate non-pipeline Greenhouse Recruiting job that was imported from your HRIS.

By transferring, you'll move the scorecards to the appropriate interview stages. Make sure you place candidates in the _Offer_ stage so they don't receive automated notifications from the previous interview process.

**Note** : You can't transfer a candidate if they have a pending offer on the pipeline job.

Imagine an example candidate named Ashish has received strong scorecard feedback on your pipeline job. 

When Ashish reaches the offer stage, your team is reminded to [transfer](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360031249311) them to the non-pipeline job.

When the candidate is transferred to the non-pipeline job, they're placed in the offer stage, and all the previous scorecards transfer with them.

Your team can then generate the offer and get approval as necessary to hire the candidate for your non-pipeline job.

#### Reporting (optional)

If your organization relies on reporting and compliance for your evergreen positions, check out these tips to ensure your pipeline jobs are up-to-date:

  * **Accurate opening dates** : [Update the pipeline job's open date](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/16711979322907) on the **Job** **Info** page to reflect when recruiting began or when the Greenhouse Recruiting job was opened.
  * **Use a custom job field** : Create a short text [custom job field](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/202609855) named "Pipeline Job ID" for the job positions mapped from your HRIS. Copy the Greenhouse Recruiting job ID from your pipeline job. It appears on the job dashboard as the last string of numbers in the page URL.



Enter the Greenhouse Recruiting Job ID in the "Pipeline Job ID" custom field on the non-pipeline, hiring job. This ensures you maintain a link to the pipeline job for your downstream reporting.

  * **Recruiting start date:** Create a custom job field named "recruiting start date" on the hiring (non-pipeline) job. When you are ready to hire someone, you can search for all jobs with the "Pipeline Job ID" and find the most recent hire date, and assign that date to the "recruiting start date" field on the job.



### Manage job positions with multiple openings

Create a position or requisition in your HRIS with the number of available openings. The job import integration will send these jobs to Greenhouse Recruiting and map them to individual Greenhouse Recruiting requisition IDs.

Go through the recruiting process as normal, hiring candidates onto the openings in Greenhouse Recruiting.

When exported from Greenhouse Recruiting, the candidates will fill the corresponding openings in your HRIS. When you fill the last opening on the job, the Greenhouse Recruiting job will automatically close. This should also close the position or requisition in your HRIS when the new hire fills the last opening.

### Add positions to open requisitions in your HRIS

In certain HRIS platforms, you can add positions to open requisitions. Since you can also add openings to open requisitions in Greenhouse Recruiting, if you have the ability in your HRIS to add positions to open requisitions, you can discuss adding openings to open requisitions with your integration developer. Check out our [Developer Resources](https://developers.greenhouse.io), and in particular the [Harvest API](https://developers.greenhouse.io/harvest.html) endpoints [GET: List jobs](https://developers.greenhouse.io/harvest.html#get-list-jobs) and [POST: Create new openings](https://developers.greenhouse.io/harvest.html#post-create-new-openings).

**Learn more**

[HRIS Link best practices](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360059570892)

[HRIS Link and data preservation](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/4493539946651)

# Sterling, A First Advantage Company, Seamless Enhanced (US/EMEA) integration

Sterling’s extensive partner ecosystem offers flexible pre-built integration options and a dedicated team of trusted experts making for a quick and easy implementation.

Integrating an HR system doesn’t have to take weeks. Together with their partners, [Sterling](https://www.sterlingcheck.com/) helps clients activate a straightforward set-up for standard integrations in days. That's why 60% of Sterling’s global business is integrated with Application Programming Interfaces (APIs) or Applicant Tracking Systems (ATS).

You can count on Sterling to provide:

  * Hand-in-hand support delivering white-glove service.
  * Proprietary automated onboarding tools for fast integration.
  * Continued investment by consistently adding new integrations.



Teams can save time by configuring screenings to automatically trigger when their candidates reach a specific stage in the hiring process, removing the need to access their Client Hub dashboard for screening details.

Sterling’s integration with Greenhouse Recruiting allows recruiters to launch background screenings for candidates directly from Greenhouse.

#### In this article

  * Enable the Sterling Seamless Enhanced / Greenhouse Recruiting integration
    * Configure your webhook oauth credential
    * Create a webhook 
    * Create a Harvest API key
  * Use the Sterling Seamless Enhanced integration with Greenhouse Recruiting
    * Initiate an order
    * View order status and results
  * Additional considerations
    * Generating integration users
    * Configuring additional packages as custom fields
    * Reviewing order status and score information
    * Status and results post back
  * Additional resources



### Enable the Sterling Seamless Enhanced / Greenhouse Recruiting integration

#### Configure your webhook oauth credential

To integrate the Sterling’s Seamless Enhanced integration with Greenhouse Recruiting, you’ll first need to connect with your Sterling to review the integration process and receive a few data points you’ll need in order to set up the integration.

After connecting with Sterling, you’ll need to create the webhook oauth credentials to use when configuring the webhook. 

  * **Configure** → **Dev Center** → **Web Hooks** → _Web Hook OAuth Credentials_



Once on this screen, the user must input the below to configure OAuth for their client:

  * **Name this credential** : Sterling-Dynamic
  * **OAuth Token URL** : Test Environment: <https://integration.int.com/oauth/screeningdirect/v2/token>  
Production Environment: [https://integration.sterlingts.com/oauth/screeningdirect/v2/token](https://integration.int.sterlingts.com/oauth/screeningdirect/v2/token)
  * **Client ID** (provided by Sterling)
  * **Client Secret** (provided by Sterling)
  * Set the _Grant Type_ to **Client Credentials**



Click **Create Web hook oauth credential** when finished.

#### Create a webhook

After configuring your OAuth credentials for the Sterling Seamless Enhanced integration, you'll need to create a webhook.

Follow the steps in [ this article](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/5888163727003) to create your webhook. As a standard, Sterling supports one webhook per integration, but can address a request for multiple web hooks on a client-by-client basis.

Use the values listed below to configure the webhook:

  * **Name** : A descriptive name for your integration. Most customers choose _Sterling-Dynamic_ integration.
  * **When** : Candidate has Changed Stage
  * **Endpoint URL** : The Endpoint URL provided by Sterling
  * **Secret Key** : The Secret Key provided by Sterling



Once done, navigate to **Advanced Settings** and locate the _Web Hook OAuth Credential_ field.

Set the webhook oauth credential to **Sterling-Dynamic** and click **Create Web hook**. 

#### Create a Harvest API key

A Harvest API key must also be created for the Sterling Seamless Enhanced / Greenhouse Recruiting integration. Follow the steps in [this article](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/5888163769883) to create the key, and verify that the permissions below are selected when configuring the integration.

  * **Harvest API Type** : Harvest
  * **Partner** : Sterling
  * **Description** : _Sterling Harvest API Key_



**Note:** You cannot access the full Harvest API key again after clicking**I have stored the API Key.** If you lose your API key and need to access it later, you must create a new API key, provide it to Sterling and then revoke access to the original key.

#### Permissions

On the subsequent page, very the following permissions are selected:

**Applications**

  * Get: Retrieve Application

**Jobs**

  * Get: Retrieve Job

**Custom Fields**

  * Get: Get Custom Fields
  * Patch: Update Custom Fields

**Candidates**

  * Patch: Edit Candidate
  * Get: Retrieve Candidate



When finished, click **Save**.

Your Harvest API key for the Greenhouse Recruiting / Sterling Seamless Enhanced integration is created and configured. 

### Use the Sterling Seamless Enhanced integration with Greenhouse Recruiting

#### Initiate an order

To initiate a background check, navigate to the **All Jobs** tab in Greenhouse Recruiting and select a job.

From the job dashboard, select the **Candidates** tab from the left-hand menu panel to view the your applicants.

Select a candidate to place the order for and navigate to the candidate profile. 

**Advance** the candidate into the designated Sterling _Background Screening_ stage.

**Note:** The Sterling Seamless Enhanced integration is configured to automatically send the candidate a Sterling e-invite once candidates have been moved into a designated integration stage, [configured per client](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/5888163696923), typically titled _Background Check_.

#### View order status and results

After successfully submitting your order, the order status will update in Greenhouse Recruiting. Select the **Private** tab on the candidate profile to locate an order status update.

The _Candidate Details_ tab will update the _Sterling Status_ , _Sterling Comments,_ and _Screening Level Results/Score_ as the candidate’s background screening is being fulfilled.

Once the order is complete, Sterling will post the _Order Status_ , _Order Result/Score_ , _Screening Level Result/Score_ , _Sterling Comments_ , any PII and the _Sterling Report URL_ back to Greenhouse Recruiting. 

To view the detailed final report, click the link under _Sterling Report URL_.

The report URL will redirect you to Sterling for you to Log in. Once signed in, access the **Order Manager** to view the order and report details.

**Note:** To view the order status and results within a candidate's **Private** tab, a user must be either a Site Admin with the [additional permission](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360021113491) to**see private notes, salary info, manage offers, request approval, and approve jobs/offers** assigned or a Job Admin [who can view and edit private candidate and application fields](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360039518131).

### Additional considerations 

#### Generating integration users

The Sterling Integration team will be responsible for creating the initial client user, who will then become the Super User and can add new integration users via Sterling. Sterling requires the following fields to create new users:

  * First name
  * Last name
  * Email address



#### Configuring additional packages as custom fields

To add the list of packages, you will need to get the package names from Sterling and then do the following:

  * **Login** to Greenhouse Recruiting → **Configure** → **Custom Options** → **Jobs** → _Sterling Package_ →[ Enter the list of packages in the _Options_ field](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/202609855) → Check off **Mark Private** → **Save**



Optional [custom fields](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/10978274576667) can be added to the Sterling Seamless Enhanced integration and can be used for posting back additional data points from Sterling upon the client’s request, configuring sub-accounts/billcodes, etc. Reach out to [Sterling support](https://www.sterlingcheck.com/contact/) or your Sterling AM for any questions.

  * Login to _Greenhouse Recruiting_ → **Configure** → **Custom Options**
  * The user can determine what aspect of the integration they’d like to add [the custom field](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360001421452).
  * Custom Options → [Jobs](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/202609855) (or you can select any Company Custom Fields)



#### Reviewing order status and score information

#### Status

The following statuses are supported within the Sterling integration with Greenhouse Recruiting:

Sterling status | Description | Status in Greenhouse  
---|---|---  
Initiated | Background Check Order is launched.  **Note:** This status indicates that the order is successfully initiated. An e-invite is sent to the candidate to come to Sterling’s Candidate Hub and provide the required information. | Initiated  
Error | The Background Check Order request errored out. | Error  
Pending | Candidate received the e-invite and successfully submitted the required information to Sterling. Sterling has started fulfilling the order. | Pending  
Complete | Background Check Order is fulfilled. | Complete  
Pre-Adverse Action Initiated | Client has initiated Adverse Action. | Pre-Adverse Action Initiated  
Pre-Adverse Action Sent | Pre-Adverse Action Letter is sent to the candidate. | Pre-Adverse Action Sent  
Adverse Action Paused | Client has paused the Adverse Action. | Adverse Action Paused  
Adverse Action Resumed | Client has resumed the Adverse Action. | Adverse Action Resumed  
Adverse Action Sent | Final Adverse Action is sent. | Adverse Action Sent  
Adverse Action Cancelled | Client has cancelled Adverse Action. | Complete  
  
####  Scores

The following scores are available within the Sterling Seamless Enhanced / Greenhouse Recruiting. Order scores are available both with Sterling’s Client Matrix Application (CMA) and without CMA.

Client Matrix Application (CMA) based order scores are available both at the order and screening levels. Sterling provides 2-Level and 3-Level scores with CMA.

The following scores are supported with 2-Level CMA:

  * Passed
  * Review



The following scores are supported with 3-Level CMA:

  * Level 1
  * Level 2
  * Level 3



Results/Scores | Description | Results/Scores in Greenhouse Recruiting  
---|---|---  
Clear | Indicates all screenings are completed and meets client criteria | Clear  
Passed | Passed  
Level 1 | Level 1  
Consider | Indicates all screenings are completed and order has discrepancies | Consider  
Review | Review  
Level 2 | Level 2  
Level 3 | Level 3  
  
The following scores are supported without CMA:

  * Clear
  * Consider



#### Status and results post back

Custom Fields have been pre-configured to post back the Sterling _Order Status_ , _Order Result/Score_ , _Screening Level Results/Scores_ , _Comments_ , and _Report URL_.

### Additional resources

For additional information not covered here, reach out to your Sterling Account Manager or check

<https://fadv.com/customers/>

**More from Sterling**

[Sterling Interactive (US/EMEA) integration](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/201293385)

[Sterling (RISQ)(APAC) integration](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/10033850918427)

# Sign your E-Signature documents

**Permissions:** Employees

**Product tier:** Available for the Greenhouse Onboarding subscription tier

Your organization can assign E-Signature documents as part of your onboarding plan to automate the paperwork process and collect important signatures from you.

This article covers how to complete and download your assigned E-Signature documents in Greenhouse Onboarding.

#### In this article

  * Review your assigned documents
  * Sign a document
  * Download a completed document
  * Additional resources



### Review your assigned documents

When you've been assigned E-Signature documents, you can review which documents you need to complete:

  * From the **Documents to Sign** section of your [Greenhouse Onboarding homepage](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/115002199766)
  * From the **Documents** tab in your [employee profile](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/5759718119707)



### Sign a document

From your Greenhouse Onboarding homepage, scroll to  _Documents to Sign_.

Click **Needs Signing** next to the E-Signature document you want to sign.

Alternatively, you can navigate to **Documents** in your employee profile.

Click the **three dots** icon next to the document you want to sign, then click **Sign**.

Your E-Signature document or form will appear in a dialog box. Click **Get started** to begin signing.

Click on a required E-Signature field to add your signature.

Draw, type, or upload your signature, then click **Insert**.

Repeat this step for all required signatures in your E-Signature document.

Click **Continue** , then click **I agree** to complete your E-Signature.

### Download a completed document

Once you've signed your E-Signature document, you can download a copy to keep for your own records.

# JobTwine integration

JobTwine streamlines the recruitment process with intelligent tools and a user-friendly platform, helping you find the right talent for your organization 3x faster.

By helping companies conduct structured interviews using intelligently-curated playbooks, JobTwine offers a full-stack interview solution ranging from efficient job creation to seamlessly collecting feedback.

JobTwine’s integration with Greenhouse Recruiting allows recruiters to schedule and conduct interview rounds for their jobs. 

#### In this article

  * Enable the Greenhouse Recruiting / JobTwine integration
    * Create a Harvest API key 
    * Create web hooks and finish setup 
  * Use the JobTwine integration with Greenhouse Recruiting
    * Add the JobTwine stage to your interview plan
    * Export candidates to JobTwine
  * Additional resources



### Enable the Greenhouse Recruiting / JobTwine integration

#### Create a Harvest API key 

To configure the JobTwine integration, you’ll first need to create a Harvest API key.

Follow the steps in [this article](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/5888163769883) to create the key, and verify that the permissions below are selected when configuring the JobTwine integration.

#### Credentials

In the _Create New Credential_ box, make the following selections:

  * **API Type:** Harvest
  * **Partner:** JobTwine or _Unlisted Vendor_
  * **Description:** JobTwine Harvest API Key



#### Permissions

Verify that the following permissions are selected for the JobTwine integration:

**Candidates**

  * GET: Retrieve Candidate
  * POST: Add Note
  * POST: Add Attachment



**Jobs**

  * GET: Get Hiring team
  * GET: Retrieve Job



**Job Openings**

  * GET: List Openings For a Job



**Job Posts**

  * GET: Retrieve Job Post for Job



**Job Stages**

  * GET: Retrieve Job Stage
  * GET: List Job Stages for Job



**Scheduled Interviews**

  * GET: List Interviews for Application
  * GET: Retrieve Interview



**Scorecards**

  * GET: Retrieve Scorecard
  * GET: List Scorecards for Application
  * GET: Retrieve Application's Scorecard



**Users**

  * GET: Retrieve User



When finished, click **Save**.

Your Harvest API key for the Greenhouse Recruiting / JobTwine integration is created and configured.

Provide your created key to your JobTwine representative to complete configuration. 

**Note:** You cannot access the full Harvest API key again after clicking **I have stored the API Key**. If you lose your API key and need to access it later, you must create a new API key, provide it to the integration partner, and then revoke access to the original key.

#### Create web hooks and finish setup 

To complete setup for the Greenhouse Recruiting / JobTwine integration, you’ll need to:

  1. [Get your JobTwine Organization ID](mailto:support@jobtwine.com)
  2. Create 3 webhooks



Follow the steps in [this article](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/5888163727003) to create you web hooks after working with JobTwine to receive your JobTwine organization ID. Use the values listed below to configure each webhook:

**Webhook 1: Job post created**

  * **Name** : JobTwine integration
  * **When** : Job post created
  * **Endpoint URL** : [The Endpoint URL provided by JobTwine](https://domain.name/webhook/webhook/{yourJobTwineOrgId})
  * **Secret Key** : The Secret Key provided by JobTwine



**Webhook 2: Job post updated**

  * **Name** : JobTwine integration
  * **When** : Job post updated
  * **Endpoint URL** : [The Endpoint URL provided by JobTwine](https://domain.name/webhook/webhook/{yourJobTwineOrgId})
  * **Secret Key** : The Secret Key provided by JobTwine



**Webhook 3: Candidate has changed stage**

  * **Name** : JobTwine integration
  * **When:** Candidate has changed stage
  * **Endpoint URL** : [The Endpoint URL provided by JobTwine](https://domain.name/webhook/webhook/{yourJobTwineOrgId})
  * **Secret Key** : The Secret Key provided by JobTwine



**Note:** To get your JobTwine Organization ID, [contact JobTwine](mailto:support@jobtwine.com).

After receiving your JobTwine Organization ID and completing your webhook set up, the JobTwine integration will be available for use in Greenhouse Recruiting. 

### Use the JobTwine integration with Greenhouse Recruiting

#### Add the JobTwine stage to your interview plans

After enabling the Greenhouse / JobTwine integration for your organization, you'll need to add JobTwine as an interview stage on your jobs. 

**Note:** JobTwine will ignore all jobs without JobTwine configured as an interview stage.

[When you're adding a new stage to an interview plan](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/115002194903), the JobTwine stage will display for selection within the listed stage options. Select the JobTwine stage to add it to the interview plan.

Once you've added JobTwine to your interview plan, you'll need to confirm any external job post status is set to **Live**.

Navigate to the **job dashboard > Job Setup > Job Posts **to toggle the post status to **Live.**

**Note:** JobTwine will ignore all jobs that are not live externally or are turned **OFF**. 

If the posting is offline, toggle to **Live**. 

Once the job post status is Live and JobTwine is configured as an interview stage, the job configuration will be pulled into the JobTwine system.

Now, you can navigate to the JobTwine platform, and use one of JobTwine’s intelligently curated playbooks to create your first job round - or create one of your own entirely.

#### Export candidates to JobTwine from Greenhouse Recruiting 

To export candidates for scheduling using the Greenhouse Recruiting / JobTwine integration, the candidate must first be active in the configured JobTwine interview stage.

**Note:** Candidates not currently active in a JobTwine interview stage will not be pushed to JobTwine. 

Click **Move Stage** to manually advance candidates to the JobTwine stage or [create a stage transition rule](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360053129752) to automate candidates being moved to this stage.

After advancing candidates to the JobTwine stage, JobTwine will input the candidate into the system for scheduling. 

The candidate will be automatically scheduled for the first job interview round once moved. 

From here, you can easily schedule the candidate with either JobTwine or your own interviewers, create more job rounds, move the candidate through interviews based on the interview feedback received.

Actions taken in JobTwine for candidate scheduling will be synced using candidate notes within the [candidate's **Activity Feed**](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360037386272) in Greenhouse Recruiting. 

If more information is desired to be shared or transferred between Greenhouse Recruiting and JobTwine by your team, reach out to JobTwine Customer Success to discuss additional field additions. 

### Additional resources

For additional information not covered here, reach out to [support@jobtwine.com](mailto:support@jobtwine.com).

# Entelo integration

Entelo is the world’s first all-in-one, source-to-hire recruitment automation platform that’s changing the way companies hire. Entelo's mission is to deliver remarkably intelligent end-to-end experiences for Talent Acquisition. Entelo provides your organization with technology that leverages data science, machine learning, predictive analytics, candidate engagement, and recruitment marketing best practices to help your teams find the right talent and hire faster. All while delivering an exceptional candidate experience.

Greenhouse Recruiting's integration with Entelo ensures you have all the information you need to confidently take action on a candidate, whether you are viewing their profile within Entelo or Greenhouse. As an integrated Greenhouse Recruiting user, you'll have access to the following features:

  * Discover which candidates have already been added to Greenhouse Recruiting, and what actions have been taken on them, without leaving the Entelo Search results page
  * Prioritize candidate rediscovery or new pipeline development by including or excluding Greenhouse Recruiting candidates respectively from searches run on Entelo
  * View all Entelo Track activity within a candidate’s Greenhouse Recruiting profile to get a better understanding of their past engagement history

# Supported formats for resumes, cover letters and other candidate uploads

#### In this article

Supported candidate uploads

Other candidate uploads

Large or unsupported candidate files

### Supported candidate uploads

When creating your job post, you'll ask candidates to submit documents, like resumes and cover letters. As part of their application, candidates can upload the following file types:

  * .doc
  * .docx
  * .pdf
  * .rtf
  * .txt



Candidate uploads can be **up to 100 MB** , which will support most cover letters and resumes. 

### Other candidate uploads

You can also ask candidates to upload other files that are relevant to your hiring process. From your **job post** , scroll to "Custom application questions" and select "Add custom question." 

From the "Answers" dropdown menu, choose "Attachment."

Candidates can upload **doc, docx, pdf, rtf and txt** files that are a maximum of **100 MB**.

### Large or unsupported candidate files

If you'd like candidates to submit videos, portfolios, or other files larger than **100 MB** , ask them to upload the file to a third party site (like Google Drive) and share the link with your hiring team.

From your **job post** , select "Add custom question." 

Go to "Answers" and choose "Short text box" to allow candidates to enter the URL for the third-party hosted file.

# Offer section overview

**Permissions:** –

**Product tier:** Available for Plus and Pro subscription tiers

Every offer is unique.

For example, your organization may want different language on offer letters if the job opening is Full-time, Part-time, or Contract. When using normal templates, Site Admins would have to create a separate template for each selection in this field. This problem becomes even more complicated when you have more than one custom offer field and want specialized text for each combination.

With offer sections, you can enter language for custom offer fields that show different text based on the selection in the custom offer field. You can also include tokens inside of the offer sections to further customize and personalize your offer letters, and reduce the amount of templates recruiters will need to sift through for each offer document. 

**Note:** If a new option is added to the custom offer field, an offer section will not be created by default. A Site Admin must define the offer section for each new option. Additionally, if an existing custom offer field option is renamed or deleted, any configured offer section text for that option will be removed.

For more information on how to configure and manage offer sections, check out the links below: 

  * [Create offer section](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360039122371)
  * [Edit offer section](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360039122851)

# Assign candidate tags automatically (auto-tag)

**Permissions:** Job Admins, who can create, edit, and delete job posts, and Site Admins

**Product tier:** Available for new subscription tiers (Core, Plus, and Pro)

With **Auto-Tag** , you can set up [application rules](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/203105595) that will automatically assign a certain tag to a candidate based on their answers during their application. You can then use these tags to [filter the _All Candidates_ page](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360043184152) to get a more specific view of your available candidates.

**Example:** For the custom job post question, "What cities are you available to work in?", you can configure auto-tagging so candidates who answer _Boston_ are automatically tagged with **Available for Boston**. 

#### In this article

  * Create custom candidate tags
  * Create a custom job post question
  * Create an auto-tag application rule
  * View auto-tagged candidates



### Create custom candidate tags

**Note:** To create custom candidate tags, Job Admin users must also have the [user-specific permission](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/205614645) **Can manage company metadata**.

Navigate to the _Custom Options_ page and select**Candidate Tags.**_(**Configure** icon  > **Custom Options** > **Candidates Tags**) _

Click **Create New Candidate Tag**.

Enter a label for your tag and click **Create Candidate Tag**. 

### Create a custom job post question

After you create a custom candidate tag, you'll need to add a custom job post question that will be associated with your application rule. 

**Note:** Auto-Tagging can be configured only for questions of the following type: 

  * Yes/No
  * Single select
  * Multi select



Navigate to the _Job Posts_ tab for the job where you want to assign tags. _(**Jobs** > select a job from the list > **Job Setup** >**Job Posts**) _

Click the Edit icon  next to the job post.

Scroll down the page to the _Custom Application Question_ section and click **Add Custom Question**.

Enter your question in the text field and choose the question type.

**Note** : Remember, auto-tagging rules can only be used on Yes/No, single-select, and multi-select question types.

If you chose a single-select or multi-select question, list the response choices in the _Options_ field. When you have finished, click **Add**.

Scroll to the bottom of the _Edit Job Post_ page and click **Save** to confirm the changes.

### Create an auto-tag application rule

After you create a custom tag and define an application question, you'll create an application rule that will automatically tag any matching candidates.

To create a new rule, stay on the Job Posts page on a job, and click **Manage Rules** in the Application Rules column. 

**Note:** This button will have a different label (such as **2 Rules**) if you previously added application rules.

Click**Add a Rule**. If you want to modify an existing rule to auto-tag candidates, click the **Edit** icon  instead.

Select your job post question and the candidate's response in the top half of the page. Then, select the **Tag** checkbox.

Select the correct tags from the dropdown menu. You can select more than one tag.

When you're finished, click **Save**.

### View auto-tagged candidates

You can view any automatically tagged candidates by selecting the tag in the **Candidate Tag** filter on the _Candidates_ page. 

For more detailed information on filtering candidates, [click here](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360043184152).

# Calendly integration

**Permissions:** Job Admin and above

**Product tier:** Available for new subscription tiers (Core, Plus, and Pro)

Calendly streamlines the scheduling process by allowing others to directly schedule meetings in available time slots on your calendar.

Greenhouse Recruiting's integration with Calendly allows you to schedule candidate interviews directly from Greenhouse Recruiting with your own Calendly link or with the Calendly link of another user assigned to the job.

**Note** : This integration is available for all Calendly users, including unpaid, premium, and pro accounts.

People who wish to schedule to and from their calendars must enable this integration on their personal Greenhouse Recruiting accounts.

#### In this article

  * Enable the integration
  * Use the integration
    * Calendly email template
    * Schedule an interview
    * Schedule interviews in bulk
    * Schedule an interview with another person's Calendly link
    * Reschedule or cancel an interview with Calendly
    * Use stage transition rules with Calendly



### Enable the integration

To enable Calendly, click **Integrations** on your navigation bar.

Search for **Calendly** and click **Connect**.

Enter your work email address and click **Continue**.

Follow the prompts on Calendly to complete the setup process.

**Note:** If you sign up for Calendly with a Google, Office 365, or Microsoft Exchange email address, you'll be prompted to log in using the username and password for that account. This allows you to access Calendly using your account's credentials so you don't have to create and manage a new password. Alternatively, click **Sign up** on the Calendly login page to create a Calendly username and password.

Select **Allow** on the permissions request.

On the final page, click **Connect to Calendly** to complete the integration setup.

You'll be redirected to Greenhouse Recruiting where you will see the option to disconnect Calendly, indicating the integration setup was successful.

### Use the integration

#### Calendly email template

**Note** : To configure a custom Calendly email template for your entire organization, you need to be a Site Admin, or a Job Admin with the additional user-specific permission 'Can manage company email and social media templates.'

Greenhouse Recruiting provides a default email template to request an interview through Calendly. You can also create and send a customized email template to request an interview through Calendly.

**Note** : Unlike other customizable email templates in Greenhouse Recruiting, the Calendly email type doesn't support office and department-specific templates. It also doesn't support email attachments.

To create a new email template for Calendly, click the **Configure** icon on your navigation bar then select **Email** **Templates**.

Click **\+ New** under _My Templates_ or _Organization-wide templates_.

Select **Calendly Email** from the type, and construct your email template as you wish. Tokens available for use in the email are listed above the email body.

**Note** : Don't include a Calendly link in the body of the email. Greenhouse Recruiting will automatically generate a link in the email.

When finished, click **Save** , and your email template is ready for use.

**Tip** : Learn more about [creating custom email templates](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/115004020946).

#### Schedule an interview with Calendly

To schedule an interview with Calendly, find the interview on the Stages tab of their candidate profile and click **Schedule with Calendly**.

**Note** : You can't use Calendly to schedule on stages with multiple interviews or with multiple Calendly events.

Configure the details of the email. Greenhouse Recruiting will automatically include the Calendly scheduling link.

Once the candidate selects an interview date and time, the interviewer will receive an email notification from Calendly.

**Note** : The email notification sent to the interviewer from Calendly won't contain a link to the candidate's [interview kit](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/115002226826).

**Tip** : After the interview has been scheduled, you can set an [automatic email reminder](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/17435302491547) to be sent to the candidate 24 hours before the interview.

#### Schedule interviews with Calendly in bulk

To use the bulk scheduling feature, all candidates included in the bulk action must be on the same job, in the same stage, with exactly one interview that is ready to be scheduled.

Click**Candidates** on your navigation bar.

Expand the _Application Type_ filter panel and set the _Type_ to candidates only _._

Expand the _Jobs_ filter panel and click **Filter By Job** to select a single job.

Use the **Stage** filter to select a specific stage for the job.

Use the filter **Pipeline Tasks** and check **To Be Scheduled**.

After you've correctly filtered the list of candidates, click **Bulk Actions**.

Select the candidates and click **Edit Selected (#)**.

Click **Schedule with Calendly**.

Select your name or the name of the interviewer from the **Calendly Interviewer** dropdown.

Choose an event type from the **Calendly Event Type** dropdown.

When finished, click **Send email**.

**Note** : The bulk action feature won't send a Calendly email invitation to candidates who have already been sent a Calendly email invitation.

#### Schedule an interview with another person's Calendly link

To send a different user's Calendly link when scheduling a candidate interview, the user must have a Calendly account, with the Calendly integration enabled, and they must have Job Admin level or higher permissions on the same job.

To schedule an interview with another user's Calendly link, navigate to a candidate's profile who needs to be scheduled for an interview and click **Schedule with Calendly**.

Select your teammate's name from the **Calendly Interviewer** dropdown and choose an event type from the **Calendly Event Type** dropdown. Greenhouse Recruiting will populate the event types your teammate has configured in their Calendly account.

When finished, click **Send****Email**.

Greenhouse Recruiting will add your teammate's Calendly link to the email and send it to the candidate's email address. Once the candidate selects an interview date and time, the interviewer will receive an email notification from Calendly.

Additionally, the scheduled interview will also be available on the candidate's profile.

#### Reschedule or cancel an interview with Calendly

An interview scheduled through the Calendly integration can be rescheduled by any user with at least Job Admin level permissions on the job.

Greenhouse users can reschedule directly from the candidate's profile in Greenhouse Recruiting.

Navigate to the candidate's profile and find the interview that needs to be rescheduled. Click **Reschedule**.

Select a new date and time for the interview.

Click **Confirm**.

Click **Update Event** when finished.

A confirmation email will be sent to the interviewers and the candidate informing them that the interview has been rescheduled.

**Note** : Interviews scheduled with Calendly can also be rescheduled by the candidate.

To do so, candidates need to locate the interview confirmation notification email where they can click **Reschedule** to propose a new time.

#### Cancel an interview with Calendly

An interview scheduled through the Calendly integration can be canceled by any user with at least Job Admin level permissions on the job.

Navigate to a candidate's profile and find the interview that will be canceled.

Click **Cancel**.

A confirmation email will be sent to the interviewers and the candidate informing them that the interview has been canceled.

Interviews scheduled through the Calendly integration can also be canceled by the candidate. Candidates can cancel from the confirmation email sent by the email provider informing them that a new event has been added to their calendar. From the interview confirmation email, the candidate can click **Cancel**.

### Use stage transition rules with Calendly

You can configure a [stage transition rule](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360048178672) to automatically send a Calendly request when a candidate is moved to a specified stage.

To edit a Calendly request stage transition rule created by another user, you must have enabled the Calendly integration in your Greenhouse Recruiting account.

**Note** : If you haven't enabled the Calendly integration, you can still view and delete Calendly request stage transition rules created by others.

**Tip** : Changes to a Calendly configuration, such as a user disconnecting their Calendly account from Greenhouse Recruiting, may prevent the Calendly request stage transition rule from running. To resolve this, [edit](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360048337832), [delete](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360048335732), and recreate the Calendly request stage transition rule.

**Learn more**

[Calendly and Microsoft Teams](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360052219651)

[Troubleshoot the Calendly integration](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/13503895279387)

# Structuring offices and departments for your HRIS integration

This guide details the role of offices and departments in Greenhouse Recruiting and outlines the options for assigning these values to jobs imported from your HRIS.

If you still have questions about the appropriate office and department structure for your organization after reviewing this guide, please contact your Greenhouse Customer Success Manager.

#### In this article

  * How are offices and departments used in Greenhouse Recruiting?
  * Can I import my office and department structure from my HRIS?
  * Assigning jobs to offices and departments through an HRIS integration
  * Additional resources



### How are offices and departments used in Greenhouse Recruiting?

Offices and departments impact the following areas within Greenhouse Recruiting:

  * User permissions
  * Job and offer approvals
  * Job board configuration
  * Dashboard and reporting filters
  * Custom field configurations
  * Email template and offer template configurations



Check out the following article for more details: [Office and department-dependent workflows](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360029591631-Office-and-department-dependent-workflows). 

### Can I import my office and department structure from my HRIS?

Yes, you can import your office and department structure from your HRIS. If you're using [HRIS Link](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360055282972), it will create or update your Greenhouse Recruiting offices and departments based on any changes made to the corresponding fields in your HRIS.

Check out the following article to learn more: [FAQ: Import offices and departments with HRIS Link](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360059152791).

If you are building an API-driven integration, it is possible to create and update offices and departments through the Harvest API.  
Check out the following article to learn more: [Sync offices and departments from an external system](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360029625351).

If you prefer to maintain your Greenhouse Recruiting office and department structure manually, you can do so in Greenhouse Recruiting on the _Organization_ page.

As a general rule, we strongly recommend creating an office and department structure in Greenhouse Recruiting that you do not expect to change frequently. Frequent changes to your Greenhouse Recruiting offices and departments could mean frequent manual re-assigning of jobs and permissions and restructuring of default approvals.

### Assigning jobs to offices and departments through an HRIS integration

There are two options we recommend when importing organizational values from an HRIS.

#### Option 1: Map HRIS values directly to your Greenhouse Recruiting office and departments structure

If there are HRIS fields and option values that align with the needs and structure of your Greenhouse offices and departments, we recommend mapping these field values to your Greenhouse Recruiting office and department structure, as long as the field values are relatively static.

When you import a job from an HRIS, the office or department that you want to assign the job to must already exist in Greenhouse Recruiting. Assigning a job to a Greenhouse Recruiting office and department at the time of job creation ensures any office- and department-dependent approval flows and user permissions are configured in Greenhouse Recruiting are applied.

#### Option 2: Use job custom fields to represent HRIS organizational values, and create a separate office and department structure for Greenhouse Recruiting

If there are no HRIS fields whose values align with the office and/or department values needed for Greenhouse Recruiting, you can maintain a separate office and department structure in Greenhouse Recruiting. Any HRIS organizational values you want to import with jobs, such as _Cost Center_ and _Supervisory Organization_ , can be added as custom job fields.

**Note** : If you’re building an API-based job import or using HRIS Link with these options, you'll still need additional logic in the integration layer to determine the correct Greenhouse Recruiting office and department to assign to the job through the API. This can be implemented via an evaluate expression calc field, a custom object in your HRIS, or integration logic. If using a RaaS-based job import, users can assign the office and department manually when they create the job in Greenhouse Recruiting.

### Additional resources

  * [Set up HRIS Link office and department import](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360058921191)
  * [Import offices and departments with HRIS Link](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360058975151)
  * [FAQ: Import offices and departments with HRIS Link](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360059152791)
  * [Office and department-dependent workflows](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360029591631)
