# Structured hiring guide

****

**With structured hiring, you define the role requirements, the attributes of successful candidates and the evaluation process for each role you open.**

Now that you’ve learned how to set up jobs during implementation, it’s time to level-up with the basics of structured hiring. Here are five steps you can follow to start building your structured hiring process.

### Here’s the plan

  * Set up a kickoff meeting

  * Create a scorecard

  * Schedule interviews

  * Set expectations for scorecard submission 
  * Facilitate a roundup meeting




# Step 1

### Set up a kick off meeting

A [kickoff meeting](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360007247092-Structured-Hiring-Role-Kick-Off-Meeting) for a new role is the first step in the structured hiring process and it should happen before a role is opened. This is when the hiring team – typically the hiring manager, recruiter and coordinator – define the following: 

  


  * The ideal candidate based on the [business objectives](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360007247092-Structured-Hiring-Role-Kick-Off-Meeting#%E2%80%9Cobjectives%E2%80%9D) of the job
  * The [skills, traits and qualifications](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360007247092-Structured-Hiring-Role-Kick-Off-Meeting#%E2%80%9Cquals%E2%80%9D) that will make someone successful in the job
  * The [roles and responsibilities](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360007247092-Structured-Hiring-Role-Kick-Off-Meeting#%E2%80%9Croles%E2%80%9D) of the hiring team during the hiring process



Ready to go? Use this [worksheet](https://www.greenhouse.io/guidance/structured-hiring-101-worksheets-3) to help you organize and facilitate an effective kickoff meeting.

Once you determine the details of your kickoff meeting, use the [job kickoff](https://www.greenhouse.io/blog/set-your-structured-hiring-process-up-for-success-with-the-job-kickoff-form) feature under the “Job Setup” tab. This intuitive, comprehensive tool provides a natural flow to guide you through the kickoff conversation and ensure you’re capturing all the information you need to start recruiting successfully.

# Step 2

### Create a scorecard

The kickoff meeting should uncover all the information you need to [create a relevant scorecard](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/115002194863-Configure-New-Scorecard).

Your scorecard is part of your interview kit and is where you’ll define attributes for a successful candidate and outline interview questions for each interviewer. Here are the best practices steps for creating a scorecard:

**Create a job in Greenhouse**

We recommend copying from [a template job](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360038222812-Create-a-Template-Job) you or your team has created and eventually [building a set of job templates](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360038222812-Create-a-Template-Job) to choose from.

**Configure categories for attributes**

Categories are used to organize your scorecard into sections, based on the sets of attributes you’ll interview for. We recommend including three or four categories per job.

**Fill in the attributes for each category**

Attributes are the specific skills and qualifications required within each category. Use no more than five or six attributes per category so you can realistically evaluate them and make them specific. 

To keep each interviewer focused and efficient, be sure to take these actions when building the rest of your interview kit:

**Assign focus attributes**

Within your interview kit, [assign focus attributes](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360018399451-Focus-Attributes-on-Scorecards) from your scorecard so interviewers can more easily identify the attributes each interview should assess.

**Create custom questions**

Build [custom questions](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/115002276366-Create-Custom-Questions-for-Interview-Kits) based on the assigned focus attributes to ensure every interview has a unique set of questions that keep your candidates engaged.

**  
Pro tip – You can also [link focus attributes to specific interview questions.](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360018399451-Focus-Attributes-on-Scorecards)**

# Step 3

### Schedule interviews 

Scheduling interviews within Greenhouse is key for driving structured hiring buy-in across your company because it enables a seamless experience for all your interviewers.

With Greenhouse Recruiting, you can coordinate, sync and manage your organization's interview schedule across multiple interviewer calendars. Think of Greenhouse as a compiler that aggregates changes made to an interviewer's calendar, and then pushes those updates via email to the relevant candidate's calendar. 

**The**[**Greenhouse scheduling model**](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360021717371-Greenhouse-Scheduling-Model)**guides you through scheduling functionality.**

Our email and calendar integrations simplify the scheduling process and work with the systems you already use, including: [Google Calendar](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360021799232-Enable-Google-Calendar), [Outlook 365 ](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/115003943972-Basic-Setup-Outlook-365-)and [Calendly](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360029359472-Enable-Calendly-Integration).

# Step 4

###  Set expectations for scorecard submission 

Before you begin interviewing, make sure your interview team is clear on how and when they’re expected to submit their scorecards. We recommend a minimum submission timeline of one business day following an interview, but the sooner, the better! 

We created our scorecard rating setup using science-based survey methods that account for the various ways an interviewer could interpret a scorecard. Our carefully crafted [scorecard rating system](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360035935611-Scorecard-ratings-overview) provides your organization with the best possible platform to reduce bias and individual differences.

Greenhouse will automatically send a reminder to your interviewers one hour after each interview has ended. You can also set up additional [automatic](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360047691292) and [manual reminders](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360027281232-Send-Scorecard-Reminders#h_99d9ee11-fe33-4e80-80ac-a53d8499ddfe) to keep your hiring team accountable.

**Use**[**these customizable training templates**](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/115003739232-Greenhouse-Roll-Out-Toolkit-Start-Here-)**and share**[**this Learn Greenhouse course**](https://learn.greenhouse.io/interviews-and-referrals/863666)**on how to submit interview feedback using interview kits to help set your interviewers up for success when submitting a scorecard.**

# Step 5

### Facilitate a roundup meeting

Once late-stage candidates have finished their pre-offer interviews and scorecards have been submitted, the next step in making an informed hiring decision is gathering the hiring team for a [candidate roundup meeting](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360007247872-Structured-Hiring-Candidate-Round-Up). These meetings can take 30 minutes to an hour, and should be where you constructively review scorecard data gathered during the interview process. Focus on candidates one by one with your team and aim to come out of the meeting with a hiring decision. 

A good roundup meeting should accomplish the following:

  * A decision on who you will extend an offer to
  * A short-list of actions required to make an offer
  * A review of any lessons learned and how you can apply them to the next role



In the roundup meeting, encourage hiring teams to focus on attributes, not gut feelings, to ensure the assessments are backed up by behavioral examples.

For example, if an assessment is vague, ask: “Can you provide an example?” or “Can you explain what made you feel that way?” 

**A final note:**

Once you’ve extended an offer and the candidate accepts, the final step in the hiring process is [marking a candidate as hired](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/200242039-Mark-Candidate-as-Hired-With-Offer-Approvals-). Completing this important step ensures the job is closed and your time-to-hire data is accurate.

**Note:** As your structured hiring process should always be a work in progress, it should be your goal to measurably improve with each iteration.

# Relode integration

The Relode marketplace provides employers with access to the largest network of independent recruiters and current labor market data via Relode Insights.

Using Relode Insights, employers can develop their hiring strategy by analyzing supply and demand in specific labor markets along with related salary ranges and diversity and inclusion metrics. Relode also offers employers access to a network of independent recruiters, allowing an organization to add thousands of recruiters to their team with the click of a button. 

The Relode integration allows employers to easily see their active jobs from Greenhouse Recruiting in Relode and receive qualified candidates from Relode recruiters directly into Greenhouse Recruiting. This enables employers to review labor market insights for each job and to broadcast the open job to the Relode recruiter network to source candidates, all while using your Greenhouse Recruiting hiring workflow to enhance the candidate experience.

#### In this article

  * Configure setup permissions in Greenhouse Recruiting
  * Create a Harvest API key for the Greenhouse Recruiting / Relode integration
  * Set up Relode as an agency in Greenhouse Recruiting
  * Enable the Greenhouse Recruiting / Relode integration on Relode

  * Use the Relode integration with Greenhouse Recruiting
  * Additional resources



### Configure setup permissions in Greenhouse Recruiting

To configure the Greenhouse Recruiting / Relode integration, you'll need the developer permission **Can manage ALL organization's API Credentials**.

To assign this permission, find a Greenhouse Recruiting user in your organization who is a **Site Admin** with the user-specific permission **Can edit another user's advanced permissions** to update your account.

Have the Site Admin update your permissions by navigating to the user page via **Configure** icon  >**Users** > **Your Name**.

The Site Admin should scroll to the _User-Specific_ _Permissions_ panel on your user page and expand the _Developer Permissions_ dropdown menu.

Select **Can manage ALL organization's API credentials** and click **Save**.

Repeat as necessary for any other user that needs to set up the integration.

### Create a Harvest API key for the Greenhouse Recruiting / Relode integration

_**Note:** To generate an API key, you must have the developer permission **Manage ALL organization's API Credentials**._

Click on the **Configure** icon  and select**Dev Center** on the left.

On the _Dev Center_ page, click **API Credential Management**.

From the _API Credential Management_ page, click **Create New API Key** to generate the API key for Relode.

In the _Create New Credential_ box, make the following selections:

  * **API Type:** Harvest
  * **Partner:** Relode
  * **Description:** Relode Harvest API Key



Click **Manage Permissions**.

Click **Copy** to save your API key to your clipboard. Store the API key in a secure location to provide to Relode later.

Click **I have stored the API Key** once you have copied and saved the key.

_**Note** : You won't be able to view the API key after clicking_ _**I have stored the API Key**. If you lose your API key or need to access it later, you'll need to generate a new key and provide it to Relode._

Select the checkboxes next to each permission box to associate it with the API key. The following permissions are needed for the Relode integration:

**ALL permissions** | **GET permissions**  
---|---  
Applications | 

  * Approvals 
    *       * Get: List Approval Flows For Job
      * Get: Get single approval flow

  
Candidates | 

  * Custom Field Options 
    *       * Get: Custom field options

  
Tags | 

  * Custom Fields 
    *       * Get: Get custom fields

  
EEOC | 

  * Offices 
    *       * Get: Retrieve Office
      * Get: List Offices

  
Scorecards | 

  * Job Openings 
    *       * Get: List Openings For a Job

  
Offers | 

  * Job Stages 
    *       * Get: Retrieve Job Stage
      * Get: List Job Stages
      * Get: List Job Stages for Job

  
Scheduled interviews | 

  * Job Posts 
    *       * Get: List Job Posts
      * Get: Retrieve Job Post for Job
      * Get: List Job Posts for Job

  
Activity Feed | 

  * Jobs 
    *       * Get: Retrieve Job
      * Get: List Jobs

  
Job stages | 

  * Custom Locations 
    *       * Get: Retrieve Custom Location for Job Board

  
Rejection reasons | 

  * Departments 
    *       * Get: Retrieve Department
      * Get: List Departments

  
Sources | 

  * Users 
    *       * Get: List User Future Job Permissions
      * Get: List User Job Permissions
      * Get: List Pending Approvals

  
Close reasons |   
Education |   
Demographic data |   
  
When you're finished, click **Save**.

Your Harvest API key for the Greenhouse Recruiting / Relode integration is created and configured.

Follow the steps below to complete the integration setup.

#### **Select the desired user for the Harvest API connection**

When candidates are created in Greenhouse Recruiting from Relode, the candidate's Activity Feed will show _Created via Harvest API on behalf of [the user you have chosen to associate with the API Connection]._

You can either choose an existing user or create a new user to show for new candidates created via the Greenhouse Recruiting / Relode integration.

_**Note:** The user you select must have **Site** **Admin** permission in Greenhouse Recruiting or the integration will not work properly._

To create a new user for the integration, navigate to **Configure** icon and select **Users** on the left.

Click **\+ New Users**.

Assign the user **Site** **Admin** permission.

Next, navigate to the user page again by clicking **Configure** icon  then click **Users**.

_**Note** : You may need to check 'Never signed in only' to view the new user in the list._

Find and click the name of the user you created or intend to use for the integration. Copy the user ID located in the URL on your browser, and store it in a secure location to provide to Relode later.

In the example below, the user id is **4537761003**.

### Set up Relode as an agency in Greenhouse Recruiting

All candidates submitted through the Relode integration will have Relode as their source.

To set up Relode as an agency, select **Ellipsis** icon  then click **Sourcing**.  
  


If Relode is not already set up as an agency, click **Add** **Agency** and input Relode's name.  
  


### Enable the Greenhouse Recruiting / Relode integration on Relode

Once you've completed the steps above, click to [submit this form](https://forms.office.com/Pages/ResponsePage.aspx?id=kbv2A3EDMkWyYDPdl5OfxRbkiN842lhNotHyP99tk8FUNjk3QlpOMTVUMDFZVlpPQUQ2WlRTQjMwTy4u) to the Relode team. You will need the following information to submit the form:

  * The Harvest API key from Greenhouse Recruiting
  * The user ID of the Greenhouse Recruiting user with whom you want to associate new candidates from Relode
  * Name of a default hiring stage on Greenhouse Recruiting for which all Relode candidates will be associated with



_**Note** : The stage you select must be a default stage and exist on all your jobs, like Application Review._

### Use the Relode integration with Greenhouse Recruiting

Once the integration is enabled, Relode will automatically synchronize all open jobs from Greenhouse Recruiting. These jobs will initially appear in a pending status in your Relode client portal.

Each job will have the following information from Greenhouse Recruiting:

  * Job title
  * Job location
  * Job stages and interview plans
  * Job hiring team
  * Job custom field info
  * Job post location
  * Job post description
  * Job openings
  * Job employment type
  * Job post application questions
  * Job departments
  * Job offices
  * Job notes



With each job you can review the Labor Market Insights by selecting the **Insights** tab on the job, or you can open the job to the Relode network of recruiters.

Once the integration is enabled, candidates submitted from the Relode network of recruiters will automatically be added to your organization's job in Greenhouse Recruiting. 

Candidates sourced from Relode to Greenhouse Recruiting include the following information:

  * First name
  * Last name
  * Email
  * Phone number
  * Address / location
  * Candidate's job position
  * Candidate's websites
  * Resume
  * Notes about the candidate including career highlights and desired salary



Additionally, candidates will show answers to the qualifications on the job in Relode which could include:

  * Certifications and licenses
  * Skills
  * Education
  * Languages
  * Custom questions
  * Interview availability
  * Willingness to relocate or travel (if applicable)
  * Availability to start



As you move and interview candidates in Greenhouse Recruiting, the candidate's status will be updated in Relode. This allows your Relode job manager to have real-time updates about the candidates progress so they can keep the referring recruiters informed.

The following information from Greenhouse Recruiting will automatically show in Relode:

  * Stage changes
  * Scorecard submitted
  * Offer letter sent
  * Interview updates



To locate candidates sourced from Relode in Greenhouse Recruiting, navigate to the **All** **Candidates** page and filter by **Source** on the left.   


On the candidate's profile, you can view their resume, profile information and their responses to Relode's application questions by selecting the **Activity** **Feed** tab.  


### Additional resources

**Do I have to associate a Site Admin with the Greenhouse Recruiting / Relode Integration?**

You can choose to use a Job Admin permission level for the user associated with the integration; however this will require your team to manually assign each job to the user. For each job in Greenhouse Recruiting you want submitted to Relode you will need to follow these steps:

From the **All** **Jobs** page, select your job and click **Job** **Setup** on the job.

Select **Hiring** **Team** on the left.  


Scroll to the _Who can see this job?_ section.

Search for the user associated with the Relode integration and set the desired permission level. Click **Save**.  


Repeat this for any other jobs you want to associate with the integration.

For additional information not covered here, reach out to your Relode CSM or visit [Relode Client Support](https://client-support.relode.com/).

# Send recruiting updates to coworkers or managers

You can easily share recruiting updates with your colleagues with the [candidate pipeline email](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360017980012).

To configure this email, click **Reports** on your navigation bar, then click **Essentials** **Library** on the left. From here, choose the **Reports** tab.

Scroll to the _Manage Expectations with Hiring Managers_ section and click **Candidate Pipeline Email**.

Use the filters on the left to choose which jobs to include in the update.

Select the specific jobs to be included in the message by checking the box beside the job name.

Up to 50 jobs can be included in a single email. 

When finished, click **Next**.

Select the stages on which you want to report and click **Next**.

A preview of the email will display in a pop-up window. Complete the **To** and **CC** fields to configure the recipients of the email. If you need to update the email text or add any notes, you can type in the **Body** field.

When finished, click **Send** **Report**.

You can read more about the candidate pipeline email here: [Candidate pipeline email report](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360017980012).

# Release notes: February 2026

Greenhouse Software regularly releases new product features, updates, and improvements. You can stay up-to-date by following our [release notes](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/200929955) or checking out the [latest feature releases](https://www.greenhouse.com/greenhouse-latest-features) page.

#### This month's releases

  * Greenhouse Recruiting
  * API
  * Integrations
  * Bug fixes



### Greenhouse Recruiting

#### Real Talent**™** is now available

**Greenhouse Real Talent™** is a top-of-funnel solution designed to help recruiting teams focus on real, qualified candidates faster. It brings together AI-powered Talent Matching, spam protection, fraud detection, and CLEAR® identity verification directly inside the Greenhouse workflow.

Real Talent reduces noise, protects against misrepresentation, and gives teams greater confidence in who they advance, all while keeping humans fully in control of hiring decisions.

[Read more about Real Talent.](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/45127324799003)

**Fraud detection**

Fraud detection flags suspicious applications by analyzing signals like phone number, email, IP address, and location, giving recruiters an early warning as they review applicants.

[Read more about fraud detection.](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/42738009117467)

**Spam blocklist**

Spam blocklist lets you block specific IP addresses or email domains and addresses based on patterns you’ve already seen, like repeat spam submissions or known bad actors. You decide who to block and can update the list anytime.

[Read more about the spam blocklist.](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/41595563125787)

**Identity verification**

Confirm candidate authenticity with integrated identity verification. Identity checks can be triggered at key moments in the process, like before interviews or offers, without slowing things down.

[Read more about identity verification.](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/40966215931291)

**Talent Matching**

AI-powered filters organize applications based on how they match your job criteria, such as skills, industry, and experience. Assistive filters make it easy to review the strongest matches first and quickly spot potential fraud risks.

Recruiters define and weigh the job criteria, see exactly why a candidate was flagged and filter applicants by priority candidates, fraud status, application date, location, and more. Talent Matching never advances or rejects candidates automatically.

[Read more about Talent Matching.](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/41396009937307)

Contact your account team to learn more about how to get access to Real Talent for your organization.

#### Scheduling buffer times

Schedulers can now add buffer time before and after interviews when creating self-scheduling requests or sending a scheduling link in Greenhouse. Buffers can be set in 15-minute increments and are automatically factored into interviewer availability, so candidates only see time slots that include protected prep or follow-up time.

Buffer times help prevent back-to-back interviews, reduces interviewer fatigue, and supports more thoughtful evaluations. By automatically building in breathing room, teams can create a more sustainable interview schedule without adding manual coordination or risk of errors.

[Read more about buffer times.](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/46278259991835)

#### Custom offer field dependencies

Organizations can now configure offer template dependencies based on offer custom field values, such as Relocation or Bonus Type. With support for single-select and multi-select custom fields, teams can control which templates are available for a given offer based on its field selections.

This helps reduce template selection errors and simplifies template management as teams version and update offer documents.

[Read more about custom offer field dependencies.](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360039294531)

#### Self-service setup for custom SMTP domains

Organizations can now fully manage their email sending settings directly under **Configure** > **Email** settings, instead of having to contact Technical Support to enable the feature. In addition to configuring custom SMTP, organizations can switch between custom SMTP and Mailgun and enter all required details right from the app, instead of contacting Greenhouse support.

[Read more about self-service email domain configuration.](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360002116131/live_preview/01KGMJX8TRHM883T371P3D8NQ5)

### API

  * You can now filter applications in Harvest v3 by the stage name string using the [List applications endpoint](https://harvestdocs.greenhouse.io/reference/get_v3-applications).



### Greenhouse Onboarding

#### Scheduled reporting

Greenhouse Onboarding administrators can now schedule reports to be sent automatically on a recurring basis. Reports can be configured to run daily, weekly, or monthly and are delivered by email with a secure link to access the report in Greenhouse Onboarding.

Scheduled reporting reduces the need to manually generate recurring reports and helps teams stay informed about onboarding activity. Reports are accessed through secure authentication in Greenhouse Onboarding rather than static email attachments, supporting stronger data security.

[Read more about scheduled reporting in Greenhouse Onboarding.](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/207150866/live_preview/01KJD8AXCKGHGQGRWMXMBTDXXV#h_01KJD8A5H7W7RRBCDT64C8NXT0)

### Integrations

  * **Candidate testing** : [MyCulture.ai](https://integrations.greenhouse.com/partners/myculture-ai) uses culture assessments modeled to your culture & values to help identify red flags or secure the perfect match.
  * **Candidate testing** : [Prevue](https://integrations.greenhouse.com/partners/prevue) allows recruiters and hiring teams to incorporate assessment insights directly into their hiring workflow.
  * **Job boards:**[SEEK Ad Sync](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/46531347613723) enables automated job posting to SEEK using a feed from Greenhouse, allowing organizations to centrally manage ad rules, branding, and spend visibility.
  * **Job boards:**[Apply with SEEK](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/115002864266) allows candidates to apply to Greenhouse-hosted job boards using their SEEK profile, automatically pre-populating supported application fields to improve completion rates.
  * **Optimization** : [LinkedInRSC+](https://integrations.greenhouse.com/partners/rsc-for-linkedin-hiring-assistant) unlocks the ability to connect LinkedIn projects to Greenhouse requisitions, unifying applicant evaluation and management.
  * **Optimization** : [TalentinoAI](https://integrations.greenhouse.com/partners/talentinoai) is an advanced recruitment platform that uses AI to streamline the hiring process from candidate assessment to final decision.
  * **Optimization** : [SwiftLynx AI](https://integrations.greenhouse.com/partners/swiftlynx-ai) offers a reliable resume analysis tool that transforms high-volume candidate data into clear and concise insights.

# CLARA integration

CLARA’s integration with Greenhouse Recruiting allows CLARA to process candidates, producing CLARA scores in near realtime.

#### In this article

  * Create a Harvest API key
  * Complete Integrate with CLARA
  * Use the CLARA integration with Greenhouse Recruiting



### Create a Harvest API key

To configure the CLARA integration, you’ll need to create a Harvest API key. 

Follow the steps in [this article](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/5888163769883) to create the key, and verify that the permissions below are selected when configuring the CLARA integration. Be sure to copy the API key as you will need to paste it in CLARA in the next step.

#### Credentials

In the _Create New Credential_ box, make the following selections:

  * API Type: Harvest
  * Partner: CLARA or Unlisted Vendor
  * Description: CLARA Harvest API Key



#### Permissions

Verify that the following permissions are selected for the CLARA integration: 

  * All permissions



### Complete Integrate with CLARA

To configure the integration, you’ll need to enter the API key from Greenhouse, into CLARA. 

Follow the steps below to complete the integration:

  1. In [app.getCLARA.io,](http://app.getclara.io) go to **Settings** > **Integrations**
  2. Click on **Add Integration** , and select **Greenhouse** , and click on **Connect to ATS**
  3. Follow the prompts to enter the API key that was provided by Greenhouse the first section.  

  4. You’re all done. CLARA will sync with Greenhouse. This might take a bit - once it is done, you will see Greenhouse has an active status, as shown below:  




### Use the CLARA integration with Greenhouse Recruiting

Whether you're a seasoned recruiter or a new user, our platform offers powerful tools to streamline the candidate screening process. Follow these steps to add efficiency to your evaluation process and help you collaborate seamlessly with your team.

**Step 1: Log In**

Begin by logging in to CLARA with your Recruiter or Partner Admin credentials.

**Step 2: Navigate to the Job Candidates page**

Once logged in, find candidates by scrolling to the specific job you're managing and clicking into it.

You'll notice that CLARA has already pre-sorted candidates into categories such as _Not Qualified_ or _Pre-Qualified_ based on their CLARA scores that reflect the specific requirements set for the role.

**Step 3: Access candidate application profiles**

Click into a candidate card to open the Candidate Application Profile.

Here, you'll find a wealth of information including the CLARA Score and details, Requirements Match, a Candidate summary, detailed education and experience information, and a comments section for internal communication.

**Scores added to Greenhouse on-behalf-of users**

The scores you find in the Candidate Application Profile are shared in Greenhouse under the candidate details section. 

****

**Step 4: Drag-and-drop candidates**

As you review candidates, you can manage them in the CLARA platform by dragging and dropping their candidate cards between columns/categories. This streamlines your work by allowing you to quickly organize and prioritize candidates for further consideration or next steps.

**Step 5: Share qualified candidates with the hiring manager**

Once you've identified a list of qualified candidates, click on the "Share with Hiring Manager" button above the columns on the upper-right side of your screen.

This action will open a popup window enabling you to include a personalized message for the Hiring Manager or to provide additional information that may assist in their decision-making process. When you click the "Share with Hiring Manager" in the popup window, your message will be delivered and the Hiring Manager will be notified.

**Step 6: Review the Hiring Manager's decision**

Once you've sharing the qualified candidates with the Hiring Manager, they will have an opportunity to make comments or to advance their selections. Once they have done so, you will receive a notification that will appear in the upper right-hand corner of your screen of your screen.

The next time you visit the Job page, you will see that the candidates they have chosen to advance will appear at the top of the page.

****

### Additional resources

For additional information or troubleshooting not covered here, reach out to [support@getclara.io](mailto:support@getclara.io) or click on the Partner Help Center on [app.clara.io](https://app.clara.io)

# Amiqus integration

Amiqus is a leading provider for businesses managing high-volume onboarding, enabling digital verification of new employees and candidates in minutes. The platform is an accredited Identity Service Provider (IDSP) for Right to Work and a registered DBS umbrella body, providing a faster and more compliant hiring process.

Amiqus’ integration with Greenhouse Recruiting allows users to seamlessly add Amiqus’ background checks as a stage in a job's interview plan.

#### In this article

  * Enable the integration
  * Locate a user ID
  * Create a Harvest API keyGenerate a job board API key
  * Generate a job board API key
  * Set up the integration in Amiqus
  * Use the Amiqus integration
  * Additional resources



### Enable the integration

To enable the integration, you’ll need:

  1. To have the integration enabled on Amiqus. Email [support@amiqus.co](mailto:support@amiqus.co) to request this feature.
  2. To be an admin user on Amiqus.
  3. To have the "Can manage ALL organisation's API Credentials" permission on Greenhouse. You can learn more about permission levels [here](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/201122629-Developer-permissions).
  4. Amiqus will need a Greenhouse Recruiting user ID to associate with updates and changes created by the integration.



### Locate a user ID

Click the **Configure** icon  on your navigation bar and then click **Users** on the left. 

Click **Export to Excel**.

A spreadsheet will be downloaded to your computer. Open the Excel file and locate the user ID in the **User ID** column.

### Create a Harvest API key

Follow the steps in [this article](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/5888163769883) to create the key, and verify that the permissions below are selected when configuring the Amiqus integration.

#### Credentials

In the Create New Credential box, make the following selections:

  * API Type: Harvest
  * Partner: Amiqus
  * Description: Amiqus Harvest API Key



#### Permissions

Verify that the following permissions are selected for the Amiqus integration:

  * All Permissions



### Generate a job board API key

Follow the steps in [this article](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/5888210160155) and use the information below when creating your API key:

  * API Type: Job Board
  * Partner: Amiqus
  * Description: Amiqus job board API key



[Click here](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/13446638483355-Create-a-job-board-API-key-for-an-integration) for more detailed information on setting up a job board API key for a partner.

### Set up the integration in Amiqus

Once you have all the above, navigate to the **Workflow >Team apps** area of your Amiqus account (<https://id.amiqus.co/team/workflow/apps>)

Click **Connect Greenhouse account**. 

Copy your **External Trigger Token** and store it somewhere – you’ll need it later.

Enter the rest of the information in the pop-up window and click**Connect**.

Follow the steps in [this article](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/5888163696923) to work with Greenhouse support representative and add the assessment stage in your interview plans. You’ll need to securely send them the API key you copied from Amiqus.

#### Create templates in Amiqus

Before you can send requests from Greenhouse, you'll need to have at least one _Live_ request template set up in Amiqus, from which to select from. You can find information you need to create request templates in the following articles:

  * [How to use request templates](https://business-support.amiqus.co/hc/en-gb/articles/360004157937-How-to-use-request-templates)
  * [How you can customise your workflow](https://business-support.amiqus.co/hc/en-gb/articles/360018559258-How-you-can-customise-your-workflow)
  * [Workflow and Admin Overview Training Video](https://business-support.amiqus.co/hc/en-gb/articles/13104826794781-Workflow-and-Admin-Overview-Training-Video)



Please note that any messaging within your templates will be the same for all candidates; there are no dynamic fields within the messaging (eg for the candidates name).

### Use the Amiqus integration

Once the Amiqus integration is enabled for your organization, you will be able to add the Amiqus Background check as an [interview stage](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/115002194903-Interview-plan-overview#h_01F76JFVX7SXZ8R5ME855TY8XN).

You can send this to a candidate by selecting the Send Test button next to the interview stage. The assessment instructions will be sent by Amiqus.

  1. In the Interview Plan of [a new job](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/115002194903-Interview-plan-overview#h_01F76JFHVBENFBK0BMK2D45SFW) or [when editing a current job](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/115002194903-Interview-plan-overview#h_01F76JG8F7SNMJ0655B0Y9N86Q), select Add Stage.
  2. Choose Amiqus and click Add. Then move this stage to the place in the plan you would like the Amiqus Request to be sent. You can change the order of stages in an interview plan by clicking and dragging on the stage name.   

  3. Optionally, once the stage is in the interview plan, you can modify it by selecting the pencil icon next to the stage name. Here you can select the specific background check template from your Amiqus account.
  4. Whenever a candidate reaches this stage, the Send test to candidate option will be ready to select.  

  5. After it has been sent, an assessment’s status will display in Greenhouse Recruiting.  




#### Set up notifications

If you would like to receive notifications on the check status, we recommend [assigning yourself and/or a colleague to the person and/or request](https://business-support.amiqus.co/hc/en-gb/articles/360002394338-Using-assigning) in Amiqus, that way you'll be notified when the candidate completes the request.

You can do this on an individual basis within each person or request, or you can set this up within a request template.

You can [customise your notification settings](https://business-support.amiqus.co/hc/en-gb/articles/360002402357-Customising-notification-settings) at any time, choosing from in app and/or email notifications.

#### Check results

Once the candidate has completed their request, they'll be marked as Ready for Review in Amiqus. Once you are happy with the check results, you will need to [mark the request as Reviewed](https://business-support.amiqus.co/hc/en-gb/articles/360002386678-How-to-mark-a-request-as-reviewed).

**Once the check has been marked as Reviewed, the assessment's status will be sent to Greenhouse and iinclude a link to view the background check in Amiqus.**

### Additional resources

For additional information not covered here, reach out to [support@amiqus.co](mailto:support@amiqus.co).

The [Amiqus Support Centre](https://business-support.amiqus.co/hc/en-gb) contains information about all [check types](https://business-support.amiqus.co/hc/en-gb/sections/16724806059293-Check-Types) including how to review the results. A few of the common check types have been listed below:

  * [Identity Report: Results](https://business-support.amiqus.co/hc/en-gb/articles/18470813065629-Identity-Report-Results)
  * [Photo ID Verification: Reviewing the Results ](https://business-support.amiqus.co/hc/en-gb/articles/16931800604573-Photo-ID-Verification-Reviewing-the-Results-with-facial-similarity-and-motion-liveness)
  * [Photo ID Verification: Reviewing the Results - Right to Work](https://business-support.amiqus.co/hc/en-gb/articles/16725591807773-Reviewing-the-Results-Right-to-Work)
  * [Automated Employment Referencing: Reviewing The Results](https://business-support.amiqus.co/hc/en-gb/articles/17767206482077-Automated-Employment-Referencing-Reviewing-The-Results)



For full details on setting up and using this integration to initiate background checks, see [Amiqus’ support article here](https://business-support.amiqus.co/hc/en-gb/articles/28386132319005-Using-Greenhouse-with-Amiqus).

# Diversity, Equity, and Inclusion (DE&I) overview

**Permissions:** **–**

**Product tier:** Available for Pro subscription tier

Diversity, Equity, and Inclusion (DE&I) is an extension of our [structured hiring](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360007245452) philosophy. While there are many ways our core product helps companies make structured hiring decisions, we decided to build DE&I because we wanted to do more to help companies scale and operationalize inclusive behavior in their hiring processes.

We've partnered with some amazing people to build DE&I. One of these partners is Paradigm, a consulting company that works with clients to design DE&I strategies. They have a lot of practical knowledge from doing this on a 1:1 basis with clients, and we've taken that experience and infused it into our new tool. We've also assembled an academic advisory board with professors at universities from around the country who focus on these questions to help guide our solutions. DE&I is rooted in the guidance from these sources and is designed based on this research.

#### Learn more

# inhire integration

Inhire is an automated sourcing platform for recruiting tech talents, reaching out directly to thousands of tech, vetted candidates. Greenhouse Recruiting’s integration with inhire allows getting candidates sourced with inhire to be added to your Greenhouse instance.

#### In this article

  * Create a Harvest API key for the inhire integration
    * Credentials
    * Permissions
  * Add custom source to track candidates from inhire
  * Finish setup on the inhire platform
  * Use the inhire integration with Greenhouse Recruiting 
  * Additional resources 



### Create a Harvest API key for the inhire integration

To configure the Greenhouse Recruiting/inhire integration, you’ll need to create a Harvest API key. Follow the steps in [this article](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/5888163769883) to create the key, and verify that the permissions below are selected when configuring the inhire integration.

#### Credentials

In the _Create New Credential_ box, make the following selections:

  * **API Type:** Harvest
  * **Partner:** inhire (optional)
  * **Description:** inhire Harvest API Key



Store the API key in a secure location, you will need to paste it into inhire in the next step.

#### Permissions

Verify that the following permissions are selected for the inhire integration:

**Applications**

  * GET: Retrieve Application
  * GET: List Applications



**Candidates**

  * GET: Retrieve Candidate
  * GET: List Candidates
  * POST: Add Candidate
  * POST: Add Attachment
  * POST: Add Application
  * POST: Add Prospect



**Job Posts**

  * GET: List Job Posts
  * GET: Retrieve Job Post for Job
  * GET: List Job Posts for Job



**Job Stages**

  * GET: Retrieve Job Stage
  * GET: List Job Stages
  * GET: List Job Stages for Job



**Jobs**

  * GET: Retrieve Job
  * GET: List Jobs



**Scheduled Interviews**

  * GET: List Interviews for Application
  * GET: Retrieve Interview
  * GET: List Interviews



**Sources**

  * GET: List Sources



**Users**

  * GET: Retrieve User
  * GET: List Users
  * GET: List User Future Job Permissions
  * GET: List User Job Permissions



### Add custom source to track candidates from inhire

Click the **Configure** **icon** in upper right corner. From the left menu, click **Custom Options** then click **Sources**.

Click **Create New Source.** In the popup that appears, enter the following information:

  * **Sourcing Strategy** : 3rd Party Boards
  * **Name of Source** : inhire.io



**Note** : In the _Name of Source_ text box, it's important that you type _inhire.io_ exactly as it appears here. inhire identifies the source by this tag, so any incorrect text may prevent the integration from working properly.

### Finish setup on the inhire platform

Provide your Harvest API key to your inhire onboarding team so they can set up the integration. If you'd like to complete setup yourself, follow the steps below.

Log in as an **Admin** into your inhire account. Right-click on your email address in the top right corner and choose **Settings**.

Select**Integrations** and click **Greenhouse.**

Enter the previously generated Greenhouse Harvest API key and an email address associated with your Greenhouse Recruiting account. These items will be used to create candidates.

**Note:** inhire recommendeds using an email address of a user with Site Admin permissions to ensure they have access to all jobs. This user will be used by inhire while adding candidates to fill the **On-behalf-of** section in API requests.

Click **Next** to finish the setup.

**Note:** If you want to edit the GDPR consent template that candidates accept when applying to your jobs, modify the text in the **Consent template** field and click **Save.**

### Use the inhire integration with Greenhouse Recruiting

In the previous section you defined the API key for the integration. Now, it is time to bind your process on the inhire Platform with the corresponding recruitment process in Greenhouse Recruiting.

For example, if you want to map a job called "Senior ML Engineer" in inhire to a job called "Machine Learning Engineer" in Greenhouse Recruiting, you'll want to follow the steps below:

Go to the **Processes** page on inhire and click on the three vertical dots button and choose the **Edit** option from the menu.

Scroll down end toggle the **Integrate with ATS** option.

After clicking on the list, choose the corresponding recruitment process retrieved from your Greenhouse instance.

In order to test integration, click **Test Integration** and inhire will add a test candidate to your Greenhouse job.

Select **Process Customization** and click **Process Preview.**

Click **Save** to save your integration into the database.

You’ll need to repeat this process with all processes on inhire that you want to bind with corresponding jobs in Greenhouse.

### Additional resources

For additional information not covered here, reach out to [hello@inhire.io](mailto:hello@inhire.io) or review the inhire setup guide in the inhire Help Center: [How to integrate with inhire.](https://inhire.io/helpcenter/how-to-integrate-with-inhire/)

# Template jobs and custom HRIS integrations

Access the latest version of Harvest API documentation at [**harvestdocs.greenhouse.io**](http://harvestdocs.greenhouse.io).  
  
Harvest API v1 and v2 will be deprecated and unavailable after August 31, 2026. Please make sure that your existing custom integrations use the latest version of Harvest (v3) by this date and any new integrations are developed with the latest version of Harvest API.

If you're building an API-driven job import integration with your HRIS, this guide is intended to help your team decide whether to create all new jobs using one existing Greenhouse Recruiting job as a template or using multiple template jobs.

#### In this article

  * Why are existing jobs needed to create new jobs through the Harvest API?
  * Do all new jobs have to use the same template job?
  * One template vs. multiple template jobs
  * Job approvals



### Why are existing jobs needed to create new jobs through the Harvest API?

Creating a job through the Harvest API is like using the **Copy an Existing Job** option when creating a new job as a user in Greenhouse Recruiting.

In order to create the job through the API, you must identify the job ID of an existing Greenhouse Recruiting job that you want to use as the template for the new job. You cannot use a blank or sample template. However, the template job's status can be open, closed, or draft.

Greenhouse Recruiting's template jobs are simply regular jobs that have been marked as template jobs. Read more here: [Best practices: Template jobs](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360006876232).

The selected template job can be used to populate parts of the job that cannot be configured via the API (denoted by *) and / or components that may be out of scope for your integration developer, such as:

  * Scorecard*
  * Interview plan*
  * Job post questions*
  * Hiring team
  * Notifications*



The API will primarily be used to fill in the job info (including standard and custom job fields). Depending on the scope of your integration, the job post title, job post description, and the hiring team may also be added through the API. However, be sure to check with your integration developer if you're not sure which job data will be added through the integration.

### Do all new jobs have to use the same template job?

No, your integration can create all new jobs using one template, or using different templates. We recommend working with your primary Greenhouse Recruiting users and integration developer to decide which option will best fit your needs. Our recommendations and considerations are outlined below.

### One template vs. multiple template jobs

**Considerations** | **One template job** | **Multiple template jobs**  
---|---|---  
Summary< | Recommended if your interview plans and scorecards are relatively consistent across offices and departments, or if your team is comfortable with updating jobs in Greenhouse Recruiting after they've been added through the integration. | Recommended if your job Interview Plans and Scorecards are highly varied across offices, departments, or other job criteria.  
Prerequisites< |  Create one primary template job that includes only the information that should be found on all jobs, as that information will be included on all new jobs created via the API. Any additional information that's required can be added after the new job is imported from HRIS. Alternatively, you can create one primary template which combines all information from a few different templates. After a job has been created in Greenhouse Recruiting, you can go in and remove any stages / attributes that don't apply. | Create all necessary template jobs ahead of building the integration and share the relevant job IDs with your integration developer.  
Integration Development< | No integration logic is required- all new jobs will be created using the same template job. |  **Option 1** : Maintain custom integration mapping or integration logic that dictates how jobs should be assigned to a particular template (for instance, all jobs in Cost Center A and Location A should be created using Greenhouse Recruiting template job A).    
**Option 2** : Create a single select custom object / field in HRIS which will pull in a list of all Greenhouse Recruiting template jobs using the Harvest API (template jobs should be categorized under a "Template" office or department so you can use the office/department parameter to filter the [`GET: List Jobs`](https://harvestdocs.greenhouse.io/reference/get_v3-jobs) response). When creating a job in your HRIS, a user should select the appropriate Greenhouse Recruiting job template from this dropdown.  
Updating New Jobs in Greenhouse Recruiting | Once the job is in Greenhouse Recruiting, you may need to update each section of the job individually (like scorecard, interview plan, etc.). However, when editing a job, you can easily copy interview stages, scorecard attributes, and job post questions from other jobs. | Jobs added via the API will likely require less updates once they are in Greenhouse Recruiting, but the interview plans, scorecards, etc. can still be updated if needed.  
  
### Job approvals

If there are no new job approvals configured for your organization, new jobs will automatically be added as _Open_. However, if you have [default approval flows ](https://app.greenhouse.io/configure/approval_flows)configured in Greenhouse Recruiting to open new jobs, then new jobs added through the API will be in _Draft_ mode until they are approved. Each job will inherit the approval flows set for all new jobs, or for the department and / or offices the job is assigned to if you have department- and office-specific flows configured. 

If no department and / or offices are assigned in the API request to create the job, the new job will inherit the department and / or offices set on the template job and their corresponding default approval flows.

# Moving candidates and prospects across jobs with different job admin permission levels

When a user has different levels of access across jobs, they can move a candidate to another job where they have permissions that are the same level or lower but cannot move a candidate to another job where their permissions are higher.

For example, if a user's Job Admin level on your Marketing Assistant job includes the permission stripe 'Can email candidates,' but the user's Job Admin level on the VP of Marketing job does not include this permission. The user's Job Admin levels on the two jobs are otherwise identical.

In this case:

  * Moving or adding a candidate from Marketing Assistant to VP of Marketing is allowed, because the user is moving a candidate from a job where they have higher (additional) permissions to one where they have lower (fewer) permissions.
  * Moving or adding a candidate from VP of Marketing to Marketing Assistant is not allowed, because the user would be moving the candidate from a job where they have lower permissions to a job where they have higher permissions. This could allow the user to email the candidate, which they were not able to do on the candidate's original job. This essentially allows the user to upgrade their own permissions past where they have been set, however inadvertently.



Similar logic also impacts the ability of Job Admin users to merge candidates and prospects. To learn more about this, click [here](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360039867211).

To learn more about job admin permission levels, [click here](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360039518131).

# Job post request email

**Permissions:** Job Admin and above who can email candidates

**Product tier:** Available for new subscription tiers (Core, Plus, and Pro)

If a candidate or referral is [manually](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/115002195063) added to your Greenhouse Recruiting account, you may want them to complete the job post application so you have all the information you need, including any answers to [custom job post questions](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360025222851). 

The job post request email is designed for this purpose. Ask candidates to complete the job post by sending them a job post request email. The email is available for [live, offline](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/16183212618139), and [internal](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360020285291) job posts.

**Tip** : This article is about manually initiating a job post request email. You can also set up a rule to [automatically send the job post request email](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360052440032) when candidates are added.

#### In this article

  * Configure job post request email templates
  * Send job post questions to individual candidates or referrals
  * Send job post questions in bulk to candidates or referrals



### Configure job post request email templates

Greenhouse Recruiting provides you with the editable email template _Default Job Post Request_ to use when sending candidates a job post.

To view or edit the default job post request email template, click the **Configure** icon  on your navigation bar, then select **Email Templates** on the left.

Scroll to _Default Job Post Request_ and click the **Edit** icon .

Customize the template name, sender address, subject line, and content using the provided email tokens.

**Note** : The `{{SUBMISSION_LINK}}` token provides a URL to the specific job post so your organization can collect the candidate's structured data.

When finished, click **Save**.

If you want to have multiple versions of the job post request email, you can [create a new email template.](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/115004020946) When creating the new template, be sure to select **Job Post Request** from the _Type_ dropdown.

### Send job post questions to individual candidates or referrals

**Note** : A job post request email cannot be sent to candidates that have already submitted a job post.

To send job post questions to an individual candidate who was manually added to your account, navigate to their profile.

Job post questions can be send in the **Application Questions** section of the _Applications Details_ tab on the right side of the page.

Click **Send** to open the email window.

**Note** : To send job post questions to the candidate without basic fields included, check the box for **Hide basic fields**.

Configure any settings on the email, including the associated job post and email template.

**Notes:**

  * In the send job post window, you'll see the `{{SUBMISSION_LINK}}` token represented by a placeholder link of `https://grnh.se/r/tokenX`. The placeholder link will be replaced with a valid submission link when the email is sent to the candidate.
  * Attachments will not be included in Job Request emails. To include another document in this email, it must be included as a hyperlink within the email body.



When finished, click **Send Email**.

The candidate will receive an email with a submission link to submit responses to the job post questions.

Responses submitted by the candidate / referral will be added to their profile.

**Note** : Responses to job post questions will work with Greenhouse's [auto-tag](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360000060551) feature but will not work with [auto-reject](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360000653472).

The Greenhouse Recruiting user who sent the job post form will be notified once the manually added candidate or referral submits their response.

### Send job post questions in bulk to candidates or referrals

To send job post questions to multiple candidates simultaneously, click **Jobs** on your navigation bar and select a job from the list.

Click the **Candidates** tab on the job.

From the _Candidates_ page, expand the **Jobs** filter on the left and click the checkbox for **To be sent.** Click **Bulk Actions** at the top-right.

Select each candidate you would like to send job post questions to by selecting the checkbox beside their name. Once all relevant candidates have been selected for the bulk action, click **Edit Selected (#)**.

From the subsequent dialog box, click **Send Job Posts**.

Select a job post and template from the respective dropdowns.

**Note** : To send job post questions to the candidate without basic fields, check the box for **Hide basic fields**.

When finished, click **Send Email**.

All candidates selected will receive an email with a submission link that they can follow to submit responses to job post questions. Responses will be merged with the appropriate candidate's existing profile.

**Note** : Responses to job post questions will work with Greenhouse Recruiting's [auto-tag](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360000060551) feature but will not work with [auto-reject](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360000653472).

The Greenhouse Recruiting user who sent the job post forms will be notified once the manually added candidates submit their response.

# VONQ integration

VONQ offers recruitment marketing technology to turn passive and active candidates into qualified applicants. To steer recruitment teams' success, VONQ offers performance data analytics and job market insights.

Greenhouse Recruiting's integration with VONQ allows users to push active jobs to VONQ's platform to easily create advertisement campaigns and distribute their jobs to over 2000 channels.

  * Create a job board API key
  * Find your job board token
  * Use the VONQ integration with Greenhouse Recruiting



### Create a job board API key

To enable the integration, you'll need to create a job board API key for VONQ.

Follow the steps in [this article](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/5888210160155) and use the information below when creating your API key:

  * **API type:** Job Board
  * **Description:** VONQ Job Board API key



Copy the job board API key and forward it to your VONQ representative using a secure method.

### Find your job board token

To make your job posts available to VONQ, you'll need to send your job board token to VONQ.

You can find your job board URL by navigating to **Configure** > **Job Boards & Posts **> **Ellipsis** icon next to your job board > **Edit Board Settings** , then scroll to the URL field.

# Bob recruitment integration

HiBob is a cloud-based global HR platform that enables your organization to manage employee data and automate HR tasks. Bob's recruitment integration with Greenhouse Recruiting allows users to export candidate data to Bob when a candidate is marked as hired in Greenhouse Recruiting.

How the integration works:

  * [**Workforce planning**](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/17643694837659-Bob-workforce-planning-integration)******integration:** Create new Jobs and/or Job openings in Greenhouse from Workforce planning in Bob. This integration is only available to customers who have Bob’s Workforce planning module.
  * **Recruitment********integration:** Import details of new hires from Greenhouse to Bob. (Candidates will be pushed to Bob when they are marked as Hired in Greenhouse).



#### In this article

  * Set up the integration
    * Enable on Bob
    * Create a webhook
  * Use the Bob integration
    * Add a new hire to Bob
  * Additional resources



### Set up the integration

The Bob recruitment integration with Greenhouse Recruiting allows users to export candidate data to Bob when a candidate is marked as hired in Greenhouse Recruiting. The following candidate fields are mapped between Bob and Greenhouse Recruiting:

**Bob field** | **Greenhouse Recruiting field**  
---|---  
Email | Primary email  
First name | First name  
Surname | Last name  
Title | Job name  
Start date | Offer start date  
Site | Job office  
Department | Primary job department  
Personal phone | Primary home phone  
Personal mobile | Primary mobile phone  
Contract | Offer employment type  
Documents | Candidate attachments  
  
After connecting the integration, you can [customize data mapping](https://help.hibob.com/hc/en-us/articles/13609951421969) in the integration settings on the Bob platform.

**Note** : Candidate offer documents are automatically added to a confidential documents folder on Bob.

To include additional custom fields, your customized Bob fields should have the same custom field name used in Greenhouse Recruiting. Applicant, candidate, job, and offer custom fields are supported. However, long and short-text field types aren't supported.

Calculated Bob fields aren't supported either, even if the custom field in Greenhouse Recruiting has the same name. For instance, you can't map the weekly hours field in the employment table in Bob because it's a calculated field.

#### Enable on Bob

Log in to Bob, and select **Settings** >**Integrations** on the left.

Click**Recruitment**.

On the Greenhouse tile, click **Connect**.

Click **Create key and webhook**.

Click **Copy link** next to the endpoint URL and secret key fields. Save the information to enter in Greenhouse Recruiting in the next step.

#### Create a webhook

Next, create a webhook in Greenhouse Recruiting. Follow the steps in [this article](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/5888163727003) to create your webhook. Use the values listed below to configure the webhook:

  * **Name** : Bob integration
  * **When** : Candidate has been hired
  * **Endpoint URL** : The endpoint URL provided by Bob in the previous step
  * **Secret Key** : The secret key provided by Bob in the previous step



Once complete, the integration is configured and ready to use.

### Use the Bob integration with Greenhouse Recruiting

#### Add a new hire to Bob

When a candidate is marked as hired in Greenhouse Recruiting, you'll be sent an email from Bob. Click **Complete the hiring process** in the email.

You'll also get an in-app notification in Bob. Click the **Bell** icon at the top-right of the home page to complete the hiring process.

The newly hired candidate's details will be pushed to Bob when you complete the action in the email or in-app. You'll be directed to Bob with _Add a new hire_ open. Select a new hire template and click **Start**. Complete the add new hire process in Bob.

**Note** : New hire candidate attachments are synced from Greenhouse Recruiting and stored in the employee's confidential documents folder in Bob.

### Additional resources

Check out these resources from Bob:

  * [Map data for ATS integrations](https://help.hibob.com/hc/en-us/articles/13609951421969)
  * [Set up ATS Notifications](https://help.hibob.com/hc/en-us/articles/4409792726545/hc/en-us/articles/4409792374673)
  * [Add a new hire](https://help.hibob.com/hc/en-us/articles/4409776091281#h_01GR0Y69XQMCAVEQC5MNME6NWN)



For additional information or troubleshooting not covered here, reach out to your organization's Bob account team.

# HireRoad integration

HireRoad is a recruitment and workforce analytics pureplay and is built to integrate all sources of disparate recruitment, HR and talent data, and deliver end-to-end reporting and workforce analytics. Our business tackles a universal problem - disconnected recruitment, HR, workforce & talent data, stuck in disparate systems across HR and the business, underutilized for decision-making purposes. This results in cobbled-together spreadsheets which don’t stand steady when it comes to data integrity, multiple data sources, powerful visualization and segmentation.

We are the reporting, analytics, and decision-support umbrella overarching all company’s transactional recruitment, HR and talent systems, and data sources. Our out-of-the-box solution quickly and seamlessly connects all relevant data sources to deliver must-have talent acquisition & workforce analytics. Our Talent Acquisition Edition is built specifically for organizations looking to gain deep insight into both recruitment efficiency and effectiveness. Our clients simply feed us their raw format data, and we do the rest. Companies using Greenhouse can now integrate seamlessly with HireRoad through the Harvest API. It’s as simple as that.

#### In this article

  * Create a Harvest API key for the HireRoad integration
    * Credentials
    * Permissions
  * Frequently asked questions
  * Additional resources



### Create a Harvest API key for the HireRoad integration

To configure the Greenhouse Recruiting / HireRoad integration, you'll need to create a Harvest API key.

Follow the steps in [this article](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/5888163769883) to create the key, and verify that the credentials and permissions below are selected when configuring the HireRoad integration.

#### Credentials

In the _Create New Credential_ box, make the following selections:

  * **API type:** Harvest
  * **Partner:** HireRoad
  * **Description:** HireRoad Harvest API key



#### Permissions

Verify that the following permissions are selected for the HireRoad integration:

  * **Select all permissions**



### Frequently asked questions

**What if I need changes to the dashboards, scorecards, or analytics?**

We know your reporting and analytics needs are constantly evolving so we’ve simply built your ongoing changes into our subscription model. In that way, our turnkey managed service will ensure your analytics continually address your business objectives. Consider us your extended recruitment and workforce analytics team.

**Who are the main users of HireRoad?**

# Choreographed introduction emails

**Permissions:** Owners and Coordinators

**Product tier:** Available for Greenhouse Welcome and Greenhouse Onboarding subscription tiers

Choreographed introductions help your onboarding team notify employees about the latest group of new hires who've joined your organization, giving employees a chance to learn more about their new teammates.

Greenhouse Onboarding provides four default choreographed introduction email templates to get you started:

  * **Department-wide hello:** Introduce an entire department to their new teammates
  * **Manager notification:** Send managers a reminder when their new hires are about to start
  * **Onboarding class:** Introduce new hires in the same cohort to each other
  * **Buddy program instructions:** Introduce new hires to employees assigned to be their onboarding buddies



You can also create custom choreographed introduction templates to fit your team's needs or to notify other specific groups of employees in your organization.

Selected recipients will receive choreographed introduction emails automatically on a date relative to the new hire cohort's start date, based on the schedule you configure for each template.

#### Learn more

  * [Add a new choreographed introduction template](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360049052771)
  * [Edit your choreographed introduction templates](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360049052851)
  * [Deactivate choreographed introduction emails](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360048564072)



#### New hire cohorts

Choreographed introductions use new hire cohorts to determine which new hires should be featured in each email. New hires are grouped based on their start date and the cohort criteria defined in your template, including a new hire's department, location, employment status, or other criteria.

For each template, you'll want to define new hire cohort criteria. You'll also schedule when choreographed introduction emails should be sent, relative to the start date for each new hire cohort.

**Example:** You've created a department-wide choreographed introduction email for the **Engineering** department. Your template is set to send on the following schedule:

  * Mondays
  * 1 week before new hires start



It's Monday. Next week, these new hires will join your organization:

  * Isaac Ellig, Software Engineer I, starting next Monday 
  * Seoyun Kim, Sales Manager, starting next Tuesday
  * Rosa Lopez, Software Engineer IV, starting next Tuesday



Based on your template's criteria, the following new hires will be grouped into a new hire cohort and included in today's choreographed introduction email for the Engineering department:

  * Isaac Ellig
  * Rosa Lopez

# Approvals overview

Approvals allow you to configure one or more users to sign off on a job action before it’s allowed to take place.

#### In this article

  * Types of approvals
    * Job approvals
    * Offer approvals
  * Configure approvals
    * Choose an office, department, or all jobs
    * Choose job approvals or offer approvals
    * Assign, edit, or remove approvers
  * Troubleshoot approvals



### Types of approvals

There are two types of approvals: Job approvals and offer approvals. They work in mostly the same way with some minor differences.

#### Job approvals

Use [job approvals](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/sections/360000937312) to control when users can open jobs and generate offers. Depending on which actions you want to control, you can set up job approvals with [one step or two steps](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360025756071).

#### Offer approvals

Use [offer approvals](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/sections/360000932811) to control when a user can extend a generated offer to a candidate. Unlike job approvals, offer approvals can only include one step.

### Configure approvals

Job approvals and offer approvals are configured in the same way. Learn more about [creating a new approval process](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360062257351).

### Troubleshoot approvals

Use the [Approvals FAQ](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/18222984976795) to troubleshoot issues with approvals.
