# Make confident, informed hiring decisions

Your hiring success ultimately depends on your team’s ability to choose the best candidates for your open roles. Making the right decisions requires the right information. Interviews should be intentionally designed to gather the most crucial data and feedback at the appropriate times. This not only makes it easier to use these insights when making hiring decisions, it gives your hiring team a clear set of standards for feedback and discussion. That’s how you build a hiring process at scale. 

The effectiveness spectrum of companies’ hiring processes is what we call the [Greenhouse Hiring Maturity™](https://www.greenhouse.com/hiring-maturity) curve, which we break down into four stages: chaotic, inconsistent, systematic and, finally, strategic. 

As companies [climb the Greenhouse Hiring Maturity curve](https://www.greenhouse.io/blog/greenhouse-hiring-maturity-business-success), we see them start to focus on key behaviors and strategies that help them consistently make quality hires with confidence. 

### Select your stage of hiring:

  * Chaotic/inconsistent
  * Systematic
  * Strategic



### **Chaotic and inconsistent stages**

At these stages, it’s important to lay the groundwork to make more effective hiring decisions. Strengthen your hiring team’s relationships by aligning on role requirements and feedback expectations before meeting with any candidates. Empower team members with clear processes and training to increase consistency in your interviews. 

**Key actions for enabling change management  
**

Train your interviewers

  * Establish and review how to properly prepare for and conduct interviews, when and where to provide feedback and other components of your hiring process
  * Use the Greenhouse interviewer [training template](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/115003739232-Greenhouse-roll-out-toolkit-Start-here) and our [instructional video](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/115002226826-Interviewer-guide-Using-interview-kits) to get started



Take action in Greenhouse with the following configuration:  
[Require scorecards to be submitted for every interview ](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/115005259466-My-interview-doesn-t-require-a-scorecard-to-be-submitted-How-do-I-change-that-in-an-interview-kit-)  
[Learn how to create scorecard attributes for every job in this Designing Scorecards Webinar](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360039613472-Designing-scorecards)

Employ strategies to mitigate unconscious bias during interviews

  * Unconscious bias training transcends the recruiting process and can apply to all areas of your business, but is particularly important when it comes to making data-driven hiring decisions
  * For ideas on how to reduce bias and train interviewers accordingly, check out our [blog post](https://www.greenhouse.io/blog/how-unconscious-bias-affects-employee-experience-and-how-to-reduce-it)



Optimize hiring team alignment and collaboration by implementing kickoff meetings for every new role

  * Establish and maintain best practices for your structured hiring process
  * Collect all the information you need to align on expectations about process goals and methods
  * Familiarize yourself with the [job kickoff form](https://learn.greenhouse.io/job-kickoff-form-feature-overview) and use it to streamline inputs
  * See our [blog post](https://www.greenhouse.io/guidance/how-to-implement-structured-hiring-step-1-role-kick-off-meeting) and [efficient decisions course](https://learn.greenhouse.io/make-efficient-hiring-decisions) for guidance on implementing kickoff meetings



### Additional configurations to make in Greenhouse with your team

  * Create approval chains in Greenhouse to facilitate job and offer approvals – [Job approval articles](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/sections/360000937312-Job-approvals), [Offer approval article](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360035625832-Offer-Approval-Overview) and Learn Greenhouse course: [Offer approvals](https://learn.greenhouse.io/working-with-offer-approvals)
  * Learn how to schedule interviews in Greenhouse with Google Calendar or Outlook 365 – [Scheduling course menu](https://learn.greenhouse.io/page/schedule-with-greenhouse), [Google Calendar support articles](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/sections/360000691071), and [Outlook 365 support articles](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/sections/360000692812)



### **Systematic stage**

You’ve already built out a structured hiring process where you consistently gather feedback from interviews, but there’s still room to improve. Use these tips to move up the Hiring Maturity curve with a more consistent, strategic hiring process.

**Key actions for enabling change management:**

Prepare interview questions and facilitation guidance for your interviewers

  * Develop a consistent set of questions for each interview and interviewer
  * Make sure these questions directly evaluate each attribute the interviewer is meant to be rating in their feedback
  * Check out our [blog post](https://www.greenhouse.io/guidance/a-quick-easy-guide-to-structured-interview-questions) for inspiration and guidance on crafting your own strategic interview questions



Take action in Greenhouse with the following configuration:  
[Mitigate bias and gain clarity on interview feedback by requiring notes from interviewers DE&I ](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360004977491) 5 mins  
[Evaluate candidate attributes more thoroughly by adding custom questions to interview kits ](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/115002276366-Create-custom-questions-for-interview-kits) 15 mins

**Create a scalable action plan for responding to feedback**

  * Build out a standardized review process to follow after each interview that focuses on the most essential skills and qualifications evaluated at each point in the process
  * Check out our [blog post](https://www.greenhouse.io/guidance/how-to-implement-structured-hiring-steps-5-and-6-interviewing-candidates-and-reviewing-feedback) and [efficient hiring decision course ](https://learn.greenhouse.io/make-efficient-hiring-decisions)for guidance on designing a more effective decision-making process



### Additional configurations to make in Greenhouse with your team

  * Configure and automate scorecard reminder notifications [support article](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360047691292-Scorecard-reminder-notification)
  * Create and designate template jobs to streamline job creation [support article](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360006876232-Best-practices-Template-job)
  * Establish nuanced levels of access by creating custom permission levels [Learn Greenhouse course](https://learn.greenhouse.io/job-admin-levels)



### **Strategic stage**

You’re using a structured process to select great candidates for almost every role, giving your company the confidence and tools it needs to consistently hire for whatever is next. But even the best companies can continue to grow their hiring expertise. In that spirit, here are a few tips to help you truly become a leader in the space:

**Key actions for enabling change management:**

Create a framework for how your team will make final hiring decisions

  * Align your team on what to consider when making final decisions and who will be responsible for each part of the process
  * Check out our [blog post](https://www.greenhouse.io/guidance/how-to-make-great-hiring-decisions) and [efficient hiring decision course](https://learn.greenhouse.io/make-efficient-hiring-decisions) for additional guidance on improving late-stage decision-making



Follow this up with further action:  
[Streamline final candidate evaluations by defining the most important attributes for candidate roundups](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360003464191-Focus-Attributes-for-Candidate-Roundup)  
Conduct [final roundup](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360007247872-Structured-hiring-Candidate-round-up) meetings with the [hiring team](https://learn.greenhouse.io/running-a-candidate-roundup) prior to making hiring decisions

Conduct a post-hire analysis when you close a role

  * Improve and iterate on your hiring plan based on feedback
  * Update the scorecard, interview questions and anything else based on discussions with your hiring team
  * Look at data from your recent hiring process to help identify opportunities for improvement
  * Watch [this webinar](https://learn.greenhouse.io/maximizing-advanced-reporting-tools) on maximizing advanced reporting tools
  * Register for one of our [live training events](https://learn.greenhouse.io/calendar#type_live-training,topic_reporting) on reporting



### Additional configurations to make in Greenhouse with your team 

  * Guide interviewers to target specific feedback by assigning focus attributes in interview kits [support article](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360018399451-Scorecard-focus-attributes)
  * Assess candidate skills with take home test assignments[ support article](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/200887825-Set-up-take-home-test)
  * Mitigate bias by anonymizing take-home test grading DE&I [support article](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360017706471-Anonymize-Take-Home-Tests)



### 

**Learn more with other Hiring Maturity advancement guides**

[Identify and attract the best talent for your organization](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/4404324034587)

[Own every moment of your hiring process](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/4404475165467)

[Use data to drive operational excellence and improve over time](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/4404475145883)

# Dover integration

Greenhouse Recruiting's integration with Dover allows users to track candidates through all stages of the hiring process and prevent duplicate outreach by automatically adding Dover candidates to Greenhouse and excluding candidates already in Greenhouse from Dover outreach.

#### In this article

  * Create a Harvest API key for the Greenhouse Recruiting / Dover integration
  * Create a Dover source in Greenhouse Recruiting
  * Enable the Dover integration
  * Use the Dover integration on Greenhouse Recruiting
  * Additional resources



### Create a Harvest API key for the Greenhouse Recruiting / Dover integration

To configure the Greenhouse Recruiting / Dover integration, you'll need to create a Harvest API key.

Follow the steps in [this article](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/5888163769883) to create the key, and verify that the credentials and permissions below are selected.

#### Credentials

In the _Create New Credential_ box, make the following selections:

  * **API type:** Harvest
  * **Partner:** Dover
  * **Description:** Dover Harvest API Key



#### Permissions

Verify that the following permissions are selected for the Dover integration:

**Applications**

  * Select all



**Candidates**

  * Select all



**Note** : DELETE permissions are optional.

**Tags**

  * Select all



**Users**

  * Select all



**Note** : DELETE permissions are optional.

**Scheduled interviews**

  * Select all



**Activity Feed**

  * Select all



**Jobs**

  * Select all



**Note** : DELETE permissions are optional.

**Job stages**

  * Select all



**Rejection reasons**

  * Select all



**Sources**

  * Select all



**Prospect pool**

  * Select all



When finished, click **Save.**

Your Harvest API key for the integration is created and configured to be provided to Dover in a later step.

### Create a Dover source in Greenhouse Recruiting

In order to tell which candidates in Greenhouse Recruiting were added by Dover, you'll need to create a custom source for Dover.

To create a Dover custom source in Greenhouse Recruiting, click the **Configure** icon on your navigation bar, then select **Custom** **Options** on the left.

Select **Sources** on the left, then click **Create New Source**.

Select **Other** from the dropdown menu and enter **Dover** as the source.

Check out this article for more information: [Add custom source](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/200721664).

### Enable the Dover integration

Navigate to [Dover > Setup > Company](http://app.dover.io/setup/company) and select **ATS** **Settings**.

Select _Greenhouse_ from the dropdown under _Which ATS do you use?_

Follow the steps listed to configure your integration:

  1. Provide the correct [subdomain](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/201111684) (for instance, if your Greenhouse URL says app3.greenhouse.io, enter _app3._ into this field)
  2. Confirm you have created a Dover source as detailed above.
  3. Enter the Harvest API Key you created in Greenhouse Recruiting earlier.
  4. Confirm Dover has the correct permissions as detailed above



Once you have completed the setup, you'll see the following confirmation screen:

To set up individual jobs, navigate to [Dover > Jobs](http://app.dover.io/jobs) and click _Setup_ next to the job you're onboarding.

Navigate to **ATS** **Settings** and select the Greenhouse Recruiting job name and the user we should post on behalf of from the dropdown menus. The user you select must have full access to the job. Dover will use the selected user ID to add and make all edits to candidates.

When finished, click **Save**.

### Use the Dover integration on Greenhouse Recruiting

Accessing Greenhouse Recruiting from the Dover app is easy. If a candidate has been added to Greenhouse Recruiting, you'll find a link to their profile in your Greenhouse at [Dover > Pipeline](http://app.dover.io/pipeline) and on the candidate thread in Slack.

By default, candidates will be added to your Greenhouse Recruiting when they are interested and you approve them in Dover. Candidates are added to the stage in your Greenhouse Recruiting that corresponds to the first stage of your [interview plan](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/115002194903), and you can select the appropriate stage during onboarding.

**Note** : It may take up to one hour for candidates to sync to Greenhouse Recruiting.

Once an interview has been scheduled through Dover, you'll see the event details listed under _Interviews_ on the candidate's profile in Greenhouse Recruiting.

Dover also has the option to add all candidates that we contact as prospects. Speak with your Dover engagement manager if you're interested in this option.

#### Candidate exclusion

Dover won't reach out to anyone that has had any activity in Greenhouse Recruiting for the previous year, regardless of the job they were sourced for. This applies to prospects as well.

#### How are candidates tracked?

Dover will track candidates across stages in Greenhouse Recruiting. If a candidate stage is updated in Dover, the candidate will be moved in Greenhouse Recruiting – and vice versa.

  * Recruiter screen / Initial call → Initial Call
  * Hiring manager screen/ Technical phone screen → Pre-onsite
  * Onsite / Face-to-face → Onsite
  * Offer → Offer



If the candidate was rejected or marked as _withdrew_ in Dover, they will be rejected in Greenhouse Recruiting.

### Additional resources

#### Links in Dover are not working

If Dover is adding candidates to Greenhouse Recruiting but the links in Slack or Email aren't working, it means Dover is probably pointing to the wrong Greenhouse Recruiting subdomain. If this is happening, reach out to Dover Support and provide the URL you see when you login to Greenhouse Recruiting.

Examples include:

  * [app.greenhouse.io](http://app.greenhouse.io)
  * [app2.greenhouse.io](http://app2.greenhouse.io)
  * [app3.greenhouse.io](http://app3.greenhouse.io)
  * [yourcompanyname.greenhouse.io](http://yourcompanyname.greenhouse.io)



#### Unable to find correct job in Dover

When onboarding a new job through Dover, if the dropdown on the **ATS** **Settings** page in the Dover app is showing some results but not the one you're looking for, be sure the job is active in Greenhouse Recruiting. Dover only shows active jobs.

**Note** : Dover uses the internal job name from Greenhouse Recruiting. The internal job name (visible inside Greenhouse Recruiting) and external job name (shown to candidates on your job boards and careers pages) may be different.

If you have more than 100 active jobs or users, please follow the steps below to provide Dover Support with your job name and ID so they can correct the error:

To find the job ID:

Navigate to Greenhouse Recruiting and click on **Jobs** > select or search for your job > copy the **#** from the URL in your browser.

#### Additional help

For information or troubleshooting not covered here, reach out to [support@dover.com](mailto:support@dover.com) or contact your Dover Support owner in Slack.

# Prospect pools and stages

**Permissions:** Job admin or above, who can manage CRM and unattached prospects

**Product tier:** Available for new subscription tiers (Core, Plus, and Pro)

Managing prospects is an important task for quickly finding qualified candidates. Prospect pools and stages allow your organization to manage prospects more efficiently.

In Greenhouse Recruiting, a **prospect pool** is a larger group of available prospects, such as talent for the upcoming year. You can control which users can see prospect pools and prospects by assigning a job, department or office to individual pools. Prospect pools without restrictions are visible to all CRM users.

A **stage** is a smaller group inside of a pool where you can track prospects at a more detailed level. Like interview stages, pool stages can represent specific contact points, such as first contact, interested groups, or on-hold prospects.

#### In this article

    * Assign a default prospect pool
    * Create a new prospect pool
    * Add or edit a stage to a prospect pool
    * Edit a prospect pool's settings
    * Delete a prospect pool
    * Archive a prospect pool
    * Restore an archived prospect pool



#### Assign a default prospect pool

To view or change your organization's default prospect pool, go to **Configure** , then select **Organization**. Scroll to **Default Prospect Pool** and select a pool.

#### Create a new prospect pool

To create a new pool, select **CRM** at the top of the page. Scroll to **Prospect pools** , then select **See all.**

Next, select **Create a prospect pool.**

****

Add a name and description. Then select your pool's jobs, departments and offices. Select **Create**.

**Note:** Your prospect pool will inherit the permissions of its jobs, departments and offices. Depending on their permissions, some users may not be able to view the pool or its prospects.

You're now in your new prospect pool, where you'll manage your prospects, stages and settings.

### Add or edit a stage to a prospect pool

To add a stage, go to the **Stages** tab, then select **Add or edit**. Select **Add a new stage.**

Click **Select a prospect pool** to reuse a stage from another prospect pool.

**Tip:** Reorder your pool's stages with the drag-and-drop icon.

#### Edit a prospect pool's settings

You can configure and edit your prospect pool in the **Settings tab**. Here you can add or edit:

  * Pool names
  * Pool description
  * Admins
  * Departments
  * Offices
  * Jobs



#### Delete a prospect pool

Deleting a prospect pool completely removes the pool from your organization. When a pool is deleted, you won't be able to view candidates that were previously added to the pool.

To delete a prospect pool, select the ellipses icon next to the pool. Choose **Delete** from the dropdown menu. Select where you'd like to move the pool's existing prospects. Then, confirm you want to delete the pool and move its prospects.

#### Archive a prospect pool

You can archive a prospect pool by selecting the ellipses icon and choosing **Archive** from the dropdown menu.

**Note:** A CRM Admin can archive or restore any prospect pool. However, normal CRM users must be a Prospect Pool Admin to archive or restore a specific prospect pool. To learn more, [click here](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/4411120566299).

#### Restore an archived prospect pool

To restore an archived pool, select **Archived pools** from the stages filter.

Find the prospect pool that you'd like to restore, and select the **ellipses** icon. Then, click **Restore**.

# Edit opening on job with one-stage approval process

**Permissions:** Site Admin, and Job Admin who can edit job info

**Product tier:** Available for new subscription tiers (Core, Plus, and Pro)

In Greenhouse Recruiting, the process to edit openings on an existing job depends on that job's approval process.

This article covers how to edit the following details for openings on a job that has a [one-stage approval process](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360025478652).

#### In this article

  * View your openings
  * Opening ID
  * Opening Status
  * Open Date for Opening
  * Target Start Date for Opening
  * Close Date for Opening
  * Close Reason for Opening
  * Custom Opening Field for Opening



### View your openings

To start, click **Jobs** from the navigation bar and **select the job** from the  _All Jobs_ dashboard. 

Navigate to the **Job Info** page. (**Job Setup** > **Job Info**)

Scroll to the bottom of the page until you reach the _Openings_ panel and click **Manage Openings**.

Select a **specific opening** from the left-hand panel of the  _Manage Openings_ dialog box.

The details for the selected opening will populate in the right-hand panel. Continue editing your opening using the following sections of this article. 

### Opening ID

Opening IDs allow your organization to track openings on jobs in a systematic fashion based on naming conventions unique to your company's internal processes. 

Add the **Opening ID** for the select opening, then click **Save** when finished.

### Opening Status

An opening's status can be toggled between open and closed. [Click here](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360028137532) to learn more about how to close an opening on a job.

Change the status of an opening by selecting **Open** or **Closed** from the _Status_ dropdown menu. Then, click **Save** when finished. 

### Open Date for Opening

The Open Date allows your organization to see when a job opening was opened. This field is editable since some organizations may have [evergreen jobs](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360000891392) that are perpetually open and requires you to update the Open Date for more accurate [Time to Fill](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/204635705) data. 

Click the **Open Date** and use the calendar to select a new date. Then, click **Save** when finished. 

**Note** : If you manually change an opening's open or close dates, you should ensure that the job open and close dates (under **Job** **Setup** > **Job** **Info**) are also changed to match. This ensures your reports don't show disparate data.

****

### Target Start Date for Opening

An opening's Target Start Date allows your organization to set a goal against a job opening. This can help keep your hiring team on track and allows your organization to measure hiring performance.

Click the **Target Start Date** and use the calendar to select a new date. Click **Save** when finished. 

### Close Date for Opening

An opening's Close Date can only be edited when the opening's status is set to closed.

Click the **Close Date** and use the calendar to select a date. 

**Note** : If you manually change an opening's open or close dates, you should ensure that the job open and close dates (under **Job** **Setup** > **Job** **Info**) are also changed to match. This will ensure your reports don't show disparate data.

Add a close reason (optional). Click **Save** when finished. 

### Close Reason for Opening

An opening's Close Reason can only be edited when the opening's status is set to closed. 

Click the **Close Reason** and select an option from the dropdown menu. Click **Save** when finished. 

### Custom Opening Field for Opening

A [custom opening field](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360036372071) allows your organization to record select information on a per opening basis rather than for the entire job. 

Custom opening fields are displayed at the bottom of the page. Edit the response of the custom field and click **Save**. 

The response to the custom opening field is recorded and the response will appear in the [Job Status report](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360003333251). 

**Note** : Custom opening fields can be edited for **Open** , **Pending** , and **Closed** job openings.

# Talytica integration

Talytica is a SaaS-based company focused on personal talent analytics to make hiring fair, simple and effective. Talytica combines best-practices in psychological assessments with advances in data analytics and machine learning to predict the performance and tenure of each new job applicant before you hire.

Greenhouse Recruiting's integration with Talytica allows your organization to automate assessments, reference checks, and phone interviews, as well as leverage applicant machine learning scoring models to determine if candidates are a _pass_ , _consider_ , or _fast-track_ (must be configured in Talytica and requires several hundred historical candidate records in Greenhouse Recruiting).

  * Enable the Talytica integration
  * Use the Talytica integration
    * Add the Talytica assessment stage
    * Configure the assessment stage
    * Send the Talytica assessment
    * Review the assessment results
  * Additional resources



### Enable the Talytica integration

In order to enable the integration, your organization will need to contact Talytica to request your API key. Once you have received your API key, fill out the form at [www.greenhouse.io/asksupport](http://support.greenhouse.io/direct) or _[click here](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/requests/new)_ to open a ticket.

**Note** : Don't send the API key in this initial email. Greenhouse Technical Support will respond with a [SendSafely link](https://www.sendsafely.com/howitworks/) for you to securely share your API key.

Once Greenhouse Technical Support receives your API key via SendSafely, we'll email you to confirm that your API key has been set up in your account and that your integration is enabled.

**Note:** To verify your identity, Greenhouse Technical Support might request you provide a [support verification code](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360022771952) before adding the API key to your organization's account.

### Use the Talytica integration

There are two main approaches your team can take:

  1. Simplify a complex hiring process by replacing several existing stages with Talytica's _All-in-One Multi-Test._
  2. Add more disciplined automation to stage with Talytica's modular tests. These modular tests allow you to work with other testing providers for some stages if you prefer.



**Example one: Simple Approach**

This general multi-test includes the following assessments:

  * Personality Assessments
  * Ideal Organizational Type
  * Strong Career Interests
  * Automated Phone Interviews
  * Automated Reference Checks



**Example two: Modular Approach**

Below is an example of setting up several Talytica stages to advance the candidate through using a modular approach. This is part of the power of Talytica as these stages are close to fully automated.

You can add the following stages under the Talytica stage:

  * **Talytica Custom _Pass_ or _Interview_ Pre-Screen**
    * This is a Custom model built from your historical data within Greenhouse Recruiting. You will have to contact Talytica to add it. It requires at least 100 people having been advanced to ‘interview’ and at least 200 total applicants. If you have these, Talytica can build a model that will give the probability that a candidate will be advanced to the interview stage.
  * **Talytica Culture Fit & Personality Assessments**
    * These are tests for Culture Fit, Organizational Preference, Strong Career 
      * Interests and Personality (Cognitive is also available). These help predict culture fit, turnover and performance - and can be customized for customers with more than 100 candidates per position.
  * **Talytica Automated Phone Interviews**
    * This gives you the ability to use pre-recorded phone interview questions and listen to the candidates responses prior to talking to them. Emotional qualities of the voice characteristics are also ‘auto-scored.’ This gives you the ability to make much more rapid, more informed decisions on who to advance.
  * **Talytica Automated Reference Checks**
    * Rapid, accurate, completely automated reference checks that save time and allow you to move reference checking to various stages.
  * **Talytica _All-In-One_ Multi-Assessment**
    * This includes b) through d) above and all stages are sent to the Candidate as one, integrated 10-20 minute assessment.
  * **Custom Tests**
    * Talytica has full customization as well as Cognitive Tests and the ability to add machine learning based predictions to nearly anything Talytica has. Contact Talytica to learn more.



#### Add the Talytica assessment stage

Once the Greenhouse Recruiting / Talytica integration is enabled for your organization, you'll be able to add the Talytica assessment as an Interview stage.

To do this for an existing job, navigate to a job (**Jobs** > **Job Name**) and click **Job Setup**.

Click **Interview Plan** and then click**Add a Stage**.

Select the **Talytica** stage.

When finished, click **Add**.

#### Configure the assessment stage

Once the stage has been added to the job's interview plan, click **Edit** beside it.

On the _Edit Interview Kit_ page, you will see a dropdown that reflects all the assessments you have set up previously in Talytica.

Select the appropriate assessment, assign at least one Greenhouse Recruiting user to grade / review the submitted assessment, and then click **Save**.

**Note:** All configurations of the assessments themselves, as well as the email template, will need to be completed in Talytica.

#### Send the Talytica assessment

When a candidate is moved into the Talytica interview stage, Greenhouse Recruiting will display a **Send Test** link on the candidate's profile. Click the **Send Test** link.

**Note:** When you send an assessment from Greenhouse Recruiting, the interview instructions actually are sent to the candidate by Talytica.

Use the subsequent box to:

  * Confirm the email address of the candidate
  * Select which assessment the candidate will take
  * Assign a grader



Click **Send Test** when finished.

The candidate will receive an email invite to take the assessment.

#### Review the assessment results

After completing the assessment, it will be scored automatically by the Talytica system, with the option for you to listen to recorded responses and add manual scores to the audio assessments in the Talytica portal.

The status of the assessment will be viewable in Greenhouse Recruiting. The following statuses are available:

  * Take Home Test to be sent
  * Waiting for candidate to submit test
  * Scorecard due from [designated grader]



Once the Talytica assessment is completed and the grader has submitted a scorecard, the Interview Kit will contain a link to the candidate's results in Talytica.

You can also log into your [custom Talytica portal](https://portal-dev.talytica.com/) for more in-depth reports (contact the Talytica team to enable this feature). The portal will maintain a copy of all candidate records. It also will contain more detailed information behind every candidate (see examples below).

**Custom candidate predictions:**

**Answer validity and conscious deception scores:**

**Culture fit and organization preference scores:**

**Job experience and personality:**

**Reference checks:**

### Additional resources

For additional information or troubleshooting not covered here, reach out to [info@talytica.com](mailto:info@talytica.com) or call (424) 625-5857.

# Schedule recurring report

**Permissions:** Job Admin or above

**Product tier:** Available for new subscription tiers (Core, Plus, and Pro)

Greenhouse Recruiting allows your organization to schedule a recurring report that will be automatically emailed to specified users at a regular cadence.

Scheduled reports include the report data in the message body, as well as an Excel download of the data attached to the email. Reports containing sensitive information will have a download link instead of a file.

**Note** : A custom report must be [saved](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/115003218066) before a recurring email can be configured and scheduled.

#### In this article

  * Set up a scheduled report
  * Receive a scheduled report
  * Send a report to a user who doesn't have permission to view the report



### Set up a scheduled report

To setup a scheduled report, click Reports on your navigation bar and open the report you want to schedule.

Click **Schedule** in the top of the report.

__

Configure the details for the scheduled report, including the name, recipients, email subject, and an email message.

Define your schedule at the bottom of the page by selecting the frequency and timing for the delivery. These options will change based on if your schedule is occurring.

The following frequency options are available for selection:

  * Weekly
  * Bi-weekly
  * Monthly
  * Quarterly



__

When finished, click**Save Schedule**.

**Note** : If Bi-weekly is selected as the frequency, the report schedule will begin on the next date following selection. For example, if Monday is selected for a bi-weekly recurring report schedule, the report will send the immediate next Monday and then skip the next.

If Quarterly is selected, the report will be sent on the final day of the quarter. Quarterly reports will be sent on March 31, June 30, September 30, and December 31 throughout the year.

### Receive a scheduled report

The selected users will receive an email of the report on the selected days at the time you selected when setting up the report. The email body will include a view of your message text and report data. An Excel file will also be attached to the email containing the contents of the report. 

Users may see a slightly different report based on their permission. See the next section for more information.

### Send a report to a user who doesn't have permission to view the report

When you email a report to another person, Greenhouse Recruiting will first check the recipient's permissions to see if they are allowed to access the report. If the specified user cannot access data in the report (like private candidate data), the report will not be sent.

Recipients may see a slightly different version than the original scheduled report since Greenhouse Recruiting mirrors the recipient's permissions before delivering the email. If a recipient doesn't have access to a particular job in the report, that information will be redacted.

# Add custom fields to HRIS Link for Workday®️

**Permissions:** Site Admin, and Job Admin who can manage custom fields

**Product tier:** Available for new subscription tiers (Core, Plus, and Pro) with HRIS Link add-on

HRIS Link makes it easy to import any and all data from your HRIS into Greenhouse Recruiting in the form of [custom fields](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/202609855). This article outlines how HRIS Link maps report fields to Greenhouse Recruiting fields, and how to incorporate new data fields into your integration.

#### In this article

  * Field mapping logic
  * Add a custom new field in HRIS Link
    * Add a new field in HRIS Link with 500+ open jobs
  * Additional resources



### Field mapping logic

In order to map each report field to a Greenhouse Recruiting custom field, HRIS Link looks for a basic text match between the report column header and the following Greenhouse Recruiting custom field attributes (in order):

  1. Immutable field key
  2. Field name



**Note:** When performing the text match, HRIS Link replaces all underscores ("_") with spaces, and ignores casing.

If HRIS Link can't find an immutable field key that matches the report column header, HRIS Link looks for a match on the field name itself.

**Example**

**Note** : Immutable field keys are generated automatically at the time a custom field is created in Greenhouse Recruiting. You can open a ticket with [Greenhouse Technical Support](https://support.greenhouse.io/direct) if you need to modify an existing immutable field key.

### Add a new custom field in HRIS Link

To add a new custom field to HRIS Link, create the [custom field](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/202609855) in Greenhouse Recruiting via **Configure** > **Custom Options** > **Jobs** or **Users** > **Add Field**.

**Note** : For [custom user fields](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/7626796336283), HRIS Link supports single-select, multi-select, yes / no, and user field types. Read more here: [Setup HRIS Link user import > Add custom user fields to your report](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360058479852#h_01GESZ151VGM7AAG1WCWWNW8AM).

For more information on supported custom job fields, check out: [Setup HRIS Link job import > Add custom job fields to your report](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/4403889907355-Setup-HRIS-Link-job-import-with-job-requisitions-enabled#h_01F1GN30JTSZW1Z3TEA2VRJXQP).

Copy the field name and immutable field key.

If the Greenhouse Recruiting custom field is a single-select or multi-select field type, add all option values that exist in the HRIS.

**Note:** You can use [custom field options syncing](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360002158492) to automate this step.

Add the new data field to your HRIS Link report, using a column header value of either the immutable field key (recommended) or the custom field name.

Verify the newly added field appears on the HRIS report with the correct column header.

Once the above steps are completed, HRIS Link imports values from the newly added field on the next integration run.

For any errors, check out our troubleshooting guide [here](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360059154811).

### Add new fields to HRIS Link with 500+ open jobs

HRIS Link will run every 15 minutes when your integration is enabled. HRIS Link leverages Greenhouse Harvest API to create and update jobs in your Greenhouse Recruiting tenant.

When there are more than 500 open jobs in Greenhouse Recruiting that are utilizing HRIS Link, adding or updating fields in your integration may take longer than 15 minutes, causing unexpected integration errors.

In this case, you can reach out to HRIS Link support to request an integration pause.

  1. Open a ticket with [Greenhouse Technical Support](https://support.greenhouse.io/direct) to request an integration pause.
  2. A member of our team will arrange a time to pause the integration to allow your team to update your report.
  3. After your team confirms the report has been updated, our team will manually push an integration run and verify successful completion.



### Additional resources

  * [Import jobs with HRIS Link](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360058912031)
  * [Import user accounts with HRIS Link](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360058975731)
  * [Define custom job fields to import from HRIS](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360059988351)

# CLEAR FAQ for candidates

Greenhouse and CLEAR® have partnered to offer secure identity verification within the hiring process. This partnership allows employers to confirm candidate identities through CLEAR®’s trusted service, adding confidence and safety without sharing personal documents directly with the employer.

#### In this article

  * Why am I being asked to complete a CLEAR® verification?
  * Is CLEAR® making decisions about who gets hired?
  * How does CLEAR® support fairness for underrepresented or LGBTQ+ candidates?
  * Does facial hair or weight gain impact verification?
  * How do I complete a CLEAR® verification?
  * Can I decline a verification request?
  * Is there a time limit for completing verification requests?
  * Who do I contact to check the status of my application or to appeal a verification result?
  * How can I update my information or ID?
  * Where do I go for other questions and support?
  * How is my personal data used during identity verification?
  * Does Greenhouse store my personal data?
  * Can I ask CLEAR® to delete my information?
  * How do I contact CLEAR support and view my data or transaction history?



#### Why am I being asked to complete a CLEAR® verification?

Employers use CLEAR® to confirm a candidate’s identity in a secure and consistent way. It protects both candidates and companies from impersonation or fraud.

#### Is CLEAR® making decisions about who gets hired?

No. CLEAR® only confirms that a person is who they say they are. It does not screen, score, or influence hiring decisions in any way. It’s simply a way to verify identity and check that the person behind the profile is real.

#### How does CLEAR® support fairness for underrepresented or LGBTQ+ candidates?

CLEAR®’s technology is designed to be agnostic to race, gender, and age. It doesn't make decisions based on demographic attributes. Additionally, CLEAR®’s flexible matching can use stable identifiers like date of birth instead of relying solely on names which may change over time.

#### Does facial hair or weight gain impact verification?

CLEAR's facial recognition technology focuses on stable features, making it unaffected by changes like weight, facial hair, or expressions. Obstructions like sunglasses or masks can interfere — but religious head coverings are fully supported, as long as the face and eyes are visible.

#### How do I complete a CLEAR® verification?

CLEAR® verification requests will be sent to the email the employer has on record. Once the email is received, you must create a free MyGreenhouse account to complete the request. If you already have a MyGreenhouse account, you can access the CLEAR® task on your dashboard.

#### What documents are accepted?

A government-issued ID, such as a passport, is required to complete identity verification. You can view the list of accepted document types for your country [here](https://docs.clearme.com/docs/supported-document-types-1).

#### Can I decline a verification request?

Yes, candidates can decline to complete a verification request and should contact the recruiter for next steps.

#### Is there a time limit for completing verification requests?

Verification requests must be completed within 14 days of receiving the email, or within 10 days of starting the verification process.

#### Who do I contact to check the status of my application or to appeal a verification result?

Contact the employer and discuss it with the recruiter directly.

#### How can I update my information or ID?

If you need to update identifying information, such as the government ID you used during verification, you can contact CLEAR® directly. Email memberservices@clearme.com or start a chat with CLEAR’s Digital Ambassador [here](https://www.clearme.com/support/how-do-i-contact-clear).

#### Where do I go for other questions and support?

For basic troubleshooting inquiries regarding CLEAR® verifications and Greenhouse, use the question mark icon in the Greenhouse support site.

If you’re having trouble completing an identity verification, visit [CLEAR’s website](https://www.clearme.com/). CLEAR offers an AI ambassador that can help with common issues and answer questions about the verification process. To start a chat, click the chat icon in the bottom-right corner of the page.

For any questions for your specific verification or company process, contact the employer.

#### How is my personal data used during identity verification?

When you complete identity verification, you submit your information directly to CLEAR®. Greenhouse does not send your information to CLEAR®.

After verification, Greenhouse receives the verification result and key identifiers, and shares it with the employer who sent the request.

#### Does Greenhouse store my personal data?

Greenhouse stores a limited set of personal data related to your identity verification request, including your full name, email address, phone number, IP address, and the verification result.

Greenhouse does not receive or store any other information used to complete the identity verification request, such as government ID images or a selfie. This information is submitted directly to CLEAR®.

#### Can I ask CLEAR® to delete my information?

You have full control of the information you provided to CLEAR® for your identity verification. If you wish to request deletion of your information, you may submit your request [here](https://my.clearme.com/v3/privacy/data-request) or [privacy@clearme.com](mailto:privacy@clearme.com). 

#### How do I contact CLEAR support and view my data or transaction history?

If you need help with your CLEAR account or identity verification, you can contact CLEAR’s Member Care team the following ways:

  * **Phone** : 1‑855‑CLEARME (253‑2763)
  * **Email** : [memberservices@clearme.com](mailto:memberservices@clearme.com)[](mailto:memberservices@clearme.com)
  * **Live Chat** : Available at [www.clearme.com/support](http://www.clearme.com/support)



You can also visit [www.clearme.com](http://www.clearme.com/) to log into your CLEAR account and access the Member Portal. From there, you can:

  * View your account details
  * See past identity verification events (if applicable)
  * Manage your personal information and communication preferences
  * Request deletion of your data at any time by emailing [privacy@clearme.com](mailto:privacy@clearme.com)[](mailto:privacy@clearme.com) or by submitting a request [here](https://my.clearme.com/v3/privacy/data-request)

# Lattice integration

Lattice’s integration with Greenhouse Recruiting allows for mutual Greenhouse and Lattice customers to seamlessly transfer hired candidates from Greenhouse to Lattice.

#### In this article

    * Create a Harvest API key
    * Finish setup in Lattice
    * Use the Lattice integration with Greenhouse Recruiting
    * Frequently asked questions
    * Additional resources



### Create a Harvest API key

To configure the Lattice x Greenhouse integration, you’ll need to create a Harvest API key.

Follow the steps in [this article](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/5888163769883) to create the key, and verify that the permissions below are selected when configuring the Lattice integration.

#### **Credentials**

In the _Create New Credential_ box, make the following selections:

  * **API Type:** Harvest
  * **Partner:** Lattice or Unlisted Vendor
  * **Description:** Lattice Harvest API Key



#### **Permissions**

Verify that the following permissions (All GET for each section) are selected for the Lattice integration:

  * **Applications**
    * GET: Retrieve Application
    * GET: List Applications
  * **Candidates**
    * GET: Retrieve Candidate
    * GET: List Candidates
  * **Custom Field Options**
    * GET: Get custom field options
  * **Custom Fields**
    * GET: Get custom fields
  * **Jobs**
    * GET: Retrieve Job
    * GET: List Jobs
    * GET: Get hiring team
  * **Offers**
    * GET: List Application Offers
    * GET: Retrieve Application’s Current Offer
    * GET: Retrieve Offer
    * GET: List Offers



### Finish setup in Lattice

In Lattice, navigate to **Platform** > **Integrations** > and scroll to the bottom of the page to find **Greenhouse** underneath the _ATS_ category

Once connected, you test the connection by clicking the **Manual Sync** button. Once you feel comfortable with the integration, you can reach out to your Lattice point-of-contact and they will turn the integration on to run once a day at 2:00 AM PST.

### Use the Lattice integration with Greenhouse Recruiting

Use the Lattice x Greenhouse integration to reduce the need to manual data entry when you hire a candidate. After you mark a candidate as hired in Greenhouse and run a sync, the candidate will automatically flow into Lattice.

The following attributes are mapped from Greenhouse to Lattice. The integration also brings over custom attributes, as long as fields are configured exactly the same in the two systems.

**Greenhouse Recruiting field** | **Lattice field**  
---|---  
Candidate \ Personal Email | Personal Email  
Candidate \ Legal Name - First Name | First Name  
Candidate \ Legal Name - Last Name | Last Name  
Candidate \ First Name + Last Name | Preferred Full Name  
Offer \ Start Date | Start Date  
Candidate \ Work Email | Work email  
Candidate \ Phone Number [ personal ] | Phone Number  
Candidate \ Address[home] - Address Line 1 | Address line 1  
Candidate \ Address[home] - Address Line 2 | Address line 2  
Candidate \ Address[home] - City | Address city  
Candidate \ Address[home] - State | Address state  
Candidate \ Address[home] - Zipcode | Address postal code  
Job \ Department | Department  
Job \ Title | Job Title  
  
### Frequently asked questions

**When is an employee sent from Greenhouse to Lattice?**

When an employee is marked as hired in Greenhouse, they will be brought over to Lattice and “dropped” in the onboarding state.

**What does the Greenhouse integration use as a unique identifier?**

Personal Email.

**Will anything sync after my employee’s start date?**

No. After the employee's start date, their information won't be included in any Greenhouse syncs. At that point, Lattice is the source of truth for their information. This behavior ensures the employee can update their information in Lattice, without having it repeatedly overwritten with the details they submitted during their initial hiring.

**When I connect my Greenhouse and Lattice accounts, what candidates are included in the sync?**

After you connect Greenhouse and Lattice with your API Key, any candidate marked as hired after that date will be included in syncs to Lattice.

**I changed an employee’s information in Greenhouse Recruiting, will those changes show in Lattice?**

If an employee's information is changed in the offer document, you will need to mark the candidate as unhired, update the information, and then mark the candidate as hired. This allows the sync to process the updated information.

If the employee's information is changed on their candidate profile, and they haven't hit their start date, the updated information will be included in the next sync.

**What types of employees sync from Greenhouse Recruiting to Lattice?**

The integration supports bringing over US employees from Greenhouse to Lattice.

### Additional resources

For additional information or troubleshooting not covered here, reach out to [hriscare@lattice.com](mailto:hriscare@lattice.com)

# Admin access to employee profiles

**Permissions:** Owners and Coordinators

**Product tier:** Available for Greenhouse Onboarding and Greenhouse Welcome subscription tiers

As Admins, [Owners](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360019575491) and [Coordinators](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360019575511) can view and manage employee profiles in Greenhouse Onboarding.

#### In this article

  * Access employee profiles
    * Info tab
    * 30-day goals tab
    * Admin tab
    * Tasks tab
    * Documents tab
    * Feedback tab
    * Email activity tab
  * Additional resources



### Access employee profiles

To access an employee's profile, click on their name under _My New Hires_ (if they directly report to you) or enter their name in the **Search bar** at the top of your home page.

**Note** : Employee profiles are only available for employees who've been officially converted to new hires and onboarded. Learn how to [onboard your pending hires](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360029352891). 

The header of their employee profile includes their name, [pronouns and pronunciations](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/4564402907291), job title, department, start date, work email, and the option to manage their profile picture.

The employee's profile includes the following tabs:

  * Info tab
  * 30-day goals tab
  * Admin tab
  * Tasks tab
  * Documents tab
  * Feedback tab
  * Email activity tab



#### Info tab

On the Info tab, you'll find additional personal information for the employee, details about their manager, and a list of their direct reports if the employee is assigned as a manager to other users.

**Note:** Coordinators have access to view or edit employee information based on permissions granted by your organization's Admin Owner. For example, coordinators may be able to view an employee's ethnicity but cannot edit it.

Any field with a **private********icon** next to it indicates that the information is not viewable to other employees in your organization unless they have specified permissions granted by the Admin Owner.

Click **Edit** to add or make changes to the employee's information. Once finished, click **Save**.

#### 30-day goals tab

Use the 30-day goals tab to configure and assign [onboarding goals for newly-hired employees](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/9265626455067).

#### Admin tab

The admin tab allows you to perform certain administrative actions for an employee, such as:

  * Resending the ['Your next steps' email](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360020389692) and/or the ['Welcome to the Team' email](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360020389712)
  * Deleting the employee's profile 
  * Viewing any [Administrative access](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360019200392) or [Custom access](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360019516351) assigned to the employee 
  * Editing the employee's employment status
  * Editing the [Other criteria rule](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360000863252)



**Note** : Only Owners can delete an employee's profile or view/edit the Other criteria rule. Owners need to grant permission for Coordinators to view and edit an employee's employment status.

If you are an Owner and need to delete an employee profile, click **Delete Profile** in the _Additional Actions_ section. Then, select **Yes, delete it** to confirm the action.

Click **Edit** to update an employee's  _Employment Status_ or to add an  _Other Criteria_ rule. Click **Save** when you're done updating these Admin fields.

#### Tasks tab

The Tasks tab shows all [tasks](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360000525691) assigned to an employee, their manager, and other users in your organization, such as their Onboarding Coordinator.

Click **Create a New Task** to create and assign a new task to your employee. Click **Add an Existing Task** to assign an existing task that's already been created by your organization.

#### Documents tab

The Documents tab shows all [documents](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/216488683) and [e-signatures](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/115003695071) assigned to your employee by you or your organization.

**Note** : Only Coordinators with permission granted by the Admin Owner to manage employee documents and signature requests can view the Documents tab. E-signature documents are only available for the Greenhouse Onboarding subscription tier. 

Click **Add Document** or **Request Signature** to add a new document or send an e-signature request to your employee. 

Click the **ellipsis icon** to **Cancel** a signature request or **Download** a signed document. If your employee has completed multiple signatures, you can select **Download All** to download all available signed documents.

If an e-signature requires a counter signature, you can also [reassign the counter signer](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/8857059763099) to a different user in your organization. Click the **ellipsis icon** then **Edit Counter Signer** to change the assigned counter signer.

#### Feedback tab

You can send [feedback questions](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/115003877872) to an employee about their role and their experience with your organization in the Feedback tab. Each completed question provides details on the employee's answer date, response, and any additional comments they provided.

#### Email activity tab

Use the email activity tab to see a list of all the Greenhouse Onboarding [emails](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360000515452) that your organization has sent to an employee, their manager, or other users with assigned tasks related to this employee.

**Note:** The email activity tab does not include [choreographed introduction](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360048564092) emails.

Each entry in the email activity tab includes the email subject line, the recipient's address, and the time the email was sent.

**Note:** The email activity tab is only available to users with [Owner access](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360019575491).

### Additional resources

  * [View and manage an employee profile](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/5759718119707)
  * [Manager access to employee profiles](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/13298081921179)

# Jira integration

**Permissions:** Owners

**Product tier:** Available for Greenhouse Welcome and Greenhouse Onboarding subscription tiers

Developed by Atlassian, Jira is a bug-tracking and agile project management tool.

You can integrate Jira as a [third-party task system](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360022403771) with Greenhouse Onboarding to automatically assign onboarding tasks to Jira via email.

#### In this article

  * Retrieve your Jira email address
  * Configure your Jira email settings
  * Enable Jira in Greenhouse Onboarding
  * Additional resources



### Retrieve your Jira email address

Greenhouse Onboarding uses your organization's Jira email address to send your onboarding tasks to Jira's ticketing system.

**Note** : You'll need to set up a mail server and service with Jira for the integration to work correctly. [Learn more](https://confluence.atlassian.com/adminjiraserver073/creating-issues-and-comments-from-email-861253784.html).

To enable Jira as a [third-party task system](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360022403771), contact your organization's Jira administrator to retrieve your **Jira email**. You'll use this later to enable the Jira integration in Greenhouse Onboarding.

### Configure your Jira email settings

Configure your Jira email settings so Greenhouse Onboarding can send tasks to Jira.

Open your Jira account, then navigate to **Configure** > **System** > **Mail** > **Incoming Mail**.

Click**Add incoming mail handler** , or click **Edit** next to an existing mail handler.

From the _Mail Handler_ window, assign the following:

  * Name
  * Server
  * Handler



**Note** : We recommend using the following for your mail handler settings:

  * **Name** that mentions Greenhouse Onboarding (for example, "Greenhouse Onboarding task"
  * **Create a new issue or add a comment to an existing issue** for Mail Handler Type



Click **Next** when you're done.

In the next window, specify the following:

  * Project where Greenhouse Onboarding should add tasks
  * Type of issue that should be created
  * Default Reporter



**Note** : Make sure to select a **Default Reporter** to ensure Jira will pick up tasks as incoming issues.

When you're done, click **Save**.

### Enable Jira in Greenhouse Onboarding

Once you've configured and copied your Jira email address, navigate to [Greenhouse Onboarding](https://onboarding.greenhouse.io/).

From your Greenhouse Onboarding homepage, navigate to **Settings** > **Company Info** > **3rd-Party Task Systems**.

On the _3rd-Party Task Systems_ page, click **Add New**.

Give your new 3rd-party task system a **name** and select Jira with the **System** dropdown.

Paste your copied Jira email address in the **Email Address** field.

Since your Greenhouse Onboarding tasks can include tokens (which may reveal personally identifiable information), you'll need to define which fields Jira can view.

Use the **Viewable Fields (Optional)** dropdown to select which fields Jira can view.

**Note** : If a task with a non-viewable token is assigned to Jira, Greenhouse Onboarding will block Jira from accessing the information.

When you're finished, click **Save and Close**.

Your Jira account will be added as a third-party task system in Greenhouse Onboarding. Repeat these steps for any additional Jira accounts you need to integrate with Greenhouse Onboarding.

This Jira account (and any additional projects connected as third-party task systems) can now be assigned tasks from Greenhouse Onboarding.

When you assign tasks in Greenhouse Onboarding, they'll appear in Jira under your selected project.

Your team can action the task or ticket like any other in a Jira project.

### Additional resources

  * [3rd-party task systems overview](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360022403771)

# Appogee HR integration

At Appogee HR, we're proud to offer simple HR and project tracking solutions that are easy to use, empower your employees and advance with you as your business needs evolve. People software that's as easy as 1, 2, 3! So easy in fact that your teams can start using our solutions straight away, reducing people admin enabling your employees and managers to get on with their jobs in the most productive way possible.

Greenhouse Recruiting's integration with Appogee HR allows HR Managers to be notified when a candidate has been hired in Greenhouse and enables them to be imported to Appogee HR and set up as new employees.

In this article:

  * Configure setup permissions in Greenhouse Recruiting
  * Create a Harvest API Key for the Greenhouse Recruiting/AppogeeHR integration
  * Use the AppogeeHR integration with Greenhouse Recruiting
  * Additional resources



### Configure setup permissions in Greenhouse Recruiting

To configure the Greenhouse Recruiting/Appogee HR integration, you'll need the developer permission **Can manage ALL organization's API Credentials**.

To assign this permission, find a Greenhouse user in your organization with **Site Admin** level permissions and the specific **Can edit another user's advanced permissions** role to update your account.

The Site Admin can update your permissions by navigating to your user page. Click the **Configure** icon  >**Users** > **Your Name**. 

Scroll to the _Permissions_ panel on your user page and expand the _Developer Permissions_ dropdown menu. 

Select **Can manage ALL organization's API credentials** in the _Developer Permissions_ section and click **Save**.

Repeat as necessary for any other user that needs to set up the integration.

### Create a Harvest API Key for the Greenhouse Recruiting/Appogee HR integration

_**Note:** To generate an API key, you must have the developer permission **Manage ALL organization's API Credentials.**_

Click on the **Configure** icon  and select the**Dev Center** on the left.

Select **API Credential Management** in the Dev Center.

From the API Credential Management page, click **Create New API Key** to generate the API key for Appogee HR.

In the _Create New Credential_ dialog box, make the following selections:

  * **API Type:** Harvest
  * **Partner:** Appogee HR
  * **Description:** Appogee HR Harvest API Key



Click **Manage Permissions**.

Click **Copy** to save your API key to your clipboard. Store the API key in a secure location to provide to Appogee HR in the next step.

Click **I have stored the API Key** once you have copied and saved the key.

_**Note:** You won't be able to view the API key after clicking **I have stored the API Key**. If you lose your Appogee HR API key, you will need to generate a new one. _

Select the checkboxes next to each permission box to associate it with the API key.

The following permissions are needed for the Appogee HR integration:

**Candidates**

  * GET: Retrieve Candidate



**Offers**

  * GET: Retrieve Offer
  * GET: List Offers



**Jobs**

  * GET: Retrieve Job



When you're finished, click **Save**.

Your Harvest API key for the Greenhouse/Appogee HR integration is created and configured.

Next, navigate to Appogee HR. In the System Config menu, click **Greenhouse** under Integrations. Paste the API Key into the relevant box.

Click **Validate API Key**.

Follow the instructions in the [Web Hooks](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1Qg3ZNXdMLmpABUz6w24A2KTxv5hsDcxm9mHebHEEbsM/edit?usp=sharing) document to complete the integration setup.

### Use the Appogee HR integration with Greenhouse Recruiting

When a candidate has been marked as Hired in Greenhouse, a notification will be triggered, and you will be able to import them into Appogee HR.

To view and import them, go to **Organization** > **Employees** > **Offer Accepted**.

Click on the employee you want to import. Some of their information will have pulled through from Greenhouse.

Add their Team and Work Profile and click **Next**.

Their start date will be populated with the start date from Greenhouse. Either change it here or just click **Next**.

Edit or add their contact details, or click **Next**.

Finally, select the access you wish them to have and whether you want to set up the Onboarding Portal for them, then click **Next**.

The employee will be successfully imported.

### Additional resources

  * [Setting up the Greenhouse Integration](https://help.appogeehr.com/en/support/solutions/articles/22000271066-setting-up-the-greenhouse-integration)
  * [Adding users from Greenhouse](https://help.appogeehr.com/en/support/solutions/articles/22000271092-adding-users-from-greenhouse)



Please contact [help@appogeehr.com](mailto:help@appogeehr.com) for troubleshooting assistance regarding the integration.

<!-- source: https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360007247092-Structured-hiring-Role-kick-off-meeting -->

# Structured hiring: Role kick-off meeting

The role kick-off meeting is meant to set up the search for success and save time during the interviewing process. Generally, this meeting is the first step in the structured hiring process and is roughly an hour long.

Meeting attendees include the Recruiter on the role and the Hiring Manager but can also include anyone else assigned to the Hiring Team for the role, such as a Coordinator and/or Sourcer. 

In the meeting, the Hiring Team will explore three key areas, as well as define what short-term and long-term success looks like in the role. 

In this article  


  * Defining the job's business objective
  * Identifying candidate skills, traits and qualifications
  * Dividing hiring team roles and responsibilities
  * Additional resources



### Defining the job's business objective

Before we define an ideal candidate by the business objectives of the job we need to qualify what we mean by objectives and why we distinguish them from tasks. Simply put, the distinction between the two is that objectives focus on long-term and big-picture results, while tasks tend to emphasize the daily activities of a new hire. 

By focusing on the intended outcomes of a successful hire you can distinguish between a superstar hire and an average performer. This reorients the conversation from short-term needs to long-term goals. While the structure and format of your role kick-off meeting is entirely up to your team, we've taken the liberty to provide some questions to help you get started thinking about the business objectives of the job:

  1. What goals need to be achieved a year from now for you to determine that the hire is successful?
  2. What will a superstar hire accomplish in a year?
  3. For a superstar to accomplish that, what do they need to do in the first 90 days?



These objectives will provide your team with a roadmap to build out other elements of your structured hiring plan.

### Identifying candidate skills, traits and qualifications

Once the role and objectives are defined, use that list to map out the skills, traits, and qualifications a candidate will need to have in order to be successful. We think of skills as well-defined abilities, e.g. knowledge of a particular type of software or coding language, while traits describe someone’s personality, e.g. action-oriented or team player. Qualifications and experience are attributes like degrees, certificates, or particular career milestones.

Feel free to use the table below as a possible template when mapping skills, traits, and qualifications:

Role | Objective  | Attributes  
---|---|---  
Manage a team of sales people | Support sales team to outperform sales goals | Proven success managing team of multiple sales people   
Sets sales strategy for the region | Optimize sales strategy and conversion rates (QoQ) | Demonstrated ability to improve sales pipeline efficiency  
Optimizes sales process | Diagnose process bottlenecks, create action plan  
  
In the case of more complicated or unusual jobs, we recommend that your Hiring Team reconvene at the beginning of the Sourcing process to review a few profiles together. This will help ensure that everyone on the Hiring Team is aligned about what potential candidates look like.

### Dividing hiring team roles and responsibilities

Division of responsibilities makes the hiring process more efficient. Use the kick-off meeting to allocate the various responsibilities of the hiring process to members of the Hiring Team. Generally, a Recruiter guides the overall hiring process and creates the structure for success, while the Hiring Manager works as the subject matter expert (SME) for the role. As an SME, the Hiring Manager will be tasked with providing feedback and creating the technical and/or job-specific pieces of the interview.

Below is the typical division of labor between a Recruiter and a Hiring Manager. Feel free to use or amend the table to suit your Hiring Team.

Recruiter | Hiring Manager  
---|---  
Builds scorecard | Provides feedback on all drafts and candidate profiles  
Designs interview process | Writes technical pieces of interview: e.g. take-home exercise, code review, finance-specific behavioral questions  
Drafts interview questions  
Drafts outreach list  
  
### Additional resources

For more information about the role kick-off meeting, download the guides attached to this article. Based on your screen size, this may appear at the bottom or on the top right side of the page.

# How do I use Quick Select?

**Permissions:** Job Admin, who can add users to their assigned jobs, and Site Admins

**Product tier:** Available for Plus and Pro subscription tiers

Quick Select is a feature that allows you to search for specific users by name or email address, select the users, and then complete a bulk action to [assign job-based permissions](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/207334246) to the group of users.

In this article, we will discuss how to search for users manually by name within the Quick Select feature, as well as how to paste a list of users from another source into Quick Select.

In this article

  * Search for users with Quick Select
  * Paste a list of users to Quick Select



### Search for users with Quick Select

Navigate to the _Users_ page and click **Bulk Actions**. _(**Configure** > **Users** > **Bulk Actions**) _

Click **Quick Select**.

Type in the name of the first user you wish to edit. Select the user's name from the list when it appears. Repeat this process to add all users whose permissions you wish to edit in your bulk action.

**Note:** Quick Select's type-to-search functionality / manual entry supports searching by user name only. If you prefer to search for users by email address, the email address must be copied from an external source, then pasted into the **Search for users to select** field.

When you are finished adding users, click **Edit Selected (#)** at the bottom of the _Quick Select_ dialog window.

Continue with your Bulk Action.

### Paste a list of users to Quick Select

You can copy and paste a list of users or email addresses to automatically choose them in the Quick Select Window. This functionality can be useful if you have a list of names or email addresses already outside of Greenhouse Recruiting (such as in an _.xlsx_ or _.docx_ file) which all require the same permissions update.

**Note:** If any names or email addresses are entered which do not match existing users in your Greenhouse Recruiting instance, those values will be skipped during the Bulk Action.

# Enable job notifications for multiple jobs

**Permissions:** **Job** **Admin** and above

**Product tier:** Available for new subscription tiers (Core, Plus, and Pro)

Job notifications automatically update configured users on recent actions that have occurred for a particular job. Users can be added to the notification list for job events across multiple jobs based on the following criteria:

  * A user can only add other users to the notification list on jobs where they (the adding user) have Job Admin permission levels or above
  * Added users to the notification list must also have Job Admin permission levels or above on the job



Job notifications are sent via email and can be configured for the following events that occur for a job:

**Job Event** |  **Description**  
---|---  
[Weekly recruiting report](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360016456671-Weekly-Recruiting-Report) | A weekly email that summarizes the week's recruiting activity for the job.  
[New applicants](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360028659832) | An email is generated for each new candidate that applies to the job.  
[New internal applicants](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360028978271) | An email is generated for each new internal applicant to the job.  
[New referrals](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360029035211) | An email is generated for each referral submitted to the job.  
[New agency submissions](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360028757892) | An email is generated for each new agency submission to the job.  
[Stage transitions](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360029079151) | An email is generated when candidates enter into stages configured for notifications.  
[New scorecards](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360029087331) | An email is generated when interviewer scorecards are submitted for stages configured for notifications.  
  
_**Note:**[Stage transition](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360029079151) and [new scorecard](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360029087331) notifications can be enabled on a per-job basis only. _

To enable notifications across multiple jobs, click the **Configure** icon  on your navigation bar and select **Notifications** from the left.

On the _Notifications_ page, select the _Set Notifications by_ option for **User**.

Navigate to a user from the subsequent list and click **Edit** to the right of **# jobs** inline with the user's name.

From the subsequent dialog box, click **Turn all on** inline with any job event. The user will be added to the notification list for all jobs where you have Job Admin level permissions or above.

Click **Done** when finished.

Repeat as necessary for other job events and other users.

# Add candidate to another job

**Permissions:** Job Admins and Site Admins

**Product tier:** Available for new subscription tiers (Core, Plus, and Pro)

Greenhouse Recruiting allows your organization to add an existing candidate to another job's pipeline. This process would essentially create a separate application for a new job alongside the original job. In this case, your organization would retain all historical data on the original job and the candidate would progress through the interview plan for both jobs simultaneously.

_**Note** : Adding a candidate to another job should not be confused with _[_transferring a candidate_](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360031249311) _to a different job._[_Click here_](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/115002867346) _for more information._

To add a candidate to another job, open their profile and click **Add or transfer** in the top right corner of the page and choose **Add candidate to another job** from the menu.

Select the new job and stage from the pop-up window. When you're done, click **Next**.

_**Note** : Candidates can only be added to a job where the user has appropriate permissions._

**Tip:** Any Job Admin can add a candidate to another job. The **can view and edit candidates and prospects** permission is only required to view the candidate's profile on the new job after adding them.

Select the checkbox next to any documents that should be attached to the candidate's record new job. When you're finished, click **Add** to finalize the change.
