# LinkedIn Limited Listings

**Permissions:** Site Admin

**Product tier:** Available for new subscription tiers (Core, Plus, and Pro)

Your organization can post jobs from your job board to LinkedIn for free using LinkedIn Limited Listings. While these free job ads won't appear as prominently as ads purchased directly through LinkedIn's paid ads, they can help expand your reach and allow you to access more candidates at no additional cost to your organization.

Unlike other free external job boards such as Indeed, which are enabled on a per-job basis through the job post, LinkedIn Limited Listings are handled at the organization level in Greenhouse Recruiting. LinkedIn Limited Listings posts will either be on or off for every job that's currently live on your job board.

On **January 1, 2026** LinkedIn will require all LinkedIn Limited listings include a company email address.

#### In this article

  * Enable LinkedIn Limited Listings
  * Add your company email address
  * General considerations
    * Job post details
    * Visibility
    * Reporting
    * Job post locations
    * Pay ranges



### Enable LinkedIn Limited Listings

Greenhouse Recruiting needs your organization's LinkedIn company ID to associate posted jobs with your organization on LinkedIn Limited Listings.

**Tip** : Follow the steps in [this article](https://www.linkedin.com/help/linkedin/answer/a415420/associating-your-linkedin-company-id-with-the-linkedin-job-board-frequently-asked-questions?lang=en) to find your organization's LinkedIn company ID.

With your LinkedIn company ID, you're ready to enable LinkedIn. Log in to Greenhouse Recruiting, and click the **Configure** icon  on your navigation bar.

Click **Job Boards** **& Posts** on the left.

Locate the job board on which you wish to enable LinkedIn Limited Listings, and click the **Ellipsis **icon next to the job board. Click **Edit Board Settings** from the dropdown.

**Note** : If you want to enable LinkedIn Limited Listings for multiple job boards, repeat these instructions for each job board.

Scroll to _Turn on Limited Listings on LinkedIn_ and click **Yes**.

Paste your [organization's LinkedIn ID](https://www.linkedin.com/help/linkedin/answer/a415420/associating-your-linkedin-company-id-with-the-linkedin-job-board-frequently-asked-questions?lang=en) in the _Company ID_ field. This ensures your LinkedIn job posts are associated with your organization.

When finished, click **Save** at the bottom of the page.

Any candidates who apply through a link on one of your LinkedIn Limited Listings posts will be added to Greenhouse Recruiting with the source LinkedIn Limited Listing.

**Tip** : To use tracking links on LinkedIn, check out [Create a tracking link for a single job post](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/4405093302427).

### Add your company email address

LinkedIn now requires organizations using Limited Listings add a company email address. To add an email address, go to **Configure** > **Job boards and post.** Scroll to "Global Partner Settings."  
  
Add a company email address to the "XML feed company email" field. Then click "Submit."

### General considerations

There are some important distinctions between LinkedIn paid ads and LinkedIn Limited Listings with Greenhouse Recruiting:

#### Job details

LinkedIn Limited Listings uses an algorithm to review your job posts and generate a high-level _Job Details_ section, which is displayed next to each of your Limited Listings posts. This section includes auto-generated settings like the following:

  * Seniority level
  * Industry
  * Employment type (Full-time, part-time, contract)
  * Job functions



Job details are auto-generated by LinkedIn and can't be edited in Greenhouse Recruiting. If the job details added to your LinkedIn Limited Listings are incorrect, reach out to LinkedIn support directly for assistance.

#### Visibility

LinkedIn Limited Listings only appear through LinkedIn's search after relevant paid LinkedIn paid job slots and ads.

Additionally, Limited Listings don't appear in recommendations on LinkedIn. This means LinkedIn Limited Listings are visible only to the subset of LinkedIn members who are actively searching for jobs.

Limited Listings can't be sponsored across LinkedIn. If you're interested in flexible paid posts, check out [LinkedIn job wrapping](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/205423745).

#### Reporting

If you post jobs to LinkedIn Limited Listings, you won't have access to LinkedIn job analytics, suggested matches, people who have viewed the job, or other special LinkedIn data analyses. Consider [Greenhouse Recruiting reports](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360034704071) instead.

#### Job post locations

At least one location must be provided in order to publish a job post to LinkedIn Limited, including for remote positions. Your job post won't save in Greenhouse Recruiting without a valid location entered, even with remote job post enabled. Remote jobs can be indicated using the **Work type** field in the _Post details_ section at the top of the page.

If you're posting a remote job, flexible job, or job with multiple locations, add **Searchable locations**. You can add up to seven locations. For remote roles, Searchable locations can be added at the city or country level. When job seekers search a location on LinkedIn, your job post will be surfaced in the results. **Searchable locations** don't appear on your job post.

**Tip** : Learn more about [remote job posts](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360043197972) on Greenhouse Recruiting.

#### Pay ranges

If your job post doesn't include a pay range, LinkedIn may provide an estimated pay range for your job post. To avoid automatic salary estimates on third-party job boards, use Greenhouse Recruiting's [pay transparency](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/13304010418075) to add pay ranges to your job post.

**Learn more**

[Use LinkedIn with Greenhouse Recruiting](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/115003795152)

[LinkedIn Easy Apply integration](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/115005389566)

[Applicant source tracking for LinkedIn job wrapping](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/205423745)

# Recruiting.com integration

With this integration, users can automatically push open requisitions from Greenhouse Recruiting to Recruiting.com career site and social media. Candidates will be redirected back to the Greenhouse application to apply.

#### In this article

  * Configure the Recruiting.com integration
  * Typical career site implementation timeline
  * Recruiting.com integration FAQs



### Configure the Recruiting.com integration

To set up the integration, users need to provide Recruiting.com with a link to a current job post.

The Recruiting.com team will then create a scrape, which takes approximately 3-5 business days. The scrape is built into the overall career site implementation timeline.

### Typical career site implementation timeline

The career site build process timeline is based on your organization's availability to approve the mock, wireframe, and demo site in the time allotted. Any amount of time over the allotted feedback period will result in a delay of at least one business day for each day the deadline is missed.

  * Day 1: Kick-off Call
  * Day 5: Client delivers assets
  * Day 10: All content complete for mock/wireframes
  * Day 14: Mock and wireframes complete
  * Day 15: Mock presentation
  * Day 17: Client approval of mock
  * Day 23: Demo site presentation
  * Day 25: Client approval of demo site
  * Day 28: Site versioned and ready for launch



### Recruiting.com integration FAQs

**What is Job Scraping?**

The Recruiting.com job scrape periodically crawls the job listings in the client’s Greenhouse ATS, recreates the job listings, and then posts them as separate pages on their career site. To put it more simply, job scraping is the process of copying the job listings within Greenhouse and posting them on their career site.

**If I make changes to the jobs in Greenhouse Recruiting, when will the career site reflect these changes?**

The changes will be reflected on the career site as soon as the next scrape occurs, which is dependent on the frequency of the scrape.

**How does job scraping change where a client posts their jobs?**

Clients would still post their jobs in Greenhouse Recruiting as usual. If the job postings show locations and categories through Greenhouse Recruiting, they will be mirrored on the career site.

To learn more about the benefits of job scraping, read our resource page [here](https://www.recruiting.com/product-help/how-the-recruiting-com-job-scrape-works-with-your-ats) or contact our Recruiting.com team at partnerships@recruiting.com.

# Edit an approval process for a specific job

**Permissions:** Site Admin who can see private notes and salary info, manage offers, approve jobs/offers, and create and override default approvals, and Job Admin who can view and edit offers, approve/request approval on offers, and who can edit offer approvals

**Permissions:** Site Admin, and Job Admin who can edit forms

**Product tier:** Available for new subscription tiers (Core, Plus, and Pro)

# My interview disappeared from Greenhouse Recruiting

If interviews have disappeared from Greenhouse Recruiting but still appear on your calendar and the candidate’s activity feed, information may be missing from the calendar event.

Try any of the steps below to re-sync Greenhouse Recruiting with your calendar.

#### In this article

  * Is the Greenhouse Recruiting calendar email included on the event?
  * Is the interview kit link in the body of the event?
  * Did you make changes to the event in your calendar, but didn’t send updates to all attendees?
  * Additional resources



### Is the Greenhouse Recruiting calendar email address included on the event?

When you schedule an interview through Greenhouse Recruiting, the calendar event automatically includes a unique [calendar email address](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360050154551) to keep your event synced with Greenhouse Recruiting.

Removing the calendar email address from your event may cause it to un-sync and disappear from a candidate’s profile.

To re-sync your calendar with Greenhouse Recruiting, find [your organization’s calendar email address](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360050154551) and add it to the event on your calendar. When you save the event, make sure to send the update to all attendees.

**Note** : A Greenhouse Recruiting calendar email address is **_schedule@[plant name].greenhouse.io_.** For example, _schedule@iris.greenhouse.io_ is a calendar email address.

The scheduling email address is customized for your specific configuration. To find your calendar email address, visit [Identify your organization's calendar email address.](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360050154551)

### Is the interview kit link in the body of the event?

When you schedule an interview through Greenhouse Recruiting, an [interview kit](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/115002226826) link is automatically generated in the body of the calendar event. This link is tied to the specific interview stage, interviewers, and candidates.

Any changes to this link – including removing it – can cause the event to un-sync and disappear from Greenhouse Recruiting.

To re-sync your calendar with Greenhouse Recruiting, add the interview kit link to the body of your calendar event. When you save the event, make sure to send the update to all attendees.

### Did you make changes to the event in your calendar, but didn’t send updates to all attendees?

Any changes to the time, date, or attendee details must be saved and sent to all attendees. 

To correct this, make a small update to the body of the event, such as adding extra punctuation or minor text, then save your change and choose to send the update to all attendees. Make sure the Greenhouse Recruiting calendar email address is listed as an attendee on the event.

The changes you made to your calendar event should sync and your event should appear on both your calendar and in Greenhouse Recruiting.

**Note** : Once an event is scheduled, you cannot move it to a new calendar. For example if you were to move an event from John’s calendar to Suleika’s calendar, the event may not sync with Greenhouse Recruiting.

If you need to move a scheduled interview to a new calendar, it’s best to delete the scheduled interview and create a new one through Greenhouse Recruiting.

If your event is still not syncing after you've tried these steps, reach out to [Greenhouse Technical Support](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360044626412-Greenhouse-Support-operating-hours).

### Additional resources

  * [Schedule an interview](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360045420091)
  * [Schedule interview to personal calendar (Google Calendar)](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360022018271)
  * [Outlook 365 integration](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/115003943972)
  * [Why didn't the interview I scheduled show up in Greenhouse Recruiting?](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/200241979)
  * [Identify your organization's calendar email address](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360050154551)

# 'Your next steps' email

**Permissions:** Owners and Coordinators

**Product tier:** Available for the Greenhouse Welcome and Greenhouse Onboarding subscription tiers

The 'Your next steps' email is a follow-up email sent from Greenhouse Onboarding to a new hire after they've been assigned an [onboarding plan](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360000683352). In this email, new hires will receive a summary of any tasks or E-Signature documents that need their attention.

**Note:** Learn more about [setting the delivery schedule](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360027921091) for your organization's 'Your next steps' email.

#### In this article

  * Default 'Your next steps' email sections
  * Edit the default 'Your next steps' email
  * Customize the 'Your next steps' email
  * Additional resources



### Default 'Your next steps' email sections

When new hires receive a 'Your next steps' email, they'll see the following core sections:

Section title | Section info  
---|---  
Get Started button | New hires can click this button to navigate to Greenhouse Onboarding.  
Documents Awaiting Your Signature | Any e-signature documents assigned to your new hire will appear here.  
Upcoming Tasks to Complete | Any upcoming onboarding tasks that require attention will appear here.   
Your Manager | The new hire's direct manager and title.  
Your Department | The new hire's department.  
Your Location | The new hire's work location.  
  
**Note:** Upcoming Tasks to Complete are [tasks with assign dates](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360000525691) on or before the scheduled delivery date of the 'Your next steps' email. This section will not appear for tasks with an assign date beyond the 'Your next steps' delivery date.

### Edit the default 'Your next steps' email

Learn more about editing the default 'Your next steps' email and configuring your email's delivery with the following resources:

  * [Edit the 'Your next steps' email template](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360020389632)
  * [Configure 'Your next steps' email delivery schedule](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360027921091)



### Customize the 'Your next steps' email

Your organization can create custom variations of the default 'Your next steps' email to personalize them for new hires with different locations, departments, employment statuses, or other criteria. New hires will receive a custom 'Your next steps' variation instead of the default email if they match the applied filter criteria.

To create a new 'Your next steps' email, navigate to **Settings** > **Onboarding Plan** > **Emails**.

Scroll to _Your next steps_ and click **Create template**.

Use the email template editor to set up the following:

  * Publish or turn off your new email variation
  * Name your template
  * Add a subject line
  * Build your email message
  * Assign new hire filter criteria



**Note:** Make sure each 'Your next steps' email variation has **match criteria** applied to filter for specific new hires. This ensures that the correct email variation will reach new hires with matching locations, departments, employment statuses, or other criteria.

When you're done, click **Save and Close**.

Your organization's new 'Your next steps' email will be sent to any new hires who fulfill the criteria you've selected.

### Additional resources

  * [Edit the 'Your next steps' email template](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360020389632)
  * [Configure 'Your next steps' email delivery schedule](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360027921091)

# AssureHire integration

AssureHire leads the industry in technology and automation, resulting in the fastest end-to-end background screening, verifications, and drug testing experience.

Greenhouse Recruiting's integration with AssureHire makes it simple to manage the entire screening process in one system: submit background check orders, send candidate screening invites, track progress, view reports, and even initiate adverse action.

#### In this article

  * Set up the AssureHire integration
    * Configure custom options
    * Create a Harvest API key
    * Create a webhook and complete setup
  * Use the AssureHire integration
    * Track status of background check order
    * View final background check report
  * Additional resources



### Set up the AssureHire integration

#### Configure custom options

To configure the AssureHire integration, you'll need to add both a [custom candidate field](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/202609675) and a [custom job field](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/202609855) in Greenhouse Recruiting.

**Note** : To configure custom options in Greenhouse Recruiting, you'll need to be a **Site** **Admin** or **Job** **Admin** with the [additional user-specific permission](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360020855632) '**Can manage custom fields** '.

#### Add a custom candidate field

To add a custom candidate field for the AssureHire integration, click **Configure** and select **Custom** **Options** from the left-hand panel. Under _Company custom fields_ , select **Candidates** and then, click **Add field**.

Make the following selections on your new custom candidate field:

  * **Field** **Name** : Background Report
  * **Description** : Background Report
  * **Type** : URL Field



When finished, click **Save**.

#### Add a custom job field

To add a custom job field for the AssureHire integration, click **Configure** and select **Custom** **Options** from the left-hand panel. Under _Company custom fields_ , select **Jobs** and then, click **Add field**.

Make the following selections on your new custom job field:

  * **Field** **Name** : Background Package
  * **Description** Background Package
  * **Type** : Single select



**Note** : Be sure to add background check packages to the _Options_ field with each package separated by a line break.

When finished, click **Save**.

#### Create a Harvest API key

Next, you’ll need to create a Harvest API key for the AssureHire integration.

Follow the steps in [ this article](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/5888163769883) to create the key, and verify that the permissions below are selected when configuring the AssureHire integration.

#### Credentials

In the _Create New Credential_ dialog box, make the following selections:

  * **API Type** : Harvest
  * **Partner** : AssureHire
  * **Description** : AssureHire Harvest API Key



#### Permissions

Verify the following permissions are selected for the AssureHire integration:

**Candidates**

  * GET: Retrieve candidate
  * GET: List candidates
  * POST: Add note



**Users**

  * GET: Retrieve user
  * GET: List users



**Activity Feed**

  * GET: Retrieve activity feed



**Custom Field Options**

  * GET: Custom field options
  * POST: Create custom field options
  * PATCH: Update custom field options



When finished, click **Save**.

Your Harvest API key for the AssureHire integration is created and configured.

Provide your Harvest API key to your [AssureHire onboarding team](https://assurehire.com/signin) so they can finish setting up the integration.

#### Create a webhook

Next, you'll need to create a webhook for the AssureHire integration. Follow the steps in [ this article](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/5888163727003) to create your webhook.

**Note** : Greenhouse Recruiting will need two pieces of information to setup a new webhook for your AssureHire integration: the AssureHire's Endpoint URL and AssureHire's Secret Key. 

To retrieve this information, [contact AssureHire Support](https://support@assurehire.com) and include the following subject line:

  * Greenhouse Endpoint URL & Secret Key Request: [YOUR COMPANY NAME]



Once you receive the AssureHire Endpoint URL and Secret Key, you can create a new webhook. Use the values listed below to configure the webhook:

  * **Name** : AssureHire Integration
  * **When** : Candidate has changed
  * **Endpoint URL** : https://assurehire.com/partners/greenhouse/webhook
  * **Secret Key** : `Enter the Secret Key provided by AssureHire Support`



When finished, click **Create webhook**.

The AssureHire integration is now configured and ready for use. 

### Use the AssureHire integration

#### Submit background check order

When candidates are moved into the **Offer** stage, a background check order will automatically trigger from AssureHire.

If a candidate is not in an **Offer** stage, the background check order has not been initiated yet.

#### Track status of background check order

Once you've moved the candidate into the **Offer** stage, the background check is automatically ordered. You can track the status of the background check by clicking the **Activity Feed** on the candidate profile in Greenhouse Recruiting.

To view the status of a background check, click the link in the **Activity** **Feed** note from AssureHire.

#### View final background check report

Once a background check report is completed, AssureHire will send you an email notification with a link to click on the final report.

AssureHire also posts a status update in the candidate's **Activity Feed** with a link that when clicked will allow you to view the final background check report as well.

The completed background check report is also attached to the candidate's **Details** tab in Greenhouse Recruiting.

Click the AssureHire URL below _Background_ _Report_ to view the final report in AssureHire.

### Additional resources

For information not covered here, reach out to AssureHire Support at [support@assurehire.com](mailto:support@assurehire.com).

# join.com integration

join.com's integration with Greenhouse Recruiting allows your organization to sync your jobs to join.com and import candidates to Greenhouse Recruiting.

#### In this article

  * Set up the integration
    * Retrieve a user ID
    * Create a Harvest API key
    * (Optional) Create a custom field for sourcing
    * Enable the integration
  * Use the integration
  * Additional resources



### Set up the join.com integration

#### Retrieve a user ID

join.com requires a Greenhouse Recruiting user ID to associate with the integration requests. It's recommended to create a new [integration system user (ISU)](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/4405511253659) in Greenhouse Recruiting specifically for the integration. However, you can also [find an existing user ID](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/10765948752027) to authenticate the integration requests.

Copy the user ID for use in a later step.

#### Create a Harvest API key

Next, create a Harvest API key. Follow the steps in [this article](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/5888163769883) to create the key. In the _Create New Credential_ box, make the following selections:

  * **API type:** Harvest
  * **Partner:** join.com
  * **Description:** join.com Harvest API key



Verify that the following permissions are selected for the join.com integration:

**Applications**

  * Select all



**Candidates**

  * Select all



**Custom fields**

  * Select all



**Sources**

  * Select all



#### (Optional) Create a custom candidate field for a secondary source

If you'd like to have the original source of the candidate displayed in Greenhouse Recruiting, your organization can create a custom candidate field to capture the platform from which the candidate originated — for instance Indeed or LinkedIn.

**Note** : To create a custom candidate field, you'll need to be a Site Admin or Job Admin who can manage company metadata.

To use secondary sources, [create a custom candidate field](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/202609675) and use the following settings:

  * **Field name** : Join original source
  * **Field type** : Short textbox



After you create the custom candidate field, Greenhouse Recruiting will generate an immutable field key:

Copy the immutable field key for use in a later step.

#### Enable the integration

Enable the integration on [join.com](http://join.com/) by navigating to [**Settings** > **Integrations**](https://join.com/company/integrations). Enter the information copied in the previous steps.

### Use the integration

After setup and enablement of the integration, it can take 1 — 2 working days for all jobs to be indexed on [join.com](http://join.com/) and for the first applications to be sent to Greenhouse Recruiting.

To avoid duplicate applications in Greenhouse Recruiting, only new applications are imported. If you still have applications on join.com that you would like to send to Greenhouse Recruiting, use the export functionality on join.com.

Once the integration is enabled:

  * Your jobs will be synchronized once a day, meaning that new jobs will be created and old jobs will be archived automatically. You're free to create additional jobs or edit the existing jobs on join.com.
  * New candidates that apply on join.com will be sent to Greenhouse Recruiting at the time of application and will be updated if the candidate uploads more information.
  * Candidates received previously will not be sent to Greenhouse Recruiting to avoid duplication. If you want older candidates to be available on Greenhouse Recruiting, you can export them on join.com.
  * If a candidate applies to multiple positions, the candidates won't be duplicated in Greenhouse Recruiting.



### Additional resources

Email [contact@join.com](mailto:contact@join.com) or reach out to your join.com account manager for help troubleshooting the integration.

# Cloudtalk integration

CloudTalk is an AI business calling software for recruitment teams.

CloudTalk is a cloud-based business phone system built for teams that handle a high volume of calls and need seamless hiring workflows. Designed for fast-growing SMBs, Cloudtalk is empowering recruitment and staffing agencies—as well as internal talent teams in startups and enterprises—to connect with candidates faster, track every conversation automatically, and scale outreach without sacrificing call quality or data accuracy.

Cloudtalk’s integration with Greenhouse Recruiting enables users to make and receive calls, send SMS, and log every candidate interaction automatically in Greenhouse to streamline your hiring workflows and improve efficiency.

#### In this article

  * Create a Harvest API Key
  * Set up the Cloudtalk integration
  * Use the Cloudtalk integration
  * Additional resources



### Create a Harvest API Key

To configure the integration, you’ll need to create a Harvest API key.

Follow the steps in [this article](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/5888163769883) to create the key, and verify that the permissions below are selected when configuring the CloudTalk integration.

#### Credentials

In the _Create New Credential_ box, make the following selections:

  * **API Type:** Harvest
  * **Partner:** CloudTalk or Unlisted Vendor
  * **Description:** CloudTalk Harvest API Key



#### Permissions

Verify that the following permissions are selected for the CloudTalk integration:

  * GET: Retrieve Candidate
  * GET: List Candidates
  * POST: Add Note
  * GET: List Users



These permissions are required to allow CloudTalk to display candidates, log call activity, and associate notes with the correct users in Greenhouse.

### Set up the Cloudtalk integration

To set up the integration, go to your CloudTalk Dashboard:

  1. Navigate to Account > Integrations
  2. Find Greenhouse and click + Add  
  
[](https://downloads.intercomcdn.com/i/o/keho9m4r/1654388302/a5494bf21f5364b7ad5bdc335af8/Screenshot+2025-08-05+at+11_28_19.png?expires=1754524800&signature=dc2615514b8801b01c739ae33fddde598995f6d5e4e4ff254f1314e25dc6022a&req=dSYiEsp2lYJfW%2FMW3nq%2BgcGbUb4C4Jsyaxh7QFc1o762uHaLEN1bySW05ufi%0AF%2BBnXfmrEjbetVAANzNzFNqOOJo%3D%0A)



You’ll be asked to provide the following:

  * Your authentication name
  * Harvest v1/v2 API Key
  * Greenhouse Subdomain
    * This is the first part of your Greenhouse URL.
    * E.g. app2.greenhouse.io → Subdomain = app2



4\. After filling in the details, click **Create**.

Once credentials are submitted:

  * You must toggle the Integration Status to Active manually before saving
  * You can add a Caption (name of the integration instance)
  * You can apply a Contact tag to synced candidates in CloudTalk
  * Select which numbers should be used for calls and SMS



### Use the Cloudtalk integration

When the Greenhouse integration is configured, CloudTalk automatically syncs candidate records and logs communication activities between the two platforms.

#### Candidate synchronisation

  * Initial import: Candidate records from Greenhouse are pulled into CloudTalk with first name, last name, email, and phone number.
  * Ongoing updates: Any updates to candidate details in Greenhouse are reflected in CloudTalk, including the Created timestamp on new records.
  * No deletions: Removing a candidate in Greenhouse does not delete them in CloudTalk.
  * Job listing behaviour: Each candidate is linked to one main job listing. If they are registered for a second job on a new candidate profile, CloudTalk will import it separately.
  * Fields available in CloudTalk: For the main job listing, CloudTalk surfaces the link to the ATS listing and the applicant’s current stage.



#### Contact export

When contacts are created or updated in CloudTalk, the integration can export the contact with the following fields to Greenhouse: ID, First Name, Last Name, Email, Phone, Applications.

#### Call activity

After each call, CloudTalk adds a Note on the candidate. The note includes:

  * CloudTalk number
  * Caller’s number
  * Duration
  * Tags
  * Notes
  * Recording link



_All the CloudTalk Phone Call Activity will appear in the Contact Activity as a structured Note_

#### SMS activity export

All inbound and outbound SMS messages sent through CloudTalk are logged to the candidate’s activity history in Greenhouse and linked to their primary job listing whenever possible.

_All the CloudTalk SMS Activity will appear in the Contact Activity Feed as a Note_

### Additional resources

For additional information or troubleshooting not covered here, reach out to support@cloudtalk.io

Learn more

  * [How to Configure Cloudtalk <> Greenhouse integration](https://help.cloudtalk.io/en/articles/11937842-configure-greenhouse)
  * [How to use Cloudtalk <> Greenhouse integration](https://help.cloudtalk.io/en/articles/11938372-how-to-use-cloudtalk-with-greenhouse)

# Offer forecast overview

**Permissions:** Job Admin and above

**Product tier:** Available for new subscription tiers (Core, Plus, and Pro)

Offer forecast uses machine learning from the recruiting process to make a prediction for each job about when an offer might be accepted and when a new hire's start date might begin. Use offer forecast to hone your recruiting pipeline, communicate timelines, and engage your team towards a common goal.

#### In this article

  * [Feature highlights](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/115005312666#h_01HA4XR7W3K9BXC8JK0J9D55ZB)
  * [Get started](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/115005312666#h_01HA4XR7W38PXW7EVHY2JGG39C)



### Feature highlights

#### A new, more accurate machine learning model

Previously known as Greenhouse Predicts, offer forecast has been revamped with a new name, a new look, and a new, more accurate model. Offer forecast is now powered by an ensemble machine learning model trained on historical metadata, including millions of applications across hundreds of thousands of filled jobs.

By training offer forecast on huge amounts of data, we’ve built a more accurate forecast you can trust to communicate timelines. **[Learn more](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360002797252)**.

#### Make more informed decisions

One of the biggest challenges for recruiting teams is accurately predicting when a role will be filled. Offer forecast helps by predicting candidate offer acceptance and new hire start dates, allowing teams to more easily strategize, make informed decisions, and effectively communicate timelines.

### Get started

To get started, navigate to a job in Greenhouse Recruiting. Offer forecast appears as a pane on the right side of the job dashboard.

**Note** : The start date prediction in the offer forecast widget is not yet available for customers in Silo 101. **[Learn more](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360002798612#h_01HD4R5TYF4QM90PNJ7H54N909)**.

Set a target start date for your job opening, and offer forecast will project an anticipated offer acceptance date, as well as a predicted start date for the new hire.

Learn more about [how to use offer forecast](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/18710896459163).

**Learn more**

[Use offer forecast](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/18710896459163)

[How offer forecast works](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360002797252)

**Note** : If you would like to sync an external email thread back to the candidate’s Activity Feed, we recommend using either the [Greenhouse Gmail add-on](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360003111031-Greenhouse-for-Gmail-Google-Add-on-) or [Maildrop](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/201990630-Maildrop).

Greenhouse Recruiting's FlyOnTheWall feature allows your [hiring team](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/115002194983-Hiring-Team-Overview) to discuss a candidate over external email while logging the email thread in the candidate's **Activity Feed**.

When you use the **Email the Team** option on a candidate profile or [@mention](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360013153651--mentions) team members on a [candidate note](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360031123652), Greenhouse Recruiting automatically CCs the appropriate FlyOnTheWall email address onto the email message and adds a unique token to the signature of the message. This token tells Greenhouse Recruiting which candidate should be associated with messages in this email thread.

### FlyOnTheWall email address and token

The appropriate FlyOnTheWall email address and token are automatically attached to the generated email when using the **Email the Team** or **@mention** features. The token appears at the bottom of the generated email.

FlyOnTheWall requires the original team email message to be initiated from the candidate’s profile in Greenhouse Recruiting so we can add the unique token. If you email the hiring team from outside of Greenhouse Recruiting and later copy the FlyOnTheWall email address to the thread, the messages will not be matched to a candidate due to the lack of an assigned token.

As long as the team continues to include the FlyOnTheWall email address in the CC of the email thread and keeps the unique token in every message, all emails in the thread will be saved to the candidate’s **Activity Feed**.

# Feedback questions

**Permissions:** Coordinators and Owners

**Product tier:** Available for Greenhouse Welcome and Greenhouse Onboarding subscription tiers

Use the feedback feature in Greenhouse Onboarding to survey new hires about their onboarding experience and assess how successful your onboarding program is.

Greenhouse Onboarding provides default feedback questions that will automatically be sent to your new hires once the [feedback feature is enabled](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/115003877872). You can create new feedback questions at any time, as well as edit and delete existing feedback questions.

#### In this article

  * Create new feedback questions
  * Edit a feedback question
  * Delete a feedback question
  * Additional resources



### Create new feedback questions

To create a new feedback question, click **Settings** on your homepage navigation bar.

Select **Feedback** from the left panel of the  _Settings_ page.

On the  _Onboarding Feedback_ page, click **Add a Question**.

In the _New Feedback Question_ window, enter your new feedback question in the **Question to ask new hire** field.

Select a time to send this question to new hires. Choose from the following options:

  * **On Start Date** – send this question to new hires on their start date
  * **Custom** – specify how many days after the start date to send this question to new hires



Use the following optional filters to send feedback questions to a specific set of new hires instead of all new hires from your organization:

  * Department matches – send this question to new hires from a specific department
  * Location matches – send this question to new hires in a specific location
  * Employment status matches – send this question to new hires with a specific employment status
  * Other criteria matches – send this question to new hires with specific other criteria applied



**Note:** You can make multiple selections for each filter.

You can also choose to notify specific users in your organization when new hires answer this feedback question. Select to notify users with a custom role, such as Manager, Mentor, or Onboarding Coordinator, or select specific Greenhouse Onboarding users.

**Note:** You can select multiple recipients to receive notifications when this question is answered.

When you're done, click **Save and Create Another** to configure another custom feedback question or click **Save and Close** to save this question and return to the _Onboarding Feedback_ __ page.

### Edit a feedback question

To edit an existing feedback question, click to select it from the list of questions on the _Onboarding Feedback_ page.

In the _Edit Feedback Question_ window, you can edit the following fields:

  * Question to ask new hire
  * When should this question be asked?
  * Applies to new hires whose (Department matches, Location matches, Employment Status matches, Other Criteria matches)
  * Who should be notified when this is answered?



Click **Save and Close** when you're done editing the feedback question.

### Delete a feedback question

To delete an existing feedback question, click to select it from the list of questions on the _Onboarding Feedback_ page.

Click **Delete** in the _Edit Feedback Window_. Click **Yes, delete it** to confirm that you'd like to delete this question.

**Note** : Deleting a feedback question is a permanent action that cannot be undone.

### Additional resources

  * [Feedback overview](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/115003877872)
  * [Feedback: New hire perspective](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/115003848871)
  * [Feedback: Notification of responses](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/115003863711)
  * [Feedback reports](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/115003862472)

# Custom user fields overview

Custom user fields are a type of custom option that allow you to add your own unique labels to user profiles. Custom user fields give you more control over how you categorize your users and assign user permissions.

**Example:** Imagine your organization introduced a policy that only users who are Directors should be assigned as hiring managers on jobs in Greenhouse Recruiting.

You could add a custom user field for "Seniority" and include "Director" as an option. After assigning the value of "Director" to the appropriate users, you could then filter by "Director" on the _Users_ page. You could then use bulk editing to change that user's permissions to **Job Admin: Hiring Manager** on their assigned jobs.

For a walkthrough of this feature, check out our video below:

#### In this article

  * Feature highlights
  * FAQ



### Feature highlights

#### Use current filters more intuitively

Previously, the **Department** and**Office** filters on the _Users_ page queried users based on departments and offices on jobs they were assigned to. Now, the filters are titled **User Department** and **User Office**. They'll query users based on the department and office assigned on their user profile.

**Example:** Previously, if you selected "Marketing" from the Department dropdown, the users list would show the users who have been assigned a job in the Marketing department.

Now, if you select "Marketing" from the User Department dropdown, the users list will show users who have "Marketing" selected as the User Department on their profile.

#### Create custom options for users

Add custom fields to your user profiles. Choose between single select, multi select, yes/no or user field types.

Custom user fields can be assigned, edited or removed from a user by going to the **Custom Options** section on a user's profile.

#### Use custom options as filters

Filter your users based on any of the custom user fields and values you set up. Continue to use our **Export to Excel** functionality to take additional action on your results.

### FAQ

#### Why do the User Department and User Office filters work differently now?

Based on feedback we received from customers, we adjusted the User Department and User Office filters to work more intuitively. The updated functionality gives you the power to find, filter and assign permissions to users more easily.

#### Once I create a new custom user field, where does it show up in Greenhouse Recruiting?

Once you've added at least one custom user field, you'll see a new Custom fields section on the _Edit User_ page. Each custom field will appear as a dropdown. From here, you can change the value for or remove the value for an assigned custom field.

You can also use custom user fields as filters on the _Users_ page.

#### Can I manage custom user fields in bulk?

Yes. You can manage custom fields in bulk with the [_Users_](https://developers.greenhouse.io/harvest.html#users) and [_Custom Fields_](https://developers.greenhouse.io/harvest.html#custom-fields) endpoints of our Harvest API or with [HRIS Link](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360058975731).

**Learn more about custom user fields**

[Manage custom user fields](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/7987443593499)

[Filter by custom user fields](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/8218796834459)

# Greenhouse Onboarding emails overview

**Permissions:** Owners and Coordinators

**Product tier:** Available for Greenhouse Welcome and Greenhouse Onboarding tiers

Greenhouse Onboarding provides a variety of emails that your organization can use to keep track of new and pending hires, tasks, E-Signatures, feedback, and onboarding goals. Use these email notifications to stay on top of critical onboarding activities.

#### In this article

    * Set the time zone for user-specific emails
  * Types of Greenhouse Onboarding emails  

    * New hire notifications
    * E-Signature emails
    * Feedback emails
    * Reports emails
    * Tasks emails
    * Goals emails

### Turn on Greenhouse Onboarding emails

Before you can set up any Greenhouse Onboarding emails, a user with Owner permissions first needs to [turn on emails for your organization](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360020657171).

To activate all emails, navigate to **Settings**. Select **Onboarding Plan** > **Emails** from the left panel of the _Settings_ page.

Under  _Global Settings_ , click the **toggle button** to activate **All emails for organization**.

### Email delivery time zone

#### Set the time zone for organization-wide emails

Owners can define the default time zone for your organization's email deliveries. Any active emails are sent according to your organization's set time zone.

To set your organization's default time zone, hover over the time zone listed under _Email delivery time zone_. Click the **pencil icon** to edit your time zone.

#### Set the time zone for user-specific emails

Any user-specific emails, such as task reminders, will be sent according to an individual user's timezone. You can update your personal account timezone in **Account settings**.

On the _Notification Settings_ page, click **Adjust timezone to change delivery time of email notifications** to set up your individual timezone.

**Note:** If an individual user doesn't have an assigned timezone, they'll receive emails according to the organization's timezone. 

### Types of Greenhouse Onboarding emails

# Complete your new hire goals

**Permissions:** Employees

**Product tier:** Available for Greenhouse Welcome and Greenhouse Onboarding subscription tiers

New hire goals are created by your hiring manager to provide you with a structured onboarding experience and outline key objectives specific to your role.

Unlike [tasks](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/211582023), which commonly focus on administrative actions at the organization or department level, new hire goals allow you to track your progress toward onboarding milestones and activities in one place. This creates stronger alignment between you and your hiring manager by defining what success looks like for the first 30 days in your new role.

#### In this article

  * Receive onboarding goals by email
  * Access your onboarding goals
    * Preview onboarding goals on your homepage
    * View onboarding goals in your employee profile
  * Complete your onboarding goals
    * Understand your onboarding goals
    * Update the status of your onboarding goals



### Receive onboarding goals by email

You'll receive an [email](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/12198189055387) notifying you once your manager creates and shares your 30 day onboarding goals.

Click **View my 30 Day Goals** to open your new hire goals in Greenhouse Onboarding.

**Note:** Greenhouse Onboarding sends this email when your manager manually [shares onboarding goals](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/9265706878619) from your employee profile. Reach out to your manager if you haven't received this email!

### Access your onboarding goals

You can view your new hire goals at any time directly in Greenhouse Onboarding.

#### Preview onboarding goals on your homepage

On your Greenhouse Onboarding _Home_ page, use the **My 30 day goals** widget to preview your assigned onboarding goals.

Click **Go to 30 day goals __** to open your onboarding goals in your employee profile.

#### View onboarding goals in your employee profile

Your [employee profile](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/5759718119707) is the central hub for your onboarding goals. You'll use the  _30 day goals_ tab to access full goal descriptions and update the status for each of your assigned goals.

Navigate to **Profile** from your Greenhouse Onboarding homepage. 

Click the **30 day goals** tab from your employee profile to open and update your onboarding goals.

### Complete your onboarding goals

You'll find a list of all onboarding goals assigned to you by your manager in the _30 day goals_ tab of your employee profile.

#### Understand your onboarding goals

Each onboarding goal includes a description provided by your manager. You can use these details to better understand your objective and your manager's expectations for each goal.

Click the **caret** next to any goal to expand and read the goal's description.

#### Update the status of your onboarding goals

As you work on your assigned goals, you should update each goal's status to help you and your manager track your progress.

Use the **Status** dropdown to apply any of the following statuses to your goals:

  * To do
  * In progress
  * Need help
  * Completed



**Note:** Your manager will receive an email each time you change a goal's status to **Need help**.

**Learn more about new hire goals**

# Informed hiring guide

### Your guide to making more informed, data-backed hiring decisions  


Structured hiring is the core of any strategic hiring process. When done right, it defines a clear process and enables companies to make better, data-based decisions. 

You know the basics of the process, so here are some helpful reminders to ensure you are following a defined workflow and making measurable improvements. These steps will also help you track how well you are able to make informed hiring decisions by evaluating your scorecard submission rate.

**Performance benchmark:** A scorecard submission rate of 90% or more indicates you’re effectively making informed decisions. Ensuring scorecards are regularly submitted helps your team generate the data needed to drive informed hiring decisions across the organization.

### Here’s the plan

  * **Schedule all interviews through Greenhouse**

  * **Upgrade scorecard creation and submission**

  * **Establish offer approval processes**

  * **Develop and run retrospective debriefs**




# Step 1

### Schedule all interviews through Greenhouse 

We offer a number of calendar integrations so you can practice informed hiring and centralize all scheduling through Greenhouse. This ensures you’re capturing the complete data set on interview volume, as well as preparing your hiring team with interview kits included in each meeting invitation.

Leverage any of our [scheduling integration partners](https://www.greenhouse.io/integrations?category=productivity-collaboration&q=&page=1) to help your team be as effective as possible and boost your calendar functionality 

# Step 2

### Upgrade scorecard creation and submission

Use the tools that are readily available within Greenhouse to set up scorecards more efficiently and with a focused approach. By implementing the following steps, you’ll be able to increase scorecard submission rates so you can make smarter, data-driven decisions.

  * Learn how to effectively use [job templates](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360006876232-Best-Practices-Template-Job) to create scorecards from previous roles, help drive consistency in job stages and gain better data quality 
  * Make each interview purposeful with specific [focus attributes](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360018399451-Focus-Attributes-on-Scorecards) and [custom questions](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/115002276366-Create-Custom-Questions-for-Interview-Kits) so interviewers are clear on their goals, every attribute is covered and interviews are never redundant 
  * Work with hiring managers to train interviewers, set scorecard completion goals and ensure everyone understands how submitting scorecards can help your company make better informed and more fair decisions
    * Check out the comprehensive [Learn Greenhouse course](https://learn.greenhouse.io/building-a-scorecard-1/572191) on building a scorecard



# Step 3

### Establish offer approval processes

Include all necessary stakeholders in the offer approval process for new hires so nothing slips between the cracks (applicable for Advanced/Expert packages only).

  * Read the [offer approval guide](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360035625832-Offer-Approval-Overview) to learn how to map out approval chains and create a plan for extending offers to candidates 
  * Understand how to configure your default approval process [here](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360035987291-Configure-Default-Offer-Approval), then head straight to the [app](https://app.greenhouse.io/configure/approval_flows) to get started
  * Check out this [Learn Greenhouse course](https://learn.greenhouse.io/working-with-offer-approvals) on working with offer approvals for additional guidance on scorecards



# Step 4

### Develop and run retrospective debriefs

It’s easy for a team to start conducting retrospective debriefs, and it’s the one process that can improve all your other hiring practices.

  * Create the habit of having a retrospective debrief after each job is closed to evaluate what went right and what didn’t work out the way it was intended – so you can uncover areas of opportunity and improvement
  * Create [agile HR flows](https://www.greenhouse.io/blog/hr-agile-with-retrospectives) through hiring debriefs
  * For better-informed decision making and a more inclusive hiring process overall, leverage our [standard demographic data report](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/7987759577243-Standard-demographic-data-report) and [Diversity, Equity and Inclusion reports](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/sections/360002478831-Diversity-Equity-and-Inclusion-reports) (available for Expert tier customers)

**Keep a pulse on your progress**

# Testlify integration

Testlify helps hiring teams to better estimate how well a candidate will perform in the role. Streamline and reduce hiring effort by initializing assessments from Greenhouse Recruiting as an integrated part of the candidate journey. 

Testlify’s integration with Greenhouse Recruiting allows you to seamlessly add Testlify’s assessment to a job's interview plan, plus receive scores and view assessment reports directly from the candidate's Greenhouse Recruiting profile.

#### In this article

  * Generate an API token in Testlify
  * Enable the Greenhouse Recruiting / Testlify integration
  * Use the Testlify integration with Greenhouse Recruiting
  * Additional resources



### Generate an API token in Testlify

First, you'll need to create an API token in Testlify. To do this, log in to Testlify and navigate to the _Settings_ tab. 

From the left menu, click **API Key** , then click **Generate Key.**

Copy the API key and store it somewhere safe. You will need to provide it to Greenhouse Technical Support during the next step.

### Enable the Greenhouse Recruiting / Testlify integration

Follow the steps in [this article](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/5888163696923) to provide your API token to Greenhouse Technical Support and add the assessment stage in your interview plans. 

Once you’ve set up your interview plans and configured your take home test, you’ll be able to send the test to candidates.

### Use the Testlify integration with Greenhouse Recruiting

Once the Greenhouse Recruiting / Testlify integration is enabled for your organization, you will be able to add the Testlify assessment as an interview stage.

You can send an assessment to a candidate by selecting the**Send Test** button next to the interview stage.

After it has been sent, an assessment’s status will display in Greenhouse Recruiting.

Once the candidate has submitted their test, the Interview Kit will contain a link to view the submitted test in the Testlify application. 

To see a candidate’s results in Testlify, click **View** **Report.**

### 

Assessment results for the candidate appear in PDF format. Additional authentication is not required to view candidate’s results.

### Additional resources

If you have questions or need help with this integration, reach out to [support@testlify.com](mailto:support@testlify.com)

# Talent Llama integration

In today’s job market, traditional screening methods have become impractical. Applicant volume has skyrocketed and conventional screening leads to bias and inconsistency, causing hiring teams to miss out on top talent. At Talent Llama, we’ve built a simple, integrated AI Talent Screening experience that reduces time-to-hire while giving every candidate a fair chance.

Talent Llama’s integration with Greenhouse Recruiting allows hiring teams to automatically import and invite candidates to interview from any stage in the Greenhouse candidate pipeline. As interviews are completed, recruiters can move top candidates to the next stage or reject them directly from the Talent Llama evaluation screen.

#### In this article

  * Connect Greenhouse to Talent Llama
    * Create a Harvest API key
    * Create an Integrated System User (ISU)
    * Save the Integration in Talent Llama
    * Create webhooks
  * Use the Talent Llama integration with Greenhouse Recruiting
    * Import applicants from Greenhouse
    * Turn on automatic invitations (Optional)
    * Edit linked job interview stages
    * Update applicant status from Talent Llama Evaluation
    * View Talent Llama Evaluation Summary in Greenhouse
  * Additional resources



### Connect Greenhouse to Talent Llama

From Talent Llama, in the Side Navigation at the bottom, click the “...” menu, then Integrations. Then click the ‘Connect’ button next to Greenhouse.

To connect Talent Llama with Greenhouse Recruiting, you’ll need to create a Harvest API Key and an Integrated System User (ISU) Id.

#### Create a Harvest API key

Follow the steps in [this article](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/5888163769883) to create the API key, and verify that the permissions below are selected when configuring the Talent Llama integration.

**Credentials**

In the _Create New Credential_ box, make the following selections:

  * **API Type:** Harvest
  * **Partner:** Talent Llama or Unlisted Vendor
  * **Description:** Talent Llama Harvest API Key



**Permissions**

Verify that the following permissions are selected for the Talent Llama integration:

  * **Applications**
    * GET: Retrieve Application
    * GET: List Applications
    * POST: Add Attachment to Application
    * POST: Move Application
    * POST: Reject Application
  * **Candidates**
    * GET: Retrieve Candidate
    * GET: List Candidates
    * POST: Add Note
  * **Job Openings**
    * GET: List Openings For a Job
  * **Job Posts**
    * GET: List Job Posts
    * GET: Retrieve Job Post for Job
    * GET: List Job Posts for Job
  * **Jobs**
    * GET: Retrieve Job
    * GET: List Jobs
  * **Job Stages**
    * GET: List Job Stages for Job
    * GET: Retrieve Job Stage
    * GET: List Job Stages
  * **Rejection Reasons**
    * GET: List Rejection Reasons



Once you have the API Key, in Talent Llama, enter this value in the **API Key** field.

#### Create an Integrated System User (ISU)

To update data in Greenhouse Recruiting from within Talent Llama, like archiving or changing stages, you’ll need to create an integrated system user. Follow the steps in [this article](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/4405511253659-Create-an-ISU-for-an-integration) to create your ISU, then [this article](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/10765948752027-Find-your-Greenhouse-Recruiting-user-ID) to find the User Id for the ISU you created. In Talent Llama, enter the value of the User Id for the **Talent Llama ISU Id** field.

#### Save the Integration in Talent Llama

With both the **API Key** and **Talent Llama ISU Id** entered, you can now click **Save** and, if connected correctly, will see additional information under the Greenhouse Integration in Talent Llama.

#### Create webhooks

To automatically add applicants from Greenhouse Recruiting to Talent Llama when applicants first submit an application, or when they move into a stage, you’ll need to create two webhooks. Follow the steps in [this article](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/5888163727003) to create each webhook. Use the values listed below to configure the Applicant Created and Stage Changed webhooks (they must be created separately):

**Webhook 1: Applicant created**

  * **Name** : Talent Llama Integration
  * **When** : Applicant Created
  * **Endpoint URL** : Copy the **Webhook URL** from Talent Llama
  * **Secret Key** : Copy the **Secret Key** from Talent Llama



**Webhook 2: Stage changed**

  * **Name** : Talent Llama Integration
  * **When** : Stage Changed
  * **Endpoint URL** : Copy the **Webhook URL** from Talent Llama
  * **Secret Key** : Copy the **Secret Key** from Talent Llama



### Use the Talent Llama integration with Greenhouse Recruiting

With your integration Connected and Webhooks set up, you can now send Talent Llama interview invitations when candidates first apply or when they move into one or more stages.

#### Import applicants from Greenhouse

From the **Applicants** tab, click the button to the right that says **Import from Greenhouse**

****

Find the **Job** from Greenhouse by typing the job name

Select the **Job** from which you want to import applicants

Select one or more **Stages** from which you want to import applicants

Click **Start Import**

Check the status of any import by clicking the **Import History** button at the top of the **Applicants** tab

****

#### Turn on automatic invitations (optional)

If you want full automation of interview invitations, you can configure Talent Llama to auto-send email invitations when applicants are imported. Make sure to review your Email Invitation content under Account Settings before activating.

#### Edit linked job interview stages

If you’ve made a mistake when selecting Interview Stages, or changed your hiring workflow, you can edit the Interview Stages that will be synced with Talent Llama. When applicants move into one of these Interview Stages, their application will automatically be imported into Talent Llama.

#### Update applicant status from Talent Llama Evaluation

When applicants finish their interview, Talent Llama provides an instant evaluation. With the Talent Llama and Greenhouse Connection, you can modify the applicant’s status in Greenhouse directly from the Talent Llama evaluation. You’ll know an applicant is synced to Greenhouse from the logo and Interview Stage showing next to the applicant’s name.

****

**Change Interview Stages:** Select the Interview Stage you’d like to move the Applicant to and submit

****

**Archive (Reject):** Select the Archive Reason, add an optional note, and submit

****

#### View Talent Llama Evaluation Summary in Greenhouse

Applicant Status changes can be seen in Greenhouse immediately. Talent Llama will also push evaluation results to the Greenhouse **Candidate Profile** screen under **Notes**.

****

That’s it, happy interviewing!

### Additional resources

For additional information or troubleshooting not covered here, reach out to [support@talentllama.com](mailto:support@talentllama.com).

# Send on behalf of permission management

**Permissions:** Job Admin and above with a Sourcing Automation seat

**Product tier:** Available for the Plus and Pro subscription tiers

**Note:** If you're trying to send emails on behalf of another person but don't see their name as an option in the **From** dropdown, send this article to them so they can grant you access.

Sourcing Automation users can send [campaign pool emails](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/5045604930843) on behalf of other users in your organization or on behalf of an email alias. You'll need to set up the correct permissions to send emails on behalf of another user or an email alias.

#### In this article

  * Allow users to send step emails on your behalf
    * Confirm your Sourcing Automation setup
    * Grant access to send emails on your behalf
  * Remove a user's permission to send on your behalf
  * Send on behalf of an email alias



### Allow users to send step emails on your behalf

You'll need to grant access to other Sourcing Automation users for them to send campaign step emails on your behalf. Follow the steps below to set up this permission:

#### Confirm your Sourcing Automation setup

Confirm that you've been granted a Sourcing Automation [seat](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/4952434968091) and that your email is [authenticated](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/5131512808091). Users can only send emails on behalf of other authenticated seat members.

#### Grant access to send emails on your behalf

Next, specify which users should have access to send emails on your behalf.

Click your **initials** in the top-right corner of your Greenhouse Recruiting dashboard and select **Account Settings** from the dropdown.

Navigate to **Personal Settings** , then scroll to the _Email Permissions_ section.

Select one of the following permissions:

  * **Allow anyone with job or site admin permissions to send emails from my address**
  * **Allow only specific people to send emails from my address**



If you limit permission to specific users, select their **names** from the dropdown menu. Users granted permission to send emails from your address will appear below the dropdown field.

Your changes will be saved automatically.

Once you've granted permission to send emails on your behalf, your email will appear in the **From** dropdown any time an authorized user [configures senders for a campaign pool step](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/5045604930843). 

### Remove a user's permission to send on your behalf

You can also remove access for users who you've previously granted permission to send on your behalf.

Navigate back to **Account Settings** > **Personal Settings** and scroll to the _Email Permissions_ section.

Hover over the user's name and click **Remove**.

Your changes will be saved automatically.

**Note:** If a campaign owner's permission to send on your behalf is removed before a step email is sent, the campaign will pause until the sender is updated for that step. Greenhouse Recruiting will notify the campaign owner by email if this error occurs.

### Send on behalf of an email alias

Sourcing Automation users also have the option to send campaign step emails on behalf of an email alias.

In order to use this feature, a Sourcing Automation admin will need to turn on the correct permission policy. In addition, your email alias will have to meet specific requirements to work with Sourcing Automation.

Learn more about [sending campaign pool emails on behalf of an email alias](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/15370403808027).

**Note:** Sending on behalf of email aliases is available for Gmail accounts only. Aliases created with other email service providers are not supported at this time.

# Add or edit a user email address

**Permissions:** –  
  
**Product tier:** Available for new subscription tiers (Core, Plus, and Pro)

Every Greenhouse Recruiting user account has at least one associated email address that is used for logging into the system and for email communication. This article will cover how a Greenhouse Recruiting user can add or update the email address(es) associated with their account. 

#### In this article

  * Primary vs. secondary email address
  * Manage your email address
    * Add an email address to your account
    * Change your primary email address
    * Delete a secondary email address
  * Manage another user's email address



### Primary vs. secondary email addresses

For any given Greenhouse Recruiting user account, you can have a **Primary** and **Secondary** email address. Both types of emails can be used to sign into Greenhouse Recruiting.

However, only the **Primary** email address will receive Greenhouse Recruiting emails (such as notifications, reminders, and interview kits).

Secondary email addresses are helpful if you want to select different email addresses in the **From** field when sending emails from Greenhouse Recruiting.

### Manage your email address

#### Add an email address to your account

You can update your email address by modifying your **Personal Information** under _Account Settings_. _(Your initials in the top right corner > **Account Settings** > **Edit** icon)_

Click **Add another email**.

Enter your email address into the field and click **Save** at the bottom of the page.

Greenhouse Recruiting will send a verification email to the provided email address. Click the **verification link** included in the email and input your password on the following page to verify the email address.

**Note** : If a non-primary email address is ever edited, Greenhouse Recruiting will send an additional verification email to verify the edited email address.

#### Change your primary email address

You can change the address marked as **Primary** on your _Account Settings_ page.

To update your email, navigate to your Account Settings page and click the Edit icon under Personal Information. _(Your initials in the top right corner > **Account Settings** > **Edit** icon)_

Select the **Primary** button next to the correct address.

**Note:** Unverified emails can't be marked as **Primary**.

Click Save at the bottom of the page.

#### Delete a secondary email address

To delete a secondary email address associated with your user account, navigate to the _Personal Information_ page. _(Your initials in the top right corner > **Account Settings** > **Edit** icon)_

Click the **X** icon next to the email address you want to remove.

**Note** : Only secondary email addresses can be deleted.

When you're finished, click **Save** at the bottom of the page.

### Manage another user's email address

**Note:** Only Site Admins can update or modify other users' email addresses. 

Go to **Configure** > **Users** and select a user from the list. 

On the _Edit User_ page, find the user's existing email address(es). Click **Add another email**.

Add the new email address.

To set the new email address as the user's primary email address, click the circle under **Primary**. To delete the email address, click the **Delete** icon.

When you're done, scroll down and click **Save user details**.

**Tip:** The **Save user details** button will always appear right before the Permissions section. The sections that come before it may vary.

From the _Edit your Job Post_ page, you can edit the following:

Click **Save** to save your edits.

# Deactivate users in bulk

**Permissions:** Site Admin

**Product tier:** Available for new subscription tiers (Core, Plus, and Pro)

In order to preserve your organization's historical data, you are unable to completely delete users from your Greenhouse Recruiting account. Rather than deleting users, Greenhouse Recruiting allows your organization to deactivate users' accounts so the users can no longer access your system or be assigned any responsibilities.

#### In this article

  * Deactivate users in bulk
  * Deactivated users' historical data
  * Additional resources



### Deactivate users in bulk

Click the **Configure** icon  in the upper-right corner, then select **Users** from the left side menu.

**Tip** : If desired, use the filters panel to narrow the list of users you see.

Click **Bulk Actions**.

Select the users you want to edit by clicking the checkbox to the left of their names.

When finished selecting users, click **Edit Selected (#)**.

In the dialog box that appears, click **Deactivate Users**.

A dialog box will ask you to confirm the deactivation. Click **Deactivate**.

For guidance on reactivating a deactivated user, click [here](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/115004494583).

### Deactivated users' historical data

Any responsibilities assigned to the deactivated users are preserved as historical data in your Greenhouse Recruiting account. This historical data is represented by a strikethrough in a user's name wherever that user had responsibilities.

In the above example, the user was once an offer approver on this specific job. Once deactivated, the user's name still appears as it did previously, but now with a strikethrough in their name.

### Additional resources

  * [Reactivate a deactivated user](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/115004494583)
  * [Deactivate a user](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/115004791523)

# New hires report

**Permissions:** Owners, Coordinators, and users with custom access to manage new hires

**Product tier:** Available for Greenhouse Welcome and Greenhouse Onboarding subscription tiers

Use the new hires report in Greenhouse Onboarding to see a complete list of your organization's newest hires and their progress on e-signatures, tasks, and onboarding goals.

#### In this article

  * View new hires report
    * New hires report columns
  * Filter new hires
    * Filter by start date
    * Filter by department
    * Filter by location
  * Add a new hire
  * Additional resources



### View new hires report

To find your new hires report, click **Reports** in the top navigation bar.

Select **View new hires report** from the _Reports_ panel.

On the _New Hires_ page, you'll find a list of all your organization's new hires.

**Note:** Users with [custom access to manage new hires](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/17555021401115) will see only the new hires that match the defined criteria for their custom role.

#### New hires report columns

Column name | Field info  
---|---  
Name | The new hire's name  
Manager | The name of this new hire's manager  
Department | The new hire's assigned department  
Location | The new hire's work location  
Start date | The new hire's assigned start date  
Goals assigned | The number of [onboarding goals](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/9265626455067) assigned to this new hire  
Goals completed | The percentage of onboarding goals that the [new hire has completed](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/9265765891995)  
Signature requests | The number of [e-signature requests](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/115003695071) assigned to this new hire  
Open tasks | The number of [tasks](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360000525691) assigned to this new hire that are incomplete  
  
**Note:** The **Signature requests** column is available only to the Greenhouse Onboarding subscription tier.

### Filter new hires

You can filter your report for increased visibility to quickly find specific new hires who've joined your organization. In the _Filter by_ panel, use any of the following filters to narrow your report results:

  * Start date
  * Department
  * Location



**Note:** You can make up to one selection for each report filter.

Click **Reset filters** to clear your filter selections and see the entire list of new hires again.

#### Filter by start date

Use the **Starting between** filter to search for new hires who started at your organization during a specific time range.

#### Filter by department

Use the **Departments** filter to search for new hires in specific departments at your organization.

#### Filter by location

Use the **Locations** filter to search for new hires in specific office locations.

### Add a new hire

Owners and Coordinators can also add new hires to your Greenhouse Onboarding account directly from the new hires report page.

**Note:** Users with [custom access to manage new hires](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/17555021401115) can't add a new hire in the new hires report.

Click **Add a new hire** in the top right corner of the new hires report.

This will take you to the  _Add New Hire_ flow, where you'll [create your new hire's employee profile and set up their onboarding plan](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360000683352).

When you're finished, click **Assign Plan** to create your new hire's profile. Click **Back to Home** after you've reviewed the new hire summary.

The new hire you've added will now appear in your new hires report.

### Additional resources

  * [Add a new hire and assign their onboarding plan](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360000683352)
  * [Assign custom access to manage new hires](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/17555021401115)
  * [Custom access roles](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360019516351)
