# Using offer forecast in the EU

**Permissions:** Job Admin and above

**Product tier:** Available for new subscription tiers (Core, Plus, and Pro)

Offer forecast uses the power of machine learning to predict when an offer might be accepted and when a new hire's start date might begin. Use offer forecast to streamline your hiring process, set clear timelines, and engage your team towards a goal. 

In this article, we've collected answers to a few frequently asked questions about using offer forecast in the European Union.

The guide outlines common questions for organizations with accounts on [Silo 101](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360056365191). For all other silos, [click here](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360002798612).

#### In this article

  * How does offer forecast work?
  * Why isn't a start date prediction provided for organizations with accounts in the EU?
  * How do you predict the offer acceptance date?
  * Which forecast statuses are available for organizations in the EU?
  * Can I report on offer forecast predictions?



#### How does offer forecast work?

Offer forecast is powered by a machine learning model called LightGBM or Light Gradient Boosting Machine. This model is trained on input variables from filled jobs to derive an output called time to hire. Some of the data used to train the model include the following:

  * Number of candidates in each milestone
  * Steps in the hiring plan
  * Months an organization has been using Greenhouse Recruiting
  * Days a job has been open
  * Days since a job was last updated
  * Offer status, if any
  * Average hiring speed
  * Time to hire from previous jobs
  * Lots of other things



Learn more about [how it works](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360002797252).

#### Why isn't a start date prediction provided for organizations with accounts in the EU?

Offer forecast is based on US standards, which typically involve a fixed 2-week lead time from the moment an employee accepts a role to the actual start date. However, in the EU, the lead time for employee onboarding is often variable and can vary significantly.

Start date predictions in offer forecast are designed to be most effective in scenarios where a fixed 2-week lead time is the norm, making it less suitable for regions with diverse lead time requirements.

For customers [on the EU silo](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360056365191), the same functionality as the US version is offered, except the widget will not include a start date prediction. The widget will only include a predicted offer acceptance date and target start date.

#### How is the offer acceptance date predicted?

Offer forecast considers jobs across all regions, the US & EU, to predict an offer acceptance date. The model takes into considerations organizations across all [silos](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360056365191).

#### Which forecast statuses are available?

Organizations will see a predicted offer acceptance dance and start date, if you've [set a target start date](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/19573002102299).

A predicted start date or variable lead time won't display, however, even for US-based roles. Since a start date prediction isn't available, the _On Track_ and _Needs Help_ statuses also won't be seen.

#### Can I report on offer forecast predictions?

We don't store historical predictions over time in Greenhouse Recruiting. As a result, offer forecast data doesn’t appear in any reports.

**Learn more**

[Offer forecast overview](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/115005312666)

[How offer forecast works](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360002797252)

[Use offer forecast](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/18710896459163)

[Offer forecast FAQ ](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360002798612)

# Release Notes: April 2026

Greenhouse Software regularly releases new product features, updates, and improvements. You can stay up-to-date by following our [release notes](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/200929955) or checking out the [latest feature releases](https://www.greenhouse.com/greenhouse-latest-features) page.

#### This month's releases

  * Greenhouse Recruiting
  * Greenhouse Onboarding
  * Integrations
  * Bug fixes



### Greenhouse Recruiting

#### Buffer times in interview scheduling

Customers can now add buffer time before and after interviews across all scheduling flows in Greenhouse, including automated and manual scheduling. Buffer times ensure interviewers have dedicated time to prepare, complete scorecards, or take a break, without extra coordination or manual blocks.

[Read more about interview buffer times.](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/46278259991835)

#### Auto-replace declined interviews for Outlook

Outlook integrations now support [auto-replacing declined interviewers](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/40649924884891), allowing teams to quickly fill gaps in calendars and avoid last-minute scheduling issues. 

[Read more about automatically replacing declined interviewers.](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/40649924884891)

#### Talent Matching UI enhancements

We've updated the Talent Matching UI to more clearly show how skills contribute to a candidate’s overall match. Customers can now see a breakdown of calibrated skills and supporting resume terms, along with improved explanations that make it easier to understand why a candidate is rated as a strong or limited match. 

[Read more about Talent Matching.](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/41396009937307)

#### Download job posts as a PDF

Customers can now download job descriptions directly from Greenhouse as a PDF, making it easier to store, share, and reference them when needed. This eliminates the need for manual copy and paste or API access, helping teams stay prepared for audits, compliance reviews, and internal documentation.

#### Multi-location support for third-party job boards

Customers can now post jobs to third-party job boards with multiple locations and work types, including remote and hybrid options, directly from Greenhouse. This makes it easier to represent roles accurately, improve candidate discovery, and avoid creating duplicate jobs for each location.

[Read more about creating an external job post.](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360020285311)

#### Auto-merge updates

Organizations can now choose which specific criteria must match before a candidate is automatically merged. 

[Read more about auto-merge.](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/208063316-Auto-merge)

#### Adding team members as cc'd on stage transition emails

Customers can now include coordinators, recruiters, and other hiring team members as CCs on automated stage transition emails using a role-based selection in Greenhouse. This helps keep the right people informed across key candidate communications without extra manual follow-up.

**Note:** Self-scheduling, identity verification, and take-home tests cannot have cc'd team members added.

#### Split e-Signature documents on the candidate profile

Customers using Greenhouse’s native e-signature can now choose to store signed documents as separate files on the candidate profile instead of a single combined PDF. This gives teams more flexibility to review, download, and manage individual documents as needed. 

To gain access to this feature, please reach out to your Account Team.

#### Add IP address to candidate packets and GDPR retention rules

IP address is now collected and stored as part of candidate device information. It can be included in candidate packets and selected in GDPR retention rules to support Real Talent features.

Read more about [candidate packets](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360000916572) and [setting up retention rules](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360002418112).

#### Available email tokens when creating stage transition emails

Stage Transition rules in Greenhouse now display the full list of available email tokens when configuring emails, matching the experience in email templates. This makes it easier for admins to build accurate, personalized messages without needing to guess which tokens are supported. 

[Read more about creating stage transition rules.](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360048178672)

#### Export Harvest API v1/v2 credentials

Customers can now export their Harvest API v1 and v2 credentials directly from the Dev Center in Greenhouse. Previously, auditing these credentials required manual support from the Greenhouse team. This self-serve export makes it easier to review existing integrations and plan your migration ahead of the Harvest v1/v2 deprecation on August 31, 2026.

[Read more about exporting Harvest API credentials. ](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/115000521723-Manage-Harvest-API-credentials-permissions#export-harvest-v1v2-api-credentials)

#### Other changes

  * GDPR filters on the All Candidates page have been renamed "Privacy and Compliance" and have updated menu options to better reflect the system behavior.



### Greenhouse Onboarding

#### Update to .csv uploader

Customers can now use Greenhouse Onboarding’s CSV Uploader to bulk update custom fields, such as cost centers, employee IDs, and other team-specific data. Built-in validation and row-level error handling make it easier to catch issues and complete large updates without manual entry or support help, giving teams more control and saving time.

#### Field validation for custom fields

Customers can now control how new hires and others enter data into custom fields in Greenhouse Onboarding — including fields like SSNs and other critical information. Field validation reduces data entry errors, supports stronger integrations, and saves teams time spent on data cleanup.

[Read more about adding field validation.](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360024972792-Manage-onboarding-fields#add-field-validation)

### Integrations

#### New partners on the hiring cloud

  * **Candidate background check** : [Accurate ACCEL](https://integrations.greenhouse.com/partners/accurate-accel) provides a robust screening solution designed to address the challenges employers face while meeting local regulations and safeguarding data privacy.
  * **Candidate background check** : [Amiqus](https://integrations.greenhouse.com/partners/amiqus) is a leading provider for businesses managing high-volume onboarding, enabling digital verification of new employees in minutes. 
  * **Candidate testing** : [Casium](https://integrations.greenhouse.com/partners/casium-assessments) helps employers evaluate immigration pathways for candidates through attorney-led assessments requested directly from within Greenhouse.
  * **Candidate testing** : [InterviewFlowAI](https://integrations.greenhouse.com/partners/interviewflowai) is revolutionizing the recruitment landscape by leveraging the power of artificial intelligence to transform the hiring process. 
  * **Candidate testing:** [MarioHR](https://integrations.greenhouse.com/partners/mariohr) provides an innovative assessment solution for modern hiring.
  * **Candidate testing** : [Textmetrics](https://integrations.greenhouse.com/partners/textmetrics) helps recruiters write inclusive, clear and effective job descriptions directly inside Greenhouse.
  * **Job board** : [Dstribute](https://integrations.greenhouse.com/partners/dstribute-io) distributes Greenhouse job postings to required OFCCP channels, covering state job banks, veteran organizations and diversity outreach networks.
  * **Optimization** : [Joveo's](https://integrations.greenhouse.com/partners/joveo-programmatic-job-advertising) AI Job Advertising for Greenhouse improves the effectiveness of recruitment marketing spend through performance-based job advertising.
  * **Optimization** : [Virvell](https://integrations.greenhouse.com/partners/virvell) provides AI-powered pre-screen interviews, voice reference checks, and background verification in one platform. 



#### Partners who have migrated to Harvest v3

  * [ModernLoop](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/48562730720155)
  * [The Predictive Index](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/47961878830491)



### Bug fixes

  * Fixed an issue where outdated Outlook interview invites were sent to interviewers.
  * Fixed an issue where the Outlook 365 integration was not working for the Singapore time zone.
  * Fixed an issue where users were not correctly notified of an error when attempting to schedule private interviews on shared Outlook calendars.

# Veremark integration

Veremark provides a range of character, background and identity checks that can be performed on candidates These checks include character references, employment checks, National ID verification, criminal record and a number of other background checks. Veremark provides a result and detailed reports for each check taken.

Greenhouse Recruiting's integration with Veremark allows you to seamlessly add Veremark's assessment to a job's interview plan. In this article, we will cover how to:

#### In this article

  * Enable the Greenhouse/Veremark integration
  * Add Veremark stage to job’s interview plan
  * Configure Veremark stage
  * Send and review the test
  * Additional resources



### Enable the Greenhouse/Veremark integration

To start, contact your Veremark representative (support@veremark.com) to receive your API key. Once you have received your API key, [click here](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/requests/new) to open a ticket with Greenhouse or visit [www.greenhouse.io/asksupport](http://support.greenhouse.io/direct).

**Note:** Do not send the API key in this initial email.

The Greenhouse Technical Support team will respond with a [SendSafely link](https://www.sendsafely.com/howitworks/) for you to enter your API key. A notification will be sent to the Greenhouse Technical Support team after you have entered your API key and they will email you to confirm that your API key has been set up in your account and your integration is enabled.

**Note:** To verify your identity, the Greenhouse Technical Support team might request you provide a [Support Verification Code](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360022771952) before adding the API key to your organization's account.

### Add Veremark stage to job’s interview plan

Once the Greenhouse/Veremark integration is enabled for your organization, you're able to add the Veremark assessment as an Interview stage.

To do this for an existing job, follow the steps below:

  1. Navigate to a job (**Jobs** >**Job Name**)
  2. Click **Job Setup** from the left navigation bar
  3. From the _Job Setup_ page, navigate to**Interview Plan** on the left panel
  4. Click **Add Stage**
  5. From the _Add Stage_ dialog box, select **Veremark**
  6. Click **Add** to apply the stage to the job's interview plan



### Configure Veremark stage

Once the stage has been added to the job's interview plan, click **Edit Take Home Test**.

Use the provided dropdown menu to choose **assessments** that you have previously set up in Veremark.

Assign at least one **Greenhouse Recruiting user** to grade/review submitted assessments.

When finished, click **Save**.

**Note** : Keep in mind that all configuration of the assessment itself, as well as the email template, will need to be done in Veremark.

### Send and review the test

When candidates are moved into the Veremark interview stage, Greenhouse displays a _Send Test_ link.

**Note** : When you send a test from Greenhouse, the interview instructions are actually sent by Veremark.

The status of the assessment is viewable in Greenhouse on the candidate's profile. 

Once the candidate has submitted their test, the **Interview Kit** contains a link to view the submitted test on Veremark.

After you click the Interview Kit on the candidate’s profile, you're taken to a page where the URL is available to view the test results on Veremark.

### Additional resources

Please see Veremark's FAQs <https://www.veremark.com/faqs> and pricing info at <https://www.veremark.com/pricing>

Please contact [support@veremark.com](support@veremark.com) for troubleshooting assistance regarding the integration.

# Billing page overview

**Permissions:** Job Admins, Site Admins who can view and edit billing contact information on the billing page 

**Product tier:** Available for new subscription tiers (Core, Plus, and Pro)

Site Admins can manage key billing details for their organization directly in Greenhouse, including contact information, headcount, and renewal contacts. These updates help ensure invoices are delivered correctly and renewals stay on track.

#### In this article

  * How to access the billing page
  * Update billing contact information
  * Update tax information
  * Update renewal contact information
  * Update company headcount
  * Notification 120 days before renewal
  * View billing changes in change log



### How to access the billing page

To access your billing details, log into Greenhouse and navigate to **Configure** > **Billing**.

This page includes account-level information, such as your assigned account team and the details that appear on your invoices.

### Update billing contact information

**Note:** Only Site Admins with permission to view and edit the billing page can see and modify detailed information.

Your billing contact information is used to generate and deliver invoices for your account. If this information is outdated, billing documents may not be delivered, which could interrupt your Greenhouse plan. Periodically, we may request an account review to make sure the information is up-to-date.

You can update your billing contact at any time by clicking the **Edit** icon next to that section.

### Update tax information

Site Admins can now add a tax ID to support invoicing and local tax compliance requirements. This information appears on future invoices and is shared with the Greenhouse finance team.

To add a tax ID, go to **Configure > Billing**, then scroll to the _Tax information_ section and click **Edit**.

In the Edit tax information modal, select your country’s **tax ID type** from the dropdown menu. Available types include:

  * VAT ID (EU/UK)
  * TIN/EIN (United States)
  * BN (Canada)
  * GSTIN (India)
  * ABN (Australia)
  * Other



Enter your organization’s **tax ID** in the corresponding field, then click **Save**. Once saved, the tax ID will appear in the Billing page and be synced with Salesforce for compliance and reporting purposes.

The field is required for organizations in Australia, Canada, the EU, Mexico, and South Africa. Character formats may vary depending on the selected country. For example:

  * EU VAT IDs must start with a two-letter country code followed by 8–11 characters (e.g. IE12345678)
  * Canadian BN (BC) must follow the format PST-1234-1234
  * Mexican IDs must be 12 digits



Greenhouse does not validate tax ID formats at entry but recommends using the official format for your country.

### Update renewal contact information

The renewal contact is the person Greenhouse will reach out to about your upcoming plan renewal. Keeping this contact up to date ensures that your team receives timely renewal information.

To update this contact, click the **Edit** icon next to the renewal contact section.

### Update company headcount

Greenhouse uses your company headcount to help tailor your subscription and billing details. If your organization grows or changes, make sure to update your headcount to reflect the current number.

To update this information, click the **Edit** icon next to the company headcount field.

### Notification 120 days before renewal

Greenhouse will display a reminder to your dashboard 120 days before your subscription renewal date. This notification gives your team time to review your plan, update contact information, and make any necessary adjustments.

To make sure all your information is up to date, click **Review** and you'll be taken through several steps where you can review and update different pieces of billing information.

Keeping your contact details current ensures this notification reaches the appropriate person and helps prevent disruptions to your account.

### View billing changes in change log

The Billing page includes a change log where Site Admins can audit updates made to billing-related fields. This includes filters for events like:

  * Billing contact updated
  * Tax information updated
  * Company headcount updated
  * Renewal contact updated



To learn how to use the change log, refer to [Greenhouse Recruiting change log](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360037767471).

Reviewing this log regularly helps ensure your account information stays accurate and up to date.

# MyGreenhouse Stages

**Permissions:** Site admins

**Product tier:** Available to all product tiers

Help candidates understand where they are in your hiring process—without exposing internal details—by giving them clear application transparency in MyGreenhouse. 

MyGreenhouse Stages let you map your internal hiring stages to clear, candidate-friendly stages (like “Interviewing” or “Offer Sent”), add optional descriptions to provide helpful context, then schedule when you'll share your stages with candidates. It’s a simple way to improve transparency, reduce recruiter follow-up, and create a more polished candidate experience.

#### In this article

  * Overview
  * Setup MyGreenhouse Stages
    * Internal setup
    * Create stages
    * Preview stages
    * Publish stages



### Overview 

MyGreenhouse Stages let you give candidates a polished and transparent hiring process without sharing internal stage names with them. Create a group of candidate-facing stages by mapping your internal stages to simplified, human-friendly labels. Stages are created at the department level, applied to all jobs in that department, and automatically update based on candidate movement. 

Once published, candidates will see their current stage in MyGreenhouse—no extra emails or manual updates required.

**Tip:** To give candidates the best experience, [share tasks and application status](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/35745912017435).

### Set up MyGreenhouse Stages

To create candidate-facing stages, go to **Configure** > **MyGreenhouse** and scroll to "MyGreenhouse Stages." Select "Create new" to get started. 

#### Internal setup

First, you'll complete your internal setup.

To help your team stay organized, give your MyGreenhouse stages an internal name. This name won't be visible to candidates.

Next, choose which departments these stages will apply to. When published, candidates who apply to jobs in these departments will see their current candidate-facing stage on their application in MyGreenhouse.

#### Create stages

Give each stage a candidate-facing name (e.g., “Phone Interview”).

Select which internal stages will be included in this candidate-facing stage. You can add multiple internal stages to each MyGreenhouse stage.

Add a description to provide prep tips or expectations. _(Optional)_

#### Preview stages

Next, see how your stages will look to candidates. As you build your MyGreenhouse stages, you’ll preview a list of your stages in the righthand panel. Select **Preview** for a full view of how your stages will look to candidates.

#### Publish stages

Decide whether you want to show candidates your new stages immediately or schedule a publishing delay. When you're happy with your setup, save your draft. Then, return to **MyGreenhouse Settings** to**** enable your new MyGreenhouse Stages.

Select the dropdown menu next to your new stage, then set to "Live."   
  
Now that your MyGreenhouse stage setup is published, candidates applying to jobs in the selected departments will see their current stage on their application in MyGreenhouse. When you move a candidate into a new internal stage, their MyGreenhouse stage will automatically update.

You can edit, unpublish, or customize stages from this page at any time.

The [identity verification](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/40966215931291) daily digest is an email notification that summarizes identity verification activity for a job. It helps your team stay up to date on candidate verification status without needing to check each profile individually.

The digest is sent once per day, whenever there is new activity.

### Add users to the notification list for the daily digest

To add users to the notification list for the daily report, click**Jobs** from the navigation bar and select a job from the list.

Click**Job Setup** and navigate to **Notifications** on the left.

Scroll to the _Candidate notifications_ section and click **Configure** beside _Identity Verification Daily Digest_.

Click the _Participants_ dropdown and select the appropriate person. You can select a person by name, or you can select the [hiring managers](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360016572311) listed on the job's hiring team. When finished, click **Save**.

**Note** : Only users who have appropriate permissions on the job and for identity verification will populate in the dropdown.

All selected users will receive a daily email that contains updates to candidates' identity verification status.

### Remove users from the notification list for the daily digest

To remove users from the notification list, navigate to the name of a user listed in the _Participants_ dropdown and click **X** to the right of their name.

Repeat as necessary for other users and click **Save** when finished.

# Interviewing activity per job report

**Permissions:** Job Admin and above

**Product tier:** Available for new subscription tiers (Core, Plus, and Pro)

How much interviewing are you actually doing as a company? Are those interviews helping to move candidates further through your pipeline?

The interviewing activity per job report enables your organization to answer these types of questions across all jobs. One of the best metrics you can glean from this report is whether you are effectively using your interviewers' time.

For example, if scheduled interviews and scorecards submitted are relatively high, but you are mostly rejecting candidates, you might be spending too many hours interviewing people who are not a good fit. In this case, more vetting early on could eliminate candidates who would never pass your more resource-expensive face-to-face stage anyway.

**Tip** : Need help troubleshooting this report? Check out [Troubleshoot a report](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/13710986142107).

#### In this article

  * Interviewing activity per job report
  * Interviewing activity per job report filters
  * Interviewing activity per job report visualization



### Interviewing activity per job report

To create an interviewing activity per job report, click **Reports** on your navigation bar.

Click **Essential** **Reports** on the left. 

Scroll to the _Stay on top of Current Recruiting Activity_ section and click **Interviewing Activity**.

The interviewing activity per job report will generate.

The report includes data in the following columns:

**Column** | **Description**  
---|---  
Candidates entered |  Shows how many candidates were moved into a particular stage in a given period. It could contain duplicates if you moved one candidate into a stage on two different jobs. Candidates who bypass a stage will not be tallied for that stage. For example, if a candidate was moved directly from application review to the face-to-face interview, all the stages between will not record that candidate in their tallies. **Note** : This column only appears on the report when using **Filters** **and** **more** to sort rows by stage or milestone.  
Candidates exited |  Shows how many candidates were moved out of a particular stage in a given period, including rejections. It could contain duplicates if you moved one candidate out of a stage on two different jobs. **Note** : This column only appears on the report when using **Filters** **and** **more** to sort rows by stage or milestone.  
Candidates rejected | Shows how many applications were rejected from a particular stage in a given period. It could contain duplicates if you rejected one candidate from two different jobs.  
Interviews created | The number of interviews that were created and sent to interviewers in a particular period. Meant to show how much scheduling is being done, this column ignores the date the interview takes place and only looks at when it was initially set up.  
Number of interviews | The number of interviews that happened or are set to take place in a given period. Meant to show how many interviews actually took place, this column ignores the interview creation date and only looks at when it was scheduled to occur.  
Candidates interviewing | The number of candidates with any interviews scheduled for a given period. One candidate could have four interviews as part of a face-to-face stage, but this column will only count one distinct person for all of those interviews. It could contain duplicates if you scheduled one candidate on two different jobs.  
Scorecards submitted | The total number of scorecards submitted by all of your users in a given period. Assuming one is filled out for every interview that takes place, this will give you an idea of how many total interactions your staff has had with candidates.  
Candidates rated | The number of candidates with any scorecards submitted for them in a given period. One candidate could have four scorecards as part of a group interview stage, but this column will only count one distinct person for all of those scorecards. It could contain duplicates if you submitted scorecards for one candidate on two different jobs.  
Tests sent | The total number of unique take home tests sent to candidates. Re-sending a test does not impact this number  
Tests submitted | The number of completed take home tests received. A test sent in a previous time period may be completed in a later period.  
  
### Interviewing activity per job report filters

Click**Filters and more** to apply filters to further refine your report.

The interviewing activity per job report can be filtered by the following:

  * Job
  * Job status
  * Department (and [subordinate departments](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/211537106#h_04e68745-af71-4c3a-b49f-8a9848eaf19a))
  * Office (and [subordinate offices](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/211537106#h_04e68745-af71-4c3a-b49f-8a9848eaf19a))
  * User
  * Hiring team role
  * Custom job field
  * Activity date
  * Recruiter
  * Stage
  * Exclude Application Review stage



**Note** : By default, the activity date for the report is set to the current year.

You can organize rows on the report by job, recruiter, source, or department

**Note** : Filtering by recruiter doesn't show you that recruiter's actions; it only shows you candidates who have that user listed as their recruiter.

### Interviewing activity per job report visualization

The interviewing activity per job report will visualize the number of activities per job.

The visualization presents a bar chart with each job displayed on the _y_ -axis and the total number of activities displayed on the _x_ -axis.

You can hover over each point in the visualization for additional details.

Since the visualization displays data from your report, changes made to the report via **Filters and more** like adjusting the date filters or the jobs selected will impact the visualization.

# Assign or edit an employee ID 

**Permissions:** Site Admin who can edit another user's advanced permissions

**Product tier:** Available for Plus and Pro subscription tiers

In some organizations, an employee ID can be a more stable identifier than an employee's email address or name. Greenhouse Recruiting allows your organization to associate an employee ID with a user's account.

The employee ID field in Greenhouse Recruiting can be any alphanumeric string that your organization assigns to its employees. Greenhouse Recruiting enforces employee ID uniqueness, so there will be an error message if you attempt to save a pre-existing employee ID used by another user.

#### In this article

  * Add employee ID to a Greenhouse Recruiting user profile
  * Add employee ID to Single Sign-On (SSO)
  * Edit employee ID via Harvest API



### Add employee ID to a Greenhouse Recruiting user profile

To assign an employee ID to an individual Greenhouse Recruiting user profile, click the **Configure** icon  in the upper-right hand corner and select **Users** from the left-hand panel.

Select a user profile from the subsequent list.

From the user's profile, navigate to the _Employee ID_ field and input the user's employee ID.

When you finish, scroll to the bottom of the section and click **Save user details**.

### Add employee ID to Single Sign-On (SSO)

For organizations using a Single Sign-On (SSO) provider to log into Greenhouse Recruiting, it is possible to add the Employee ID in your SSO provider. By adding the employee ID in your SSO provider, the employee ID will automatically be updated each time they log into Greenhouse Recruiting.

For more information on configuring employee ID with your SSO provider, [click here](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360040753811).

### Edit employee ID via Harvest API

Once employee ID is set up for your organization, it will appear in web hooks and the Harvest API when retrieving lists of users. Additionally, you can make an API call regarding a single user by using only their Employee ID. Check out our [Harvest API documentation](https://developers.greenhouse.io/harvest.html#the-user-object) for more information.

# Zelt integration

Zelt is a software application you can use to automate HR and IT tasks in your company. Now you can onboard new joiners, run payroll, manage holidays and automate IT tasks in a single system, from providing laptops to setting up accounts across your cloud applications. This saves you time and money, and is more secure.

Zelt’s integration with Greenhouse Recruiting allows you to automatically import successful hires to Zelt and send them into the desired onboarding flow when it’s the right time - automatically.

#### In this article

  * Create a Harvest API key for the Zelt integration
    * Connect your Greenhouse Recruiting API key with Zelt 
  * Use the Zelt integration with Greenhouse Recruiting
    * Set up automated onboarding with Zelt
    * Manually onboard candidates in Zelt 
  * Additional resources



### Create a Harvest API key for the Zelt integration 

To configure the Zelt integration, you’ll need to create a Harvest API key.

Follow the steps in [this article ](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/5888163769883)to create the key, and verify that the permissions below are selected when configuring the Zelt integration.

#### Credentials

In the _Create New Credential_ box, make the following selections:

  * **API Type:** Harvest
  * **Partner:** Zelt or _Unlisted Vendor_
  * **Description:** Zelt integration Harvest API Key



#### Permissions

Verify that the following permissions are selected for the Zelt integration:

**Applications**

  * GET: List applications



**Candidates**

  * GET: List Candidates
  * GET: Retrieve Candidate



**Offers**

  * GET: List offers



**Users**

  * All permissions



When finished, click **Save**.

Your Harvest API key for the Greenhouse Recruiting / Zelt integration is created and configured. Copy the Harvest API key to provide to Zelt in the next step.

#### Connect your Greenhouse Recruiting API key with Zelt 

To enable the Greenhouse Recruiting / Zelt integration, you'll need to connect your existing Greenhouse account. To begin setup, navigate to Zelt and select the **Apps** tab.

Locate **Greenhouse** and click **Connect.**

In order to connect, enter your generated Harvest API key created in the prior step. 

Once connected you will be able to start onboarding successful hires manually or via a scheduled synchronization - using your preferred onboarding template.

Head over to **Greenhouse Settings** in Zelt to set this flow up.

You can also set up a webhook so that newly hired candidates can be created in Zelt straight away. Follow the steps in [this article ](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/5888163727003)to create your webhook.

Use the information provided in Zelt settings of the integration to create a webhook in Greenhouse.

### Use the Zelt integration with Greenhouse Recruiting**  
**

#### Set up automated onboarding with Zelt

Once your successful hire was sent to an automated onboarding flow, you can check on the progress of your new joiner in the Onboarding section of your Zelt account. Click on the employee name and see any completed and remaining tasks that you have assigned to this person. You can also send reminders directly from the HR Admin Onboarding lobby.

New hire onboarding lobby:

#### Manually onboard candidates in Zelt 

Start by going to the Greenhouse app in Zelt. You will find it in your Company connected apps.

In Greenhouse, navigate to **Candidates** tab. 

Select a successful candidate who you would like to onboard in Zelt manually, provide their preferred work email address and select the required Onboarding flow from the drop-down select and click **Onboard**.

All existing candidate details will be pre-populated in the first step of the Onboarding flow and you will have a chance to review that the _Job Title_ , _Start date_ , _Salary_ and any other information you have provided in Greenhouse for this employee as you onboard them in Zelt.

As a last step, you can choose to invite new hire to onboard or save them as a draft for now.

The onboarding lobby will be automatically populated with your selected tasks from the chosen Onboarding workflow. You will have a quick overview of any remaining to-dos and onboarding tasks from this page.

### Additional resources

For additional information or troubleshooting not covered here, reach out to [support@zelt.app](mailto:support@zelt.app) or message Zelt directly via in-app chat.

# Inclusively integration

Inclusively’s Workforce Inclusion Platform helps employers unlock the power of today’s workforce by opening doors to untapped talent.

Greenhouse Recruiting's integration with Inclusively reduces issues and time with manual job ingestion and candidate submittal, providing a quick and efficient way for potential candidates to apply to jobs.

#### In this article

  * Create a Harvest API key for the Inclusively integration

### Create a Harvest API key for the Inclusively integration

To configure the Greenhouse Recruiting / Inclusively integration, you’ll need to create a Harvest API key.

Follow the steps in [this article](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/5888163769883) to create the key, and verify that the permissions below are selected when configuring the Inclusively integration. #### Credentials

  * GET: List Users



**Save** when finished. 

#### Provide Harvest API Key to Inclusively

After configuring your Inclusively API key in Greenhouse Recruiting, you'll need to provide the key to Inclusively to complete setup. 

**Note:** The user setting up the Greenhouse Recruiting / Inclusively integration must have an email address that matches their email within the organization's Inclusively account.

To provide your key, navigate to Inclusively > **Company Profile** and select **ATS Integration**.

Click **Link ATS**.

From the list of ATS's, select **Greenhouse Recruiting**. Review the access request and click **Continue**.

**Enter** your Greenhouse API Key. 

When finished, click **Submit.**

### Use the Inclusively integration with Greenhouse Recruiting

The Greenhouse Recruiting / Inclusively integration is an API-driven integration and there is little to be seen within the Inclusively platform other than the above ATS linking. This integration provides the following functionality:

  * Automatic Job Ingestion from Greenhouse, currently nightly.
  * All Jobs are kept in sync, including adding new or remove non active jobs
  * Candidates are directly submitted to Greenhouse upon connecting to a job
  * Candidate name and contact information
  * Inclusively Candidate Resume



Inclusively adds information for the application process also. During this process Inclusively will add new candidates as Prospects. Prospects then get converted into Candidates when the Application is added, linking the Prospect to a Job. The last step is to add an attachment to the candidate.

**Note:** The user who enables the Inclusively integration for the company will be set up as the “On-behalf-of” user Inclusively uses for all data changes made to submit candidates. If you do not want a particular user, Inclusively suggests setting up a service user for this.

For example, you can create a user called “Inclusively Automation”, with a corresponding email address Inclusively can use to link Greenhouse accounts to Inclusively accounts. Steps to create a service user can be found [here](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/4405511253659-Create-an-ISU-for-an-integration).

#### Sync candidates from Inclusively to Greenhouse Recruiting

When a candidate finds a job for one of Inclusively’s Greenhouse customers that they would like to connect to (our terminology for “apply) within the Inclusively platform, they click on the connect button on the job card:

After hitting **Connect** , candidates will be asked to confirm some information.

Once done, they'll click **Send** to send their application to the organization's Greenhouse Recruiting account.

# Splash integration

Splash is an event creation tool that enables your organization to capture attendee insight and measure event impact.

Greenhouse Recruiting's integration with Splash allows you to automatically sync candidate data between the two systems to quickly and accurately track candidates sourced and influenced by your events.

#### In this article

  * Use the Splash integration with Greenhouse Recruiting
    * Organization level integration
    * Event level integration



### Use the Splash integration with Greenhouse Recruiting

There are two different ways to configure your Splash-Greenhouse integration:

  * **Organization level:** All events you create will be connected to Greenhouse Recruiting.
  * **Event level:** Configured _a la carte_ — event by event — meaning events you do not configure and activate the integration for will not be connected to Greenhouse.



#### Organization level integration

To enable an organization level integration between Greenhouse Recruiting and Splash, navigate to the [Integrations dashboard](https://splashthat.com/account/integrations) on your Splash account.

Click **New Integrations**.

Choose **Greenhouse** from the list of available integrations.

Follow the instructions in the subsequent dialog box to authenticate your account.

Once the account authentication process is complete, you can enter an Integration **Name** , select a **Trigger** , and choose an **Action**.

**Note** : For this particular integration, only Attendee actions are available, so you can only set Attendee as the Trigger.

For example, if the Attendee Action being configured is **RSVP Yes** , that means when a guest registers for an event in Splash, that information will be sent to Greenhouse.

Next, map the Greenhouse Remote Fields for `first_name` and `last_name` to **First Name** and **Last Name** Contact fields in Splash.

It is recommended to map your applicant's email field, too, which will ensure you have a way of uniquely identifying the candidate.

Click **Save**.

**Note** : `first_name` and `last_name` are required fields in Greenhouse and cannot be removed.

Most customers choose to sync Resume and Job Position information submitted in Splash back to Greenhouse. For the latter, it's particularly useful to be able to connect the position being applied for to a Greenhouse Job ID.

#### Event level integration

Navigate to the Event page's Form tab in Splash. Click **Add Question**.

Select the Resume question from the menu add a custom question for Job Position.

When selecting which job to apply for, the options should follow the syntax **Label{{job_id}}** — the ID within the brackets in the Job ID in your Greenhouse instance.

When a guest RSVPs, the value inside the brackets will appear in the contact information of your guest list.

Next, map your newly added Splash questions to Greenhouse fields.

It's also recommended that you map the Splash _Event Domain_ field to your Greenhouse field for `website_url` — this will allow you to attribute the attendee's action to a specific event.

Save your integration then toggle it **ON** to activate it.

Next, you may want to set up additional integration actions, such as for when a guest is checked into an event. The easiest way to do this is to duplicate your previously configured Greenhouse integration.

Re-name the integration and update the Action field.

Save and toggle **ON** your integration. Repeat as necessary.

# OneSpan Sign integration

OneSpan Sign provides a comprehensive suite of electronic signature solutions designed to streamline and secure the signing process for businesses of all sizes. With the OneSpan Integration Platform, Greenhouse customers can seamlessly integrate their Greenhouse solutions with OneSpan Sign to streamline creation and management of electronic signature agreements and transactions with ease. The OneSpan Integration Platform can support over 1,000 business applications, including popular tools like Salesforce, Google Workspace, and Microsoft Office, ensuring a smooth, efficient, and legally compliant signing experience.

The OneSpan Integration Platform also features pre-built integrations for rapid deployment, low-code/no-code development options, and robust security measures such as end-to-end encryption, multi-factor authentication, and access controls. Additionally, it complies with stringent security standards like ISO/IEC 27001, SOC2 Type II, and HIPAA, providing peace of mind that sensitive documents are always protected.

OneSpan’s integration with Greenhouse Recruiting allows HR teams to effortlessly manage electronic signature processes. They can initiate document signing without leaving the Greenhouse platform. Candidates and new hires can eSign from their own devices, with all signed documents stored and accessible directly within Greenhouse. This seamless integration makes it easy to send, store, and audit important documents like offer letters and onboarding forms. HR teams benefit from enhanced workflow efficiency, stronger compliance, and top-notch security standards. Streamline the hiring process and elevate document management with OneSpan and Greenhouse.

**Note:** Before enabling this integration, you’ll need to reach out to your OneSpan Customer Success Manager or write to [sales@onespan.com](mailto:sales@onespan.com) if you're interested in learning more and testing or using the OneSpan Sign for Greenhouse integration. You can also request a demo via [this form](https://www.onespan.com/products/request-a-demo).

#### In this article

  * Create a Harvest API key
  * Create a webhook
  * Use the OneSpan Sign integration with Greenhouse Recruiting
  * Additional resources



### Create a Harvest API key

To configure the OneSpan Sign integration, you’ll need to create a Harvest API key.

Follow the steps in[ this article](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/5888163769883) to create the key and verify that the permissions below are selected when configuring the OneSpan Sign integration.

#### **Credentials**

In the _Create New Credential_ box, make the following selections:

  * **API Type:** Harvest
  * **Partner:** OneSpan or Unlisted Vendor
  * **Description:** OneSpan Integration Platform Harvest API Key



#### **Permissions**

Verify that the following permissions are selected for the OneSpan Sign integration:

  * **Applications**
    * All permissions
  * **Candidates**
    * All permissions
  * **Offers**
    * All permissions
  * **Users**
    * All permissions



### Create a webhook

Next, you’ll need to create a webhook. Follow the steps in[ this article](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/5888163727003) to create your webhook. Use the values listed below to configure the webhook:

  * **Name:** OneSpan Sign Integration Platform when [name of event]
  * **When:** Candidate has changed stage or Offer approved
  * **Endpoint URL:** The Endpoint URL is dynamically generated and provided during setup with OneSpan professional services.
  * **Secret Key:** The Secret Key is dynamically generated and provided during setup with the OneSpan professional services, it will match the Endpoint URL above.



**Example of an Endpoint URL from the OneSpan Sign Integration Platform**

**Note:** This event must match the value selected in the When field.

**Example of a secret key from the OneSpan Sign Integration Platform**

### Use the OneSpan Sign integration with Greenhouse Recruiting

The OneSpan Sign integration streamlines the eSignature process during recruitment and onboarding. As a Greenhouse administrator, you can configure this integration to trigger automatically at any stage of the recruitment process or when an offer has been approved. OneSpan Professional Services and/or OneSpan support team will assist you to select & configure your desired workflow.

The following example will focus on the scenario when a job offer has been approved.

When a Greenhouse user creates an offer for a candidate, they fill in the required offer fields. Next, the user generates the offer document and attaches any necessary documents. The Greenhouse user will then submit the offer for approval. Once the approver approves the offer, this launches the eSign process.

The OneSpan Sign integration collects the candidate’s information and documents that need to be signed. It creates a new OneSpan Sign Electronic Signature package. OneSpan Sign automatically sends a secure link for the signing ceremony to the candidate.

The candidate receives the email, opens the link to the OneSpan Sign signing ceremony page, and reviews and eSigns the documents.

Admins: During the initial setup of the OneSpan Sign integration, you can customize the signing ceremony page to match your company’s branding. Additionally, you can enable user authentication and identity verification before document signing. These options apply to all transactions created through the integration.

Once the candidate signs the documents, the Greenhouse offer process is automatically marked as “Hired”. The OneSpan Sign transaction identifier is added to the candidate’s offer, and the signed PDF and Evidence Summary report are bundled in a single zip file under the Offer Documents section of the process.

### Additional resources

For additional information or troubleshooting not covered here, reach out to [support@onespan.com](mailto:support@onespan.com) or visit our community site at[ https://community.onespan.com](https://community.onespan.com/) or our support site at[ https://support.onespan.com](https://support.onespan.com/).

# Email domain verification quick start guide

**Permissions:** Users with "Can configure email settings" permission

**Product tier:** Available for new subscription tiers (Core, Plus, and Pro)

**Tip:** Check out our [overview article](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/11672225954971) for information on how to get started.

Greenhouse Recruiting allows you to send emails from within your account that will appear to the candidate as being sent from your organization's domain.

Part of setting up your Greenhouse Recruiting account involves verifying your organization's domain to ensure your emails are delivered consistently and securely.

#### In this article

  * About domain verification
  * Add your domain to Greenhouse Recruiting
  * Update your DNS settings
    * Access your DNS settings
    * Access your Greenhouse Recruiting values
    * Add your Greenhouse Recruiting values to your DNS account
  * Test your DNS records
  * Additional resources



### About domain verification

Verifying your domain communicates to email providers that they can trust the use of your domain for Greenhouse Recruiting emails.

Verifying your email domain involves copying values in Greenhouse Recruiting, adding them to your DNS settings, and testing in Greenhouse Recruiting that the settings were successfully added.

### Add your domain to Greenhouse Recruiting

Log in to your Greenhouse Recruiting account. Go to **Configure** > **Dev Center** > **Email Settings**. Find the section marked with a **1**. Find the text box(es) on the right side of the section.

Refer back to the domain or subdomain you chose in **Step 1** of the [email verification overview](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/11672225954971). Enter your domain in the text box. Leave out `https://` and `www`. Then, click **Register**.

If you've previously added a domain and want to add a new one, click **Add another**.

**Note:** If you manage multiple brands in your Greenhouse Recruiting account, you'll need to add and verify the domains for each brand.

**Note:** If you enter a [root domain](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/11672225954971#h_01GNJ7DV1873XH9E9QVNX3AE4S), Greenhouse Recruiting will automatically add `gh-mail` to the beginning of the URL. [Learn more.](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/11919501911835#h_01GPC9112QC6615GJJCDWWWGJJ)

When your domain has been registered, you'll receive a success message at the top of the page and the icon next to your domain will turn from an ellipses  to a check mark . Refresh the page to see your domain added to a table farther down the page.

### Update your DNS settings

#### Access your DNS settings

Find the area in your account where you can [edit your DNS settings](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/11919501911835-Email-domain-verification-FAQ#h_01GPC90TTRTTQWXMGDRZ0RW8DJ). The process of finding and navigating this section of your account will differ depending on the [DNS provider](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/11919501911835#h_01GPC90PMEZHSCB411TB6VM8Q4) you use.

#### Access your Greenhouse Recruiting values

Log in to your Greenhouse Recruiting account in a separate tab in your browser. Go to **Configure** > **Dev Center** > **Email Settings**.

Scroll down to the table. You should see columns for Type, Priority, Hostname, and Required Value.

To allow your Greenhouse Recruiting to send emails from your domain, you'll need to copy and paste the information from this table into your DNS settings.

Each row of values is known as a record. You'll need to add each record to your DNS settings individually. 

#### Add your Greenhouse Recruiting values to your DNS provider

**Note:** We recommend copying and pasting any existing values in your DNS settings in a separate place before making changes. If you need to revert your changes, you can refer back to this information.

After you've found out how to [update your DNS settings](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/11919501911835#h_01GPC90TTRTTQWXMGDRZ0RW8DJ), continue by adding a new record.

The information you enter for your new record will look something like this:

  * **Record type:** Copy and paste the value from the **Required Value** column in Greenhouse Recruiting
  * **Host:** Enter the domain or subdomain you chose in Step 1 of the [email verification overview ](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/11672225954971)
  * **Value:** Copy and paste the value from the **Required Value** column in Greenhouse Recruiting



**Note:** Make sure to copy the entire value.

  * **TTL (Time To Live):** Select the shortest amount of time



**Note:** This field is optional.

Enter a record for each row in your table.

### Test your DNS records

After configuring your DNS settings, go to the _Email Settings_ page in Greenhouse Recruiting and click **Check DNS Records Now**.

When the icons in the table turn from ellipses  to check marks , your domain has been verified.

If your icons don't change, double-check that you correctly entered the values from the table in Greenhouse Recruiting into your DNS settings. Then, click **Check DNS Records Now**.

### Additional resources

For a more comprehensive guide with additional information for IT teams, check out our article [here](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/201111684).

If you need help, visit our [FAQs](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/11919501911835) or reach out to the Greenhouse Recruiting [Technical Support](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/requests/new) team.

# Criteria HireSelect integration

Criteria is a leading provider of web-based, pre-employment testing services. Criteria's mission is to make high-quality pre-employment testing solutions accessible to companies of all sizes. The Criteria HireSelect testing system is a SaaS solution that enables organizations to better manage their most important asset — their human capital — by providing state-of-the-art assessment tools. Criteria HireSelect features aptitude, personality, emotional intelligence, and skills tests.

Greenhouse Recruiting's integration with Criteria HireSelect allows users to send Criteria assessments and receive results in Greenhouse Recruiting.

#### In this article

  * Setup Criteria HireSelect integration 
    * Request Assessment API key from Criteria
    * Create a Harvest API key
    * Create custom fields
    * Add the Criteria stage to your job's interview plan
  * Use the Criteria HireSelect integration
    * Send and review a Criteria test
    * Send Criteria tests in bulk
  * Additional resources



### Setup Criteria HireSelect integration

#### Request Assessment API key from Criteria

To configure the Greenhouse Recruiting / Criteria HireSelect integration, contact your Criteria Customer Success Manager to request your Assessment API key. Once you've received your key, [reach out to Greenhouse Technical Support](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/requests/new) to enable the key.

**Note:** Don't send your API key in this initial email. Greenhouse Technical Support will respond with a [SendSafely link](https://www.sendsafely.com/howitworks/) for you to securely share your API key.

Greenhouse Technical Support will email you to confirm once the API key has been set up.

**Note:** To verify your identity, Greenhouse Technical Support might request a [support verification code](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360022771952) before adding the API key to your organization's account.

### Create a Harvest API key for the Criteria HireSelect integration

To configure the integration, you'll also need to create a Harvest API key.

Follow the steps in [this article](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/5888163769883) to create the key, and verify that the credentials and permissions below are selected when configuring the key.

#### Credentials

In the _Create New Credential_ box, make the following selections:

  * **API type:** Harvest
  * **Partner:** Criteria HireSelect (optional)
  * **Description:** Criteria HireSelect Harvest API key



#### Permissions

Verify that the following permissions are selected for the Criteria HireSelect integration:

**Candidates**

  * PATCH: Edit Candidate



**Custom field options**

  * GET: Custom field options



When finished, click **Save**.

Your Harvest API key for the Greenhouse Recruiting / Criteria integration is created and configured. You will provide the Harvest API key to the Criteria team in a later step.

### Create custom fields

To create custom fields for the integration, click the **Configure** icon  on your navigation bar, then click **Custom** **Options** on the left.

Click **Candidates**.

Click **Add Field**.

Enter the following details:

  * Field name
  * Field type



When finished, click **Save**.

After you save the new field, the _Immutable Field Key_ will populate. Copy and save the immutable field key to provide to the Criteria team in a later step.

Repeat this process for all fields that are needed.

Once all fields are created, provide the following details to your Criteria Customer Success Manager so the can set up the integration:

  * Harvest API Key
  * User ID for integration requests (Check out [Create an ISU in Greenhouse Recruiting for an integration](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/4405511253659).)
  * Immutable field keys for custom fields



### Add the Criteria stage to your job's interview plan

Once the Greenhouse Recruiting / Criteria HireSelect integration is enabled for your organization, you'll be able to add the Criteria assessment as an interview stage.

To do this for an existing job, navigate to a job (**Jobs** > select your **Job**) and click **Job Setup**.

Click**Interview Plan** on the left, then click **\+ Add a Stage**.

From the _Add Stage_ box, select the Criteria stage.

When finished, click **Add** at the bottom to add the stage to the job's interview plan.

#### Configure the Criteria stage

Once the stage has been added to the job's interview plan, click **Edit**.

Use the dropdown menu to select the appropriate test battery for the job.

Scroll down to the _Graders and Notifications_ panel and select at least one Greenhouse Recruiting user to grade/review the assessments, then click **Save**.

**Note:** If you'd like to add additional testing to another stage, simply replicate the steps above. You may want to name the second testing stage something different so you can differentiate them (like 'Criteria 2' instead of 'Criteria'). To edit the stage name hover over the stage name and click the **Edit** icon.

### Use the Criteria HireSelect integration

#### Send and review a Criteria test

When a candidate is moved into the Criteria interview stage, Greenhouse Recruiting will display a **Send Test** link on the candidate's profile.

Click **Send Test** to deliver the test to the candidate.

**Note:** When you send a test from Greenhouse Recruiting, the interview instructions actually are sent to the candidate by Criteria.

Use the subsequent box to:

  * Confirm the email address of the candidate
  * Select which assessment / question set the candidate will participate in
  * Assign a grader



When finished, click **Send Test**.

**Note:** All configurations of the assessments, as well as the email templates, will need to be setup in Criteria HireSelect.

The test will be sent immediately with a link from Criteria to take the assessments.

Once the assessments are completed the graders, recruiter, and / or coordinator (depending on how you've configured notifications in Greenhouse Recruiting) will receive an email notification from Greenhouse Recruiting.

Click **View** **Report** on the candidate scorecard to see a PDF of the candidate's scores.

**Note:** The data in the custom fields and the link to the score report appear immediately upon completion of the assessments.

To view data in any configured custom fields, navigate to the candidate's profile and click the **Details** tab.

### Send Criteria tests in bulk

**Note:** Candidates must be in the same job and in the same stage (Criteria) in order to send the test in bulk.

To send the Criteria test in bulk, navigate to the**Candidates** tab and click the **Pipeline Tasks** filter on the left.

In the _Pipeline Tasks_ menu, click the _Test Status_ dropdown menu and select **To Be Sent**.

The list of candidates will be filtered to only those with tests to be sent. Navigate to the top right of the _All Candidates_ page and click **Bulk Actions**.

Check the boxes next to the candidates to whom you would like to send the test (or click **Select All**). Click **Edit Selected (#)** when finished.

Click **Send Tests**.

Review the details and click **Send Test**.

The tests will be sent to the selected candidates.

**Note:** If you select a different test than that which is associated with the job req, an email notification will not be sent to the grader from Greenhouse Recruiting when the results for those tests are completed.

### Additional resources

For additional information or troubleshooting not covered here, reach out to [integrations@criteriacorp.com](mailto:integrations@criteriacorp.com).

# Joveo CMS integration

Joveo’s Career Sites (CMS) empowers organizations to build hyper-personalized and dynamic career sites that reflect their brand identity while delivering a seamless and engaging experience for candidates. Designed to stand out in a competitive talent market, these career sites combine intuitive navigation with fast implementation, ensuring businesses can create impactful digital touchpoints without excessive timelines or costs.

You can realise the full potential of this integration if this is used with Joveo’s CRM integration.

The Mojo career sites are engineered to prioritize candidates, offering a highly interactive and efficient application process that minimizes time-to-apply. Integration with systems like Greenhouse ATS ensures a seamless flow of job data into the Joveo CMS, enabling near real-time updates and dynamic content across the site. This ensures candidates always see the latest opportunities, while recruiters benefit from streamlined workflows. By leveraging Joveo’s CMS, organizations can drive higher candidate engagement, maintain consistent brand messaging, and optimize hiring outcomes, transforming career sites into strategic assets for talent acquisition.

#### In this article

  * Contact the Joveo team
  * Create webhooks
  * Create a Harvest API key
  * Generate a job board API key
  * Field mapping
    * Job mapping
    * Candidate mapping
    * Application mapping
  * Use the Joveo CMS integration with Greenhouse Recruiting
  * Additional resources



### Contact the Joveo team

Customers should reach out to the Joveo team through [ats-partnerships@joveo.com](mailto:ats-partnerships@joveo.com) email or [contact Joveo](https://www.joveo.com/contact-us/) page. Once the customer decides to get onboarded to Joveo CMS - Greenhouse integration, the Joveo team will collaborate with the customer to perform the following steps.

### Create webhooks

To integrate **Joveo** with Greenhouse Recruiting, you’ll need to create 3 webhooks. Follow the steps in [this article](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/5888163727003) to create your webhooks. Use the values listed below to configure the webhook:

  * **Name:** A descriptive name for your integration. Most customers choose ‘**Joveo integration: ActionType** ’
  * **When:** Job updated, Job post created, and Job post updated.
  * **Endpoint URL:** The Endpoint URL provided by **Joveo**. It will be different per customer. Example: _https://api.joveo.com/ats/greenhouse/customer/${joveoCustomerId}/webhook-events_
  * **Secret Key:** This will be the customer secret key provided by **Joveo**.



### Create a Harvest API key

To configure the Joveo integration, you’ll also need to create a Harvest API key.

Follow the steps in [this article](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/5888163769883) to create the key, and verify that the permissions below are selected when configuring the Joveo integration.

#### Credentials

In the _Create New Credential_ box, make the following selections:

  * **API Type:** Harvest
  * **Partner:** Joveo or Unlisted Vendor
  * **Description:** Joveo Harvest API Key



#### Permissions

Verify that the following permissions are selected for the Joveo integration:

  * **Job Post**
    * GET: Retrieve Job Post
  * **Jobs**
    * GET: Retrieve Job
  * **Candidates**
    * POST: Add Prospect
    * Post: Add Attachment
    * Post: Add Application



### Generate a job board API key

Next, you’ll need to create a Job Board API key for Joveo.

Follow the steps in [this article](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/5888210160155) and use the information below when creating your API key:

  * **API Type:** Job Board
  * Partner: **Joveo** or Unlisted vendor
  * **Description:** **Joveo** job board API key



[Click here](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/13446638483355-Create-a-job-board-API-key-for-an-integration) for more detailed information on setting up a job board API key for a partner.

### Field mapping

#### Job mapping

The jobs are synced from **Greenhouse** to the **Joveo** system.

**Job and Job Posting fields ( Greenhouse )** | **Job fields ( Joveo)** | **Description**  
---|---|---  
**job_id** \- From the webhook event.**id** \- From the Job API and Job Post API.**internal_job_id** \- From the Job board API. | atsJobId | The ATS job ID.  
**name** \- From the Job API. **title** \- From the Job post API. **_(Higher precedence if job post exists)_** | title | The job title.  
**notes** \- From the Job API. **content** \- From the Job post API. **_(Higher precedence if job post exists)_** | description | The job description.  
**locations** \- From the webhook event. |  locations [ { 'state': state, 'country': country, 'city': city, 'isPrimary': True }] | The posted job location.  
**absolute_url** \- From the Job board API. | url | The job board url to apply for the job posting.  
**departments[0].name** \- From the webhook event. | department | The name of the job department associated with the job posting.  
**job_posting.live** \- From the Job post API. | status | When a job is created, posting is created but not published, Status - **CLOSED**.When a job is created, posting is created and published, Status - **OPEN**.  
**employment_type** \- From the webhook event. | remoteType | The employment type of job posting.  
**created_at** \- From the webhook event. | createdDate | The UTC datetime at which the job webhook event passed on the Joveo system for the first time.  
**updated_at** \- From the webhook event. | lastUpdatedDate | The UTC datetime at which the last job webhook event was received for job posting.  
— | updatedAt | The UTC datetime at which the last job webhook event was processed on Joveo for job posting.  
{ job_post_id } | customFields | The custom fields for Greenhouse customers to support customer specific custom business requirements.  
  
#### Candidate mapping

The candidates are synced from **Greenhouse** to the **Joveo** system.

**Candidate Fields (Greenhouse)** | **Candidate Fields ( Joveo)** | **Description**  
---|---|---  
**payload.candidate.id -** From webhook event. | atsCandidateId | The ats candidate id.  
**payload.candidate.first_name -** From webhook event. | firstName | The first name of the candidate.  
**payload.candidate.last_name -** From webhook event. | lastName | The last name of the candidate.  
**payload.candidate.email_addresses -** From webhook event. | email | The first non null email of the candidate.  
**payload.candidate.phone_numbers -** From webhook event. |  phoneNumbers Example: [ { "isPrimary": **null** ,  "countryCode": **null** ,  "phoneNumber": "9164350654",  "customFields": {  "type": "other"  } } ] | The phone number details of the candidate.  
**payload.candidate.employments -** From webhook event. |  workExperience Example: [ { "major": "Computer Science",  "degree": "",  "current": **null** ,  "endDate": "2021-01-14T00:00:00",  "location": **null** ,  "startDate": "2017-01-14T00:00:00",  "description": **null** ,  "institution": "",  "customFields": **null** } ] | The work experience of the candidate.  
**payload.candidate.can_email -** From webhook event. | canEmail | The boolean value to indicate whether email can be sent to a candidate or not.  
**payload.candidate.url -** From webhook event. | links | The link to the greenhouse candidate profile.  
**-** | insertedAt | The inserted datetime of the candidate on the Joveo system.  
**-** | updatedAt | The updated datetime of the candidate on the Joveo system  
**-** | customFields | The custom fields for Greenhouse customers to support customer specific custom business requirements.  
  
#### Application mapping

The applications are synced from **Greenhouse** to the **Joveo** system.

**Application Fields (Greenhouse)** | **Application Fields ( Joveo)** | **Description**  
---|---|---  
**payload.application.jobs[0].id -** From webhook event.  | atsJobId | The ats job id.  
**payload.application.candidate.id -** From webhook event. | atsCandidateId | The ats candidate id.  
**payload.application.id -** From webhook event. | atsApplicationId | The ats application id.  
**payload.application.status -** From webhook event. | status | The ats application status.  
**payload.application.source.name -** From webhook event. | source | The source of application.  
**payload.application.applied_at -** From webhook event. | createdDate | The applied datetime on Greenhouse.  
**payload.application.last_activity_at -** From webhook event. | lastUpdatedDate | The last updated datetime of application on Greenhouse.  
**-** | insertedAt | The inserted datetime of application on the Joveo system.  
**-** | updatedAt | The updated datetime of application on the Joveo system.  
**-** | customFields | The custom fields for Greenhouse customers to support customer specific custom business requirements.  
  
### Use the Joveo CMS integration with Greenhouse Recruiting

When jobs are posted by Greenhouse customers, it will be shown to the career site in near real time and when jobs are taken offline, jobs will be removed from the career site. 

For all the posted jobs, the Quick Apply feature is provided which redirects to web application form as shown below.  Based on customer requirements, the application form can be a basic application form or it can include job level screening questions. Once a candidate submits an application, an application will be submitted to Greenhouse.

After using the integration, you may decide you want to share more info between Greenhouse Recruiting and **Joveo**. If you would like additional information transferred over, please reach out to **Joveo** Customer Success with a list of items to add!

### Additional resources

For additional information not covered here, reach out to [ats-partnerships@joveo.com](mailto:ats-partnerships@joveo.com).
