# Create a custom report using Report Builder

**Permissions:** Job Admin and above

**Product tier:** Available for new subscription tiers (Core, Plus, and Pro)

**Tip** : For a more basic view of reports that require fewer permissions, check out [report dashboards](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/4408761575963).

#### Tailored reports to help you refine every step of the hiring process

[Report Builder](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360000954692) gives your organization the flexibility to customize reports so you can easily find data relevant to your goal. Building a report is intuitive – add and organize your data with a few simple clicks.  
You can live-preview the report as you're building it to see if you get the results and data you really need.

#### In this article

  * Create a custom report
  * Select report template
  * Customize report metrics
  * Apply report filters
  * Run and edit report
  * Share a report
  * Additional resources



### Create a custom report

To create a custom report using Report Builder, click **Reports** at the top of your navigation bar.

Click **Create** , then choose **Build a report**.  


### Select report template

Choose a report template type to begin. Report Builder offers two approaches to creating a report:

#### Build your own report

Building your own report allows you to create a report nearly from scratch. Select the category you wish to report on (such as candidates, jobs, or departments), and Greenhouse Recruiting will provide a few relevant metrics to help get you started. From there, edit the report's metrics and apply filters to create just the view you need.

#### Build report from template

Building a report from a template allows you to select one of Greenhouse Recruiting's essential reports as a starting point, and then edit the report's metrics to apply filters as needed.

[Click here](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360050783391) to learn more about the templates available in Report Builder.

When choosing a starting point, consider what specific question you aim to answer with the data from your report, and then use this to guide your template selection.

You can click into individual categories on the left to view the available templates, or search by keyword using the _Search_ field _._

**Example:** If you'd like to report on how many jobs were opened in 2022, navigate to the **Jobs** category and select the **Job Summary** report.

Click the report you wish to use as your starting point, and then click **Customize**.

You'll be directed to the _Custom report preview_ page, where you can adjust the report's default metrics and apply filters.

### Customize report metrics

**Note:** The options outlined in this section may not be available on all custom reports.

Next, add or remove columns using the _Settings_ on the left. Depending on the template you selected, you might see different options to adjust the report's columns.

To add a metric, click the **Add Column** dropdown and select from the list of available options.

To remove a metric, click the **X** icon to the right of the option.

To rearrange the order of the columns on the report, click the **Grid** icon to the left of the metric, and then **drag and drop** to the preferred location.

To clear all updates and return the report to its original settings, click **Reset** at the top.

To group rows by a specified characteristic (for instance, to group candidates by their assigned recruiter), click the _Group by_ dropdown at the top-right and select from the available options.

**Note:** The **Group by** list includes any single select, yes / no, or user field type available in the report. However, the **Group by** feature doesn't work if your report is exported / downloaded.

As you make changes to the _Columns_ or _Settings_ , the live preview of your report updates on the right side of the page.

**Note:** The live preview shows a maximum of five records. To see the full results, click **Run Report**.

### Apply report filters

To add or edit report filters, click the **Filters** button above the live preview.

To add a new filter, click **\+ Add Filter**.

For each filter you apply to a custom report, you'll select the following:

  * **Property** : The field or metric by which you want to filter the report data
  * **Operator** : The relationship between the property and the value
  * **Value** : The criteria applied to the property



Click the _Property_ dropdown to select the specific metric or data field to use as a filtering point. Next, click the _Operator_ and _Value_ drop-downs to specify the data you wish to see in your report, based on the _Property_ selection.

Report Builder allows you to apply and layer multiple filters. For additional filters, click **\+ Add Filter** again and repeat the steps above.

To remove a default or custom filter, click the **X** icon inline with the filter.

To clear all manually applied filters and return the report to its original settings, click **Reset** at the top of the panel.

To learn more about configuring filters in Report Builder, [click here](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360050783451).

### Run and edit report

When you're finished editing the filters, columns and metrics, click **Run Report** at the bottom to generate your custom report.

To adjust filters or metrics after running your report, click the **Edit Report** button at the top right of the _Custom Report_ page. You will be returned to the _Custom Report Preview_ page where you can make changes.

To export the report data, click the **Export to Excel download** button. 

An _.xlsx_ file containing the report data will be saved to your computer.

**Note** : The **Group by** feature doesn't work if your report is exported to Excel or [Google Sheets](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/115001875646). You'll need to recreate your grouping in the external app you use.

[Click here](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360050482292) to learn how to save a custom report so you can review it later, or schedule it to be sent to yourself and / or teammates at a recurring cadence.

### Share a report

To quickly share data with other members of your organization, you can email your created custom report to your colleagues. 

To share a report, navigate to your saved custom report by clicking **Reports** on your navigation bar.

Select **Saved** on the left. Open your report and click **Share**.

Select the recipient, email subject, and email body in the pop-up window.

When finished, click **Send Email**.

Your recipients will receive an email with the report. To learn what recipients see when they receive your emailed report, [click here](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/115003338503). 

**Learn more on using Report Builder in Greenhouse Recruiting**

[Report Builder overview](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360000954692)

[Report Builder filter guide](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360050783451)

[Report Builder template guide](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360050783391)

[Save, schedule, or email a custom report](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360050482292)

<!-- source: https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/208063316-Auto-merge -->

# Auto-merge

**Permissions:** Site Admin

**Product tier:** Available for new subscription tiers (Core, Plus, and Pro)

Duplicate candidate applications can cause confusion and significantly more work for your recruiting team. 

With Greenhouse Recruiting's auto-merge feature enabled, you can automatically merge new candidates and prospects who are entering your hiring pipeline as duplicates, which should drastically cut down on the amount of manual merging your team needs to do on a daily basis.

**Note** : Auto-merge does not work retroactively, so any duplicates currently in your account will still need to be [merged manually](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/115004506466).

The **Duplicate tag** in Greenhouse Recruiting helps your team quickly spot people who might already exist in your account. With duplicate tagging configuration, you choose which criteria (name, email, phone number, and LinkedIn URL) should trigger the [Duplicate tag](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/49207850415003-Configure-the-Duplicate-tag). The tag appears when a new person matches an existing person on any of the criteria you selected. 

For phone number checks, Greenhouse compares the underlying local number and ignores country codes. If the local number matches an existing person, the Duplicate tag can appear even when the country codes are different. 

The Greenhouse Recruiting Chrome extension also surfaces potential duplicates while you are sourcing candidates, but it does not use your duplicate tagging configuration. The extension always checks all four criteria (name, email, phone number, and LinkedIn URL) when it looks for duplicate profiles.

**Auto-merge** is stricter than duplicate tagging and only merges people who match the specific criteria you choose in your organization settings. You can configure auto-merge to match on email (with optional phone and/or LinkedIn), or on phone (with optional LinkedIn). Not every person with a Duplicate tag will be auto-merged; only profiles that meet your configured auto-merge criteria are merged automatically.

#### In this article

  * How to enable auto-merge
    * Optional: Set up LinkedIn URLs for auto-merge
  * Understanding the Greenhouse Recruiting data model
  * Cases where Greenhouse Recruiting will **not** auto-merge
  * Different-job merge cases
  * Same-job merge cases
  * Manually created candidates and prospects



### How to enable auto-merge

To enable auto-merge, click the **Configure** icon  on your navigation bar and then click **Organization** on the left.

From the _Organization_ page, toggle the button next to _Auto-Merge Candidates_ to **ON.**

Next, click **Manage criteria** to choose how Greenhouse should match and merge duplicate people:

  * **Email** – Matches and merges people who share the same email address. You can optionally require phone number and/or LinkedIn profile URL to match as well.



  * **Phone number** – Matches and merges people who share the same phone number. You can optionally require LinkedIn profile URL to match as well. 
    * When you use phone number as the only auto-merge criteria, Greenhouse only auto-merges profiles that share a phone number with a country code (for example, +1 212 555 1234). 
    * When you use phone number together with LinkedIn, auto-merge doesn’t require the country code to match. 
    * Older profiles or imports with phone numbers that don’t include a country code won’t be auto-merged based on phone alone.



**Note** : You can see the merge history in the **Activity Feed** on the candidate's profile. 

**Here are additional email-match scenarios to consider:**

If an email matches two different un-merged profiles in the system, Greenhouse Recruiting will assess the names of each existing profile to see if there is an identical match with the new applicant's name and merge any exact match.

If both preexisting profiles have identical email addresses and identical names, **or** identical emails and names that don't match the new applicant at all, the profile that has the most recent activity, as determined by emails, moved stages, rejections, or other activity, will be chosen and merged with the new applicant.

When deciding which criteria to use when combining profiles, Greenhouse Recruiting has identified a number of ambiguous cases where merging profiles seemed like it would cause more pain and frustration than it saved, so we opted not to automatically merge in these situations. For more information on cases where we purposefully do not auto-merge, click here.

#### Optional: Set up LinkedIn URLs for auto-merge

If you want auto-merge to use LinkedIn profile URLs as an additional match condition, first make sure you’re collecting LinkedIn URLs in a field that auto-merge can use.

  1. When you create or edit a job post, go to **Custom application questions**.
  2. Add a custom application question to ask for a LinkedIn profile URL.
  3. In the **Answers** section, select _Link answers to a custom field on the candidate’s profile_.
  4. For **Custom Field** , select _Social Media Addresses_. 



This setup saves LinkedIn URLs into the Social Media Addresses field on the candidate profile, which is the field used by both Duplicate tag and auto-merge when they look for LinkedIn matches. 

### Understanding the Greenhouse Recruiting data model

Before we explore different auto-merge cases, it's helpful to identify which information is candidate-specific and which information is application-specific to better explain how we decide which data to keep during a merge.

**Candidate-specific** information includes fields that can only have one value, no matter how many jobs a single candidate might be associated with. These include:

  * Name
  * Previous company
  * Previous title
  * Candidate custom fields



**Application-specific** information includes fields that can be different for each job a candidate is associated with. These include:

  * Stage
  * Source
  * Status
  * Recruiter
  * Coordinator
  * Application questions
  * Attachments



Information is never deleted in an auto-merge, so any deprecated fields will always be listed on the candidate **Activity** **Feed** after a merge. Additionally, a separate **Activity** **Feed** entry will inform you that a candidate or prospect was auto-merged in the first place.

**Example:** If **James Henry** applies online with an email address that matches the email of an existing candidate named **Jim Henry** , Greenhouse Recruiting can only choose one name to display for the merged profile, so the name belonging to the older profile (Jim Henry) will be removed and added to the candidate Activity Feed for posterity. For fields that support many entries, like phone number or address, we will simply save everything in a big list and let you decide which one to use later.

### Cases where Greenhouse Recruiting will not auto-merge

Greenhouse Recruiting will not auto-merge candidate profiles in the following scenarios:

  * **A candidate or prospect is created by a third-party integration (like Entelo, Hired, or Connectifier)** : Since we do not know how each and every third-party integration might be adding candidates and prospects to your account, any profiles created via the Candidate Ingestion API or Harvest API will not be evaluated by auto-merge.



**Note:** If you have given a Job Board API key to an integration partner, candidates they import could be merged automatically. Since API works just like your job board, we do not make a distinction between candidates they add and candidates who apply directly. This is an uncommon setup, but one we see every once in a while. You can see which API keys you have given out on the**Configure** >**Dev Center** >**API Credential Management** page.

  * **A candidate or prospect matches a candidate or prospect who is on one or more confidential jobs** : Because many users might not know that a confidential job even exists, we do not want to risk merging the profiles automatically and giving users insights that they shouldn't have about the candidate or the others jobs he or she might be on.


  * **An agency recruiter submits a candidate** : Since there could be questions about whether the agency should get credit for a duplicate candidate, we have decided not to merge in this case. Furthermore, some agency recruiters prefer to list their own email addresses instead of the addresses of their candidates, and it would be chaotic if every candidate from a particular agency was inadvertently merged into one giant, messy profile.


  * **A user submits a referral to Job A and they match someone else on Job A** : Much like with the agency recruiter situation above, there could be implications - (financial or otherwise) for one of your users losing credit for a referral. If two users submit the same referral, we have decided it is safer for one of your users to manually decide which user should get credit rather than choosing for you.


  * **A user submits a referral to Job A and they match someone else on Job** **B** : As a safeguard against the referrer being notified of the candidate applying to another job, we've decided that this should be a decision by one of your users to merge the profiles.


  * **A candidate applies or is added manually and matches a private candidate or prospect** : Because the concept of a private candidate applies to every job they're on, we want to protect against a case where a new candidate applies and is only accessible by a few select people. In this case we'll leave the two profiles separate so an Admin can determine whether they should have the same privacy settings or not.


  * **A candidate profile has had any data anonymized via candidate privacy tools**.



### Different-job merge cases

The easiest and most straightforward merge is done by combining candidates on two different jobs. While we still have to choose candidate-specific information that will apply to both profiles after the merge, all of the application-specific data will be preserved on each profile separately.

  * **A candidate is active on Job A, then applies online for Job B** : The two applications will be merged, with the candidate-specific information from Job A listed on the merged profile. This ensures that the hiring team from the older profile won't lose track of a candidate that they might already be working with.


  * **A candidate is rejected on Job A, then applies online for Job B** : The two applications will be merged, with the candidate-specific information from Job B listed on the merged profile. Since the old hiring team won't be dealing with this candidate anymore, the new team is assigned and will see that the candidate was previously rejected while in Application Review.


  * **A candidate is hired on Job A, then applies online for Job B** : The two applications will be merged, with the candidate-specific information from Job B listed on the merged profile. This might be common for internal applicants who are transferring to a different team or department. Rather than assign the team who initially hired them, the information from the new position will take precedence.



**Note** : If the hired candidate on Job A is marked "[private](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360039936051)," the two profiles will be kept separate.

### Same-job merge cases

When a duplicate is flagged for the same job, candidate- and application-specific information is sometimes merged into one profile, meaning a candidate applying to the same job 10 times from 10 sources could only end up with one listed on their source tab, while the rest will be deprecated on the Activity Feed.

  * **A candidate is active on Job A, then applies online for Job A** : The two applications will be merged, with the candidate-specific information from the older one listed on the merged profile. Any new information will be absorbed into the older profile and they will continue to be managed like they never applied a second time.



**Note** : The logic listed above will also apply to a prospect who matches an active prospect or any candidate.

  * **A candidate is rejected or hired on Job A, then applies online for Job A** : In this case, the two profiles will be merged, but every application will be preserved for your records.


  * **A candidate applies and matches any non-confidential prospect** : The name and source will be taken from the older, prospect profile, but the rest of the information will be added to a secondary prospect application on the same person.



### Manually created candidates and prospects

If a duplicate candidate or prospect is created via the prospecting plugin or the _Add a Candidate_ page, we handle things a little differently.

For users without permissions on the job or whose [job-based permissions](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360039518131) don't include the "**Can merge candidates and prospects"** permission, the new candidate or prospect will be added normally, with no information regarding a potential duplicate profile or a merge option presented to the user.

Once the duplicate candidate or prospect is added, the appropriate auto-merge rule will be applied. The user who submitted the candidate or prospect will not see a notification regarding the auto-merge.

For Site Admins and users with consistent Job Admin permissions on the job where they are adding the candidate / prospect, they will see the merge warning shown below.

If the user chooses not to merge the profiles, no auto-merge rule will be applied, and the profiles will not be merged.

# Add a custom offer field

**Permissions:** Site Admin, and Job Admin who can manage custom fields

**Product tier:** Available for new subscription tiers (Core, Plus, and Pro)

Offer fields provide a record of a candidate offer and can be used to generate additional documentation like offer letters and emails.

By default, Greenhouse Recruiting provides every organization with the following offer fields:

  * Employment type
  * Offer documents
  * Start date



You can also create custom offer fields to serve the needs of your organization. Custom offer fields can be used to track any offer data pertinent to your company.

### Create a new custom offer field

To create a new custom offer field, click the **Configure** icon  on your navigation bar, and select **Custom Options** from the left.

Click **Offers**.

The **Custom** **Options** > **Offers** page will list all of your organization's custom offer fields.

Click **Add Field** to create a new custom offer field.

Add information about the field on the _New offer field_ page.

Reference the table below for more information on settings available for custom offer fields:

**Offer field name** | **Description**  
---|---  
**Field Name** | The name of the custom offer field.  
**Description** | Additional context, direction, and/or summary displayed with the custom field.  
**Only show for offers made in these offices** |  Only shows the field when the job is associated with a selected office. **Note:** This option is only available for customers with an Advanced or Pro subscription.  
**Only show for offers made in these departments** |  Only shows the field when the job is associated with a selected department. **Note:** This option is only available for customers with an Advanced or Pro subscription.  
**Field type** |  The type of response that can be entered in the field. Once this option is saved, it cannot be changed. If the wrong type was selected, the offer field must be recreated. If you chose Single select or Multi select, enter each option in the available field. If you chose Currency for your field type, you'll also have a check box option for **This is a compensation field**.  
**Create new email token** |  Allows the information from the custom field to be included in email templates or offer document documentation. When this option is selected, you must enter the token text between the curly brackets. [Click here](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360039123751) for more information on offer tokens.  
**Required** | Makes the custom offer field a required field when creating any new offer.  
**Changes to this field trigger a new offer version** | Generates a new version of the offer if someone changes the field on the job. This step may require organizations to re-approve the offer in the workflow.  
  
When you're finished creating your new custom offer field, click **Save**.

# ServiceNow integration

**Permissions:** Owners

**Product tier:** Available for Greenhouse Welcome and Greenhouse Onboarding subscription tiers

ServiceNow is a customer service software and support ticketing system. If your organization uses ServiceNow as a [third-party task system](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360022403771), you can integrate it with Greenhouse Onboarding to send your onboarding tasks to ServiceNow via email.

#### In this article

  * Retrieve your ServiceNow email address
  * Enable the ServiceNow integration



### Retrieve your ServiceNow email address

Greenhouse uses your organization's ServiceNow email address to send [tasks](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360000525691) created in Greenhouse Onboarding to the ServiceNow ticketing system.

Contact your ServiceNow administrator to retrieve your ServiceNow email. You'll need this to enable ServiceNow as a third-party task system in Greenhouse Onboarding.

### Connect ServiceNow to Greenhouse Onboarding

Once you've retrieved your ServiceNow email address, log into [Greenhouse Onboarding](https://onboarding.greenhouse.io/).

From your Greenhouse Onboarding homepage, navigate to **Settings** > **Company Info** > **3rd-Party Task Systems**.

On the  _3rd-Party Task Systems_ page, click **Add New**.

Enter a **Name** for your task system and select ServiceNow from the **System** dropdown.

Paste your ServiceNow email address in the **Email Address** field.

Since your Greenhouse Onboarding tasks can include tokens (which may reveal personally identifiable information), you'll need to define which fields ServiceNow can view.

Use the **Viewable Fields (Optional)** dropdown to select which fields ServiceNow can view.

**Note:** If a task with non-viewable tokens is assigned to ServiceNow, Greenhouse Onboarding will block ServiceNow from accessing the information.

When you're finished, click **Save and Close**.

# Pool and stage reminders

**Permissions:** All users

**Product tier:** Available for Pro subscription tiers

Managing the next steps for multiple prospects across different pools and stages can be a challenge when those pools and stages have different workflows or timelines.

While Greenhouse CRM allows organizations to set reminders for individual prospects, you may quickly outgrow individual notifications as you increase the number of prospect pools and available prospects. To manage prospects at scale, you can configure reminders for an entire pool or stage.

#### In this article

  * Create a new stage reminder
  * Update a reminder
  * Review and complete your reminders
  * Export reminders
  * Reminder email example



### Create a new stage reminder

You can create a new reminder at the bottom of the _CRM_ page. _(**CRM** in navigation bar > **Create Reminder** in the right panel_)

Add the details for your reminder in the pop-up window.

**Field name** | **Description**  
---|---  
**Reminder Details** | A label or description for the reminder  
**Pool** | The prospect pool that should be associated with the reminder.  
**Stage (Optional)** |  The specific stage that should be associated with the reminder. If you choose a stage for a reminder, it will only apply to the specific prospects in that stage of the prospect pool.  
**Due Date** | The date on which the reminder email should be sent to Assigned Users.  
**Assigned Users** | CRM Admin and license holders who will receive the reminder.  
  
When you're finished, click **Create Reminder**.

The pool and stage reminder is created, and the Assigned Users will be notified on the selected Due Date. Additionally, the reminder will be added to the _Reminders_ panel for the Assigned Users.

### Update a reminder

To update an existing reminder, click the **Edit** icon on the _Reminders_ panel.

**Note:** Users can only edit pool and stage reminders where they are the creator or assignee.

### Review and complete your reminders

Once the pool and stage reminder is created, the reminder will appear in two locations for all Assigned Users:

  * On the _CRM_ page in the _Reminders_ panel, and
  * On the _My Dashboard_ page in the _My Reminders_ panel



**Note:** While the reminder will appear in the Reminders panel for the Assigned User immediately, the Pool and Stage Reminder Email is not delivered until the selected Due Date.

To **dismiss** an individual reminder, click the circle icon  on the left.

If you want to dismiss multiple reminders at once, click **Bulk Dismiss** in the top right corner of the page.

**Note:** You can only bulk dismiss reminders on the _All Reminders_ page, which can be found by clicking **See All** on the different reminders panels.

Select the reminders you want to dismiss and click **Dismiss Selected** in the top right corner.

### Export reminders

If you want to export a .csv of all your pending reminders, click See All on the reminders panel and click **Export to Excel** in the top right corner of the page.

**Note:** You can filter the reminders displayed on this page using the filters above the table.

### Reminder email example

On the assigned due date for the reminder, an email will be sent to any **Assigned Users**. you can quickly view the prospects associated with the reminder by clicking the link in the email.

Once the task is finished, you can mark it as complete in your _Dashboard_ or _Reminders_ panel.

# Business Intelligence Connector update: November 21, 2024

We are updating the Business Intelligence Connector on **November 21, 2024**.

[Download the updated schema](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/article_attachments/30772825379483)

### Overview of changes

This update to the Business Intelligence Connector includes some foundational work to prepare for improvements in 2025. 

As part of this work, this update adds the following four fields to the `Applications` table:

  * `recruiter_id`
  * `coordinator_id`
  * `recruiter`
  * `coordinator`



These fields - which are also available on the `Candidates` table - will update the Business Intelligence Connector to store recruiter and coordinator information on the application, rather than the candidate. 

Business Intelligence Connector users will then have until **January 31, 2025** to migrate their reports to the new fields. After January 31, 2025, the fields on the `Candidates` table will be deprecated.

# SkillSurvey integration

SkillSurvey's data-driven approach makes getting important, relevant feedback on candidates quicker, more cost-effective, and most importantly, more predictive of success through references. Greenhouse Recruiting's integration with SkillSurvey allows your organization to add an automated reference check stage to a job's interview plan.

#### In this article

  * SkillSurvey implementation plan
  * Create a Harvest API key for the SkillSurvey integration
    * Credentials
    * Permissions
  * Add SkillSurvey stage to the interview plan
  * Configure the SkillSurvey stage
  * Send and review the SkillSurvey assessment



### SkillSurvey implementation plan

To implement the Greenhouse Recruiting/SkillSurvey integration, you'll need to contact your SkillSurvey Custom Relationship Director (CRD) or [support@skillsurvey.com](mailto:support@skillsurvey.com). You'll participate in a kickoff call with SkillSurvey that will include:

  * A review of the integration
  * The requirements needed to set up the integration
  * The integration implementation steps and timeline



SkillSurvey will email Greenhouse Recruiting to request the integration for your SkillSurvey UAT (test) account.

Greenhouse Recruiting's support team will respond with a [SendSafely link](https://www.sendsafely.com/howitworks/) for SkillSurvey to submit the UAT credentials and URL. Greenhouse Technical Support then emails SkillSurvey confirming that the configuration has been set up in yourSkillSurvey UAT account.

When ready to go live, SkillSurvey will email Greenhouse Technical Support to request the integration configuration for your SkillSurvey production account. Greenhouse Technical Support will respond with a SendSafely link for SkillSurvey to submit the production credentials and URL.

Greenhouse Technical Support will email SkillSurvey confirming that the configuration has been setup in your SkillSurvey production account and your integration is ready to go live.

### Create a Harvest API key for the SkillSurvey integration

To configure the Greenhouse Recruiting / SkillSurvey integration, you'll need to create a Harvest API key.

Follow the steps in [this article](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/5888163769883) to create the key, and verify that the credentials and permissions below are selected when configuring the SkillSurvey integration.

#### Credentials

In the _Create New Credential_ box, make the following selections:

  * **API type:** Harvest
  * **Partner:** SkillSurvey
  * **Description:** SkillSurvey Harvest API key



#### Permissions

Verify that the following permissions are selected for the SkillSurvey integration:

**Applications**

  * GET: Retrieve Application



**Candidates**

  * GET: Retrieve Candidate



**Jobs**

  * GET: Retrieve Job



**Users**

  * GET: Retrieve Users



Provide the Harvest API key to your SkillSurvey onboarding team so they can set up the integration.

### Add SkillSurvey stage to the interview plan

Once the Greenhouse Recruiting / SkillSurvey integration is enabled for your organization, you're able to add the SkillSurvey assessment as an Interview stage.

Follow the steps in [this article](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/115002194903) to add the **SkillSurvery** stage to your job's interview plan.

### Configure the SkillSurvey stage

Once the stage has been added, click **Edit Take Home Test** on the interview plan. From there, you will see a dropdown menu that reflects the assessments (surveys) you have configured in SkillSurvey.

Select the appropriate **assessment (survey)** and then click **Save**.

An active SkillSurvey user needs to be assigned to the candidate that will be sent into the SkillSurvey Interview stage. SkillSurvey uses the email address listed under the **Source & Responsibility** to assign the Candidate to a Recruiter in SkillSurvey. This user will receive all SkillSurvey email notifications.

### Send and review the SkillSurvey assessment

Click **Send Test** under the _SkillSurvey stage_ on the candidate's profile to trigger the integration from Greenhouse Recruiting to SkillSurvey.

The Greenhouse user has an additional opportunity to modify the survey selected for the Candidate to send to their references.

Greenhouse checks for status updates sent from SkillSurvey every hour. Once the minimum amount of SkillSurvey references have responded, a link to create and view the SkillSurvey Candidate Feedback Report is sent to Greenhouse to be selected by the Recruiter.

The Greenhouse user will select the **Scorecard** link, then the SkillSurvey icon.

Next, select **View Report** to create and view the SkillSurvey Candidate Feedback Report

# Create and customize reporting dashboards

**Permissions:** Job Admin and above

**Product tier:** Available for new subscription tiers (Core, Plus, and Pro)

Custom dashboards allow teams to track key hiring metrics in one place. Users can create dashboards using prebuilt or custom widgets, arrange and resize them, and share or export visualizations for broader insights.

#### In this article

Use custom dashboards

What is a widget?

How to build a custom visualization (Plus and Pro subscription tiers)

Share a custom dashboard

Find your saved dashboards

### Use custom dashboards

To create a custom dashboard, click **Reports** on your navigation bar.

Click **Create** > **Custom dashboard**.

From here, you can choose to **Start from scratch** or choose from the list of _Essential dashboards_ to start with a dashboard that already has reports, then click **Create dashboard**.

To add reports to your new dashboard, click **Add widget** in the top-right corner. You’ll see several options for adding a widget:

  * **From widget library** – Choose from a set of prebuilt, ready-to-use widgets.
  * **From my saved custom report** – Use a widget based on a saved report created with the _Build your own template_ in the report builder. Widgets cannot be created from pipeline report types or from premade/essential reports.
  * **From scratch** – Build a new widget using the report builder.
  * **Text** – Add a simple text card to provide context or explanation.



**Note:** If your Greenhouse account is _Advanced_ or _Expert_ tier, you'll see more options under the **Add widget** menu.

Select a widget option and follow the prompts to configure it. You can rename the widget, adjust its filters, and choose how the data should be displayed. When you're done, click **Add widget**.

Now that the widget is added to your dashboard, you can hover over the bottom right side to resize it. You can also hover at the top of a widget to grab it and move it around.

Repeat this process to add more widgets to your dashboard.

#### What is a widget?

Widgets are visual building blocks of a dashboard. Each widget displays a chart, graph, or key metric based on a specific report. Clicking a widget title opens the full report view.

Users on the _Advanced_ and _Expert_ tiers can create custom widgets from scratch using the report builder. This allows for deeper customization, such as selecting specific data fields, applying filters, and choosing from different chart types.

#### How to build a custom visualization (Plus and Pro subscription tiers)

To create a widget from scratch, navigate to your dashboard:

Click Add **widget** > **From scratch**. Choose your report type and click **Customize**.

From the next screen, **Add columns** to and adjust any **filters** on your report and choose **Next: Build visualization**.

This is where you define how your data should appear on the dashboard.

In the Settings panel on the left, start by choosing the **Chart Type**. Available options may include bar, line, or pie chart types.

Under Axis, use the dropdowns to define how your data is grouped and measured.

  * **X-Axis** – Select the field to use for horizontal grouping (e.g., “Department Name” to compare by department).
  * **Y-Axis** – Choose the metric to measure (e.g., “Candidates Added” to display counts).
  * **Aggregate** – Define how to summarize the data. 
    * **Sum** – Adds all values together (e.g., total candidates added)
    * **Average** – Calculates the mean of all values
    * **Count** – Counts all entries, including duplicates
    * **Distinct** – Counts only unique values
    * **Max** – Displays the highest value in the group
    * **Min** – Displays the lowest value in the group
    * **Median** – Returns the middle value, reducing the impact of outliers



In the chart preview on the right, your selections will automatically update to reflect the changes.

To enhance readability, leave **Show tooltip on point hover** checked. This adds interactive data points when hovering over the visualization.

Once you're happy with the configuration, click **Add widget** in the top-right corner to add the visualization to your dashboard.

To view only relevant data across all widgets, click **Filters** at the top of the dashboard. Choose from a list of available options such as a job custom field, departments, offices or date ranges and the dashboard will update accordingly.

#### Share a custom dashboard

Custom dashboards can be shared with other users in your organization or exported as image files.

**Note:** Users who receive a shared dashboard can only adjust the global filters. They cannot edit widgets, drill into visualizations, or make changes to the dashboard layout.

To share a dashboard directly in Greenhouse, click the **Share** button in the top-right corner. A modal will appear where you can search for and select specific users. Once shared, those users will have access to view the dashboard in their My dashboards tab.

To share a static version outside of Greenhouse, click the **three-dot menu** in the top-right of the dashboard or any widget and select **Download as PNG**. This exports the visualization as an image that can be included in presentations, emails, or reports.

#### Find your saved dashboards

All of your custom dashboards are saved under the **My dashboards** tab in the Reports section.

From here, you can open, edit, or delete your dashboards.

# Create a form

**Permissions:** Site Admin, and Job Admin who can edit forms

**Product tier:** Available for new subscription tiers (Core, Plus, and Pro)

[Forms](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360019478952) allow your organization to collect additional structured data about a candidate after they have entered your system. Forms are created per job rather than organization-wide. For more information about how to manage forms across multiple jobs, [click here](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360019481932).

#### In this article

  * Create a form
  * Copy an existing form
  * Configure email to candidates
  * Configure a form
  * Form settings



### Create a form

To create a form, click**Jobs** from your navigation bar and select a job from the subsequent list.

Click **Job Setup** then select **Forms** on the left.

Click **Create a form**.

Now you can configure a new form or copy from an existing form.

### Copy an existing form

The _Create a form_ page allows you to create a form for this specific job. By default, the form and all of its details are blank. However, if you would rather copy a form from another job to use as a template, use the _Copy from existing form_ feature to copy a form from any job where you have Job Admin level access or above.

**Note** : Alternatively, you can create a new form from scratch without copying an existing form.

To copy an existing form from another job, navigate to the **Copy from existing form** dropdown menu on the right-hand side. Select a form from the dropdown menu.

Once the existing form is copied to your current workspace, you can edit the details of the new form without altering the original form.

Click **Save** when finished.

### Configure email to candidates

All forms are sent to candidates via an email that includes a special `{{FORM_LINK}}` token.

**Note** : Since forms are accessed through a token included in an email, you can only send forms to candidates who have an email address associated with their profile.

From the _Email to Candidate_ panel, choose from the _**From**_ dropdown menu whether the email should be delivered directly from your user account or from [no-reply@greenhouse.io](mailto:no-reply@greenhouse.io).

Next, configure the subject heading and body of the email using the available tokens in the right-hand panel.

**Note** : Remember to include the `{{FORM_LINK}}` token in the body of the email so that candidates can navigate to the actual form.

### Configure a form

When clicked, the `{{FORM_LINK}}` will direct candidates to the form configured in this step. Navigate to the _form_ panel, and give the form a candidate-facing name and an optional description.

Click the appropriate button to add a question, section header, or statement to the form.

**Note:** Every form must include at least one question.

#### Questions

Adding a question to the form allows you to pose a question to the candidate with the intention that it will be answered.

From the _Add Custom Question_ dialog box, input your question into the provided field and select whether a response is required.

### 

Next, use the _**Answers**_ dropdown menu to select how the candidate should respond to the question. Use the below table to help you understand what each answer option entails:

**Answer Type** | **Notes**  
---|---  
Link answers to a custom field on a candidate's profile |  Choosing this option allows you to link the candidate's response to an existing field on the candidate's profile. This will allow your organization to aggregate these responses in reports that allow custom fields. **Note:** Only the following custom field types are supported when linking answers to a custom field on the candidate's profile:

  * Short Textbox
  * Long Textbox
  * Yes / No
  * Single-select
  * Multi-select

  
Short Textbox | –  
Long Textbox | –  
Single-select | Candidates will select 1 answer out of the list of provided options. When configuring, place each option on its own line.  
Multi-select | Candidates can select multiple answers out of the list of provided options. When configuring, place each option on its own line.  
Yes / No | –  
Attachment |  Candidates can upload an attachment in response to the question and/or satisfy the answer requirement. Greenhouse Recruiting supports the following attachments on job forms:

  * .pdf
  * .doc
  * .docx
  * .rtf
  * .txt
  * .jpeg
  * .png

Attachments can be downloaded from the candidate's profile.  
  
Next, decide whether you would like to mark the question as private. Only users with one of the permission configurations listed below can view candidate responses to questions marked as private. For more information, please [click here](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360019755531).

  * Site Admins with the user-specific permission 'Can see private notes, salary info, manage offers, and approve job/offers,' or
  * Job Admins with the permission stripe 'Can view and edit private candidate and application fields'



**Note** : Responses linked to a custom field on a candidate's profile automatically inherit that field's permissions policy.

When finished, click **Add** to add the question to the form.

#### Section headers

A section header allows you to visually organize a form into different sections that contain relevant questions/statements.

#### Statements

Statements allow you to provide contextual information throughout the form and to possibly introduce each new section. Unlike questions, statements do not require any response from the candidate.

#### Reorder form components

To reorder any question, section header, or statement in the form, simply drag and drop to the desired position. 

### Form settings

The form settings panel allows you to determine when users are notified that a form needs to be sent and who is notified when a candidate submits a response. By default, the **Forms to send** tasks will always be assigned to the Recruiter on the job. For more information, [click here](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360019755771).

Use the stage dropdown to decide when the **Forms to send** task will be triggered for Recruiters. It is not necessary to tie a form to a particular Stage; however, without this setting, the **Forms to send** tasks will never be created.

**Note** : If a form is retroactively tied to a particular stage after the form has been created, the **Forms to Send** tasks is created for all candidates who are currently in or have passed the stage and is displayed as **overdue**.

Next, assign all users who should be notified of candidate submissions. Notifications can be assigned to whichever user is assigned to the recruiter and/or coordinator role, and specific users as well.

# Employee access

**Permissions:** Owners

**Product tier:** Available for Greenhouse Welcome and Greenhouse Onboarding subscription tiers

Greenhouse Onboarding provides default access for all employees in your organization to view and edit certain fields. This role is automatically assigned to any user who isn't a [Manager](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360021729772), [Coordinator](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360019575511), or [Owner](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360019575491) or hasn't been given [custom access](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360019516351).

**Note:** This tier acts as the default field permissions for Owner, Coordinator, and custom roles until your organization configures specific access settings for those roles.

#### In this article

  * Update employee access to fields
    * Can edit for oneself permissions
    * Viewable to company permissions
  * Additional resources



### Update employee access to fields

From your Greenhouse Onboarding homepage, navigate to **Settings**.

On the  _Settings_ page, navigate to **Data Flow** > **Permissions**.

Scroll to  _Default Access_.

Next to _Employee Access_ , click **Edit**.

Select or deselect the checkboxes to update whether or not employees can see the data. See the sections below for more detailed information on the permission types.

**Note:**

Fields marked with a red asterisk must be completed during an employee's onboarding.

Grey checkmarks and grey boxes indicate field permissions that can't be changed.

#### Can edit for oneself permissions

The **Can Edit for Oneself** permission allows employees to view and edit a field in their own [employee profile](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/4536840067611). If this checkbox is not selected, any updates to this field must be completed by an admin.

#### Viewable to company permissions

The **Viewable to Company** checkbox makes an employee field viewable to other users in your organization. Select this checkbox for each field that you want to display to everyone on an employee's profile.

Use different combinations of these checkboxes to configure the visibility and editability of your Greenhouse Onboarding data across your organization.

**Example:**

If you want a field to be both viewable to other employees and freely updated by the user, select both checkboxes.

In cases where you want a field to be visible but not editable, select the **Viewable to Company** checkbox but leave the **Can Edit for Onself** box unchecked.

In other cases, you may want an employee to be able to update a field in their profile but not display it to other users who view this employee's profile. In this situation, select **Can Edit for Onself** but leave **Viewable to Company** unchecked.

Leave both boxes unchecked if you don't want employees to edit a field in their profile and don't want this field's data viewable by other employees in your organization.

### Additional resources

Use these resources to learn more about configuring different access permissions in Greenhouse Onboarding:

  * [Greenhouse Onboarding permissions overview](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360018891992)
  * [Owner access](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360019575491)
  * [Coordinator access](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360019575511)
  * [Manager access](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360021729772)
  * [Custom access roles](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360019516351)

# Identify your organization's calendar email address

**Permissions:** Job Admin and above

**Product tier:** Available for new subscription tiers (Core, Plus, and Pro)

When you schedule an interview through Greenhouse Recruiting, a Greenhouse calendar email address must be included as a guest on the event. Including this email address as a guest ensures we receive details about the interview, such as the interviewer(s), the Interview Kit URL, any updates made to the event later, etc.

If you schedule directly in Greenhouse Recruiting using an integration such as Google Calendar or Outlook 365, the calendar email address is added as a guest to every interview automatically, with no action required on your end. However, if you use manual scheduling, Outlook for Mac, or if you schedule directly in your own calendar, you must add the appropriate Greenhouse calendar email address to every interview you schedule.

**Note:** If the Greenhouse calendar email address is not included as a guest, the interview and any subsequent updates to it will not be reflected in Greenhouse Recruiting.

Your organization is assigned a scheduling email address based on its silo. You can find the email address for your silo [here](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360056365191-Your-organization-s-silo).

Once you have the email, go to the profile of a candidate due to be a scheduled for an interview. Then, click **Schedule Interview**.

On the  _Scheduling for [Candidate]_ page, click the **Configure **icon in the top right corner. In the  _Settings_ window, click the _Calendar Type_ dropdown and select **Manual**.

When you finish, click **Save**.

The left side of the _Scheduling for [Candidate]_ page will display your organization's calendar email address. Copy this email address and save it in a secure location for future reference. Be sure to include this email address as a guest on every interview you schedule.

When you finish, click the **X** icon in the top right corner of the _Scheduling for [Candidate]_ page to exit the scheduling workflow and return to the candidate's profile.

# HRIS Link changelog

**Permissions:** —

**Product tier:** Available for Pro subscription tier with HRIS Link add-on

We regularly make updates and feature improvements to HRIS Link. This changelog shares HRIS Link's evolvement over time.

#### In this article

  * Changelog
  * Changes prior to September 2021



### Changelog

#### January 28, 2023

**Introducing HRIS Link management** – HRIS Link uses HRIS reports to import and update jobs, offices, departments, and user accounts from your HRIS to Greenhouse Recruiting. Now with HRIS Link management, you can now manage [HRIS credentials and reports](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/11006737633307) directly within Greenhouse Recruiting, saving time and enhancing your data security.

#### October 28, 2022

[HRIS Link user import](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360058975731) now supports required custom fields, if the field is required on the import report. Read more [here](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360059153471#h_01GGFKVFSW0JMQ5W1S1SK72QTF).

#### October 17, 2022

In addition to assigning users to departments and offices, HRIS Link now supports [custom user fields](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/7626796336283) on HRIS Link user import. Custom user fields allow you to capture and maintain user data unique to your organization. Read more [here](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360058975731).

Additionally, HRIS Link's default API key now includes the endpoint [DELETE: Destroy openings](https://developers.greenhouse.io/harvest.html#delete-destroy-openings).

#### March 25, 2022

We corrected an issue in which user syncs erroneously updated the incorrect Greenhouse Recruiting profile when the HRIS report included an employee ID but no email address. Now HRIS Link will present an error unless an email address is provided that matches an email address in Greenhouse Recruiting.

#### January 21, 2022

Automated export emails from HRIS Link now include the candidate name, job name, requisition ID, workflow ID, and export location in the email body.

#### December 10, 2021

HRIS Link email notifications now include the time that the workflow was run.

#### October 26, 2021

**Update to support assigning coordinator and sourcer with HRIS Link** – HRIS Link originally only included the ability to assign hiring managers and recruiters to the Greenhouse Recruiting [ hiring team](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/115002194983-Hiring-team-overview). Now HRIS Link will be able to assign users to all Greenhouse Recruiting hiring team roles, including coordinator and sourcer, as well as assign hiring team members a Job Admin level.

**How does this affect the HRIS Link integration?**

There is no impact to your existing HRIS Link integration, but you now have the additional option to assign the hiring team roles of coordinator and sourcer via HRIS Link by adding the relevant columns to your jobs report. You can review the job import report specifications [here](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360058912671-Report-specification-Import-jobs-from-Workday).

For more information on HRIS Link configuration options, click [here](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/4402422793485-HRIS-Link-configuration-options).

#### Changes before September 29, 2021

  * Adding openings to open requisitions
  * Supporting job post location for HRIS Link job import
  * Sending invitation email when creating user accounts with user sync
  * Maintaining office and department hierarchy with HRIS Link
  * HRIS Link for office and department import requiring external_id
  * Updates to the HRIS Link partnership key



#### Adding openings to an already open requisitions

**Can this option be be enabled / deactivated?**

No, this is standard integration functionality for HRIS Link.

**Note:** This option only applies if requisitions are enabled in your HRIS platform.

**How does this change the integration behavior for HRIS Link using position management with job requisitions?**

Historically HRIS Link didn't support adding positions to open requisitions after initial job creation. If a user were to add positions to the HRIS requisition, the additional positions would not appear in Greenhouse Recruiting as new openings on the corresponding Greenhouse Recruiting job. With this update, HRIS Link allows users to add positions to open requisitions in their HRIS and see those positions added as new openings in Greenhouse Recruiting.

**Does this update require adding any permissions to the HRIS Link API key?**

Yes, POST: Create New Openings. Check out the below table for an in-depth look at integration functionality.

**HRIS Link workflow** |  **HRIS Link report values** |  **Outcome** |  **Notes**  
---|---|---|---  
**Update job** |  HRIS Link job import report contains less job openings than were present on a Greenhouse Recruiting job. |  No job openings are removed from the Greenhouse Recruiting job. |   
HRIS Link job import report contains the same number of job openings that are present on a Greenhouse Recruiting job. |  No change to openings on the open job in Greenhouse Recruiting. |  The integration will not update or edit Position IDs that were historically on the report.  
HRIS Link job import report contains more job openings than are present on a Greenhouse Recruiting job. |  New job openings are added to the Greenhouse Recruiting job. The job openings in the HRIS Link report payload that are already present on the Greenhouse Recruiting job are not altered. |  If the existing Greenhouse Recruiting job is closed, we will not add any new job openings.  
  
#### Supporting job post location for HRIS Link job import

**Is this a configuration option that can be enabled/deactivated?**

No, this is standard integration functionality for HRIS Link.

**How does the integration behave with the new report header?**

If an organization provides the report header of Job_Post_Location, the integration will be able to apply a job post location-based on Greenhouse Recruiting office external id.

**Note** : This feature only works if your organization leverages a [structured job post location](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360027858591-Configure-structured-job-post-location) based on your organization's office list.

#### Sending invitation email when creating user accounts with user sync

**Is this a configuration option that can be enabled / deactivated?**

No, this is standard integration functionality for HRIS Link.

**How does the integration behave with the new report header?**

This update will only affect new user creation. When the “send_email_invite” report header is included and the values provided meet the report specifications, organizations will be able to trigger invitation emails to users upon creation of their Greenhouse Recruiting accounts via HRIS Link.

**Does this update require adding any permissions to the HRIS Link API Key?**

No.

#### Office and department hierarchy with HRIS Link

**Is this a configuration option that can be enabled/deactivated?**

No, this is standard integration functionality for HRIS Link.

**How does the integration behave with the new external_parent_id report header?**

This update will only affect new department and office creation. HRIS Link will not maintain office or department hierarchy updates that happen after initial office / department creation with HRIS Link.

When creating an office or department, HRIS Link will audit the report to see if the report header `external_parent_id` is included in the report for the new office or department. If the new office or department has a valid “parent_external_id” included, the office or department will be created in Greenhouse Recruiting subsidiary to the office / department with the corresponding `external_parent_id` in Greenhouse Recruiting.

**Does this update require adding any permissions to the HRIS Link API Key?**

No.

#### HRIS Link for office and department import requiring external_id

**How does this affect the HRIS Link integration?**

Previously we suggested that customers include external_ids for offices and departments that utilize HRIS Link. When HRIS Link expanded functionality to support hierarchy creation, the external_id report header became required for HRIS Link.

If a new office or department is created in the HRIS without an external_id and appears on the HRIS Link report, the integration will ignore said office or department on that integration run.

**Does this update require adding any permissions to the HRIS Link API Key?**

No.

#### Update to HRIS Link partnership API key

On September 23, 2021, the Greenhouse Technical Consulting team works with the Greenhouse Partnership team to create an API key that is automatically provisioned with the appropriate API key permissions for the HRIS Link integration. As the integration expands functionality with additional [ configuration options](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/4402422793485-HRIS-Link-configuration-options), the API key permissions need to be updated.

In this case, Greenhouse Recruiting updated the following API key permissions:

  * GET: List Job Post for Job
  * DELETE: Delete job
  * POST: Add hiring team member



**How does this affect the HRIS Link integration?**

If you are a current HRIS Link client, you will want to check the API key permissions for the Harvest API key that is used for the integration to ensure that the above API Key permissions are equipped.

If you have further questions about this update, reach out to [Greenhouse Technical Support](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360058320292).

# Data Facts integration

Data Facts provides Human Resource Professionals with cutting-edge, top-of-the-line background screening technology and personalized support and service.

Greenhouse Recruiting's integration with Data Facts allows users to send a background check request form to candidates automatically from within Greenhouse Recruiting. 

#### In this article

  * Create a Harvest API Key for the Greenhouse Recruiting / Data Facts Integration
    * Credentials
    * Permissions
  * Create a webhook
  * Provide Data Facts a Greenhouse Recruiting User ID
  * Create custom candidate fields
    * Field 1: Background package
    * Field 2: Background Report
  * Add background check stage to interview plan
  * Use the Data Facts integration



### Create a Harvest API Key for the Greenhouse Recruiting / Data Facts Integration

To configure the Greenhouse Recruiting / Data Facts integration, you'll need to create a Harvest API key.

Follow the steps in [this article](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/5888163769883) to create the key, and verify that the credentials and permissions below are selected when configuring the Data Facts integration.

#### Credentials

In the _Create New Credential_ box, make the following selections:

  * **API type:** Harvest
  * **Partner:** Data Facts
  * **Description:** Data Facts Harvest API key



#### Permissions

Verify that the following permissions are selected for the Data Facts integration:

  * **Activity Feed**
    * GET: Retrieve Activity Feed
  * **Candidates**
    * GET: Retrieve Candidate
    * GET: List Candidates
    * PATCH: Edit Candidate
  * **Custom Field Options**
    * GET: Custom field options
    * POST: Create custom field options
    * PATCH: Update custom field options
  * **Users**
    * GET: Retrieve User
    * GET: List Users



### Create a webhook

To integrate Data Facts with Greenhouse Recruiting, you'll need to create a webhook. Follow the steps in [this article](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/5888163727003) to create your webhook. Use the values listed below to configure the webhooks.

  * **Name** : A descriptive name for your integration. Most customers choose 'Data Facts integration'
  * **When** : Candidate has changed stage
  * **Endpoint URL** : [https://apiaN.tiltingwindmills.com/service/grnhs/[WILL BE PROVIDED]/ApplicantEvent ](https://apiaN.tiltingwindmills.com/service/grnhs/\[WILL%20BE%20PROVIDED\]/ApplicantEvent%C2%A0)
    * _**Note** : Production host is assigned at go-live. _The "N" in apiaN is specifically assigned (apia1, apia2, etc.) at go-live
  * **Secret Key** : The XML username set up for the integration
  * **Error Recipient Email:** A responsible party from the client, and other parties that need to be notified of Greenhouse Recruiting errors



### Provide Data Facts a Greenhouse Recruiting User ID

In order to send information from Data Facts to Greenhouse Recruiting using the Harvest API key, Data Facts will need a Greenhouse Recruiting User ID to associate with the data. This user account must be a Site Admin, but does not require any additional user-specific permissions. You can also [create a new user](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360027077811) for this integration.

To retrieve this User ID, [export your user list to Excel](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/200521129) and find the correct User ID in the list. Then, provide this User ID to the Data Facts team.

### Create custom candidate fields

This portion of the configuration allows you to select a background screening package for the candidate, as well as to receive a URL to the candidate's results after the background screening is completed by Data Facts. 

Create two custom users field using the following options.

#### Field 1: Background package

  * Field Name: Background Package
  * Type: Single-select



#### Field 2: Background Report

  * _Field Name: Background Report_.
  * Type: URL



After its created, each field will have an Immutable Field Key. Provide both keys to the Data Facts team.

### Add background check stage to interview plan

Next, [modify an interview plan](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/115002194903) and add a background check stage.

You'll need to repeat this step for each job that you want to integrate with Data Facts. 

### Use the Data Facts integration

You can request a candidate's background check by moving them to the Background Check stage.

Before they can be moved into the stage, you'll need to select the background package under the **Details** tab on their candidate profile.

Under the _Additional Details_ panel, find the Custom Candidate Field named _Background Check_ and select the correct package from the dropdown. Click **Save** when you are finished.

Once the package is chosen, advance the candidate to the Background Check stage. The candidate information will be sent to Data Facts to begin the background screening process. You can see updates about the status of the background screening by clicking the URL in the _Background Report_ Custom Candidate Field.

**Note:** The background screening request is sent to Data Facts as soon as the candidate is moved to the Background Check stage.

If the candidate is moved to the Background Check stage before the Background Check Package is selected, no information about the requested package will be sent to Data Facts. To resolve this issue, move the candidate backward one stage, select the **Background Check Package** , and then advance the candidate to the Background Check stage again.

# Report templates overview

**Permissions:** Site Admin, and Job Admin who can create, edit, and delete organization report templates

**Product tier:** Available for new subscription tiers (Core, Plus, and Pro)

#### Save time and improve consistency in reporting

Report templates allow you to drive a consistent framework for reporting so everyone is measuring, iterating, and improving your processes based on the same metrics. Your recruiting teams can save time by using report templates, rather than having to create reports from scratch. Once a report template is created, people in your organization can create reports from the template with [Report Builder](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360000954692).

#### In this article

  * Create a report template
  * Create a report from a report template
  * Edit a report template
  * Additional resources



### Create a report template

To create a report template, you'll first create or open an existing custom report with [Report Builder](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360000954692).

To begin, click **Reports** on your navigation bar.

Choose an existing _saved report_ from **My reports** or click **Create > Report template.**  


On the subsequent page, choose a starting point for building your custom report. Consider what specific question you aim to answer with the data from your report, and select or search for the report you wish to use as your starting point. Then click **Customize**.

On the next page, use the _Settings_ on the left to edit your report's configuration. Depending on the template you selected, you might see options to adjust the report's columns, metrics, chart type, timeframe, or other configurations. Add and remove columns to layer the data as you need.

You can further refine the report's data using _Filters_ on the right side of the page. To add a filter, click **Filters**.

Then click **\+ Add Filter**.

Report Builder allows you to apply and layer multiple filters. For additional filters, click **\+ Add Filter** again.

To learn more about configuring filters on Report Builder, [click here](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360050783451).

When you're finished editing the filters, columns, and metrics on your report, click **Run Report**.

Your custom report will generate. You can now save your report as a report template for others to use by selecting **Save** > **Save as template**.

**Note** : In order to save a report template, you'll need to be a Site Admin, or a Job Admin with the user-specific permission 'can create, edit, and delete organization report templates.'

Enter a name for your report template, and click **Create** **template**.

Your report template is now created and configured! Others in your organization will be able to create a report using your report template.

### Create a report from a report template

Once a report template is created, you can create a custom report from the template.

**Note** : You must be at least Job Admin on a job to create reports in Greenhouse Recruiting.

To create a report using a report template, click **Reports** on your navigation bar.

Click **Create** , then choose **Build a report**.  


On the next page, click **Templates**.

Select the report template you'd like to use, then click **Customize**.

On the next page, use the _Settings_ on the left to edit your report's configuration as needed. Depending on the template you selected, you might see options to adjust the report's columns, metrics, chart type, timeframe, or other configurations.

Add and remove columns to layer the data as you need.

**Note** : Any changes you make to your report only affect the individual report you're creating – not the report template. To learn more about editing a report template, click here.

You can also refine your data further using _Filters_ on the right side of the page. To add a filter, click **Filters** , then click **\+ Add Filter**. Report Builder allows you to apply and layer multiple filters. For additional filters, click **\+ Add Filter** again.

To learn more about configuring filters on Report Builder, [click here](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360050783451).

When you're finished editing the filters and metrics on your report, click **Run Report**.

### Edit a report template

To edit an existing report template, click **Reports** on your navigation bar.

Click **Report templates** on the left.

Find your saved report template in the _Report templates_ list, and hover over it to select the **Edit** icon.

On the subsequent page, you can adjust your report template's metrics, filters, and other settings. Click **Save template** to save your changes.

Delete a report template

To delete a report template, return to the **Report templates** tab and hover over your report to select the **Delete** icon .

**Note** : Deleting a report template doesn't affect any reports that have already been created using the template.

Confirm your choice by clicking **Delete** **template**.

### Additional resources

  * [Report Builder overview](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360000954692)
  * [Report Builder filter guide](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360050783451)
  * [Report Builder template guide](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360050783391)

# Create an ISU for an integration

**Permissions:** Site Admin who can edit another user's advanced permissions

**Product tier:** Available for new subscription tiers (Core, Plus, and Pro)

Access the latest version of Harvest API documentation at [**harvestdocs.greenhouse.io**](http://harvestdocs.greenhouse.io).  
  
Harvest API v1 and v2 will be deprecated and unavailable after August 31, 2026. Please make sure that your existing custom integrations use the latest version of Harvest (v3) by this date and any new integrations are developed with the latest version of Harvest API.

[Integrations](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360039539972), custom integrations, and HRIS platforms use [Greenhouse APIs](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/10568627186203) to import and update jobs, offices, departments, users, and other data in Greenhouse Recruiting.

We recommend creating an integration system user (ISU) to associate with these integration requests.

**Note:** In Harvest v3, when generating a client credential, an integration service user (ISU) is automatically generated and associated with these credentials. [Learn more about authenticating here.](https://harvestdocs.greenhouse.io/docs/authentication)

#### In this article

  * What is an ISU?
  * Create an ISU



### What's an ISU?

An integration system user (ISU) is a Greenhouse Recruiting user profile created for the purpose of running an integration. Rather than requiring a specific user at your organization to authenticate an integration, which could cause downstream errors if the person loses permissions or cannot access Greenhouse Recruiting, an ISU allows you to create a solid infrastructure for your organization's integration needs.

Additionally, the ISU will appear in all audit logs and reports, eliminating confusion about who performed a specific action.

### Create an ISU

To create an ISU in Greenhouse Recruiting, click the **Configure** icon  on your navigation bar and then click **Users**.

Click **\+ New Users** on the next page.

Enter an email address to be associated with the ISU.

**Note:** The ISU's email address should not be associated with a real user. The email address doesn't need to have a working inbox, because the ISU isn't required to log in to Greenhouse Recruiting, but the email address should use your company's domain.

Under the _Set permissions_ section, click **Site Admin** , and grant the ISU all Site Admin user-specific permissions.

When finished, click **Save**.

Once the ISU is created, locate the ISU in your users list (**Configure** > **Users**) and update the user's name to `{integration_name} ISU`.

When finished, click **Save**.

Your ISU is created and configured! You can [locate the ISU's user ID](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/10765948752027) to share with the integration if needed.

# Send a candidate’s interview schedule to interviewers

While interviewers can see a candidate's interview schedule in their [interview kit](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/115002226826), you may also want to send the schedule to interviewers via email. When you use the template in an email to the hiring team, the candidate's interview schedule will appear in the body of the email, along with any other text you provided when creating the template.
