# Schedule an interview to a shared calendar with Google Calendar

**Permissions:** Job Admin or above

**Product tier:** Available for new subscription tiers (Core, Plus, and Pro)

After you enable the [Google Calendar](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360021799232) integration, you can schedule interviews to personal or shared calendars on Greenhouse Recruiting.

**Tip** : Learn how to [schedule to a personal calendar](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360022018271).

#### In this article

  * Schedule an interview



### Schedule an interview

**Note:** To schedule to a shared calendar, you need permission to 'Make changes to events' on the shared calendar. Learn more about how to [create and manage a shared calendar on Google Calendar](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360022161532).

The scheduling process for shared calendars is the same as scheduling an interview to a personal Google Calendar, except you need to select the shared calendar from your calendar settings.

**Tip:** We recommend that you [request the candidate's availability](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/205628255) before scheduling an interview. 

Find the interview on the Stages tab of the candidate profile and click **Schedule** under your **Tasks**.

Your calendar settings are automatically selected based on your user account. Click the **Settings** icon to change to a shared calendar. 

Select the time zone, calendar type, and the shared calendar name. 

**Note:** The time zone dropdown defaults to your [Greenhouse Recruiting account time zone](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360001615351). Interviews scheduled between time zones are [automatically adjusted for the interviewer and the candidate](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360000157052) to reflect their respective time zones.

When finished, click **Save changes**. Your calendar settings will be automatically selected the next time you schedule an interview. You can switch between personal and shared calendars this way when scheduling interviews.

Next, select the interview details like date, time, and interviewers on the left. 

**Tip** : If your organization's Google Admin has configured calendars for conference or interview rooms, they can be selected in the _Resources_ dropdown. If you select a resource, it'll be added directly to your interview invite. [Learn more about scheduling resources](https://support.google.com/calendar/answer/143753).

If the candidate submits availability for the interview, it's shown in white blocks on the calendar. Availability for a selected room or resource is also shown on the calendar.

Select a time slot for your interview by clicking an open section on the calendar. You can adjust the start and end times on the left.

If you're having trouble finding an open slot on a specific day, navigate between days at the top of the page. 

**Note:** To see the availability of a member of your hiring team, you need 'Make changes to events' permission on the interviewer's calendar. [Learn more on Google](https://support.google.com/calendar/answer/37082?hl=en).

When finished, click **Customize details**.

On the next page, verify that the interview details are correct.

You can select an interviewer invite template from the dropdown, or type a message in the description field.

If you want to notify interviewers of the event by email, check **Send an email update to all interviewers**.

When finished, click **Send invites to interviewers**.

**Note:** Greenhouse Recruiting is added to all of your interviews as a guest. This ensures the interview syncs to Greenhouse Recruiting.

When you send invites, all listed interviewers will be displayed on the event as attendees.

**Tip** : Send an [interview confirmation email](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360015975112) to the candidate so they're informed of the interview details.

**Learn more**

[Google Calendar integration](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360021799232)

# Create and manage interviewer groups

**Permissions:** Site Admins, Job Admins who can manage company metadata

**Product tier:** Available for new subscription tiers (Core, Plus, and Pro)

It can be challenging to determine which interviewers should be handling which interviews if there are dozens (or even hundreds) of interviewers across multiple departments and offices in your organization.

Interviewer groups allow you to quickly identify and segment interviewers using custom labels that are unique to your organization.

#### In this article

  * Create an interviewer group
  * Add interviewers to a group
  * Add a training program to an interviewer group
  * Delete an interviewer group
  * Merge duplicate interviewer groups
  * Assign or unassign an interviewer group
  * Find grouped interviewers when scheduling an interview



### Create an interviewer group

To create a new interviewer group, click the **Configure** icon in the upper right corner and select **Interviewer Groups** from the left panel.

Click **Create New Interviewer group**. 

Enter a name for the group and click **Create**.

### Add a training program to an interviewer group 

If your organization uses interview-based training programs (such as shadowing) to train interviewers, they can be managed under the **Training Settings** tab on the interviewer group.

Then, when a user assigned to the group is added to an interview using the same group as a default group in the interview kit, it'll be counted toward their overall interview progress. 

[Read more about interview training programs here.](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/35379383064859)

### Delete an interviewer group

**Note** : When an interview group is deleted, it will be automatically removed from all users and can't be assigned to new users. When you delete a group, you can reassign the currently grouped users to another existing group. However, once it's deleted, an interview group can't be restored. 

Click **Remove** next to the interviewer group you want to delete.

Select whether or not you'd like currently grouped users to be assigned to a new group by selecting an option in the window. If you're reassigning users to a new group, select it from the dropdown menu.

**Note:** Users can only be reassigned to an existing group. If you need to assign users to a brand new group, [create it](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/205982075) before deleting the current group.

When you're ready, click**Delete Interviewer group.**

### Merge duplicate interviewer groups

Greenhouse Recruiting doesn't allow you to directly merge two duplicate interview groups. However, by deleting one group and reassigning current users to the second group, you can simplify any repeated interviewer groups in your organization. 

Select the duplicate group in the **I want any entity using this interviewer group to use this instead** field.

When you're finished, click **Delete Interviewer group**.

### Assign or unassign an interviewer group

#### Assign an interviewer group to a user

**Note:** Interviewer groups can be assigned or unassigned by Site Admins.

To assign an Interviewer group to a user in your organization, navigate to the Interviewer Groups page and open the interviewer group. 

Click **Add interviewers** above the table. 

Choose users from the list and click **Add**.

Interviewer tags can also be assigned on a user's profile by choosing an option in the _Interviewer groups_ section. Select a group from the dropdown or click **Configure Interviewer groups** to add a new group and scroll to the bottom of the section and click **Save user details**.

**Note:** A user can be assigned multiple interviewer groups.

#### Remove an interviewer group from a user

Users can be removed from a group by clicking the three dots next to their name and selecting **Remove from this group**.

Alternatively, it can be removed from their user profile by clicking the **X** icon and scrolling to the bottom of the section and click **Save user details**.

### Find grouped interviewers when scheduling an interview

After you have assigned Interviewer groups to users, you can set default interviewer groups to automatically scan users during [automated scheduled](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/36307427046555).

# Greenhouse Notetaker setup

**Permissions:** Site Admin

Greenhouse Notetaker records interviews in the background so interviewers can stay focused on the conversation and structured hiring practices. When filling out scorecards, interviewers can review interview transcripts and AI-generated notes to quickly complete feedback without losing interview context.

This feature is currently in beta and may not be available to your organization.

#### In this article

  * Turning on Greenhouse Notetaker for your organization
  * Update permissions
  * Enable on a job
  * Adding a notetaker to an interview
    * Candidate consent
  * Additional resources



### Turning on Greenhouse Notetaker for your organization

As a participant of the beta, Greenhouse Notetaker is already enabled for your organization.

### Update permissions

Site Admins can give Job Admins permission to view other interviewers' notes and transcripts.

Go to Configure, then select **Permissions** _****_ from the left-hand menu. Find _**See and manage Job Admin levels**_ on the page and select it.

Select which Job Admin levels should receive the permission _Can view AI notetaking recordings, transcripts, and notes._ It's required for Job Admins to also have _Can view and edit candidates and prospects_ permission to view other interviewers' AI notetaking materials.

### Enable on a job

A Site Admin or a Job Admin with permission to manage the job can enable Greenhouse Notetaker for interviews in the interview plan.

To enable Greenhouse Notetaker, open the job and go to **Job Setup** > **Interview Plan**.

In the _Additional Settings_ section at the bottom of the page, select the checkbox for **Enable Greenhouse Notetaker**.

After you enable Greenhouse Notetaker, choose which interviews should include a notetaker:

  * **All interviews** adds a notetaker to every interview in the interview plan, including interviews that are already scheduled.
  * **Only interviews scheduled or updated moving forward** adds a notetaker only to future interviews and interviews that are rescheduled after this setting is selected.



When Greenhouse Notetaker is enabled for a job, candidates see a disclosure that interviews may be recorded when scheduling interviews. Candidates can choose to opt in or opt out of interviews that use recording and transcription. Their selection applies to all future interviews in the hiring process.

### Adding a notetaker to an interview

You can also add a notetaker to an interview manually if Greenhouse Notetaker is enabled for the job and the candidate has opted in to recording and transcription. For example, a notetaker may not have been added automatically if the candidate recently updated their consent status.

To add a notetaker, click the ellipsis icon next to the interview and select **Add notetaker to interview**.

#### Candidate consent

If you're recruiting for a role where the candidate may not encounter the disclosure while scheduling an interview, such as an internal role, we recommend including the disclosure when communicating interview details to the candidate during your beta participation.

**Example:**_" Interviews may be recorded and transcribed so interviewers can focus on the conversation rather than taking notes. Greenhouse Notetaker, an AI-powered feature, may use the transcript to generate interview notes and summaries. You can opt out now or at any time before the interview begins by contacting your recruiter."_

### Additional resources

  * [Use Greenhouse Notetaker to record and summarize interviews](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/50523570982939)
  * [Scorecard overview](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/4414777492891)

# AccusourceHR integration

AccusourceHR's services range from employment screening and background checks to more strategic and advanced Human Capital Due Diligence services like Executive Screening. The Greenhouse Recruiting / AccusourceHR integration allows you to automatically take newly-hired candidates from Greenhouse Recruiting and add them to AccusourceHR.

#### In this article

  * Retrieve your Endpoint URL and Secret Key from AccusourceHR
  * Create a Harvest API key for the AccusourceHR integration
    * Credentials

  * Create a webhook
  * Create custom candidate fields 
    * Field 1: Background check status
    * Field 2: Background check completed date
    * Field 3: Background check result
  * Create custom job fields
    * Field 1: Background Check Package
    * Field 2: Background Check Package
  * Use the AccusourceHR integration



### Retrieve your Endpoint URL and Secret Key from AccusourceHR

To link your Greenhouse Recruiting account, contact AccusourceHR Customer Success for an **Endpoint URL** and a **Secret Key** you will need to get started. Once you have both of those items, complete the following steps to link your accounts.

### Create a Harvest API key for the AccusourceHR integration

To configure the Greenhouse Recruiting / AccusourceHR integration, you'll need to create a Harvest API key.

Follow the steps in [this article](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/5888163769883) to create the key, and verify that the credentials and permissions below are selected when configuring the AccusourceHR integration.

#### Credentials

  * **Partner:** AccusourceHR

#### Permissions

Contact AccusourceHR for a list of permissions that must be selected for this integration.

### Create a webhook

To integrate AccusourceHR with Greenhouse Recruiting, you'll need to create a webhook. Follow the steps in [this article](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/5888163727003) to create your webhook. Use the values listed below to configure the webhooks.

  * **Name** : A descriptive name for your integration. Most customers choose 'AccusourceHR integration'
  * **When** : Candidate has changed stage
  * **Endpoint URL:** The Endpoint URL provided by your AccusourceHR representative
  * **Advanced Settings:**
    * **Username and Password:** The Secret Key provided by your AccusourceHR representative 
    * **Disabled:** No



### Create custom candidate fields 

This portion of the configuration allows AccusourceHR to provide Background Check status, a link to the Background Check report (when applicable), and the date the report is completed.

[Create three custom candidate fields](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/202609675) using the following options.

#### Field 1: Background check status

  * **Field name:** Background Check Status
  * **Type:** Short textbox



#### Field 2: Background check completed date

  * **Field name:** Background Check Completed Date
  * **Type:** Short textbox



#### Field 3: Background check result

  * **Field name:** Background Check Result
  * **Type:** URL



### Create custom job fields

When you send a candidate to AccusourceHR for a background check, you'll need to select the applicable package and location necessary to complete the Background Check.

[Create two custom job fields](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/202609855) using the following options

#### Field 1: Background Check Package

  * **Field Name:** Background Check Package
  * **Type:** Single select
  * **Options:** All your screening packages on individual lines
  * **Required:** Yes



#### Field 2: Background Check Package

  * **Field Name:** Background Check Location
  * **Type:** Single select
  * **Options:** All your locations on individual lines
  * **Required:** Yes



### Use the AccusourceHR integration

Once a background check is initiated through Greenhouse Recruiting, a request to complete the background check will be sent to the candidate’s email.

The candidate will complete the required fields and sign off on the consent. AccusourceHR receives the request, then will send an update to Greenhouse Recruiting that the order is in progress. Once the report is completed in the deverus platform, a status update is sent to Greenhouse Recruiting with the results report.

After using the integration, you may decide you want to share more information between Greenhouse Recruiting and AccusourceHR. If you would like additional information transferred over, please reach out to AccusourceHR Customer Success with a list of items to add.

### Additional resources

If you have questions about this integration, reach out to AccusourceHR at [cs@accusourcehr.com](mailto:cs@accusourcehr.com).

t

# Assign a developer permission to configure an HRIS integration

When you use an HRIS platform integration, the Greenhouse team will update your organization to give access to HRIS Link. 

To finish setting up your integration, you'll need to give access to your integration developers so they can make changes in Greenhouse. You can create a new user account for them, or update an existing one.

#### In this article

  * Create a user account
    * Add developer permissions
    * Optional permissions



### Create a user account

To give a third-party or external HRIS platform developer access to configure integrations, you need to create a [Basic](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360027077811) level user account or higher for your developer.

**Tip** : Learn how to [create a user account](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360027077811) in Greenhouse Recruiting.

#### Add developer permissions

Next, add the following [developer permissions](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/201122629) to your developer's user account, based on the type of integration you're building. Your developer may need more than one permission based on your needs:

  * **Manage Job Board related API Credentials:** If you're building an integration that requires an[ API-driven careers page](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/200721644).
  * **Manage ALL organization's API Credentials:** If you're building an integration using the [Harvest API, or another one of Greenhouse's APIs](https://developers.greenhouse.io/) to send and retrieve data in Greenhouse Recruiting.
  * **Manage and configure web hooks:** If you're building an integration to export data from Greenhouse Recruiting to other systems using [webhooks](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360005574531).
  * **Configure Workday®️ integrations:** Add this permission if your developer is building a if dev is building a Workday®️ integration and your organization is in the Advanced or Pro subscription tiers. 



**Note:** The permission 'Can manage and configure webhooks' is only needed if you use a candidate export from Greenhouse Recruiting to Workday®️.

**Tip** : Learn how to [assign developer permissions](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/201122629) in Greenhouse Recruiting.

If your external HRIS platform consultant or integration developer will also perform integration testing, we recommend providing them Job Admin access in Greenhouse Recruiting.

#### Optional permissions

There are a few optional permissions you can assign to ensure your HRIS integration developers, depending on the goal of the integration:

  * Assign them to at least one test job if they need to see how custom job fields look on a job. If they'll also be test-hiring candidates, they need to be assigned a Job Admin level that has [access to private fields](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360039518131).
  * Assign them the [user-specific permission](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360021050791) 'Can create new jobs and request job approvals' if they need to test importing jobs.
  * Assign them the [user-specific permission](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360021050791) 'Can manage custom fields' if they need to test adding and updating custom fields.



**Note:** Greenhouse Recruiting is not sponsored by, endorsed by, or affiliated with Workday®️.

**Learn more**

[Custom HRIS integration overview](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/15457642584859)

[HRIS Link overview](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360055282972)

# Jobecam integration

Jobecam is a digital recruitment and selection tool making it possible to conduct redacted video interviews to reduce bias. By focusing exclusively on candidate skills and competencies, Jobecam brings diversity to companies through its software.

With Jobecam, you can publish job vacancies to multiple channels, customize online tests, and culturally match recruits. Candidate profiles are analyzed in a much more dynamic way, automatically screened and identified as the best matches for each position.

The Jobecam tool functionality allows teams to centralize the steps of their remote selection process. Pre-define questions for candidates to answer by video so scheduling interviews isn't needed. Just press play and watch.

Greenhouse Recruiting's integration with Jobecam allows you to seamlessly add Jobecam video interview assessment to a job's interview plan.

#### In this article

  * Enable the Greenhouse/Jobecam integration
  * Add the Jobecam stage to a job’s interview plan
    * Configure the Jobecam stage
    * Send and review the test
    * Configure your job board
    * Generate a job board API key
  * Use the Jobecam Integration with Greenhouse Recruiting
  * Additional resources



### Enable the Jobecam integration in Greenhouse Recruiting 

To begin the process of enabling Jobecam in Greenhouse Recruiting, contact your Jobecam representative ([suporte@jobecam.com](mailto:suporte@jobecam.com)) to receive your API key for the integration.

Once you have received your API key, you will need to securely provide the API key to the Greenhouse Technical Support team. [Click here](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/requests/new) to open a ticket with the Technical Support team.

**Note:** Do not send your API key in any unencrypted communication, such as email and support tickets. Greenhouse Technical Support will provide a [SendSafely link](https://www.sendsafely.com/howitworks/) for you to enter your API key.

The Greenhouse Technical Support team will then send an email confirming the ticket has been created and may require account verification before they can receive your API key. 

After you have entered your API key, a notification will be sent to the Greenhouse Technical Support team and they will email you to confirm that your API key has been set up in your account and your integration is enabled.

### Add the Jobecam stage to a job’s interview plan

Once the Greenhouse/Jobecam integration is enabled for your organization, you will be able to add the **Jobecam Video Interview** assessment as an Interview stage. 

To do this for an existing job, navigate to a job (**All Jobs >Job Name**) and click **Job Setup** from the listed tabs. 

From the Job Setup page, navigate to **Interview Plan** on the left-hand panel and click **\+ Add a Stage**.

From the Add Stage dialog box, select the Jobecam stage. When finished, click **Add** to apply the stage to the job's interview plan.

#### Configure the Jobecam stage

Once the stage has been added to the job's interview plan, click **Edit Take Home Test**. Use the provided drop-down menu to choose assessments that you have previously set up in Jobecam. 

Select the appropriate assessment and assign at least one Greenhouse user to grade/review submitted assessments. When finished, click **Save**.

**Note:** Keep in mind that all configuration of the assessment itself, as well as the email template, will need to be done in Jobecam. 

#### Send and review the test

When candidates are moved into the Jobecam interview stage, Greenhouse will display a **Send Test** link.

**Note** : When you send a test from Greenhouse, the interview instructions are actually sent by Jobecam.

The status of the assessment will be viewable in Greenhouse.

Once the candidate has submitted their test, the Interview Kit will contain a link to view the submitted test on Jobecam.

After you click on the Interview Kit on the candidate’s profile, you’ll be taken to a page where the URL is available to view the test results on Jobecam.

The report Link will send you to the page on Jobecam to analyze the video interview, being an anonymized process or not.

### Configure your job board

To make your open jobs available to Jobecam, you’ll need to create a job board URL and send it to Jobecam.

To locate a job board, click the **Configure** icon  and select**Job Board** from the left panel. Select the ellipses icon  and click **Edit Board Settings**.

Scroll down to the URL field and copy the URL.

#### Generate a job board API key

Click on the **Configure** icon  and select the**Dev Center** on the left panel.

Select **API Credential Management** in the Dev Center.

From the API Credential Management page, click **Create New API Key** to generate the API key for Jobecam.

In the _Create New Credential_ dialog box, make the following selections:

  * **API Type:** Job Board
  * **Description:** Jobecam Job Board API Key



Click **Create**.

Click **Copy** to save your API key to your clipboard. Store the API key in a secure location to provide to Jobecam in the next step.

Click **I have stored the API Key** once you have copied and saved the key.

**Note:** You won’t be able to view the API key after clicking **I have stored the API Key**. If you lose your API key or need to access it later, you’ll need to generate a new key and provide it to Jobecam.

When the API key is generated, send it to Jobecam through a secure method. Reach out to [suporte@jobecam.com ](mailto:suporte@jobecam.com)for additional guidance on securely providing your created API key.

### Use the Jobecam integration with Greenhouse Recruiting

After completing setup, you will be able to simply import your jobs from Greenhouse to Jobecam. When a candidate finishes the video interview process, Jobecam will send candidate applications to Greenhouse Recruiting. 

Import jobs from Greenhouse by clicking the import button.

Click the import icon.

Add interview questions and **Save.**

Review and publish the job.

Invite candidates by selecting Share or copying the job link.

After the candidate answers every question in the video interview, the application will be sent back to Greenhouse using the application API. When applying a custom question named “Jobecam Link,” we add the manager link on the fly for recruiters to be able to access the video interview from Jobecam.

### Additional resources

Access the Jobecam Support center at <https://ajuda.jobecam.com> or send an e-mail to [contato@jobecam.com](mailto:contato@jobecam.com).

Please contact Jobecam at [suporte@jobecam.com](mailto:suporte@jobecam.com) for troubleshooting assistance regarding the integration.

Want to find out more about Jobecam? Access <https://jobecam.com> to check our plans and pricing and some of our partners and clients.

# Ezra integration

Ezra provides an AI-powered interviewing platform that conducts structured, voice-based candidate assessments on behalf of recruiters. Built on more than two years of proprietary voice-AI R&D, Ezra runs consistent 15-minute interviews that evaluate skills, communication, problem-solving, and potential fraud signals, then delivers scored, recruiter-ready summaries directly into Ezra’s Greenhouse account. The result is faster, higher-quality screening that helps companies identify real talent amid high applicant volume.

Ezra integration with Greenhouse Recruiting allows you to seamlessly add your assessments to a job's interview plan. Through this integration, you will be able to:

  1. Send Ezra interviews to candidates when they reach a stage of your choosing
  2. See the results of the Ezra interview in your Greenhouse account



#### In this article

Create a Harvest API key for the integration

Add the API key to Ezra

Contact Ezra AI labs and request an API key

Use the integration with Greenhouse Recruiting

Additional resources

### Create a Harvest API key for the integration

This is done in three parts:

  * Creating the API key
  * Adding the API key to Ezra
  * Contact Ezra AI Labs to request an API key for your integration



To generate a Greenhouse Harvest API key, follow the steps in [this article](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/5888163769883) to create the key, and verify that the permissions below are selected when configuring the Ezra integration.

  * **Candidates**
    * GET: List Candidates
    * PATCH: Update Candidates
  * **Job Posts:**
    * GET: List Job Posts
  * **Jobs:**
    * GET: List Jobs
  * **Custom Fields:**
    * GET: List Custom Fields
    * PATCH: Update Custom Fields
    * POST: Create Custom Fields
    * DELETE: Delete Custom Fields



### Add the API key to Ezra

Once you have this API key,

  * Go to [app.ezraailabs.tech](app.ezraailabs.tech) and sign in
  * Go to [app.ezraailabs.tech/connectATS](app.ezraailabs.tech/connectATS) and select Greenhouse
  * Paste your API key

### Contact Ezra AI labs and request an API key

### Use the integration with Greenhouse Recruiting

**Step 1:** Click “Add Stage” and select “Ezra AI Labs”

**Step 2:** Once a candidate has reached the applicable stage in the interview process, you will have the option to “send test to candidate.” This will generate an Ezra interview and a personalized link for the candidate that you can share with them. After it has been sent, an assessment’s status will display in Greenhouse Recruiting.

Once the candidate has submitted their test, the Interview Kit will contain a link to view the submitted test in the Ezra application.

To see a candidate’s results in Ezra, click **View** **Report** .

After you follow the link, you will see the candidate’s evaluation page in Ezra with full post-interview results

### Additional resources

If you are integrating Greenhouse Ezra for the first time, then Ezra will help! Please reach out to [partnerships@ezraailabs.tech](mailto:partnerships@ezraailabs.tech) or your point of contact at Ezra and we will walk you through the process.

# Flo Recruit integration

Greenhouse Recruiting’s integration with Flo Recruit allows the transfer of candidates’ data (name, email, resume, answers to qualifying questions, events and feedback from your employees) from Flo Recruit into Greenhouse Recruiting. In this article, we will cover how to:

### Retrieve User ID

Flo Recruit needs a Greenhouse Recruiting User ID to associate with the data.

**Note** : If your organization has a general user (like recruiting@) instead of a specific person (like jane@), we suggest you use the general user so that if the specific user ever leaves the organization, the integration remains intact.

To find a Greenhouse Recruiting user's User ID, have a user with Site Admin permissions navigate to the Users configure page. (**Configure** icon  **Users**)

Click **Export to Excel**. A spreadsheet will be downloaded onto your computer.

Open the Excel file and navigate to the **User ID** column.

Select a user from the column that will be associated with any data pushed from Flo Recruit to Greenhouse Recruiting and **copy** their User ID. Store this ID in a safe place. You will need it for the integration in the next step.

**Note:** If you would prefer to create a new user specifically to be associated with data pushed from Flo Recruit to Greenhouse Recruiting, follow the steps linked [here](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360027077811).

### Create a Harvest API key for the Flo Recruit integration

To configure the Greenhouse Recruiting / Flo Recruit integration, you'll need to create a Harvest API key.

In the _Create New Credential_ box, make the following selections:

  * **API type:** Harvest
  * **Partner:** Flo Recruit
  * **Description:** Flo Recruit Harvest API key



#### Permissions

Verify that the following permissions are selected for the Flo Recruit integration:

**Candidates**

  * All permissions



To finalize your Greenhouse integration with Flo Recruit, please provide the API Key & User ID to Flo Recruit using [this form](https://forms.gle/d2KGAW4rcZuNqZpS8).

### Select candidates and integrate their data from Flo Recruit to Greenhouse Recruiting

  * Number of candidates in each job stage per source
  * Total hires per source
  * Quality percentage



**Quality percent** is a calculation of the average distance traveled in a job pipeline for all candidates for a particular source. For example, if every candidate made it all the way through a job pipeline (from application to offer), the quality percent would be 100%. However, if every candidate was rejected in the job's first stage, the quality percent for the source would be 0%. If on average, candidates made it halfway through the pipeline, the source's quality percent would be 50%.

### Candidate quality by source report filters

Click **Filters and more** to apply filters to further refine your report.

The candidate quality by source report can be filtered by the following:

  * Job
  * Job status
  * Department
  * Office
  * User
  * Hiring team role
  * Custom job field
  * Date applied
  * Include migrated candidates



You can also organize columns by stage or milestone.

**Note** : The date applied filter is set to the current year by default.

Click **Apply** to regenerate the report after applying any filters.

### Candidate quality by source visualization

The candidate quality by source report will also visualize the quality by source.

The candidate quality by source report displays results in two graphs. The bar graph on the left summarizes the sourcing strategy by the highest quality percent. The scatterplot on the right displays the distribution of candidates based on the specific source.

You can learn more about each point on the graph by hovering your cursor over a specific bar or point.

When you select a bar on the left, the scatterplot will only display candidates from the selected sourcing strategy.

**Note** : _Sourcing_ _strategies_ are default hierarchies and cannot be modified. However, your organization can add custom sources. Check out this article for more information: [Add a custom source](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/200721664).

If certain sources are skewing your data and obstructing a clear view of your data in the scatterplot, enable the **Hide Outliers** toggle to filter out high-end outliers.

#### Reading the candidate quality by source scatterplot

The scatterplot is organized into quadrants that can you understand how certain sources are performing in relation to other sources included within and across sourcing strategies.

In the lower-left quadrant of the scatterplot are the sources that have historically submitted fewer candidates of lower quality.

In the upper-left quadrant of the scatterplot are the sources that have historically submitted fewer high-quality candidates. We recommend that your organization continue to nurture and invest in these sources to increase the total number of candidates submitted by these sources.

In the lower-right quadrant of the scatterplot are the sources who have historically submitted many low-quality candidates. We recommend that your organization consider avoiding or reducing your investment in these sources.

In the upper-right quadrant of the scatterplot are the sources who have historically submitted many high-quality candidates. Sources in this quadrant are relatively high-performing in comparison to the other sources included in the visualization.

# VideoCV integration

VideoCV is a talent screening automation tool for HR professionals and recruiters, providing a straightforward and highly intuitive platform to assess pre-recorded video interviews and analyze candidates.

Greenhouse Recruiting’s integration with VideoCV allows the recruiters and managers to seamlessly connect their Greenhouse dashboard to the VideoCV platform, enabling the team to access candidates’ VideoCVs effortlessly by following a unique link on candidates’ profiles.

#### In this article

  * Create a Harvest API key for the VideoCV integration
    * Credentials
    * Permissions
  * Use the VideoCV integration with Greenhouse Recruiting
  * How to create a job advertisement in VideoCV
    * Listing settings
    * Content of the listing
    * Team members
    * Add candidate questions
    * Send video interview invites
    * View video link in Greenhouse Recruiting
  * Additional resources



### Create a Harvest API key for the VideoCV integration

To configure the Greenhouse Recruiting / VideoCV integration, you'll need to create a Harvest API key.

Follow the steps in [this article](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/5888163769883) to create the key, and verify that the credentials and permissions below are selected when configuring the VideoCV integration.

#### Credentials

In the _Create New Credential_ box, make the following selections:

  * **API type:** Harvest
  * **Partner:** VideoCV
  * **Description:** _VideoCV Harvest API Key_



#### Permissions

Verify that the following permissions are selected for the VideoCV integration:

**Applications**

  * GET: List Applications
  * GET: Retrieve Application



**Candidates**

  * GET: List Candidates
  * GET: Retrieve Candidate
  * PATCH: Edit Candidate



**Email Templates**

  * GET: List Email Templates
  * GET: Retrieve Email Template



**Job Openings**

  * GET: List Job Openings



**Job Stages**

  * GET: List Job Stages
  * GET: List Job Stages for Job



**Jobs**

  * GET: List Jobs
  * GET: Retrieve Job
  * GET: Hiring Team



**Users**

  * GET: List Users
  * GET: Retrieve User



Your Harvest API key for the Greenhouse Recruiting / VideoCV integration is created and configured. Provide your Harvest API key to your VideoCV onboarding team so they can set up the integration.

### Use the VideoCV integration with Greenhouse Recruiting

Once you have copied the Harvest API key, go to the VideoCV platform and open **Settings**.

In the _Integrations_ section, paste the Harvest API key in the **Greenhouse API token** field. Then, click **Save**.

Now the integration is complete.

**Tip:** While creating new job listings in Greenhouse, we recommend adding a **Video Interview** stage in the interview plan for more convenience.

### How to create a job advertisement in VideoCV

Go to VideoCV and click **Add a new job listing** from your _dashboard_.

#### Listing settings

Next, select a**vacancy from Greenhouse**. _The job advertisement must already exist in Greenhouse Recruiting._

Some of the fields will be auto-filled. Fill in the rest appropriate fields.

#### Content of the listing

There is an option to insert a company video showing your culture and inviting candidates to apply. The video can be recorded in the recording window or uploaded as a file or URL link.

Please also fill in the **Job description** section stating your requirements, expectations, and offerings for the candidates. You can easily write the description in the relevant field or upload the description as an image.

#### Team members

If you want to share the candidate notifications with your colleagues who don’t have a VideoCV account, enter their emails in the **Team Members** field.

Select **Each candidate** to share every candidate’s video the moment it becomes available, or select **Daily summary** to share a daily summary showing all candidates from that day.

Click **Continue** when done. 

#### Add candidate questions

In the next section, you will add questions you want the candidates to answer.

After the questions have been added, check that the information is correct.

Click **Save** , then **Publish** when done. 

#### Send video interview invites

Click **Job listings** to see the new listings.

Next, invite the candidates to the video interview from the Greenhouse Recruiting platform.

To do this, click **Send invitations to apply**.

A new window appears. You can either **enter the candidate emails manually** or **choose the candidates** from the dropdown menu.

**Note:** The dropdown menu only shows candidates from Greenhouse Recruiting that have not yet received a VideoCV invitation. So, feel free to choose **Select all**. 

Click **Send** when done.

Click on the **title** to open the listing. Inside the listing, you'll see the invited candidate. This is where the candidate video will appear once the candidate has uploaded it.

You have successfully added the job listing!

#### View video link in Greenhouse Recruiting

The link to the candidate’s video answers is visible under their candidate profile in Greenhouse Recruiting.

Click on the **candidate** , open the **Details** tab, and you'll see the link in the _Other_ section.

### Additional resources

For additional information not covered here, reach out to info@videocv.io or chat with us in the Intercom window on <https://videocv.io/en/>

# Greenhouse Recruiting Chrome extension for CRM

**Permissions:** Job Admin and above who can manage CRM and prospects

**Product tier:** Available for new subscription tiers (Core, Plus, and Pro)

**Note:** This article is for users with CRM access only. [Click here](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/8302875133083) to learn how to use the Greenhouse Recruiting Chrome extension with your Sourcing Automation seat.

The [Greenhouse Recruiting Chrome extension](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/8302339682843) is a browser plugin that allows your organization to add prospects to your Greenhouse CRM from a website, resume, or manually through the plugin without leaving your current workflow.

#### In this article

  * Step 1: Locate duplicate prospects
  * Step 2: Add a prospect to the Greenhouse Recruiting Chrome extension
  * Step 3: Upload the prospect to Greenhouse Recruiting
  * Additional resources



### Step 1: Locate duplicate prospects

When parsing information from AngelList, Github, and Indeed, highlight the prospect's **name** or **email address** to check for duplicates within Greenhouse Recruiting. The extension checks for duplicates that match one of the following details: first and last name, email, phone number, or LinkedIn URL. These duplicate checks always use all four details and are separate from the [Duplicate tag configuration](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/49207850415003-Configure-the-Duplicate-tag) used for candidate profiles in Greenhouse Recruiting.

If a duplicate isn't found, click **Prefill** to add their information to the extension. 

**Note:** If the highlight feature doesn't work, confirm that the extension has access to the website data. **Extension icon** > **Ellipsis icon** > **Manage Extensions** > Scroll to the **Site access** section > Click the site **toggle** to enable access

Now that you've checked for duplicates, continue with adding the prospect to the extension in step two.

### Step 2: Add a prospect to the Greenhouse Recruiting Chrome extension

Add prospects to the Greenhouse Recruiting Chrome extension using the following methods:

  * Add a prospect from AngelList
  * Add a prospect from GitHub
  * Add a prospect from Indeed
  * Add a prospect from LinkedIn
  * Add a prospect using their resume
  * Add a prospect manually



**Note:** An email address is required if [GDPR](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360061849112) rules are enabled for your organization.

#### Add a prospect from AngelList

Navigate to the **Source** tab from your AngelList homepage.

Select a **search** option from the _Starred_ tab or the _All Searches_ tab. Alternatively, select **New Search** to create a query. 

Click the **Greenhouse** button on the prospect's _AngelList profile_. Then, click **Continue** within the extension. _The extension may advance to the next page automatically._

**Note:** The Greenhouse button is unavailable if the prospect doesn't have a name on their profile. For example, some prospects elect to display their job title instead of their name. 

The extension parses an available first name, last name, and company from AngelList. 

Now that the prospect is added, finish uploading their information to Greenhouse Recruiting.

#### Add a prospect from GitHub

Click **Greenhouse Recruiting** from the prospect's _GitHub profile,_ then click **Continue** within the extension. _The extension may advance to the next page automatically._

The extension parses an available first name, last name, email address, and company from GitHub. 

Now that the prospect is added, finish uploading their information to Greenhouse Recruiting.

#### Add a prospect from Indeed

Navigate to <https://resumes.indeed.com/>.

Use the **search panel** to find prospects. Then, use the _filter panel_ to refine your search as needed.

Select a **prospect** from the search results to preview their profile.

Once selected, click their **name** to open their profile in a new tab.

Click the **Greenhouse** icon to add their information to the extension.

The extension parses an available first name, last name, and company from Indeed. 

Now that the prospect is added, finish uploading their information to Greenhouse Recruiting.

#### Add a prospect from LinkedIn

You're able to save a LinkedIn profile as a PDF. Once exported, the PDF can be uploaded to the extension which will import data from the document.

Click **More** from the prospect's _LinkedIn profile_ and select **Save to PDF** from the dropdown.

**Note** : Due to [LinkedIn's download limits](https://www.linkedin.com/help/recruiter/answer/a412149/export-profiles-in-recruiter?lang=en), you can only save 200 LinkedIn profiles as a PDF per month. Once this limit is reached the _Save to PDF_ button is unavailable until a new month starts. As an alternative, use the [LinkedIn RSC integration](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360036524551) to add prospects to Greenhouse Recruiting. 

The extension automatically uploads and parses information from the PDF download, and attaches it as a resume to the extension.

Additional upload options include**dragging and dropping** the saved PDF into the extension or clicking **Upload resume** to manually import the PDF from your files.

Now that the prospect is added, finish uploading their information to Greenhouse Recruiting.

#### Add a prospect using their resume

A prospect can be added to the extension using their resume.

**Drag and drop** a resume into the extension or click **Upload resume** to manually import the document from your files.

Now that the prospect is added, finish uploading their information to Greenhouse Recruiting.

#### Add a prospect manually

Manually enter the prospect's available information.

Once added, click **Continue** and finish uploading the prospect to Greenhouse Recruiting.

### Step 3: Upload the prospect to Greenhouse Recruiting

Once step two is complete, the extension allows you to do a final check for duplicate profiles and fill in additional information prior to uploading the prospect's profile to Greenhouse Recruiting. This final duplicate check uses the same fixed details (first and last name, email, phone number, and LinkedIn URL) and isn’t impacted by your [Duplicate tag settings](https://%20https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/49207850415003-Configure-the-Duplicate-tag) in the web app.

A warning appears if the prospect is a potential duplicate. Click **View** to open the existing prospect's profile in Greenhouse Recruiting.

Follow the steps below to upload your prospect to Greenhouse Recruiting:

  1. Click the **pencil icon** to edit or add information. Then, click **Done** at the top of the page once the edits are complete.
  2. Select the applicable **Pool** , **Source** , **Recruiter** , and **Job**. 
  3. Click **Edit additional details** to add information such as a coordinator, department, office, and more.
  4. After all the details are added, click **Upload prospect** at the bottom of the extension.



Once successfully uploaded, you have the option to **view** the prospect's profile in Greenhouse Recruiting from a new tab and/or return to the extension homepage by clicking **Upload next prospect**.

If you selected a prospect pool, the pool details are provided on the _Prospect application._ The profile also indicates that the prospect was created via the extension.

### Additional resources

  * [CRM overview](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360022793612)
  * [Prospects overview](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/200670155)

# Merge duplicate candidate profiles

**Permissions:** Site Admin, and Job Admin who can merge candidates and prospects

**Product tier:** Available for new subscription tiers (Core, Plus, and Pro)

Duplicate applications can cause confusion and significantly more work for your users. Greenhouse Recruiting flags a person as a possible duplicate when it finds another profile that matches your organization’s Duplicate tag settings — for example, the same email address, phone number, LinkedIn profile URL, or name. By default, the Duplicate tag uses email address, phone number, and LinkedIn profile URL; Site Admins can optionally include name if they want more sensitive matching.

To reduce friction while candidates move through your interview pipeline, Greenhouse Recruiting's merge feature allows your organization to manually combine separate candidate applications into a single candidate profile.

All Site Admins can merge candidates and prospects. Job Admins can do this if they are included in a custom permission level that has the ability to merge candidates and prospects. Custom permission levels are only available for Plus and Pro subscription tiers customers.

**Note** : If you want Greenhouse Recruiting to merge matching people automatically, enable auto-merge and configure your match criteria in your organization settings. Learn more in [Auto-merge](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/208063316).

#### In this article

  * Manually merge a single candidate
  * Merge candidate profiles in bulk 
  * How data merges work
  * Additional considerations



### Manually merge a single candidate

**Note:** In order to merge duplicate candidates, a Job Admin must have [equal job-based permissions](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360039518131) assigned across all jobs the candidate has applied to, and the candidate cannot be anonymized.

If a user is encountering trouble when merging profiles, check to confirm their [job-based permissions are consistent and assigned](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360040181991) to all jobs the candidate has applications submitted for.

To manually merge a single candidate application with another profile, navigate to the primary candidate profile you want to merge, click the ellipses icon at the top, and choose **Merge with another candidate** from the list. 

Where available, you can also click the **Duplicate** tag on a candidate profile to open the merge flow directly and determine if the potential duplicates should be merged. The Duplicate tag appears when Greenhouse finds another profile that meets your configured duplicate criteria — for example, the same email address, phone number, LinkedIn profile URL, or name. Site Admins manage which fields trigger this tag in Duplicate tag settings. The Duplicate tag still uses broader matching than Auto-merge, so many Duplicate-tagged profiles require manual review and a manual merge.

To change which fields trigger the [Duplicate tag](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/49207850415003) for your organization, a Site Admin can update Duplicate tag settings from the Configure menu.

**Note:** LinkedIn profile URL matching triggers the Duplicate tag in two ways: when two profiles share the same LinkedIn URL stored in the **Social Media Addresses** field (displayed as "Website (Social Media)" in the UI), or when two profiles are linked to the same LinkedIn profile via the **Greenhouse–LinkedIn Recruiter System Connect (RSC) integration**.

For more detail on duplicate detection and auto‑merge, see [Auto-merge](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/208063316). 

If the duplicate and primary candidates are in the wrong order for the merge, click **Switch Candidates** to change their position without losing your progress.

When the correct profiles are selected, click **Merge**.

**Note** : You cannot un-merge candidates.

### Merge candidate profiles in bulk 

To merge multiple candidate profiles into a single candidate profile, click the**Candidates** tab from the navigation bar and identify the candidates who should be merged from the subsequent list.

Click **Bulk Actions**.

**Note** : Use the search feature and [filter panels](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360043184152) on the left-hand side of the page to help narrow down the list of candidates if necessary. To easily find duplicates, you can also open the **Profile Details** filter**** and select **Show potential duplicates** at the bottom of the filter panel. 

Select the candidate profiles to be merged by adding a check in the box to the left of their name. Click**Edit Selected (#)** when finished.

From the subsequent dialog box, click **Merge**.

Select which profile should become the primary candidate profile. All other candidate profiles will be merged into this profile. To learn more about what data will be retained and what data will be deprecated as a result of setting a primary candidate profile, review the section below.

**Note** : This action cannot be undone. Candidate profiles cannot be un-merged after selecting **Merge Candidates.**

Click **Merge Candidates** when finished.

All selected candidate profiles will be merged into the primary candidate profile.

**Note:** Candidate profiles cannot be merged if data from either profile has been [deleted via the GDPR feature](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360035611851).

### How data merges work

On a candidate's profile, some fields (such as the [recruiter and coordinator assigned to the candidate](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360040346551)) can only have a single individual or value assigned. Sometimes, when a profile is merged, different values will be listed on the primary and secondary profiles. This situation is called a**conflict**.

When a conflict occurs, Greenhouse Recruiting will prioritize data from the primary candidate if it conflicts with the duplicate candidate profile.

If any of the following data in the duplicate profile conflicts with the primary profile, the primary profile's values will be used.

  * Current company
  * Current title
  * Source
  * Recruiter
  * Coordinator
  * Referral
  * Job Forms
  * Interview kit URL (_This conflict will impact any scheduled interviews you may have for the non-primary candidate. Those interviews will need to be manually updated for the merged candidate_)



**Note** : If you have enabled [Auto-merge](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/208063316), Greenhouse Recruiting will prioritize the oldest candidate profile when merging duplicate profiles.

However, in some cases, a field may be able to have multiple pieces of data (such as candidate tags or phone numbers). In this case, Greenhouse Recruiting will combine the values from the primary and duplicate profiles into a single list.

The following pieces of data will be combined if multiple values exist:

  * Data in the activity feed
  * Scorecards
  * Attachments
  * Phone number
  * Email
  * Social media links
  * Websites
  * Address
  * Education
  * Candidate tags



If any conflicts are resolved as part of the candidate merge, they'll be listed in the merged candidate's Activity Feed.

#### Additional considerations

Manually merging candidate profiles will overwrite the `candidate_id` field used to identify candidates when utilizing our [API](https://developers.greenhouse.io/harvest.html#put-merge-candidates) or [HRIS integrations](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/sections/7338486330267-HRIS-Link) in Greenhouse Recruiting.

Once the candidates profiles are merged, the candidate id of the profile marked as secondary will not be displayed in-app or within the API. As a result, merging secondary profiles with primary profiles may cause downstream integration errors. 

If your team leverages these tools, it's recommended to select the newest/active candidate record as primary to merge into any additional historical candidate record(s). It's also recommended to utilize our [`candidate_merged`](https://developers.greenhouse.io/webhooks.html#candidate-merged) webhook operating as an alert for your team in the event of any changes. 

This webhook will trigger any time a candidate is merged, including auto-merges, and will specify the `candidate_id`. It will also contain a `"new_candidate_id"` field which can be helpful for maintaining the correct candidate ID in external systems like [Workday](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360002158492).

For additional questions around leveraging candidate IDs when merging candidates, [connect with the Greenhouse Technical Support team](https://support.greenhouse.io/direct).

# Time to approve offer goal attainment report

**Permissions:** Job Admin and above

**Product tier:** Available for new subscription tiers (Core, Plus, and Pro)

The time to approve offer [company goal](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/8382420999835) represents the ideal time between when a Greenhouse Recruiting user receives an offer approval request and when they approve or deny the offer. Use the time to approve offer goal attainment report to track progress on this goal.

#### In this article

  * View time to approve offer goal attainment report
    * Time to approve offer goal attainment report visualization
  * Apply report filters
  * Additional resources



### View time to approve offer goal attainment report

To create a time to approve offer goal attainment report, click **Reports** on your dashboard's navigation bar.

On the _Reports_ page, click **Essential** **reports**.

Select **Time to Approve Offer Goal Attainment** from the _Understand Goal and Attainment Metrics_ section.

Your time to approve offer goal attainment report will generate.

Your report will display attainment percentages for your entire organization in a visualization. Below this visual chart, you'll find a breakdown of attainment percentages for individual users or departments (depending on the report filters you've applied) in a table.

Attainment percentages are relative to the [target value your organization set for this goal](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/8382420999835) and the time period you've selected as a filter for your report columns. Each percentage is calculated by the total number of actions completed on time (based on the target value you've set) over the total number of actions overall for your filtered time period.

**For example:** You've set your time to approve offer goal report to display your attainment levels per week. Each percentage represents the number of times you've approved offers within your target **divided by** the total number of times you've approved offers (whether on time or not) for that week.

**Note** : Credit for the time to approve offer goal will accrue to all approvers in the approval flow equally. For instance, if two approvers are required, and one approves in 2 hours, while the other approves in 4 hours, the time to approve offers goal will show 4 hours for both approvers.

#### Time to approve offer goal attainment report visualization

The time to approve offer goal attainment report presents your organization's attainment levels in a line chart. The attainment percentage is displayed on the _y_ -axis and the time period is displayed on the _x_ -axis.

You can hover over each point in the visualization for additional details.

This visualization will adjust each time you apply new filters from the **Filters and more** dropdown.

### Apply report filters

Click **Filters and more** to apply filters and further refine your report.

You can use the following filters on your time to approve offer goal attainment report:

  * **Rows** – select whether to display attainment levels for users or departments
  * **Columns** – select whether to display attainment levels per week, month, or quarter
  * **Activity date** – view goal attainment for a specific date range
  * **User or department filter** – view goal attainment for specific users or departments



**Note:** Activity date is set to the last 180 days by default. To optimize performance, company goals data is only available for the last 365 days.

Click **Apply** to add your selected filters and adjust your report.

# Employment status field overview

**Permissions:** Owners

**Product tier:** Available for Greenhouse Welcome and Greenhouse Onboarding subscription tiers

Fields allow your organization to collect and organize information about onboarding new hires and employees.

The **employment status** field indicates a new hire's type of employment, such as full-time or part-time. You can use this field to automatically assign specific tasks and E-Signatures through the new hire's onboarding plan.

The employment status field includes four default options which you can edit to match your organization's unique needs.

#### In this article

  * Access the employment status field
  * Edit the employment status field
    * Employment status field selection options
  * Additional resources



### Access the employment status field

From your Greenhouse Onboarding homepage, navigate to **Settings** > **Company Info** > **Fields**.

On the _Fields_ page, scroll to _Additional Information_ to find the **Employment Status** field.

**Note:** Your field's display name and field group can be edited, which means your organization may be storing this field under a different name or field group.

### Edit the employment status field

From the _Fields_ page, click your **Employment Status** field to edit it.

On the _Edit Field_ page, you can update the following elements:

  * Display name
  * Help text
  * Selection options
  * Field group
  * [Greenhouse Recruiting field](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/208314493)



**Note:** Field type can't be edited.

The employment status field includes the following selection options by default:

  * Contract
  * Full-time
  * Intern
  * Part-time



Mark the **Required for new hires and/or managers** checkbox to make sure that this field is completed each time you onboard a new hire.

#### Employment status field selection options

When editing or adding field options, you'll need to provide an original value, display name, and external value. Learn more about these values below:

**Column Name** | **Description**  
---|---  
Original Value | The original value is assigned to each employment status option when it's created. It's used as a unique identifier on the backend of Greenhouse Onboarding to track the option. The original value can't be edited. Editing the display name of an option will not change the option's original value.  
Display Name | Your users will see the display name listed in the dropdown when selecting an employment status option. It will also be displayed on a new hire's profile. Editing an option's display name will update the way it's displayed everywhere in your organization's Greenhouse Onboarding account.  
External Value | External values are used in association with third-party integrations to an HRIS. External values can be updated, allowing your team to input the matching field name your integration partner needs to successfully sync data between Greenhouse Onboarding and their platform. If you aren't using any third-party integrations, you'll likely not need to make any adjustments to this column.  
  
**Note:** The**Terminated** employment status option can't be edited and won't display when you're editing this field. However, it will always appear as an option in the employment status dropdown on an employee profile.

### Additional resources

  * [Add a new employment status field option](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360052740291)
  * [Edit employment status field option](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360052293372)
  * [Delete employment status field option](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360052740331)

# Change a job post’s status

**Permissions:** Job Admin and above

**Product tier:** Available for new subscription tiers (Core, Plus, and Pro)

A job post's status indicates whether the job is published to a job board. 

There are many reasons why an organization might strategically change a job post's status. One reason a job post may be turned off is that the hiring team has received a sufficient number of strong candidates to consider for the position and doesn't want to receive additional applications.

**Note** : A [job status](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/4402057327899) and a job post status are different statuses. Turning off a job post means the post is no longer visible to candidates. Changing a job status to [closed](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360025499691) means you’re not actively seeking to fill a position, perhaps because a candidate has been hired or your organization implemented a hiring freeze.

#### In this article

  * Job post statuses
  * Change the job post status for a single job
  * Change the job post status for several jobs
  * Additional resources



### Job post statuses

There are two job post statuses: Live and Offline.

When a job post is set to **Live** , the post appears on your organization’s internal or external job board where candidates can see it and use it to apply for the job. 

When a job post status is set to **Offline** , the job post is not visible on any job boards, even though the job itself may be open and the hiring team may be actively interviewing candidates to fill it. Turning a job post off removes the page from the internet and any links to the post stop working.

### Change the job post status for a single job

From your dashboard, navigate to the _Jobs_ page and open a job.

From the left side menu, click **Job Setup**.

Find the _Job Posts_ section, then click **Edit**.

Click the toggle next to a job post to change its status.

### Change the job post status for several jobs

If you need to change the status of multiple job posts, you can do so by viewing all the posts on a job board.

Navigate to the _Configure_ page by clicking the **gear icon**.

From the left menu, click **Job Boards & Posts**.

In the _Job Boards_ section, click the number of job posts to the right of the board name.

All job posts published to the job board are displayed. To change a post's status, click the status button next to the job name.

### Additional resources

  * [Delete a job post](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360023264611)
  * [Understanding job statuses in Greenhouse Recruiting](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/4402057327899)

# Joveo Programmatic Job Advertising integration

Joveo is the global leader in programmatic job advertising. The Joveo integration with Greenhouse Recruiting streamlines your entire recruitment process—from automated job distribution to application delivery and ROI tracking.

By connecting Greenhouse to Joveo’s Programmatic Job Advertising platform, you can leverage AI-powered media buying to deliver your jobs to the most effective channels. 

The integration ensures that jobs sync in real-time, candidates are tracked from click to hire, and all source data is accurately captured for transparent performance analytics.

#### In this article

  * Enable the integration
    * Create a Harvest API key
    * Generate a Job Board API key
    * Locate your Job Board Token
  * Configure Joveo settings
  * Use the integration with Greenhouse Recruiting
  * Additional resources



### Enable the integration

To fully configure the integration, you will need to create a Harvest API Key, a Job Board API Key, and locate your Job Board Token.

#### Create a Harvest API key

Follow the steps in [this article](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/5888163769883) to create the key, and verify that the permissions below are selected when configuring the Joveo integration.

**Credentials**

In the Create New Credential box, make the following selections:

  * **API Type:** Harvest
  * **Partner:** Joveo
  * **Description:** Joveo Harvest API Key



**Permissions (Harvest API Key V1)**

Verify that the following permissions are selected for the Joveo integration. These permissions allow Joveo to sync jobs, write "Easy Apply" candidates back into Greenhouse, and track funnel stages.

  * **Applications**
    * GET: List Applications
    * GET: Retrieve Application
    * POST: Add Application
    * POST: Add Attachment (required for Resumes)
  * **Candidates**
    * GET: List Candidates
    * GET: Retrieve Candidate
    * POST: Add Candidate
    * POST: Add Note
  * **Job Posts**
    * GET: List Job Posts
    * GET: Retrieve Job Post
  * **Jobs**
    * GET: List Jobs
    * GET: Retrieve Job
    * GET: Job Stages
  * **Sources**
    * GET: List Sources



#### Generate a Job Board API key

Next, you’ll need to create a Job Board API key for Joveo. Follow the steps in [this article](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/13446638483355-Create-a-job-board-API-key-for-an-integration) and use the information below when creating your API key:

  * **API Type:** Job Board
  * **Partner:** Joveo
  * **Description:** Joveo Job Board API Key



#### Locate your Job Board Token

To make your open jobs available to Joveo, you will also need your Job Board Token. Follow the steps in [this article](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/5888210160155-Find-your-job-board-URL) to find your Job Board Token.

### Configure Joveo settings

Once you have gathered the above information from Greenhouse, you need to enter them into the Joveo interface to establish the connection.

**Step 1:** Log in to your Joveo platform.

**Step 2:** Navigate to the Integrations Page

From the main dashboard, locate the primary navigation menu on the left-hand side of your screen. Click on Integrations to open the Third-Party Integrations hub.

**Step 3:** Select Greenhouse from the list of available ATS integrations.

On the Integrations page, you will see a catalog of available ATS providers.

  * Locate Greenhouse ATS from the list
  * Click the + Integrate button on the card



This action will launch a setup wizard to guide you through the connection process.

**Step 4:** Enter the following details into the configuration fields.

  * **Integration Name:** In the first step, you will be prompted to name the connection. We recommend using a descriptive name, especially if you plan to connect multiple accounts or environments.



  * **Harvest API Key:** Paste the Harvest API Key generated in Step 1.



  * **Job Board API Key:** Paste the Job Board API Key generated in Step 2.



  * **Job Board Token:** Paste the Token copied in Step 3.



**Step 5:** Connect your Greenhouse account

Your Greenhouse ATS is now successfully connected. The system will initiate the first sync of your open requisitions and job screening questions shortly.

Once complete, the Joveo platform will be fully equipped to distribute your jobs across our publisher network, enable seamless 'Easy Apply' submissions, and track candidate performance from click to hire—optimizing your recruitment spend in real-time.

### Use the integration with Greenhouse Recruiting

Once the Joveo integration is enabled, the data flow between the two systems is fully automated.

#### Job Synchronization & Advertising

As soon as a job is created and set to "Live" within Greenhouse, it is automatically synced to the Joveo platform.

  * Recruiters can log into the Joveo platform to view these jobs and launch programmatic advertising campaigns.



  * Joveo distributes these jobs to the most effective job boards and publishers based on your campaign goals.



#### Candidate Application Workflows

The integration supports two distinct application workflows to maximize candidate volume and quality:

1\. Redirect Apply (Traffic Sourcing)  
For standard job boards, when a candidate clicks on a Joveo ad, they are redirected specifically to the Greenhouse ATS application page via your Job Board URL. This ensures you are sourcing the best traffic directly to your branded career page.

2\. Easy Apply (Write-back)  
Joveo supports "Easy Apply" publishers (where candidates apply without leaving the job board).

  * Joveo pulls the specific job questions from Greenhouse and sends them to the publisher.
  * The job seeker completes the application on the publisher site.
  * Joveo captures the application and automatically writes the candidate profile, resume, and answers back into Greenhouse.
  * The user will see these candidates appear in Greenhouse immediately, just as if they applied via the career page.



#### ****

#### Funnel Tracking& Optimization

Joveo uses the integration to perform "closed-loop" analytics. Joveo periodically scans the application stages in Greenhouse to understand how candidates from specific sources are progressing.

  * **Optimization:** Joveo uses this data to identify which sources are generating _hires_ versus just _clicks_ , and automatically optimizes the media spend upstream.
  * **Analytics:** Full performance analytics (Spend vs. Hires) are displayed within the Joveo platform.



### Additional resources

For additional information not covered here, or for help configuring your programmatic campaigns, reach out to [support@joveo.com](mailto:support@joveo.com).

# Merge duplicate candidate tags

**Permissions:** **Site** **Admin** , and **Job** **Admin** who can manage company metadata

**Product tier:** Available for new subscription tiers (Core, Plus, and Pro)

Greenhouse Recruiting doesn't have an explicit merge feature for candidate tags. Instead, we've built functionality into deleting a candidate tag that allows your organization to reassign candidates with the tag before its deprecation. This functionality essentially achieves the same goal of merging candidates from two tags into one tag.

To merge duplicate candidate tags, click the **Configure** icon  on your navigation bar, and select **Custom Options** on the left.

Click **Candidate Tags**.

From the subsequent list of candidate tags, identify the two candidate tags that will be merged and select which of the two will be the primary candidate tag (_the tag that will remain_) and the secondary tag (_the tag whose candidates will be moved to the primary tag_).

Click **Remove** beside with the secondary candidate tag.

From the _Remove Candidate Tag_ dialog box, select the checkbox for _I want any entity using this candidate tag to use this instead:_ and select the primary candidate tag from the dropdown menu.

Click **Delete Candidate Tag** when finished.

The secondary candidate tag will be deprecated and any candidates assigned the secondary candidate tag will now be assigned the primary candidate tag.

# Control candidate data access

**Permissions:** Site admins

**Product tier:** Available for new subscription tiers (Core, Plus, and Pro)

**Note:** These features are currently in beta and available to select customers. If you’d like to participate, contact your Greenhouse account tea,.

The "Download candidate data" and "Export reports" permissions give your organization more control over how personal candidate information is shared outside Greenhouse Recruiting. Configure these permissions to specify who can and cannot download reports, resumes, candidate packets and other candidate data.

#### In this article

  * Overview
  * Configure who can download candidate data
    * What changes for Job Admins
  * Configure who can export reports
    * What changes for users
  * Learn more about Job Admin permissions



#### Overview

To help your organization meet privacy and compliance requirements Greenhouse is introducing new permissions that limit how personal candidate information can leave the platform.

  * "Download candidate data" controls whether Job Admins can download candidate data from Greenhouse _(Job Admin permission)_
  * "Export reports" controls which users can download reports _(User-specific permission)_



Limiting who can download candidate data gives your team more control over how and when candidate data leaves Greenhouse which reduces the risk of candidate data being stored on local devices and provides more control over how candidate information is shared.

#### Configure who can download candidate data

  * Go to **Configure** > **Permission policies** > **Job Admin levels**
  * Locate the new permission **Can download candidate data**
  * Turn this permission **OFF** for any Job Admin levels that shouldn’t be able to download candidate data.
  * Click "Save." The change applies immediately to all users with that Job Admin level



#### What changes for Job Admins

When in a permission stripe where "can download candidate data" is enabled, Job Admins can continue to download candidate data like they previously could as this is the current Greenhouse Recruiting default setting.

When a Job Admin is not allowed to download candidate data:

  * They'll still be able to view resumes and candidate packets within Greenhouse.
  * In some cases, they won't see links to download candidate documents.
  * In other cases, will see deactivated links and text explaining that they don’t have permission to download candidate data.



**Note** :**** Basic Users cannot download candidate data. To allow Basic Users to download documents, upgrade them to Job Admin at a level where "can download candidate data" is enabled.

#### Configure who can export reports

Exporting reports is a user-specific permission that's enabled or disabled for specific Job Admins.

  * Go to **Configure** > **Users**
  * Select the Job Admin user whose permission you're editing 
  * Scroll to **Permissions** , then **Other actions**
  * Turn **ON** or **OFF** "Can export reports" 



Select **Save permissions**. 

#### What changes for users

Job Admins with this user-specific permission **ON** can download and export reports. 

Job Admins with this user-specific permission **OFF** cannot download or export reports, but can view reports within Greenhouse.

#### Learn more about Job Admin permissions

  * [Job Admin levels and permissions](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360039518131-Job-Admin-levels-and-permissions)
  * [Edit or delete a Job Admin level](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360039863731)
