# Identity verification with CLEAR - Security & Privacy FAQ

This FAQ provides technical and processing information about Greenhouse's features, identity verifications with CLEAR, to support your evaluation the feature.

None of this is intended to be legal advice, neither are any of the answers provided intended to override or contradict the advice of your legal counsel.

#### In this article

  * Overview
  * Privacy roles and responsibilities
  * Personal data and data flows
  * Candidate experience and operations
  * Security and trust



### Overview

#### What is Real Talent’s Identity Verification Request with CLEAR?

Greenhouse’s Identity Verification Request with CLEAR helps your team focus on authentic, qualified candidates by mitigating the risk of impersonation, duplicate profiles, and other forms of fraud. It is a core component of **Real Talent** , a suite of tools engineered to block spam and detect suspicious behaviors. Identity verification operates in partnership with CLEAR, cross-checking information submitted to CLEAR against the candidate’s application data within Greenhouse.

#### Do identity verifications sent with CLEAR involve AI?

No. There are other AI features within Greenhouse — including Real Talent’s “Talent Matching” feature, but Identity Verification Request with CLEAR does not involve AI.

#### What identity checks are performed?

  * Document authenticity and tampering signals (document proofing).
  * Selfie “liveness” detection and ID matching to help prevent spoofing.
  * Device trustworthiness signals (e.g., anomalous activity, VPN/proxy usage) captured during the verification process.
  * Cross-referencing of the candidate's last name, phone number, and email address against the application data stored by Greenhouse.



[Click here to read more about identity verifications with CLEAR.](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/40893011137179)

#### What ID documents are accepted?

A government-issued ID, such as a passport, is required to complete identity verification. You can view the list of accepted document types for your country [here](https://docs.clearme.com/docs/supported-document-types).

CLEAR will not accept identification from users with documents issued by the following countries, even if the user is physically located elsewhere:

  * Syria
  * Ukraine
  * Russia
  * Iran
  * North Korea
  * Cuba



#### What countries are supported for ID verification based on their device location?

Support for ID verification based on the location of the individual’s device (not their ID document) is the following:

  * **North America:** United States and its territories, Canada, Mexico supported
  * **EU + UK (GDPR regions):** Supported
  * **India** : Supported



#### Is CLEAR able to detect and prevent verification using tampered or fake IDs?

CLEAR performs document proofing, which analyzes the ID against unique government ID features to detect fakes and tampering. CLEAR is independently certified by the Kantara Initiative at Identity Assurance Level 2 (IAL2), with authentication at AAL2, providing third-party assurance on their Identity Verification implementation.

While document proofing is robust, highly sophisticated fraudulent documents may still bypass these checks. Therefore, a layered approach to fraud prevention is critical, with document proofing as one component. Additional layered checks include:

  * CLEAR device anomaly detection relating to failed attempts, vpn/proxy usage
  * CLEAR selfie liveness checks
  * Real Talent fraud analysis checks



#### Do identity verification requests with CLEAR perform background checks?

No. Identity Verification Request with CLEAR is limited to document/biometric verification and device signals. The Greenhouse integration does not perform checks against third-party databases such as watchlists or criminal records.

It is recommended that Greenhouse users maintain existing background check processes and vendor integrations as part of their layered defense strategy against fraudulent candidates.

### Privacy roles and responsibilities

#### What are the data processing roles between each party?

CLEAR operates as a data controller with a direct relationship with the individual candidate during ID verification.

Greenhouse is the data controller for any data candidates enter into MyGreenhouse and also for the verification result data that is shared with the candidate through the candidate’s MyGreenhouse account.

A customer that initiates a request for CLEAR ID verification associated with a job application is the data controller for the verification results related to that application in the customer’s Greenhouse Recruiting account. Customers do not sign a contract with CLEAR for this feature; the candidate engages CLEAR directly during verification.

#### How should we handle a candidate’s deletion request related to CLEAR?

To delete data stored by Greenhouse (e.g., the verification result and cross-referenced basic contact fields), customers must utilize the [built-in data retention and deletion features](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360002418112-Configure-a-data-retention-rule). ID verification data is available as an option on the ‘Data to be Deleted’ list.

To delete data collected and controlled by CLEAR (e.g., the ID image, selfie, and associated identity verification artifacts), the individual must exercise their rights directly with CLEAR. CLEAR provides mechanisms for individuals to delete their data.

Greenhouse provides the following [FAQ support page](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/40497797083419-CLEAR-FAQ-for-candidates) for candidates, explaining the ID verification feature and providing instructions on how to fulfill their data privacy rights.

Candidates can delete their account from their profile page for data collected by MyGreenhouse.

#### How should we handle a candidate’s access request related to CLEAR?

The CLEAR verification data is a personal data option that customers can select when [generating a candidate packet](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360000916572-Create-a-candidate-packet) within Greenhouse.

### Personal data and data flows

**What personal data does CLEAR collect during verification?**

CLEAR collects the user’s full name, email address, government ID (including the personal data listed on the ID), a selfie, phone number, and IP address.

**What data does Greenhouse receive from CLEAR and store within the customer’s account?**

Greenhouse receives the verification status and limited fields used for cross-referencing with application data (full name, phone, email, and IP address). We display a pass/fail result for verification checks in the Candidate Profile.

The candidate is presented with a data grant approval screen during the CLEAR® ID verification process that explicitly outlines the data fields Greenhouse will receive.

#### Does Greenhouse send candidate personal data to CLEAR?

No. Greenhouse does not send candidate information to CLEAR. The candidate directly submits their data to CLEAR during the ID verification process.

#### Does Greenhouse receive or store ID images or selfies?

No. CLEAR retains the ID image/selfie and related identity artifacts. Greenhouse does not request, receive, or store this data from CLEAR.

#### Does Greenhouse receive or store any biometric data?

No. Greenhouse does not request, receive, or store biometric data from CLEAR.

#### Where can I find CLEAR’s privacy notice?

CLEAR’s privacy notice is presented to candidates in the flow and is available at[ https://www.clearme.com/privacy-policy](https://www.clearme.com/privacy-policy).

### Candidate experience and operations

#### Where in Greenhouse does verification show up and how is it triggered?

Recruiters can request verification from the Candidate Profile in the Greenhouse application. The verification process is performed by the candidate through MyGreenhouse, our candidate portal, via a guided flow.

You can read more about sending identity requests [here.](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/40893011137179) For more information on the candidate's experience, click [here](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/40497797083419).

#### Can candidates decline verification?

Yes. Candidates can opt out of verification. The decision on how to proceed with a candidate who declines is left to your recruiting team. Greenhouse does not perform candidate rejections on your behalf.

#### Can CLEAR be used for some jobs or stages only?

Yes. Teams can configure when and where to request verification (e.g., certain offices/departments and stages).

#### What if a candidate already uses CLEAR?

Existing CLEAR users generally complete a shorter flow (e.g., only a selfie/phone verification), with an automatic "step up" to request an updated ID if required by the existing configuration or due to ID expiration.

#### Can we use our CLEAR tenant if we are already using them as a vendor for corporate security use cases?

No. Greenhouse’s ID verification feature must be managed exclusively through our CLEAR tenant. We do not integrate with customer-specific CLEAR organization instances.

### Security and trust

#### Who has access to the CLEAR-collected personal data?

CLEAR, as the data controller, holds and secures the identity data (ID image/selfie). Greenhouse receives only limited data and the verification result necessary to inform the hiring team.

#### Does Greenhouse share candidate personal data from CLEAR to customers?

We display the verification result and limited cross-reference fields in-app to the customer, who becomes the data controller of this data on their Greenhouse tenant data. We do not receive or share ID images or selfies.

#### Can I limit which employees can interact with the ID verification feature in Greenhouse?

Yes. We provide job admin permission "stripes" to control who can view identity verification details and who can request identity verification details.

#### Are ID verification results from CLEAR used across customers?

No. ID verification result information is linked only to the specific job application where the verification request was initiated and is not used as a signal across customers. Each ID verification request and check is a unique operation, and we do not save/cache results and share them across customers.

#### How does Greenhouse & CLEAR keep your data safe?

Data is protected in transit using TLS 1.2+ and is protected at rest by both Greenhouse and CLEAR. Greenhouse adheres to a strict data minimization policy, requesting and receiving only the minimum amount of data collected by CLEAR necessary to power our product features.

Access to data is protected by safeguards such as multi-factor access controls that include device trust. Access to the console is very limited, requiring two levels of approval and quarterly access reviews. Staff members with access to this data must successfully complete a background check before being granted access to any customer data. Additionally, all staff members with customer data access must agree to our written zero-tolerance policy, which defines their responsibilities and the consequences (including, but not limited to, termination of employment) of abusing their access. Both Greenhouse and CLEAR undergo annual SOC 2 Type 2 audits to validate that our organizational security controls are operating as expected.

The U.S. Department of Homeland Security has certified CLEAR’s information security program at a FISMA High rating and designated CLEAR as a Qualified Anti-Terrorism Technology under the SAFETY Act.

# CRM permissions

**Permissions:** —

**Product tier:** Available for new subscription tiers (Core, Plus, and Pro)

This article covers the Job Admin, user-specific, and Sourcing Automation permissions associated with Greenhouse CRM. Click [here](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360022793612) for an overview of Greenhouse CRM.

**Note** : Some organizations in Greenhouse Recruiting may be using a legacy CRM licensing structure. For more information on the legacy CRM licensing structure, [click here](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360014882832).

### In this article:

#### In this article

  * Job Admin CRM permissions
  * CRM user-specific permissions
  * Assign CRM user-specific permissions
  * Sourcing Automation permissions



### Job Admin CRM permissions

Job Admin levels are defined sets of permissions that are granted to users on a per-job basis.

A user who is assigned to a job as a Job Admin has the following default visibility: 

  * Can see the job's Dashboard, pipeline, and reports
  * Can see all candidates on the job
  * Can add and edit candidates and referrals
  * Can be assigned hiring team roles



In addition to the default visibility, Site Admins can [enable](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360039863731) the following permissions that allow Job Admins to perform specific functions within CRM: 

Permission | With permission | Without permission  
---|---|---  
Can advance candidates / prospects | When granted, this permission allows Job Admins to [convert prospects to candidates](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360025848912) | The _convert to candidate_ button is not available  
Can reject candidates / prospects | When granted, this permission allows Job Admins to reject candidates using the [Stop considering as prospect](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360026133091) button from the prospect's profile | The _stop considering as prospect_ button is not available  
Can email candidates / prospects | When granted, this permission allows Job Admins to [email](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360026188391) prospects from the prospect's profile | The _email prospect_ button is not available  
Can create and view private prospects |  Marking a prospect as [private](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360039936051) restricts access to the prospect's profile for everyone except the prospect owner and users with access to view private prospects **Note** : If a Job Admin has **standard access** but is the _prospect owner_ of a private profile, they will have access to the profile | Job Admins can see private prospects from the _All Candidates_ page, but cannot view or manage their profiles  
Can merge candidates and prospects | When granted, this permission allows Job Admins to [merge duplicate profiles](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/115004506466) | Job Admins can see the prospect has a duplicate profile and are advised to reach out to a _Site Admin_ to merge the profiles  
Can view and create private notes | When granted, this permission allows Job Admins to view and create [private notes](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360031123492) | Job Admins aren't able to view or create private notes  
  
### CRM user-specific permissions

Users who are assigned the **Job** **Admin** permission level or higher can be assigned the following optional CRM user-specific permissions:

**Permission** | **With permission** | **Without permission**  
---|---|---  
View CRM and assign prospects to pools | When granted, this permission allows Job Admins to see the CRM, manage prospects they have access to by adding [touchpoints](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360020298312), assign [pools/stages reminders](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360020137872), and view [Talent Finder](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360022964432) | Job Admins don't have access to the CRM tab from your Greenhouse Recruiting dashboard  
Manage CRM | When granted, Job Admins can create pools and stages, and set prospect owners | Job Admins won't be able to create prospect pools and stages, or set [prospect owners](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/115002698026)  
Can create and manage recruiting events |  When granted, this permission allows Job Admins to purchase, create, and edit [events](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/115005216943) where you're an [admin](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360024600192) |  Job Admins can't purchase, create, or edit events  
Can manage unattached prospects |  When granted, this permission allows Job Admins to add [prospects](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/200670155) to jobs, convert prospects to candidates, and see the private tab for prospects in any jobs departments or offices that they have access to | CRM users **without** unattached prospect access can edit basic information, add tags and convert or reject unattached prospects in any jobs, departments or offices they have access to  
  
### Assign CRM user-specific permissions

**Note** : In order to assign user-specific permissions, you must be a **Site** **Admin** with the user-specific permission **Can edit another user's advanced permissions**.

To assign user-specific CRM permissions to a Greenhouse Recruiting user, click the **Configure** icon  on your navigation bar, then select **Users** on the left.

Click the name of the user for whom you wish to assign CRM user-specific permissions.

From the _Edit User_ page, scroll to the _User-Specific Permissions_ section.

Find _Other Actions_ and click the checkbox next to the CRM user-specific permission to be added to the user.

Click **Save** when finished.

### Sourcing Automation permissions

**Note** : When they're assigned a seat, Sourcing Automation users are automatically given CRM management access.

[Sourcing automation](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/5131929423643) is an add-on product within Greenhouse CRM that makes sourcing your superpower by helping you find, reach, and engage top talent quickly and effectively.

Once an organization purchases Sourcing Automation, users must have a **seat** in order to access its features. 

Click [here](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/4952434968091) to learn how to enable _Admin_ or _Standard_ access seats for users in your organization.

# Delete a custom demographic question set

**Permissions:** Site Admin

**Product tier:** Available for new subscription tiers (Core, Plus, and Pro)

Custom demographic question sets allow your organization to create and assign unique groupings of [custom demographic questions](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360004588971) that can be assigned on a per job basis. In this article, we will cover how to delete a custom demographic question set.

**Note** : Deleted custom demographic question sets will be removed from any and all assigned job posts and any collected data from the question set will be permanently removed from reports. 

Click on the **Configure** icon in the upper right-hand corner and select **Inclusion Tools** from the left-hand panel.

Navigate to the  _Custom Demographic Question Sets_ panel at the bottom of the subsequent page and click the name of a custom demographic question set. 

Navigate to the bottom of the subsequent page and click **Delete Question Set**.

A subsequent dialog box will ask you to confirm your decision. Click **Yes, Delete Question Set**.

The custom demographic question set will be deleted. It will be removed from any and all assigned job posts and any collected data from the question set will be permanently removed from reports.

# Tribe integration

Tribe allows you to discover talent anywhere in the world. Tribe's integration with Greenhouse Recruiting allows you to import any or all of your job postings to Tribe. When you post your jobs on Tribe, they get routed to "scouts," who are experienced and vetted recruiters in your target countries. Scouts will start sharing referrals, and Tribe will only forward referrals that they believe are the best fit.

#### In this article

  * Set up the Tribe integration
  * Use the Tribe integration
    * Import jobs from Greenhouse Recruiting
    * Add candidates to Greenhouse Recruiting
  * Additional resources



### Set up the Tribe integration

**Note** : Integration setup should only be completed once by an admin at your organization. After it's set up, people who wish to use the integration can enable and use it on Tribe.

To set up the Tribe integration, log in to [Tribe](ChooseTribe.com) using your credentials.

Click **Settings** on the left.

Click **Integrations**.

Click **Connect** beside Greenhouse.

Enter your Greenhouse Recruiting email address, then click **Authorize**.

Enter the public [job post URL](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360020561392) for any of your Greenhouse Recruiting jobs and click **Connect** **Greenhouse**.

### Use the Tribe integration

After the integration is enabled for the first time by an admin, any other users can set up the integration in a simpler way.

Log in to [Tribe](ChooseTribe.com) using your credentials.

From the home screen, click **Settings**.

Click **Integrations**.

Click **Connect** beside Greenhouse.

Enter your Greenhouse Recruiting email address then click **Authorize**.

#### Import jobs from Greenhouse Recruiting

After the integration is enabled, you can import more jobs simply by clicking on post a job. You will see all the jobs available in Greenhouse Recruiting, and you'll be able to add any or all of them to Tribe.

Once you click on a job to be imported, you can update job information and add more information about the job including job type, years of experience, must-have and nice-to-have skills, and countries where you want to hire. You can also enter the bounty you want to set.

#### Add candidates to Greenhouse Recruiting

Once you receive referrals for your job, applicants will show up on your Greenhouse Recruiting job.

### Additional resources

For additional information not covered here, reach out to [support@choosetribe.com](mailto:support@choosetribe.com).

# Scoutible integration

Scoutible is a next-generation AI for hiring, using immersive video games to identify perfect-fit candidates for jobs. Scoutible's technology identifies a person's unique cognitive and personality traits from their gameplay, and connects them with open jobs where they are virtually certain to be a top performer.  
  
#### In this article

  * Create a Harvest API key for the Scoutible integration
  * Create an integration system user (ISU)
  * Create webhooks
  * Create a custom candidate tag
  * Create a custom email template 
  * Create custom fields
  * Additional resources



### Create a Harvest API key for the Scoutible integration

To configure the Greenhouse Recruiting / Scoutible integration, you'll need to create a Harvest API key.

Follow the steps in [this article](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/5888163769883) to create the key, and verify that the credentials and permissions below are selected when configuring the Scoutible integration.

#### Credentials

In the _Create New Credential_ box, make the following selections:

  * **API type:** Harvest
  * **Partner:** Scoutible
  * **Description:** Scoutible Harvest API key



#### Permissions

Verify that the following permissions are selected for the Scoutible integration:

  * Activity feed
  * Applications
  * Candidates
  * EEOC
  * Job posts
  * Jobs
  * Rejection reasons
  * Tags
  * Users



If any of the permissions above are not checked, place a check in the box next to the appropriate permission. Click **Save** when finished.

Your Harvest API key for the Greenhouse Recruiting / Scoutible integration is created and configured. Paste the API key into the body of an email and send it to [support@scoutible.com](mailto:support@scoutible.com) with your company name as the subject line.

### Create an integration system user (ISU) for the Scoutible integration

Scoutible requires an integration system user (ISU) so that automated updates in candidate Activity Feeds are credited to the ISU.

[Check out this article to create an ISU](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/4405511253659), and enter the following details when creating a user for Scoutible integration:

  * **User emails** : [support@scoutible.com](mailto:support@scoutible.com)
  * **User permission:** Site Admin



When finished, click **Save**.

### Create webhooks for the Scoutible integration

To integrate Scoutible with Greenhouse Recruiting, you'll need to create five (5) webhooks. Follow the steps in [this article](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/5888163727003) to create your webhooks. Use the values listed below to configure the webhooks:

#### Webhook 1

  * **Name** : Scoutible invite
  * **When** : Candidate has submitted application
  * **Endpoint URL** : <https://api-dot-scoutible-app.appspot.com/api/v1/integrations/greenhouse>
  * **Secret Key** : The secret key received from the Scoutible team
  * **Error recipient email:**[support@scoutible.com](mailto:support@scoutible.com)
  * **Advanced settings****> Additional HTTP Headers: **The org key received from the Scoutible team



#### Webhook 2

  * **Name** : Job updated
  * **When** : Job updated
  * **Endpoint URL** : <https://api-dot-scoutible-app.appspot.com/api/v1/integrations/greenhouse/job>
  * **Secret Key** : The secret key received from the Scoutible team
  * **Error recipient email** : [support@scoutible.com ](mailto:support@scoutible.com)
  * **Advanced settings > Additional HTTP Headers**: The org key received from the Scoutible team



#### Webhook 3

  * **Name** : Rejected
  * **When** : Candidate or Prospect rejected
  * **Endpoint URL** : <https://api-dot-scoutible-app.appspot.com/api/v1/integrations/greenhouse/rejected>
  * **Secret Key** : The secret key received from the Scoutible team
  * **Error recipient email** : [support@scoutible.com ](mailto:support@scoutible.com)
  * **Advanced settings > Additional HTTP Headers**: The org key received from the Scoutible team



#### Webhook 4

  * **Name** : _Hired_
  * **When** : Candidate has been hired
  * **Endpoint URL** : <https://api-dot-scoutible-app.appspot.com/api/v1/integrations/greenhouse/hired>
  * **Secret Key** : The secret key received from the Scoutible team
  * **Error recipient email** : [support@scoutible.com ](mailto:support@scoutible.com)
  * **Advanced settings > Additional HTTP Headers**: The org key received from the Scoutible team



#### Webhook 5

  * **Name** : Email updated
  * **When** : Application updated
  * **Endpoint URL** : <https://api-dot-scoutible-app.appspot.com/api/v1/integrations/greenhouse/update-candidate>
  * **Secret Key** : The secret key received from the Scoutible team
  * **Error recipient email** : [support@scoutible.com ](mailto:support@scoutible.com)
  * **Advanced settings > Additional HTTP Headers**: The org key received from the Scoutible team



### Create a custom candidate tag in Greenhouse Recruiting

Next, you will create a custom candidate tag for _Played Scoutible_ which will allow you to filter between candidates who have played the Scoutible games and those who have not. This is important because the Performance Predictor results and Top Soft Skills are only available to candidates who have played Scoutible.

To create a custom candidate tag, click **Configure** on your navigation bar, then select **Custom** **Options** on the left.

Click **Candidate** **Tags**.

Click **Create New Candidate Tag**.

Enter _Played Scoutible_.

Click **Create Candidate Tag**.

**Note:** It is important to enter the name of the candidate tag exactly as shown, including capitalizing both words.

### Create a custom email template in Greenhouse Recruiting

**Note:** This step assumes Scoutible has created an invite microsite for you. This URL will be used in place of the highlighted URL found in the template body text below. If you don't have this URL, please contact Scoutible Support (support@scoutible.com) before completing this step. Otherwise, you may skip this step and move to the next step.

# Company goals

**Permissions:** Site Admin, and Job Admin who can create, edit, and delete company goals

**Product tier:** Available for new subscription tiers (Core, Plus, and Pro)

#### Measure, iterate, and improve every part of your hiring process

Company goals are organization-wide attainment targets. Use company goals to set performance targets so teams across your company can get measurably better at hiring. You can measure objectives like the time to submit scorecards or the time to approve offers. You can also set company goals by department.

Company goals are measured by a job's [hiring team](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/115002194983). Be sure to set up your hiring team ([recruiter](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360016347712), [hiring manager](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360016572311)) on each job to ensure goals are tracked effectively.

Once a company goal is set, people at your organization can track their progress against the organization's current and target attainment on their Greenhouse Recruiting dashboard.

**Note:** The company goals dashboard widget displays your individual attainment and your organization's overall attainment toward a company goal from the last 14 days to 11:59:59 PM of the previous day.

To quickly access and report on company goal attainment, click **See goal dashboard**.

#### In this article

  * Time to submit scorecards goal
  * Time to approve offers goal
  * Time to schedule available candidates goal
  * Time in stage goal
  * Time to review applications goal
  * Add department goals



### Time to submit scorecards goal

The time to submit scorecards goal is a company goal that represents the ideal time between when an interview ends and when someone submits their scorecard. Use this goal to ensure your teams are submitting scorecards in a timely manner.

**Note** : The person scheduled as the interviewer will receive credit for the time to submit scorecards goal. If an interview has multiple interviewers, each submitted scorecard will be counted in the goal.

To configure the time to submit scorecards goal, click the **Configure** icon on your navigation bar, then click **Company** **Goals** on the left.

Toggle on the **Time to submit scorecards** goal.

Hover over the goal to select the **Edit** icon.

Greenhouse Recruiting will share your organization's average attainment based on the past thirty days. We'll also share an average attainment range of all organizations with [mature hiring processes](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/4404792224795).

Set the target time in hours for your organization to submit scorecards.

When finished, click **Save changes** to create the goal.

Once a goal is set, people at your company who are impacted can track their attainment by navigating to _My Dashboard_ and viewing the _Company goals_ tile.

**Note** : You may need to [personalize your dashboard](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/115003243886) to see the company goals tile. Progress on company goals updates daily at approximately 8:00 PM EST. Your dashboard will show progress from the previous 15 days.

You can report on the time to submit scorecards goal with the [Time to submit scorecards attainment report](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/7507124760347).

### Time to approve offers goal

The time to approve offers goal represents the ideal time between when someone receives a candidate offer approval request and when they approve or deny the offer. Use this goal to ensure your teams are actioning offer approvals in a timely manner.

**Note** : Credit for the time to approve offers goal will accrue to all approvers in the approval flow equally. For instance, if two approvers are required, and one approves in 2 hours, while the other approves in 4 hours, the time to approve offers goal will show 4 hours for both approvers.

To configure the time to approve offers goal, click the **Configure** icon on your navigation bar, then click **Company****Goals** on the left.

Toggle on the **Time to approve offers** goal.

Hover over the goal to select the **Edit** icon.

Greenhouse Recruiting will share your organization's average attainment based on the past thirty days. We'll also share an average attainment range of all organizations with [mature hiring processes](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/4404792224795).

Set the target time in hours for your organization to approve offers.

When finished, click **Save changes** to create the goal.

Once a goal is set, people impacted at your company can track their attainment by navigating to _My Dashboard_ and viewing the _Company goals_ tile.

You can report on the time to approve offers goal with the [Time to approve offers report](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/9166643653403).

### Time to schedule available candidates goal

The time to schedule available candidates goal represents the ideal time between when a candidate becomes available for an interview and when they are scheduled for an interview. Use this goal to ensure your teams are scheduling candidates in a timely manner.

**Note** : Credit for the time to schedule available candidates goal will accrue for the responsible recruiter or coordinator (if present) on the [hiring team](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/115002194983) for a job.

To configure the time to approve offers goal, click the **Configure** icon on your navigation bar, then click **Company****Goals** on the left.

Toggle on the **Time to schedule available candidates** goal.

Hover over the goal to select the **Edit** icon.

Greenhouse Recruiting will share your organization's average attainment based on the past thirty days. We'll also share an average attainment range of all organizations with [mature hiring processes](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/4404792224795).

Set the target time in hours for your organization to schedule available candidates.

When finished, click **Save changes** to create the goal.

Once a goal is set, people impacted at your company can track their attainment by navigating to _My Dashboard_ and viewing the _Company goals_ tile.

You can report on the time to approve offers goal with the [Time to schedule available candidates report](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/9166289363739).

### Time in stage goal

The time in stage goal is a company goal that represents the ideal time between when a candidate is moved into a stage to when they exit the stage. Credit for time in stage goal attainment is accrued to the responsible recruiter (if present) on a job's [hiring team](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/115002194983). Use this goal to ensure your teams are actioning candidates in the pipeline in a timely manner.

**Note** : The time in stage goal doesn't include time spent in the Application Review or Hiring Manager Review stages, as candidates typically spend much less time in these stages. This helps your organization set a more accurate time in stage goal.

To configure the time in stage goal, click the **Configure** icon on your navigation bar, then click **Company****Goals** on the left.

Toggle on the **Time in stage** goal.

Hover over the goal to select the **Edit** icon.

Greenhouse Recruiting will share your organization's average attainment based on the past thirty days. We'll also share an average attainment range of all organizations with [mature hiring processes](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/4404792224795).

Set the target time in hours for your organization to move candidates through a stage.

When finished, click **Save changes** to create the goal.

Once a goal is set, people impacted at your company can track their attainment by navigating to _My Dashboard_ and viewing the _Company goals_ tile.

You can report on the time to approve offers goal with the [Time in stage goal attainment report](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/9964759087899).

### Time to review applications goal

The time to review applications goal is a company goal that represents the ideal time between when a candidate submits an application and when that candidate is advanced to the next stage or rejected during the Application Review or Hiring Manager Review stages.

Credit for attaining this goal goes to the job's [recruiter](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360016347712) for the Application Review Stage and the [hiring manager](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360016572311) for the Hiring Manager Review stage. Use this goal to ensure your teams are moving candidates through the pipeline in a timely manner.

To configure the time to review applications goal, click the **Configure** icon on your navigation bar, then click **Company****Goals** on the left.

Toggle on the **Time to review applications** goal.

Hover over the goal to select the **Edit** icon.

Set the target time in hours for your organization to schedule available candidates.

Greenhouse Recruiting will share your organization's average attainment based on the past thirty days. We'll also share an average attainment range of all organizations with [mature hiring processes](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/4404792224795).

When finished, click **Save changes** to create the goal.

Once a goal is set, people impacted at your company can track their attainment by navigating to _My Dashboard_ and viewing the _Company goals_ tile.

You can report on the time to approve offers goal with the [Time to review applications goal attainment report](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/10061338502171).

### Add department goals

You can also create department-specific goals for any of the above company goals. Click **Add****department****goal** to add a department goal under your organization's default goal.

Next, select the departments you want to include in the goal, and set your target time to submit scorecards in hours. When finished, click **Save****changes** to set your department goal.

To edit a department goal, hover over it and click the **Edit** icon.

Click **Delete goal** to delete this department-specific goal from your Company goals.

**Note** : Currently, department-level goal tracking isn’t possible on the dashboard. Instead, you'll need to run [goal reports](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/8383632617755) to track department goal progress.

**Learn more about goals**

[Goals overview](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/6829789189915)

[Individual goals](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/8381830669979)

[Report on goals](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/8383632617755)

[Goals report dashboard](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/11521533545755)

# Archive a custom offer field that has dependencies

**Permissions:** Job Admins, who can manage custom fields, and Site Admins

**Product tier:** Available for Plus and Pro subscription tiers

[Removing a custom offer field dependency](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360039294791) dissolves the relationship between parent and child custom offer fields, but keeps both fields in your organization.

[Archiving a custom offer field](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360024304872-Archive-Custom-Offer-Field) removes the field from your organization and often dissolves the relationship between the two fields. Archiving a custom offer field that is part of a dependency will impact the integrity of any dependencies.

#### In this article

  * Archive child custom offer field with a dependency
    * Archiving the child field in a standard dependency
    * Archiving the child field in a nested dependency
  * Archive a parent custom offer field with a dependency
    * Archiving the parent field in a standard dependency
    * Archiving the parent field in a nested dependency



### Archive child custom offer field with a dependency

#### Archiving the child field in a standard dependency

If the archived custom offer field is a child in a parent/child dependency, any configured dependency between the parent and child custom offer field will be dissolved.

**Example:** Archiving the **Equity** field removes the relationship between **Benefits** and the (archived) Equity field. The Benefits field will still exist.

#### Archiving the child field in a nested dependency

A **nested dependency** contains more than two layers of hierarchy. For example, if your **Hourly Pay Rate** field is dependent on the**Payment Type** , which is dependent on the **Employment Type,** it is considered a nested dependency.

If the archived custom offer field is the last option in the list, any configured dependency between the child and its immediate parent custom offer field will be dissolved. 

The dependency between any higher levels of the nested dependency will be preserved.

**Example:** Archiving **Hourly Pay Rate** will dissolve the relationship between**Payment Type** and **Hourly Pay Rate** , but keep the relationship between **Employment Type** and **Payment Type**.

### Archive a parent custom offer field with a dependency

#### Archiving the parent field in a standard dependency

If the archived custom offer field is a parent in a parent/child dependency, any configured dependency between the parent and child custom offer field will be dissolved.

Example: Archiving Benefits will dissolve the relationship between the Benefits and Equity field. However, the Equity field will still exist.

#### Archiving the parent field in a nested dependency

If the archived custom offer field is a parent in a nested dependency, the entire nested dependency will be dissolved. However, any subordinate fields will still exist and can be assigned to new hierarchies. 

**Example:** Archiving **Employment Type** dissolves both the relationship between**Employment Type** and **Payment Type,** as well as the relationship between **Payment Type** and **Hourly Pay Rate.** However, both the Payment Type and Hourly Pay fields will still exist.

# Adway integration

Adway provides a cutting-edge recruitment marketing platform that leverages artificial intelligence to automate and optimize the entire talent attraction process. By combining data-driven job advertising, employer branding, and real-time performance insights, Adway helps organizations reach the right candidates at the right time—across social media, job boards, and digital channels.

Adway’s integration with Greenhouse Recruiting allows users to: 

  * Fetch job posts from Greenhouse account via API
  * Create Ad campaigns based on the jobs retrieved
  * Gather candidate's applications (along with screening questions and CVs) and transfer them to Greenhouse via API 



#### In this article

  * Find your board token
  * Create a Harvest API key
  * Hiring Manager configuration and permissions
  * Connect Greenhouse Recruiting to Adway
  * Upload candidates to Greenhouse Recruiting
  * Additional resources



### Find your board token

You can find your Job Board URL and token by navigating to the Job Board settings. (**Configure** > **Job Boards & Posts** > **Ellipsis** icon next to job board > **Edit Board Settings**) and scroll to the URL field. Copy the value as you’ll need to paste it in Adway.

### Create a Harvest API key

To configure the integration, you’ll need to create a Harvest API key. 

Follow the steps in [this article](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/5888163769883) to create the key, and verify that the permissions below are selected when configuring the **Adway** integration. Be sure to copy the API key as you’ll need to paste it in Adway in the next step.

#### Credentials

In the _Create New Credential_ box, make the following selections:

  * **API Type:** Harvest
  * **Partner:** Adway or Unlisted Vendor
  * **Description:** Adway Harvest API Key



#### Permissions

Verify that the following permissions are selected for the **Adway** integration: 

  * **Applications**
    * Get: Retrieve Application
    * Get: List Applications
  * **Candidates**
    * Get: Retrieve Candidate
    * Patch: Edit Candidate
    * Post: Add Candidate
    * Post: Add E-mail
    * Post: Add Note
    * Post: Add Attachment
    * Post: Add Application
    * Post: Add Education
    * Post: Add Employment
  * **Job Openings**
    * Get: List Openings For a Job
  * **Job Posts**
    * Get: List Job Posts
    * Get: Retrieve Job Post for Job
    * Get: List Job Posts for Job
  * **Jobs**
    * Get: Retrieve Job
    * Get: List Jobs
    * Get: Get hiring team



### Hiring Manager configuration and permissions

The integration **only works when the hiring manager assigned to the job post is properly configured**. If the hiring manager does not have the necessary permissions to upload candidates, ensure that the **user ID** of a user with the appropriate permissions is provided. Our system will be able to perform actions on behalf of this user, allowing the process to continue smoothly.

#### Fields Mapping

This table outlines the mapping of fields from the Greenhouse object to our internal data structure. For each field in the input object, the corresponding mapped field in our system is listed, along with a brief description of its purpose. This ensures clarity on how data is transferred and transformed during the integration process.

**Source Field** | **Mapped Field** | **Description**  
---|---|---  
id | atsJobPostId | The unique ATS job post ID.  
city | adLocations.city | City of the job location.  
country | adLocations.country | Country of the job location.  
first_published_at | pubDate | Publication date of the job posting.  
title | title | Title of the job posting.  
  
Additionally, we process screening questions and public data via the Job Board to enrich the job posting information.

It’s important to note that this field mapping can be **customized** by our clients according to their specific needs. Clients have the flexibility to adjust how the data is mapped to fit their flows and requirements.

### Connect Greenhouse Recruiting to Adway

To connect your ATS (Applicant Tracking System) with Adway’s platform, follow these steps:

**1\. Navigate to the Connectors Page**

Go to the Connectors section of the platform and click the “Add” button to start creating a new integration.

**2\. Select Your ATS**

Choose the ATS you want to integrate with — in our case, **Greenhouse**.

**3\. Enter Credentials**

Provide the required authentication details:

  * **API Token** – from your Greenhouse account

  * **Board Token** – used to fetch job postings details

  * **User ID** – the identifier of the user who will submit candidate forms




**4\. Add Filters (Optional)**

You can apply filters to control which data is fetched or processed. This step is optional and can be skipped if not needed.

**Use the integration**

Once configured, you can:

  * **Run the connector manually**

  * Or wait for it to trigger automatically based on the schedule




### Upload candidates to Greenhouse Recruiting

Once all automation and nurturing processes are configured, you can begin creating social media campaigns to attract candidates through the platform.

#### Candidate Application Flow

When a candidate applies via your campaign landing page, there are two possible outcomes, depending on how the application criteria are configured:

**1\. Automatic Submission to Greenhouse**

If:

  * Application criteria are configured, and

  * The candidate meets the qualification requirements for the position




Then the system will automatically:

  * Create a candidate profile in Greenhouse

  * Submit the application

  * Upload questionnaire answers

  * Attach any uploaded files (e.g., resume, cover letter)




This process is handled automatically and requires no manual action.

**2\. Manual Submission**

If:

  * Application criteria are not configured, or
  * The candidate does not meet the required qualifications



Then no data is sent to Greenhouse automatically.

However, the candidate is still stored within the platform and can be manually submitted to Greenhouse at any time via the Candidates page.

### Additional resources

For more information or troubleshooting not covered here, you can:

Contact Adway directly through Intercom on the dashboard

Visit the [Adway Documentation](https://docs.adway.ai/integration-docs/HHaRjOp4nbF2aZBuvEbf)

# Humaans integration

Humaans is an HRIS built to be the foundation layer of an organization’s HR tech stack. It helps teams onboard and manage their employees through fast workflows, automation, and quick access to data. Designed for speed, Humaans features a beautiful people directory, document storage, time-off tracking, visual reporting, and integrates with many tools you already use.

Greenhouse Recruiting’s integration with Humaans allows you to automatically import hired candidates from Greenhouse to Humaans.

In this article

  * Retrieve Humaans’s endpoint URL and secret key
  * Create a webhook
  * Import hired candidates to Humaans
  * Additional support



### Retrieve Humaans’s endpoint URL and secret key

To enable the Greenhouse Recruiting / Humaans integration, you will need two pieces of information:

  * Humaans's endpoint URL
  * Humaans's secret key



To retrieve this information please open the **Admin** area in the Humaans app. You will need to have an Owner or Admin role to set up the integration. In the Admin area, find the _Integrations_ section and click **Configure** in the Greenhouse entry.

To enable the integration, click **Enable** **integration**.

This provides you with the endpoint URL and secret key as shown below.

Copy the endpoint URL and secret key to enter in Greenhouse Recruiting in the next step.

### Create a webhook

To integrate Humaans with Greenhouse Recruiting, you'll need to create a webhook. Follow the steps in [this article](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/5888163727003) to create your webhook. Use the values listed below to configure the webhooks.

  * **Name** : Humaans Integration
  * **When** : Candidate has been hired
  * **Endpoint URL** : The endpoint URL copied from Humaans
  * **Secret key** : The secret key copied from Humaans



### Import hired candidates to Humaans

When a candidate is marked as hired in Greenhouse Recruiting, they will be imported to Humaans and will appear under the **New hires** tab in the People directory.

From there, you can either remove the new hires or add them as a member to your company.

The following fields are imported from Greenhouse Recruiting to Humaans:

**Greenhouse Recruiting field** | **Humaans field**  
---|---  
First name | First name  
Last name | Last name  
Personal email | Personal email  
Mobile phone or Home phone | Personal phone  
Home address | Address  
Internal job name | Job title  
Department | Department  
Office | Place of Work  
Employment type | Contract type  
Start date | Employment start date  
  
**Note:** Place of work will be synced by matching the **Office** name in Greenhouse Recruiting to the **Location** label/city in Humaans. If no match is found, the location will not be imported and you will be ale to select the location when adding the new hire as a member.

### Additional support

Contact [team@humaans.io](mailto:team@humaans.io) for troubleshooting assistance regarding the integration.

# BetterCloud integration

BetterCloud helps IT teams manage and secure user activity across the digital workplace. Greenhouse Recruiting's integration with BetterCloud allows IT teams to easily add new users to Greenhouse Recruiting, update users' names, deactivate and activate users, add and remove job permissions, and add and remove future job permissions.

#### In this article

  * Create a Harvest API key for the BetterCloud integration
  * Enable the BetterCloud integration
  * Use the BetterCloud integration
  * Additional resources



### Create a Harvest API key for the BetterCloud integration

To configure the Greenhouse Recruiting / BetterCloud integration, you'll need to create a Harvest API key.

Follow the steps in [this article](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/5888163769883) to create the key, and verify that the credentials and permissions below are selected during configuration:

#### Credentials

In the _Create New Credential_ box, make the following selections:

  * **API type:** Harvest
  * **Partner:** BetterCloud (optional)
  * **Description:** BetterCloud Harvest API Key



#### Permissions

Verify that the following permissions are selected for the BetterCloud integration:

**Departments**

  * Select all



**Jobs**

  * Select all



**Offices**

  * Select all



**User Roles**

  * Select all



**Users**

  * Select all



Once complete, copy the Harvest API key to provide to BetterCloud in the next step.

### Enable the BetterCloud integration

In your BetterCloud account, enter a name for your integration in the _Name_ field.

In the _API Token_ field, paste the Harvest API key you created in Greenhouse Recruiting.

In the _Admin Email_ field, enter your email address (or the email address of the admin), and click **Install**.

### Use the BetterCloud integration

In the example below, we'll build a workflow that deactivates a Greenhouse Recruiting user when they are added to a ‘deprovision’ org unit in BetterCloud's Google domain.

In BetterCloud, click **Workflow** from the navigation menu and then click **New**.

In the _Name your workflow_ box, enter a name for your workflow.

Since the action will be triggered by a change in the Org Unit, make the following selections:

  * In the top menu under _Library_ , select **When**.
  * Under _Conditions_ , select **Org Unit**.
  * Under _Options_ , select **Org Unit**.

# Yardstik integration

Yardstik brings better trust and safety tools for companies that need to quickly screen, verify, and hire people at scale.

Yardstik's integration with Greenhouse Recruiting allows you to order and review background check screenings for candidates. To use this integration, you need a Yardstik account with the ability to create custom integrations. 

#### In this article

  * Set up the integration
    * Create a secret key in Yardstik
    * Create a webhook
    * Create a custom field
    * Create a Harvest API key
    * Enable on Yardstik
  * Use the integration



### Set up the integration

#### Create a secret key in Yardstik

First, navigate to the Yardstik developer page and click the **Integrations** section. Edit the **Greenhouse** integration. Generate an API key to use as your **Secret Key** in Greenhouse.

Copy the API key you just generated, and log in to Greenhouse Recruiting.

### Create a webhook

With your Greenhouse API key from Yardstik, create a webhook in Greenhouse Recruiting. Follow the steps in [this article](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/5888163727003) to create your webhook, and use the values listed below to configure the webhook:

  * **Name** : Yardstik integration
  * **When** : Candidate has been hired
  * **Endpoint URL** : Enter the Yardstik API URL
  * **Secret** **key** : Enter the API key from Yardstik



**Note:** For **When** , you may also use Candidate has changed stage. So the webhook will only fire once, you need to configure a custom [stage](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/115002194903) in your job's Greenhouse Recruiting hiring flow with the name _Yardstik BGC_.

In the **Advanced Settings** options, enter the following snippet to create a header to send the secret key with the request: `x-yardstik-api-key: {your-yardstik-generated-api-key}`

Create your webhook.

#### Create a custom field

Next, create a custom field to select the Yardstik Account Package for the candidate. When the integration is set up, this field will automatically include all of your available Yardstik Account Packages.

Follow the steps [in this article](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/202609855) to create a custom job field using the details below:

  * **Name** : Yardstik Package
  * **Field type** : Single-select, with one option of "None." Make this field required.



Mark the field as **Private** , and **Save** the field.

#### Create a Harvest API key

Next, create a Harvest API key for the integration. Follow the steps [in this article](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/5888163769883) to create a Harvest API key, using the details below:

  * **API type:** Harvest
  * **Partner:** Yardstik or Unlisted Vendor 
  * **Description:** Yardstik Harvest API Key



Verify that the following permissions are selected for the Yardstik integration:

Candidates

  * **GET:** Retrieve candidate
  * **PATCH:** Edit candidate
  * **POST:** Add note



Jobs

  * **PATCH:** Update job



Custom fields

  * **GET:** Get custom fields
  * **POST:** Create custom field options
  * **PATCH:** Update custom field
  * **DELETE:** Delete custom field



Custom field options

  * **GET:** Custom field options
  * **POST:** create custom field options
  * **DELETE:** Remove custom field options
  * **PATCH:** Update custom field options



Copy the created API key to a secure location for use in the next step.

#### Enable on Yardstik

Paste your Harvest API key into the Greenhouse Harvest API Key field in Yardstik. Enter the name of the Greenhouse Recruiting custom job field in Yardstik. And finally, enter a Greenhouse Recruiting Site Admin [user ID](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/10765948752027) to be associated with the integration.

**Tip** : [Create an ISU, or integration system user,](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/4405511253659) instead of using a personal Site Admin account to authenticate the integration. Rather than requiring a specific user at your organization to authenticate the integration, which could cause downstream errors if the person loses permissions or can't access Greenhouse Recruiting, an ISU allows you to create a solid infrastructure for your organization's integration needs.

When finished, click **Update**.

After the configuration is complete, turn on the Greenhouse Recruiting integration in Yardstick to enable the flow of data.

### Use the integration

When you create a job, your custom job field will automatically include the account packages you have set up in Yardstik.

Once a candidate passes through the job stage that you selected when creating the webhook, the Yardstik invitation will automatically be sent.

When the status of the Yardstik report changes, you'll be notified in the Private Notes section on the candidate's profile.

# HireRight integration

HireRight is the premier global background screening and workforce solutions provider, bringing clarity and confidence to vetting and hiring decisions through integrated, tailored solutions that drive a higher standard of accuracy. Combining in-house talent, personalized services, and proprietary technology, HireRight ensures the best candidate experience possible.

Greenhouse Recruiting's integration with HireRight allows you to order background screening services from HireRight directly through Greenhouse Recruiting.

#### In this article

  * Enable the integration
  * Use the integration
    * Submit an order
    * Check the status of an order
    * View background check results
    * Map additional field(s)
  * Troubleshoot the integration



### Enable the integration

To enable the integration, contact your HireRight account manager with the email addresses of the people who need access to the integration.

Greenhouse Technical Support will work with HireRight and your account administrator to set up the integration. Once HireRight and Greenhouse Recruiting confirm the integration is set up, you can begin placing background check orders in Greenhouse Recruiting.

**Note:** The email address provided to HireRight must match your primary email address in Greenhouse Recruiting. To add or update your account email address, [click here](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360034879332).

### Use the integration

#### Submit an order

You can send a HireRight order for a candidate in the right panel on the candidate profile by clicking **Export to HireRight**.

Click **Complete Report** to continue to complete your order. This link is used to start your order and can be used later to view the order's status. Finally, complete the order details on the HireRight platform according to your organization's processes and policies.

#### Check the status of an order

If you previously ordered a background check for a candidate and want to view the status, click **HireRight Report** on the candidate's profile. You'll be taken to HireRight to view the background check status.

#### View background check results

When a candidate's background check is complete, the **Report Details** section in HireRight displays the results of each background check and highlights any discrepancies between the applicant's profile in Greenhouse Recruiting and their completed background check.

You can view other parts of the candidate's background check in this report.

#### Map additional field(s)

You can control how additional candidate data obtained during the candidate process is sent to HireRight for background checks.

To access the integration, you'll want navigate to the HireRight Field Mappings page. _(**Configure** > **Dev Center** > **HireRight Field Mappings**)_

On this page you will find your standard field mappings that are locked and any approved custom fields that can be mapped.  
  
To edit or delete a field mapping, hover over the individual mapping, click the **pencil icon** , and follow the steps.  


### Troubleshoot the HireRight integration

#### No packages available when exporting to HireRight

If no packages are available when selecting to export a candidate to HireRight, it's possible that you don't have the appropriate permissions within HireRight. 

We recommend checking with your HireRight Admin to make sure that your email has been allowlisted and to confirm that your email address matches the email associated with your Greenhouse Recruiting account.

**Note** : Every Greenhouse Recruiting user has a primary email address and optional secondary email addresses. For this integration to work properly, the email address used to log in to HireRight must match the primary email in Greenhouse Recruiting.

**Tip** : For help using HireRight, contact [HireRight support](https://www.hireright.com/contact-us).

# Appcast organic job posts

**Permissions:** Site Admin

**Product tier:** Available for new subscription tiers (Core, Plus, and Pro)

Greenhouse Recruiting allows you to post free job ads on several partner boards, including [Appcast](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/203941579)'s expansive network of job sites. Appcast's free ads can help expand your reach, allowing access to more candidates at no additional cost to your organization.

Unlike other free external job boards such as [Indeed](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/115002006126), which are enabled on a per-job basis through the _Job Post Edit_ page, Appcast organic job posts are configured at the job board level in Greenhouse Recruiting. Once enabled, all live job posts on the job board will also appear on Appcast as organic job posts.

#### In this article

  * Enable Appcast organic job posts
  * Update or delete a job post on Appcast



### Enable Appcast organic job posts

To enable Appcast organic job posts, click the **Configure** icon in the top-right corner of the page and select **Job Boards & Posts** from the left-side panel.

Locate the job board where you want to set up the integration. Click the **Ellipsis** icon beside the job board and select **Edit Board Settings** from the dropdown menu.

On the _Edit Your Job Board_ page, scroll to **Allow candidates to apply directly from Appcast** , and select **Yes**.

When finished, scroll to the bottom of the page and click **Save**.

Once enabled, all live job posts associated with the job board will be sent to Appcast. Candidates applying through these job posts will be added to Greenhouse Recruiting with **Appcast** in the source field.

**Note:** Once a job post is published, Greenhouse Recruiting sends the job post information to Appcast within 3 – 4 hours. From there, it can take up to 48 hours for the data to be processed and the job post to appear on Appcast's website.

### Update or delete a job post on Appcast

To edit the content of a job post on Appcast or remove it entirely from Appcast's network, [edit](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/115002791566) or [delete](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360023264611) the job post on Greenhouse Recruiting. Your changes will sync with Appcast the next time Appcast receives updates from Greenhouse Recruiting.

# Add a LinkedIn prospect to the Greenhouse Recruiting Chrome extension

**Permissions:** Job Admin and above with CRM access, a Sourcing Automation seat, and a LinkedIn account

**Product tier:** Available for the Plus and Pro subscription tiers

If your organization uses Greenhouse Sourcing Automation, you can add prospects in LinkedIn to your campaign pools with the Greenhouse Recruiting Chrome extension.

**Note:** You can install the [Greenhouse Recruiting extension](https://chrome.google.com/webstore/detail/greenhouse-recruiting-chr/naooopefdfeangnkgmjpklgblnfmbaea) from the Chrome Web Store.

#### In this article

  * Add a prospect from LinkedIn
    * Add a LinkedIn prospect automatically
    * Upload a prospect's LinkedIn profile
  * Check for duplicate prospects
  * Perform an email lookup
  * Perform a phone number lookup
  * Upload your LinkedIn prospect to a pool
  * Additional resources



### Add a prospect from LinkedIn

You can add a prospect from LinkedIn to the Greenhouse Recruiting Chrome extension in two ways:

  * Go to the prospect's LinkedIn profile and prefill the extension fields
  * Save the prospect's profile as a PDF and upload it to the extension



#### Add a LinkedIn prospect manually

Open a prospect's LinkedIn profile in Google Chrome.

Click the Greenhouse Recruiting Chrome extension from the top-right extensions menu. The extension will open automatically in a separate window.

**Note:** If you haven't already, log in to your Greenhouse Recruiting account. Click **Sign in to Greenhouse Recruiting** and enter your credentials to log in.

The Greenhouse Recruiting extension will check for duplicate prospects in your Sourcing Automation campaign pools. If none are found, click **Prefill** to add your prospect's details to the extension.

#### Upload a prospect's LinkedIn profile

Open a prospect's LinkedIn profile in Google Chrome.

Click the Greenhouse Recruiting Chrome extension from the top-right extensions menu. The extension will open automatically in a separate window.

Click **More** on the prospect's LinkedIn profile __ and select **Save to PDF** from the dropdown.

**Note** : Due to [LinkedIn's download limits](https://www.linkedin.com/help/recruiter/answer/a412149/export-profiles-in-recruiter?lang=en), you can only save 200 LinkedIn profiles as a PDF per month. Once you reach this limit, the **Save to PDF** button won't be available until the next month. As an alternative, you can perform an email lookup in the Greenhouse Chrome extension or use the [LinkedIn RSC integration](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360036524551) to add prospects to Greenhouse Recruiting.

The extension automatically uploads and parses information from the PDF download and attaches it as a resume to the extension.

You can also drag and drop the saved PDF into the extension or click **Upload resume** to manually import the PDF from your files.

### Check for duplicate prospects

The Greenhouse Recruiting Chrome extension automatically checks your campaign pools for potential duplicates when adding prospects from LinkedIn. A prospect is treated as a possible duplicate when any of the following details match with another prospect: first and last name, email address, phone number, or LinkedIn profile URL. These duplicate checks always use all four details and are separate from the [Duplicate tag configuration](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/49207850415003-Configure-the-Duplicate-tag) used for candidate profiles in the Greenhouse Recruiting web app.

If a potential duplicate is found, you'll see the duplicate's current details from Sourcing Automation.

Click **View duplicate** to open this duplicate in Greenhouse Sourcing Automation and learn more.

If you've determined this prospect isn't a duplicate, click **Prefill** to add their LinkedIn profile details to the extension's fields.

### Perform an email lookup

If you'd like, you can manually perform an [email lookup](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/6018927588635) for a LinkedIn prospect on the first step of the Greenhouse Recruiting Chrome extension.

When adding a LinkedIn prospect, paste the prospect's **LinkedIn URL** into the Chrome extension.

Click **Lookup email** to perform an email lookup using your prospect's LinkedIn profile.

If an email is found during lookup, the **Email** field will automatically populate with the prospect's email. If more than one email is found during lookup, click the link under the **Email** field to select which email you'd like to save for this prospect.

If no email is found during lookup, the **Email** field will remain empty. No lookup credits will be charged.

### Perform a phone number lookup

Once you've looked up a prospect's email, you can also perform a phone lookup to locate your prospect's phone number.

**Continue** to Step Two of the Chrome extension.

Click **Lookup** next to the phone icon to perform a lookup for your prospect's phone number.

**Note:** Phone lookups are **turned off** by default. A user with Site Admin access will need to give your organization access to phone lookups in  _Permission Policies_.

### Upload your prospect to a pool

Fill out any other details you want to include for your LinkedIn prospect in Sourcing Automation, then click **Continue**.

On the extension's second step, use the **Pool** field to select a **campaign pool** or **prospect pool** for this prospect.

In the **Source** field, select **LinkedIn (Prospecting)**. If you upload a PDF of the prospect's LinkedIn profile, this field will be filled out automatically.

Under **Job details** , select the **recruiter** who located this prospect and the **job** that you'd like to connect with this prospect.

When you're ready, click **Upload prospect** to send this prospect to your pool in Greenhouse Sourcing Automation.

### Additional resources

  * [Greenhouse Recruiting Chrome extension for Sourcing Automation](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/8302875133083)
  * [Understanding lookup credits](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/6018927588635)
  * [Deactivate lookup credits for your organization](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/10727614663195)

# Edit an E-Signature template

**Permissions:** Owners and Coordinators

**Product tier:** Available for the Greenhouse Onboarding subscription tier

[E-Signature templates](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/115003695071) allow your organization to assign e-signature documents to new hires and automate essential paperwork processes for your onboarding team.

This article covers how to edit your existing E-Signature templates.

**Note:** E-Signatures are available to the Greenhouse Onboarding subscription tier only. Learn more about the [differences between Greenhouse Onboarding and Greenhouse Welcome](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/11923239216539).

#### In this article

  * Edit your E-Signature template  

    * Update your template's name and counter signer
    * Place additional fields
    * Update your template's rules
  * Delete your E-Signature template
  * Additional resources



### Edit your E-Signature template

**Note:** Changes made to your E-Signature templates will not affect E-Signature documents that have been signed already.

From your Greenhouse Onboarding homepage, go to **Settings** > **Onboarding Plan** > **E-Signature Templates**.

On the  _E-Signature Templates_ page, click the **three-dot** icon next to the template you want to update.

Select **Edit template** from the dropdown to begin editing.

#### Update your template's name and counter signer

In the template editor, use the **Name** field to edit your E-Signature template's name.

Mark the **Requires a different public facing name?** checkbox if you want a different name to be visible when employees sign this document.

If your E-Signature template includes a [counter signer](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/8857059763099), you can update the assigned user with the **Who should counter sign on this?** field.

Click **Next**.

#### Place additional fields

In the next step, edit your existing E-Signature templates to add more fields.

**Note:** You can navigate directly to this step from the  _E-Signature Templates_ page. Click the **three-dot** icon next to the template you want to edit, then select **Place Fields**.

This option is available for custom E-Signature templates that your organization has created. You won't be able to place additional fields in default I-9 or W-4 forms.

In the template editor, click and hold to drag any of the following fields into your E-Signature document:

**Signature fields**

  * Signature
  * Initials



**Auto-fill fields**

  * Date signed
  * Full name
  * Email
  * Company
  * Job title



**Standard fields**

  * Textbox
  * Checkbox
  * Dropdown
  * Radio group



When you're done, click **Continue**.

#### Update your template's rules

In the next step, update your existing E-Signature template's employee match rules and assign date to specify who should receive this template and when.

**Note:** You can navigate directly to this step from the  _E-Signature Templates_ page. Click the **three-dot** icon next to the template you want to edit, then select **Set Rules**.

Toggle the **Add to Onboarding Plan** switch on if you'd like this template to be assigned automatically to new hires when they receive their onboarding plan. 

Use the **Assign Date** dropdown to select a date relative to the new hire's start date or a custom assign date.

Use the dropdown fields for **Department matches** , **Location matches** , **Employment Status matches** , and **Other Criteria****matches** to specify which new hires should be assigned this template.

**Example:** You'd like to assign an E-Signature template to new hires who are part-time employees based in San Francisco. Select **San Francisco** for the location match and **Part-time** for the employment status match.

Toggle the **Add to Onboarding Plan** switch off if you want to assign your E-Signature template manually on a case-by-case basis.

**Note:** If you toggle this switch to off, you won't be able to configure an assign date or new hire match rules.

### Delete your E-Signature template

On the  _E-Signature Templates_ page, click the **three-dot** icon next to the template you want to update.

Select **Delete template** from the dropdown.

### Additional resources

  * [Create an E-Signature template](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/115003695071)
  * [Assign a counter signer for E-Signatures](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/8857059763099)
  * [Assign custom access to manage E-Signatures](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/19104561087899)

# Highmatch integration

HighMatch I-O Psychologists create personalized, data-driven assessments tailored specifically to your organization’s roles, culture, and challenges.

Unlike our competitors, we provide role-based pricing and expert support from our workplace psychology team. These I/O Psychologists collaborate closely with your hiring teams to ensure your assessment is delivering actionable candidate insights.

HighMatch’s integration with Greenhouse Recruiting allows you to seamlessly add HighMatch’s assessment to a job's interview plan.

#### In this article

  * Enable the integration
  * Use the integration with Greenhouse Recruiting
  * Additional resources



### Enable the integration

First, connect with your HighMatch rep and request the Greenhouse integration. Once they approve the request, they’ll reach out to you with a HighMatch API key. Follow the steps in [this article](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/5888163696923) to work with Greenhouse support to activate the HighMatch prod stage and add the assessment stage in your interview plans.

Once you’ve set up your interview plans and configured your final assessment with HighMatch, you’ll be able to send the assessment to candidates.

### Use the integration with Greenhouse Recruiting

Once the HighMatch integration is enabled for your organization, you will be able to add the HighMatch assessment as an interview stage.

You can send an assessment to a candidate by selecting the**Send Test to candidate** button once the candidate is moved to the interview stage with an added assessment. The assessment invitation will be sent by HighMatch.

After it has been sent, an assessment’s status will display in Greenhouse Recruiting.

Once the candidate has submitted their test, the Interview Kit will contain a link to view the submitted test in the HighMatch application.

To see a candidate’s results report in HighMatch, click **Go to test**.

### Additional resources

For additional information not covered here, reach out to [support@highmatch.com](mailto:support@highmatch.com), or view our full integration documentation in our Knowledge Base:

[Enabling the HighMatch Connector](https://www.highmatch.com/knowledge-base/enabling-the-highmatch-connector-for-greenhouse-recruiting/)

[Using the HighMatch Connector](https://www.highmatch.com/knowledge-base/using-the-highmatch-connector-for-greenhouse-recruiting/)
