# Goals for new hires FAQ

**Permissions:** Owners, Hiring Managers and Employees

**Product tier:** Available for Greenhouse Welcome and Greenhouse Onboarding subscription tiers

[Goals for new hires](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/9265626455067) improve the onboarding experience by allowing hiring managers to set measurable and attainable growth-related objectives for their new hires.

Read below for answers to frequently asked questions about goals for new hires. 

#### In this article

  * Frequently asked questions
    * Can I customize my goals for new hires?
    * Can I create onboarding goals in bulk?
    * Can I use my job kickoff form responses when creating new hire goals in Greenhouse Onboarding?
    * Can I copy existing onboarding goals or create goal templates?
    * Will I receive email notifications and reminders related to new hire goals?
    * Can I update my new hire's existing goals?
    * How do I share onboarding goals with my new hire?
    * How do I change the status of my assigned onboarding goals?
    * How do I check the status of my new hire's goals?
    * Can I report on my team's new hire goals?
  * Additional resources



### Frequently asked questions

#### Can I customize onboarding goals for my new hires?

Greenhouse analyzed how customers achieved successful onboarding experiences and used this data to create common goals that provide structure and clear objectives in a new hire's first 30 days.

We've provided 14 pre-defined goals that hiring managers and Owners can select from when managing new hire goals. When you [create new hire goals](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/9265706878619) for the first time, you'll see five default goals that we recommend for a well-rounded onboarding experience. You can customize this experience by adding, editing, or deleting any of the 14 pre-defined goals.

Customize your new hire's goals in the following ways:

  * Add goals from a pre-defined list of new hire goals
  * Edit the description of your new hire goals
  * Change the order of your new hire goals
  * Delete new hire goals



**Note:** Goal names cannot be customized.

#### Can I create onboarding goals in bulk?

Not at this time. Goals are created individually for each new hire from their [employee profile](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/5759718119707).

#### Can I use my job kickoff form responses when creating new hire goals in Greenhouse Onboarding?

Yes! If the hiring manager submitted a [job kickoff form](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/4416516351003) for a new hire's role in Greenhouse Recruiting, their responses to "New hire goals" kickoff questions will be available in Greenhouse Onboarding. You can use job kickoff responses to guide you when [creating onboarding goals](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/9265706878619) for your new hire.

#### Can I copy existing onboarding goals or create goal templates?

You'll need to copy existing onboarding goals descriptions manually to duplicate them for another new hire. We recommend copying and storing commonly used goals in a safe location. You can paste these goals into Greenhouse Onboarding each time you set a new hire's goals.

Onboarding goal templates are not available at this time.

#### Will I receive email notifications and reminders related to new hire goals?

Greenhouse Onboarding offers three [email notifications](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/12198189055387) related to onboarding goals that users with Owner permissions can turn on in  _Settings_.

Use these email notifications to notify hiring managers when it's time to create onboarding goals and to remind new hires when it's time to update the status of their goals.

**Note:** Hiring managers and new hires will not receive onboarding goal notifications until your organization [turns on 30 day goals emails](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/12198189055387). Make sure to turn these on to take full advantage of new hire goals!

#### Can I update my new hire's existing goals?

Yes! You can edit existing goal descriptions, add new goals, or delete goals at any time from a new hire's employee profile. Learn more about [editing onboarding goals](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/9265706878619).

#### How do I share onboarding goals with my new hire?

Once you create and save onboarding goals, you'll need to [share them with your new hire](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/9265706878619). In the  _30 day goals_ tab of your new hire's employee profile, click **Share** to send onboarding goals to your new hire by email.

#### How do I change the status of my assigned onboarding goals?

New hires can update the status of their assigned onboarding goals from their employee profile. They can use the following statuses to help track their progress toward completing goals:

  * To do
  * In progress
  * Need help
  * Completed



Learn more about [completing your assigned new hire goals](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/9265765891995).

#### How do I check the status of my new hire's goals?

Hiring managers can view the status of each new hire's goals in their [employee profile](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/5759718119707). Email notifications for status changes are unavailable at this time.

**Note****:** Hiring managers will be notified by email any time their new hire changes a goal's status to **Need help**.

#### Can I report on my team's new hire goals?

Reporting on new hire goals will be available at a later date. You can view each new hire's progress toward onboarding goals from their [employee profile](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/5759718119707).

### Additional resources

Check out the following resources to learn more about goals for new hires in Greenhouse Onboarding.

#### Learn more

  * [Goals for new hires overview](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/9265626455067)
  * [Create and manage goals for new hires](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/9265706878619)
  * [Complete your new hire goals](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/9265765891995)
  * [Goals for new hires email notifications](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/12198189055387)

# HRIS Link job import errors

**Permissions:** —

**Product tier:** Available to Pro subscription with HRIS Link add-on

Greenhouse Recruiting sends a [status email](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/4402652528923) each time HRIS Link runs to confirm whether the sync succeeded or failed. If HRIS Link fails, the email will contain an error.

HRIS Link errors serve to inform you of the cause of the problem and the suggested solution.

Check out the table below to find the error name from your email, along with details on how to solve it.

**Note** : Some errors are blocking errors, meaning updates to information in Greenhouse Recruiting are blocked by the error. You need to resolve the error in order for HRIS Link to sync properly.

**Email subject** | **Error name**  
---|---  
HRIS Link: Job import failed |  No office exists with Name or External ID <value> or No department exists with Name or External ID <value>  
HRIS Link: Job import failed |  Error message: Custom Field {CUSTOM_JOB_FIELD_NAME} has no option for value '<VALUE>'  
HRIS Link: Job import failed |  No user exists with Email or Employee ID <value>  
HRIS Link: Job import failed |  403 Forbidden  
HRIS Link: Job import failed |  401 Unauthorized  
HRIS Link: Job import completed with errors |  Hiring Manager with ID <value> cannot access job or Recruiter with ID <value> cannot access job  
HRIS Link: Job import completed with errors |  X jobs found in Greenhouse with requisition_id: <value>  
HRIS Link: Job import completed with errors |  Access denied  
HRIS Link: Job import completed with errors |  Missing required field: template_job_id or Template hiring plan does not exist  
HRIS Link: Job import completed with errors |  Resource not found  
HRIS Link: Job import completed with errors |  Something went wrong and this job is likely partially created in Greenhouse  
HRIS Link: Job import completed with errors |  Currency unit is required for currency custom fields  
HRIS Link: Job import completed with errors |  Must be one of [currency units]  
HRIS Link: Job import completed with errors |  On-Behalf-Of user does not have permission to assign this role for this job  
HRIS Link: Job import completed with errors |  Number of opening IDs does not match the defined number of openings  
HRIS Link: Job import completed with errors |  REQ_ID Partial Recruiter data provided or REQ_ID Partial Hiring Manager data provided  
HRIS Link: Job import completed with errors | {REQ_ID} Is not required, but can not be updated to blank  
HRIS Link: Job import completed with errors | No office exists with Name or External ID 'external_id'  
HRIS Link: Job import completed with errors | Must be a string; Discovered value: <value>  
HRIS Link: Failed to access Workday®️ |  We encountered an error when trying to poll your Workday®️ report  
HRIS Link: Failed to access Workday®️ |  Error message from Workday®️: 500: Processing error occurred  
HRIS Link: Failed to access Workday®️ |  Error message from Workday®️: 503: Service unavailable  
HRIS Link: Failed to access Workday®️ |  Error message from Workday®️: 400: Validation error occurred  
HRIS Link: Failed to access Workday®️ |  Error message from Workday®️: 401: Invalid username or password  
HRIS Link: Job import failed |  {REQ_ID} Server error  
  
#### No office exists with Name or External ID <value> or No department exists with Name or External ID <value>

Email subject | HRIS Link: Job import failed  
---|---  
Error information | No office exists with Name or External ID <value> or No department exists with Name or External ID <value>  
Issue | The office referenced in the HRIS report doesn't exist in Greenhouse Recruiting. The report value must exist as an office name or external ID in Greenhouse Recruiting.  
Blocking error? |  Yes, this is a blocking error. Updates will not occur in Greenhouse Recruiting until the error is resolved.  
Solution |  Take the following steps to troubleshoot this issue. **If your organization is using[structured offices and departments](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360013442831):**

  1. Audit the HRIS Link job import report, or the job in your HRIS, for the office or department name or external ID that caused the error.
  2. In Greenhouse Recruiting, go to **Configure** > **Organization**.
  3. Confirm the office or department name doesn't exist in Greenhouse Recruiting.
  4. To audit the external ID for an office or department in Greenhouse Recruiting, click the **Edit** icon  next to the office or department name. If you need to audit all external IDs, leverage [Harvest API](https://developers.greenhouse.io/harvest.html) or reach out to Greenhouse Technical Support.

**If your organization is using offices for[structured job post locations](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360027858591):**

  1. Navigate to **Configure** > **Job Boards & Posts** > **Ellipsis** icon beside your job board > **Edit Board Settings**.
  2. Audit your job post location list.
  3. If your organization isn't using the organization office list, HRIS Link can't apply job post locations when creating a job.
  4. Either update the job post location in your HRIS to reflect your organization's offices, or remove the `job_post_location` header from the HRIS Link report.

**If the office or department name / external ID doesn't exist in Greenhouse Recruiting, and you have office import or department import:**

  1. Confirm the office exists in your HRIS with the appropriate external ID and name.
  2. Confirm the office should be on the Workday®️ report. Are any filters preventing that office from being on the report?
  3. Wait for HRIS Link department or office import to run again, then audit to see if the error persists after the office with the correct ID has been created and updated by HRIS Link.

  
  
#### Error message: Custom Field {CUSTOM_JOB_FIELD_NAME} has no option for value '<VALUE>'

Email subject | HRIS Link: Job import failed  
---|---  
Error information | Error message: Custom Field {CUSTOM_JOB_FIELD_NAME} has no option for value '<VALUE>'  
Issue | This error message means the custom field option value referenced in the report "<VALUE>" does not exist as a picklist option for the job custom field in Greenhouse Recruiting.  
Blocking error? |  Yes, this is a blocking error. Updates will not occur in Greenhouse Recruiting until the error is resolved.  
Solution |  Take the following steps to troubleshoot this issue:

  1. Audit the custom option values that are available in the HRIS and copy the exact <VALUE> that's missing from Greenhouse Recruiting.
  2. In Greenhouse Recruiting, go to **Configure** > **Custom Options** > Click **Job** to view the list of job custom fields > click to edit the custom field listed in the error message.
  3. Audit the available custom options and confirm the option does not exist.

**If you aren't using a custom options sync via Workday®️ RaaS and the select list can be edited in Greenhouse Recruiting:**

  1. Add the option value exactly as it appears in the HRIS.
  2. Wait 15 minutes for the HRIS Link job import to run again.
  3. If the error persists, [click here](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/requests/new) to open a ticket with Greenhouse Technical Support.

**If you are using a custom option sync via Workday®️ RaaS and the select list can't be edited in Greenhouse Recruiting:**

  1. Manually refresh the custom option sync by going to **Configure** > **Dev Center** > **Workday Administration** > **Sync a Greenhouse custom field with a Workday Report-as-a-service** > click the **edit** icon  next to the RaaS custom option sync you wish to refresh
  2. Click **Refresh report** at the top of the page.
  3. Go to **Configure** > **Custom Options** > **Job** to view the list of job custom fields > click to edit the custom field listed in the error message.
  4. Audit the available custom options and confirm the missing value was added.
  5. Wait 15 minutes for the job import report to run again.

If the error persists, [click here](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/requests/new) to open a ticket with Greenhouse Technical Support.  
  
#### No user exists with Email or Employee ID <value>

Email subject | HRIS Link: Job import failed  
---|---  
Error information | No user exists with Email or Employee ID <value>  
Issue |  The email address or employee ID referenced in the HRIS report is not associated with an existing, active Greenhouse Recruiting user account. The HRIS report value must match an active Greenhouse Recruiting user's employee ID or email address.  
Blocking error? |  Yes, this is a blocking error. Updates will not occur in Greenhouse Recruiting until the error is resolved.  
Solution |  Take the following steps to troubleshoot this issue:

  1. In Greenhouse Recruiting, go to **Configure** > **Users** > search for the user who was included in the HRIS report (for example, the Recruiter or Hiring Manager).
  2. If you cannot find the user, you must create them in Greenhouse Recruiting.
  3. If you are able to find the user, click on their profile and verify the Greenhouse Recruiting employee ID and email address match what was included in the HRIS report.

**If your organization does not have user import:**

  1. If the value included in the HRIS report does not match the Greenhouse Recruiting user's employee ID or email address, you must update the Greenhouse Recruiting user's profile accordingly.
  2. Wait 15 minutes for the report to run again.

If the error persists, [click here](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/requests/new) to open a ticket with Greenhouse Technical Support. **If your organization has user import:**

  1. Update the employee ID or email address for the employee in question in your HRIS so it flows to Greenhouse Recruiting on the next run of the report.
  2. Wait 15 minutes for user import to run again.

If the job import error persists after user import has updated the user profile in Greenhouse Recruiting, [click here](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/requests/new) to open a ticket with Greenhouse Technical Support.  
  
#### 403 Forbidden

Email subject | HRIS Link: Job import failed  
---|---  
Error information | 403 Forbidden  
Issue | A 403 error is returned when the client is not permitted access to a resource, despite providing authentication. This might be caused by an ISU's credentials expiring, or the on-behalf-of user's (named: HRIS Link) permissions not being insufficient.  
Blocking error? |  Yes, this is a blocking error. Updates will not occur in Greenhouse Recruiting until the error is resolved.  
Solution |  Take the following steps to troubleshoot this issue:

  1. In the HRIS, audit the ISU credentials used to access the job import report.
  2. Confirm the ISU credentials are active and have permissions for the Report.
  3. Audit the Greenhouse Recruiting user named _HRIS Link_ (**Configure** > **Users**) to ensure they are a Site Admin with ALL user-specific permissions.
  4. Wait 15 minutes for the HRIS Link job import to run again.

If the error persists, [click here](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/requests/new) to open a ticket with Greenhouse Technical Support.  
  
#### 401 Unauthorized

Email subject | HRIS Link: Job import failed  
---|---  
Error information | 401 Unauthorized  
Issue | The 401 Unauthorized error indicates that the request lacks valid authentication credentials for the target resource. For instance, this could be encountered because [the integration ISU](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360060056451) is not permissioned correctly.  
Blocking error? |  Yes, this is a blocking error. Updates will not occur in Greenhouse Recruiting until the error is resolved.  
Solution |  Take the following steps to troubleshoot this issue:

  1. In the HRIS, audit the ISU credentials used to access the job import report.
  2. Confirm the ISU credentials are active and have permissions for the Report.
  3. Update the [HRIS Link report ISU](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/11006737633307) in Greenhouse Recruiting.

If the error persists, [click here](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/requests/new) to open a ticket with Greenhouse Technical Support.  
  
#### Hiring Manager with ID <value> can not access job or Recruiter with ID <value> can not access job

Email subject | HRIS Link: Job import completed with errors  
---|---  
Error information |  Hiring Manager with ID <value> can not access job. or Recruiter with ID <value> can not access job.  
Issue | The hiring manager or recruiter cannot access the job in question because their Greenhouse Recruiting user profile is deactivated or cannot be found.  
Blocking error? |  No, this is not a blocking error.  
Solution |  **Take the following steps to troubleshoot this issue:**

  1. In Greenhouse Recruiting, navigate to **Configure** > **Users** > and click the user's profile that produced the error.
  2. Confirm the Greenhouse Recruiting user in question is active and not deactivated in Greenhouse Recruiting.
  3. If the user is deactivated, reactivate the user or assign a different hiring manager or recruiter.
  4. Wait 15 minutes for the next HRIS Link job import report to run.

  
  
#### X jobs found in Greenhouse with requisition_id: <value>

Email subject | HRIS Link: Job import completed with errors  
---|---  
Error information | X jobs found in Greenhouse with requisition_id: <value>  
Issue | This error message means there are two jobs in the Greenhouse Recruiting instance with a matching job requisition ID. As a result, job import cannot update the job because job import does not know which of the two existing jobs to update.  
Blocking error? |  No, this is not a blocking error.  
Solution |  Someone within your organization must remove one of the two duplicate jobs so only one job exists with the given requisition ID. Below are some steps you can take to resolve this error:

  1. In Greenhouse Recruiting, go to **All Jobs** > search for the requisition ID > click into each of the jobs in question.
  2. Audit each job to determine which job should be maintained.
  3. Go to the _Job Info_ page of the job that will not be kept.
  4. Click the **Edit** icon  next to _Status_ > close the job > click **Save** > click **Delete**.
  5. Wait 15 minutes for job import to run again.

**Note:** Deleting a job is a permanent action that cannot be undone. If the error persists, [click here](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/requests/new) to open a ticket with Greenhouse Technical Support.  
  
#### Access denied

Email subject | HRIS Link: Job import completed with errors  
---|---  
Error information | Access denied  
Issue |  The issue occurs when the Greenhouse Recruiting [integration system user (ISU)](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360060056451) for HRIS Link can't grant another a user access to the Greenhouse Recruiting job that it's attempting to update or create. This could be due to the ISU's permissions, a hiring team's user's [deactivated](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/115004791523) status, or the ISU attempting to grant permissions to itself.  
Blocking error? |  No, this is not a blocking error.  
Solution |  Take the following steps to troubleshoot this issue:

  1. Audit the following areas: 
     * The permissions of the _HRIS Link_ user in your organization's Greenhouse Recruiting account to ensure the user is an active Site Admin User with all user-specific permissions enabled.
     * The job (by requisition ID) in Greenhouse to ensure the job in Greenhouse is not "confidential."
     * The API key used for the HRIS Link integration to ensure the permissions haven't been audited.

If you are unable to resolve the issue, [click here](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/requests/new) to open a ticket with Greenhouse Technical Support.  
  
#### Missing required field: template_job_id or Template hiring plan does not exist

Email subject | HRIS Link: Job import completed with errors  
---|---  
Error information |  Missing required field: template_job_id or Template hiring plan does not exist.  
Issue |  This message typically means the required template_job_id field is missing or includes a Job ID that is not valid in Greenhouse Recruiting. This error prevents a job from being created in Greenhouse Recruiting. or This error goes hand in hand with the _Missing required field: template_job_id_ error. This error occurs when the template job ID is not valid. This error prevents a job from being created in Greenhouse Recruiting.  
Blocking error? |  No, this is not a blocking error.  
Solution |  Take the following steps to troubleshoot this issue:

  1. Audit the Calculated Field logic for the HRIS Report and confirm it is up to date and valid.
  2. Ensure all IDs defined in the template_job_id logic exist are valid job IDs in Greenhouse.
  3. If all the template_job_ids that exist in the HRIS are also in Greenhouse Recruiting, audit the HRIS report for the specific job for which this error was triggered, and confirm the Calculated field for template_job_id defined a job ID.
  4. If no job ID was defined, revisit the calculated field logic to determine why. Wait 15 minutes for job import to run again.

**Note:** You can export the [all jobs summary report](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/203940239), which includes the Greenhouse Recruiting job ID for each job. If you prefer to audit an individual template job ID manually, append the job ID to the following URL: `https://app.greenhouse.io/sdash/{job ID}` If the error persists, [click here](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360058320292) to open a ticket with Greenhouse Technical Support.  
  
#### Resource not found

Email subject | HRIS Link: Job import completed with errors  
---|---  
Error information | Resource not found  
Issue | This error may be caused by an issue with the On-Behalf-Of User's (named: HRIS Link) permissions, HRIS Link Harvest API key permissions, access to the HRIS Report URL, or the number_of_openings being set to be 0.  
Blocking error? |  No, this is not a blocking error.  
Solution |  Take the following steps to troubleshoot this issue:

  1. Audit the permissions of the _HRIS Link_ user in your Greenhouse Recruiting account to ensure the user is an active Site Admin with all user-specific permissions enabled.
  2. Audit the HRIS Link Harvest API key to ensure it has all required API permissions.
  3. Audit the Change Log (**Configure** > **Change Log**) to see if anyone has updated HRIS Link Harvest API key permissions or the HRIS Link user.
  4. Confirm the job import report still is enabled for Web Services in your HRIS.
  5. Confirm the ISU credentials defined for HRIS Link still have access to the job import report in your HRIS.
  6. Confirm the number_of_openings defined in the HRIS report is not 0.

If all of the above is valid, wait 15 minutes for the process to re-attempt to create or update the job. If the same error occurs on a subsequent attempt, [click here](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/requests/new) to open a ticket with Greenhouse Technical Support.  
  
#### Something went wrong and this job is likely partially created in Greenhouse

Email subject | HRIS Link: Job import completed with errors  
---|---  
Error information | Something went wrong and this job is likely partially created in Greenhouse  
Issue | If you're encountering this error, you should update your [HRIS Link Harvest API key](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360059988771) to ensure the Jobs > DELETE: Delete job permission is enabled. With this permission, HRIS Link will never partially create a job.  
  
With this error, the job was partially created in Greenhouse Recruiting, but it's likely that certain aspects of the job weren't created or updated properly due to another HRIS Link error.  
Blocking error? |  No, this is not a blocking error.  
Solution |  This error should be followed by a second error message that describes the issue that caused the partial job creation. For example:
    
    
    R123 Something went wrong and this job is likely partially created in Greenhouse; On-Behalf-Of user does not have permission to assign this role for this job.

Follow the troubleshooting steps provided in the second error message. To permanently resolve this behavior and re-establish HRIS Link's ability to delete jobs, [update your HRIS Link Harvest API key](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/115000521723) to include Jobs > DELETE: Delete job.  
  
#### Currency unit is required for currency custom fields

Email subject | HRIS Link: Job import completed with errors  
---|---  
Error information | Currency unit is required for currency custom fields  
Issue | This error occurs if a currency custom field is missing the currency unit in the HRIS Report. Check out [Set up HRIS Link job import with job requisitions enabled](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/4403889907355) for the expected format.  
Blocking error? |  No, this is not a blocking error.  
Solution |  Take the following steps to troubleshoot this issue:

  1. Audit the _Currency_ field data included in the HRIS report to ensure it meets Greenhouse's Report Spec requirements (Unit must come before the amount).
  2. Confirm the currency is defined before the amount (that is, <wd:Salary>USD 100,000</wd:Salary> for a currency field, or <wd:Salary_Range>$80,000 - 100,000</wd:Salary_Range2> for a currency range field).
  3. If the currency is not defined, or is defined improperly, update the currency field format in the HRIS report
  4. Wait 15 minutes to see if the error persists after the next job import run.

If the error persists, [click here](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/requests/new) to open a ticket with Greenhouse Technical Support.  
  
#### Must be one of [list of currencies]

Email subject | HRIS Link: Job import completed with errors  
---|---

# Edit candidate alert settings in bulk

**Permissions:** Site Admin who can bulk edit jobs

**Product tier:** Available for new subscription tiers (Core, Plus, and Pro)

Candidate alerts inform users about candidates who are in an interview stage for too long. With candidate alerts, your organization can ensure that all responsible roles are aware of how candidates are progressing through your interview pipeline, and that candidates are not falling through the cracks.

#### In this article

  * Edit candidate alert settings in bulk
  * Additional resources



### Edit candidate alert settings in bulk

To bulk edit candidate alert settings across multiple jobs, click**Jobs** on your navigation bar.

Select which jobs will be included in the bulk action by clicking the checkbox to the left of the job name.

When finished, click **Edit: Stages/Interviews**.

From the _Edit Stages/Interviews_ page, click **Alert Settings**.

Use the subsequent box to input how many days a candidate should stay in each stage before an alert is triggered for the responsible roles. The days you choose for alerts will applied to every job included in the bulk edit.

When finished, click **Save**.

Before exiting, be sure to click **Save Changes** in the upper right-hand corner of the page to confirm the changes made.

### Additional resources

  * [View candidate alerts](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/11279205874459)
  * [Edit candidate alert settings](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/200346659)

# Candidates to Schedule task

**Permissions:** Job Admin or above

**Product tier:** Available for new subscription tiers (Core, Plus, and Pro)

A coordinator's ability to quickly see and schedule all appropriate candidates in a job pipeline helps streamline scheduling across your organization. The _Candidates to Schedule_ task is a feature on Greenhouse Recruiting's _My Dashboard_ page that allows a coordinator to quickly access all of the candidates they currently need to schedule for interviews.

As long as you sync scheduled interviews between your external calendar and Greenhouse Recruiting, the Candidates to Schedule task will stay updated for [coordinators](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360016347752-Hiring-Team-Role-Coordinator) assigned to a job and candidate.

**Note** : The Candidates to Schedule task can't be manually marked as completed, and will not update if your interviews are not synced between your external calendar and Greenhouse Recruiting.

To find the task, navigate to the _My Tasks_ panel on the right side of the _My Dashboard_ page and click **Candidates to Schedule**.

The next page will display all candidates who need to be scheduled and where you are the assigned coordinator.

# Greenhouse Verified Overview

**Permissions:** Site admins

**Product tiers:** Respectful and communicative verifications are available to all product tiers. Fair and prepared verifications are only available to Expert tiers.

Greenhouse verifications are displayed on your company’s job posts and show candidates that you consistently follow best practices for fair, prepared, respectful and communicative hiring.

Your company can earn verifications by using Greenhouse features that support fair hiring practices, prepared interviewers, and respectful, communicative interactions with candidates. Learn how to [enable Greenhouse Verified features.](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/28630224743323-Enabling-Greenhouse-Verified-Features)

#### In this article

  * Overview
  * Downloading Greenhouse Verified reports
  * Earning and viewing verifications
  * Turning on Greenhouse Verified for candidates



#### Overview

Greenhouse verifications show candidates that they'll have a positive experience when applying to your company. Your company can earn verifications for being Fair, Prepared, Respectful and Communicative. When you earn a verification, it's displayed on your job post. 

You can earn verifications by using these Greenhouse features:

  * Inclusion reminders 
  * Interview-specific questions 
  * Job-specific attributes
  * Anonymization
  * Candidate surveys 
  * Email stage notifications
  * Percentage of active applicants



Downloading Greenhouse Verified reports

First, you'll want to understand which verifications your company has earned and which verifications you're working towards.

Go to **Configure **, then **Job Boards and Posts**. Select **Reports** , then **Email me my Greenhouse Verified report**.

After downloading your report, you'll see a detailed breakdown of the verifications your company has earned and the ones that you're progressing toward.

#### Earning and viewing verifications

You can monitor your progress towards Greenhouse verifications within specific jobs. First, go to **Jobs** in the navigation bar, then select a job. Next, select **Job setup** , then **Job posts**. 

From here, you can view any verifications your company has earned and understand any required next steps.

**Note:** Verifications refresh once daily. Any verifications you earn today will be visible tomorrow. 

#### Turning on Greenhouse Verified for candidates

To turn on Greenhouse Verified, go to **Configure ** >**Job boards and posts**. Then, scroll to **Greenhouse Verified** and select **Show Greenhouse Verified on job posts**.

****

Learn about how candidates use[Greenhouse Verified](https://www.greenhouse.com/greenhouse-verified).

# Edit the data retention timer on a candidate profile

**Permissions:** Site Admin

**Product tier:** Available for new subscription tiers (Core, Plus, and Pro)

The [data retention timer](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360002418112#h_18e35fe6-a320-4af3-9cfc-cf673fe96637) is a timer on a candidate's or prospect's profile that notifies users in your organization when it is time to delete their personal data. The data retention timer starts when a candidate or prospect is rejected from all job applications or prospect posts. You can change the timer's end date for individual candidates or prospects.

**Note** : It's not possible to edit the data retention timer for candidates or prospects in bulk.

To edit the data retention timer for a single candidate or prospect, navigate to the candidate or prospect profile and click **Edit** on the data retention timer at the top of the page.

In the provided field, enter a new end date for the data retention timer.

When finished, click **Save**.

**Note** : Altering the data retention timer for a candidate will log an Activity Feed entry to record the change.

# Best practices: Manage evergreen roles

**Permissions:** —

**Product tier:** Available for new subscription tiers (Core, Plus, and Pro)

If there are job requisitions that always remain open, it is important to follow these best practices so your organization can collect accurate data and report on the roles in a consistent manner.

For your convenience, we have included a downloadable PDF of this article which you can click [here](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/article_attachments/360095785911) to download.

#### Make sure the number of openings is kept up to date

When you first create the role, make sure to enter the current number of openings you are hiring for. If this number increases, update it! If you plan the headcount monthly, quarterly, or annually, make sure to come back and update the number of openings any time the new headcount is approved.

If it is a role that you always have carte blanche to hire for, leave the number of openings at 1, but keep the role open anytime you make a hire.

#### Use Opening IDs to track each unique opening within the job

While the title of the job stays the same, having an alphanumeric ID will make reporting and goal setting easier.

You can either generate the IDs with the **Generate Opening IDs** button if you want to keep the IDs a numeric sequence or type them yourself if you have a different structure.

#### Mark each relevant candidate as Hired and keep the job open if it's the last opening

Every time you make a hire you should be marking this candidate as _Hired_ in Greenhouse Recruiting. When you hire against the last opening for the evergreen role, you'll be given the option to keep the job open. Select **Yes** to automatically add a new opening to the job.

Doing this consistently is essential for accurate time to hire data, as time to hire is calculated from the open date of a job opening. Once you mark the candidate as _Hired,_ the close date will be captured for one opening and the new open date will be used to start tracking time to hire for the next opening.

#### If the role is ever On Hold, make sure to close the job in Greenhouse; you can reopen the job when you're hiring again

Close the job by modifying the status on the **Job Info** page, and be sure to choose **On Hold** as the _Close Reason_.

#### Check the details of openings and time On Hold by navigating to Req IDs and Openings under Job Info

When you click **Manage Openings** , you will be able to see and adjust all of the open dates for previous openings and when the job was put On Hold.

#### Leverage reports to track metrics for each opening

If you’ve followed all of these tips, you are now ready to report on your evergreen roles. There are a few reports that will be most helpful.

#### Job status report

View each opening for the role and all of the details of when it was opened and closed using the [job status report](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360003333251).

#### Offer details report

See all of the offers extended over time for your evergreen roles, with each of the offer details on the [offer details report](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/203940589).

#### Time to fill per job report

Report on the days from open date to hire for each opening on the [Time to fill per job report](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/204635705).

#### Time to hire by candidate report

Measure how quickly you were able move each candidate from application to offer with the [Time to hire by candidate report](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/203940469). This will be a much more reliable recruiting metric if you are continuously hiring.

### Frequently asked questions

#### How do evergreen roles affect time to hire?

Time to hire is calculated off of the open date for each opening. As long as you are creating a new opening every time you get approved for additional headcount or make a hire, the time to hire will count the total number of days from opening date to hire for each unique opening. This is why it is important to always mark candidates as **Hired** and to make sure to update headcount when you start the search for additional hires. You can always retroactively update the open date for an opening by going to **Job Setup > Job Info > Edit Details**.

#### Should I open a new job every time I make a hire for an evergreen role?

No, you should just be creating a new opening within the same requisition. This will allow you to keep your data a lot more organized and reportable in Greenhouse Recruiting.

#### What if we pause hiring on the role?

If you pause hiring, close the job and select the **On Hold** close reason. Then, as soon as you are ready to start hiring again change the status back to **Open**. This will allow you to keep track of when you put the job On Hold and the duration. It will also make sure that time to hire does not include time when the job was not actually open.

#### How do I track headcount if the number of approved openings changes every quarter?

When the new headcount is approved, go to the **Job Info** section of the job and update the number of openings. For tracking purposes, make the open date for the openings the first date of that quarter, or whenever the new headcount was allocated. Then, you will be able to track time to fill for each opening accurately and for each quarter accurately.

# Candidate quality by recruiter report

**Permissions:** Job Admin and above

**Product tier:** Available for new subscription tiers (Core, Plus, and Pro)

The candidate quality by recruiter report assigns each recruiter a quality percent, which is calculated by looking at the average distance candidates' applications travel through your organization's interview pipelines. This percentage can be used to understand which recruiters are most successful in moving applications through your pipeline and turning them into new hires.

The quality percent on this report is calculated by looking at the average distance an application travels through the pipeline. If every candidate was hired, the ad campaign would have produced 100% candidate quality. If every candidate was rejected in the first stage, the quality would be 0%.

**Example** – Imagine one of your recruiters is only responsible for one candidate, an iOS developer named Henry. Henry has a pretty strong background, so they make it through 5 of your 7 stages. Since they're the only person assigned to your recruiter, your quality percent for that row would be 5/7, or roughly 71%.

  * Custom job field
  * Date applied
  * Include migrated candidates

You can organize columns by stage or milestone.

Click **Apply** after applying any filters to your report.

# Email template types

**Permissions: Job Admin** and above

**Product tier:** Available for new subscription tiers (Core, Plus, and Pro)

Greenhouse Recruiting provides default email templates for your company which are used to communicate with both internal employees and your candidates. Your team can edit the existing templates as well as create custom templates.

Every email template must be assigned a specific template type, which determines where the template will populate within Greenhouse Recruiting. The benefit of assigning email template types is that users will not have to scroll through all of your organization's templates when sending an email. Instead, the user will be presented with a shorter list of only the relevant templates based on the specific communication they need to send.

**Example:** An email template with a template type of _Candidate Availability Request_ will be available to select only after clicking **Request Availability** on the candidate's profile, and will not be available to send after clicking **Email [Candidate Name]** on the right-hand panel of the candidate profile. Only email templates with a type of _Candidate Email_ will appear after clicking **Email [Candidate Name]**.

#### In this article

  * Available email template types
  * Create more than one version of a template
  * Edit template type on existing email template



### Available email template types

**Email Template** |  **Availability in Greenhouse Recruiting**  
---|---  
[ Agency email ](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360042698372) | When assigning Agency Recruiters to individual jobs.  
[ Calendly email ](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360029649991) | When selecting **Schedule with Calendly** on a candidate's profile and sending the candidate a Calendly link.  
Candidate availability request | When selecting **Request Availability** on a candidate's profile.  
Candidate email | When selecting **Email [Candidate Name]** on a candidate's profile.  
[ Candidate interview confirmation ](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360015975112) | When selecting **Send Interview Confirmation** on a candidate's profile.  
Candidate referral receipt | When a user submits a referral.  
Candidate rejection | When selecting **Reject** > **Reject and Send Email** on a candidate's profile.  
Candidate [self-schedule](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/4409534663579) request | When selecting **Send self-schedule** **request** on a candidate's profile.  
[ EEOC request ](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/210382923) | When sending EEOC questions to a candidate via **Application** > **Job Post Questions** > **Send EEOC Questions**.  
Extending offer | When sending an offer under the _Offer Details_ tab of a candidate's profile.  
Interviewer invite | When selecting **Schedule Interview** on a candidate's profile.  
[ Job post request ](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360002568971) | When sending job post questions to a candidate via **Application** > **Job Post Questions** > **Send Job Post** , or when configuring an [automated job post request email](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360052440032).  
Scorecard due | When selecting to re-send a scorecard reminder to an interviewer from a candidate's profile.  
[Sourcing automation step](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/4984925187611) |  When sending messages to prospects in [Sourcing Automation campaign pools](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/5045604930843). **Note** : Available only to users with CRM access and a Sourcing Automation seat.   
Team email | When selecting the **Email Team** option on a candidate's profile.  
Thank you for applying | When a candidate has submitted their application.  
[ Thank you for attending ](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360003211211-Create-an-Event#h_588bc2ce-eb7c-47a1-a576-06c7a9fb955c) | When a prospect provides contact information through the Events app.  
  
_**Note:** If one of your email templates does not populate as expected when you attempt to send an email, we recommend navigating to **Configure **> **Email Templates** , locating the specific template, and confirming which template type is assigned to that template. Reference the chart above to confirm the location in Greenhouse Recruiting from which you are attempting to send the email supports that particular template type. _

### Create more than one version of a template

Most email template types support creating more than one version of the template. This allows your team to further customize for your needs, such as creating unique _Candidate Interview Confirmation_ email templates for each of your office locations, in case special instructions are required for an onsite interview experience.

Some email template types, such as the _Candidate Referral Receipt_ template, allow your team to create only one version of the template that will be used in all appropriate instances.

### Edit template type on existing email template

To edit the template type of an existing email template, navigate to the Email Templates page and click the Edit icon next to the template. (**Configure** > **Email Templates** > **Edit** ) 

_**Note:** The template type can be edited on custom email templates only. Email templates whose names are shown in bold font are default templates provided by Greenhouse. The content (such as the subject line and email body) of a default template can be edited, but the template type cannot be changed, nor can a default template be deleted. _

On the _Edit Custom Email Template_ page, click the **Type** dropdown and select the updated template type.

Scroll to the bottom of the page and click **Save** when you're finished.

# Identify and attract the best talent for your organization 

Candidates size up job opportunities from the moment they land on your career page. How your company communicates your brand, culture and available opportunities impacts your organization’s reach and the quality of your candidate pool. Creating a seamless application process and following that up with a well-structured hiring flow helps ensure that quality candidates develop a good first impression of your company and can easily apply. 

The effectiveness spectrum of companies' hiring processes is what we call the [Greenhouse Hiring Maturity™](https://www.greenhouse.com/hiring-maturity) curve, which we break down into four stages: chaotic, inconsistent, systematic and, finally, strategic. 

As companies [climb the Greenhouse Hiring Maturity curve](https://www.greenhouse.io/blog/greenhouse-hiring-maturity-business-success), they start to focus on key behaviors and strategic conversations to improve how they identify and attract top talent.

### Select your stage of hiring:

  * Chaotic/inconsistent
  * Systematic
  * Strategic



### **Chaotic and inconsistent stages**

At these stages, it’s important to lay the groundwork for a stronger candidate pipeline. Take a comprehensive look at your entire sourcing effort. Identify what’s working and what needs improvement. Read the following strategic tips and action items to help get you started (we’ve included some helpful resources too). 

**Key actions for enabling change management :**

Assess your company's referral strategy and consider incentives

  * Referrals are the #1 source of new hire quality, with high retention rates, engagement and performance
  * Incentives and a [structured referral process](https://learn.greenhouse.io/submit-referrals) are powerful ways to boost engagement – check out [this eBook](https://www.greenhouse.io/guidance/how-to-build-a-strong-employee-referral-program-2) to learn more about building a strong employee referral program



Take action in Greenhouse with the following configuration:  
[Post your referral program in Greenhouse](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/205162775-Inform-Users-of-Company-Referral-Program)

Train employees how to submit referrals and post to social media

  * Make employee participation easy and rewarding to maximize engagement and results 
  * Use the Greenhouse basic [user training template](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/201981500-Greenhouse-101-for-basic-users-Presentation-template) to introduce everyone on your team to recruiting fundamentals for using the system
  * Check out this 15-minute [all-in-one course](https://learn.greenhouse.io/interviews-and-referrals) for everyone at your company



Follow this up with further action:  
[Encourage employees to post open roles to their social accounts](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/115002226806-Post-to-Social-Media-Account-from-Greenhouse-Recruiting)

Define your employer brand and promote it with a customized career page

  * Clearly outline your values, mission, culture and anything else that makes your company a great place to work 
  * Read our [employer brand eBook](https://www.greenhouse.io/guidance/ebook-employer-branding-best-practices) for guidance on how to draft and share your company’s story
  * Give candidates a great first impression with a career page that helps them understand your culture and workplace
  * Get inspired with these Greenhouse customer [career page examples](https://www.greenhouse.io/blog/get-inspired-by-these-15-awesome-career-pages) that vary in approach and content



**Develop your DE &I strategy and start evolving your hiring practices**

  * Align with leadership on your organization's vision and strategy around building a diverse, equitable and inclusive workplace 
  * Improve employee satisfaction and your ability to attract top talent by fostering a fair culture and a sense of belonging for all
  * Identify an internal sponsor to help map out your overall DE&I strategy and lead sessions for collaborating on how to implement initiatives, get company-wide buy-in and evaluate what’s working and what still needs to be done
  * [Read our guide](https://www.greenhouse.io/blog/committing-to-diversity-equity-inclusion-get-started-here) on how to get started with DE&I and [watch our webinar](https://www.goodhire.com/resources/webinar/diversity-and-inclusion-webinar/?utm_source=webinar&utm_medium=blog&utm_campaign=dei_greenhouse_2020_02) for in-depth DE&I strategy guidance



Take action in Greenhouse with the following configuration:  
[Publish your organization's commitment to DE&I in Greenhouse](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360004977511-Company-initiative-for-DE-I-)

**Additional actions to configure Greenhouse with your team:**

[Publish job posts to free job boards](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/sections/360009844991-Free-job-posts)

[Add potential candidates as prospects in Greenhouse to build a talent database](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360022793612-CRM-overview)

### **Systematic stage**

Your company has the right foundation to find and engage top talent, but there’s room to improve. Encourage your recruiting teams to reach out to past applicants and prospects to get a more objective view of your hiring process. Work on turning your company's vision for DE&I into reality by drafting concrete goals and systematizing behaviors that support those outcomes.

**Key actions for enabling change management :**

Develop a strategy for evergreen hiring

  * Work on your strategy to build up your pipeline, consistently nurture talent and be ready to make hires on a rolling basis for the roles you have a recurring need for, especially as you grow
  * Learn best practices to [leverage your existing talent base](https://www.greenhouse.io/blog/talent-pools-heres-what-you-need-to-know) and [maintain continuously open positions](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360000891392-Best-practices-Manage-evergreen-roles-)



Take action in Greenhouse with the following configuration:  
[Publish jobs available to internal employees to the internal job board](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/200521739-Configure-internal-job-board)   
[Add structure to your talent database by adding prospect pools](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/sections/360000692091-Pools-and-Stages)  
[Collect general interest applications by adding a prospect post to your careers page](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360028950972-Create-New-Prospect-Post)

Translate your organization's DE&I commitment into concrete goals for your recruiting team

  * Set out the steps to take for specific DE&I goals and align your team on new sourcing and interviewing practices
  * Identify and support an internal DE&I sponsor to engage management across departments for organizational change 
  * Read [this blog post](https://www.greenhouse.io/guidance/how-talent-makers-champion-dei) for guidance on embodying DE&I leadership at your company
  * Check out [examples](https://www.greenhouse.com/blog/de-i-tips-from-the-new-york-times-affirm-hired-and-greenhouse) of companies that are putting their DE&I visions into action



Take action in Greenhouse with the following configuration:  
[Mitigate bias at key points in the recruiting process by turning on Greenhouse inclusion nudges](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360004923452)

### **Strategic stage**

It’s clear that attracting talent is your competitive advantage. Your sourcing tactics and hiring approach draw in great candidates. Your whole company is invested in recruiting and helping identify great candidates. In the spirit of continuous improvement, we see the most strategic companies continuing to invest in key initiatives and actions to stay on top. 

**Key actions for enabling change management :**

**Build partnerships with employee resource groups (ERGs) to increase the diversity of your pipelines, improve all people-related strategies and gain a better understanding of the range of experiences at your company.**

  * Improve focus on your ERGs to help foster a robust pipeline with increased diversity
  * Support your people team to empower your ERGs
  * Check out [this resource](https://www.greenhouse.com/blog/actioning-de-i-how-classy-empowers-its-employees-and-the-world) to see how Greenhouse customers are establishing ERGs and empowering their employees



Accelerate hiring efforts by engaging Talent Magnets across the organization

  * Encourage “talent magnet” behavior by prompting individuals to actively promote your hiring brand’s story in their networks and help create a workplace that attracts top talent 
  * Learn more about talent magnets and the Talent Maker™ mindset in our [guide](https://www.greenhouse.com/guidance/ebook-talent-maker-primer)
  * Read our [e-book](https://www.greenhouse.io/guidance/ebook-50-ways-to-be-a-talent-maker) to discover how to best support your company’s own talent magnets



Create specialized sourcing plans and hiring strategies for each unique search

  * Ensure you’re scooping up passive talent and bringing in a diverse candidate pool by referring back to specific sourcing plans 
  * Read this customer [case study](https://www.greenhouse.io/customer-stories/case-study-hellofresh-3) to learn how you can optimize your sourcing strategy



Follow this up with further action:

Diversify your sourcing and hiring efforts through your career page, third-party job boards, prospecting and more, and use the [candidate quality by source report](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/203940929-Candidate-quality-by-source-report) for insights on where you should be focusing.

**Additional actions to configure Greenhouse with your team:**

Measure progress and identify areas for improvement on your DE&I goals with [custom demographic or standard demographic questions](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360004588971-Custom-Demographic-Questions-).

Learn Greenhouse course: [Collect candidate demographic information.](https://learn.greenhouse.io/collect-candidate-demographic-information) This resource will help you determine which option is best for your organization.

**Learn more with other Hiring Maturity advancement guides**

[Own every moment of your hiring process](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/4404475165467)

[Make confident, informed hiring decisions](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/4404480806811)

[Use data to drive operational excellence and improve over time](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/4404475145883)

# Greenhouse Notetaker - Security & Privacy FAQ

This FAQ provides technical and processing information about Greenhouse Notetaker to support your evaluation of the feature.

This is not intended to be legal advice. The answers provided are also not intended to override or contradict the advice of your legal counsel.

This feature is currently in beta and may not be available to your organization.

#### In this article

  * Overview 
  * Data processing and privacy 
  * Security and AI governance



### Overview

#### What is Greenhouse Notetaker?

Greenhouse Notetaker is an AI-powered feature in Greenhouse Recruiting that records and transcribes supported video interviews, then generates AI-assisted summaries and structured notes to help interviewers complete scorecards more efficiently.

Greenhouse Notetaker is designed as an assistive tool only. It does not automatically advance, reject, rank, or score candidates. All hiring decisions remain with your recruiting team.

#### What meeting platforms does Greenhouse Notetaker support?

Greenhouse Notetaker currently supports:

  * Zoom
  * Google Meet
  * Microsoft Teams



Phone interviews and in-person interviews are not yet supported.

#### How does Greenhouse Notetaker use AI?

Greenhouse Notetaker uses AI to generate interview summaries and structured notes from interview transcripts.

The AI-generated content is assistive only and does not make hiring recommendations or decisions.

### Data processing and privacy

#### Can candidates opt out of being recorded?

Yes.

Candidates can opt out of recording during the scheduling or self-scheduling process. If a candidate opts out, Greenhouse Notetaker will not be activated for the interview.

If a candidate withdraws consent during the interview, the interviewer can remove the recording bot directly from the interview kit or meeting platform controls.

Candidate opt-in and opt-out status is tracked per application.

#### What personal data does Greenhouse Notetaker process?

Greenhouse Notetaker may process:

  * Interview audio and video
  * Interview transcripts, with speaker attribution
  * AI-generated summaries and notes
  * Interviewer names
  * Candidate names and pronouns for transcript attribution and summary generation



Greenhouse Notetaker does not process resumes, application responses, or other structured application data.

#### Does Greenhouse store interview recordings, ID images, or biometric artifacts?

Greenhouse stores interview recordings, transcripts, and AI-generated notes associated with Greenhouse Notetaker.

However, Greenhouse does not generate or store biometric identifiers, facial recognition templates, or similar biometric artifacts.

Recordings and transcripts are retained according to your organization’s configured data retention settings.

### Security and AI governance

#### Is customer or candidate data used to train AI models?

Greenhouse does not use interview recordings, transcripts, or AI-generated notes to train machine learning models.

# Send an interview confirmation email

**Permissions:** Job Admin and above

**Product tier:** Available for new subscription tiers (Core, Plus, and Pro)

Candidates are not included in the calendar event created through the initial [scheduling process](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360045420091).

Once an interview is scheduled, you can confirm the date and time with the candidate by sending an interview confirmation email.

#### In this article

  * [Send an interview confirmation email](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360015975112#h_01EFFTN7QX9T5CMV80FGTV5JPD)
  * [Include calendar files](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360015975112#h_01F5Y7TT7PEHFZGMEW397BBBXC)



### Send an interview confirmation email

After an interview has been scheduled, you can send the interview confirmation by clicking the Send interview confirmation under the _Interviews_ section in the **Stages** panel.

From the _Availability_ dialog box, edit the email and fields if desired. By default, the email uses the [template](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/115002573326) **Candidate Interview Confirmation Message**.

**Note:** If the scheduled interview includes a [Zoom meeting link](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360042222612), be sure to paste the link into the body of the email.

### Include calendar files

Calendar files allow candidates to add a scheduled interview to their personal calendars via a downloadable (_.ics_) file. By default, Greenhouse Recruiting includes the calendar files in the interview confirmation email. You can uncheck the box to remove the .ics calendar file. 

**Note** : If all of the scheduled interviews are back-to-back with no gaps in-between, one calendar file is attached with the start time of the first interview and the end time of the last one. If there are gaps, multiple files will be added, although Greenhouse will attempt to consolidate them wherever possible.

Once the interview confirmation email is sent, the calendar files are added as an attachment to the email.

**Note:** Calendar files are not linked to the scheduled interviews in Greenhouse, so if you make a change to the date or time of an interview, you'll need to manually send the candidate an updated calendar file.

#### What does the candidate see?

The way the file is displayed for the candidate varies with each mail/calendar client.

Typically, the candidate will need to download and/or add the .ics file(s) to their calendars.

The body of your email will also be displayed in the calendar files, so anything the candidate needs to know should be readily available to them.

# Best practices: Get the most from Agencies

If you partner with outside recruiting agencies or contract agency recruiters, you know how important it is to have great communication and centralized data.

Agencies allows you to seamlessly integrate agencies into your overall recruiting process. Using the _Agencies_ homepage, your assigned agencies can submit candidates, view information about the current and next stage of candidates, and receive feedback about their submissions.

We've collected some best practices to help you and your agency partners get the most from Agencies.

#### In this article

  * Turn on notifications
  * Leverage reporting
  * Include agencies on relevant emails
  * Agency notes
  * Sharing feedback



### Turn on notifications

It's best to turn on notifications for new agency submission emails for each of your jobs. By doing this, whenever an agency submits a new candidate, you'll receive an automated notification. The notification will warn you if this candidate might be a duplicate of another candidate in your system.

To turn on notifications for new agency submissions, click **Configure** on your navigation bar and then select **Notifications** from the left panel.

Next, select **Set notifications by** **User**.

Click **Edit** next to the user names that should receive this notification.

Navigate to the new agency submission emails section and click **Turn all on**. You can also use the dropdown menu from the top to turn on notifications for a single job at a time.

Click **Done** when you're finished.

### Leverage reporting

With your agency submissions coming into Greenhouse Recruiting, leverage reporting to measure the quality of submitted candidates. This can help you narrow down which agencies are the most successful. The [candidate quality by source report](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/203940929) offers a great snapshot.

To run this report, click **Reports** from your navigation bar and then select **Essential** **reports**.

Scroll to  _Learn from Past Recruiting Efforts_ and select **Candidate Quality by Source**.

Your report will generate.

Learn more about the [Candidate quality by source report](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/203940929).

### Include agencies on relevant emails

When an agency recruiter submits a candidate, their email will be connected to the candidate. When you **Email the candidate** or **Email the team** , you can cc the agency or agency recruiter to keep them informed.

Emails sent through Greenhouse Recruiting are tracked on the candidate's activity feed.

### Agency notes

Agencies can [provide notes about the candidates they submit](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/202924839) or any candidates submitted by recruiters on their team. This fosters better communication on the agency side and ensures you have everything you need to know about a given candidate. Encourage your agency recruiters to consider leaving notes in Agencies with helpful context about their candidates.

### Sharing feedback

When you reject a candidate who was submitted by an agency, you can add _Rejection Notes to Agency_. These notes show up as feedback for the agency recruiter in Agencies. Rejected candidates won't be able to see your rejection notes.

# Add prospects to a campaign pool

**Permissions:** Job Admin and above with CRM access and a Sourcing Automation seat 

**Product tier:** Available for new subscription tiers (Core, Plus, and Pro) with the Sourcing Automation add-on

**Learn more about Sourcing Automation**

[Overview](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/5131929423643)

[FAQ](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/5224485120411)

[Reports](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/5204394650011)

Once a [campaign pool](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/5045604930843) is created, prospects can be added in the following ways: 

  * Using the [Greenhouse Recruiting Chrome extension](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/4947637389083)
  * Using the [LinkedIn RSC integration](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/204110135)
  * [Bulk importing](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/203871039) prospects from a spreadsheet
  * Adding a prospect through [Harvest API](https://developers.greenhouse.io/harvest.html#post-add-prospect)
  * Adding a new prospect to Greenhouse Recruiting
  * Updating an existing prospect's profile 
  * Starting a new prospect process in bulk
  * Moving prospects to another pool in bulk



**Note**

  * When adding a prospect through these methods, the user associated with the request must have a [sourcing automation seat](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/4952434968091) to select a campaign pool.
  * If a prospect is added to a campaign pool without an email address, a lookup is performed based on the priority configured in your account settings. Learn more about lookup credits [here](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/6018927588635). 



This article outlines how to use some of the various methods to add prospects to a campaign pool. 

#### In this article

  * Add a new prospect to Greenhouse Recruiting
  * Update an existing prospect's profile
  * Start a new prospect process in bulk
  * Move prospects to a campaign pool in bulk



### Add a new prospect to Greenhouse Recruiting

Click **Add** in the navigation bar, then select **Add a Candidate** from the dropdown menu. 

Select **Prospect** so the _Add a Prospect_ page appears.

Drag and drop a resume into the upload box or select **Choose File** to manually upload a resume from your files. Information from the resume will parse to its respective field. 

**Note** : Review our support article, [unsuccessful resume parse](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/200989175), if the resume doesn't import successfully. 

Click the dropdown menu under **Pool** and select a **Campaign Pool**. 

Once you select the campaign pool, any prefilled data you configured in the [campaign pool settings](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/5045604930843) tab auto-populates on the page. 

**Note** : A pool stage is not available to select as campaign pools don't have stages. Instead, campaign pools have email steps that determine the number of emails sent to a prospect if they don't respond.

Continue filling out the rest of the page with the prospect's information. Once finished, click **Add this prospect** at the bottom of the page. 

Now that your prospect is added to the campaign pool, learn more functionality through the following resources:

  * [Manage prospects in a campaign pool](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/5285464148379)
  * [Launch a campaign pool](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/5045604930843)



### Update an existing prospect's profile

You can locate a prospect's profile in two ways:

  * Finding the prospect on the _All Candidates_ page using the filters.
  * Opening a prospect pool the prospect through CRM (**CRM > Ellipses **icon next to the prospect pool >**view in candidate search**)



Click on a **Prospect's Name** to access their profile. 

Once on the prospect's profile, click the **P****encil icon** inline with the _Pool_ name. 

The pencil icon allows you to either move their prospect application from a prospect pool to a campaign pool or start the prospecting process by adding them to a campaign pool for the first time. 

**Note** : Since campaign pools provide automated email sequencing and activity tracking, adding a [Touchpoint](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360020298312) is not required at this step. Also, a _pool stage_ is not available to select as [campaign pools](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/5045604930843) do not have stages. Instead, campaign pools have email steps that determine the number of emails sent to a prospect if they do not respond. 

Now that your prospect is added to a pool, learn more functionality in the following resources:

  * [Manage prospects in a campaign pool](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/5285464148379)
  * [Launch a campaign pool](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/5045604930843)



### Start a new prospect process in bulk

You can run a bulk prospect process by clicking **Bulk Actions** at the top of the _All Candidates_ page.

**Note:** Use the filters to narrow down the list of candidates to only prospects in the pool. You can select these filters automatically by opening the prospect pool from the CRM page (**CRM** > ellipses icon >**view in candidate search**)

Add a **checkmark** next to all prospects that are starting the prospecting process or click **Select All**. 

Click **Edit Selected**. 

Select **Start New Prospect Process** within the _Candidates_ section.

Select a **Campaign****Pool** from the dropdown and fill in the remaining fields.

**Note** : A Pool Stage is not available to select as campaign pools do not have stages. Instead, campaign pools have Email Steps that determine the number of emails sent to a prospect if they do not respond. 

Once finished, click **Start New Prospect Process** at the bottom of the dialog box. 

Now that your prospect is added to a pool, learn more functionality in the following resources:

  * [Manage prospects in a campaign pool](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/5285464148379)
  * [Launch a campaign pool](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/5045604930843)



### Move prospects to a campaign pool in bulk

Once you've narrowed down a list of prospects on the All Candidates page, you can do a bulk action to move the prospects to another pool or stage.

When you're running this bulk action, you'll need to select a new campaign pool. Once the new pool is selected, click **Save**. 

**Note** : A [pool stage](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360024904051) is not available to select as campaign pools do not have stages. Instead, [campaign pools](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/5045604930843) have Email Steps that determine the number of emails sent to a prospect if they do not respond.
