# Permissions cheat sheet

This list includes common actions taken in Greenhouse Recruiting along with the product tier and permissions you'll need to perform them.

#### In this article

  * Grant developer permissions to your IT team
  * Allow your IT team to add new users
  * Give a user access to your CRM
  * Assign permissions to a user for all future jobs
  * Assign permissions to users in bulk
  * Add a user as an approver on a job
  * Add a user as an interviewer on a job
  * View private candidate profiles
  * Edit your scorecard after it's been submitted
  * View all the submitted scorecards for a candidate's application
  * View a candidate's offers
  * Mark a candidate as hired
  * View the profile of a hired candidate
  * View reports
  * Deactivate a user



### Grant developer permissions to your IT team

  * **Product tier:** Available for new subscription tiers (Core, Plus, and Pro)
  * **Assigner permissions:** Site Admin with the [user-specific permission](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360021113491) **Edit another user's advanced permissions**
  * **Assignee permissions:** Select one or more permissions in the _[Developer permissions](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/201122629) _section of the user profile.



### Allow your IT team to add new users

  * **Product tier:** Available for new subscription tiers (Core, Plus, and Pro)
  * **Assigner permissions:** Site Admin with the [user-specific permission](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360021113491) **Edit another user's advanced permissions**
  * **Assignee permissions:** Site Admin or Job Admin with the user-specific permission**[Invite new users](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360027077811) to Greenhouse and reactivate deactivated users**.



### Give a user access to your CRM

  * **Product tier:** Available for new subscription tiers (Core, Plus, and Pro)
  * **Assigner permissions:** Site Admin with the [user-specific permission](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360021113491) **Edit another user's advanced permissions**



**Note:** Some specific [CRM features](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360022793612) may only be available to higher subscription tiers.

  * **Assignee permissions:** Permissions depend on what you want the user to be able to do in the CRM. Learn more about CRM permissions [here](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/4411120566299).



### Assign permissions to a user for all future jobs

  * **Product tier:** Available for new subscription tiers (Core, Plus, and Pro)
  * **Assigner permissions:** Site Admin
  * **Assignee permissions:** Job Admin level with [job-based permissions](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360040181991) assigned for [All Future Jobs](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/200242029)



**Tip:** You can also [exclude a user](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360040753871) from having permissions on future jobs.

### Assign permissions to users in bulk

  * **Product tier:** Available for Plus and Pro subscription tiers
  * **Assigner permissions:** Site Admin, or Job Admin with the [Job Admin permission](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360039518131) **Can add and remove users to their assigned jobs**
  * **Assignee permissions:** Select one or more permissions using the [bulk actions](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/207334246) feature.



### Add a user as an approver on a job

  * **Product tier:** Available for Plus and Pro subscription tiers
  * **Assigner permissions:** Site Admin with the [user-specific permission](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360021113491) **Create and override default approval flows**
  * **Assignee permissions:** Job Admin with the [Job Admin permission](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360039518131) **Can view and edit private job fields and approve/request approval on jobs**



### Add a user as an interviewer on a job

  * **Product tier:** Available for new subscription tiers (Core, Plus, and Pro)
  * **Assigner permissions:** Site Admin or Job Admin
  * **Assignee permissions:** Any permission level, added to the _Interviewers_ dropdown in the [interview scheduling](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360050744912) window



### View private candidate profiles

  * **Product tier:** Available for new subscription tiers (Core, Plus, and Pro)
  * **Assigner permissions:** Site Admin with the [user-specific permission](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360021113491) **Edit another user's advanced permissions**
  * **Assignee permissions:** Site Admin with the [user-specific permission](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360021113491) **Create and view private candidates** , or Job Admin with the [user-specific permission](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/205614645) to **view and edit candidates and prospects** and **Create and view private candidates** who is also assigned to one of the private candidate's jobs



### Edit your scorecard after it's been submitted

  * **Product tier:** Available for new subscription tiers (Core, Plus, and Pro)
  * **Assigner permissions:** Site Admin or Job Admin
  * **Assignee permissions:** Job Admin on the job the scorecard is associated with 



### View all the submitted scorecards for a candidate's application

  * **Product tier:** Available for new subscription tiers (Core, Plus, and Pro)
  * **Assigner permissions:** Site Admin with the [user-specific permission](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360021113491) **Edit another user's advanced permissions**
  * **Assignee permissions:** Job Admin assigned to a [Job Admin level](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360039518131) with the permission to **view and edit candidates and prospects** and **Can view candidate scorecards submitted by other users** set to **Always** or**After Submit**



[Learn more](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/16187220652059) about scorecard visibility settings.

### View a candidate's offers

  * **Product tier:** Available for new subscription tiers (Core, Plus, and Pro)
  * **Assigner permissions:** Site Admin or Job Admin
  * **Assignee permissions:** Site Admin with the [user-specific permission](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360021113491) **See private notes, salary info, manage offers, request approval, and approve jobs/offers** , or Job Admin with the [Job Admin permission](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360039518131) **View and edit offers and approve/request approval on offers**



**Tip:** Offers can also be viewed as [file attachments in emails](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/200670265).

### Mark a candidate as hired

  * **Product tier:** Available for new subscription tiers (Core, Plus, and Pro)
  * **Assigner permissions:** Site Admin or Job Admin
  * **Assignee permissions:** Site Admin or Job Admin assigned on the job you want to hire the candidate for



**Note:** Organizations using offer approvals will require a different product tier and permissions. [Learn more](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/200242039).

### View the profile of a hired candidate

  * **Product tier:** Available for new subscription tiers (Core, Plus, and Pro)
  * **Assigner permissions:** Site Admin, or Job Admin with the [Job Admin permission](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360039518131) **Can advance candidates/prospects**
  * **Assignee permissions:** Job Admin with permission to view and edit candidates assigned to at least one job on the candidate's profile



### View reports

  * **Product tier:** [Essential reports](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360034704071) are available for all subscription tiers. [Custom reports](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360050317592) are available for Plus and Pro subscription tiers.
  * **Assigner and assignee permissions:** Different reports require different permissions. To view an Essential report, the appropriate user must grant the [correct permissions](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360034704071) for that report. To view a Custom report, a Site Admin or Job admin must [share the report](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360050317592) from the report page.



### Deactivate a user

  * **Product tier:** Available for new subscription tiers (Core, Plus, and Pro)
  * **Assigner permissions:** Site Admin
  * **Assignee permissions:** Site Admin



[Learn more](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/115004791523) about deactivating users.

# API-only custom application question

**Permissions:** Job Admins, who can create, edit, and delete job posts, and Site Admins

**Product tier:** Available for new subscription tiers (Core, Plus, and Pro)

Custom application questions allow your organization to collect information from candidates when they are applying to a job. Candidate responses to custom application questions can subsequently be viewed and configured for reporting purposes.

Every custom application question can be configured to meet varying privacy concerns your organization may have. Custom application questions can be configured with one of the following privacy settings:

  * Standard
  * [Private](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360025086132)
  * API only



#### In this article

API only custom application question overview

Add API only custom option application question

### API only custom application question overview

API only is generally considered the most restrictive privacy setting your organization can assign to a custom application question. When a question is marked as API only, candidate responses to the question will not surface in the Greenhouse Recruiting application and can only be viewed via the Greenhouse API.

Greenhouse Recruiting assumes there are fewer users who have access to your organization's API than who have permission to view private candidate data within the application. This more restrictive privacy setting can be useful for certain candidate information you don't want surfaced in Greenhouse Recruiting.

**Use case** : The API only setting for custom application questions can be useful if your organization plans to ask its own EEOC or demographic questions instead of using Greenhouse Recruiting's built-in EEOC questions. Answers to these questions are very sensitive, and you can use the API only setting to restrict response visibility within the app and in a candidate export.

_**Note** : Responses to API only custom application questions still populate in the Greenhouse Business Intelligence Connector._

### Add API only custom application question 

To add an API only custom application question to an existing job post, click**Jobs** from the navigation bar and select a job from the subsequent list > Click**Job Setup** > Navigate to **Job Posts** > Navigate to a job post and click the **Edit** icon  next to the job post title.

Navigate to _Custom Application Questions_ and click **Add Custom Question**. From the subsequent dialog box, enter the necessary information for the custom application question. Select **API only** in the _Privacy_ section.

Click **Add** when finished.

_**Note** : Once a custom application question's privacy setting is marked and saved as API only, it cannot be changed._

Click **Save** at the bottom of the page to confirm the change.

# Anonymize take home tests

**Permissions:** Site Admin

**Product tier:** Available for Pro subscription tier

To promote inclusive and diverse hiring, you can hide candidate's identifying information during assessments like [Take Home Tests ](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/200887825)to reduce the potential influence of bias during the grading process. When tests are anonymized, the results will still be tied to the candidate's profile, but the grader will complete the assessment without knowing the identifying candidate information.

#### In this article

  * Enable anonymous take home tests for your organization
  * Turn on anonymous tests for a job
  * Assess an anonymous take home test



### Enable anonymous take home tests for your organization

Click on the **Configure** icon in the upper right-hand corner and select **Inclusion Tools** from the left-hand panel.

Turn on **Anonymous take home test grading** in the  _Interviewing_ section.

### Turn on anonymous tests for a job

Once the organization setting is enabled, Job Admins can choose to **Hide candidate name and details from grader** when setting up a take home test.

To update this setting for a job, navigate to the **Job Setup** tab and choose **Interview Plan** on the left side of the page.

Edit or create a _Take Home Test_ stage.

Scroll to the bottom of the page and select **Hide candidate name and details from grader** in the  _Additional Settings_ section.

**Note:** This option is only available on Take Home Test stages. 

### Assess an anonymous take home test

When a test is ready, the graders will receive a trimmed-down email that does not include the candidate's information.

The interview kit will also leave out the candidate's name and the link to their profile to discourage interviewers from doing too much research before assessing the test.

# Custom options sync errors

**Permissions:** Job Admin and above with the user-specific permission 'can configure Workday® integrations'

**Product tier:** Available for Plus and Pro subscription tiers

A custom options sync is an HRIS integration that allows you to import and update custom field settings so you can reduce the chance for human error during data input.

Custom options sync errors are delivered via email to Job Admin and above who can configure Workday® integrations. Use this guide to determine what an error means and how to resolve it.

#### In this article

  * Common errors
  * FAQ



### Common errors

Most custom options sync errors are the result of permission or password issues. Double-check if the following is affecting your sync:

  * Incorrect username or password combination in Workday®
  * Incorrect report permissions, meaning the Workday® ISU no longer has access to report data
  * Outdated URL endpoints



If you're receiving a specific error via email, check out the following table for more information:

**Error** | **What to know**  
---|---  
      
    
    OpenURI::HTTPError (500 Internal Server Error)

| Workday® is having a problem with their server. Give them a moment and try again, or [check their status page](https://community.workday.com/trust/status) for more information.  
      
    
    StandardError (Invalid XML; IDs and Names must be equal)

| Each XML entry on your report has two required elements: a human readable name and a reference ID. These must be equal.  
      
    
    OpenURI::HTTPError (503 Service Unavailable)

| Workday® is having a problem with their server. Give them a moment and try again, or [check their status page](https://community.workday.com/trust/status) for more information.  
      
    
    Net::ReadTimeout (Net::ReadTimeout with #)

| A timeout is affecting our ability to read the XML. [Reach out to Greenhouse Technical Support](https://support.greenhouse.io/direct) if the issue persists.  
      
    
    Error: Net::OpenTimeout Failed to open TCP connection

| A timeout is affecting our ability to read the XML. [Reach out to Greenhouse Technical Support](https://support.greenhouse.io/direct) if the issue persists.  
      
    
    Errno::ECONNRESET (Connection reset by peer)

|  [Allowlist Greenhouse Recruiting IP addresses](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360002110971) to ensure custom options sync runs as expected.  
      
    
    Savon::SOAPFault ((SOAP-ENV:Client.validationError) Invalid request)

| Either the Workday® ISU that manages this report no longer has the correct permission or the Workday web services version isn't supported. Custom options sync only supports Workday® web services version 23.0 and 24.2.  
      
    
    Savon::SOAPFault ((SOAP-ENV:Server.processingError) Processing error occurred. The task submitted is not authorized.)

| The Workday® ISU doesn't have the correct permission to access this report. Resolve the permissions issue in Workday.  
      
    
    Nokogiri::XML::XPath::SyntaxError (ERROR: Invalid expression: /wd:Report_Data/wd:Report_Entry/wd:Employee ID-Employee Name- Employee Status)

| First name and last name can't be blank. Employment status must be `1` for active or `0` for inactive.

### FAQ

Greenhouse categorizes Workday sync errors into two types to ensure you're alerted without being overwhelmed. 

### Why did I only receive one custom options sync error email?

Greenhouse sends a one-time email notification when the sync fails because of a configuration error, such as expired credentials or an invalid URL. After the first email, Greenhouse marks the integration as failing and pauses the sync to prevent repeated notifications.

To resume the sync, update your integration settings or click **Refresh** in Greenhouse to reset the failing status.

### Why am I receiving multiple custom options sync error emails?

Greenhouse sends multiple email notifications when the sync fails because of a transient error, such as a network timeout or data formatting issue. In these cases, the sync isn't paused.

Greenhouse continues retrying the sync on its regular schedule and sends an email for each failed attempt until the issue is resolved.

**Note** : Greenhouse Recruiting is not sponsored by, affiliated with, or endorsed by Workday®.

# HiPeople integration (legacy)

Unlock your team’s best hiring capabilities and improve your quality of hire with HiPeople, an assessment and reference check tool that keeps your hiring data-driven, on point, and on time. 

With a focus on assessments, reference checks, candidate experience, and onboarding, HiPeople makes it fast and delightful for teams to make better hiring decisions.

Greenhouse Recruiting’s integration with HiPeople allows you to easily invite candidates to HiPeople assessments and checks directly from Greenhouse Recruiting, and receive results back directly in the candidate profile.

#### In this article

  * Set up the HiPeople integration
    * Create a Harvest API key
    * Add your API key to HiPeople
    * Create webhooks and complete setup
  * Use the HiPeople integration
    * Connect a HiPeople role to Greenhouse Recruiting
    * Start a reference check
    * Review reference check results
  * Additional resources



### Set up the HiPeople integration

#### Create a Harvest API key

To configure the HiPeople integration, you’ll need to create a Harvest API key. 

Follow the steps in [this article](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/5888163769883) to create the key, and verify that the permissions below are selected when configuring the HiPeople integration.

#### Credentials

In the _Create New Credential_ box, make the following selections:

  * **API Type:** Harvest
  * **Partner:** HiPeople (optional)
  * **Description:** HiPeople Harvest API key



#### Permissions

Verify that the following permissions are selected for the HiPeople integration:

**Candidates**

  * Select all



**Activity Feed**

  * Select all



**Jobs**

  * Select all



**Job Stages**

  * Select all



**Rejection Reasons**

  * Select all



When you’re finished, click **Save**.

Your Harvest API key for the HiPeople integration is created and configured. Copy the API key to provide to HiPeople in the next step. 

#### Add your API key to HiPeople

To add your created API key credentials, navigate to HiPeople and **Log In**. Select **My** **Organization** to access your settings and click **Greenhouse**. 

In the _Set Greenhouse API key_ pop-up window, paste the created API key and then, click **Set**.

In the box that appears next, copy the contents within the _Endpoint URL_ and _Secret key_ fields. You will need this information to create a webhook in the next step. 

#### Create webhooks and complete setup

To integrate HiPeople with Greenhouse Recruiting, you'll also need to create three webhooks. Follow the steps in [this article](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/5888163727003) to create your webhook. Use the values listed below to configure the webhook:

**Web hook #1**

  * **Name:** HiPeople [Candidate Stage Change]
  * **When:** Candidate has changed stage
  * **Endpoint URL** : Enter the endpoint URL from the HiPeople dashboard
  * **Secret key** : Enter the secret key from the HiPeople dashboard



**Web hook #2**

  * **Name:** HiPeople [Candidate Hired]
  * **When:** Candidate has been marked as hired
  * **Endpoint URL** : Enter the endpoint URL from the HiPeople dashboard
  * **Secret key** : Enter the secret key from the HiPeople dashboard



**Web hook #3**

  * **Name:** HiPeople [Candidate Rejected]
  * **When:** Candidate has been rejected
  * **Endpoint URL** : Enter the endpoint URL from the HiPeople dashboard
  * **Secret key** : Enter the secret key from the HiPeople dashboard



Click **Create Web hook** when finished.

### Use the HiPeople integration

#### Connect a HiPeople role to Greenhouse Recruiting

After enabling the HiPeople integration, you will be ready to use the integration. 

To begin, you'll need to connect the a role in HiPeople to the corresponding job posting in Greenhouse Recruiting.

In HiPeople, find the role you wish to integrate and then, go to the **[ . . . ]** menu > **Manage ATS automation**.

Select the role from Greenhouse Recruiting that you would like to integrate with this HiPeople role.

**Example** : In the example below, we're integrating Customer Success Manager in Greenhouse Recruiting with Customer Success Manager in HiPeople:

On the next page, you must connect the HiPeople stages to the Greenhouse Recruiting stages as defined in your job setup.

For example, you might like to connect the HiPeople Assessment to Inbox, and the HiPeople reference checks to Reference Check as shown below:

**Example** : In HiBob

**Example** : In Greenhouse Recruiting

Review your selected ATS pipeline stage & role selections and then, hit **Confirm**.

You are now ready to start using HiPeople for all the candidates within the Greenhouse role(s) linked above. Move the candidate in Greenhouse to the respective stage, and HiPeople automatically takes care of the rest.

#### Start a reference check

To start the reference check for the candidate, navigate to the candidate profile in Greenhouse Recruiting, and move the candidate to the _Reference Check_ stage.

That's it! The request for the candidate to submit their references is on its way!

You can see the progress of the reference check for this candidate by going to the respective role in HiPeople – the candidate profile is synced and a reference check invite has been sent automatically.

#### Review the results of the reference check

As soon as one of the candidate's referees has provided their feedback, you will receive an email with an invitation from HiPeople to review the reference check results.

In addition, you can access the reference check results through an automated PDF report on a link in the candidate's Activity Feed tab that will appear as soon as the reference check is completed.

### Additional resources

For additional help or troubleshooting not covered here, reach out to HiPeople support team at [support@hipeople.io](mailto:support@hipeople.io).

# Sandbox FAQ

**Permissions:** Basic and above

**Product tier:** Available to Pro subscription tier

A [sandbox](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/16904526959899) is a test environment that allows you to evaluate configurations, workflows, integrations, and more — all without disturbing real data or your recruiting teams. Your sandbox works just like a production environment, with the same features and capabilities, enabling you to test real-world scenarios.

We've collected answers to a few commonly asked questions about sandbox.

#### In this article

  * Who can access a sandbox?
  * What are some common uses for a sandbox?
  * How do I create a new sandbox?
  * Is access to sandbox logged in the production change log?
  * How do I mirror data from my production environment?
  * Can single sign-on (SSO) be enabled in my sandbox?



#### Who can access a sandbox?

Anyone who is added as a user to your sandbox can access the sandbox. However, logins are not interchangeable between your sandbox and your production environments. When accessing a sandbox, ensure you're using sandbox-specific login credentials. [Learn more](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/17057985865371).

#### What are some common uses for a sandbox?

You can use your sandbox as a safe place to play with data, test configurations, and evaluate real-world scenarios. Here are some common uses for sandboxes:

  * [**Train new users**](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/17053185557787#h_01H53G50W9ZRMV7PXECJG8DCNE) to craft the best possible recruiting team.
  * [**Test communications**](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/17053185557787#h_01H53G56GWDPGFWQ0HQ33VKN4E) like offer letters and candidate emails.
  * [**Try new integrations**](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/17053185557787#h_01H53G5BF7NS4EEVF7DXRXYVVQ) to deepen your tech stack.
  * [**Build configurations**](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/17053185557787#h_01H53G5FRJ33M35NPA59CWV09S) that expand and scale your organization.
  * [**Test APIs**](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/17053185557787#h_01H53G5PE2YR1W29DV2D5T8935) so your developers are prepared for success.



#### How do I create a new sandbox?

Organizations that are Pro subscription tier are able to use a sandbox. Your Greenhouse account team can help you enable a new sandbox.

#### Is access to sandbox logged in the production change log?

No, access to your sandbox isn't recorded in the production change log.

#### How do I mirror my production environment?

[Sandbox sync](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/14111892585627) replicates the look and feel of your Greenhouse Recruiting production environment, making it easy to test changes without impacting live data or workflows. It’s ideal for testing offer and email templates, integrations, permission policies, and more. Contact your Account Manager to learn more.

#### Can single sign-on (SSO) be enabled in my sandbox?

Yes, you can enable SSO on a sandbox. We recommend using a sandbox instance of your SSO to add the sandbox Greenhouse Recruiting environment.

**Learn more**

[Sandbox overview](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/16904526959899)

[Use a sandbox](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/17053185557787)

[Troubleshoot a sandbox](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/17057985865371)

# Tracking links overview

**Permissions:** —

**Product tier:** Available for new subscription tiers (Core, Plus, and Pro)

A tracking link is a unique URL that candidates can use to apply for jobs. When a candidate applies through a specific tracking link, Greenhouse Recruiting allows you to track the source of the applicant to measure the success of external job boards, ads, or marketing campaigns.

#### In this article

  * How do tracking links work?
  * Manage your custom sources
  * Create a new tracking link
  * Additional resources



### How do tracking links work?

A tracking link is made up of two parts:

1\. The **job post URL** links to the application page for your job post or to your overall job board. 

2\. A**source token** is a combination of numbers and letters at the end of your URL that uniquely identifies the source of the tracking link.

When you create a new tracking link, Greenhouse Recruiting will automatically add a unique source token to the end of your job post URL.

**Example:** If you create a tracking link for your job board URL <https://example.com/jobs>, Greenhouse Recruiting will add the Source Token on the end of the URL to create a link that looks like this: <https://example.com/jobs?gh_src=abc123>.

### Manage your custom sources

Before you can create a tracking link, the unique source must be created in Greenhouse Recruiting. You can manage your sources by selecting the **Configure** icon, then click **Custom** **Options** on the left side. Select **Sources**.

Here you can view and manage default Greenhouse Recruiting sources and create new custom sources. [Click here](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/200721664) for more information about managing custom sources.

### Create a new tracking link

You can create tracking links for an entire job board or a single job post. For more information, check out the following articles:

  * [Create a tracking link for a job board](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/201823760)
  * [Create a tracking link for a single job post](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/4405093302427)

# Checklist for launching Greenhouse Onboarding

**Permissions:** Owners

**Product tier:** Available for Greenhouse Welcome and Greenhouse Onboarding subscription tiers

If your organization is launching Greenhouse Onboarding for the first time, you'll want to double-check that you've set up everything your team needs to get started. You should preview your onboarding activities and emails to ensure that new hires and members of their onboarding team have a smooth experience.

Use the below checklists to review different elements of your Greenhouse Onboarding setup before launch. Since the user experience in Greenhouse Onboarding varies by role, we've created checklists for each role. This will allow you to preview and update any aspect of each user's onboarding process before you launch.

# Ferretly integration

Ferretly offers social media background checks for candidates that leverage artificial intelligence and human analysis to surface specific behaviors from publicly available social media posts and web/news posts. The Ferretly report provides key insight into candidate character, ensuring they align with your corporate values.

Ferretly’s integration with Greenhouse Recruiting allows you to seamlessly add Social media background checks to a job's interview plan.

#### In this article

    * [Permissions](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/undefined#h_01HRA1RQDCJSK2GR7QX6AREK84)
  * [Use the Ferretly integration with Greenhouse Recruiting](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/undefined#h_01HRA1RQDCANT73F7TSG0MM0C3)

# Aspect integration

Aspect is an interview intelligence platform that automatically records interviews and generates human-level AI notes and summaries. Aspect frees your recruiters and hiring managers from the constraints of note-taking, enabling them to fully engage with your candidates.

Aspect's integration with Greenhouse Recruiting sends AI note tokers to Greenhouse scheduled interviews, then posts interview summaries on the candidate activity feed.

#### In this article

  * Set up the integration
    * Create a Harvest API key
    * Enable on Aspect
    * Create webhooks
  * Use the integration with Greenhouse Recruiting
  * Additional resources



### Set up the integration

#### Create a Harvest API key

First, create a Harvest API key in Greenhouse Recruiting. Follow the steps in [this article](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/5888163769883) to create the key, and verify that the permissions below are selected.

In the _Create New Credential_ box, make the following selections:

  * **API** **type** : Harvest
  * **Partner** : Aspect or Unlisted Vendor
  * **Description** : Aspect Harvest API Key



Verify that all the permissions for the following sections are selected for the API key: 

  * Job openings
  * Departments
  * Users
  * Scorecards
  * Applications
  * Approvals
  * Jobs
  * Candidates
  * Job posts
  * Scheduled interviews
  * Email templates
  * Job stages
  * Close reasons
  * Offices
  * Custom fields
  * Education
  * Activity feed
  * Custom locations
  * Offers
  * Tags
  * Custom field options
  * Rejection reasons
  * Prospect pool
  * User roles
  * EEOC
  * Tracking links
  * Sources



When finished, copy the Harvest API key to a secure location for use in the next step.

#### Enable on Aspect

Next, log in to Aspect and click **Settings**.

**Note** : In order to post interview summaries to the candidate activity feed, log in to Aspect with the same email address used with your Greenhouse Recruiting account.

Click **Integrations**.

Enter the API key generated in the previous step, and for the webhook secret, enter any value.

Click **Update**.

Click **Sync** to immediately sync jobs and candidates to Aspect.

Finally, copy the webhook secret and webhook endpoint for use in the next step.

#### Create webhooks

Create 4 webhooks in Greenhouse Recruiting using the information from Aspect. Follow the steps in [this article](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/5888163727003) to create your webhooks in Greenhouse. Use the values listed below to configure the webhooks:

**Webhook 1**  
---  
**Name** | Most people use Job updated — Aspect integration.  
**When** | Job post updated  
**Endpoint URL** | The Endpoint URL provided by Aspect  
**Secret key** | The secret key provided by Aspect  
**Webhook 2**  
---  
**Name** | Most people use Job created — Aspect integration.  
**When** | Job created  
**Endpoint URL** | The Endpoint URL provided by Aspect  
**Secret key** | The secret key provided by Aspect  
**Webhook 3**  
---  
**Name** | Most people use Candidate or prospect updated — Aspect integration.  
**When** | Candidate or prospect updated  
**Endpoint URL** | The Endpoint URL provided by Aspect  
**Secret key** | The secret key provided by Aspect  
**Webhook 4**  
---  
**Name** | Most people use Candidate has changed stage — Aspect integration.  
**When** | Candidate has changed stage  
**Endpoint URL** | The Endpoint URL provided by Aspect  
**Secret key** | The secret key provided by Aspect  
  
When finished, the integration is set up and ready to use.

### Use the integration with Greenhouse Recruiting

Once the integration is set up, an Aspect note taker will process your interview, and post the interview summary to the candidate's Activity Feed in Greenhouse Recruiting. Notes posted on the candidate's Activity Feed are created on behalf of the user who set up the integration with Aspect.

### Additional resources

For additional information or troubleshooting not covered here, reach out to [info@aspect-hq.com](mailto:info@aspect-hq.com) or visit [Aspect HQ](https://aspect-hq.com/).

# Use Greenhouse Notetaker to record and summarize interviews

**Permissions:** Site Admins and Job Admins

**Product tier:** Available for Plus and Pro subscription tiers

Greenhouse Notetaker helps interviewers stay focused by automatically recording interviews and generating AI-powered notes and summaries. After the interview, recordings, transcripts, and generated summaries are available alongside scorecards to help teams complete evaluations more efficiently and consistently.

This feature is currently in beta and may not be available to your organization.

#### In this article

  * Add a notetaker to an interview
    * Removing a notetaker
  * Candidate consent
  * Using Greenhouse Notetaker during an interview
    * Controlling the notetaker from the scorecard
  * Review interview recordings and notes
    * View recordings and transcripts
    * Filling out scorecards with the AI-generated summaries
  * Configure Greenhouse Notetaker
    * Turning Greenhouse Notetaker on for jobs
    * Permissions
  * Additional resources



### Add a notetaker to an interview

To add a notetaker to an interview, the following conditions must be met:

  * Greenhouse Notetaker must be enabled for your organization
  * Greenhouse Notetaker must be enabled for the job
  * The candidate must provide consent for interview recording and transcription



To add a notetaker, click the ellipsis icon next to the interview and select **Add notetaker to interview**.

**Note:** Interviews can be rescheduled until 10 minutes after the scheduled end time. If an interview is rescheduled while it’s in progress or within this timeframe, any recordings, transcripts, and generated notes collected for the interview are removed.

If an interview is rescheduled while it’s in progress or within 10 minutes after the scheduled end time, Greenhouse displays a warning before the interview is updated. Rescheduling the interview during this timeframe removes any recordings, transcripts, and generated notes already collected for the interview.

An icon next to the interview name displays the status of Greenhouse Notetaker. A filled purple icon indicates that a notetaker is scheduled to join the interview. A greyed-out icon indicates that the candidate didn’t provide consent, the selected video conferencing platform isn’t supported, or Greenhouse Notetaker isn’t enabled for the interview.

#### Removing a notetaker

Greenhouse Notetaker can be removed from an interview at any time before the interview starts. If a candidate withdraws consent after a notetaker has already been scheduled, Greenhouse automatically removes the notetaker from the interview and no additional action is required. In either case, the notetaker won’t join the interview call.

To manually remove a scheduled notetaker, click the ellipsis icon next to the interview and select **Remove notetaker**.

### Candidate consent

To add Greenhouse Notetaker to an interview, the candidate must provide consent to be recorded and transcribed. When Greenhouse Notetaker is enabled for a job, candidates can provide consent through the following scheduling methods:

  * Self-schedule requests
  * Availability requests



### Using Greenhouse Notetaker during an interview

The notetaker joins the meeting one minute before the scheduled interview start time. In the meeting, it appears as a participant tile named _Greenhouse Notetaker_ followed by the scheduled interview time, which helps distinguish between multiple notetakers if overlapping interviews occur in the same meeting session.

Once the notetaker joins the meeting, recording begins automatically.

**Note:** Depending on the meeting host's video conferencing settings, they may need to let the notetaker in manually.

Unless Greenhouse Notetaker is manually removed from the meeting, it remains in the call until one minute after the scheduled interview end time, even if the meeting continues longer.

Greenhouse Notetaker also automatically leaves the call when all participants exit the meeting.

If back-to-back interviews overlap within the same meeting session, multiple notetakers may temporarily appear in the call until the earlier interview’s notetaker exits.

#### Controlling the notetaker from the scorecard

The primary way to manage Greenhouse Notetaker during an interview is through the scorecard. While the interview is in progress, a red **Recording** status appears at the top of the page.

You can manually stop the recording at any time by clicking **Stop recording** either in the page header or at the top of the Interview Questions section of the scorecard.

### Review recordings and transcripts

#### View recordings and transcripts

After the interview ends, Greenhouse begins generating the recording, transcript, and AI-generated notes. Processing may take a few minutes.

Once processing is complete, a tab containing the interview recording and transcript appears in the menu at the top of the page.

The transcript includes clickable timestamps that allow you to jump to specific parts of the interview recording. You can also search the transcript for specific words or phrases mentioned during the interview.

Transcripts that were deleted or couldn’t be generated won’t appear in this tab.

#### Filling out scorecards with the AI-generated summaries

Question notes are automatically generated for each interview question and summarize how the candidate responded. These notes include supporting details and insights from the interview transcript. Each point in the summary includes a clickable timestamp that links directly to the relevant part of the transcript.

Greenhouse also generates an overall interview summary that provides a factual recap of the conversation and highlights key topics discussed during the interview.

You can add question notes and the overall interview summary directly to the scorecard by clicking **Add to summary** beneath each generated section.

If no questions are added to the interview kit, Greenhouse Notetaker automatically identifies questions asked during the interview and generates relevant question notes from the transcript.

To support structured hiring practices, interviewers are encouraged to add their own evaluation of the candidate in the _Key Takeaways_ section of the scorecard. If an interviewer adds generated notes without including their own assessment, a reminder appears before the scorecard is submitted. This reminder doesn’t prevent scorecard submission.

### Configure Greenhouse Notetaker

Before Greenhouse Notetaker can be used in interviews, it must be enabled through a layered configuration process at the organization, job, and interview levels. Organization-level settings allow Job Admins to enable the feature for jobs, while interview-level controls allow users to add or remove a notetaker for individual interviews based on candidate consent and scheduling needs.

#### Turning Greenhouse Notetaker on for jobs

A Site Admin or a Job Admin with permission to manage the job can enable Greenhouse Notetaker for interviews in the interview plan.

To enable Greenhouse Notetaker, open the job and go to **Job Setup** > **Interview Plan**.

In the _Additional Settings_ section at the bottom of the page, select the checkbox for **Enable Greenhouse Notetaker**.

After you enable Greenhouse Notetaker, choose which interviews should include a notetaker:

  * **All interviews** adds a notetaker to every interview in the interview plan, including interviews that are already scheduled.
  * **Only interviews scheduled or updated moving forward** adds a notetaker only to future interviews and interviews that are rescheduled after this setting is selected.



#### Permissions

Configure your Job Admin stripes by navigating to Configure and selecting **Permissions**. Find and click the link to **See and manage Job Admin levels**.

Job Admins will first need to be assigned the permission stripe _Can view scorecards submitted by other users_ in either the _Always_ or _After submit_ state. Then, the permission _Can view AI notetaking recordings, transcripts, and notes_ can be assigned.

### Additional resources

  * Setup guide
  * [Scorecards overview](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/4414777492891)

# Weekly recruiting report

**Permissions:** Job Admin and above

**Product tier:** Available for new subscription tiers (Core, Plus, and Pro)

The weekly recruiting report is an email notification sent to specific users regarding the weekly activity for a job. As a general overview, the weekly recruiting report provides stakeholders with information about how your hiring process is going and can be easily emailed to anyone in your organization, such as a hiring manager in constant need of updates.

#### In this article

  * Add users to the notification list for the weekly recruiting report
  * Remove users from the notification list for the weekly recruiting report



### Add users to the notification list for the weekly recruiting report

To add users to the notification list for the weekly recruiting report, click**Jobs** from the navigation bar and select a job from the list.

Click**Job Setup** and navigate to **Notifications** on the left.

Scroll to the _Other Notifications_ section and click **Configure** beside _Weekly Recruiting Report_.

**Note** : The report Is sent to recipients every week on the calendar day the job was originally opened for candidate recruitment (for example, every Monday). The text of the email notification for the weekly recruiting report cannot be edited.

# Candidate profile redesign overview

**Permissions:** Job Admins who can view and edit candidates and above

**Product tier:** Available for new subscription tiers (Core, Plus, and Pro)

The candidate profile is one of the most important pages in Greenhouse. It’s where recruiters, hiring managers, and the rest of the hiring team come together to participate in structured hiring. This article will help you understand the profile’s layout, learn about its features, and find resources to get your team working smoothly.

#### In this article

  * Overview and updates
  * How the profile is organized
  * Key features
  * Training resources
  * Frequently asked questions



### Overview and updates

The candidate profile is designed to help your team work together more seamlessly. This version brings important details to the surface, organizes information more clearly, and introduces features that make it easier to keep hiring moving forward.

We’ve continued to refine the profile since launch, guided by customer feedback. Updates include AI-powered scorecard summaries, automated scheduling suggestions, streamlined workflows, clearer visibility into key details, and changes that better match how hiring teams work together.

Learn how customer feedback informed the candidate profile experience in our blog post, [_From feedback to features: How your input helped evolve the candidate profile._](https://www.greenhouse.com/blog/from-feedback-to-features-how-your-input-helped-evolve-the-candidate-profile)

#### Ongoing improvements

**Better visibility**  
We’ve adjusted the layout so information is easier to scan at a glance. The header now includes key details like contact info, time zone, and local time, while the All Stages view in the main panel has been expanded to show interview and scorecard details. You can also expand interview stages to see the full process without losing context.

**Easier navigation**  
You can move between candidates and complete actions more easily. Use the arrows at the top of the screen to jump between profiles, access common actions without opening hidden menus, and view a candidate’s activity across jobs from the **All Jobs** tab.

**Improved usability**  
The profile is optimized for smaller screens, so you can review candidates on any device.

### How the profile is organized

The candidate profile is organized into three main sections—the header, main panel, and right panel. This video walks through each one, showing you where to find key details like scorecards, offers, and tasks, and how to stay organized as you collaborate with your team.

#### Header

The header is designed to give you the essentials up front, so you can understand who the candidate is and take action without leaving the page. It surfaces the most important details—name, [pronouns](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360055919252), contact info, time zone, and [tags](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360004149852)—at the top of the profile where they’re always visible.

From here, you can quickly take the actions that move hiring forward: email a candidate, add or transfer them to another job, update their status, or return to the job they applied for.

For faster access, use keyboard shortcuts:

  * **R** → open the candidate’s resume

  * **X** → reject the candidate

  * **M** → move the candidate to another stage




#### Main panel

The main panel is where you manage a candidate’s progress through the hiring process. It’s designed to bring together the tools your team uses most, so you can review their progress, schedule interviews, and make decisions without leaving the page.

**Stages**

Open an interview stage to review planned interviews, schedule new ones, send confirmations, and assign scorecards. Candidate availability can be requested or entered manually.

**Scorecards**

Track which scorecards are pending or submitted, and open any scorecard to review detailed feedback.

**Offer details**

Manage everything related to offers in one spot, including approvals, documents, and the offer packet.

**Activity feed**  
View a complete record of updates to the candidate, from stage changes to notes. Filters and search make it easy to find specific updates when needed.

#### Right panel

The right panel organizes supporting details into tabs, so you can quickly access application data, team notes, and tasks without cluttering the main panel. Click any tab to open or collapse the panel, or select the icon in the top left corner to close and open the panel. 

**Candidate details**

This tab shows the candidate’s personal and professional information, including their name, contact details, current role, and time zone. Answers to custom application questions will be reflected here as well.

**Application details**  
See when a candidate applied, who referred them, and which recruiter or coordinator is responsible. You can also manage application documents and send e-Signature agreements directly from this tab.

**All jobs**  
See a candidate’s full history across jobs, including active and past applications with their outcomes. This gives you a clear view of their journey with your organization.

**Notes**  
Leave updates for your team, filter or pin key messages, and [@mention](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360013153651) teammates to keep everyone aligned. Notes live in one place so context isn’t lost in emails or chats.

**Tasks and reminders**  
Track what needs attention, from requesting availability to scheduling interviews.

Some candidate information may be sensitive. Toggle on **Private mode** at the top of the right panel to hide it across all tabs and the main panel.

### Key features

The candidate profile includes features that surface insights at the right time, streamline everyday workflows, and help hiring teams stay aligned throughout the process.

#### Quick navigation and insights

Work faster and stay focused with tools that highlight key details and bring the right information to the surface, helping your team make decisions with confidence.

  * [AI-generated scorecard summaries](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/34878281840923): Surface the main takeaways from scorecards and link directly to the full feedback behind them.
  * [Keyboard shortcuts](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/10737253281051): Navigate between panels, switch tabs, move through candidates, and perform actions quickly using your keyboard.
  * [Calculated custom offer fields](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/31723991042075): Automatically prefill values for custom offer fields, reducing manual entry and keeping data consistent.



#### Streamlined scheduling

The candidate profile includes tools to simplify scheduling so you can spend less time coordinating and more time focusing on candidates.

  * [Scheduling suggestions:](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/36255269371419) Automatically generate interview time slots that respect interviewer preferences, candidate availability, and your team's working hours.
  * [Scheduled take home tests](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/200734889): Assign and send exercises at a set time, then track submissions and evaluations directly in the candidate profile.



#### Collaboration and clarity

Keep everyone on the same page with features that surface the right context and make collaboration more inclusive.

  * [e-Signature agreements](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/27637882883995): Send and collect signature requests with Adobe Acrobat Sign directly from the candidate profile at any stage of the hiring process.
  * Pinned notes and filters: Apply filters to quickly narrow down notes by type or author, and pin critical items so they remain at the top of the **Notes** tab for quick reference.

  * [Preferred name](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/29532706145691): Display the name a candidate prefers to go by, creating a more personal experience from the start.




### Training resources

Training and resources are available to help you and your team feel confident working in the candidate profile. Whether you prefer quick videos, a self-paced course, or live support, there are options to fit your workflow.

Our customer trainers have prepared courses and videos to help you and your team get started with the candidate profile. You can take these courses or watch the videos on [Learn Greenhouse](https://learn.greenhouse.io/).

Watch these quick videos to learn about specific areas of the candidate profile:

  * [Candidate information](https://learn.greenhouse.io/candidate-profile-candidate-information/2067033)
  * [Messaging and tasks](https://learn.greenhouse.io/candidate-profile-messaging-and-tasks/2067034)
  * [Managing candidates](https://learn.greenhouse.io/candidate-profile-managing-candidates/2067035)



All of these videos are also available in our [comprehensive walkthrough](https://learn.greenhouse.io/candidate-profile-in-depth-walkthrough) of the redesign.

For more in-depth training, you can join our on-demand training course, [_Hire better together with the new candidate profile_](https://learn.greenhouse.io/hire-better-together-with-the-new-candidate-profile-1/1947496) _._ See all upcoming events and register on the [live training calendar](https://learn.greenhouse.io/calendar).

### Frequently asked questions

**Has the new candidate profile caused any permission changes?**

No. Users retain the same job-level permissions they had before.

**How are** _**Tasks**_**in the new candidate profile different from** _**My Tasks**_**on the** _**My Dashboard**_**page?**

The _My Tasks_ section on the dashboard shows your tasks across all jobs. In the candidate profile, Tasks are tied to a specific candidate’s job and can be seen by anyone assigned to that job.

# Change detection with HRIS Link

**Permissions:** —

**Product tier:** Available for Pro subscription tier with HRIS Link add-on

When an HRIS Link sync is initially enabled, your Greenhouse technical consultant will trigger a one-time import that updates Greenhouse Recruiting records and ensures data is in sync with your HRIS. 

Once HRIS Link is running, data is updated in Greenhouse Recruiting only if there's an update to the data in the HRIS report. This means if someone in your organization makes an update to a job, department, office, or user in Greenhouse Recruiting, that update won’t necessarily be overwritten the next time HRIS Link runs. Data will only be overwritten in Greenhouse Recruiting the next time an update is made to that job, department, office, or user in your HRIS.

**Example:** If you were to update the cost center for a job in Greenhouse Recruiting from _Operations_ to _Engineering_ , but there was no change to the corresponding job in your HRIS, _Engineering_ would remain selected as the cost center on the job in Greenhouse Recruiting until an update is made to the job in your HRIS.

To prevent data from falling out of sync between your HRIS and Greenhouse Recruiting, we recommend leveraging the _API only_ setting on job custom fields where your HRIS should be the source of truth. This locks down the field and prevents users from making manual updates in Greenhouse Recruiting. Check out [Harvest-only custom job fields](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/115005136763) to learn more.

# Manager access

**Permissions:** Owners

**Product tier:** Available for Greenhouse Welcome and Greenhouse Onboarding subscription tiers

Manager access provides greater visibility and control for your managers so they can be more hands-on in your organization's onboarding plan. Manager access is granted in addition to the default [employee access ](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360019514671)for users who have been selected as a manager for another employee.

#### In this article

  * Assign manager permissions
  * Configure manager permissions
  * Customize manager access to employee fields  

    * View only
    * View and edit
    * Hidden
  * Additional resources



### Assign manager permissions

Unlike [administrative](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360019200392) or [custom](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360019516351) roles, which must be manually assigned to users, manager access is granted automatically when you select a user to be the **Manager** for another employee.

**Note:** Learn more about [adding new hires to Greenhouse Onboarding](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360000683352) and [updating employee profiles](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/5759718119707).

### Configure manager permissions

You can update the default access permissions for all managers in your organization on the _Permissions_ page.

Navigate to **Settings** > **Data Flow** > **Permissions**.

Scroll down to the _Default Access_ panel and click **Edit** next to **Manager Additional Access**.

Your organization can configure the following administrative permissions for managers.

  * **Can manage employee documents and signature requests** – allows managers to view and manage their employees' documents and signature requests
  * **Can only view the tasks that have been assigned to direct reports** – allows managers view-only access to their direct reports' onboarding tasks
  * **Can view and edit tasks that have been assigned to direct reports** – allows managers to view and edit tasks in their direct reports' employee profiles



**Note:** Learn more about [setting manager access to view or edit employee tasks](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/16336320416155). 

### Customize manager access to employee fields

Your organization can also configure the employee fields that managers have access to view or edit for their direct reports.

**Note:** Manager view and edit access to their direct reports' employee fields will be set to [Employee Access](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360019514671) by default until you grant additional access.

Each field permission is made up of two types of access:

  * **Can Edit for Direct Reports** – managers can update the field for their direct reports
  * **Can View for Direct Reports** – managers can only view the field on their employee's profile



**Note:** The **Can Edit for Direct Reports** permission is used in conjunction with the [employee access permission](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360019514671) **Can Edit for Onself.** If the employee's permission is configured, but the manager's permission is not, only employees and administrators will be able to update this field.

#### View only

You may want a manager to see an employee field but not be able to update this information themselves. For example, you can allow a manager to view the**Date of Termination** field, but only allow Owners and Coordinators to update the value.

For this configuration, select the **Can View for Direct Reports** box only. Leave the **Can Edit for Direct Reports** checkbox unchecked. 

#### View and edit

Select both checkboxes to allow managers to see and edit an employee field.

Employee fields that managers have access to edit will be included in that user's [manager form](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/208216756).

#### Hidden

Uncheck both boxes to keep a field completely hidden from managers.

### Additional resources

  * [Manager access to employee profiles](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/13298081921179)
  * [Set manager access to view or edit employee tasks](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/16336320416155)

# Maildrop

**Permissions:** Job Admin or higher

**Product tier:** Available for new subscription tiers (Core, Plus, and Pro)

Greenhouse Recruiting's Maildrop feature is a convenient way to create and add candidates/prospects to jobs. Additionally, the feature enables your organization to log external email conversations you may be having with candidates/prospects into your Greenhouse account.

In this article, we will cover how to retrieve your organization's job-specific Maildrop email addresses, and detail some ways your organization can leverage the feature.

#### In this article

  * Overview
  * Retrieve your organization's Maildrop addresses
    * Locating job-specific Maildrop addresses
    * Locating Maildrop address to log conversation and create unattached prospects
  * Use Maildrop in Greenhouse Recruiting 
    * Attach candidates to a job 
    * Bulk resume processing
    * Log candidate/prospect conversation 
    * Create unattached prospects



### Overview

**Note:** Maildrop is specifically limited to Greenhouse Recruiting users.

To successfully forward a message from your inbox to create a candidate/prospect or log email conversations, Maildrop must recognize your email address (meaning the email address [must be associated](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360034879332) with your Greenhouse Recruiting user account).

If you plan to forward messages from multiple email addresses, be sure to add those additional email addresses to your user account.

To add multiple email addresses to your user account, select your initials in the top right corner and select **Account Settings** from the dropdown menu.

Navigate to the _Personal Information_ panel and click the **Edit** icon .

From the _Edit Personal Information_ page, click **Add another email** and enter the additional email address(es). When finished, navigate to the bottom of the page and click **Save**.

### Retrieve your organization's Maildrop addresses

Every open job in your organization is assigned a unique Maildrop email address so users can create candidates in Greenhouse Recruiting via email.

Your entire organization also has access to a separate general Maildrop address that can be used to log email conversations with candidates/prospects, and to create unattached prospects. In this section, we will briefly examine where to find the two types of Maildrop addresses.

Both types of email addresses can be found on your organization's [Greenhouse Maildrop page](https://app.greenhouse.io/people/instructions/maildrop).

To navigate to the Greenhouse Maildrop page, you'll need to open the _Add a Candidate_ page. You find find this page under **Add** > **Candidate**. 

From the _Add a Candidate_ page, click **Forward Resume via Email** on the left side.

**Note** : Greenhouse Recruiting does not support auto-forwarding to a Maildrop address from your email client.

Find the email addresses as needed. Check out the sections below for more information on finding a specific address.

#### Locating job-specific Maildrop addresses

From your organization's _Greenhouse Maildrop_ page, navigate to the table at the bottom of the page.

This table will list every Open job in your organization with the corresponding job-specific Maildrop email address. Use each job's respective Maildrop email address to create candidates and attach them to the job via email.

#### Locating Maildrop address to log conversation and create unattached prospects

Your organization's Maildrop address to log email conversations with candidates/prospects and create unattached prospects can be found in Use Case**2 and 3** on the [Greenhouse Maildrop page](https://app.greenhouse.io/people/instructions/maildrop).

Use this Maildrop address to log email conversations with candidates/prospects and create unattached prospects via email.

### Use Maildrop in Greenhouse Recruiting 

#### Attach candidates to a job

Using the Maildrop feature you can easily forward an email from your inbox to a job's unique Maildrop address to create a candidate for that job. Emails forwarded to a job's unique Maildrop address can include attached resumes, cover letters, and so on. All that information will be attached to the new candidate's profile.

If a forwarded message includes an attached resume, Maildrop attempts to parse the resume to help build the candidate's profile in Greenhouse Recruiting.

Since resumes generally follow a fairly standard format, the parsing technology uses that standard structure as a guide to interpret the content and pull out the name, email address, phone number, mailing address, current title, and the current company of the candidate.

Occasionally, a candidate might provide a resume that doesn't follow a standard format, or that includes embedded images. In cases like this, the content cannot be interpreted to build the candidate profile. This causes resume parsing to fail, and the candidate won't be added to Greenhouse Recruiting.

If resume parsing fails, your organization must [add the candidate manually](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/115002195063-VIDEO-Manually-Adding-Candidates).

If a forwarded message does not include an attached resume and the email is sent to the generic Maildrop address, Maildrop will attempt to build the candidate’s profile using the information in the email itself, including the name and email address of the candidate. If the candidate's email cannot be found in the system, a new prospect profile will be created instead.

**Note** : You'll receive an email notification from [no-reply@greenhouse.io](mailto:no-reply@greenhouse.io) that confirms either the candidate was successfully created, or that Maildrop failed to create a candidate and you must add the candidate manually.

In addition, if you send a resume that matches an existing candidate profile (name and email address) to a job-specific Maildrop address, Greenhouse Recruiting adds the resume to the existing candidate profile as an attachment.

#### Use Maildrop for bulk resume processing

If a member of your organization or an agency wants to create multiple candidates for a job using Maildrop, simply add **BULK** (all capitalized letters) to the subject heading of the email.

Entering **BULK** in the subject heading is critical, as this indicates to Maildrop the message includes multiple resumes to be processed. If you don't include **BULK** , Maildrop processes only one of the resumes and overlooks the rest.

**Note** : You must enter **BULK** in all caps in the subject line, or the bulk processing will fail.

Attach multiple resumes to the email and send to the job's unique Maildrop address.

You will receive an email notification letting you know how many candidates were created successfully and how many candidates (if any) failed.

**Note:** We recommend limiting resume attachments to 10–15 per email when using the bulk resume processing feature.

#### Log candidate/prospect conversation

**Note:** If the candidate/prospect is an internal employee at your organization who has a user account in Greenhouse Recruiting, Maildrop cannot be used to log your email conversation. The Maildrop logic purposefully ignores email addresses belonging to internal users at your organization to avoid incorrectly adding them as a candidate.

When a Greenhouse Recruiting user initiates a message to a candidate/prospect from within Greenhouse, that outgoing message is automatically logged in the **Activity Feed** of the candidate’s profile page. To log any other conversations that go to your email inbox and other email conversations that take place outside of Greenhouse, you can either forward an existing email thread to your organization's general Maildrop address, or BCC your organization's general Maildrop address as you send messages.

**Note** : Logging prospect conversations via Maildrop count as both a [CRM touchpoint](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360020298312) and an email in the prospect's Activity Feed, and are counted in the [Prospecting Activity Report](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/204636785-Prospecting-Activity-Report).

#### Create unattached prospects

Your organization can also use Maildrop to keep track of a prospect in Greenhouse Recruiting but not attach them to a specific job. This is a great option for referrals and promising candidates who do not match any open positions. Instead of forwarding a message to a job's unique Maildrop address as you would use to add a Candidate, you’ll instead simply forward the message to your organization's general Maildrop address.

Just as with adding a candidate, the information that is used to build the prospect profile depends on whether a resume was attached to the message.

Additionally, including **BULK** (all capitalized letters) in the subject of an email message with multiple resumes attached creates prospects in bulk (if the resumes can be parsed successfully).

**Note** : You'll receive an email notification from [no-reply@greenhouse.io ](mailto:no-reply@greenhouse.io)letting you know whether or not prospects were added successfully.

<!-- source: https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360007247412-Structured-hiring-Scorecard-definitions -->

# Structured hiring: Scorecard definitions

The scorecard is a list of the skills, traits, and qualifications someone will need to have in order to be successful in the upcoming role. These attributes are what the interview process will be designed to test and verify for each candidate.

Scorecard Definitions and the next step, [Interview Planning](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360007249492), are often done in tandem. Together, they enable you to define and formalize desired candidate attributes into an interview process that screens for these agreed upon attributes.

In this article, we will cover the goals of this step and provide some resources on how you can use Greenhouse to achieve these goals.

### Scorecard definition goals 

The scorecard you define for the role is the basis for the interview process. Future interviews for the role will be designed to test and verify the components of this scorecard. When finished with this step, your hiring team should have a clear vision on the details of the role you are hiring for, the attributes necessary for someone to be successful in the role, and the right candidate's profile.

The process your team uses to define the scorecard is up to you. Some advice we can offer about this step is to:

  1. Keep it brief- the more attributes you add to the scorecard, the more interviews you will need to assess each candidate.
  2. Be realistic- stick to attributes that a candidate will need to truly be successful in the role.
  3. Be mutually exclusive and collective exhausting - that is, do not pick attributes that overlap with each other. Instead focus on how these individual attributes, when considered together, provide a comprehensive image of a candidate.



To learn more about how you can leverage Greenhouse to design insightful scorecards, follow the links below:

  * [Best Practices: Creating a Scorecard](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360003500291-Best-Practices-Creating-a-Scorecard)
  * [Best Practices: Thinking Through Scorecard Categories](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360003500231-Best-Practices-Thinking-Through-Scorecard-Categories)

# Touchpoints

**Permissions:** –

**Product tier:** Available for Pro subscription tiers

Touchpoints refer to interactions either by telephone, email, or in-person, where a recruiter has made contact with a prospect. These points of contact can help your organization's recruiting team view the progress made with a given prospect and plan for the appropriate next steps.

#### In this article

  * Add touchpoints to a prospect
  * View touchpoints on a prospect
  * Edit or delete touchpoints on a prospect



### Add touchpoints to a prospect

From the prospect's profile, click **Add Touchpoint** in the main panel.

In the _Add Touchpoint_ box, provide information for the following fields:

Type |  Categorize the touchpoint into one of three different types:

  * Email
  * Phone
  * In-person

  
---|---  
User | Identify the Greenhouse Recruiting user who performed the touchpoint.  
Date | Enter the date when the touchpoint happened.  
Note | Provide other members of your team with any additional context or description regarding the touchpoint.  
  
When finished, click **Save**.

**Note** : Emails sent through Greenhouse Recruiting are also considered touchpoints and will automatically be added to the prospect's **Activity Feed** as both an email and touchpoint. This includes emails that log prospect conversations via [Maildrop](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/201990630-Maildrop).

### View a prospect's touchpoints

Touchpoints added to a prospect's profile are recorded in their profile's **Activity Feed**. You can filter the feed to only include touchpoints using the fields at the top of the page.

**Note** : Emails sent through Greenhouse Recruiting are also considered touchpoints and will automatically be added to the prospect's **Activity Feed** as both an email and touchpoint. This includes emails that log prospect conversations via [Maildrop](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/201990630-Maildrop).

### Edit or delete a prospect's touchpoints

Not every touchpoint entry will be perfect when initially submitted. You can update a touchpoint to correct mistakes, change the details of a touchpoint, or add additional notes by clicking **Edit** in the Activity Feed on the prospect's profile.

# Tracking link blocked on Craigslist

**Permissions:** Site Admin, and Job Admin who can create, edit and delete job posts

**Product tier:** Available for new subscription tiers (Core, Plus, and Pro)

[Tracking links](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/216904366) are unique URLs for your job's online application that can be pasted on an external job board or as part of the marketing of the job. When candidates apply through a tracking link, they'll be tagged with a pre-determined source and credit**.**

At this time, tracking links and job post links don't work on Craigslist. This is due to the fact that Craigslist blocks all tracking links to prevent spam, including from applicant tracking systems (ATS) like Greenhouse Recruiting.

In order to track any candidates who learn about a job in your organization from Craigslist, create a [custom application question](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360025222851-Add-Custom-Question-To-Job-Application-) such as: _How did you hear about this job?_ and include **Craigslist** as an available option.
