# JobPixel integration

JobPixel makes it easier than ever to supercharge your talent brand with authentic video! Collect, organize, and share real videos from real people to increase candidate flow, improve candidate experience and reduce time to hire.

Enhance your job pages with an engaging video from your hiring manager telling applicants all about the position. Video job descriptions truly resonate with candidates and help you turn your hiring process into an engaging conversation.

Then, hear directly from candidates, in their own words, why they’d be a great addition to your team following their application submission. Skip the phone interview, identify candidate intent, accelerate your hiring, and identify the best fit candidate faster through their video introductions.

JobPixel integration with Greenhouse Recruiting allows you to do the following:

  * Use JobPixel as an assessment partner for providing and receiving candidate’s video introductions
  * Automatically create a JobPixel job post with video assignment from Greenhouse Recruiting webhooks
  * Use auto-embed feature to automatically add targeted videos to the Greenhouse Recruiting job description pages based on the job profile



#### In this article

  * Enable the JobPixel integration
  * Map job titles to videos in JobPixel
  * Configure your webhook
  * Automatically embed videos on your public job description pages
  * Use the JobPixel integration with Greenhouse Recruiting to request candidate videos
  * Additional resources



### Enable the JobPixel integration

To initialize your JobPixel integration for Greenhouse, reach out to [integrations@jobpixel.com](mailto:integrations@jobpixel.com) and request the following:

  * an API key for the JobPixel stage
  * Basic Auth credentials
  * a Secret Key for configuring a webhook that will be used for the Greenhouse Recruiting integration



Once you’ve received the details from JobPixel, follow the steps in [this article](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/5888163696923) to work with Greenhouse Technical Support and add the JobPixel stage to your interview plans. You can then complete the configurations in JobPixel and Greenhouse Recruiting for your desired use case(s).

### Map job titles to videos in JobPixel

JobPixel uses webhooks to automatically assign videos to job postings from Greenhouse Recruiting. If you have JobPixel configured for post-application candidate assessments, JobPixel uses these video assignments for video introduction request invites.

Here we assign videos for the job titles. We use wild card patterns to match the job titles that are imported through the webhook.

You can use an asterisk (*) symbol to create a wildcard pattern. For example, `*developer*` will match to job titles like _Software Developer_ , _Senior Developer - Frontend,_ and so on.

You can create multiple patterns to attach videos to the corresponding job titles. For jobs that don't align with any existing wildcard patterns, you can also create a default video that posts to jobs that don't have a matching rule.

### Configure your webhook

To integrate JobPixel with Greenhouse Recruiting, you’ll need to create a webhook. Follow the steps in [this article](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/5888163727003) to create your webhook. Use the values listed below to configure the webhook:

  * **Name** : JobPixel integration
  * **When** : Job Post Created, Job Post Updated
  * **Endpoint URL** : https://api.jobpixel.com/api/v1/integrations/greenhouse/job
  * **Secret Key** : reach out to [integrations@jobpixel.com ](mailto:integrations@jobpixel.com)to get this.



Apart from the secret key, we use basic authentication for these webhook endpoints. Reach out to [integrations@jobpixel.com](mailto:integrations@jobpixel.com) if you have not already received your http auth credentials and secret key. Keep the password field blank.

Click **Advanced settings** to configure basic authentication username

Make sure webhook is not disabled and click **Create Webhook**. This activates the webhook. When you create or update the job post, it updates the job description based on the videos you configure in JobPixel.

### Automatically embed videos on your public job description pages

To automatically embed these videos on your public job description pages, simply check the toggle under _Enable Job Description Auto Embed_ on your Greenhouse configuration page in JobPixel.

### Use the JobPixel integration with Greenhouse Recruiting to request candidate videos

Once the JobPixel integration is enabled for your organization, you will be able to add the JobPixel Video Introduction assessment as an interview stage. Please refer to the screenshot below.

You can send an assessment to a candidate by clicking the**Send Test** button next to the interview stage.

Select the appropriate test and the person who should grade the assessment, then click **Send Test.**

After it has been sent, an assessment’s status will display in Greenhouse Recruiting.

Once the candidate has submitted their video introduction, the Interview Kit will contain a link to view the submitted result in the JobPixel application.

Click **JobPixel** to see the report.

To see a candidate’s video introduction in JobPixel, click **View** **Report** .

After clicking**View Report,** you will be redirected to the JobPixel where you will see the video introduction the candidate has submitted.

### Additional resources

For additional information or integration questions not covered here, reach out to [integrations@jobpixel.com](mailto:integrations@jobpixel.com).

# Format text with the rich text editor

Many text fields in Greenhouse Recruiting include a formatting toolbar that offers options to format your text.

If a text field doesn’t have a toolbar, formatting is not supported for that field.

#### In this article

  * Formatting options
    * Text
    * Paragraph
    * Insert item
    * View source code
  * Best practices for entering code in a text box



### Formatting options

#### Text

Format your text to emphasize or make certain words stand out.

|  **Bold** **Bold your text.**  
---|---  
|  **Italic** _Italicize your text._  
|  **Underline** Underline your text.  
  
#### Paragraph

Format your paragraphs to create visually separate sections or lists. 

|  **Align left** Aligns a paragraph of text to the **left** side.  
---|---  
|  **Align center** Aligns a paragraph of text to the **center**.  
|  **Align right** Aligns a paragraph of text to the **right** side.  
|  **Bullet list**

  * Example
  * Example
  * Example

  
|  **Numbered list**

  1. Example
  2. Example
  3. Example

  
|  **Decrease indent** Moves your paragraph to the left. This option is only available after you've used the _Increase indent_ tool.  
|  **Increase indent** Moves your paragraph to the right.  
  
#### Insert item

Provide additional context to your text by inserting a link, image, or other item.

|  **Horizontal line** Inserts a horizontal line to visually separate sections of text. 

* * *  
  
---|---  
|  **Insert/edit link** Adds a [hyperlink](https://www.greenhouse.com/) to your text.   
|  **Insert/edit image** Learn how to insert an image [here](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/115003515106).  
|  **Insert/edit media** Learn how to insert a video [here](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/115003515106).  
  
#### View source code

Viewing source code can be useful if you want to see the source of any unexpected formatting or to add custom HTML not available in the toolbar.

|  **Source code** The _Source Code_ field shows the HTML tags applied to your text.  
---|---  
  
### Best practices for entering code in a text box

You may need to enter portions of code into a text box in Greenhouse Recruiting, such as when completing a scorecard for an interview that included a coding exercise. 

When entering code in the text box, paste it using `CTRL + shift + V` to prevent entering unintended formatting from your code editor.

Then apply _Code_ formatting to the text you added (_Paragraph > Inline > Code_). This format adds the tag `<code>` around the text, which tells your browser to display the text within the tag, rather than render it.

**Note** : For security purposes, you can't save executable code like JavaScript in a text field. Executable code will be removed, and no error message will be displayed.

# Duplicate interviews are appearing on the candidate profile, instead of multiple unique interviews

If you have scheduled multiple, unique interviews, yet these are all appearing as duplicates of the same interview, this is likely due to the interview kit URL that is being used in the calendar details section.

Usually we see this if the body of a calendar invite is copied and pasted to create other interviews.

### Steps to resolve

  1. Click on the correct name of the interview from the candidate profile. This will take you to the interview kit for this interview.
  2. Copy the URL of this interview kit page.
  3. In the external calendar invite details, replace the existing link with this newly copied link.
  4. Send the update to all attendees so that Greenhouse Recruiting can capture this change.



This interview kit link maps the scheduled interview to the correct candidate profile and correct stage / interview.

# Create Harvest API credentials for an integration

**Permissions:** Basic and above who can manage ALL organization’s API credentials

**Product tier:** Available for new subscription tiers (Core, Plus, and Pro)

Access the latest version of Harvest API documentation at [**harvestdocs.greenhouse.io**](http://harvestdocs.greenhouse.io).  
  
Harvest API v1 and v2 will be deprecated and unavailable after August 31, 2026. Please make sure that your existing custom integrations use the latest version of Harvest (v3) by this date and any new integrations are developed with the latest version of Harvest API.

Some integrations require Harvest API credentials to connect to your Greenhouse Recruiting account. Check out the [integration documentation](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/sections/4405932824091-Integrations) for information on a specific integration.

#### In this article

  * Create Harvest API credentials for an integration



### Create Harvest API credentials for an integration

Click the **Configure** icon  on your navigation bar, then click **Dev Center** on the left.

Click **API Credential Management**.

Click **Create new API credentials.**

Make the following selections:

  * **API type** : Choose _Harvest_ or _Harvest v3 (OAuth)_
  * **Partner** : Select the name of the integration that requested the API credential. If the integration isn't listed, select unlisted vendor. If you're creating a custom integration, select custom.
  * **Description** : Give your API key a descriptive name.



When finished, click **Manage permissions** or**View and store credentials**(depending on which Harvest version you chose.)

After the the credential is created, click **Copy** , and paste the credentials in a secure location to provide to the integration later.

Click **I have stored the client credentials**.

**Note:**

  * For Harvest v3, the client secret is shown only once. The client key remains visible.
  * For Harvest v1/v2, the API key is shown only once and can't be viewed again after clicking I have stored the API key.



Next, confirm the permissions requested by the integration are assigned to your new API key. If any of the requested permissions are not assigned to the API key, assign them.

**Note:** Be aware that providing permission to your data is similar to assigning a user access to the data in-app. Learn more at [Manage Harvest API credentials permissions](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/115000521723).

When finished, click **Save**. 

Provide the API key to your contact at the integration.

# Release Notes: 2021 August 20

In an effort to improve our suite of products, Greenhouse Software regularly releases new product features, updates, and improvements. Stay up to date with what's new at Greenhouse by **Following** our [release notes](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/sections/360000710732-Release-Notes).

Find our releases for this week below:

  * Bug fixes



### **Bug fixes**

  * Fixed an issue where users could not mark a candidate as hired on a closed or draft job.
  * Fixed an issue where recurring scorecard reminders were sending one last time after they were addressed.
  * Fixed an issue where end-of-day scorecard reminders were not sending. 
  * Fixed an issue in the Job Ad Market where an error displayed if a campaign was created for a source that is no longer available for job ads. 
  * Fixed an issue where the correct Start Date was not showing on reports or dashboards in Greenhouse Onboarding if it was sent over by Greenhouse Recruiting.

# Delete candidates' personal data in bulk

**Product tier:** Available for new subscription tiers (Core, Plus, and Pro)

When multiple candidates' retention timers have expired, you can delete their data in bulk all at once. In this article, we'll cover how to delete personal data for multiple candidates and / or prospects on Greenhouse Recruiting.

# GigaMe integration

The Greenhouse / GigaMe integration provides the following advantages:

# Certn integration

Certn helps fast-moving teams run background checks directly inside Greenhouse. With automation that kicks in the moment a candidate moves stages, and real-time updates that flow back into your ATS, you can screen faster, without the back-and-forth or manual triggers.

This integration lets you:

  * Add Certn as a stage in your interview plan
  * Automate background check requests
  * Access candidate reports via secure link or PDF
  * Maintain a seamless experience for your team and your candidates



#### In this article

  * Set up the Certn integration
  * Use the Certn integration
  * Additional resources



### Set up the Certn integration

#### Retrieve your API key

To enable the integration, please log into Certn. Navigate to the **Settings** > **Integrations** and select **Add** next to the Greenhouse icon. You will receive an API key that you will need to save to submit to Greenhouse. Important: You will not be able to access this API key again after leaving the page. Make sure it is saved somewhere secure before proceeding.

Ensure that you know which region that you are located in. There are 3 region specific stages that you can select from when configuring your Greenhouse Integration:

  * Certn [EMEA]
  * Certn [North America]
  * Certn [AU]



**Secure API Key Submission**

The Greenhouse Support Team will respond with a [SendSafely link](https://www.sendsafely.com/howitworks/) where you can enter your API key. You will need to provide the regional stage you need enabled in your response to Greenhouse. For example: API KEY ########, Certn [EMEA]

**Note:** The Greenhouse Support Team may request a [Support Verification Code](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360022771952) to verify your identity before adding the API key to your organization's account.

Once this is done, the Greenhouse Support Team will enable your integration, and you will receive a confirmation email from them.

#### Configure the stage

Once the appropriate region specific Certn stage is enabled for your organization, you will be able to [add the Certn background check as an interview stage](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/21338859258267).

### Use the Certn integration

**Note:** A Certn background check (referred to as “assessment” in the Greenhouse platform) can only be sent to active candidates. If a candidate has already been [marked as hired](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/200242039), a Certn background check won't be sent. 

#### Send and review the test

You can send a background check to a candidate by selecting the **Send Test** button next to the interview stage.

After it has been sent, a check status will display in Greenhouse Recruiting.

**Note:** If you want to automate background checks being sent to your candidates, [create a stage transition rule](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360053129752).

Once [configured](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360048178672), background checks will be triggered to send automatically after a candidate moves into the defined partner stage.

#### **View candidate results**

Once the candidate has submitted their test, the **Interview Kit** will contain a link or pdf to view the Certn report in Certn.

### **Additional resources**

For additional information on the integration not covered here, reach out to [Certn](https://certn.co/contact/) or check out these support articles 

  * [Certn Greenhouse setup](https://help.certn.co/hc/en-us/articles/49116197506835-Certn-Greenhouse-Setup)
  * [Certn Greenhouse user guide](https://help.certn.co/hc/en-us/articles/49116102350483-Greenhouse-Certn-User-Guide)

# Business Intelligence Connector and custom fields

**Permissions:** –

**Product tier:** Available for Plus and Pro subscription tiers

Custom fields represent data unique to your organization. The specific setup, amount, or possible values you use for custom fields may differ greatly from another organization. Because of this unpredictability, we created Business Intelligence Connector to be flexible enough to support any custom field you create.

You can query a specific custom field using the custom field column in the associated table. 

#### In this article

  * How it works
    * with SQL
    * in Tableau



### How custom fields work on Business Intelligence Connector

Imagine your organization has created two custom fields to store information not offered by default in Greenhouse Recruiting: Employment Type and Salary Range.

When viewing a table, you may expect `Employment Type` and `Salary Range` to display as separate rows on the [`jobs_custom_fields`](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360001892012#:~:text=The%20job%20custom%20fields%20table) table. However, Business Intelligence Connector abstracts custom fields into two columns: one, labeled `Custom field` returns the specific field like Employment Type, and the second column called `Display value` returns its values, like Contract. By joining these two columns, you can query unique values to best fit your reporting needs.

**Note:** If you want to report on multiple custom fields at once, you will need to separate distinct custom fields from each other, which you can then use in your analysis.

#### SQL

To report on custom fields in SQL, break the custom fields table into multiple tables, one per distinct custom field. Then, you can use these temporary tables in your SQL statement.

For example, you can create a table representing Employment Type via the following SQL query:
    
    
    SELECT job_id, display_value as "Employment Type" FROM job_custom_fields WHERE custom_field = "Employment Type" 

Using this pattern, you can create individual tables for each custom field and then include them in your FROM statement to join the tables together, creating one column per custom field.

#### Tableau

To report on custom fields in Tableau, use the following formula structure that combines a [Level of Detail Expression](https://onlinehelp.tableau.com/current/pro/online/mac/en-us/calculations_calculatedfields_lod_overview.html) with a CASE expression:
    
    
    { FIXED [ID# of the custom field object] :
    max( CASE [Custom Field]
    when "name of custom field"
    then [Display Value]
    end)
    }

After you've created the custom field, it will appear in your list of dimensions, and you can add it to your report.

**Learn more**

[Guide to Business Intelligence Connector](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360001892012)

[Frequently asked questions](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/4405638814235)

# Add LinkedIn InMail steps to a campaign pool

**Permissions:** Job Admin and above with CRM access, a Sourcing Automation seat, and LinkedIn RSC

**Product tier:** Available for new subscription tiers (Core, Plus, and Pro) with the Sourcing Automation add-on

**Learn more about Sourcing Automation**

[Overview](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/5131929423643)

[Manage prospects in a campaign pool](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/5285464148379)

[Create and manage campaign pools](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/5045604930843)

With LinkedIn RSC [enabled](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/115005677303), you can add LinkedIn InMail steps to a campaign pool.

For both email steps and LinkedIn InMail steps, each step equates to one message. While you can add as many steps as you like, it is recommended to have at least three, but no more than four steps in your campaign pool for optimal results.

**Note:** Campaign pool steps set to use LinkedIn InMail **do not send automatically**. Each step using LinkedIn InMail will create a task in the Tasks tab to remind you when it's time to send these steps manually.

#### In this article

  * Create a LinkedIn InMail campaign pool step
  * Add and review copy for a LinkedIn InMail step
  * Save and send a LinkedIn InMail step
  * Additional resources



### Create a LinkedIn InMail campaign pool step

From your Greenhouse Recruiting dashboard, click the **CRM** > **My active campaign pools** and click **See all**.

Click to open an existing campaign pool or [create a new campaign pool](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/5045604930843).

In your campaign pool, navigate to the **Steps** tab, then click **Add step**.

Next, set a **wait time** for your step.

**Note:** Campaign pool steps using LinkedIn InMail **do not send automatically**. When a step's wait time has passed, Sourcing Automation will create a task reminding you to send this step **manually**.

If your LinkedIn InMail step is the first step in your campaign pool, set the wait time to **0 days**. This will remind you to send the message after 10 minutes of either launching the pool or adding prospects to an active pool.

If your LinkedIn InMail step is not the first step in your campaign pool, set the wait time at a value above 0.

From the **Action** dropdown menu, select **Send** **LinkedIn InMail**.

**Note:** This selection can't be changed once you've saved and launched this step.

### Add and review copy for a LinkedIn InMail step

Next, create the content for your LinkedIn InMail step.

#### Add InMail copy with an email template

Select a template from the **Template** dropdown menu if you'd like to use one of your existing [email templates](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/115004020946) in this campaign step.

**Note** : LinkedIn InMail steps support plain text only. Any rich text formatting used in your email template will be removed.

#### Add InMail copy manually

You can also write your step's subject line and message content manually.

Use the **Subject** field to give your InMail message a subject line.

Type or paste your message's body content into the field below your subject line.

Use the **Insert token** dropdown to add [default tokens](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/4984925187611) or [custom candidate tokens](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/202609675) to your subject line and email body. Once your InMail step is sent, these tokens automatically fill in personalized information tied to each individual prospect.

As you compose your InMail message, the Sourcing Automation **e****mail coach** will offer suggestions to help you improve your message delivery and avoid spam filters.

Email coach suggestions are highlighted under the message field. Click **View** to see suggestions.

Any suggestions with a red **X** require your attention. Once you've reviewed these suggestions, click **Done** to return to your email and make any suggested changes.

**Note** : While email coach suggestions are highly recommended, they are not required. You can save and send LinkedIn InMail steps even if you don't incorporate suggestions.

### Save and send a LinkedIn InMail step

Click **Save changes** when you're done with this LinkedIn InMail step and need to create additional steps in a new campaign pool.

Click **Save & launch** if you're adding this step to an existing campaign pool.

Unlike other email steps in campaign pools, LinkedIn InMail steps **do not send automatically**. When it's time to send your LinkedIn InMail message to prospects, a new task will appear in your campaign pool's **Tasks** tab to remind you to manually send this message.

Learn how to [send your LinkedIn InMail messages](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/9617625162139) within Greenhouse Sourcing Automation.

### Additional resources

  * [LinkedIn RSC and Sourcing Automation FAQ](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/9617629277723)
  * [Send LinkedIn InMail using Sourcing Automation](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/9617625162139)
  * [Create and manage campaign pools](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/5045604930843)

  * [Apple Safari](https://support.apple.com/en-us/HT204416)
  * [Mozilla Firefox](https://support.mozilla.org/en-US/kb/update-firefox-latest-release)
  * [Microsoft Edge](https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/topic/microsoft-edge-update-settings-af8aaca2-1b69-4870-94fe-18822dbb7ef1)



3\. Clear your browser's cache / cookies.

  * [Google Chrome](https://support.google.com/accounts/answer/32050?hl=en)
  * [Apple Safari](https://support.apple.com/guide/safari/clear-your-browsing-history-sfri47acf5d6/mac)
  * [Mozilla Firefox](https://support.mozilla.org/en-US/kb/how-clear-firefox-cache)
  * [Microsoft Edge](https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-edge/delete-cookies-in-microsoft-edge-63947406-40ac-c3b8-57b9-2a946a29ae09)



4\. Refresh the report in Greenhouse Recruiting by opening it, then copy / paste the report URL into the Google Sheets Connector again to see if the report populates.

**Note** : Refreshing a report on Greenhouse Report Connector only refreshes the _data_ on the report. It does not refresh or sync newly applied filters. If you change filters on your report, you should [import the report](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/115001875646) again rather than refresh it.

5\. If the issue persists, try an incognito browser.

### "An error occurred while trying to retrieve your report"

Occasionally, users will encounter an error claiming that "authorization is required to perform that action."

Typically, this error is caused by the following situations:

  * A change on the Google Sheet where you are no longer an "editor" under the sharing settings. The owner can update these settings to fix the issue.
  * You are using multiple Google accounts on your browser and unintentionally trying to view the sheet from the second account. Switching accounts and trying the extension again may fix the issue.



### Additional support

If the above troubleshooting steps don't resolve your issue, [contact Greenhouse Technical Support](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360058320292) for help.

Gloat is an anonymous AI-based integrated career development and recruitment platform matching talent with open positions in real time. Gloat's anonymity feature enables top tier talent to stealthily job search from the comforts of their current positions.

# Pebl integration

Pebl’s Global Work Platform is the smarter way to build and scale a global workforce. In one unified solution, we help companies hire, pay, and support talent in 185+ countries covering Employer of Record, contractor management, payroll, immigration, benefits, equity, and more.

With built-in compliance, localized expertise, and AI-powered automation, Pebl helps you onboard talent in minutes. Trusted by 1,500+ companies, Pebl delivers the speed, scale, and confidence you need to grow anywhere.

Pebl’s integration with Greenhouse Recruiting allows you to manage your global workforce in one place with AI-powered tools, real-time insights and seamless integrations. Hire, pay and support talent anywhere with confidence.

#### In this article

  * Create a Harvest API key for the Greenhouse Recruiting / Pebl integration
  * Create new custom offer field
  * Create a webhook
  * Use the Pebl integration with Greenhouse Recruiting
  * Additional resources



### Create a Harvest API key for the Greenhouse Recruiting / Pebl integration

To configure the Greenhouse Recruiting / **Pebl** integration, you’ll need to create a Harvest API key.

Follow the steps in [this article](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/5888163769883) to create the key, and verify that the permissions below are selected when configuring the **Pebl** integration.

#### Credentials

In the _Create New Credential_ box, make the following selections:

  * **API Type:** Harvest
  * **Partner:** Pebl
  * **Description:** Pebl Integration Harvest API Key



#### Permissions

Verify that the following permissions are selected for the Pebl integration:

  * **Applications**
    * All permissions
  * **Approvals**
    * All permissions
  * **Candidates**
    * All permissions
  * **Custom Fields**
    * All permissions
  * **Jobs**
    * All permissions
  * **Job Posts**
    * All permissions
  * **Offers**
    * All permissions
  * **Users**
    * All permissions



Click **Save**.

Greenhouse Recruiting will generate the API key and display it in a subsequent dialog box. Click **Copy** to save your API key to your clipboard. Please store the API key in a secure location for now. You will provide the API key to your Pebl Client Account Manager for further setup within Pebl’s software.

Once the API key is stored securely on your local computer, click _I have stored the API Key_ to close the dialog box.

**Note** : You cannot access the full API key again after clicking _I have stored the API Key_. If you lose your API key and need to access it later, you must create a new API key, provide it to the integration partner, and then revoke access to the original key.

### Create new custom offer field

Please connect with the Pebl Sales Solutions team before completing this section. They will provide details on the fields you need to create.

To create a custom offer field, click the **Configure icon** on your navigation bar. From the _Configure_ page, click **Custom Options** on the left. Next, select **Offers**.

From the _Custom Fields: Offers_ page, click **Add Field** to create a custom offer field.

In the dialog box that appears, configure the new offer field. Provide a _Field Name_ and _Type_ , then configure who should see the field.

When you have finished customizing your application field, click **Save**.

For a configuration walkthrough, please reach out to Pebl.

### Create a webhook

Next, you’ll need to create a webhook. Follow the steps in [this article](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/5888163727003) to create your webhook. Use the values listed below to configure the webhook:

  * **Name** : Pebl integration
  * **When** : Offer Created
  * **Endpoint URL** : The Endpoint URL provided by Pebl
  * **Secret Key** : The Secret Key provided by Pebl
  * **Error recipient email:**[leave blank]
  * **Disabled?** : No



Once you complete the above steps, please contact your Pebl Sales Solutions Engineer at [salessolutions@pebl.com](mailto:salessolutions@pebl.com).

### Use the Pebl integration with Greenhouse Recruiting

  * The Pebl Sales Solutions team will assist you in setting up and configuring the integration.
  * After completing the setup, the data will flow and sync between the two systems automatically.
  * The integration uses Greenhouse Recruiting's webhook capability to trigger the data from your Greenhouse Recruiting platform into Pebl once a new offer is created or approved, depending on your webhook configuration.
  * Pebl’s Sales Engineering team will work closely with you to ensure your Greenhouse Recruiting application is configured with the necessary fields for this integration to run smoothly. This may involve creating new custom fields.
  * On the Offer, you will create a new “Pebl Sync” custom field to indicate the candidate is assigned for Pebl integration.
  * The integration will only run for candidates marked for Pebl syncing.
  * The candidate's data will be synced with the Pebl cloud-based software automatically, preventing any manual data errors.
  * In addition, the integration will trigger the onboarding process in Pebl.
  * Notification emails will be sent to your team and Pebl account managers based on the user's notifications preferences. These emails will be sent by Pebl not Greenhouse Recruiting.



### Additional resources

For additional information or troubleshooting not covered here, reach out to [https://hellopebl.com/contact/](mailto:https://hellopebl.com/contact/).

# HRorganizer integration

HRorganizer provides self-service assessments for every type of job. HRorganizer has replaced the selection psychologist with an expert system which drives the creation of online assessment programs and provides clear decision-support information to recruiters and hiring managers. Think of it as an automated, independent, second opinion of your candidates. 

Greenhouse Recruiting's integration with HRorganizer allows you to seamlessly add HR organizer's assessment to a job's interview plan.

#### In this article

  * Create a Harvest API key for the HRorganizer integration
    * Credentials
    * Permissions
  * Retrieve user ID for integration
  * Contact HRorganizer to finish setup
  * Add the HRorganizer Stage a job's interview plan
    * Configure the HRorganizer stage
  * Use the HRorganizer integration
  * Additional support



### Create a Harvest API key for the HRorganizer integration

To configure the Greenhouse Recruiting / HRorganizer integration, you'll need to create a Harvest API key.

Follow the steps in [this article](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/5888163769883) to create the key, and verify that the credentials and permissions below are selected when configuring the HRorganizer integration.

#### Credentials

In the _Create New Credential_ box, make the following selections:

  * **API type:** Harvest
  * **Partner:** HRorganizer
  * **Description:** HRorganizer Harvest API key



#### Permissions

Verify that the following permission is selected for the HRorganizer integration:

  * **Applications**
    * POST: Add Attachment to Application



### Retrieve user ID for integration

In addition to the Harvest API key, HRorganizer requires the user ID of a Site Admin user in your Greenhouse Recruiting account. To get this ID, [export your user list to Excel](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/200521129) and find the **User ID** in the downloaded spreadsheet.

### Contact HRorganizer to finish setup

After the sections above are complete, contact your HRorganizer representative at [support@HRorganizer.com](mailto:support@HRorganizer.com) with the following information:

  * Your Harvest API key
  * The User ID



After they've received this information, HRorganiation will provide another API key. [Open a ticket](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/requests/new) with the Greenhouse Technical Support team to finish setup. 

The Greenhouse Technical Support team will respond with a [SendSafely link](https://www.sendsafely.com/howitworks/) for you to enter your API key. A notification will be sent to the Greenhouse Technical Support team after you have entered your API key and they will email you to confirm that your API key has been set up in your account and your integration is enabled.

**Note:** To verify your identity, the Greenhouse Technical Support team might request you provide a [Support Verification Code](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360022771952) before adding the API key to your organization's account.

### Add the HRorganizer Stage a job's interview plan

After the configuration is finished, the HRorganizer stage can be added to a job's [interview plan](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/115002194903). Add the HRorganizer stage to each job. 

### Configure the HRorganizer stage

Once the stage has been added, click **Edit** and select the correct assessment and grader from the available fields. 

**Note:** The assessment options, instructions, and email templates must be set up in HRorganizer.

### Use the HRorganizer integration

When candidates are moved into the HRorganizer interview stage, Greenhouse Recruiting will display a **Send Test** link. 

Select a recipient, test, and grader from the dropdown menu. 

**Note:** When you send a test from Greenhouse Recruiting, the interview instructions actually are sent by HRorganizer. 

After its sent, the assessment's status will display in Greenhouse Recruiting. 

Once the candidate has submitted their test, the reports instantly will be available for viewing under the [_All Attachments_ section on the candidate's profile](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/202815509).

**Note:** To update the configuration of these resports, [contact HRorganizer](mailto:support@HRorganizer.com).

### Additional support

Contact [support@HRorganizer.com](mailto:support@HRorganizer.com) for troubleshooting assistance regarding the integration.

# Options for exporting candidate data to an HRIS

There are a couple of options for exporting candidate data from Greenhouse Recruiting to your external HRIS. 

#### Options

  * Custom integration via 'candidate hired' webhook
  * Custom integration via Harvest API



### Custom integration via 'candidate hired' webhook

A 'candidate hired' webhook can trigger as soon as a person clicks **Mark Candidate as Hired** in Greenhouse Recruiting. The webhook payload contains all application, candidate, job, and offer data needed to kick off or complete the hire business process in your HRIS. 

**Tip** : If you intend to use Greenhouse technical consultants for configuring your integration, check out [Integrations and technical consulting checklist](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/5912974462235).

#### Requirements

You must use a listener service to receive the 'candidate hired' webhook.

For more information, check out the following resources:

  * [Developer documentation: web hooks](https://developers.greenhouse.io/webhooks.html)
  * [Export hired candidates via webhook](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360002158372)



### Custom integration via Harvest API

Your organization can use middleware to poll Greenhouse Recruiting for hired candidate data on a scheduled basis, and use the data returned to kick off or complete the hire business process for each of those candidates in your HRIS. Read more about candidate export via API here: [API approach to candidate export integration](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/4405338951963).

**Tip** : If you intend to use Greenhouse technical consultants for your custom integration, check out our [Integrations and technical consulting checklist](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/5912974462235).

#### Requirements

Your organization must use middleware to build this integration.

If you would like to further discuss hire integration options, contact Greenhouse Technical Support or your account manager.

# Calendly and Microsoft Teams integration

Organizations that have enabled the Greenhouse Recruiting / Calendly integration can enable additional integrations in Calendly, which can then be used as part of your scheduling workflow in Greenhouse.

In this article, we will discuss enabling and using the Calendly / Microsoft Teams integration. 

**Note:** The Calendly / Microsoft Teams integration requires your organization to have either a **Microsoft 365 Business** account or an **Office 365 Education** account. 

#### In this article

  * Enable Microsoft Teams integration in Calendly
  * Update default event type in Calendly
  * Schedule interview in Greenhouse Recruiting with Microsoft Teams conferencing link
  * Available video conferencing partners in Calendly



### Enable Microsoft Teams integration in Calendly

With the Greenhouse Recruiting / Calendly integration [enabled](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360029359472-Enable-Calendly-Integration), navigate to the Calendly platform and click **Integrations**. 

From the Calendly  _Integrations_ page, click the **Microsoft Teams Conferencing** tile. 

On the subsequent page, click **Integrate Now** in the right-hand panel. 

You will be directed to an OAuth flow to sign into Microsoft. Select an existing account or provide your Microsoft credentials when prompted. 

You will be directed back to Calendly. Confirm the integration is connected. 

### Update default event type in Calendly

Next, you will configure Microsoft Teams Conferencing as the default for a specific event type. Navigate to your Calendly dashboard by clicking **Home** at the top of the page. 

On your Calendly dashboard, scroll through your event types and click the event whose default even type you wish to update. 

On the subsequent page, click **What event is this?**. 

On the subsequent page, navigate to the  _Location_ field and click **Edit**. In the subsequent dialog box, click the top dropdown menu and select **Microsoft Teams**. 

Click **Update** when finished. 

Click **Save & Close**. 

Moving forward, every Calendly meeting booked using this event type will include an automatically generated Microsoft Teams Conferencing link. 

Repeat these steps to make Microsoft Teams Conferencing the default for additional events if needed. 

### Schedule interview in Greenhouse Recruiting with Microsoft Teams conferencing link

To schedule a Microsoft Teams Conferencing interview through Calendly, return to Greenhouse Recruiting and navigate to a candidate profile where scheduling is required. 

Click **Schedule with Calendly** next to the appropriate interview. 

In the  _Schedule with Calendly_ dialog box, click the  _Calendly Event Type_ dropdown and select an event type you have configured to use Microsoft Teams. 

_**Note:**[Click here](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360029686091) for more information on scheduling an interview through Calendly._

Adjust the email if needed, and then click **Send Email** when finished.

Greenhouse Recruiting will append a Calendly link to the email and send it to the candidate's email address. Once the candidate uses the Calendly link to schedule a meeting time, an event will be added to the interviewer's calendar that contains a Microsoft Teams Conferencing link. 

### Available video conferencing partners in Calendly

The following additional [video conference partners](https://calendly.com/pages/integrations/video-conference) can be integrated with Calendly and selected for default scheduling: 

  * Google Meet
  * Zoom
  * GoToMeeting
  * Join.me

# Crosschq integration

Crosschq is an end-to-end hiring intelligence platform designed to help improve hiring efficiency, candidate experience and quality of hire. Recruiting and HR teams use Crosschq to automate their reference check process, source prospects, and collect valuable insights from candidates and employees about their interview and work experience.

Greenhouse Recruiting's integration with Crosschq allows your organization to seamlessly add reference checks and surveys to your existing hiring process.

In this article

  * Set up the Crosschq integration
    * Configure API settings
    * Create a Harvest API key
    * Add your API credentials to Crosschq
    * Create a webhook
    * Configure app settings
    * Add the Crosschq stage to a job's interview plan and complete setup
  * Use the Crosschq integration with Greenhouse Recruiting
    * Configure Crosschq templates
    * Requestors and Hiring Managers
    * Send a Crosschq assessment
    * View a Crosschq report
  * Additional resources



### Set up the Crosschq integration

To begin setup, navigate to your [Crosschq administrator account](https://org.crosschq.com/login) and **Log in**. 

Search for the Greenhouse connector from **Organization Settings > Connectors**. Then, click **Manage** from the Greenhouse section.

On the following page, turn on the Greenhouse connector by clicking the toggle on the right. The toggle should turn green to indicate successful connection.

#### Configure API settings

**Share token with Greenhouse (for 360 references)**

A Crosschq token is stored within the Greenhouse API settings. When shared with Greenhouse, the token will allow you to trigger reference requests when a candidate reaches the Crosschq reference stage in your Greenhouse pipeline. Copy the token.

Once you have obtained your API token, contact Greenhouse Technical Support by using [live chat or opening a ticket](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360058320252-Access-live-chat-in-app). After sharing the token with Greenhouse, their support team will connect the two platforms to one another.

**Note** : For data security purposes, do not include the API key when opening a new ticket.

If, at any point, you need to adjust connector settings, simply return to **Organization Settings > Connectors > Greenhouse** and click on the**Manage** button.

#### Create a Harvest API key

Next, you’ll need to create a Harvest API key.

Follow the steps in [this article](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/5888163769883) to create the key, and verify that the permissions below are selected when configuring the Crosschq integration.

#### Credentials

  * **API Type:** Harvest
  * **Partner:** Crosschq or Unlisted Vendor
  * **Description:** Crosschq Harvest API key



#### Permissions

Verify that the following permissions are selected for the Crosschq integration:

**Applications**

  * GET: Retrieve Application
  * PATCH: Update Application
  * POST: Add Attachment to Application



**Candidates**

  * GET: Retrieve Candidate
  * GET: List Candidate
  * POST: Add Prospect
  * POST: Add Employment



**Users**

  * GET: Retrieve User
  * GET: List User



**Job Stages**

  * GET: Retrieve Job Stage
  * GET: List Job Stages
  * GET: List Job Stages for Job



**Jobs**

  * GET: Retrieve Job GET: Hiring team



**Prospect Pool**

  * GET: List Prospect Pools



**Custom Field**

  * GET: Custom fields
  * POST: Create custom field
  * PATCH: Update custom field



**Education**

  * GET: Degrees GET: Schools



**EEOC**

  * GET: Retrieve EEOC Data for Application
  * GET: List EEOC



**Departments**

  * GET: List Departments



**Rejection Reasons**

  * GET: List Rejection Reasons



**Offices**

  * GET: List Offices



**Sources**

  * GET: List Sources



**Save** when finished.

Your Harvest API key for the Crosschq integration is created and configured. Copy the API key to provide to Crosschq in the next step.

#### Add your API credentials to Crosschq

After creating the API key for the Crosschq integration, navigate back to the Greenhouse Connector API settings in Crosschq (**Organization Settings** >**Connectors** > **Greenhouse**) to provide the key. 

Using the **Harvest APIKEY** field, paste the created API key. When finished, click **Save Changes**. 

#### Create a webhook

Webhooks allow specific events to be updated in real-time in Crosschq, as well as trigger campaign surveys in Crosschq Voice. Crosschq supports the following Greenhouse webhooks:

  * Candidate Hired
  * Candidate Rejected



To enable these webhooks, copy the _Webhook Hired URL_ from the Greenhouse connector API settings in Crosschq.

The _Webhook Hired URL_ in Crosschq will be used to create both hired and rejected status webhooks in Greenhouse.

Next, you’ll need to create the webhooks in Greenhouse Recruiting. Follow the steps in [this article](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/5888163727003) to create your webhook. Use the values listed below to configure the webhook:

**Web hook #1:**

  * **Name** : A descriptive name for your integration. Most customers choose Crosschq integration
  * **When** : Candidate has been hired
  * **Endpoint URL** : The Endpoint URL provided by Crosschq, paste the Greenhouse Webhook Hired URL that you copied from Crosschq.
  * **Secret Key** : The Secret Key provided by Crosschq, copy and paste the token field from the Greenhouse API settings in Crosschq.



**Web hook #2:**

  * **Name** : A descriptive name for your integration. Most customers choose Crosschq integration
  * **When** : Candidate Rejected
  * **Endpoint URL** : The Endpoint URL provided by Crosschq, paste the Greenhouse Webhook Hired URL that you copied from Crosschq.
  * **Secret Key** : The Secret Key provided by Crosschq, copy and paste the token field from the Greenhouse API settings in Crosschq.



**Save** when finished.

#### Configure app settings

Once your API settings are saved, you can configure additional settings for specific Crosschq Apps.

#### 360 settings

When you enable _Attach Crosschq 360 Report to candidate's profile upon completion_ , we will upload completed reference reports to the candidate's profile in Greenhouse if the reference was initiated from the ATS.

#### Recruit settings

The additional Recruit settings allow you to export prospects from Crosschq to Greenhouse. To enable this feature, you will need to set up a prospect pool from the CRM section in Greenhouse. Click [here](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360024904051) to learn more about setting up a prospect pool.

If you do not have the CRM function in Greenhouse, you can still export prospects and [manually upload](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/115002195063) them to Greenhouse.

#### Enable the Crosschq integration - Recruiter Setting

To enable the Recruiter Setting for the Crosschq integration, you’ll need to [create an Ingestion API key](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/5888200444571) and provide it to Crossch. 

Follow the steps in [this article](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/5888200444571) for more information on creating an Ingestion API Key. Once the key is created, provide it to Crosschq so they can set up the integration with Greenhouse Recruiting.

When finished, navigate back to the Greenhouse Connector App Settings in Crosschq. Enable the prospect export feature by clicking the toggle on the right. The toggle should turn green.

Under the **Token** field, paste the copied Candidate Ingestion API key.

Next, enter in a Greenhouse admin email to be associated with the connection.

Under the **Greenhouse Prospect Pool** field, select the correct pool for where Crosschq prospects should be exported.

The Pool ID Number is actually the name of a prospect pool. Your Greenhouse admin will likely want to create a specific prospect pool for Crosschq candidates, and then select that pool from the drop-down menu.

Lastly, if you want to enable automatic exporting of prospects to Greenhouse, click the final check box in this section.

After completing the Greenhouse connection, all of your prospects will automatically or manually export into Greenhouse.

**Note** : To learn how to manually export prospects from the Crosschq Recruit module into your ATS, [click here](https://support.crosschq.com/knowledge/candidates-export).

#### Additional 360 configuration

The following sections will outline extra steps to make sure your Greenhouse connection is successfully linked.

#### Add the Crosschq stage to a job's interview plan and complete setup

Once the Crosschq integration is configured, for every job that you want to leverage Crosschq, you'll need to [add the Crosschq stage to a job's interview plan](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/21338859258267).

To do this for an existing job, navigate to **Jobs** >**Job Name** > **Job Setup.** From the _Job Setup_ page, navigate to **Interview Plan** >**Add stage** and then select the _Crosschq_ stage.

When finished, click **Add** to apply the stage to the job's interview plan.

### Use the Crosschq integration with Greenhouse Recruiting

#### Configure Crosschq templates

Templates are reference request configurations that are used to trigger requests from ATS connectors. You have to set up your Crosschq templates to be able to send Crosschq requests from an ATS.

Within Crosschq, go to **Organization Settings > Templates**. Select **Create New Template.**

Enter the required information such as the template name, add an ATS Tag for that template, and create a description of the template. 

Within the Request Settings, add in the position, select the appropriate survey, and configure the number/type of references you want to be associated with this request. Please note, the relationship type can either be specified or you can select any relationship type and let the candidate determine the type of reference. Additionally, you can add customized notes to each specific reference request, i.e. "_Please provide a manager reference from X company_."

From there, add optional hiring manager information. Finally, you can create custom emails or text messages associated with each template by filling out the custom notifications section. When you are done, select **Create Template.**

****

At any point, if you need to edit or delete a template select the three dots next to the template and you will be able to manage from there.

#### Requestors and Hiring Managers

Crosschq pulls the Recruiter from the details section within a candidate's profile in Greenhouse. 

Crosschq will assign as requestor the GreenHouse user listed as "Recruiter" within the candidate's profile. If there is no recruiter listed in the candidate's profile, Crosschq will assign the user listed as the candidate's "Coordinator". If there are no users listed as recruiter or coordinator, Crosschq will assign the user listed as "Credited To" within the source section.

As for the Hiring Managers, Crosschq will add all users listed as Hiring Managers within the job's hiring team in Greenhouse.

#### Send a Crosschq assessment 

To send a candidate through the Crosschq process in Greenhouse, move your candidate to the Crosschq stage and select **Send Test**.

**Note:** If you want to automate Crosschq assessments being sent to your candidates, [create a stage transition rule](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360053129752).

Once [configured](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360048178672), assessments will be triggered to send automatically after a candidate moves into the partner assessment stage.

Ensure the candidate's email address is correct, select the [Crosschq template](https://support.crosschq.com/knowledge/greenhouse#SetTemplates), and select whom you would like to "grade" the request/have access to notifications, usually, this is the recruiter/candidate owner.

Then, click the **Send Test** button to send the Crosschq to the candidate.

The candidate will receive an email message that includes a link to begin the Crosschq process.

You will then be able to keep track of each request status change by accessing the _Activity Feed_ section of Greenhouse.

#### View a Crosschq report

When the candidate completes the self-reference and all of the references respond to the surveys, the report will be available within the Greenhouse platform. Additionally, the recruiter and hiring manager will also get an email informing them that the Crosschq report is completed. (If the hiring manager doesn't have a Crosschq account a link to create a Viewer account will automatically be sent to the hiring manager.)

The figure below depicts an example in which a candidate has received his overall Crosschq score and the process is complete.

To view the Crosschq report, click the report icon next to the Crosschq stage. On the following page, click**View Report**.

The user will be directed to the completed report in Crosschq. Note that only users with Crosschq accounts will be able to access the report within Crosschq.

If pdf generation and ingestion is enabled in your Crosschq account, you can also find an attached Crosschq report from the **Details** section of the Greenhouse candidate profile or under **All** **Attachments**.

Greenhouse users with enterprise accounts will be able to view a more detailed version of the Crosschq report and status updates related to the report. To access this, users will select the private tab within the _Candidate Details._

### Additional resources

For questions or information on the integration not covered here, reach out to [support@crosschq.com](mailto:support@crosschq.com).

# Metaview integration

Metaview is an interview intelligence platform that gives you unprecedented visibility into what is happening in interviews, and unique data, insights, and training flows to help interviewers calibrate and improve.

Greenhouse Recruiting's integration with Metaview allows you to use your data available in Greenhouse (like offer acceptance / rejection) to enrich Metaview's data and get more predictive insights from interviews.

When finished, click **Save** **changes**.

The integration process will begin. This can take up to 48 hours to complete, and you will be emailed once the integration setup is successful.

### Use the Metaview integration with Greenhouse Recruiting

The integration with Greenhouse allows Metaview to capture your organization's interviews as well as the details you already have available in Greenhouse such as offer acceptance/rejection, candidate demographics, and scorecards—all to enrich the insights we're able to provide.

# Save candidate search

**Permissions:** Job Admins who can view or edit candidates or above

**Product tier:** Available for new subscription tiers (Core, Plus, and Pro)

There is no in-app functionality that enables a user to save a candidate search in Greenhouse Recruiting. However, since the URL for the **All Candidates** page reflects all filters applied to the candidate list, Greenhouse Recruiting recommends that you bookmark the page after you have applied your filters to save the candidate search. This will allow you to conveniently run a specific search whenever you like without resetting the filters.

**Use-case** : You frequently use the **All Candidates** page to check for interviews that need to be scheduled by a specific coordinator. Rather than applying the filters and generating the list of candidates every time you want to run this search, apply the filters once and bookmark the page. When you access the bookmark in the future, the list of candidates will populate with the most up-to-date information from your system based on these filters.

To bookmark and save a candidate search, click the**Candidates** tab from the navigation bar.

Use the filters on the left to narrow down the list of candidates. These filters will populate the next time you access the page through the bookmark.

With your filters set for this candidate search, follow the process to create a new bookmark for your specific web browser:

  * [Apple Safari](https://support.apple.com/guide/safari/bookmark-webpages-to-revisit-ibrw1039/mac)
  * [Mozilla Firefox](https://support.mozilla.org/en-US/kb/bookmarks-firefox#:~:text=To%20bookmark%20a%20page%2C%20just,star%20in%20the%20address%20bar.)
  * [Google Chrome](https://support.google.com/chrome/answer/188842?hl=en&co=GENIE.Platform%3DDesktop)
  * [Microsoft Edge](https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-edge/add-a-site-to-my-favorites-in-microsoft-edge-eb40d818-fd1f-cb19-d943-6fcfd1d9a935)



When you access the bookmarked **All Candidates** page, the query will run with your filters applied, and provide the most up-to-date results.

# Terminate employees

**Permissions:** Owner

**Product tier:** Available for Greenhouse Welcome and Greenhouse Onboarding subscription tiers

Terminated employees refer to former employees who have since left your organization. Users with Owner access can update employment statuses in Greenhouse Onboarding to mark employees as terminated. 

**Note** : Terminating an employee in Greenhouse Onboarding will make the employee hidden from all current employees. Owners and Coordinators will be able to access a terminated employee's record through search.

#### In this article

  * Pre-termination checklist
  * Terminate an employee
  * View and manage terminated employee profiles
  * Additional resources



### Pre-termination checklist

Before terminating an employee in Greenhouse Onboarding, your organization will want to ensure that any direct reports, open tasks, or planned tasks are reassigned to another employee. Follow the checklist below to ensure a smooth transition once the employee's profile is terminated:

[Reassign direct reports](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360026122431)  
[Reassign or delete open tasks assigned to the terminated employee](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/13260067443995)  
[Reassign any planned tasks](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360049725052)

Once you've reassigned direct reports and reassigned or deleted the necessary tasks, you're ready to terminate an employee profile.

### Terminate an employee

To terminate an employee in your organization, use the **search bar** to open the employee's profile.

Click the **Admin** tab in your employee's profile.

On the _Admin_ page, scroll to **Employment Status** and click **Edit**.

Change the employee's **Employment Status** to **Terminated** and set their **Date of Termination** _._ Click **Save** when you're done.

In the next window, review and confirm that you'd like to terminate this employee.

When you're ready, click **Terminate Employee**.

### View and manage terminated employee profiles

This employee will now be marked as terminated in Greenhouse Onboarding. The employee will appear in tasks and reports until their termination date has arrived.

After the termination date, terminated employees are hidden from current employees and removed from tasks and reports. Owners and Coordinators can continue to access terminated employees' profiles by search.

### Additional resources

  * [Rehire an employee in Greenhouse Onboarding](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360004880972)

Shared calendars enable your team to maintain a centralized scheduling system so that authorized members of your team can schedule, reschedule, and delete to a single calendar.

**Note** : The steps for shared calendar setup may vary depending on how your organization has configured its Outlook 365 settings. Check with your organization's Outlook account admin or [learn more on Microsoft](https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/office/share-an-outlook-calendar-with-other-people-353ed2c1-3ec5-449d-8c73-6931a0adab88#ID0EBBF=New_Outlook).

### Create a shared calendar

To create a shared calendar, determine who should own the calendar, then have the owner login to the Outlook 365 web app and navigate to the calendar pane on the left.

Click **Add** **calendar**.

Click **Edit my calendars** to share an existing calendar, or click **Create blank calendar** to create a new calendar.

Enter a name for the calendar, and if necessary, choose a color and charm.

Select a folder for the calendar, then click **Save**.

Find your new calendar under the _Edit my calendars_ tab, and click**Share calendar**.

Enter the email address or name of the person with whom you want to share your calendar, and choose **Can** **edit** from the permissions dropdown.

**Note** : The person's email address on Outlook 365 must match their primary email address on Greenhouse Recruiting.

The people who you invite will receive an email invitation. They should click **Accept and view calendar** on the email.

Once complete, your team can use the shared calendar to schedule interviews on Greenhouse Recruiting with the Outlook 365 integration.

# Set up HRIS Link job import with job requisitions

**Permissions:** —

**Product tier:** Available for Pro subscription tier with HRIS Link add-on

With HRIS Link, you can programmatically import jobs from Workday®️ to Greenhouse Recruiting. To use HRIS Link with job import, construct a report as a service (RaaS) in Workday®️ that meets Greenhouse Recruiting specifications.

**Note** : This article is specific to organizations with job requisitions enabled on Workday®️. If you don't use job requisitions on Workday®️, check out [HRIS Link without job requisitions](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/4403988430235).

#### In this article

  * Set up HRIS Link job import 
    * Report specifications
    * Sample report output
    * Sample report definition
    * Recommended filters
  * Add custom fields to HRIS Link



### Set up HRIS job import

**Note** : HRIS Link currently only supports Workday®️.

First, create a RaaS job import report in Workday®️ using the report specifications below. The primary business object in your report should be Job requisition. Once constructed, [enter the report URL and your ISU credentials](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/11006737633307) in HRIS Link.

#### Report specifications

**Note** : HRIS Link relies on an exact match of the report column header. Some report column headers are required or case-sensitive. In most cases, you need to override the default value when adding columns to your Workday®️ report. 

**Report column header** |  **Workday®️ field** |  **Greenhouse Recruiting field**  
---|---|---  
`Requisition_ID` ✓ Required ✓ Case-sensitive |  Job requisition ID |  [Requisition ID](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360061697231)  
**Note** : The unique value for the `Requisition_ID` field is used to determine if the job already exists in Greenhouse Recruiting.  
` Number_of_Openings ` ✓ Required ✓ Case-sensitive |  Number of openings total |  Number of [openings](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/4402057774747)  
**Note** : The `Number_of_Openings` field refers to the number of job openings on this job requisition.  
` Template_Job_ID ` ✓ Required ✓ Case-sensitive |  Calculated Field (Evaluate Expression) |  [Template job ID](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360059668131)  
**Note** : The `Template_Job_ID` field value must be a valid Greenhouse Recruiting job ID. This field is only required on initial job creation and not on any subsequent updates.  
` Opening_ID ` ✓ Case-sensitive |  Position ID |  [Opening ID](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360037953951)  
**Note** : The `Opening_ID` field is nested within the `Position`, like this:
    
    
    {  
       "Position": [
      
          {"Opening_ID": "123"},
      
          {"Opening_ID": "456"}
      
         ],
      
    ...
      
    }

Greenhouse Recruiting allows up to 100 open openings at a time for each Greenhouse Recruiting job. [Learn more](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360058731532).  
` Name ` |  Job title |  [ Internal job name ](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/115002799383)  
` Job_Post_Name ` ✓ Required |  Job posting title |  [External job name](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360020285311)  
**Note** : The `Job_Post_Name` field is only required on initial job creation and not on any subsequent updates. This value cannot be edited after job creation.  
` Job_Post_Description ` ✓ Required |  Job description |  [Job post description](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/115002791566)  
**Note** : The `Job_Post_Description` field is only required on initial job creation and not on any subsequent updates.  
` Job_Post_Location ` ✓ Required |  Varies |  [Job post location](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/115002791566)  
**Note** : The `Job_Post_Location` value must match an `external_id` for one of your Greenhouse Recruiting offices. The `Job_Post_Location` field is only required on initial job creation and not on any subsequent updates.  
` Office_IDs ` |  Varies |  [Office](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360029179271)  
**Note** : The ` Office_IDs` field value must match an `external_id` for one of your Greenhouse Recruiting offices. The value can be semicolon delimited to assign more than one office to a job.  
` Department_ID ` |  Varies |  [Department](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360029179271)  
**Note** : The ` Department_ID` field value must match an `external_id` for one of your Greenhouse Recruiting departments.  
` Recruiters ` |  Primary Recruiter - Employee ID |  [Recruiter](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360016347712)  
**Note** : The `Recruiters` field value must contain the employee ID or email address of the job's recruiters, delimited by a semicolon.  
` Recruiter_Role_ID ` |  Calculated Field (Text Constant) |  Job Admin role for recruiter  
` Hiring_Managers ` |  Supervisory Org - Employee ID |  [Hiring manager](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360016572311)  
**Note** : The `Hiring_Managers` field value must contain the employee ID or email address of the job's hiring managers, delimited by a semicolon.  
` Hiring_Manager_Role_ID ` |  Calculated Field (Text Constant) |  Job Admin role for hiring manager  
` Sourcers ` |  Primary Sourcer - Employee ID |  [Sourcer](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360016347852)  
**Note** : The `Sourcers` field value must contain the employee ID or email address of the job's hiring managers, delimited by a semicolon.  
` Sourcer_Role_ID ` |  Calculated Field (Text Constant) |  Job Admin role for sourcer  
` Coordinators ` | Primary Coordinator - Employee ID | [Coordinator](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360016347752)  
**Note** : The `Coordinators` field value must contain the employee ID or email address of the job's hiring managers, delimited by a semicolon.  
` Coordinator_Role_ID ` |  Calculated Field (Text Constant) |  Job Admin role for coordinator  
` Status ` ✓ Case-sensitive |  Job requisition status |  Job status  
**Note** : The `Status` field value must be one of `open`, `closed`, `frozen`, or `filled`. Only jobs with an `open` status will be imported to Greenhouse Recruiting. HRIS Link will notify recruiters when there is a disparity between the job status in Workday®️ and Greenhouse Recruiting. [Learn more](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/4402652528923).  
` Close_Reason ` |  Job requisition close reason |  [Close reason](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/213351483)  
**Note** : The `Close_Reason` field value must be a case-insensitive text match to an existing [close reason](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/213351483) in Greenhouse Recruiting.  
` Notify_Email ` |  Varies |  N/A  
**Note** : You can add multiple email addresses for status notifications, delimited by a comma. This is the email address that will receive a notification when the corresponding job is created in Greenhouse Recruiting, or, if the `Status` column is included, when the requisition status in Workday®️ report doesn't match the Greenhouse Recruiting job status.  
` Custom Fields ` |  Check out the Add custom fields to HRIS Link section. |  Check out the Add custom fields to HRIS Link section.  
**Note** : Add any custom fields to your Workday®️ report. HRIS Link will match the column header name to the name of your custom field in Greenhouse Recruiting.  
  
Once you've constructed your report, [enter the report URL and your ISU credentials](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/11006737633307) in HRIS Link and reach out to your Greenhouse technical consultant.

They'll enable HRIS Link, and jobs created or updated in Workday®️ will automatically sync to Greenhouse Recruiting. [Learn more](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360058912031).

#### Sample report output

Once your HRIS Link job import report is built, you should receive output similar to the below example of a valid report entry in SimpleXML:

**Example**
    
    
    <wd:Report_Data>  
    <wd:Report_Entry>  
              <wd:Opening_ID>201456</wd:Opening_ID>  
              <wd:Requisition_ID>R100000</wd:Requisition_ID>  
              <wd:Template_Job_ID>42002</wd:Template_Job_ID>  
              <wd:Job_Name>Software Engineer</wd:Job_Name>  
              <wd:Job_Post_Name>SSE II</wd:Job_Post_Name>  
              <wd:Office_IDs>New York City</wd:Office_IDs>  
              <wd:Department_ID>Engineering</wd:Department_ID>  
    </wd:Report_Entry>  
    </wd:Report_Data>

#### Sample report definition

[Click here](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/article_attachments/11114020734107) to download a sample report definition exported from Workday®️ which provides additional guidance on how to build a job import report.

#### Recommended filters

We recommend that your HRIS Link job import report include all open and closed job requisitions. HRIS Link won't import closed jobs, but it will compare job statuses across Workday®️ and Greenhouse Recruiting to ensure parity.

Your HRIS Link job import report should exclude job requisitions that have been closed for longer than 1 day. This filter allows HRIS Link to capture job status changes, while simultaneously preventing the report size from growing increasingly large.

### Add custom fields to HRIS Link

In addition to the standard fields listed in the specifications above, HRIS Link supports importing data into custom job fields of all [types](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360001421452).

**Tip** : When importing data into single-select or multi-select field types in Greenhouse Recruiting, we recommend [custom option sync](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/360002158492) to ensure the best experience.

For all fields, the report column header must match either the custom field immutable key, like `cost_center`, or the field name, like Cost Center _,_ in Greenhouse Recruiting.

HRIS Link supports [role-based approvals](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/19316003622427) with custom job fields as long as the field is present on your report.

# Best practices: Scorecard categories

**Permissions:** –

**Product tier:** Available for new subscription tiers (Core, Plus, and Pro)

As you're diving into scorecard configuration, one key element is setting up your scorecard categories. We suggest using our sample template if you're having trouble defining the categories that you'd like to use.

Greenhouse Recruiting's sample scorecard supports you in creating this structure with the following four default scorecard categories:

#### 1\. Details

Is the candidate eligible to be considered for the role? Evaluate the basic requirements to be considered for the job.

**Example attributes** : Able to work in the US, fits salary range, willing to do required travel

#### 2\. Qualifications

Does the candidate have the necessary qualifications? Verify the concrete previous experiences or certifications that are required to fill the role.

**Example attributes** : Engineering degree, HR certification, SaaS experience

#### 3\. Skills

Does the candidate have the work product and skills? Consider the skills and expertise that an ideal candidate would have honed throughout their career.

**Example attributes** : Event coordination, lead generation, budget management

#### 4\. Personality traits

Will this candidate add to the company culture? Understand the personality and culture add of the candidate.

**Example attributes** : Entrepreneurial, likes to learn new things, passionate

* * *

If the default scorecard categories don't resonate with you, check out the other ways some organizations have categorized their scorecards:

  * **Interview type** : Phone interview, take home test, culture fit, department interview, executive interview
  * **Skill type** : Job description, department requirements, company values, general requirements

# Job board scrolling issues

**Permissions:** \--

**Product tier:** Available for new subscription tiers (Core, Plus, and Pro)

When a user visits your job board, there's a chance they're scrolling through multiple opportunities. In some cases, scrolling issues on your board can make it frustrating to skim multiple opportunities in one session. 

Check out the section below for some common scrolling issues and possible resolutions. 

#### In this article

Job Board scrolls back to the top of the page when the user clicks the "Back" button

Job board scrolls to the top of the page when the user clicks a job link

**Note:** You'll need to know your organization's[ job board integration type](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/200721644) to choose the best solution for your organization.

### Job Board scrolls back to the top of the page when the user clicks the "Back" button

When a user selects a job, the post will open in the new window or page. If a user selects a job and then returns to the job board using the browser's **Back** button, the page will load at the top, forcing the user to scroll back down to the list of opportunities. 

If your job board is hosted by your company ([integration options 3, 4, and 5](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/200721644)) you can control this behavior with your website's code. However, you'll need to contact whoever developed your organization's website to correct this.

If you're using integration options 1 or 2, you can turn on **Don't scroll to top of page on page load** to make sure the page loads back on the job board if the user goes back to the job board using the browser's **Back button.**

To turn this setting on, navigate to your job board configuration options (_Configure > Dev Center > Configuring Your Job Board_) and select the correct job board from the top right corner of the page.

Select **Don't scroll to top of the page on page load** in the _Configure_ box. Now, when a user selects a job and the page reloads, the page will stay in the same place.

### Job board scrolls to the top of the page when the user clicks a job link

When a user chooses a job link from the job board, it will open in a new window or page. However, if you are hosting or embedding a Greenhouse Recruiting job board inside your own website, your website's code may be conflicting with with the embedded Greenhouse iFrame (the technology used to display the job board) and cause the page to scroll to the top of the screen when a new job post loads.

To fix this issue, you'll need to reach out to the development team responsible for your organization's website and ask them to fix the scrolling issue on page refresh. This issue is most common with integration options 2, 3, 4, and 5. 

Alternatively, to completely avoid this issue, Greenhouse can host your job board through integration option 1. 

[Click here](https://support.greenhouse.io/hc/en-us/articles/200721644) for more information on the job board integration options.
